# Book 1: Scars — Professional Edit (Continued)

Book 1: Scars — Professional Edit

Project Overview

Target: Convert entire manuscript to consistent third-person limited, past tense. Polish prose while preserving Akari's core personality and all plot beats. Ensure canon Tokyo Revengers characters sound authentic to their source material.

Character Voice Reference Guide:

Character Voice/Speech Pattern Personality Notes

Sanzu Haruchiyo Casual, teasing, protective. Uses "sweetheart" naturally. Sharp edges when angry, soft with Akari. Obsessive loyalty, violent capability, hidden tenderness. Unhinged but controlled around her.

Mikey (Sano Manjiro) Simple, direct. Childlike sweetness masking darkness. Short sentences. Rare emotional vulnerability. Charismatic, deeply traumatized, capable of terrifying blankness. Dark impulses he suppresses.

Kakucho Earnest, straightforward. Loyal to a fault. Slightly formal. Steady presence, moral compass, protective without being overbearing.

Izana Regal, measured. Hints of instability beneath composure. Uses "family" as a weapon. Traumatized by abandonment, desperate for belonging, capable of cruelty born from pain.

Draken (Ryuguji Ken) Blunt, protective. Big brother energy. Practical. Loyal, grounded, doesn't tolerate bullshit but deeply caring.

Mitsuya Takashi Polite, responsible. Older brother vibes. Gentle but firm. Mature, nurturing, surprisingly dangerous when pushed.

Takemichi Earnest, emotional, occasionally pathetic but determined. Brave in the face of fear, selfsacrificing, cries easily but never gives up.

Ran Haitani Playful, flirtatious, theatrical. Calls people pet names. Sadistic amusement, genuinely cares for few people, enjoys chaos.

Rindou Haitani Quiet, observant, deadpan. More reserved than Ran, equally dangerous, fewer words.

Baji Keisuke Direct, rough, loyal. Protective of those he cares about. Fierce, sacrificial, hidden softness.

Hanma Shuji Chaotic, mocking, theatrical. Enjoys pushing buttons. Unpredictable, drawn to strength, serves his own amusement.

Kisaki Tetta Controlled, calculating, condescending. Manipulative, desperate for validation, genuinely believes he's right.

CHAPTER ONE

Akari stood at the edge of a skyscraper, wind tearing through her hair and whipping across her face as she looked out over Yokohama. Beside her stood Izana and Kakucho, silent sentinels against the sprawling cityscape below. Flashing signs and streams of headlights glittered in the darkness, a living organism of light and motion.

"Are you sure you want to go through with this, Akari?" Izana's voice barely carried over the wind.

"Yeah." She didn't turn to look at him, keeping her eyes fixed on the horizon. "I need to do this for my own sake." A pause. "I'll miss you, though."

She studied his side profile—the sharp lines of his face, the platinum hair that caught the city lights like spun silver. He didn't respond, but she hadn't expected him to.

FLASHBACK

Reform School had been a love-hate relationship. The hate part was obvious—the walls, the rules, the constant violence. The love part had been Izana and Kakucho, two constants in a world designed to break people down.

Beating people up had been the norm. When Tenjiku formed with Izana as its leader, Akari had felt something she hadn't felt in years: hope. She'd trained until her muscles screamed, fought until her knuckles split, and earned her place as third-in-command. Kakucho held second. They were a trinity, unstoppable.

Once released, they'd stayed in Yokohama, pouring everything into the gang's growth. Every day brought new challenges, new fights, new victories. Akari's name spread through the underground until it reached the ears of those who mattered. "Scarlet Snake," they called her. She'd hated it at first—the reminder of the scars that curved up her cheeks like a permanent smile. But the name stuck, as names do.

Her division, Scarlet, handled the bloody work. Murder. Torture. Everything in between. She enjoyed that side of the job more than she cared to admit, which was precisely why the name fit.

They'd designed their uniforms themselves—red, naturally. Every day with the gang brought something new, and she loved being part of it.

But that chapter was ending.

END FLASHBACK

Morning sun stabbed through her eyelids. Akari groaned, rolling out of bed with all the grace of a dying fish. She packed her belongings into three cardboard boxes—she didn't have much, and the new apartment came furnished—then slipped her phone and wallet into a small bag.

The doorbell rang as she was still getting dressed.

"One second!"

She pulled on her face mask, attempted to tame her wolf cut into something presentable, and hurried to the door.

"Oh, Izana! Good morning." She stepped aside. "Do you want to come in for a bit?"

"Morning." He offered her a small smile. "Sure, if that's okay."

He took off his shoes, stepped into the main room, and settled onto her small couch. "Nearly time, huh?" His voice was quiet, his eyes fixed on his hands in his lap.

"Yeah..." She glanced away. "I'll come visit once I've settled in. Or you can come see me. I promise I'll keep in touch."

"Okay..."

Akari retreated to her bedroom, made the bed, and gave the room one last quick tidy before picking up her boxes. She looked around at the place she'd called home for five years, then closed the door behind her.

"Are you going to keep that mask on the whole time you're in Tokyo, too?"

"Oh, yeah. Definitely." She grinned beneath the mask. "I don't want people asking stupid questions. But there's no way I'm getting bullied for it. I can beat them up on the spot." She raised an arm and flexed. Izana laughed quietly.

"Isn't it time you left? You're going to miss your train."

"Oh, shit. You're right!"

She grabbed her three boxes and small bag, carrying them outside. She waited for Izana to step out before locking the apartment door behind them.

"I'm going to give you the key to my apartment here, okay?" She handed it to him. He nodded, slipping it into his uniform pocket.

"I'll walk you to the train station." He took two of the three boxes.

They walked side by side to Yokohama Station, talking about how Tenjiku would be at a loss without "Scarlet." When they reached the platform, Izana handed the boxes back. She placed them on her assigned seat, then returned to the train door.

"I miss you already," she joked. Izana snickered.

"I have two little surprises for you."

"What are they?" She tilted her head.

"First..." Izana took her wrist and drew her into a tight hug, arms wrapping around her waist. "I'm going to miss you a lot. You and Kakucho have given me—and the whole gang—a reason to keep going. I'm going to cherish Tenjiku until the day it disbands. So make sure you come back, okay?"

"Sure. But what if I join another gang in Tokyo?" She smiled beneath the mask.

"Do whatever you like. As long as you're alive, I'll be happy." His expression was serious. "And secondly..."

He whistled.

A wave of red uniforms flooded down the stairs and onto the platform. Tenjiku, in full force, stood before her.

"We all wanted to thank you, 'Scarlet Snake.'" Izana's voice rang out. "Thank you for all your hard work, Division Three Leader Akari!"

"Thank you!" Tenjiku roared in unison.

Akari's eyes stung. She blinked rapidly, refusing to cry in front of them.

She wrapped her arms around Izana again and pressed a quick kiss to his cheek. "Thank you for everything, Izana. I'll text you when I get there."

She let him go and stepped back onto the train. The whistle blew. The doors closed. She sank into her seat, watching through the window as every Tenjiku member bowed their heads in unison.

She was still wearing her Tenjiku uniform out of respect.

Akari pulled out her phone, untangled her earphones, and turned up the music.

CHAPTER TWO

The train finally halted, and Akari stepped out into Shibuya, Tokyo. She lowered the volume, removed her earphones, and packed them away before grabbing her boxes. Her eyes swept the platform, cataloguing exits and potential threats—old habits dying hard.

Outside, airplane lights twinkled where stars should have been. Evening bleeding into night was her time of day. She chuckled quietly to herself.

People gave her the stink eye as they passed, avoiding her like she carried something contagious. The Tenjiku uniform, she guessed. She hated the bustle of people around her. Yokohama was crowded, but not like this—this was sardines in a tin, pressed shoulder to shoulder with strangers who wouldn't meet her eyes.

She didn't know where her new apartment was.

Akari asked for directions, but no one was willing to help. Sighing, she set down her boxes, pulled out her phone, and typed in her new address. She memorized the route and made her way through unfamiliar streets.

Finally, she stood in front of her new apartment building. She'd passed her new school on the way— close by, thankfully. She pulled the keys from her back pocket and pushed one into the keyhole.

Noises on the other side of the door.

Her hand stilled. That wasn't supposed to happen.

She set her boxes down outside, muscles coiling with tension. Then she swung the door open, standing in the doorway, blocking the exit.

Silence.

She moved through the apartment slowly, checking every corner, every shadow. Nothing. Maybe she'd imagined it—air displacement, old pipes, something.

Footsteps behind her.

A hand clamped over her mouth. Cold metal pressed against her throat.

"Shut up, or I'll slit your throat."

Akari didn't freeze. She closed her eyes, drew a deep breath, and drove her elbow into his stomach. The knife clattered to the floor. She scooped it up and knocked him unconscious—just for the sake of it.

He lay crumpled on her floor while she retrieved her boxes, brought them inside, and locked the front door behind her. She kept one eye on his prone form as she grabbed towels and bedsheets from the bedroom, sat him up on a chair, and tied him securely.

He started groaning. Coming to.

"Who are you and why are you here?" Her eyes bored into him.

Silence.

"Don't make me use that knife you gifted me." Her eyes creased—smiling beneath the mask. She watched him weigh his options, then waved the blade lazily.

"Fine. I'll tell you." His voice shook despite his efforts to hide it. "There were rumors at school that a delinquent was going to be living here. Sanzu ordered me to check if anyone was here yet."

"Who's Sanzu?"

"He's the vice president of Division 5 of a gang in Tokyo. Tokyo Manji Gang, or Touman. No one can go against him—he's scary, crazy, and hella strong. Isn't that enough?"

"Yeah, that's enough." She pulled down her mask, letting him see her scars stretch as she smiled. The terror on his face said everything. "Now promise me you won't say a word about meeting me here, okay?"

"Okay, okay, I promise!"

She chuckled, untying him. "You're free to go. See you at school tomorrow!"

She opened the front door and waved as he sprinted down the street.

"Finally." She sighed heavily, closing the blinds and turning on the lights. You never knew who might be watching.

She unpacked, setting out her uniform for tomorrow. As she washed her face, she remembered to text Izana.

Me to Izana:

I got to my new apartment safe, so don't worry. Text you again soon?

She turned off her phone, placed it on the bedside table, and looked at her uniform hanging on the door. Excitement flickered in her chest.

A quick check of her bank account—¥10,000 for the week from her father. About a hundred dollars.

Due to family issues and an abusive household, she lived on her own. She had no interest in exposing herself to that toxicity again.

Tenjiku had been her second home, her second family. Kakucho and Izana were like brothers to her. They meant everything.

She made instant ramen for dinner, mentally planning tomorrow. Convenience store after school—she needed food. Then lights off, and she tucked herself into bed.

CHAPTER THREE

The alarm rang at 6:30 AM. School started at 8:00. Akari didn't particularly care if she was late on her first day.

She dragged herself out of bed, her shoulder-length wolf cut a disaster. A quick shower, brushed teeth, then she examined her new sailor uniform in the mirror. Cute, but the skirt was way too long. She rolled it up. Better.

Her ear piercings would definitely get called out. Whatever.

She packed her bag and sent Izana another text. He hadn't checked the one from last night either.

Me to Izana:

I'm about to go to school now. Wish me luck!

She grabbed a banana and a piece of bread, put on her shoes, and left, locking the door behind her.

The school bell chimed as she walked. Already late on her first day. She started running—then realized she'd forgotten her jumper. Another ten minutes wouldn't kill her. She went back, grabbed it, and ran to school again.

What a way to start the day.

Inside, she changed her shoes. The corridors were empty—she had no idea where to go. She ran around for a bit, completely lost, until she rounded a corner and collided with someone tall.

She looked up. A boy with a black mask, long blonde hair, and striking blue eyes stared down at her.

"Sorry." She spoke quickly. "I'm new, so I don't know where to go."

His eyes widened slightly. "Oh, you must be the new girl everyone's talking about. I'll take you to our class." His tone was flat. Uninterested.

"Thanks."

Walking beside him was awkward. He didn't speak, so she broke the silence.

"I'm Kurokawa Akari, by the way. Nice to meet you."

He just looked at her and nodded.

You didn't have to act like that, she thought, irritated.

He opened the classroom door. "Wait here. I'll let the teacher know." He shut the door in her face.

She heard chairs screeching, the teacher yelling. "Why'd you leave the classroom, Haruchiyo! I'll like to see you after class!"

Then silence. The door slid open, revealing the teacher. He closed it behind him.

"Hello, Kurokawa. We were expecting you today. Hope you had no trouble finding our classroom. I can excuse you for being late today, but I won't accept tardiness again. Do you understand?"

"I was able to find this classroom thanks to the boy in the mask, sir. And yes, I understand."

"Care to explain the piercings, disastrous haircut, and the mask as well?"

"Sir, whatever the rule is, I will not be removing my mask or piercings, and I will not be changing my hair either. If you like, I can see you after class—just like the 'Haruchiyo' kid—but it's not going to change anything. Now, excuse me. I'd like to introduce myself to the class."

She smiled and walked past him, sliding open the door. She wrote her name on the blackboard.

"Morning, everyone. I'm Kurokawa Akari. I came from Yokohama Reform School. Feel free to ask any questions if you have any. Thanks."

She watched the faces of her classmates shift from curiosity to terror at the words "reform school." Except for Haruchiyo. He looked at her with a funny expression.

"You can sit next to Haruchiyo, Kurokawa," the teacher said, annoyed.

She walked to her seat, plopped down, and took out her books. Her phone vibrated—Izana had finally replied.

Izana to you:

You should be fine. Tell me if anything happens.

Me to Izana:

Of course, I will. Don't you worry!

Haruchiyo tapped her shoulder. She looked up—the teacher was heading her way. She quickly shoved her phone under her skirt (he wasn't going to ask her to flip it up) and grabbed a pen, pretending to pay attention. The teacher saw her "working" and returned to the front.

"Thanks," she whispered.

Again, just a nod.

Class dragged on until the lunch bell finally rang. Everyone left for the cafeteria. Just her and Haruchiyo remained.

"Aren't you going to eat?" she asked.

"I could say the same to you."

She sighed. "...I don't like eating in front of people."

She saw him twitch.

"Same." His voice was quiet. "I have a scar under my mask. I usually keep it hidden."

"No way... same here." His eyes widened with curiosity. "How about we show each other on the count of three?"

He hesitated, then nodded.

"Alright then. One. Two. Three!"

She removed her mask, watching as he did the same. Two diamonds on each side of his mouth—cute, actually. It suited his face.

He started laughing.

CHAPTER FOUR

Akari stared at him, more confused than offended. His laughter echoed in the empty classroom, tears forming at the corners of his eyes.

"Sorry, it's just—you look like a snake." He wiped at his eyes. "Sorry, I didn't mean to be rude."

"They didn't call me Scarlet Snake for nothing." She shrugged.

"Scarlet Snake? What's that?"

Fuck. Really fucked up now.

"Oh, um—it's just a game I play!"

Nice save, Akari.

"Oh, that's cool then." He pulled his mask back on. "Do you wanna join me and my buddies on the roof for lunch?"

"Sure. Lemme get my food."

She grabbed her lunch and followed him to the door. As they walked through the halls, she noticed the other students' expressions—fear, whispered conversations that weren't as quiet as they thought.

"Hey, isn't that the new girl from Yokohama Reform School?"

"I heard that was a place for delinquents..."

"You reckon she's a delinquent?"

"Doesn't she know who Sanzu is?"

Akari turned at the name. Sanzu. She'd forgotten about him. Where was he?

She continued following Haruchiyo to the roof, where his friends were waiting.

"Yo, Sanzu. We were waiting for you."

Sanzu...?

No way.

I'm so stupid.

Akari grabbed Haruchiyo—Sanzu's—collar and tripped him, pinning his hands behind his back.

"What's the meaning of this, Akari?" Sanzu asked, his buddies frozen in shock.

She shot them a death glare. "Don't interfere, boys."

They stepped back.

"I guess it's my turn to laugh now, isn't it? Haruchiyo Sanzu, Division 5, Vice-Captain of Touman." She pressed her knee against his neck. His mask had fallen to the floor.

"Well, I can tell you're no ordinary girl, Akari. Good job yesterday night." He flashed her a cunning smile.

"I'm not stupid. I was part of a gang too."

"How about you get off me and we talk about it like people? Or do I need to force you?"

Before she could reply, he flipped her off him, pinning her beneath him. She blushed, keeping her face neutral.

Please don't notice. Pleaseee.

"Fine." She rolled her eyes. He got up, and she dusted off her skirt.

His friends had left. Just the two of them now.

"Do you wanna join our gang, Akari?"

The question shocked her. She hadn't expected it so quickly.

"Sure." The answer came fast. "I was thinking about something to kill time with anyway." She emphasized the word kill, watching for his reaction.

He reacted.

"What was your role in your former gang?"

"I was third commander, and Captain of my division, 'Scarlet.' We handled murder, torture, and all the other gory shit, if that helps explain it."

He shot her a look, then began to laugh, covering his face.

"You're the same as me. You'd fit perfectly in my division." He was cackling now. "Certainly not a position anyone would expect from you, though. A weak-looking girl."

That does it.

"I'll join your division. I'm going to do it to kill time and prove myself. Better watch your back, Sanzu."

She shot him the largest, most evil smile.

"Alright, that's done. There's a gang meeting today, so I'll take you. It's not until 8 PM, so I'll see you at your place later. See ya."

He left her alone on the rooftop.

She looked down at the school grounds, admiring the view. It reminded her of the times she'd spent with Izana, looking down at the streets of Yokohama. The school bell chimed. She couldn't be bothered with class—she ran back, grabbed her bag, waved at Sanzu, and left.

CHAPTER FIVE

Akari took a detour to the convenience store near the school, buying food for the next few days. She was minding her own business when a tap on her shoulder made her turn.

"What's up?"

"...Are you okay?" The boy—the same one who'd broken into her apartment—looked at her with concern. His face was covered in bruises. "Sanzu didn't do anything to you, right?"

"I'm okay. Don't worry about me." She lifted his chin to get a better look at his face. His ears turned a couple shades redder. "Did Sanzu do this to you?"

He averted his gaze.

"I see. I'll do something about it, so don't worry. What's your name?"

"Takemichi..."

"Alright, Takemitchy it is! I'll see you around then!"

She was about to leave when he called out again.

"Can I grab your number before you leave? Just in case something were to happen?"

She gave him a blank look. "Sure."

He handed her his phone. She typed her number in, handed it back, and headed to the cashier. She paid for her food and left, waving to him as she headed out the door.

At home, she packed away her groceries, changed into comfortable clothes, and collapsed onto her bed. A quick check of her phone—3:00 PM, no new messages.

She drifted off to sleep.

FLASHBACK

The sounds of crashing ceramic and yelling woke her. Five years old, tiptoeing to her bedroom door, opening it to see her parents arguing.

"Why does she have to look like you? You know I can't stand your face!" Her mother's voice was shrill.

She noticed Akari peeking through the door and dragged her out.

"Disgusting."

Her father watched as her mother grabbed a knife, lifted it to the corners of Akari's mouth, and ran it in a quick motion. Then the other side.

"What do you think you're doing to our daughter?! You're going too far!"

"What do you mean, our daughter?" Her mother scoffed and walked out the door.

Akari never saw her again.

Her father carried her to his car. All she tasted was the sweet copper of her own blood. Euphoric.

At the hospital, the doctors were horrified. A young child, in such a state. She faintly remembered her father lying to them before passing out.

END FLASHBACK

"Akari! Oi, Akari!"

Someone shook her awake.

"Get up, it's 7:45 PM right now."

She jolted upright. No one should be here.

She bumped heads with whoever was waking her.

"Owww," they both said.

"Oh, sorry. Wait—what the fuck are you doing in my house, Sanzu?!"

He just glared at her.

"I know where you live, remember? I picked the lock, dummy." He rolled his eyes. "Hurry up and get dressed. We're gonna be late."

He left the room, rubbing his forehead.

She dressed quickly—Tenjiku uniform—and left the house. Sanzu was waiting outside, leaning against his motorcycle.

Damn, that's cool.

"Hurry up and get on." He put a helmet on her head. "Make sure to hold on tight. Don't want you falling off." He grinned.

She wrapped her arms around his waist, feeling him flinch slightly. The engine roared to life. Her hair fluttered everywhere. She felt cold, but warm at the same time—adrenaline rushing through her veins, wishing it would go on forever.

The bike stopped.

"Akari, we're here." He tapped her shoulder. "I'm going to talk to my captain and see if he'll talk to our leader. Wait here."

She nodded, watching him leave. She removed the helmet, placed it on his motorcycle, and sat down next to it. His bike was cool. Made her want one, but she definitely didn't have the money.

She was too busy admiring the bike to notice footsteps behind her.

A figure knocked her out. She slumped to the floor, feeling her body being carried before everything went black.

CHAPTER SIX

SANZU POV

She was gone.

He'd left her alone for two minutes. Two minutes. He knew she was strong, but he was still worried. She'd worn her previous gang uniform—fuck, that was a bad idea.

"Oi, Sanzu." A booming voice called. He turned to see a fellow gang member—too minor to bother remembering his name. "Is that your bike? 'Cause your girlfriend just got knocked out and taken away by Baji."

Shit.

He ignored the guy and ran straight for the meeting area. There she was—slumped at the top of the steps, leaning on Baji.

He rushed up the stairs, only to be pushed back down by Draken himself.

"What do you think you're doing, Sanzu?" Draken's voice was ice. "Why are you bringing a spy to our gang meeting?"

I'm screwed.

"I wanted her to join my division. I was hoping to ask Mucho, but it seems I was too late."

"We'll start our meeting first. When she wakes up, we'll ask the girl." Mikey's voice cut through the tension.

YOUR POV

Akari woke to a crowd of at least a hundred people in black uniforms. The Musashi Shrine. She saw some staring at her, but most were focused on the man standing next to her. She didn't want to turn around, so she kept scanning the crowd.

The gang was separated into five groups. She found Sanzu at the very front, at the edge of the gang. She shot him a look. He raised an eyebrow as if to say, We're in trouble.

"Meeting dismissed. You can all leave now."

The crowd dispersed. Murmurs, shuffling feet, then only the important people remained—and Sanzu.

"So, who are you?" The man beside her spoke.

"I'm Kurokawa Akari. Call me Akari. I came from Yokohama Reform School, and I now attend ____ High. Same as him." She pointed at Sanzu. "I was in a gang in Yokohama called Tenjiku. I was third-in-command and led my own group, 'Scarlet.' Our division was in charge of the same things as Sanzu's group. I—"

"She's quite strong." Sanzu cut her off. "I wasn't paying attention, but she was able to knock me down."

The members' eyes widened.

Sanzu began introductions. "This is Baji. He's the one who knocked you out. Captain of Division One."

Baji glanced at her, flashing pointy teeth.

"Mitsuya is Captain of Division Two." Mitsuya offered a small smile. He looked too nice for this kind of gang.

"Pah-chin is Captain of Division Three." Pah-chin just stared. She stared back.

"Nahoya, or Smiley, is Captain of Division Four." Smiley's eyes were wide, but he smiled. A little unsettling.

"Mucho is Captain of Division Five—my group." Mucho nodded.

"Draken is Vice Leader. And the leader is Mikey."

Draken looked her up and down. She felt a little violated. Mikey looked uninterested, eating whatever he was eating.

"Thanks for the introduction, Sanzu." She gave him a small smile. "So, am I allowed to join this gang or not?"

"Oh, so you were serious," Mucho whispered to Sanzu.

"Mhm. I wanna see her fight full out, though," Sanzu replied. "She seems interesting."

"Oi, Mikey." Draken's voice cut through. "What do you think?"

"If she's able to land a hit on me, then I'll consider it. Especially since she came from another gang—you never know if she's a spy or not."

"Sure, I'll fight you." Akari's voice was steady. "Don't go easy on me, though."

"Mhm, okay. How's tomorrow, right here, same time?"

"Sure thing!" She grabbed Sanzu's wrist and dragged him away. "Sanzu, can you drive me back home?"

"Uhhh, sure..." He didn't try to escape her grip, so she loosened it.

She thought about everything that had happened as he drove her home.

"Thanks for everything, Sanzu. I'll see you tomorrow at my place again?" She hoped he could drive her again tomorrow night.

"Sure, I don't mind. Umm, about Mikey. He likes to use—"

"I don't wanna hear it." She cut him off. "It wouldn't be fair if I know how he fights, but he doesn't know about me. Anyways, see you tomorrow!"

She got off his bike, returned his helmet, and climbed the steps to her apartment. She looked down to see him watching her until he was sure she was inside.

Why is he watching me? Why am I red...

She turned on the lights and heard the sound of a motorbike riding away. She took off her Tenjiku uniform, showered, ate dinner, and headed to bed.

Then a knock on the door.

Sanzu had just left. Who could it be?

She tiptoed to the front door and peered through the peephole.

A familiar face.

Mikey.

CHAPTER SEVEN

Akari opened the door slowly, staring at him. She'd left her mask in the bathroom—it must have been shocking for him to see her face.

He didn't react.

"Nice scar you got there." He walked into her apartment.

"Why are you here?" She asked, a little terrified.

"I'm not gonna do anything strange. Trust me on that. I just came to ask you a few questions privately. Is that okay?"

If it's so I can win his trust, then I don't mind.

"Sure thing. So what's up?"

She opened the door wider, and Mikey entered. He took off his heavy boots, lined them up neatly against the wall, then took a quick glance around before sitting on the couch. She sat opposite him.

"Who's the boss of Tenjiku, and why'd you move?"

"Izana Kurokawa. I moved because none of the schools in Yokohama wanted me. My dad works in Tokyo, so he's able to do something if something were to happen. He doesn't care about me, so it's fine either way. Is that all?"

"Why 'Scarlet Snake'?"

"I don't know. I didn't make the name myself. Must've been because my scar makes me look like a snake, and because I like the idea of blood." She gave him a small smile, her scar stretching.

"How do I know I can trust you?"

"What else have I got to lose other than my life? If Tenjiku were to attack your gang, I'm going to just watch. I ain't taking sides."

She raised an eyebrow, watching him react slowly. He didn't do much, just mumbled.

"Also, you might wanna think about letting Draken inside if you're gonna stay for a while. It's cold outside."

"Oh, so you noticed."

She walked to the front door, opened it, and went to find Draken. "Oi, Draken. It's cold, so come inside."

He popped out from the staircase and began walking toward her. "Thanks," he mumbled. She swore she heard his teeth chattering.

"Do you guys want anything to eat, or are you gonna keep asking me questions?"

"I'll take warm tea, please." Draken stated. "I'm so fucking cold." He nudged Mikey.

"I'll take one too, and then we'll leave. Thanks, Akari." Mikey paused. "By the way, you're already in the gang. Asking the questions changed my mind. I just wanna see how good you are, so make sure you still come tomorrow evening."

"Okayyy." She handed the green tea to Draken and Mikey, then left the room to get her stuff ready for school tomorrow. She heard Mikey calling for her.

"Yea?"

"Do you wanna lift tomorrow after school to the Shrine, or are you okay?"

"Nah, I'm okay. I've got Sanzu to do that for me, so I'm good. Thanks for asking though."

"She's got him wrapped around her finger," Draken said, chuckling. Akari turned bright red.

"Hmph, sure I do." She pouted.

"Trust me, I know you do. He's never let anyone ride his bike, so that says more than a lot," Mikey said. "Anyways, thanks for the hospitality. I'll see you tomorrow evening then."

He got up, left the two empty cups in the sink, put on his boots, and headed out. Draken followed.

"Cya, Akari." Draken said.

"Bye-bye, Akari-chin." Mikey smiled—a genuine, warm smile.

"Yea, cya tomorrow. I'm gonna beat you, Mikey!" She flexed her biceps.

"Ohhh, bring it!" Mikey laughed as he left.

She closed the front door, turned off all the lights, and dozed off, ready for school and the match against Mikey.

Loud knocking woke her.

"Oi, Akari! Get your ass up."

Groaning, she got out of bed to open the door.

It was Sanzu.

CHAPTER EIGHT

Akari was so sick of interruptions. First Mikey and Draken, now Sanzu. Couldn't she get a moment's peace?

She opened the door, the ice-cold breeze hitting her face. Sanzu stood in the doorway. It was 2 AM.

"What?" Her voice was cold. She grabbed his hand and dragged him inside.

"Can I hide out here until we leave for school? Someone's at my place, and I'm pretty sure they're out to kill me."

"Karma's a bitch, isn't it?" She raised an eyebrow. "Do you know who it is?"

"Probably Moebius or some other gang. I didn't do shit yet." He paused. "But thanks for letting me in. Much appreciated."

"Exactly, so don't do it to others." She punched him lightly in the stomach. "That's for Take-chan. You're lucky I'm not doing anything else to you." She smirked.

"Okay, okay, I'm sorry."

Footsteps at the front door.

She grabbed his hand and dragged him to her bedroom. "What—" She clasped a hand over his mouth.

"There's someone at the front door. I think they followed you," she whispered. She grabbed her mask and put it over her scar. "Stay in my room and don't come out until I tell you to."

Loud knocking.

"Oi, I know you're in there, Sanzu. Come on out."

"Akari, you're gonna go to the door wearing that...?"

She looked down. She'd completely forgotten she was wearing thin pajamas. She looked back at Sanzu— a small tint of red across his face.

"I'm gonna kill you later, Sanzu. And yes, I'm gonna go like this so it looks like I just woke up. Now. Don't. Come. Out. Of. The. Room."

She closed her bedroom door and walked toward the front door.

Jeez, why can't they just leave me alone?

More knocking. "Open up, Sanzu!"

She opened the door slowly—only for him to slam it open, the door hitting her forehead and cutting it open.

"Well, isn't that a nice thing to do, mister."

He was shocked, eyes wide, stuttering. "I-I'm so sorry, ma'am. And for your forehead too. I'll, umm, take my leave now."

"Now, now. Don't think I'll just let you go. Gimme your name and gang, and maybe I'll just forget about it." She smiled at him nicely. She watched his face, him thinking about running. "I can report you to the police instead, if you prefer. I have cameras in my peephole."

"Uhh, fine. I'm Osanai, and I'm the leader of Moebius. Okay, that's done. Cya."

He trotted off.

She felt blood running down her face. She took off her mask, not wanting to dirty it. She licked the corner of her mouth where blood was starting to collect. Sweet, as always.

She walked back to her bedroom and swung the door open. Sanzu was sitting on the floor, reading a book. Unexpected.

"That was quick—" He glanced her way and stared. "Akari, your forehead..."

"Hmm? Oh, yeah, I realized. We can go to the hospital later. You're gonna get ganged up on if you come with me, and I can't just leave you here either."

"That's gonna leave another scar," he said, worried.

"It's on the edge of my forehead, near the hairline. So no one's gonna notice."

"Do you wanna skip school? We can go to the hospital instead."

"Sure, my health over education." She flashed him a smile.

She went to the kitchen and grabbed the medicine box. She heard Sanzu come out to watch.

"Need help?"

"Yea, I think I do."

She handed him the cotton ball, alcohol, and tweezers. He dipped the cotton ball into the alcohol and dabbed it on her wound. It stung. He saw her flinch.

"Sorry, Akari."

"Nah, it's not your fault."

He dried the area with tissue and stuck a bandage on it. He cleaned up the rubbish and gave her back the medicine box.

"We're definitely checking that at the hospital tomorrow."

"Okay, Mum." She rolled her eyes. "Can we sleep now? I got interrupted twice already."

"Sure."

She stumbled to her bed, sleepily. He watched as she got in. He pulled the blanket over her neck and let her fall asleep comfortably.

SANZU POV

She looked so peaceful sleeping. He left the room, closing the door as gently as possible. He went to the bathroom, took a quick shower, and prayed she wouldn't be mad tomorrow morning.

The hot water ran down his skin and through his hair. God, I wish I was back at home. But I never thought Akari would let me in so easily. Shouldn't she be more careful about letting men into her apartment? Not saying I would do those things... She is pretty cute though... that's for only me to know.

He dried his hair with his t-shirt, not wanting to use her towel, and left the shirt hanging to dry. He grabbed the blanket on the couch she'd set out for him and lay down. It was still cold, but he could deal. He drifted off, waiting for what tomorrow might hold.

AKARI POV

She'd noticed Sanzu tucking her in, but she was wide awake and red. Her head began to swell, so she went to grab an ice pack from the kitchen. She saw him on the couch, completely out, shivering under the blanket.

His hair was wet. He'd taken a shower. He was going to catch a cold.

She carried him to her bedroom. He was heavy, but not too bad. She lowered him onto her bed and covered him with warmer blankets. She knew she wouldn't be able to sleep anymore, so she sat on the desk chair with an ice pack on her forehead and began to read the book he'd been reading.

The Art of Not Giving a Fuck.

A good book, she thought, chuckling.

She turned her attention back to Sanzu as he turned in his sleep.

"...No, Akari, don't do that," he mumbled.

He just said my name in his sleep.

She squealed. Internally. And smiled at his sleeping face.

Editing Notes for Continuation

Key decisions made:

1. Third-person limited, past tense — Close following of Akari's perspective while allowing natural

observation of other characters

2. Sanzu's voice — Casual, teasing, protective. His internal monologue shows his obsessive loyalty and

hidden vulnerability

3. Dialogue preservation — Original dialogue kept where it worked; smoothed where awkward, but

maintaining the characters' distinct speech patterns

4. Prose polish — Sentence variety, sensory details, improved transitions, but keeping the original's

directness

5. Akari's personality — Sharp, damaged, capable, surprisingly tender. Her humor and darkness both

preserved

6. Pacing — Flashbacks integrated more smoothly; scene transitions clarified

7. Romantic/sexual tension — Implied through physical awareness, charged moments, and internal

reactions rather than explicit content

# CHAPTER NINE

- *SANZU POV**

Sanzu woke in Akari's bed. He didn't remember falling asleep there—she must have carried him over.

- Damn, she's strong.*

"Morning." She was smiling at him. "Did you sleep well?"

"Yea, thanks for carrying me here. Don't you feel tired?" He asked, to which she turned back to her book.

"I'll sleep after we come back from the hospital." She paused. "Anyways, get dressed and take me to the hospital. I think the swelling has gone down a bit."

He looked down and realized his shirt was still hanging on the couch. He got up out of her bed and opened the bedroom door to leave—when she grabbed him by the ear.

"Next time, ask me if you want to shower. I would've provided a towel and clothes at least."

"Sorry," he said, rubbing his ear. She released her grip. "I'll ask next time."

He left the room to get his shirt and saw food laid out on the table. Breakfast. He felt a pang of guilt at the hospitality.

"Make sure you eat. I've already eaten, so hurry up," she called. "I'm gonna take a quick bath, and then let's go to the hospital."

She left the room. He sat down at the table and began eating.

- Yum.*

- *AKARI POV**

She walked into the bathroom and turned on the tap, watching the water fill the tub. She undressed and stepped into the water, the warmth washing over her body. She touched her forehead—still swollen. She kept the bandage on, worried the water might make the injury worse.

Knocking on the bathroom door.

"What?" She was annoyed at the interruption. "Can't let me out of your sight anymore, San-kun? Are you worried about me?" She teased, chuckling.

"You wish. Just wanted to say thanks for the meal."

"You could've told me that *after* I came out of the bath. Anyways, I'm nearly done, so wait for me on the couch."

Footsteps leading away from the door.

She finished up, dressed in comfortable clothes, and walked out with a towel around her head. She sat on the couch next to Sanzu and dried her hair. He just sat there awkwardly, not knowing what to say.

"Umm, I'm so sor—" he started.

"I don't wanna hear your lame apology. You can make it up to me instead." She cut him off. "Drive me around when I want, and for now I'll be happy."

He stared at her before responding. "I—okay."

"Okay, so let's go. Take me to the hospital, San-kun."

She saw his ears go a little red at the new nickname. He got up off the couch, and she followed him out the door. She locked it behind her and followed him down the stairs.

"I have a small problem," he started. She looked at him, genuinely concerned. "My motorbike is at home."

She sighed loudly, facepalming—only to forget about her forehead and wince.

"Careful, Akari," he started. "I'm gonna walk home and come back with the motorbike."

"Sorry, but no." She shook her head. "You're gonna get assaulted, so I'm coming with you."

"Okay, suit yourself."

He started walking toward his place. She followed a couple of steps behind, looking around as they entered an unfamiliar area. He suddenly stopped, causing her to bump into his back. She peeked her head from behind him and saw Osanai again.

- Jesus, not again. Just leave him alone...*

"What do you want, Osanai?" Sanzu asked.

"Oh, aren't you the girl from last night?" Osanai asked her, completely ignoring Sanzu's question. "I knew you guys knew each other."

"So what if we do?" She stepped forward. "What are you gonna do about it?"

She felt Sanzu holding her t-shirt back, trying to prevent her from rushing in.

"What?" she whispered.

"He's got men hiding. Trust me. It's not gonna end well if we continue."

"So what do you expect me to do then?"

"I'll give you the keys to my motorbike. Pretend to run away, climb over the back fence, get the motorbike, and come help me. Now go!"

She ran in the opposite direction.

"Come back here, you bitch!" Osanai yelled.

She didn't look back. She found a small alleyway, climbed onto the top of the wall, and made her way to his motorbike. She placed the helmet on her head and started the engine, roaring it as a signal to Sanzu. She stepped on the accelerator and rode toward his direction. She saw him being chased by Osanai and his gang. She made a quick stop in front of him. He was battered and bruised—not surprising, since it was ten to one. He jumped on the motorbike, and she left Osanai in the dust.

"I'll get you soon!" Osanai yelled.

"How'd I do?" she asked Sanzu after a couple minutes of driving slowly, having successfully outrun Osanai's gang.

"Take over for me. I feel nauseous."

She stopped the bike and got off as Sanzu sat in front. She sat behind him, wrapping her arms around his waist.

"You did really well, considering you've never ridden a bike by yourself before. We'll go to the hospital now. So hold on."

She felt safe near Sanzu as he drove. It wasn't long before they arrived. The doctors led her away and stitched up her forehead. They were honestly scared for her—a young girl with so many scars. She just shrugged it off. She met back up with Sanzu in the waiting room.

"Okay, let's go. I'm sleepy." She said to Sanzu. He just nodded.

They got home, stumbling through the front door. She felt Sanzu carrying her to her bed, tucking her in. This time, she really fell asleep.

- *SANZU POV**

She fell asleep again. He watched her for a bit, then sat on the bed, leaning against the wall. He still felt guilty for involving her in his mess. He felt a tug at his sleeve. She was pulling it. He let her pull it; she was dragging him toward the window side of the wall. With no choice, he lay down next to her, watching her face—decorated with scars, old and new—before he fell asleep as well.

# CHAPTER TEN

- *AKARI POV**

She woke to Sanzu's arm wrapped around her waist. A shiver crawled up her spine, redness flushing her cheeks. He nuzzled closer—definitely aware of her flustered state, teasing her.

She sighed and rolled over to face him, flicking his forehead.

"Owww," he said, rubbing it.

"Get up, you teddy bear. It's time to go again."

"Okayyy." He got up groggily and dragged her with him off the bed.

She brushed her hair quickly, grabbed her Tenjiku uniform, grabbed Sanzu's hand, and rushed out the door to his bike.

Once they got to Musashi Shrine, she saw everyone from yesterday.

"Hey, Akari-chin," Mikey said.

"Geez, what happened to you guys?" Draken asked.

She looked at Sanzu before replying. "Moebius," they said together.

"I see. They've started their attack already." Baji said.

"Tch." Pah-chin was clearly annoyed. "More people are going to get hurt, you know."

"We'll have a meeting tomorrow at the warehouse about it, so don't worry, Pah-chin." Mikey turned back to her. "So, are you ready, Akari?"

She looked back at Mikey and smiled. "Oh, hell yea."

She gave Sanzu her mask and Tenjiku uniform, flashing him a small smile that everyone noticed.

"So the rules," Draken announced. "Akari wins if she's able to hit Mikey. Mikey wins if he's able to knock Akari to the floor. Fair?"

She pondered for a bit before speaking up. "Can it be the same for both of us? Like, whoever lands a hit wins?"

"Don't get too cocky, Akari," Mikey said. "But sure, I'm okay with that."

"Okay then. Three, two, one. Start!"

She watched Mikey's movement. He didn't move. The stalemate continued for a couple of seconds before she began to run at him. She launched a left hook, which he blocked. She saw him lift his right leg—an attempt to knock her out by hitting her temple—but she blocked that too. Gasps from the others.

She launched another punch, then a kick, both successfully blocked. The exchange continued until she retreated back to where she'd started. She took a deep breath, felt her eyes haze over, becoming blurry. She licked her lips and ran at full speed. Mikey, anticipating a left kick, blocked the side of his head—but she jumped right over him, landed behind him, and slid her foot between his legs. He turned around a little too late, and she knocked him to the floor. She attempted to punch him but stopped before doing so. It was a stalemate—he had a foot ready to swing at the back of her head.

Everyone was shocked.

"Uhh, nobody wins," Draken said. "Neither of you was able to hit the other."

"Damn." She got up off Mikey. "I was so close."

"So was I." Mikey reached his hand out for her to shake. "Good fight, though."

She accepted. "Likewise."

"Mitsuya, can you?" Mikey asked.

"Sure, gimme a couple days, will you?" Mitsuya said. "Sanzu, can you drive Akari to my school tomorrow after school?"

"Sure," Sanzu replied.

She was completely clueless but didn't bother asking.

"Akari, come to the warehouse with Mitsuya tomorrow. I'll need you there." Mikey stated.

"I—umm, okayyy..."

"Anyway, welcome to the Tokyo Manji Gang, Akari. I'll put you under Mucho and Sanzu's division, since you already know about their job." Mikey said. "Okay, you guys can leave now. Cya tomorrow!" He turned around, and Draken followed.

"Akari, good job. That was a really good fight. I haven't seen Mikey fight like that before." Sanzu plopped a helmet on her head and handed her the mask and uniform.

"Oh, thanks." She got on his bike, and he drove her home.

"Are you sure you'll be okay at home?" she asked Sanzu.

"Yeah, I will. But I'll stay over at your place, 'cause they know where you live too."

"Okay. Damn, you're making moves, San-kun." She winked at him, opening the door to her apartment, laughing. She didn't realize Sanzu was blushing madly.

"I don't have a spare futon, so you're gonna have to share with me. I don't really care, so..."

"Anyway, go take a shower. You stink!" She pushed him into the bathroom, pinching her nose. She could hear him laughing as he disappeared behind the door.

Once she heard the water running, she got a spare towel and the largest clothes she had and left them in front of the bathroom door.

She knocked. "I left a towel and some clothes on the floor outside the bathroom."

"Thanks," she heard Sanzu exclaim.

She turned on the kitchen stove and began to boil pasta, simmering tomato sauce in a separate pan. She strained the pasta, put it in the pan, and began to mix it—when she heard footsteps behind her.

"Ooooh, pasta." He said. "I haven't had it in so long."

"Get the plates and utensils and set them on the table, will you?" She didn't pay attention to what he said.

She heard him grabbing the plates, bringing back some unpleasant memories. She suppressed them, trying not to show it on her face.

"You okay?" Sanzu asked.

"Hmm? Oh, yea. My head still hurts from this morning." She pointed at her forehead. He pulled her out of the kitchen and made her sit down on the chair as he took over cooking.

She watched his back as he continued to mix the pasta. He brought the pan over, steam rising into the air, then disappearing.

"Thanks," she said.

"It's the least I can do after everything." He said. "Now eat. You need to regain your strength since neither of us ate lunch."

"Thank you for the food," they both said before digging in.

"Ohh, this is nice," he said.

"Of course it is."

Once they finished eating, she sat on the couch holding an ice pack to her forehead while Sanzu washed the dishes.

"Do you want Panadol?" he asked.

"Nah, I'm okay. A little sleep and I should be fine."

She began to walk to her bed. Sanzu dried his hands and followed. He turned off all the lights and turned on the bedroom light.

She walked toward her bed but tripped on the rug in the middle of the room. She was falling—but a strong arm held her up, and she heard a large bang.

Sanzu was holding her body with one arm while holding himself up with the other. He looked down at her and stared, wiping the hair away from her eyes.

"You need to be more careful, Akari."

"Mhm." She responded. "Sorry."

She fell asleep in Sanzu's arms.

# CHAPTER ELEVEN

- *SANZU POV**

Akari fell asleep in his arms. And he couldn't move. At all. He could try to get her on the bed, but she'd wake up.

He needed to sleep too. He was tired.

He tried anyway. She stirred in his arms as he laid her on the bed. He lay down next to her, falling asleep only after kissing her soft lips tenderly.

He woke facing the wall, with a small bruise on his forehead. He groaned, getting up—only to turn around and get pulled back down by Akari. Not wanting to fall on her, he propped himself up.

"What?" He stared at her beneath him, into her eyes.

He leaned down closer to her face, watching her react—before she placed a hand over his mouth.

She moved off him and grabbed her school uniform before heading to the bathroom.

She finished her shower and got changed, a towel around her head. The smell of bacon rushed to her.

She followed the smell and watched Sanzu cooking bacon and eggs for both of them. She walked behind him and gave him a small pat on the back.

"Thank youu!" She said cheerily. She took out two plates and the cutlery before he served it. She brought it to the table, and he sat down.

"Thank you for the meal," they both said before digging in.

"Why is Sanzu battered and bruised, but she isn't?"

"He drove me to the hospital, so leave him out of it." She glared at the teacher. Scared, not wanting to affiliate himself with them, he accepted it and moved on.

By the time lunch arrived, the rumors had spread even faster. That's what happens in schools.

She suddenly remembered Take-chan.

"Oi, Sanzu. What class is Takemitchy in?"

"Next door. Why?"

She arrived at Takemitchy's classroom and slammed open the door. He saw her and nodded. He walked over, and she closed the door behind him. His reaction changed when he saw Sanzu.

"Don't worry too much, Take-chan. Just come with us to the roof."

The three of them walked up a couple flights of stairs and finally reached the rooftop.

"Sanzu, apologize." His eyes widened in shock. "Now."

She heard him sigh before he apologized to Takemitchy.

"Sorry, Takemichi, for making you do what you did."

He walked closer and whispered a couple words she couldn't hear. She saw Take-chan's eyes widen a bit before he smiled, putting up a small thumbs up.

"Apology accepted, Haruchiyo-kun."

All three of them, done with the apology, left the roof.

"What'd you say to him, huh?" She asked Sanzu.

"I'll tell you when the time is right." He ran away from her to reach class first.

School finally ended. Sanzu drove her straight to Mitsuya's school. He walked right in with no respect and marched up to the room where Mitsuya was. He slammed open the door, and she peeked from behind his back.

Multiple sewing machines.

"A hidden stitch would be better there, Fuyumi."

"Ah, okay."

She did *not* expect to see this, out of everything. She knew he was too nice to be in a gang.

"Yo, Mitsuya," she exclaimed. He turned his head to the door.

"You finally came, Akari, Sanzu."

"So why are we here?" Sanzu said impatiently.

"I'm gonna be making your gang uniform, Akari." Mitsuya stated. She was excited. "Sanzu, you can go home. I need to take Akari to the meeting tonight anyway."

"Okay, cya later Akari, and thanks Mitsuya." Sanzu took his leave.

"Man, he's really changed after meeting you," Mitsuya said. "He's become more considerate and wellbehaved, so thanks."

"Oh, I didn't do anything."

"Anyways, can you go into that room? I need to take measurements."

She walked into the small curtained-off room. A girl walked in and told her to undress, leaving only her undergarments. Mitsuya walked in with measuring tape and began taking her measurements.

It wasn't long before he finished, and she put her school uniform back on.

"Sorry if you felt uncomfortable," Mitsuya said. "It's the best way to get the sizing accurate."

"Nah, don't worry about it." She stepped out of the curtain room. Most of the girls from earlier had gone home. The sunset sky colored the classroom with a pale orange hue.

"Anyways, let's go to the meeting." Mitsuya walked her through the school to his bike. He tossed her a helmet, and she clung to his waist as he took off.

After a while, they arrived at an abandoned warehouse, rubbish piling on one side. She followed Mitsuya through a hole in the fence and slid open the back door.

"About time, Mitsuya," Mikey said, seeing them walk in. She was shocked to see Takemitchy as well. "Alright, let's get started."

He rode his motorbike to the hospital as fast as he could after hearing from Mikey that Akari went into cardiac arrest. Mikey followed.

- Thank fuck.*

# CHAPTER EIGHTEEN

- *AKARI POV**

She opened her eyes to blank walls and a couple of cords embedded in her body. She tried to move but winced from a stinging pain in her abdomen. She slowly sat up.

Everything came back.

The festival. The fight. The stabbing. Draken. Passing out.

She didn't remember anything after that.

She felt around her abdomen and found a small patch of bandage covering her stab wound. She looked around and saw Sanzu's gang jacket folded neatly on the bedside table. A small note stuck out of the breast pocket. She took it out, and another smaller sticky note fell onto her lap.

- Don't open the other note until I get there. I'll come back to visit again soon. — Sanzu*

She smiled widely, blushing at Sanzu's small note. She put the other note back into the breast pocket when her room door opened.

Mikey.

He stared at her in shock, glad she was awake. He entered and shut the door behind him. He waltzed to her slowly and sat on the small stool next to the bed. She reached her hand out, and he grabbed it in a rush. She pulled him onto the bed and wrapped her arms around his shoulders, pulling him into a tight hug.

"I'm so sorry I made you worry, Mikey," she whispered.

He didn't reply, just hugged her tighter, sniffling into the crook of her neck. She rubbed his back.

"You said you were never gonna leave me. And then you go and do something like this. I got so scared." He started. "I was really worried, but make sure you console Sanzu the most, okay? He hasn't left his house at all, except to visit you."

"I'll take care of him, so leave him to me." She said, becoming fretful about his condition. Mikey nodded and let go.

"I'll come to visit again tomorrow, so I'll see you then." He got up and went out the door.

She heard commotion outside before the door slammed open and a body ran to her, stopping suddenly. Arms wrapped around her waist, pulling her into a tight hug.

"Don't ever do that again," Sanzu said.

She lifted his chin and kissed his forehead lightly before hugging him back tightly. She saw his red, swollen eyes—something she'd never see from Sanzu again. She felt herself tear up as she hugged him tighter.

"I'm—I'm sowwy," she said, crying into his shoulder.

They sat there, sniffling and tearing up for a couple of minutes before she spoke up, calming down.

"So what's with that note in your jacket?" She sniffled.

"Long story short, Hanma came to visit you the day you were hospitalized and told me to give you the note. 'For your eyes only,' he said. So I haven't looked at it. But I wanted to be here when you opened it. Now that you're awake and I'm here, we can finally see what's in it."

She reached for the note, taking it out of the jacket. She unfolded it.

Two images.

A manji symbol and a headless angel.

In the middle was a "vs" sign and a date.

- 31st October, or Bloody Halloween.*

Smaller writing at the bottom:

- Congrats on waking up. Good thing you survived—you're a vital part of our plan, so we needed you to

wake up. See you soon~? — Hanma*

She turned it over. Nothing on the back. She faced Sanzu, who was looking over her shoulder.

"Well, he seems nice." She rolled her eyes.

"I really hope you said that in all sarcasm," Sanzu responded.

"Shouldn't we tell Mikey about this?" She asked, puzzled. "How do we know we can trust him?"

"We should wait and see. We'll go from there." Sanzu said. "Something might happen at the next Touman meeting in two days, so we'll wait until then. Hurry up and get better so you can attend. Oh, and there's also a ceremony for the new Third Division captain, so make sure to be there."

"Oh, okayyy."

"Anyways, hurry up and get better. Call me when you get discharged, so I can come pick you up." Sanzu messed up her hair.

"Mhm," she said quietly.

Sanzu leaned down and kissed her forehead before leaving her alone.

She thought about the Bloody Halloween Hanma had mentioned.

She had a really bad feeling about this event.

"Nice, Baji!" Hanma said. "I'm more than happy to have you aboard. Here." He tossed a Valhalla uniform to Baji.

"Akari~? Tell Mikey that in a week from now, on October 31st, in an abandoned car lot. Valhalla vs Touman. Our final fight!" Hanma winked, remembering the note he'd given her earlier.

She was annoyed. She turned her back toward Valhalla and left their hideout. She dialed Sanzu.

"Babe, can you pick me up? I'm outside an abandoned game center."

"Sure, sweetheart. Gimme five minutes and I'll be there."

She ducked into a small alleyway and slumped onto the floor. She looked up at the sky, littered with small stars drowning in the city's light pollution. Tears fell from her eyes. She truly felt bad for Mikey.

She sniffled as she heard Sanzu's bike approaching. She quickly left the alleyway—only to be dragged back in by a man with a strong grip on her wrist.

# CHAPTER TWENTY-THREE

"What the f—" She was cut off by a hand. *Baji.*

"Didn't you leave already?" he asked.

"I'm waiting for Sanzu to pick me up." She looked away so he wouldn't see her wet face.

He did.

"Sanzu, huh." He smirked. "Look after him good, okay?"

"Uhhh, sure thing."

"Why were you crying?" Baji noticed the tears. "Was it my story?"

She ignored his question. Part of her wanted to hug him. It must've been really hard to carry that much guilt.

"So I was right." He said. "It was really hard to tell that story, but if I won them over, then whatever works, will work." He sighed, eyebrows creasing.

She couldn't help it anymore. She walked closer to Baji and wrapped her arms around his waist.

"Oi! What are you—" He started, then realized.

She squeezed him tighter, rubbing his back.

"No one should go through that," she started. "It's so painful. I know how it feels. So if you need anyone, you can tell me anytime."

She was immediately reminded of her dark past but blocked it out.

A small silence.

She felt a drop of liquid on the top of her head. He was crying. He squeezed her back tightly. She continued to pat his back until she heard Sanzu calling her name.

"Thanks, Akari." He released her from the hug, wiping away his tears. "Take this."

He shoved a note into her hand and ran further into the alleyway until darkness swallowed him.

She walked out and saw Sanzu leaning against his bike, furiously looking around. He spotted her and sighed heavily in relief.

"Let's go home," she said, immediately jumping onto his bike, saying nothing more.

Sanzu didn't say anything either, noticing her slightly red eyes.

He trailed in behind her as she entered her apartment. She sank into the couch and leaned her head back, staring at the plain ceiling. She replayed everything that had happened after school—her head bursting with new information.

"Sanzu," she said. He came out of the bedroom, changed into warmer clothes.

"Yea?"

"I'm going to tell you everything, so listen very carefully." She patted the seat next to her. He shuffled over and sat down. She got up, rolled over onto Sanzu's lap, and sat on him, wrapping her arms around his shoulders, leaning her head into his neck.

Sanzu was shocked but only returned her hug.

It took a while, but she told him everything. Sanzu didn't say a word, listening and absorbing, rubbing her back for support.

"And where's this note Baji gave you?"

She reached into her pocket and pulled it out.

- Be careful around Valhalla. Hanma said something about you being part of the plan. Talk to Chifuyu if

you need anything. I might contact you again.*

- Take care,*

- — Baji*

"Well, he seems nice," she said, earning a small glance from a jealous Sanzu.

She laughed, noticing his face. She poked his squishy cheeks. "Don't worry, I won't ever leave you." She pecked his forehead.

"Mhm," Sanzu replied. "Moreover, we need to get Mikey on this. Should we call him over tonight?"

"Yea, I think we should do a small Division Captain meeting here," she suggested. "But we'll keep Baji's note a secret."

Sanzu nodded.

"I'm going to ask them to bring Take-chan too. I told him earlier that we were gonna have a study session. Hope he got the message behind it, though..." she said.

She got off Sanzu's lap, rolled onto the vacant spot on the couch, and took out her phone, dialing Mikey.

"Who's this?" Mikey picked up.

"Mikey, it's Akari here."

"Ohhh, Akari-chi—" She cut him off.

"Gather all the Division Captains at my place ASAP. I have news." She said. "Oh, and grab Take-chan for me too."

"Who's Take-chan?"

"Takemichi. Anyways, see you in a bit." She hung up.

After a couple of minutes, there was a knock at the door.

"Sanzu, can you get that?" She yelled as she changed out of her school uniform. She was in the middle of undressing when someone swung open the bedroom door.

"Akari-chin, everyone is—" Mikey stopped functioning, staring at her half-naked body.

"Okay, are you done staring?" She said.

Mikey turned bright red and closed the door slowly behind him. She sighed, quickly got changed, and left the bedroom.

"Thanks for coming, everyone," she started. "As you heard, I was invited to the Valhalla hideout as a witness. They have declared war on us on the 31st of October, otherwise known as 'Bloody Halloween.'"

"Damn, that was really quick of them," Mitsuya stated. Everyone nodded.

She continued to tell the story of Baji leaving the gang but left out the death of Mikey's brother and Baji's note—she decided to tell Mikey privately after everyone left.

There were so many people in her house—it was confusing what was going on after she told them what happened.

After a couple hours, they started leaving one by one. Mitsuya, being the nice boy he is, helped her clean up.

"Thanks, Mitsuya, but Sanzu and I can do it," she said, tilting her head at Sanzu.

"Well, I did most of it, so I guess I can leave the rest to you," he said. "Have a goodnight, Akari, Sanzu."

Mitsuya left, leaving just her, Sanzu, Draken, and Mikey.

"Draken, we should go too. It's already late." Mikey said. He walked to the door and was about to leave.

"Mikey, wait." She grabbed his wrist. "I have something important to tell you."

A long pause lingered before he spoke.

"He told you, didn't he?" Mikey said quietly, looking at the floor.

She nodded. "Yea..." she said quietly. "I don't know what it feels like, but I can say that Baji still holds the guilt from then to this day."

"WHAT DO YOU KNO—" Mikey finally looked up at her. He froze. He looked deep into her eyes and saw the same guilt that Baji had. The same look.

"Like I said, I don't know the pain you feel, but I know the guilt." She started to tear up. She took a small step toward Mikey, and he took one back. She took another two steps forward, trapping Mikey against the door. She hugged him tightly and whispered.

"I'm so sorry." Tears fell again.

Mikey also teared up. She heard him sniffling as he reciprocated her hug. They stayed like that for a while before parting.

"I also got a note from Baji." She handed it to him. He read it briefly.

"What does this note mean? About you being part of Hanma's plan?" Mikey asked.

"I don't know, but Hanma gave me a note on the day I woke up at the hospital too, with a similar message. That I'm a vital part of their plan." She pondered what it could mean.

"Anyways, it's getting late, so you two should head home," she said to Draken and Mikey.

They nodded and left.

"See you soon," the two said.

"Sweetheart, as much as I love you..." Sanzu started. He placed a knife at her neck. "What are you hiding?"

# CHAPTER TWENTY-FOUR

She was shocked. She never thought Sanzu would read into her actions so quickly.

"Did I give too many hints away, Babe?" She turned her head.

"Don't move." He said quickly. "You're going to listen to me."

"Okay, fine," she said, giving up.

"Move over to the couch and sit. You're gonna answer all my questions. I don't care if we miss school tomorrow—you're gonna answer them all. Now walk."

He pushed her back lightly toward the couch, removing the knife from her neck.

"Babe, you know we can't miss school. Our attendance is already so low..."

Sanzu sighed in defeat. "Okay, fine."

"So ask away," she said. "What do you wanna know?"

"You said you understood the guilt that Baji felt. What did you mean by that?"

She sighed heavily and leaned back against the couch.

"It has to do with my past. It's a long story."

- *AKARI'S PAST — TW**

It all started when her mother married her father and decided they wanted a child. Her.

She was born with her father's features—they were awfully similar. She had her mother's personality. Dark, cold, and mysterious, but kind and warm whenever she needed to be. The mother she always knew was warm, caring, and kind—until that day when everything changed.

It turned out both of her parents were involved in gangs. Two separate gangs that were always at each other's throats. Their marriage was a mere truce between the two gangs.

Her father had known the whole time, while her mother truly believed the marriage was formed out of love. Once her mother found out, she was never the same again.

Akari was only five when the incident happened. Ceramic plates dropped, breaking against the hard floor. Her mother holding a knife, ripping the corners of her lips so she'd look less like the father she despised.

She was fourteen, living alone with her father. He'd been drinking all night due to whatever stress he was under. It was one of those nights where he'd mistake her for her mother and lash out.

She was lucky she'd been sent to a martial arts school as a child, so the damage done by her dad was minimal. Yet he always overpowered her and threatened her with whatever weapons he had.

It was on that night that her father had a drunken argument with her, believing she was her mother.

"Go back to the gang, darling, and this war between us will never cease to end!" Her father yelled.

"What are you talking about?" She yelled back, completely unaware.

"Don't act like you don't know, you bitch!" He yelled. "YOUR gang forced me to sign the contract. They blackmailed me, threatening me with my sister and her family. I had no choice. You can't tell me you didn't know about the contract when it was your gang who brought it up. And you blame me?! Your poor daughter has a permanent scar on her face because you thought she looked too much like me. You didn't have to go so far! That's your daughter! You probably never even fucking loved her!"

He was out of breath.

"Fuck you," he said, going back to downing his alcohol.

She stood in the lounge room, shocked. Her jaw hit the floor. She was beyond controllable rage. Her nails dug into her palms, trying to keep her anger in.

- Was I made out of love?*

- What was my point of existence?*

- Do my parents even love me?*

- Is this why I haven't seen my mum in years?*

- Where is she now?*

Thoughts poured out of her head. She went crazy.

- What's the point of living if you were made because of a contract?*

She spent the next month gaining information from her father, trying to pry out her mother's current location. She finally found her. In another prefecture. Gifu.

She didn't tell her dad anything about her plans. She bought a train ticket from Yokohama to Gifu.

She rode the train for about two hours and finally got out, breathing the chill, non-polluted air. She took a taxi to a place two streets from her mother's home address.

She hadn't seen her in ten years, so she wondered if her mother would recognize her. She walked for a bit and finally got to her place. A large apartment complex with many small apartments.

She walked up the flights of stairs and stood in front of the door.

- 30A.*

She rang the doorbell and stood against the wall behind her, staring at the door. Faint footsteps on the other side.

"Yes?" Her mother stopped talking. She started to tear up. "Akari, is that you...?"

Akari saw nothing but red. She walked toward her mother's open arms and went in for a hug.

Except her father's words continued to play out in her head. It made her go crazy. She was losing herself.

By the time she regained her calm state of mind, she was inside her mother's apartment.

Warm liquid was dripping down the knife she was holding. Blood.

She stared at her hands, still holding the knife. Her mother was still alive, whispering words.

"I think I'm aware as to why you did this, Akari. Just know that I always loved you, even if my marriage with your father was forced. I regret scarring your beautiful face, but that can be your memory of me, since there's nothing else... I'm so sorry, honey. I wish I could've seen you every day, but your father was too much to deal with after finding out. I'll love you forever."

She grabbed Akari's cheeks, staining them red with her own blood. Akari grabbed her mother's hand on her cheek, her own tears falling, unable to accept what she'd just done.

Her mother's hand went cold after a few minutes.

Akari screamed—absolute pain, her heart shattering into two hundred million pieces.

- I just killed my mother.*

- I just killed my mother.*

Reality and guilt set in. She was a murderer. It was the gangs' fault. But she knew she couldn't do anything, so she locked everything inside. She locked all her emotions for a long period of time.

From that point on, every time she looked in the mirror or someone pointed out her scar, she died a little inside. A permanent reminder of how she killed her mum.

A neighbor, hearing her scream, knocked on the front door.

"Kurokawa-san? Are you okay?"

She walked to the front door, dropping the knife on the way, blood still staining her hands. She opened the door, and the neighbor dropped to the floor seeing the blood.

"Call the police. Don't even bother with the ambulance. Hurry up, or I'll kill you too."

The neighbor ran back to her room to do as she said.

She came back, watching over Akari like a hawk. "Why?" she asked. "She was such a nice person! How could you do that to her?!"

Akari ignored her emotions and answered coldly. "I'm her daughter." Was all she said.

Sirens in the distance.

"When they get here, tell them I've given up and will surrender. Just tell them to knock on the door."

She walked back into her mother's apartment and sat on the couch. Preparing herself emotionally, she switched off all emotions. She felt cold.

- Perfect.*

She stared at her dead mother and closed her eyelids. A light knock on the door.

"Police, open up!"

She walked to the door and opened it, hands up.

"Let's go," she said coldly, walking out. The officer placed handcuffs around her wrists and led her away.

# CHAPTER TWENTY-FIVE

After being held at the Gifu police station for a long time, she was finally transported to Yokohama Reform School, where she met Izana and Kakucho.

"What are you in for?" Izana asked after the first day.

"Murder." She said quickly. "Two years."

"Damn, that's not something you see every day." Izana said.

Kakucho just stared at her weirdly.

From that day on, she was able to warm up to Izana and Kakucho. They were the ones who made her unlock her emotions. They made her feel normal—not normal for murdering your mum, but you get the point.

Tenjiku was created with Izana as leader after all members were released. She moved out of her father's apartment without telling him. He didn't bother looking for her. As expected.

Tenjiku—especially Izana and Kakucho—was her family.

Until her dad came across her one day. The rumors of Tenjiku had spread quickly, to his own gang.

He found her apartment, knocked down the door, and burst in. He grabbed her by the collar, lifted her into the air. He slapped her hard once and dropped her on the floor.

She just stared at him, turning off her emotions.

"You're moving to Tokyo. I've finally found a school that would accept you. So pack up your things and leave in two weeks. Don't make me come after you."

She was speechless. Two years after the murder of her mum, he didn't give a shit about her until now.

- Who the fuck does he think he is?*

She was fuming. She wanted to talk back, but he said something that made her spine tingle.

"I know your gang. Don't make me massacre them."

He threatened her again. It was the same every time, and she had no choice but to listen.

So she packed her things and left Yokohama for Tokyo.

- *END FLASHBACK**

"And that's the whole story," she said to Sanzu as morning light began to fill the room.

They'd stayed up the whole night. Sanzu was speechless.

She yawned. "Is that all you need, or have you got more questions?"

Sanzu just stared blankly. After a while, he shook his head.

"Don't worry, you'll be beside me forever, whether you like it or not." She told him. "I plan on killing my father sooner or later, though. Keep that a secret between us, will you—?" She winked.

"Anyways, let's head to school early so we can sleep."

"Sure," he said.

They got ready quickly and rode his motorbike to school, arriving at about 6:30 AM. School didn't start until 8:40, so they had a little over two hours to sleep.

She opened the classroom door and threw her bag onto her desk. Sanzu sat on his chair and leaned against the wall near the window. She walked up to him.

"Can I sleep here?" She pointed at him.

"That's my lap." He stated, visibly confused.

"I know what I said."

He got the hint and welcomed her into his open arms. She sat on his lap and felt his arms wrap around her waist. She leaned her head on his shoulder, and they both drifted off.

She woke to the sound of the bell and shuffling feet. She'd indeed fallen asleep on Sanzu—he was still asleep. She peeked around the classroom. Their classmates were staring. She smiled at them, not wanting to cause a stir.

A girl in front of her whispered, "The teacher's going to be here soon. Don't get in trouble for being in a relationship."

"It's okay. He won't do that to us," she said. "Since he doesn't want to affiliate himself with gang shit. But thanks anyways." She nodded, smiling.

She turned her attention back to Sanzu, poking his squishy cheeks to wake him up.

"Oiiii, babeeee," she whispered into his ear. She felt him shiver. He buried his head further into her neck.

"Mmm, five more minutess," he whined.

"Teacher's gonna be here soon... get up." She got up off his lap and stretched.

Sanzu pulled her back down onto his lap.

"How about I make a deal with you, babe?" He opened one eye.

"If you let me go now and go through classes with me now, I'll skip last period with you on the rooftop. Deal?"

He pondered for a minute. "Fine..."

"Okay, good." She pecked his forehead, got off his lap, and sat at her desk—right next to him.

The teacher walked in the second she sat down. Exponential graphs. *Ew.*

She looked out the window, watching the blue sky, the white fluffy clouds bending and forming new shapes. Birds flew freely without a worry.

The bell rang for lunch. She grabbed her lunch and looked at Sanzu—already out of his seat, lunch in hand, waiting.

They made their way to the rooftop. She closed the door behind her and walked to the very edge, looking down at the pavement, watching students walk past. Sanzu wrapped his arms around her waist, hugging her from behind, resting his chin on her head.

"Babe, are you okay?"

"Why do you ask?"

"No reason. You're just a bit more clingy today." She said. "Did my past have that much of an effect on you?"

A long silence before he spoke.

"You know how you said you were going to kill your dad sooner or later?" She nodded. "Aren't you going to miss your family? Aren't they your only family?"

She pondered before replying.

"I can always be part of a family, even if we're not blood-related." She said. "Just like how I've got Izana and Kakucho in Yokohama, and you and the gang here."

She turned around to face Sanzu, looked up at him, and tilted his chin down.

"You're already family to me." She kissed his lips. She felt him smirk into the kiss.

They parted after a couple minutes.

"You know what?" he said. "I'll come with you."

"For what?" she asked, genuinely confused.

"The murder of your father."
