# CHAPTER TWENTY-SIX

"What?!" She said, shocked.

"You heard me, sweetheart~. I'll come with you." He smiled.

"Damn, okay. Sure." She sat down.

"Just let me know when you're planning it, and I'll help you plan it out. We need to lure him out somewhere abandoned too."

"Well, aren't you experienced?" She chuckled briefly, interrupted by the bell for last period.

Sanzu walked away and leaned against the wall next to the rooftop door. She saw him patting his lap. Getting the message, she walked over and sat on his lap. The cold wind sent shivers down her spine, but sitting next to him warmed her up.

They sat on the rooftop until the sun began to set. She just sat on his lap the whole time—not a word, just enjoying each other's company.

"Let's go home." Sanzu moved underneath her. "Ahhh~, my legs are so stiff." He groaned.

"Oops." She got off him, laughing at his trembling legs.

After a couple minutes, Sanzu was back to normal. They walked down the stairs, back to their classroom, grabbed their bags, and left.

They went to his place today—for the first time in like three days.

It was clean.

Not really a surprise since no one had visited in four days. She dumped her school bag on the floor, in a corner so no one would trip. She made her way into Sanzu's bedroom and opened the door. She jumped onto his bed and didn't move. It smelled just like him.

"What are you doing?" he asked.

"Sleeping." She breathed in the smell of him.

"Well, obviously not." He made his way over and lay down.

She sat up, leaning against the wall. Sanzu moved his head onto her lap. She ran her fingers through his blonde hair, over and over. It wasn't long before his breathing regulated, eyes closed. She continued to run her fingers through his hair and began parting it into two, giving him a very sideways, wonky French braid.

After she finished, she'd dozed off with Sanzu sleeping on her lap.

A couple days passed. She'd gotten yelled at by Sanzu the following morning because when he untied his hair, it was all wavy. She was rolling on the floor, clutching her stomach from laughter. It wasn't long before he began to laugh along. He'd gone to school with wavy hair. Funniest day she'd had in ages.

However, today was the night before Bloody Halloween. Technically, Bloody Halloween Eve. School had just finished, and she was walking home, holding hands with Sanzu.

"Oh shit, I forgot!" She exclaimed. "I need to go to the convenience store!"

"Want me to come with you?" Sanzu asked. "It's getting late too."

"Nahh, I'll be alright." She said. "Go home first, make dinner, and wait for me. I won't take long." She winked.

"Okay, see you in a bit. Don't forget we have a meeting tonight." He leaned down and kissed her forehead.

She giggled and walked in the opposite direction.

She walked into her regular convenience store and browsed for food for tomorrow and the day after. The store only had snacks and quick, unhealthy meals—she was sick of them. She decided to take a longer walk to the supermarket.

She walked in, carrying a small shopping basket, browsing each aisle. She bought the basics—bread, milk, pasta, eggs, some fruits and vegetables. Happy with her choices, she paid and carried the shopping home.

She felt a presence. Someone was following her.

She walked back to the convenience store, hoping there would be people. There were. She walked up to the cashier, making sure no one was in hearing range.

"Can you show me the security footage from two minutes ago? I think someone is following me..."

The cashier nodded and asked her to follow her into the back room. She showed the footage from when Akari entered.

"Rewind a little," Akari said. "Pause, right there."

A hooded man. Taller than her. She couldn't tell who it was.

- Damn it.*

"Thank you so much," she said to the cashier.

"No problem. Get home quickly and stay safe, love." She said, going back to work.

Akari nodded and left the store, standing out of the way of the automatic doors. She knew the hooded man was waiting for her to look away. She thought of a quick plan and headed back inside.

"Oh, you're back," the cashier said.

"Yea, umm, can you do me a favor?"

"Sure thing. What can I do for you?"

She walked out of the store again, sighing. She carried her groceries and started walking home. With all three bags in one hand, she took out her phone and dialed Sanzu.

It was at this point she knew she was done for. The hooded man rushed behind her and placed a chloroform-filled handkerchief over her nose. Of course she struggled, trying not to breathe it in, but she had no choice.

"What's up, sweetheart?" She heard Sanzu say on the other end.

The hooded man chuckled, ending the call.

She took a small breath in—more than enough to force her to sleep.

# CHAPTER TWENTY-SEVEN

"Oh, you're back," I said, seeing the girl walk back into the store. She wore a black mask over her face, hair cut neat but ragged, piercings decorating both ears.

"Yea, umm, can you do me a favor?"

"Sure thing. What can I do for you?"

She looked around again before leaning over the counter, pretending to buy more items.

# CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT

She went silent. Out of everything, she never expected something like this.

"Who's gonna be the lucky fifty~?" Hanma yelled to the crowd.

She snickered to herself. Her father had put her through intensive martial arts training as a child, so fifty teenagers weren't much of a big deal. It was the one thing she was grateful to her father for. She just had to conserve her energy. She knew they were gonna play dirty, so she braced herself for the worst.

She looked at Hanma. "Do you have a spare hair tie?"

He looked at her like she was stupid.

"Can't believe you actually expect me to have one." He burst into loud laughter, the rest of Valhalla following.

"Here!" someone in the crowd yelled. He walked forward and extended his hand, hair tie in hand.

She reached out to take it. He grabbed her wrist and pulled her toward him. She realized he'd turned his back to her. He was going to flip her over his back and slam her onto the floor.

She let him do so, but as he flipped her, she landed on her feet. His hand was about to let go, but she grabbed on. She turned her back against him and used his momentum to flip him over, slamming his back onto the floor. She took the hair tie from the same hand she'd grabbed.

She began to tie her hair into a low ponytail, looking around. Hanma wolf-whistled in the corner of her eye. She gave him a small smile, nodding.

"Alright, boys, go have your go at her!" He yelled at the top of his lungs.

There were five groups of ten that rushed at her, one at a time. Lucky that all fifty didn't rush at once.

The first ten were all the same—randomly throwing punches and kicks. She easily evaded all their attacks.

- Mikey would beat these ten in minutes,* she thought. *I'm going to do better.*

She looked at her surroundings and grabbed a short but sturdy rope. She rushed at the horde, successfully evading their attacks for the second time. She used the rope and tied it swiftly around one man's throat, tightening it. He desperately tried to get his fingers between the rope and his neck. Holding the rope, she unleashed a high axel kick to the back of another man who rushed at her, trying to free his friend. She knocked him out cold. She saw the whites of the first man's eyes before he slumped onto the floor. Unconscious.

- Two down, forty-eight to go.*

She jumped over the two unconscious bodies and continued her attack on the eight remaining members.

She launched a right hook at one man's jaw and a left high kick into another's temple. The man held his jaw and charged again. She punched him straight in the face. A small crunch, then he collapsed with a disfigured nose.

- Six more in the group of ten.*

She ran back, trying to catch her breath and get some space. She drew a line in front of her with the blood of the guy with the broken nose.

- The line of her defense.*

Guy Five breached the line. She ran straight up and launched a high kick to his temple, knocking him out in one hit.

Guys Six and Seven charged together. Seven tried to hold her back, pinning her arms behind her back.

"Hurry, knock her out!" Seven yelled at Six.

Six tried to punch her in the gut. She used all her might to lift her body upward, climbing onto Seven's shoulders. Six ended up hitting Seven's stomach. He fell to the floor in pain as she skillfully jumped off Seven's shoulders and launched a flying twisting kick to Six's head.

- He's out.*

She grabbed Seven's ankles and swung him around and around, gaining enough momentum, and released him into the last two guys of Group One.

- Ten down, forty to go.*

She took a few deep breaths, trying to get her heart rate under control. She didn't want to accidentally kill someone.

She put her hand up, wanting to ask Hanma a question.

"Yes, darling~?" He asked.

She clicked her tongue, annoyed at the name-calling, but let it slide.

"What are you gonna do if I accidentally kill a person? Or people?"

"Hmmm..." He pondered for a couple minutes, letting her gain her normal resting heart rate. He jumped down from his podium and whispered into her ear so he didn't freak out the other forty members.

"Because I took a liking to you, I'll dispose of the bodies myself. So do whatever you want, darling~?" He lifted her chin. "Is that a good enough response?"

"Oh, more than I can ask for~?" She grabbed his hand from her chin. "I won't disappoint~"

"Make it entertaining, will you?" Hanma waltzed back to his throne.

She turned her attention back to the forty remaining members.

"Come at me, you fucking bitches!!"

# CHAPTER TWENTY-NINE

- *TW: DEATH**

The roar of the Valhalla gang echoed through the hideout, shaking the walls and broken glass panels.

She took a deep breath, knowing from this point on things were going to get tough. Twenty men charged. She sighed, visibly annoyed.

She closed her eyes and let the noise drown itself out. Then flashed them open.

- Silence.*

- Men moving in slow motion.*

- She was in the zone.*

Men were "running" toward her from all directions. She chose a smaller guy and grabbed his arms, pinning them behind his back. She whacked the back of his neck, knocking him unconscious. She went around the circle, slowly increasing her strength with each knockout. After about fifteen men had collapsed with the same method, a loud shock broke her concentration.

Another ten joined in, taking her by surprise. One whacked her over the head with a wooden bat. Blood ran down her forehead, oozing onto her face, dripping onto the floor.

- Great.*

She still had twenty-five men to knock out.

The shock reverberated inside her head. Her eyes glued to the floor, watching the blood drip and puddle. Her vision blurred. Her heart rate went through the roof.

- She lost herself.*

- *HANMA POV**

He watched from the podium as Akari got hit on the back of the head with a wooden baseball bat. She stood still. Didn't move. About fifteen men charged at her, but she didn't flinch. He wouldn't say he was worried, but the men were inching closer by the second, and she still didn't move. He was curious how she was going to get out of this one.

Just as a guy was about to land a punch square on her nose, she looked up and caught it. She jumped into the air, pulling the hand down toward the floor. She landed on top of the guy and kicked his head into the ground. He began to laugh, noticing another man pulling out a knife.

- She's gonna massacre everyone now.* He thought, sighing deeply. *I'll have a lot of work to do now...*

He watched, amused, as the man charged with the knife. His fellow gang members covered for him. Her facial reaction didn't change—she was completely in control of her body and the situation.

She punched Guy One in the guts, sending him flying. She caught Guy Two by the collar, punching his face a couple times until an audible crack resonated. She threw him to the side like a ragdoll. She caught Guy Three's punch and didn't hesitate to punch at his elbow, breaking his arm, bending it in the other direction. Guy Three's pained yell echoed through the arcade.

Guy Four, with the knife, hesitated after seeing his mates get beat up—but that was his downfall. Hanma snickered, knowing what was going to happen. Akari waited for him to get close, swatted his hand to the side, the knife skidding onto the floor. She raised her leg and swung it around onto his temple. She didn't stop.

He watched as she desperately ran toward the knife, arming herself. The remaining eleven men glanced at him in sheer desperation and fear.

"The fuck are you looking at?" He spat. "Either you get injured by her hands, or you die by mine." He shrugged, carefully lacing the lie into his words, giving the men false hope.

Akari changed her grip on the knife to a reverse grip and charged at the remaining men.

- Total: twenty-one to go.*

He glanced at the last ten men sitting in the corner, waiting for their turn. He honestly didn't know what made them think groups of ten were enough. He waved his hand, shooing them into the fight. They complied.

He turned his attention back to Akari. Honestly, he was a bit shocked. In the small span of two minutes he'd looked away to usher the other boys on, she'd slit the throats of five men. They lay limp on the floor, blood gushing. Splotches of blood on her face and clothing.

He stared in shock.

- We need someone of her strength in Valhalla,* he thought, but it was Kisaki's decision in the end. He

did question Kisaki's decision to kidnap her, though.

- Was kidnapping her really the best option? We've lost a sixth of our men to one teenage girl...*

She continued her rampage, murdering or severely injuring the others. With only two men left, she dropped the knife and looked around, turning her head from side to side.

"What happened, darling~?" He asked, curious about the change in momentum.

"Did I do all this?" she asked.

He didn't know what to say. All this time she was fighting, was she not aware?

- What a monster.*

"Yes, that was all you." He said. "You still have two left."

He watched her face change. She cackled, running her fingers through her loosely tied hair. She finally calmed down.

"I see," she said. "I've lost it again." She mumbled incoherent words before starting to fight again.

- *AKARI POV**

The blankness in her head slowly began to fade as she regained a clear state of mind. She loosened the grip on whatever she was holding. She looked around, seeing a large pile of bodies on the floor, puddles of blood. She wiped her forehead, wiping away sweat and blood.

"What happened, darling~?" Hanma asked, still on his throne, admiring the fight.

"Did I do all this?" She wondered if she'd really lost herself again.

Hanma paused, looking around at the ground she was on.

"Yes, that was all you." He stated. "You still have two left."

She couldn't take it anymore. She laughed, finding the death of these men amusing. She ran her fingers through her hair, getting loose strands away from her eyes. She calmed herself after her head hurt from laughing too hard.

She mumbled to herself. "I wanna sleep... Sanzu, where are youuuu..."

She focused on the last two men standing. She wasn't shocked to see fear in their eyes—she'd literally just killed ten or more people. She watched their eyes trail to the knife on the floor.

"You looking at this?" She pointed to the knife. She picked it up and held it over her face, running the blade over her cheek softly. Small amounts of blood oozed out from the fresh wound. She glanced at the knife, seeing her reflection, blood staining her face, hiding in the grooves of her scar.

"I'll be nice." She brought the knife down to her side. "I won't use it at all. I'm tired."

She threw the knife at one of the corpses. It stuck into the back of the body.

She watched the last two men, then charged. They charged at her, fear in their eyes, preparing for a gruesome death. She launched a high kick, dropping it onto the back of one man's head. His body slammed onto the floor. Using that same leg, she swung sideways, the heel colliding with the temple of the second guy. He flew into the wall and slumped down.

- Total: fifty down, zero to go.*

She looked at Hanma.

"Can I leave now?"

She rolled her eyes and scrolled through her phone, looking for Sanzu's number as she walked out of Valhalla's hideout.

She checked the time.

- 2:44 AM.*

She sighed, tired after fighting fifty men. She remembered being at the store at 7:30 PM, probably kidnapped fifteen minutes later. The fighting probably took about two or more hours. Everything added up.

She called Sanzu, leaning against the building wall for support.

# CHAPTER THIRTY

"Hey, babe." She said, sleepily. "Can you pick me up outside the game center again? Same place as last time..."

She just sat there, waiting for Sanzu.

After a couple seconds, he arrived.

"Akari!" He hugged her. "Geez, you worried me."

She hugged him back, glad to feel safe again. She nuzzled her head into his chest as his hand crept up to support her head. That was when he noticed the bleeding from the back of her head.

"Akari, I'll take you home so you can fall asleep." He said, in a soothing voice.

She followed him to his bike and wrapped her arms around his waist as she fell asleep.

- *SANZU POV**

He realized she'd fallen asleep after starting up the motorbike. He took off his jacket and tied it around her waist, then his, so she wouldn't fall off. He drove a bit slower.

He arrived at the hospital and carried her in his arms to the ER. It was probably 3 AM by now, so the hospital was quiet. A nurse arrived, saw Akari's state, and just nodded, asking him to follow.

He followed the nurse into a room with a bed. He placed Akari down carefully.

"The doctor will be here soon." The nurse said, leaving.

He watched Akari's sleeping figure, her chest rising and falling so slowly. He wiped the baby hairs off her face.

He looked around and saw a small hand towel, which he wet to wipe off the dried blood on her cheek and face.

- I don't think this is all hers,* he thought. *She wouldn't have lost this much blood from a mere head

injury.*

Akari stirred a little, groaning, but calmed down.

The door slid open, revealing the doctor.

"Oh, not you again." He stared dead into Sanzu's eyes. "You need to be more careful. I've seen you two three times in two months. What's wrong with her this time?" He sighed deeply.

"She got hit in the back of her head, and she's bleeding."

The doctor nodded and began to examine Akari. Within a few minutes, he left, giving Sanzu a small lecture on how to look after her better.

After the doctor left, he carried Akari back to the motorbike and drove them home. Bloody Halloween wasn't until noon, so they both had time to catch up on missed sleep.

After arriving at her apartment, he carried her into her bedroom and lowered her onto the bed. He covered her with the blankets and left the room. He quickly texted Mikey.

- *SANZU TO MIKEY:**

- I found Akari. Took her to the hospital. She got hit in the back of the head with something, but other

than that, she's fine.*

After a couple minutes, Mikey responded.

- *MIKEY TO SANZU:**

- Okay, that's good. I don't like to rush the healing process, but Bloody Halloween is at noon, so make

sure to be there. Up to you if you decide to bring Akari.*

He turned off his phone and made himself comfortable on the couch, thinking it'd be better for Akari to have some space tonight—well, this morning.

He stared at the ceiling for a while, and it wasn't long before he drifted off too.

He woke to a loud knock on the door. He groaned, patting his unrolling long hair out of his eyes, and walked to unlock the front door.

He heard the sound of a motorbike leave just outside as he opened the door. Of course, there was nobody. He looked around and noticed a bundle of flowers on the floor. A letter addressed to Akari stuck to the bundle.

- To Kurokawa Akari.*

That was all that was written on the envelope.

- Strange.*

He brought the flowers and letter inside and placed them carefully on the dining table. He checked on Akari—she was sweating profusely on her bed. He ran to get a wet towel and placed it over her forehead. She cooled down and opened her eyes.

"Oh, Sanzu," she said, breathing out a sigh of relief. "I just had a bad dream. Don't worry too much."

He kneeled on the floor and rested his head on her stomach. She began to run her fingers through his hair as she talked.

"I know what I did was questionable last night. I'm sorry." She started. "But I had no choice. It was either that or get innocent people involved, like that lady from the convenience store."

He nodded, not wanting to interrupt.

"They knocked me out with chloroform and brought me to the Valhalla hideout. Hanma gave me a deal: either defeat fifty of their men or do him a favor. I was a little worried what the favor would be, so I fought to the best of my ability..." She quieted down. "I lost my cool and ended up killing about ten people, though..."

He placed his hand on hers, still raking through his hair. He intertwined his fingers with hers and looked into her eyes.

"That's okay. You did what you needed to do. If anything, I'm proud of you—and glad that you made it back to me." He kissed her bruised knuckles and smiled. "There's a letter and flowers for you on the dining table. They came this morning."

She slowly sat up, and he got off her stomach. He helped her out of bed and walked a few steps behind her out of the room. They both sat on the couch as she opened the letter.

She stared at it and dropped the flowers.

She was shocked at the contents.

- Baji really was aiming for Kisaki—just as Akari said!*

Kisaki's right-hand man grabbed the back of Baji's jacket and threw him. He tumbled down the tower of cars to the bottom.

"Swat him dead, like the buzzing fly he is," Kisaki said.

"Let's see you try, Kisaki," Baji said.

Chifuyu ran in front of Baji and stretched out his arms.

"What the fuck are you doing, Chifuyu? Outta my way." Baji said calmly.

"Don't do this, Baji-san. If you're gonna go against Touman, you're going against Mikey. If you wanna save Touman from Kisaki, now isn't—"

Baji cut him off, swinging the rod into his head.

"I'm here to protect you! If you really wanna get past me, then I won't hold back." Chifuyu said.

"Then do it. You got ten seconds."

"Huh?"

"If you don't kill me, you won't be able to stop me."

Baji continued to count down, but Takemichi couldn't take it anymore. He rushed toward Baji and grabbed his waist.

- I'm gonna have to save you!*

"Let's stop Baji-kun together! Chifuyu!!"

"I can't, Takemitchy... I can't hit Baji-san." Chifuyu said, tears streaming down his face.

Baji, trying to escape, whacked the back of Takemichi's head with his elbow. He was slowly losing consciousness, but he remembered Mikey and Akari's unconscious state, and Hina's death.

- I'm not going to lose anyone anymore.*

- Wait.*

- Hold on...*

- Kisaki didn't kill Baji... It was Kazutora!*

He looked back to Mikey and didn't see Kazutora's passed-out body. Akari was also no longer there.

"Baji! Behind you!"

Akari appeared from above Baji, jumping down to their level, chasing after Kazutora. Takemichi realized Kazutora was bad news and attempted to push him away from Baji.

# CHAPTER THIRTY-THREE

Takemichi knocked Kazutora out of the way as he fell with him.

"Are you okay?" He asked Baji.

"Yea, just a scratch. Thanks for the save." Baji turned to Akari, who was panting, out of breath. She fell to her knees, kneeling next to Baji. He patted her head softly. She didn't move—just sat there, eyes wide, watching everything unfold.

He heard Chifuyu in the background, going off at Kazutora for trying to kill Baji.

"I'm glad you're alive," Takemichi said.

"What the hell is your problem? I'm taking Kisaki down, so just you watch me, Takemichi!" Baji said.

- What the hell? What's going on here? It's so messed up. I have no idea what I'm supposed to do!!*

Baji just whacked his head, stared down at him, and walked away.

"Why are you in such a hurry, Baji-san?" Chifuyu mumbled.

- Baji might be strong, but 50-to-1 is tough.*

"He'll be fine. I know it," Akari whispered behind him.

He made his way up the tower of cars, bashing members of Kisaki's gang. In no time, he was holding the metal rod at Kisaki's throat.

"Checkmate, Kisaki." Baji growled.

"Go ahead and kill me if you can!" Kisaki stated.

A moment of silence hung in the air—before Baji coughed up blood.

Chifuyu and Takemichi ran toward him.

Akari removed her Touman jacket and tied it around Baji's waist, trying to put pressure on the wound.

"Kazutora doesn't fuck around after all! I see now! He lured Baji into Valhalla so he could kill him when he least expected it!" Kisaki said.

"Right? Leader?" Kisaki continued.

"Oi, Chifuyu, hold the jacket still and apply a little pressure to the wound. Call an ambulance for me, okay?" Akari said.

Chifuyu nodded, listening, taking out his phone. Akari got to her feet and walked slowly over to Mikey.

"I wanted to kill you for so long. As soon as you got out of juvie, I was gonna kill you. But the one who kept telling me not to was Baji. He said, 'Kazutora just wanted to make you happy. That's why he can't accept it. Even though he killed your brother, to make himself believe that he wasn't the bad guy, he had no choice but to decide that you were his enemy.' Ken-chin. This fight is over." Mikey said, climbing down the tower.

Akari stopped walking toward Mikey and watched as he walked to the ground. Mikey turned around quickly and gave her a look. She seemed to get the message and followed him down.

"Huh? The fight's over? You tryin' to fuck with me, Mikey?" Hanma exclaimed.

Mikey stood in front of Hanma, getting stared down. Akari finally caught up and just looked dead at Hanma.

"Mikey said it was over." She said sharply.

"Don't fuck with me, darl—"

Akari cut Hanma off, lifting her leg up and around his head in a blink. She swung her leg all the way through until Hanma's head met the ground heavily. His mouth frothed a little. She regained her balance, placing her leg down softly.

"Finally." She leaned down to Hanma's level and grabbed his hair. "I've been dying to do this to you after everything yesterday. I'm grateful for you getting rid of the—" she coughed. "But this is karma, bitch!"

She let go, and Hanma's head landed on the floor a second time.

Commotion from the Valhalla members.

"Hanma's down in one kick?"

"Oh, fuck! It's the chick from last night!"

- What the hell happened last night to make the Valhalla members so afraid of Akari?!*

"Run! The two of them alone are more than enough to kill us!" Valhalla exclaimed, scattering.

"People can betray anyone, so let's end this, Mikey. Will you die? Or will I?" Kazutora said, eyes wide.

Mikey ignored his questions, punching him in the face.

- Yeesh, scaryyy.*

"If all you can do is destroy the things I care about, then I'll destroy you." Mikey walked closer. He leaned to Kazutora's level. "Right here, right now."

Another punch. Then another. Then another.

"Mikey is gonna kill Kazutora at this rate..." Mitsuya stated. "Nobody can stop him now."

"I'm so fucking helpless!!" Takemichi yelled, watching in terror. The sound of Mikey punching Kazutora echoed.

Akari tried to hold Mikey back. "Mikey, that's enough!" She desperately grabbed both his arms. It didn't work.

"OI, MIKEY!" Baji yelled.

Mikey froze. Turned his head.

"Baji, you shouldn't move! You're gonna lose more blood!" Akari yelled, letting go of Mikey and staring at Baji.

"It's fine, Akari. Don't worry about me..." He staggered down the cars toward Mikey. "You got mad just for me? Thanks, man." He smiled at Mikey.

- What? Baji-kun is alive? But he's bleeding so much...*

"I'm not gonna die. This wound ain't gonna kill me." Baji continued stumbling toward Mikey.

- There's no way. It's gotta be a fatal injury!*

"So don't worry about it, Kazutora." Baji pulled out a different knife. "You won't be the one to kill me."

He stabbed himself in the guts.

- WHAT!*

"Baji! What the fuck!" Akari ran over as quickly as she could.

Takemichi made his way over, as Chifuyu held up Baji's body.

"Why'd you do that? What was the point of everything you've done for me?! I've only just got to know you..." Akari said, slowly quieting down.

"Why would you—what were you trying to achieve by stabbing yourself?" Takemichi said, tears blurring his vision.

"Takemichi... come closer." Baji said.

He leaned down.

"Kisaki is the real enemy."

- Fuck! I knew it. Naoto! We've got a reason!*

"I realized back when Pah stabbed Osanai. 'I'll get Pah out of prison. In exchange, make me the Third Division Captain.' I just happened to be there at the right place, right time. Kisaki is not our Third Division Captain!" Baji's eyes wavered, breathing heavier.

"No matter what happens, Pah's the only captain of the Third Division. Pah-chin. Mitsuya. Draken. Mikey. Kazutora. Touman's founding members are my treasure. I really wanted to fix this on my own... but I couldn't. I died on my own. Mikey has no reason to kill Kazutora..." Baji panted, tears forming.

"Takemichi. I'm leaving Mikey and Touman in your hands!"

- Please don't. You can't die!!*

"Akari. Come here." Baji said.

She shuffled closer, squeezing his hand tightly.

"Look after Mikey, will you? I know you have Sanzu, but Mikey's really going to crumble after this. I need you to be able to support him, in my stead. Can you do that for me?"

She nodded, tears falling onto Baji's face.

"Yea, I can do that..."

She leaned down and kissed his lips.

He laughed. "Damn, my first and last kiss..." She chuckled a little at that.

"Thanks for everything, Baji. I'll never forget what you've done for me." She stood, tears pouring out. She turned her back, walking over to Sanzu, not looking back, struggling to wipe her tears.

"Chifuyu..."

"Yea?"

"I'd kill for some peyoung yakisoba right now."

"I'll go buy you some." Chifuyu's jaw trembled.

"We'll split it, right?" Chifuyu sniffled.

Baji showed a large grin for the last time. "Thanks, Chifuyu..."

"...Baji-san...?"

Chifuyu's tears overflowed.

"BAJI-SANNNN!!" His yell echoed around the abandoned car lot.

# CHAPTER THIRTY-FOUR

"I'll kill you!" Mikey repeated, punching Kazutora over and over.

- Damn it! I couldn't do anything. I'm such an idiot! I'm the worst!*

"AAAAAAGH!" Takemichi yelled, rushing in front of Mikey, trying to stop him.

"Move, or I'll kill you too." Mikey stared into him.

"You have to stop this, Mikey!"

Mikey ignored his pleas and punched him. He got flung to the side but immediately stood up.

"Baji-kun didn't want this!"

Kicked to the side again.

"You don't talk about him."

"He's already dead, for god's sake!" *Why don't you get it! What do you think Baji died for in the first place? It was for you two, for Touman! Baji wasn't killed by Kazutora—he decided to kill himself. He didn't want Kazutora to feel responsible. He wanted you to forgive Kazutora! He did it 'cause he loved you guys... Why don't you get it??*

Mikey was silent, staring at the ground. Takemichi watched him kneel, picking up the charm he'd found back when Baji left Touman.

"Where'd you get this charm...?" Mikey stared at it.

"During that gathering at the shrine..."

Draken and Mitsuya seemed to recognize it too.

"Baji... had this the whole time...?" Mikey's eyes lit up for a brief second, then faded. "This is the charm from the day we formed our gang... I didn't create Touman. Baji did. 'If one of us gets hurt, we'll all protect them. I want a gang that's all for one, one for all.' That's what our gang was founded on."

Draken, Mitsuya, Kazutora, Chifuyu, and Akari were spilling tears.

"I'm so sorry, Baji." Mikey stared at his body.

- *AKARI POV**

This was heartbreaking. She hadn't known Baji long, but he'd left a large effect on her. She grabbed Sanzu's hand, squeezing tightly. He squeezed back, rubbing his thumb across her hand.

Sirens echoed.

"Let's go, guys. It's the cops."

The overseers started to leave, escaping from the sirens.

"I'm staying with Baji. You guys go on. This is my fault, so I'll take responsibility." Kazutora stated.

"Got it." Mikey walked away.

"Touman's leaving too!" Draken yelled.

"Right!"

"Mikey. I won't ask you to forgive me. I'll live my whole life with Shinichiro-kun and Baji's deaths on my shoulders." Kazutora bowed at Mikey's back.

With that, Bloody Halloween ended.

- *TWO WEEKS LATER**

"Chifuyu, let's go." Akari said.

They walked to the cemetery, carrying flowers and Baji's favorite—Peyoung Yakisoba. She sat in front of Baji's grave, next to Chifuyu.

"Hey, Baji!" She talked to his gravestone. "We came to visit."

"Baji-san. It's just like the first time we met. I brought you some peyoung yakisoba, just like I promised. Half's for you."

Chifuyu began to shake, crying. She patted his back.

"What am I supposed to do from now on?!" Chifuyu exclaimed, lowering his head to the ground.

After leaving the cemetery and parting ways with Chifuyu, she called Draken.

"Hey Draken, I have a question. Can we meet up?"

"Uhhh, sure. Let's meet in front of your school."

"Aight, bet."

She walked to the school gates to find Draken already there, leaning against his motorbike.

"So what was it you wanted to ask?"

"Can you take me to the tattoo parlor where you got that tattoo?"

"Sure. Why are you going, though?"

"Secret!" She gave him a small smile.

"Geez, okay. Here, get on." He tapped the seat behind him. She jumped on, grabbing his waist as he drove off.

"Okay, we're here." Draken stopped in front of a small corner store and pointed at the small staircase leading upward. "Cool, thanks."

She walked up the stairs. "Oh, can you send Sanzu a text of the location? I need him to pick me up in... two hours!"

"Just do that yourself, you lazy ass. Jesus."

"Hey! I heard that!" She laughed as she disappeared from his sights.

She opened the door at the top of the staircase and saw a man with blonde hair in a weird hairstyle, tattoos running over his face.

"Hello, sir!" She was clearly excited.

"Get out if you think this is a joke," the guy said.

"Pfft, nah. I'm serious about wanting a tattoo."

He looked at her like she was a strange creature.

"Do you have parental permission for a tattoo?"

"Nope."

"Then leave."

"Aww, please~" she whined. "I don't have parents anyway." She shrugged.

A small silence as he thought.

"...Fine. Just don't get me in trouble, will you?"

"Sure thing!"

"Lie down on the seat for me." She waltzed over and sat down. "So what design, and where?"

She showed him the design—a feather with small birds flying out from it.

"Can I have it here?" She lifted her shirt. His eyes widened at the scar on her abdomen.

"Jesus, what happened to you? You're full of scars."

"That one's a stab wound." She pointed at the one from 8/3. "Can you do the design over it and make it a little bigger so the scar doesn't show?"

"Okay." He stuck a stencil marking on her abdomen. "Is this good?"

She stood, holding her shirt up, looking in the mirror.

"Yea, that's good placement."

She lay back down.

"Aight, I'm going to start now." He dipped the needle into the black ink.

She felt it dig into her skin, following the stencil marks inch by inch. He wiped down the extra ink and continued the cycle.

About an hour later, the main door opened, revealing Sanzu staring at her body with furrowed eyebrows.

- Draken actually sent the message!*

"Hey, babe," she said.

The tattooist smiled to himself, continuing his work.

"What are you doing here? Are you crazy?" Sanzu asked.

"Nahh, I'm getting a tattoo."

"Yea, I can see that." He went quiet.

"There, you're done!" The tattooist stuck clear film onto her new tattoo. "Take the film off after three days and keep it clean. I hope I don't see you again soon, to be honest..."

She laughed, handing him the money. "Thank you for the tattoo, sir!" She grabbed Sanzu's hand and led him out.

"So a tattoo? For what?" Sanzu asked.

"To remember Baji, since he left such a large effect on me."

"Why there, though?"

"'Cause he was stabbed, and I was too. Similar enough spot. The irony..." She trailed off, remembering. She stopped, feeling a drop of rain on her head. She remembered the warmth of his hand patting her head.

"Watching over me right now, huh?" She looked up, going quiet.

"Come on, sweetheart, let's go home. This rain isn't gonna get lighter." He sighed. "You can stand in the rain when we get home, since you like it so much."

"Mmm." She let him drag her to his motorbike.

Once he stopped in front of the apartment complex, he parked under a covered area. He sat on the stairs, watching her get drenched by the heavy rain.

She lay down on the concrete, feeling the warmth of the rain soaking into her skin. She couldn't hold it in anymore. Her tears overflowed uncontrollably. She wiped at her eyes over and over, but they kept flowing.

Sanzu noticed and joined her in the rain, sitting next to her. She got up and sat in his lap, burying her head into his neck, crying her heart out. He patted and rubbed her back the whole time. They sat in the rain, feeding off each other's warmth.

"Baji must be crying too, huh," she said, looking up, calming down a little.

"Yeah... explains the rain." Sanzu said quietly. "Let's go inside. He wouldn't want us to cry anymore than this over his death."

He pulled her to her feet, holding her hand as he walked up the stairs and into her apartment. She opened the door to a dark house, the sound of rain hitting the window panels.

"Take a bath first. Don't want you getting sick." Sanzu pushed her into the bathroom.

She didn't let go of his hand.

"What is it, sweetheart?" He looked into her swollen eyes.

"Come with me..." she said, looking away.

Sanzu hesitated. "...Okay."

He left and came back with clothes and towels for both of them as she filled the tub with hot water. She undressed and entered the tub once it was filled. She watched the water level rise as Sanzu entered, sitting behind her. She leaned back into his chest, and he wrapped his arms around her waist, resting his head on her shoulder.

They enjoyed each other's company in that brief moment, in silence.

"Don't hesitate to let your emotions out again, okay, sweetheart? I'm always here for you." Sanzu said, muffled.

"Yea, I'll try my best."

They didn't move for a good few minutes, enjoying each other's warmth. After a bit, she moved away to grab the shampoo.

"Here, turn around."

Sanzu turned, letting her lather shampoo into his hair, massaging his scalp thoroughly, washing away any grime. She grabbed the shower-head and rinsed his hair. Beautifully long blonde hair.

"You turn around now. Your hair must be worse than mine since you lay on the concrete." He snickered.

"Wow, okay. Low blow." She rolled her eyes, turning her back to him.

She felt him squeeze shampoo onto her head, massaging it into her scalp, washing away all the grime, dirt, and worries. She melted at his careful touch. He made sure not to scrub too hard, remembering her head might not have healed yet.

He rinsed off the soap and looked at her.

"Man, your hair is really flat right now." He said, used to seeing her with a well-styled, voluminous wolf cut.

"Oh, shut up." She hit his chest lightly.

She got out, grabbing her towel, drying off. Sanzu said he wanted to stay in the tub a little longer. She changed and headed to the kitchen, making a quick dinner.

She laid out dinner as Sanzu walked out without a t-shirt, wet hair.

"Geez, you're such a child."

"What? I didn't do anything!"

"That's the problem! Go wear a t-shirt! You're gonna catch a cold. And get me a small towel—you need to dry your hair!"

Sanzu sighed in defeat. "Yes, ma'am." He disappeared with a small smile, coming back with a t-shirt and a smaller towel.

"Dinner's gonna go cold now." She scrubbed at his hair, trying to dry it as much as possible. Long hair took a while...

After a while, they finally ate dinner. Done and tired, they went to bed, Sanzu following.

"Goodnight, babe." She shuffled closer.

"Goodnight, sweetheart." Sanzu sent shivers down her spine as he breathed down it. His arm over her waist, hugging her close.

She felt really safe in his arms.

# CHAPTER THIRTY-FIVE

She woke to an empty bed. She tossed and turned for five minutes before slowly sitting up and opening the curtains. Sunlight poured in, reflecting off almost every surface, blinding her.

She got off the bed and walked out.

"Morning..." No response.

She walked to the kitchen table and saw a small note.

- About time you woke up. You missed school today, sweetheart.*

- — Your babe ♡*

"Why's he at school so early for..." She looked at the clock.

- 1:35 PM.*

"Oh, it's only 1:35..." She mumbled, rubbing her eyes. Then it hit her. "Wait, 1:35 PM?! Why didn't that asshole wake me up?"

She contemplated going to school but figured it was too late. She washed her face, ate a quick brunch, then rolled around on the floor, staring at the ceiling.

- We need more food. Big shopping today.*

She changed into warmer, baggy clothes and left, walking slowly toward the school gates. By the time she got there, only ten minutes until the bell. Being the bad bitch she is, she walked into the school, changed into indoor shoes, walked into her classroom, slammed the door open, grabbed Sanzu's bag and wrist, and dragged him out.

"Sorry for the disturbance~" she said to the teacher, sending a small smile, closing the door behind her.

"Did you really have to do that...?" Sanzu grabbed his bag.

She stopped walking, turned to face him, hands on her hips, giving him a disapproving look. He tilted his head, confused.

She jabbed her fingers hard into his stomach. He leaned over, crouching on the ground.

"What... what was that for..."

"For not waking me up in the morning. Now, let's go." She laughed at his state, pulling him off the ground and running down the stairs.

She changed shoes again, waited for the slow Sanzu, and walked to the bike racks. He rolled his motorbike out and threw her his helmet.

"Shall we go home now, sweetheart?"

"Nope, we need to do a big shopping trip today. There's nothing in the fridge or pantry." She started. "We also have a meeting tonight at 8 PM, so we have four hours."

"Okay, what are you waiting for then? Drive~!" She wrapped her arms around his waist. He flinched, then sighed in relief, driving off.

They arrived at the supermarket. She grabbed the largest trolley available—large enough to fit her in it.

"Let's go and find everything we need!" She was excited—this was their first large shopping adventure together.

They walked from aisle to aisle, loading basic foods.

- Bread. Milk. Eggs. Pasta. Rice.*

"Do we need all these snacks, babe?" She asked, concerned about the shitload of chips, fizzy drinks, and other snacks he unloaded. She gave him a disappointed look. He got the message and began putting them back.

"Fine, only one of each..." She felt bad for him. His face brightened as he placed one back.

They walked around more, bagging a large variety of vegetables and fruit. In the household items aisle, she subtly placed cleaning materials, sanitary items, three rolls of bandages, and instant ice packs into the trolley.

"Geez, that's a lot." Sanzu noticed the sanitary pads and disappeared. She walked to the cash register, handing the cashier item after item. Sanzu ran back just in time, unloading a bunch of snacks.

"Babe, what did I say about snacks..."

"Not for me—for you." He walked ahead, placing the bagged items back into the trolley.

She stood there, confused. *But I don't need many snacks...*

She paid and guided the trolley to his motorbike.

"How are we going to take all this home?" She was concerned about the number of trips. But he was already two steps ahead, tying a thick rope to the shopping trolley.

"Let's go, sweetheart—" He secured the trolley with one last knot.

She hopped on. He drove slowly, careful not to run over any cracks. The sound of the shopping trolley rattling behind the motorbike made her laugh. She saw the disappointed looks of adults, while children and teenagers laughed at their innovation.

They finally got home and trudged up the stairs carrying grocery bags, trying not to fall backward. After three trips, they carried everything inside and began packing it away. She was still confused about the extra snacks...

She packed the cleaning products and sanitary items into the bathroom. *Ohh, the sanitary items!* She finally realized his intentions.

- Aww, he's so cute...*

She ran toward Sanzu, who was tying plastic bags to reuse as garbage bags.

"Babe, catch!" She launched herself at him.

He dropped everything and caught her.

"What the fuck!? Don't do that when I'm not ready... what do you think would've happened if I wasn't paying attention and dropped you?"

"Thanks, babe, for the snacks." She pecked his lips. "I'll share some with you."

She parted, but he attached his lips back onto hers. She melted into the kiss, feeling his tongue brush lightly against her lips.

"If you don't want your period, just ask me. I can make it disappear for nine months, if you'd like." He walked to the couch and dropped her.

She got what he meant and blushed madly, covering her face. "How can you say that with such a straight face~" She grabbed a cushion and threw it at him.

He started laughing, holding his stomach, tears falling. She started laughing too, then got off the couch and chased him around the house, trying to poke his abdomen. She enjoyed the terror on his face as he ran, desperate to keep his life.

They lay on the wooden floor, out of breath. She looked at the clock.

- 7:30 PM.*

"Doesn't hurt to get to Musashi Shrine early, does it?"

"Nah, it's fine. Let's get dressed and go."

She walked into the bedroom and changed into the Touman uniform. She peeked at Sanzu's figure as he watched her change.

"Ahaha, you perv."

"Nothing I haven't seen before." He replied calmly.

"Geez." She sighed. "Shall we go now?"

She walked out and closed the door, buckled on her boots, and left. They drove to Musashi Shrine.

They walked up the enormous number of stairs and saw nobody at the top.

Nobody except Mikey, sitting on the other flight of stairs in front of the shrine. He just looked down at his shoes, not noticing their arrival.

"Hey, Mikey..." She approached slowly. He widened his eyes, not realizing someone had gotten so close. Due to shock, he swung his leg upward toward her temple.

She blocked it swiftly and tapped his face lightly.

"Oh, Akari-chin. Sorry about that." He sat back down, patting the spot next to him. She complied.

"I'm guessing you're not holding up well." She patted his back. "You don't have to put up this front in front of me and Sanzu. We'll listen to everything."

He just looked at her with dark, murderous eyes.

# CHAPTER THIRTY-SIX

Those dark eyes pierced into the depths of her soul. She felt like he knew everything about her and her past with that one glance. She shivered.

Mikey began to speak quietly.

"I nearly lost myself that day. I nearly killed Kazutora... If it wasn't for the charm that fell out of Takemitchy's pocket, I think I would've genuinely killed him." He stared at the floor.

"You know, Mikey, I'm really glad Take-chan stopped you. You should thank him later. You're lucky you have people who care about you. You see, I'm just like you. When I get mad, or when my heart rate goes too high, I lose myself. I experienced the same thing—wanted to kill someone so badly. You had Takechan to stop you. I didn't."

She felt him look up at her as she gave him a small smile.

"Technically, I'm a murderer. When Hanma's gang kidnapped me the night before Bloody Halloween, I lost myself, and I killed at least ten people. I understand if you don't want me in your gang anymore, and I'll gladly leave Touman if that's what you want. But just be grateful you have people around you who are happy to listen and help. I was in the dark too, like you are now. But I found people—like my other gang members in Yokohama, and now, Touman. Yes, I still have the guilt from my first murder. I'll never forget it. But I don't want someone I know to feel the same regret and guilt that I felt."

Mikey just listened.

"So if you ever need someone, don't hesitate to contact me. I'll be here for you. I promise I won't leave you. Sanzu won't leave you either, 'cause he's my loyal bitch!" She winked at Mikey.

"Hey! I heard that!" Sanzu yelled from a distance. They both laughed.

She turned to face Mikey and stared into his face. He stared back, then leaned into her, hugging her.

"Hope Sanzu doesn't get jealous," he said, chuckling lightly.

She chuckled back, rubbing his back.

"How are you taking his death?" She asked quietly.

"Getting better, but it's been worse."

"I see." She paused. "I didn't know him long, but he left a huge mark on me. Inside and out. I felt like he genuinely cared for all the Touman founders. So I don't know the pain you're going through..."

"What do you mean, inside and out...? He didn't hurt you physically, did he?"

"Oh, no. That came out wrong. Sorry. He just left a huge impact on me, and I decided to honor him." She unbuttoned her top and showed him the tattoo. He stared at it.

"Oh, you hid the stab scar with the tattoo, in memory of Baji...?" He trailed off.

"Yea, I did. It hit me hard, especially since it was raining on the way back. I was in agony. I had the largest outburst." She remembered that day again, sniffling.

"Mmm," was all Mikey said.

She squeezed him tighter. "Don't leave me either, Mikey. I'll never forgive you."

A comfortable silence lingered as they remained in each other's arms, comforting each other over the death of a fellow friend and gang member.

The sound of motorbikes echoed in the distance, heading their way. They parted.

"Don't hesitate to come knocking at my place if you ever need anyone," she said as she left him and made her way to Sanzu, who was sitting on the floor where the Fifth Division usually stood.

The Touman members slowly filled the shrine.

Mikey stood at the front and began to speak.

"Bloody Halloween. Touman's 150 versus Valhalla's 300. Despite being at a disadvantage, each of you held yourselves up, which led to us claiming victory. Shuji Hanma, the vice-president of Valhalla, has a message for us."

Hanma appeared out of nowhere and walked to the front. He noticed her and gave a small smile. She stuck her tongue out at him.

"Valhalla has never had a leader, so in the wake of our defeat, we're joining under Touman's banner. Valhalla is now affiliated with the Tokyo Manji Gang!" He announced.

Both she and Takemichi were shocked.

"What?" Takemichi exclaimed.

"So Touman has 450 guys now?"

"This kicks ass. Touman! Touman! Touman!"

"However, it was only thanks to Tetta Kisaki that this was able to happen. Please step forward!"

Kisaki walked forward, and Mikey, Hanma, and he joined hands as a form of alliance.

"There's one more thing to discuss." Mikey said. "Though we gained much from Bloody Halloween, there's also someone we lost. The First Division Captain, Keisuke Baji, died that day."

Silence hung in the air. He looked over at her, and she nodded, signaling him to take a breath. He did and continued.

"We must reflect on this reality and his death seriously. I'll let you say the rest, Vice-Captain of the First Division, Matsuno Chifuyu."

Chifuyu stepped forward.

"I considered leaving Touman, but our leader stopped me. Leading the First Division is a huge responsibility for me, so I'm gonna name the guy I wanna follow. Hanagaki Takemichi, I nominate you as the First Division Captain."

"What?" Takemichi said. "Me?!"

"Our leader and I decided that Baji-san left this responsibility to you." Chifuyu smiled while tears fell.

"Hanagaki Takemichi. Raise your head and give us your response." Mikey yelled.

Takemichi raised his head to the sky and yelled at the top of his lungs. "I'LL DO MY BEST!"

He was crying. She poked Sanzu's side. They both began to laugh together, as Draken, Mitsuya, and Mikey followed suit.

- --

# CHAPTER THIRTY-SEVEN

After Sanzu drove them home, she quickly showered while he made dinner. A knock on the bathroom door.

"Hey, sweetheart, you have a message from Izana." A small hint of jealousy in his voice.

"Okay, thanks for letting me know."

She finished up, dried off, changed into clean clothes, placed the dirty ones into a basket, and loaded them into the washing machine.

"Babe, do you have any clothes to wash?" She yelled.

He came scuttling over with another basket. She separated whites from colored, washing the colored first.

"Dinner's ready, by the way."

She walked out with a towel around her neck and sat at the dinner table.

After dinner, she sat on the couch and read Izana's text.

- Hey Akari.*

- Haven't heard from you in a while, so I'm coming over to Tokyo to check up on you. I'll be there with

Kakucho. Come find me at the train station tomorrow morning at 9 AM.*

"WHAT!" She yelled, scaring Sanzu, who came running from the bedroom.

"What happened?" He asked, worried.

"Umm, Izana and Kakucho are coming to Tokyo tomorrow."

"I see." He said quietly, sitting on the floor, leaning against the couch. "Do you want me to move back to my place for the time being?"

"Nah, you can stay with me. I'm sure Izana will understand our relationship." She nudged him with her elbow. "No need to worry!" She leaned over and kissed his forehead.

"So what are you guys gonna do tomorrow? You're lucky it's a weekend."

"Mmmm, he said station at 9 AM, so maybe we can eat something and then do something fun! You're coming with me!"

"What? You're kidding..." He was clearly worried about being left out.

"No, I'm being serious. Get to know them while you're there. They're good people at heart, I promise." She began to braid his long hair.

"...Fine." He said. "But I'm taking you on a date—just the two of us—once they leave."

"Ooooh, okayy." She was ecstatic.

- --

It was 8:45 AM, and they stood outside the gates of the train station, waiting for the 9:00 AM train from Yokohama. People walked back and forth, closely packed. Too close for her liking.

She felt Sanzu wrap his arms around her shoulders, placing his chin on top of her head. She instantly felt calm and safe from the bustling crowd.

For this reunion, she wore nothing special—just comfortable clothes, with her black mask. Sanzu also had his mask on, so they matched.

The board said the train from Yokohama had arrived. She leaned further into Sanzu's body, looking around.

"Oi, Akari!" A voice called from the distance.

- Izana.*

She felt Sanzu's grip loosen. She looked up at him. He nodded. She turned and ran toward Izana, flinging herself at him. He caught her and swung her around.

"It's been so long! How have you been?" She asked as he put her down.

"Good." He said quickly.

Kakucho appeared from behind Izana. She ran to hug him too.

"Kaku-chan!" She squeezed him tightly.

"Have you been looking after Izana for me?" She whispered.

"Yea, the gang's been quiet without you. Izana seemed a little down too, though he doesn't show it." Kakucho replied. "He—"

"Who's that guy who was hugging you earlier, Akari?" Izana cut off Kakucho.

"Hmm? Oh, that's my boyfriend." She smiled at Sanzu, waving. He walked over.

"I'm Haruchiyo Sanzu, Akari's boyfriend. Nice to meet you." He bowed a little.

"He'll be hanging out with us all day, so make sure to be nice to him." She elbowed Izana, who was staring daggers at Sanzu.

Izana and Kakucho were her family. Whoever she dated needed to be accepted by both—especially Izana.

"I'm Kakucho." He introduced himself. "And this is Izana." He pointed at him, as Izana kept staring at Sanzu.

She smacked the back of Izana's head. "I said be nice."

Izana turned his head, no longer paying attention to Sanzu.

"Now, let's go eat something. I'm sure the two of you are hungry." She dragged Izana with one hand and intertwined her other with Sanzu's.

Poor Kakucho followed behind alone.

They walked to a cafe with good reviews. She pushed open the door.

"Welcome to ____ cafe. How many people are going to be with you today?" The waitress looked worried, especially since she was surrounded by three men significantly taller than her. The waitress seemed particularly scared of Kakucho because of his scar. Akari just laughed to herself.

"Only four people, thanks."

"O-oh, sure. Follow me."

They sat down, and the waitress handed out water glasses and menus.

"Press this button when you're ready to order." She backed away slowly.

"She's so scared of you, Kakucho!" Akari laughed, clutching her stomach.

"It's not my fault I have a scar on my face!"

"I think we're all equally scary to her," Izana said, earrings swaying.

Sanzu took off his mask, and she did the same. Izana stared at her.

"I-is that a new scar on your forehead...? Who did it? I'll kill them!"

"No one knows where he is, so it's fine." She said. "Moreover, you're the only one at this table without a scar on your face, Izana. If anything, you're the most friendly-looking." She pointed at him.

"Should I make one for you?" She tilted her head, smiling as she stared into his violet eyes.

- --

# CHAPTER THIRTY-EIGHT

A glum silence at the table before she burst out laughing.

"Pfft, I was kidding." She wiped tears from her eyes. "I won't let anyone cut your precious face."

"Can we order now?" Izana whined, done with her jokes. He stared at the menu so seriously, it was like he was gonna kill it.

"I'm gonna get the katsudon, with a soda." Kakucho said. "What about you guys?"

"Mmm, I'll just get a smoothie," Sanzu said, looking around the cafe.

"Okonomiyaki for me!" Izana pointed furiously at the menu.

"I'll take the special coffee jelly," she said, piling up the menus and ringing the bell.

The waitress walked over, looking close to tears.

"W-what can I get for you all?" She stuttered.

"One katsudon, one okonomiyaki, one soda, one smoothie, and one special coffee jelly, please."

"And what smoothie would that be? We've got chocolate, strawberry, banana, and vanilla."

She looked at Sanzu, who was in lalaland. She pinched his thigh under the table. He jumped and glared at her. She rolled her eyes.

"What flavored smoothie, dumbass?"

"Oh, umm, strawberry." He said quickly.

"Well, you heard him. One strawberry smoothie, then. Thank you." The waitress bowed and left. "You need to pay more attention, babe."

"Oooh, name-calling already—" Kakucho raised his eyebrows.

"Oh, shut up!" She kicked his shin under the table, causing his knee to hit the bottom of the table.

"You guys are just like children," Izana said, looking out the window.

"That's funny, coming from the one who's pouting all the time." She rolled her eyes. Izana pouted and looked away, proving her point.

"So, how'd you two meet, anyway?" Kakucho asked.

She and Sanzu flinched and looked at each other.

She smirked. "He ordered someone to break into my house to see the rumored delinquent. I got his name from the guy he ordered. Then I saw him at school. I joined his gang, and then—"

"You joined their gang?" Izana said.

"Yup. I got bored doing nothing."

"What gang?"

"Tokyo Manji Gang." Sanzu stated before she could answer.

"...Okay, cool." Izana said. "Don't do anything stupid."

"Yea, a little too late for that," Sanzu said, eyeing her abdomen. "She already got stabbed and got a tattoo recently."

"You bitch—" she mumbled.

"Say what?" Kakucho asked, shocked.

"Yea, she got stabbed, got a tattoo, got kidnapped, murdered ten or more people—you name it." Sanzu repeated, adding more to the list, smiling at her.

She flipped him off, sticking her tongue out.

"Show me the scar," Izana demanded.

"You can't—"

"I said show me."

With no choice, she stood and lifted her shirt, revealing the tattoo.

"Where's the scar?" Kakucho asked.

"It's under the tattoo." She felt for it. "Goes from here to here."

"Umm, ma'am, can you put your shirt down, please? There are other people here." The waitress said as she brought the food.

"Oh, my bad." She pulled her shirt down.

The waitress placed the food in front of each person. Kakucho and Izana stared at theirs, then began to eat. She and Sanzu watched as they gobbled it down.

"So why the feather?" Kakucho asked between munches.

"Touman lost a gang member a few weeks back. I didn't know him well, but I owe him my life. It's my way of thanking him."

Kakucho nodded.

"Oh, by the way, your dad came to our gang recently." Izana stated.

She stopped eating the coffee jelly.

"He was asking about you. Of course, I didn't say anything."

She breathed a sigh of relief. "Thanks for that, Izana."

That got her thinking, though. "He knows where I live, so why can't he just visit? Not that I want to see him..."

"Yea, maybe that's why, stupid." Kakucho said.

She continued eating the coffee jelly. The bitterness and sweetness were perfectly balanced. She was about to eat the last bite when Sanzu took it from her. She stared at the empty spoon, then at him.

"You bitch!" She jabbed his stomach, grabbed his smoothie, finished it in one gulp, and slammed the glass on the table.

"Nice coffee jelly, by the way," Sanzu rang the bell. The waitress arrived, and he ordered four more coffee jellies.

"Well, you two sure are a dynamic couple," Kakucho snickered. Izana just mumbled under his breath.

The waitress came back with four coffee jellies.

"You guys should try it too. It's good." Sanzu passed them out. The waitress smiled, trying to hide her fear, and left.

A moment of silence before Izana spoke. "Oh, it is good."

"So how's Tenjiku doing without me?"

"Oh, definitely quieter without you. We have some new members too. You remember the Haitani brothers?"

She nodded, vaguely remembering them from Bloody Halloween and the juvenile detention center.

"Yea, I saw them a couple weeks back."

"Both of them joined Tenjiku," Kakucho finished.

"So now Tenjiku is stronger than before." Izana said.

"I love how you're indirectly saying I'm weak," she snickered.

"Glad you got the hint." Izana eyed her.

The four continued talking, each waiting for Izana to finish his coffee jelly.

A sudden crash and a yell.

"Oi, you bitch! Do you know who you just spilled juice onto?!" A voice yelled through the cafe.

"I'm so sorry! I'll pay for the laundry cleaning!" The waitress bent down to clean the mess.

"You know what?" The guy said. "You can pay me back in other ways." He smirked.

That irritated her. She walked over.

"Oi, get the fuck out, you sick fuck." She stared down at the guy, hiding the waitress behind her.

# CHAPTER THIRTY-NINE

"Wanna say that again?" He said, visibly upset.

"I said, get the fuck out, you sick fuck." She repeated.

"You've really got the nerve to say that to me." He stood up—much taller than she expected. Long blue wavy hair, piercing eyes, tattoos over his chest.

She didn't budge.

"You wanna take her place instead?" He grabbed her chin. She grabbed his hand and threw it to the side.

"Pay for your meal and leave. No one needs a nuisance like you in a cute cafe like this." She looked up at him.

He went to grab her neck, but she dodged—almost shocking him. Sanzu, Izana, and Kakucho got up. Sanzu pulled her back.

Noticing this, the blue-haired man smirked.

"Fine." He slammed money onto the table, smashing it. He walked out, slamming the door.

She breathed a sigh of relief, thankful it didn't escalate. She squatted next to the visibly shaken waitress.

"You okay?"

The waitress looked at her like she was a madwoman for standing up to a freak like that. She slowly nodded, standing up.

"Thank you so much! I'll ask the manager if I can give you four a 50% discount..." She disappeared to collect the money from the smashed table.

"Yikes, what a monster." Akari stared at the table on the floor.

"I've seen that guy somewhere," Sanzu mumbled. "But I don't know where..."

"Mm, that's really helpful," Izana stated.

The waitress came back with the receipt, 50% discount applied. They split the bill and paid.

"Thank you and come again!" The waitress walked outside with them, bowing.

Akari waved.

"What do you wanna do now?" She asked.

"Sleep." Sanzu said.

"Relax or go sightseeing," Kakucho said.

"I don't really care." Izana looked around.

"Let's go sightseeing then!" She dragged the boys to the nearest train station.

She jumped over the ticket booth, the others following. They boarded the first train to Asakusa, standing near the doors, watching the scenery. The ride was quiet and calm—even a bomb wouldn't disturb the peace.

The doors opened, and she stepped out, ushering the boys. They jumped over the ticket gates, running as the ticket master chased them. Their laughter echoed through the station, followed by angry whistles.

"Oh shit, they're actually coming after us!" She hadn't expected this. "Hurry up, they're gonna catch us."

She led them through the nearest alleyway, into another—a maze. Surely the station masters wouldn't follow.

"Tch, they're gone." One man said.

"Phew, that was close." She breathed.

Izana smacked the back of her head. "Owww."

"We had money. We could've just bought tickets, you know."

"Where's the fun in that, you party pooper?" She winked.

Kakucho and Sanzu snickered.

"That's the Akari we all know." Kakucho laughed louder. She pouted.

"Anyways, we're in Asakusa, so we're gonna check out the shrine. Let's go!"

A large lantern hung in the middle of the shrine, between two statues—the God of Thunder and the God of Wind. They walked in, past the crowds, to the praying area. She threw in a coin, clapped twice, and made her wish.

- I wish everyone around me lives an honest, happy life.*

She bowed and walked away from the box, waiting for the boys to finish. They explored the nearby area and came across a park with a river running through it.

"It's getting late, so after we rest here, we're gonna leave." Kakucho said.

She nodded.

She found a cherry blossom tree, buds not yet blooming. The twisting branches waved in the wind, leaves flying. She sat at the base and leaned into it, closing her eyes, enjoying the wind and chirping birds.

A head on her shoulder. Another on her lap.

She laughed quietly. "Man, I feel like a mom with three man-children." She brushed her hand through Sanzu's long hair on her lap.

"Akari." Izana started, jaw moving on her shoulder.

"Mmm?"

"Come visit us in Yokohama once, will you? Bring Sanzu with you too. Today was fun..."

She was shocked to hear that from him. But glad.

"Sure, I'll have to come during school break or a weekend. Is that okay?"

"Yeah... that's good." Izana mumbled.

"We'll make sure to have an action-packed day waiting for the two of you," Kakucho added.

She pondered.

"Actually, there's one thing I have to do before going to Yokohama."

"What's that?" Sanzu asked.

"I'm gonna kill my father. I can't have him interrupt my life anymore. I won't leave school yet, but that's something I need to do before going to Yokohama."

Izana and Kakucho stared with wide eyes, then nodded.

"If you see him in Yokohama asking for me, tail him. He probably moved back. Send me his address. I'll kill him, then come visit. Does that sound good?"

"Yea, that's good," Izana said, eyeing Sanzu on her lap. She noticed his gaze.

"He's helping me murder my dad, so don't worry." She glanced at Sanzu, then back up. She stared at the orange sky, spotted with pink and purple clouds.

"Time for us to go." Izana stood in front of their train. "See you soon, I guess."

She hugged him tightly. "I'll come to you alive, so don't worry."

She let go and hugged Kakucho, who stood like a log before hesitantly wrapping his arms around her.

"Look after him well, will you?" Kakucho nodded, letting go.

"Well, it was nice meeting you," Sanzu said, nodding at the two.

"Likewise." Izana turned around.

"See you soon, Akari, Sanzu." Kakucho followed Izana into their express train.

Sanzu and Akari watched the train leave, waving from the platform, before heading to their own platform, back home.

# CHAPTER FORTY

It was a couple weeks since Izana and Kakucho visited Tokyo. It was lunchtime at school, and she was staring out the window.

"Hey, sweetheart." Sanzu interrupted her thoughts.

"Hmm?"

"Are you free to go bowling with me today after school?" He asked quietly, turning his head away a little.

She grabbed his head and turned it toward her. She stared at his slightly flustered face and giggled.

"Aww, you asking me on a date?"

Sanzu nodded. "Our first official one."

He was right. It *was* their first date. That made her nervous but excited.

"You have enough money, right? I've only got ten dollars with me."

"Yea, I've got enough for the two of us. Don't worry." He pecked her forehead and left the classroom, leaving her alone with the others staring at the lovey-dovey interaction.

"What are y'all starin' at?" She said, colder than expected.

She spent the rest of the school day daydreaming and staring out the window, occasionally stealing glances at Sanzu. The bell rang, students rushing out.

"Okay, let's go, sweetheart." Sanzu grabbed her wrist and led her out of school to the bowling center.

"Here." She handed him the ten dollars. He took it and paid for one game, handing her bowling shoes.

"We're in lane four."

She nodded and made her way to the lane. She placed her stuff on the seats and looked for an ideal weight ball.

"Can you get that ball for me?" He pointed to a green one in the corner.

"Sure."

She grabbed the green ball—quite heavy compared to her red one—and carried it to their lane.

She looked around and saw familiar faces.

"Hey, babe." She poked his side.

"Mmm?"

She tilted her head in their direction. "Isn't that Take-chan and Hina, and that dude from Touman?"

She watched Hina roll the ball slowly down the lane. She laughed—it was cute.

"Mhm," he sighed.

"Why the heavy sigh?"

"I was hoping we could have a date where no one would interrupt us, but I guess that really can't happen..."

"Aww, geez." She looked back at him. "Maybe next time." She gave him a little smile.

Sanzu nodded and went to grab his ball. He approached the lane, let go—eight pins. He waited for the machine to fix the pins, then rolled again. Spare!

"Sheesh, damn baby." She clapped.

"My turn!" She grabbed her red ball, approached, and rolled hard and fast.

STRIKE!

"HELL YEA!" She jumped up and down.

"Damn, we were totally in sync," the guy next to her said. She looked at the score—he also got a strike. So did Take-chan.

"What are the chances?" She laughed. "Hey Take-chan! Hina!" She waved.

"Oh, I know you!" The tall guy said. "You're Sanzu's girl, aren't you? Touman's one female member."

She looked at Sanzu and walked over, joining him on the couch.

"Oh, hey Hakkai," Sanzu said, nodding. "Hey Takemichi."

"My captain has said a lot about the two of you." Hakkai smiled. "You know, Mitsuya?"

She nodded.

"Are we all on dates or something?" Hina said.

"Nah, she's Yuzuha. She's my sister." Hakkai said. "You're his girl, right?" He turned to Hina.

"Yup."

"I'm Tachibana Hinata, nice to meet you!" She bowed to Hakkai and Yuzuha.

"You guys all seem cool," Hakkai smiled widely. "We should all go over to my place." He slung his arm over Takemichi's shoulder.

"Ah, okay," Takemichi replied.

"Come on, you three." Yuzuha reached for Hinata and Akari's wrists. She let her, dragging them toward their place. She looked over and shrugged at Sanzu. He breathed out a large sigh, grabbed her bag, and followed.

"You don't look like you'll be any good in a fight. Why are you even a captain in Touman?" Yuzuha asked Takemichi, glancing over her shoulder. "Hakkai can probably even outrank you, but he's got no interest in that."

"You're right. Shiba-kun does look strong." Hinata said.

She and Sanzu laughed at Hinata's honesty.

There was a large silence between the siblings.

"Just thinking about being at the top gives me the shivers. I like being free!" Hakkai said.

"That's so cool, Shiba-kun." Hinata responded. He seemed to ignore her.

"Don't feel bad, Hina-chan. My little bro freezes up when any girl other than me talks to him." Yuzuha laughed.

"Damn, that's unfortunate. He seems popular with the girls." She laughed a little too loudly.

"Do you get along with your captain, Mitsuya-kun?" Takemichi asked.

"He drilled into me about how cool and uncool delinquents can be. He's like a real older brother to me."

"He likes Mitsuya way too much. Check out his phone. Mitsuya is on his standby screen." Yuzuha showed them his phone.

"Damn, that's a little creepy," Sanzu said quietly.

"Even though mine is Hakkai!" She continued.

"I don't think that's any better," Sanzu said.

"Oh, we're almost at my place," Hakkai said.

She could faintly hear the low rumbling of motorbike engines.

"Hakkai... I think we're in trouble." Yuzuha said. "Bro's coming back home."

A large gathering of white gang jackets in front of their house.

"Hanagaki, Hinata, Akari, Sanzu. You guys should go home." Hakkai said.

"What?" Takemichi said.

A voice echoed through the quiet street. "Well, well, well. If it isn't our young master, Hakkai!"

"Koko..."

"I've seen these guys before," another guy in white said. "That's Touman's First Division Captain, and Fifth Division Vice-Captain." He pointed at Takemichi and Sanzu.

"What? On our turf? Are you trying to fuck with us?" Koko exclaimed. "You guys ain't leaving in one piece."

Sanzu stood in front of her as she hid Hinata behind her. This wasn't going to end well.

# CHAPTER FORTY-ONE

"This whole area is the Black Dragon's territory. If any other gangs come swaggering in, the boss instructed us to kill them." Koko said.

"You know what that means, don't you?"

There was a long pause.

"What? That we're dead? I think we all get the idea already." She said, loud enough for the gang to hear.

"Sweetheart, there's no point in riling them up," Sanzu whispered.

She nodded but had no plans of holding back.

"Stay back, Akari, Hina. They don't go easy on us girls." Yuzuha said.

"Don't worry about me." She said. "Take-chan, watch Hina for us."

"So that's Hanagaki?"

"Didn't expect him to be such a pussy."

"Who's the bitch with the scars?"

Hakkai walked toward one of the closest men. "I thought I told you not to hurt my friends."

"Hakkai," the guy sighed. "Weren't you listening? We don't take orders from you."

"Wanna get the girls killed too?"

Hakkai snapped. He unleashed his fist, making contact with his face. He continued to punch him to the ground.

"Fuck off, you scumbags." Hakkai said. "Sorry to get you all involved in this mess. The boss of the Black Dragons is Taiju Shiba."

"Our older brother," Yuzuha and Hakkai said in unison.

"Where's Taiju right now?"

"Convenience store," Koko said quickly.

"Fucking pain in the ass." Hakkai mumbled.

The blonde kid next to Koko ran up to Hakkai and pulled out a pocket knife. "Watch your mouth, asshole."

"Isn't this getting interesting?" She said to Sanzu. He glanced back, then at the gang. She walked to stand in line with Sanzu.

"Talk shit about our boss, and I'll kill you." The blonde kid stated.

"You've got no chill." Hakkai said.

"Think I won't do it?"

She watched Yuzuha creep up behind Inui and land a spinning heel kick to the side of his neck. She wolfwhistled.

"Damn, Yuzu!"

She sent a small smile before turning back to the gang. "Don't touch my brother."

"You guys should go now," she said, turning to Hinata and Takemichi. "Sanzu and I are gonna stay behind to watch, just in case something bad hap—"

"Akari! Behind you!" Hinata yelled.

A figure ran toward her. He hooked his elbow around her neck, sending her flying. She took a defensive posture before landing, limiting her damage.

"Akari!" Sanzu rushed to her. She continued to cough after the sudden attack.

"That's just not fair! You guys look like you're having so much fun!!" He walked toward her, flinging the worried Sanzu to the side. "Let me join in!" He lifted her by the collar.

"Fuck off, you sick fuck!" She spat.

"Ohh, I remember you. You're that bitch from the cafe. Not so tough now, are we?" He punched her stomach, sending her into the wall. She slumped against it, eyesight fading. She held her head with one hand, trying to calm down.

"Akari!" Sanzu ran over.

"Cute boyfriend you've got, Akari." Taiju mocked. "Too bad your other two friends aren't here."

Sanzu attempted to lift her and carry her on his back. Taiju didn't hesitate, continuing to attack Sanzu, trying to get him to cast his attention away from her.

"Hakkai! Take responsibility as a fellow Touman member!"

"Taiju... they didn't know this was Black Dragons territory. He really didn't know, so please..." Hakkai said.

"I don't give a shit. You're my little brother. That comes before Touman. Family bonds are more important than friends, aren't they?" Taiju said.

"Taiju! Don't corner Hakkai like that!" Yuzuha said. Taiju glanced at her, then whacked her to the side.

"You beat up women too? That's despicable," Takemichi said.

Taiju turned his attention to Takemichi. Sanzu used this time to break away.

"Takemichi, stay out of this!" She groaned, trying to get up. Sanzu helped her. Both leaned on each other, helping each other off the concrete.

Taiju laughed at Takemichi's comment.

"Keep your nose out of the Shiba family's business, you little shit. Watch this carefully, Hakkai. Your big bro's gonna fix your problem for you. That's what family is about!" Taiju whacked Takemichi's head, over and over.

"Takemichi!" She yelled. Still dizzy, she crept up to Taiju, landing a flying kick to the back of his head.

He looked at her.

"You little shit!" He turned his attention back to her, and they began exchanging blows.

"Holy shit!" The Black Dragons watched.

She was holding on, but the sudden attack from Taiju earlier took its toll. She couldn't see straight, relying on the sound of his footsteps to avoid his hits.

"Akari isn't gonna hold on for much longer! Hakkai!" Sanzu yelled in desperation.

She took another blow to the stomach, stumbling back.

"Taiju! Stop!" Hakkai yelled.

"Huh?" Taiju blocked one of her kicks.

"Please!"

"Hakkaaaaaai. When you ask someone a favor, you gotta give something in exchange. Offer me something of equal worth. If you don't, then this is where she's done for." Taiju lifted her tired body by the collar.

She lifted her upper body, wrapping her legs around his neck, squeezing as tightly as she could. She felt his shoulder blades moving.

- He's gonna punch me. This is the end.*

"I'll quit Touman." Hakkai said.

She felt no movement in Taiju's shoulder blade.

"I'll join the Black Dragons so I can support you. So in exchange, let Akari go!"

She felt him flinging her around as he let go of her body. Not able to remain conscious any longer, she passed out, hearing Taiju's laugh and Sanzu calling her name.
