# CHAPTER FORTY-TWO

"Oh, you woke up." Sanzu said, walking alongside her. He would've carried her, but he was limping a little, trying to hide it.

"Sorry, Hakkai. It's all my fault that you're leaving Touman."

Hakkai ignored her apology and turned to Sanzu. "That's the first I've seen anyone exchange blows with him. Your girlfriend is incredible."

"If he didn't hit me first, he would've been a goner in one kick." She chuckled.

He continued to carry her to her apartment silently.

"Yea, I live just around the corner. Thanks, Hakkai."

She slid down his back and waved. She watched as he disappeared.

She glanced at Sanzu. He was staring at her, up and down, then back up.

"What, are you perving on me?" She crossed her arms.

He took a step toward her and wrapped his arms around her shoulders. "Don't do something rash like that again."

"Mmm." She breathed into his chest. "Sorry, but I can't promise that. Another storm is brewing, and due to my curiosity, I wanna bring back Hakkai from the Black Dragons."

He let go and looked deep into her eyes. He sighed, turning his head away—a sign of defeat.

"Just don't do anything stupid, 'kay?"

She nodded, following him up the stairs. She heard him switch on the bedroom light as she went to get the first aid kit. Then dead silence.

She carried the box to the bedroom and opened the door.

"Babe—" She stopped mid-sentence, smiling to herself at Sanzu's tired state—passed out on her bed.

She sat on the edge and began unpacking the necessary items. She patched up the sleeping Sanzu, who only groaned and winced from the rubbing alcohol. She chuckled quietly. Sticking the last patch on his cheek, she brushed the hair from his face and bent down to lightly kiss the scars at the edges of his lips. Covering him with the blanket, she left and headed to the bathroom.

The water filled the bathtub quickly, mist rising. She placed the first aid box on the sink basin, removed her clothes, and lowered herself into the hot water. Her cold skin warmed up in no time. She ran her

fingers through her flat hair and leaned into the water, now covering her whole body. She sighed, feeling the bliss of peace.

She got out, turned on the shower, washed her hair and body quickly, then tied her hair into a tight bun and entered the tub again.

She began humming a familiar tune—one of her favorite songs. The echo gave her nostalgic memories of the Yokohama apartment. Splashing the water made her miss the ocean in Yokohama, the happy times with Izana and Kakucho—Izana drowning Kakucho, random guys hitting on her and pissing the two boys off, beach volleyball, stealing food from unattended stalls, sand fights, and everything else she could list.

She sighed again, exiting the tub. Wrapping a towel around her body, she applied patches and bandages to her wounds, wincing only slightly. Forgetting her clean clothes in the bedroom, she crept quietly back in. Tiptoeing to the closet, she grabbed her clothes.

"Sweetheart, are you doing this on purpose?" Sanzu mumbled, rubbing his eyes. He looked her up and down, covered only by a bath towel.

She flushed bright red.

"I—uh, just finished my shower, and I forgot my clothes?" She stuttered. *Bad timing.* "Don't be such a perv!" She threw whatever she was holding.

Her bra.

- Fuck me!!*

- Smartest move of your life.* She facepalmed in embarrassment.

Sanzu smirked, holding her bra up and twirling it around his fingers. "Sure, you didn't do that on purpose either." He rolled his eyes playfully.

She grabbed another bra from the drawer and rushed out, muffling her annoyed yells. She heard Sanzu's laughter erupting from the bedroom as she slammed the bathroom door.

"Fuck me," she said to herself, putting her clothes on.

"Anytime, sweetheart~?" A voice said on the other side of the door.

"Sanzuuu! Don't be annoyinggg!" She whined, opening the door and shoving the medicine box into his chest as she stormed off to her bedroom. She threw the covers over her head, curled into a ball, mumbling incoherent swear words.

Sanzu's footsteps approached—then stopped. Suddenly, a mass of weight on top of her. She screamed as he began to tickle her, powerless under him.

"Ahahaha, oh my gosh, s-stop!" She cried out, drowned out by their laughter.

She crawled out from underneath the blankets and threw a pillow at his face, holding it there. His grip weakened. *Your chance.*

She pushed him down, sat on him, and began to tickle him.

"Ahahaha—oh my gosh, stopp~" He said in a high-pitched voice, imitating her earlier words.

Then it dawned on her. *He wasn't ticklish.*

"Having fun trying to tickle me, sweetheart~?" He smirked.

Already annoyed, she pouted, got off him, and turned around to sleep.

"Awww, seeing you mad is funny." He whispered into her ear, poking her cheeks. She squirmed. He chuckled, snaking his arms around her waist, pulling her body into his. She felt him breathing down her neck.

"Thanks for treating my wounds," he said softly, kissing her neck.

"Mmm," she replied, already falling asleep. "Night, babe."

"Goodnight, sweetheart~?"

She picked up the call just in time.

"Hello?" She groaned. It was 11:30 AM on a Saturday.

She nodded and got off the floor. She quickly removed her pajamas and changed into her gang uniform, ignoring Sanzu's existence. She heard him wolf-whistle.

She walked into the warehouse. Pretty much all the captains were there, staring at her. Of course, Hanma and Kisaki had to be there too. She rolled her eyes.

"Cheeky motherfuckers. Let's stomp their asses." Smiley said, smiling but visibly angry.

"Wow, very nice way of saying I lost, Mucho." She rolled her eyes. "He came from nowhere. He hooked my neck with everything he had. He's literally built like a beast. I have limits too, you know?"

"We beat the ninth generation before. The tenth is totally different." Mitsuya stated, looking at her patches and nodding. She nodded back, giving a small thumbs up—*I'm okay.*

"You're missing the point! It wasn't Takemitchy's fault that he didn't know where the Black Dragons' turf was. So why the hell did you take him there, Hakkai?" Smiley asked.

"You're the boss's little bro, aren't ya?"

"Hakkai didn't mean to—" Takemichi started.

"Shut the hell up!" Mucho cut him off.

She watched the tension escalate, turning sour, as everyone's attention turned to Hakkai.

"I won't make any excuses. Hate me, beat me, do whatever you want. As his little brother, I'm prepared for the consequences. So, leader! I, Hakkai Shiba, Tokyo Manji Gang's Second Division Vice-Captain, request permission to leave Touman!"

"...And that's okay with you?" Mikey asked.

A large silence before Takemichi spoke.

"Stop right there! I object!" He walked up to Mikey. "Here, calm down with a tasty snack!" He handed a dorayaki to him.

"Don't want it. Don't interrupt."

"Is this funny to you, jackass?" Draken yelled.

"Pfft!" She covered her mouth at his embarrassing actions.

"I'll leave it up to Mitsuya, since he's the Second Division Captain."

Mitsuya stood and walked toward Hakkai.

"Sorry, Taka-chan. I've already made up my mind." Hakkai said quietly.

"Don't look so sad, Hakkai. I understand." Mitsuya walked away and out of the warehouse.

"Taka-chan! It was a pleasure working with you!" Hakkai yelled.

"Huh? What are you saying? I didn't say you could leave." Mitsuya turned around, smiling. "Let me talk to Taiju!"

Everyone dispersed. She walked out, taking out her phone to call Sanzu.

So do what he does. And report back to me when you learn something. I'm putting my trust in you for this." He slowed as they arrived at her apartment.

She noticed Inui appear behind Mitsuya. Her body moved without thought—her leg went flying, kicking the bar away from his hands. It landed with a loud clang.

"That was dirty, Inui-kun." She glared.

"Don't talk like you know me."

"Didn't think you'd be here, princess." Taiju sneered down at her. "Was my last beating not enough for you?"

"I could say the same to you, you old man." She jeered, turning her head away.

"Mitsuya, Hakkai, he's all yours!" She pointed at Taiju. Visibly irritated, he launched at her.

As much as she wanted revenge, she held her inner self in. She released a kick, swinging upward at Taiju's chin. It connected—his head tilted up, leaving his body open. She launched a couple punches at his abdomen before stopping. He wasn't her main target.

Her phone vibrated. She sighed, took it out, and answered.

"Look, gimme one second and I'll get back to you." She placed the call on hold and turned back to Mitsuya and Hakkai. They stared in awe.

"I'm leaving Taiju to you two, so get up." They complied without complaint.

"Thanks for the save, Akari," Mitsuya said, still panting.

"Thank me later." She smiled, giving him a small peace sign.

"I don't think it's a good idea to turn your back to us—" Inui yelled, but she swung her leg in a helicopter motion, tripping him. She grabbed the metal pole and placed it at his neck.

Koko didn't expect this and began his attack. She sighed, disappointed he didn't get the message. She kept the pole at Inui's neck and waited for Koko to get close enough—then gave him a large gut punch, sending him to the floor, clutching his stomach. He fell next to Inui. She leaned down to their level, grabbing both their ears.

"You two would do better if you had planned your attack a teeny bit better~" She smiled, pinching harder.

"Oi! Take-chan! Chifuyu! They're all yours!" She pointed at the two boys on the floor.

She got up, brushed the dust off, and walked down the aisle of the chapel, away from Taiju, Inui, and Koko, who all stared in shock.

"I'm gonna take this call, so you guys do whatever you need to do. Give a yell if you need me." She opened the main door and walked outside into the cold snowy night.

# CHAPTER FORTY-NINE

- *TW: MURDER / DEATH**

The doorbell echoed through the house. Heavy footsteps approached. She quickly hid behind Sanzu's taller frame, feeling him puff up to hide her. She tightened her grip on the knife, taking a deep breath to calm her nerves.

The door opened, revealing her father's drunken state. Button-up shirt—pale yellow with sweat marks and alcohol spills—buttons mismatched. His hair, what was left of it, was a mess. He slurred his words, reaching his hand forward to grab Sanzu's chin.

"M/N?" His words were slurred. "Is that really you?"

She felt the anger and disgust in his tone. A small tap on her body from Sanzu—his hands were behind his back, nudging her on. An electrical current surged through her from his touch, unlike anything she'd felt. Energy urged her forward.

She ran out from behind Sanzu, pouncing onto her father's body, stabbing him once through the heart. Blood seeped through his white dress shirt, staining it bright red. He coughed up blood, splotching onto her face. Disgusting.

She kicked him harshly inside the apartment and shut the door behind her, Sanzu following.

She removed the knife and landed another into his abdomen.

"Akari, that's you, isn't it?" He murmured, coughing up more blood.

She wiped his blood off her face, ignoring his words.

"Why are you doing this?"

"I have no obligation to answer your questions. Hurry up and die." She spat.

He stared at her, reaching for the knife in his abdomen. He pulled it out and wobbled toward her. She spun around, landing a heavy kick into his body. He crashed into the sliding glass window leading to the balcony, smashing the glass.

She walked slowly toward him, but Sanzu pulled her back.

"Wait for him to die first." He warned, overlooking the body. Sanzu ushered her to check the rest of the house.

She nodded and walked through. Workloads of paper littered his study—all gang-related. She clicked her tongue and took a good look at the symbol of his gang.

- Ryūken.*

She burned it into her memory. Taking out the lighter, she held a single piece of paper above the small flame brightening the room. The paper caught fire quickly, spreading toward her fingertips. She let the flame reach near her fingertips before throwing the burning page onto the stack. In the corner of her eye was a safe, key left in the keyhole. She turned it and opened it.

Money and drugs.

Disappointment.

"Didn't think you were one to sell drugs," she whispered. She took the money, stuffed it into her bag, and threw the drugs onto the burning pile. Spraying deodorant into the flame, it spread fast, catching the edge of the curtains, flying upward to the ceiling. She watched in awe as the fire lit up her eyes.

"Akari." Sanzu called from the other room.

She turned, closing the study door.

"Yea?"

"He's dead now."

"Okay, cool. I took his stash of money and burned his drugs." She looked at her father's dead body leaning against the couch. "Let's get him to the bathtub."

Sanzu nodded, lifting the torso. She took the legs, and they stumbled toward the bathroom, dumping his limp body into the bathtub.

"Hey, sweetheart, you don't mind if I skin him and dismember his body, right?" Sanzu asked, gripping the knife.

"Yea, go right ahead. Don't take too long, though."

She walked out, leaving Sanzu to do his thing. Smoke began to leak from under the study door, wafting upward, filling the main room. She tightened her mask and made her way to the kitchen, cleaning the bottoms of her shoes to remove the blood so she wouldn't leave footprints.

She removed her black clothes, leaving her in sports shorts and a sports bra. Sanzu walked out.

"It's done."

He saw her removing her clothes and did the same. She pointed to his shoes—he understood. She piled up their clothes, flicked the lighter, and sprayed the flame with the deodorant. Like a flamethrower, the flame traveled far, catching the clothes on fire. She walked around the house, setting fire to anything flammable.

She watched their clothes turn to ash before getting ready to leave.

"Let's go back to Izana now." She grabbed Sanzu's hand, leading him toward the front door.

They evaded the blood splotches, making it out safely. Closing the front door and locking it from the inside, she noticed smoke pouring out from the broken window.

"We should probably make a run for it." She pointed to the smoke. "Have you got the knife?"

"Yup." Sanzu said. "We can bury it somewhere no one will find it."

"Okay, good. Let's run!" She laughed, grabbing his hand and running toward Izana's place.

She knocked three times, paused, then three more. Kakucho opened the door and pulled them in quickly.

"Done?" Izana asked, coming out from the bathroom with a towel around his waist and neck.

"Yup!" She gave him a thumbs up. "I haven't seen you without earrings for a long time. It's weird."

"Oh, shut up..." Izana walked to his bedroom.

"You guys should take a bath too. Wash off all the blood." Kakucho said.

She and Sanzu looked at each other and nodded, walking to their shared room for pajamas and towels.

"Make sure you two sleep early. Tomorrow is a long day at the beach!" Kakucho yelled after them.

"Yayyyy! Beach!" She jumped onto the bed.

"Hurry up and get your stuff. We need to sleep early if you don't wanna be tired at the beach tomorrow." Sanzu gave her a disapproving look.

They bathed together, watching the water slowly turn pink. She laughed at the sight.

"Finally, I'm free." She sighed, leaning back into Sanzu's chest. He ran his fingers through her hair, twirling it around his fingers.

# CHAPTER FIFTY

She woke early to an alarm and Sanzu shaking her awake.

"Wake up! We're going to the beach, remember?"

"Oh yeah!" She suddenly woke up, clashing heads with Sanzu. A sense of deja vu. "Oops, sorry..." She rubbed her forehead.

"Everyone ready to go?" She yelled. Silence. The boys just stared at her eating breakfast.

The salty air invaded her nose, making it crease. Listening to the waves crashing against the sand made her feel calm. She walked onto the sand and trudged into the water. It wasn't as cold as she thought. Today was a particularly warm winter day—sun shining brightly, not a cloud in sight.

"Finally! I missed this!" She stretched her arms in delight, stripped down to her swimmers, and threw her clothes toward the boys. She ran toward the ocean and dove in. Cold at first, but she got used to it quickly. She looked back at the boys, who stared in disbelief.

She splashed him. Then dove underneath, pulling on his legs, dragging him under. She latched onto his torso, not letting go, as he struggled to stand up, hair in his field of view.

"Wonder where he's going..." she said.

"Hey!"

# CHAPTER FIFTY-ONE

"Let's go, babe. Charge!" She yelled as Sanzu and Kakucho moved toward each other.

"Sure," Kakucho said.

"Alright, happy one first." She ran back once she clicked the button. "Three, two, one. Cheese~"

She put up a peace sign and smiled. She checked the photo—it turned out quite good, everyone smiling, including Izana.

"One more, a funny one!" She ran back. "Three, two, one—"

"Time to pack up, sweetheart!" Sanzu called.

She packed up, pulled her clothes over her now-dry swimsuit, and took one last look before leaving the beach.

She stared at the back of Mucho's head, looking around for Sanzu. No luck.

Izana's voice echoed.

"From now on, Tenjiku will slowly rise to the top. We'll take over the gangs in Tokyo, get involved with the mature underground businesses. It doesn't matter if it's Yakuza or what—we'll destroy anyone who opposes us. We will dominate the underground world of Japan!"

His speech sent shivers down her spine. She opened her mouth to scream out, but a gloved hand slammed it shut.

"Nuh uh, love. Don't even think about it." Ran loomed over her face. She stared back at his purple eyes, then closed her mouth. He released her. "I suggest you behave."

Motorbikes echoed in the distance.

"Touman has arrived!" Someone shouted.

She was relieved—thinking Mikey and Draken would arrive—but the gang was led by Takemichi. She was gobsmacked.

"Where's Mikey and Draken?" She mumbled.

Ran chuckled. "Guess you didn't hear the news yet. They're at the hospital."

She stopped moving. She sighed, knowing why. "So she's already gone..." She looked down.

- I'm so sorry, Emma. It's all my fault.*

She sighed again, blocking out the guilt. She diverted her attention to Touman's entrance.

Peh-yan stepped forward, facing Madarame. Peh-yan landed a blow, instantly knocking him out. Wriggling free from Ran, she yelled at the top of her lungs.

"Way to go, Peh!"

Ran pulled her back by her hair. Touman looked in her direction—her back held tightly against Ran's chest, his hand around her neck.

"I thought I told you to behave." He whispered into her ear.

She ignored him, made eye contact with Peh, and gave him a huge smile.

"LET'S GO!" Both Tenjiku and Touman yelled, clashing.

Ran let go of her neck. She coughed.

"I suggest you don't move from this point." Ran leapt down with Rindou.

Obviously not listening, she sat there watching, keeping her eyes on Izana as he stomped on Madarame's head. Take-chan ran through the opening made by his fellow gang members, making his way to Kisaki. Peh-yan continued fighting his way through Tenjiku when Izana interrupted him.

"Bring it on!" Peh-yan yelled—only to be kicked to the side by Izana's brutal kick.

She sighed, knowing the outcome, and made her way down. She walked slowly, hands still cuffed in front of her, toward Takemichi.

"Yo, Take-chan!" She nudged him.

"Ohhh, Akari! Glad to see you're okay." He didn't take his eyes off his surroundings.

Mochizuki came out from Takemichi's blind spot.

"Take-chan! Duck!" She swung her heel above his head, contacting Mochizuki's cheek. Chifuyu came out of nowhere and landed a punch to his face.

"I'll take care of him, so you two move on ahead." Chifuyu turned to Mochizuki.

"Have you seen Sanzu, by the way? I need to talk to him."

"What? Didn't you guys break up? He's fighting for Tenjiku." Takemichi stated.

"Oh, I know. I just want to talk with him."

"Then he should be with Mucho. I don't know what you're planning, but be careful." Takemichi continued toward Kisaki.

She looked around and found Mucho's head in the distance. Making her way over, she came across Ran and Rindou fighting Hakkai and Angry.

- The worst two to come across at the moment.*

# CHAPTER FIFTY-SIX

She watched the two brothers fight Hakkai and Angry. They were beat down again and again while Hakkai and Angry were at war between themselves. She was busy kicking down Tenjiku members— hardly worth her attention. It was weird, beating down her former gang members, but she didn't care. Her promise to Mikey echoed in her mind.

- If Tenjiku were to attack your gang, I'm going to just watch. I ain't taking sides.*

She was such a hypocrite, taking sides. She began to rethink her decision. But Izana wasn't himself—he was being used by Kisaki Tetta, the mole. Izana being used by someone was so unlike him. She felt more than motivated to free him from his spell.

"We are the babies of the family! Let us show you the power of relying on others!" Hakkai and Angry yelled at the Haitani brothers.

She snickered, watching them charge. Ran charged Hakkai and hit him with a baton. Angry was tackled by Rindou, who dove for his leg.

"And there goes your leg!" Rindou twisted it the wrong way.

"Angry!" She ran toward him. His screams overcast the yelling of the other men. She swung her leg at Rindou's face—he evaded, stepping back. "Angry! Stay strong!" She lifted him. He leaned on her.

"Love, what do you think you're doing? Didn't I tell you not to move from your spot?" Ran sneered.

"Shut up, bitch," she mumbled.

"Angry, can you balance alright?" He nodded, his weight easing. She left him, tilted to his left, and headed to Hakkai to support him.

"Hakkai! Let's do this!"

"Akari! What about your arms?"

"I'll be fine."

"To hell you'll be fine!" Rindou laughed, appearing out of nowhere behind her.

She turned, swinging her leg at his face—too slow. He caught her arms, throwing her off balance, and broke her left arm. An audible crack. She bit her lip hard, blood trickling down her mouth. Rindou pushed her over, and she fell heavily on her back.

"Ack!"

Rindou sat on her stomach and began punching her face. Blood poured from her nose. She tilted her head to avoid more hits.

"Akari, don't be a wuss." Rindou whispered.

She shivered, uncomfortable being so close to someone who wasn't Sanzu. *Where even was he?*

She used her remaining strength, lifting her stomach, causing Rindou to fall forward near her face. Not wanting their heads to clash, he planted an arm next to her head. She hooked her leg into his neck and flung him backward. He rolled a couple meters away, giving her time to stand.

She spat out the blood pooling in her mouth.

She turned to Hakkai, becoming minced meat by Ran. Rindou glared and charged again.

"Guess I should've gone after your leg the first time!"

Distant wails turned her attention away. Rindou stopped and looked too.

"Please stop dis awready, you dummies! Weeeeh!" It was Angry, crying, mumbling. He was standing, walking normally—as if his leg wasn't broken.

"Angry. It's alright, man, you can stop..." Hakkai mumbled from the floor.

She used the time to slowly back away from Rindou.

"Angry..." she mumbled.

"Oh well." Rindou walked up to Angry. "I'll just break another part of your body then!" He sped up, attempting to tackle him. He grabbed Angry's waist, trying to fling him down.

Angry didn't budge.

"The last time I cried was in the fourth year of elementary. The next thing I knew, everyone was taken down. Then Big Bro told me: 'Next time, please don't cry again. Because if you do... you turn into a murderer.'"

"Rindou!" Ran yelled—too late.

Angry landed a heavy punch to his face, knocking him out instantly. He slumped, grabbing everyone's attention. Angry moved swiftly behind the worried Ran.

"You're too slow, braidhair."

Ran was also on the ground, knocked out. Tenjiku members quivered, running from Angry. She smiled, cheering.

"Hold the fuck up, you shit!" Mochizuki left his fight with Chifuyu. "I put trust in you guys! I can beat 'Angry' on my own!" He wrapped his arm around Angry's neck.

Angry didn't say a word—just landed another heavy punch to the back of Mochizuki's head. He swung through, and Mochizuki was on the floor, twitching before ceasing to move.

"So who's next?" Angry mumbled.

Mucho strutted up.

"So you're Touman's dark horse, huh?"

"Mucho..."

"I won't go easy on you!"

Mucho grabbed Angry's arm and swung him onto his back, attempting to slam him. Angry used Mucho's momentum—instead of Angry landing, Mucho was on the ground with Angry's leg on his neck.

- No need for her to go after him now.*

She breathed a sigh of relief and spotted Sanzu in the distance. She ran toward him, trying not to move her arm.

"Sanzu!"

He turned, eyes widening. She wanted to slap him and hug him at the same time.

"Sanz—" He launched a punch, narrowly missing her face.

"Wha—"

"Akari, we need to act like enemies, so fight me. But at a level that looks like we're fighting. I announced we broke up so they'd buy me into Tenjiku."

She nodded, swinging her leg at his head—slower than normal.

"Izana isn't normal. Kisaki's taken complete control." Sanzu spoke.

She eyed Izana, standing proudly over the fight, watching every move.

"You have to save Izana by killing Kisaki. Kisaki is the one behind everything, including Emma. Now run away from me and toward the center of the battle. Toward Kakucho. Help Takemichi."

She understood, turning heel and running toward Takemichi. Sanzu went back to attacking the remaining Touman members.

"That's enough, Takemichi! Touman lost!" Chifuyu's voice exclaimed. "400 versus 50. We knew right from the beginning we can't win this fight. Look, there's no one else standing. At this rate, you're going to die..."

She made her way to where Takemichi stood, watching everything unfold. Takemichi was bloody and bruised, Kakucho behind his wounds. Everyone in Touman had heavy injuries, but Takemichi's was another level.

"Touman will never lose!" Takemichi exclaimed, earning glances. "As long as I am here, Touman will never lose!"

He grabbed his uniform, staggering to his full height. She watched in utter shock. She felt eyes on the back of her head—she turned, noticing Sanzu had made his way over. He stood next to Mucho, who looked a little glum after his defeat.

"What're you doing, Kakucho? Hurry up and end it already!" Izana's voice echoed.

"Kaku-chan will not win against me. I just know it by looking at him. He looks like he doesn't have enough determination." Takemichi said.

Kisaki made his move, walking past Kakucho, standing proudly in front of Takemichi. Not a single scratch on his face.

"So you're saying you have it then, Takemichi?" Kisaki pulled out a gun and stuck it to Takemichi's head. But he didn't budge.

- Fuck, the courage he has against a gun is scary.*

Even Kisaki was shocked. He stared for a couple seconds.

"Kisaki. What's holding you back?" Takemichi smirked.

A gunshot echoed. She felt the vibrations embed deep in her bones.

"Take-chan!" She exclaimed.

Takemichi took a knee, grabbing his left leg.

"What's wrong, Kisaki? I won't die if you're aiming at my foot." Takemichi asked. "I don't give up. Even if I die, I will not give up!!"

Kisaki trembled, placing the gun at Takemichi's forehead.

"I'll kill you."

"Go ahead. Do it."

Kisaki didn't pull the trigger. Instead, he whacked Takemichi's face with the gun, sending him to the floor. He was limp but slowly rose. He stumbled toward Kisaki and landed a punch to his face.

"Kisaki! I'll beat your shitty rotten brain til you make some sense!"

# CHAPTER FIFTY-SEVEN

"Get up. How can you make someone like Draken a murderer? I just don't get it. How can you kill Emma?!" Takemichi charged, landing another blow. Izana blocked it.

"Don't interfere, Izana!"

"Move, Kisaki." Izana started. "Let me kill everyone here." He smiled.

"I won't let you, you asshole!" Takemichi charged. Izana kicked him, and he flew to the side.

"Don't fuck around, trash."

Takemichi stood, continuing to attack. He got knocked down over and over.

"You guys fucked up Mikey! And I'll protect Mikey from that!" Takemichi swung once more—but stopped. "What took you so long?" He placed his fist in the air. "I told you, I won't lose."

"Huh? What are you talking about?" Izana asked.

"Thanks, Takemitchy." Mikey's voice came from behind.

He ignored Izana and Kisaki, walking straight to Takemichi, hugging him.

"But why? You're not in the right mental state to come... Draken-kun? Why are the both of you here?!"

"You can get off now, Hina-chan." Draken revealed Hina sitting on his bike.

"I'm sorry, Takemichi-kun. I got myself here." Hina spoke quietly, tearing up.

"Half, huh." Mikey started. "200 versus 2 is a bit... you guys handicapped?"

"Don't fuck around, asshole!"

"Are you stupid?"

"It's you who's handicapped!"

"No, you guys are the ones fucking around. Who do you 200 people think I am? Huh? I can take down even 20,000 men!" Mikey yelled, sending shivers down spines.

He turned to face Touman. "What's wrong, you guys? Let's have some fun! It's a showdown, isn't it?"

"Come on, yell out loud, Touman!" Draken exclaimed.

Out of the corner of her eye, she saw Izana running toward Mikey. She rushed into his way, swinging her leg at his head. He blocked, and she nearly lost balance.

"Akari. Move out of the way!" Izana yelled.

"Izana! Stop! Why are you doing all this? This isn't the Tenjiku I know!" She planted her foot, preparing for another blow.

"Oh, shut up! You wouldn't know how I feel! You were the one who killed your family!"

That shut her up. She felt her soul crumbling. Everyone's eyes turned to her.

"Akari... is this true?" Mikey asked.

She ignored him, full attention on Izana.

"Wow. Really low blow." She chuckled. "At least you had family that were willing to accept you! But you chose not to! You were my family! But I guess you're gonna push me away too!"

She sprinted at Izana, hooking her leg around his neck. He caught it, tilting her off balance. With no arms to brace her fall, she fell hard. She winced, trying to support her broken arm. He leaned down and grabbed her hair, lifting her face to his. He whispered into her ear.

"You know nothing, so don't get involved."

He threw her hair to the side, kicking her hard in the abdomen. She coughed, watching as he made his way to Mikey, swinging his leg, landing a brute blow. Mikey blocked.

"Shinichiro's dead. Now Emma is too. So? Are you feeling empty yet?" Izana smirked.

"You're quite strong, brother." Mikey wiped his mouth of blood.

She sat up, trying to breathe, Izana's kick having forced all the oxygen out. She watched the battle between Mikey and Izana.

"Let's settle this for good, brother."

"I wonder how you're still standing."

Mikey landed a forceful kick to Izana's head—guarded with ease. Izana rushed in close. Mikey continued landing blows, only for them to be blocked. Mikey rushed in again, attempting a flying kick, but was kicked back by Izana—his hands in his pockets. Mikey flew back, near her.

"Mikey..." she mumbled.

"Since the initial plan didn't work, I'll just kill you." Izana's face turned dark.

Mikey pounced again, attacks countered. Izana landed a punch to Mikey's temple.

"Let me ask you something. Why did you kill our sister?"

"Mikey. Let me tell you a secret. Since Shinichiro can't be my 'ideal brother' anymore, I'll kill all your friends... that's why I decided to burn you down to ashes and turn you into Shinichiro." Izana grabbed Mikey's throat. "So can you please be painfully empty already?"

"So that's why you killed Emma?"

Izana swung his leg quickly, contacting Mikey's face, flinging him down.

"You took everything away from me, Manjiro! That's why I'll kill you!" Izana continued landing blows. Mikey didn't respond—just got punched, flung around like a ragdoll.

"Are you kidding me right now, Mikey?! Is this seriously all the power you got?! I'm really gonna kill you, you know?!" Izana laughed hysterically.

"You're not interested in anyone, huh..." Mikey spat out blood. "Not even the friends who fight for you?"

"Fighting for me?" Izana laughed. "Wrong! They're frightened of me—that's why they're fighting. They're all in the same playhouse with the Touman kids! In Tenjiku, there is only fear and an interest in it! Shit like trust and friendship are just delusions!"

"You know that's a lie, Izana!" She shouted. "What was everything we did together then?!" Tears welled up.

"Shut up! Stay out of it!"

"How long are you going to decide things on your own?" Mikey asked.

"Shinichiro and Emma are dead now... aren't you alone too?!"

"You're wrong, Izana... you still have a brother, and I too have a brother." Mikey blocked Izana's kick. "Brother, I just wanna save you."

"Shut up!" Izana kicked—Mikey dodged.

"You're starting to miss." Mikey punched Izana square on the nose, then landed a powerful kick to his temple, collapsing him. He quickly stood.

"What the hell? So you had it in you all this time, huh, Mikey?" Izana punched—evaded again.

"Why did you become like this? Why can't you love your own siblings?! If only you could've opened up your heart, Emma and I would've been happy to take you in. Why, Izana?!" Mikey yelled.

"Shut up already!" Izana attacked again, only to be evaded and countered.

"Shinichiro, Emma. Why? Why are you on his side?"

Izana yelled an ear-piercing scream and made his way to Kisaki.

"Kisaki! Give me that!" He took the gun and pointed it at Mikey's head.

"If I lose this fight, that means I've lost everything, right?"

"Izana..."

"Die, Mikey..."

"Try and shoot me, Izana. You'll be satisfied, right?"

"Don't test him, Mikey! He's not playing around!" Draken yelled.

"What's wrong, Izana? Pull the trigger! Try and shoot me!" Mikey shouted again.

She stood, stumbling toward Izana. She kicked the gun out of his hand—it clattered on the floor. Kakucho followed, standing next to her.

"You two... the fuck are you doing?"

"Izana, I think that's enough, okay? Let's end this and go back to how we were before, okay?" She spoke softly.

"Izana, we lost." Kakucho stated. "I only fought for you. No matter how twisted your thoughts are, I'd gladly die for you. I'm sure Akari is the same. So please, stop showing yourself like this... I don't wanna see you in such a horrible state!"

"Hey, you executives. Don't just stand there and watch. Hurry up and kill Kakucho and Akari." Izana turned to the executives.

"Izana! They're not moving! It's the end! Wake up!!" She shouted.

"Don't you get it? Not even the executives, including me, can win this! Tenjiku lost, Izana!" Kakucho shouted, tears overflowing.

"Shut upppp!" Izana yelled.

A gun clicked nearby. She pushed Kakucho out of the way with her body—just in time. The bullet pierced through her right shoulder. Blood splattered onto Izana's face. She coughed blood, landing heavily on her knees.

"Akari!" Mikey exclaimed. Both gangs stared in shock.

"God fucking dammit, you're so annoying!" Kisaki exclaimed. "Again and again... my plans are always ruined by Hanagaki and Akari. When I am unable to use Mikey, I have no choice but to use Izana instead, but now you're in my goddamn way again, Akari!"

"Shut up, Kisaki! How many times are you gonna kill for your so-called plan? Was Baji and Emma not enough for you?" She yelled, coughing more blood as she rushed toward him.

"Die!" Kisaki stated.

She was pushed to the side. She heard the gunshots but didn't feel anything.

"Izana?!"

She fell heavily, panting.

"Izana!" Kakucho's voice rang out, footsteps approaching.

"Izana... what are you doing?" She mumbled. Kakucho kneeled between her and Izana's body.

"My body moved on its own..." Izana coughed. "Mikey, there's something I want to tell you..." Mikey walked closer. "It's Tenjiku's defeat."

"Izana, why?" Kakucho asked, tears spilling.

"I'm sorry, Kakucho, but you and Akari are all I ever had." He smiled.

"Somebody call an ambulance!" Mucho yelled.

"Mikey, listen carefully. There was one time where I coincidentally met the mother who threw me away... She told me that I was just the child of her ex-husband with a Filipino woman. Me, Shinichiro, you, and Emma—we are not siblings. I am blood-related to no one at all. Mikey, you wanted to save me, right? There is no way to save me now, is there?" Izana mumbled.

"Izana, you were always my family. Blood-related or not. You were always there for me, so you are my family." She coughed out.

No response.

"...Izana...?"

She sat up slowly. Tears overflowed. Izana was already gone.

# CHAPTER FIFTY-EIGHT

She sat up straight.

Screaming her heart out, she desperately tried to grip Izana's cold hand with her non-broken arm, her other arm following.

"You can't leave me too!" She wailed, leaning her forehead into his chest. Tears overflowed, staining his already blood-stained uniform. Kakucho grabbed her shoulders, pulling her back. He broke your handcuffs—her wrists red from rubbing. He was also crying. She grabbed Kakucho's hand and connected hers with his and Izana's. The final reunion.

She wailed again, her voice echoing throughout the dock. She wiped her tears and slumped onto Kakucho, panting. Her vision narrowed.

She leaned on Kakucho for support. He lay her down next to Izana.

"We lived such great lives, didn't we?" Kakucho uttered quietly.

She laughed a little. "Yeah, we really did." She smiled, tears still escaping. She stared at the night sky as small white flakes began to flutter down. The snow melted instantly in her blood, pooling around her.

"Kaku." She coughed.

"Yeah?"

"I'll see you again soon, right?"

"Of course. We're family, after all." He sniffled, grabbing her hand with both of his.

"Members of Touman and Tenjiku. Everyone listen up! Our dispute ends here. An ambulance and the cops will arrive shortly. Before any of us get into trouble, get out of here as soon as possible! I'll be the only person who stays! Dismissed!" Mikey yelled. Touman and Tenjiku members began to walk out.

"Mikey, you get out of here too!" Mucho announced, the other Tenjiku executives agreeing. Mucho looked at Sanzu and waved him over.

"Go say a couple words to your girl, then leave. Don't need you getting caught either."

Sanzu nodded and walked toward her. Ran was already there.

"Somehow I've always admired you. Captain, I'll hold onto the way you lived your lives, dearly." Ran whispered, closing Izana's eyelids.

"Come back stronger, love." He muttered before standing and heading to where his brother was.

She didn't want to react to Ran's comment. She didn't care anymore. Tunnel vision. She squinted, trying to grasp at the figure near her.

"I'm so sorry, sweetheart. It wasn't supposed to be like this." Sanzu grabbed her hand, running his thumb over her palm.

"Sanzu..." She recognized his touch. "Come visit me later when it's safe, okay?" She sputtered.

"Of course. I'll bring everyone." He smiled. She saw his figure bending closer. She felt his lips on her forehead.

"Get some rest." He closed her eyelids.

It became easier to breathe as sound and sight failed. She was enveloped in pitch black.

"I'll never forgive you, Kisaki." Mikey growled, sheer anger tearing through his voice.

A motorbike approached.

"Kisakii!" Hanma reached out, grabbing Kisaki. "Gotcha! You owe me one, 'kay, Kisaki?" He smirked, making his getaway.

"You got it!" He grabbed onto Draken, who sped up, gaining on Hanma.

killing Naoto, killing Emma, ruining the Shiba siblings, Izana and Akari, and killing Hina. Again and again.*

"Yes! I will run until my legs break!"

They both took a breather. He looked around. He recognized it immediately.

"Don't space around, you idiot!" Kisaki punched him again.

"Shut the fuck up, you asshole! Just give up already! You lost, Kisaki! So weak that all you do is manipulate and use others. Moebius, Valhalla, and Tenjiku! You can't do anything yourself!" He screamed, bombarding him with punches.

Kisaki caught his hand, grabbed the other, and they pushed against each other.

"Are you stupid? You don't always have to use brute force to get to the top!" Kisaki bent his head back and slammed it into Takemichi's. He let go, grabbing his head. "The key to getting what you want is a perfectly crafted plan!"

# CHAPTER FIFTY-NINE

"Takemichi-kun!" Hina's sweet voice distracted his quaking hands.

"Hina... Mikey-kun..."

"Kisaki!!" Mikey yelled.

"Huh?" Kisaki had run in the moment he turned his head. He chased.

"Kisaki! It's over! Everyone knows what you're up to! No one trusts you anymore! Your pathetic dreams are gone!"

"Like hell I'll let it end! I can start over again and again! One day, Tachibana will be mine! One day, for sure!"

"No way! I won't let that happen! I won't let you go back to the future again!" He yelled, still under the speculation that Kisaki could time-leap.

Kisaki stopped running, standing in the middle of the empty road.

"What? You're not...?"

There wasn't a moment for Kisaki to answer. Screeching wheels. A large bang.

Kisaki had just gotten hit by a truck.

"Kisaki?" He watched him try to get up, his body mangled and disjointed.

"Shit! What the hell? What's going on?! I can't stand up!?" He yelled. "I don't want to die..." He mumbled. Then stopped moving. Dead quiet.

Mikey caught up with Hina.

"What happened?" Mikey asked.

"Kisaki's dead..."

The silence enveloped the air, words stuck in his throat. The final long battle was finally over, but his hands were still trembling.
