- *AKARI POV**

She woke way too early. The sky was still dark, stars faintly twinkling. She sat up, wincing. Her arm was in a cast, bandages tightly wrapping her shoulder.

Unaware of how many days had passed, she looked around for a calendar. Her phone sat on the bedside table, charged. Messages from Sanzu, Kakucho, and Mikey poured in.

- Text me when you wake up.* — Sanzu

- How are you feeling?* — Kakucho

- Text me when you're available to talk.* — Mikey

She ignored them, putting the phone down and staring outside. She hated this. Hated being stuck in this hospital room. Claustrophobic. Trapped.

Her heart rate shot through the roof. She breathed in through her nose, out through her mouth, calming down. She swung her legs off the bed, grabbed her phone, slid the ward door open, and left. Tiptoeing down the empty corridor, she waited for the elevator, took it to the rooftop, and cautiously opened the door.

A small gust of wind brushed through her hair as she stepped out. She felt closer to the sky. Dawn was breaking, light shining through pale clouds. She walked to the edge, clinging to the green wire fence. Staring down at the ground, memories from that night flooded back. She tried to block them out, but they intruded—the same scene repeating over and over.

- Izana was now dead.*

That fact was still unbelievable. A raw wound. She sat on the cold ground, lay down, and looked at the sky, growing brighter. Warm tears rolled down her cheeks. She wiped them away, but they continued to flood. She felt like she'd lost a part of herself when Izana died.

- --

Back in her hospital room, small knocks sounded. She rolled over, back facing the door. It slid open, footsteps approaching the side of the bed.

"Sweetheart, I know you're awake. Talk to me..." Sanzu pulled out a small stool.

She turned to face him. He sat with a pained expression, then held out his arms.

- She couldn't ask for anything more.*

She moved to the edge of the bed and wrapped one arm around his neck. His arms snaked around her waist, pulling her into him. She sat on his lap, sniffling into his shoulder.

"I'm sorry, Sanzu," she sniffled.

"No, it should be me being sorry. I know how much Izana meant to you, but I couldn't do anything. I'm sorry." He hugged her tighter, breathing into her neck. He rocked a little on the stool, and she swayed. It was comforting. Her breathing relaxed.

Another knock.

"Who is it?" she asked quietly.

"It's Kakucho. Can I come in?"

"Sure..."

The door slid open. Kakucho walked in, staring at the floor before making solemn eye contact. He sat next to Sanzu on a separate stool.

"You feeling okay?" He noticed the wet patch on Sanzu's shoulder.

She nodded slowly, turning to stare out the window.

"Umm, wanna come with me to the orphanage?" Kakucho stuttered, looking away.

"Sure. Now?"

"When your body is good enough to walk normally."

"Yea?" She slid off Sanzu's lap, stood carefully, Sanzu supporting her. "Let's go now, then."

Kakucho stared, then turned to Sanzu, who just shrugged in defeat. Kakucho sighed and opened the door.

- --

They arrived at the orphanage—a plain grey building with a small backyard, patches of grass. He walked into the main corridor, and she followed behind.

"We used to chase each other down these halls." He walked further, out the back door. "We would play in the snow together, making igloos. Making plans for the future gang. Or Tenjiku."

He turned to the narrow area between the orphanage wall and the fence. He gathered dirt, the pile slowly growing. He placed Izana's symbolic earrings in the dirt.

"Rest well, Izana." He turned away and out of the gap.

She kneeled, patting the small pile.

"Forever in my heart," she whispered, standing and dusting off her hospital garments. She followed Kakucho back to the hospital.

- --

# CHAPTER SIXTY

She was in the middle of her thoughts when her phone rang. Midday. Kakucho had already left, and Sanzu had gone home to collect clean clothes. She picked up without checking the caller.

"Who's this?"

"Hey, Akari-chin. Can you come today?" Mikey's voice was quiet.

"Huh? Where?"

"Emma's funeral." A small pause. "I'm sure she would've loved to see you again."

She was too depressed over Izana; she'd forgotten Emma was also gone. A lump caught in her throat— the guilt she had for causing Emma's death.

"I—um..." She was torn. Should she go? Should she really meet the others, since she was the partial reason for the battle?

"Akari." Mikey's voice was weak. "Please come."

He cut the call. Thoughts ran through her head.

A nurse walked in. "You're discharged. You can go home. Just don't put too much work into your arm. Work on its recovery slowly." She walked out swiftly.

Sanzu came in, placing clothes at the foot of the bed.

"Babe. I'm discharged now. Also, I need to go shopping."

"What? Where? For what?"

"I need to buy a suit. A black one. Emma's funeral."

He stared before his eyes softened.

"Okay, let's go."

She changed out of her hospital gown into her own clothes. He reached his hand out, and she took it, walking out of the hospital.

- --

"You think this is okay?" She walked out of the change room in a black suit.

Black dress pants that slipped on easily, flaring at the ankles. A white dress shirt with hardly any creases, tucked in. She'd had difficulty with the shirt due to the new cast—had to wear a larger size. The black suit top draped over her shoulder, as she couldn't pass her injured arm through. A black pair of high heels completed the look. (Cast on left arm, fingertips to elbow, bandages wrapping her shoulder from the bullet wound.)

"I think that's good, sweetheart." Sanzu glanced up and down, meeting her eyes.

"Make sure you take good care of the suit. You might need it again in the future. Hopefully not for the same reasons."

She nodded, paying the cashier.

"I'll just wear it out now." The cashier nodded, removing the tags, patting the shoulders of any dust.

"Thanks for shopping with us."

"Babe." He looked over as she walked out. "Do I look okay?"

Sanzu opened his mouth, then shut it.

"Honestly, no. But I don't think anyone is okay." He took her hand and led her to his motorbike. "Mikey's place, right?"

She nodded.

"I think we're late, but I don't wanna see everyone, to be honest. As long as I'm there in the end, I think it'll be fine."

She gripped his waist tighter than normal, dreading a possible confrontation. Sanzu felt her nails dig into his sides and just sighed deeply.

The bike slowed a couple houses down from Mikey's.

"It's the house on the corner." He pointed. "I'll pick you up in an hour?"

She nodded as he left. The clatter of her high heels echoed through the quiet street. Muffled noises as she walked closer.

She still looked like she normally did—hair, piercings, scars. She'd left the mask at the hospital. The only things different were the overwhelming aura she put off as she walked into the house with scars, a sling on one arm, suit draped over her shoulders like Mikey did with his gang uniform.

She opened the gate, walked to the front door, breathed in sharply, and rang the doorbell.

Slow, heavy footsteps. The door opened, revealing an old man—small but definitely not fragile.

"Good evening. Sorry I'm late, but I'm here to pay my respects to—" The lump returned, unable to say her name.

"Thank you for coming. This way." He turned and walked down the corridor. She followed.

He slid open the paper door. Mikey and Draken were alone, sitting in front of Emma's photo. The smell of incense was strong. Draken turned, eyes red. Mikey hadn't turned, still staring at the photograph.

"Sorry I'm late. I didn't have the correct clothing..." She sat next to Draken, tucking her legs under her.

She placed her right hand out and her head landed harshly on the floor.

"Emma, I'm so sorry for dragging you into this mess. I hope you're resting well. I promise to look after Mikey and Draken, so look over me. Okay?" Tears rolled down her already puffy eyes. She raised her head, wiping them away.

She continued to look at Emma alongside Draken and Mikey.

"I'm sure Emma would be grateful to you for doing that," the old man said from behind, shuffling to sit next to her.

"Thank you, sir." She turned and bowed her head. "And I'm so sorry for your loss." She kept her head down.

A warm, soft hand on her head. "I'm sure she's already watching you. She'll be telling you to raise your head. So, young lady, I'll leave the boys to you." He bowed slightly. She nodded, wiping her tears.

"Thanks for coming, Akari," Mikey said quietly, walking her to the front door.

"I'm sorry, Mikey. This is all my fault for having connections with Tenjiku. If I never joined Touman, then none of this would have hap—"

"Akari. You've done plenty for Touman, and I thank you for that. So keep your head up. Not to mention, we've both lost a family member too..."

"They're both watching over us. They all are." She tilted her head back to stare at the night sky, littered with dimly shining stars.

"Akari, I leave myself in your care." Mikey bowed his head.

She could only stare at the back of his head.

"Yeah..." She tapped the back of his head to ask him to lift it. Faintly, the sound of Sanzu's motorbike approached.

"I'll see you again soon." She hesitantly hugged him before swinging the gate open and leaving.

- --

Arriving home for the first time in a long while, she missed the smell. But it was trashed—garbage piling in corners.

"You really didn't try hard enough to keep things clean, babe." She chuckled. Sanzu was already cleaning up.

"I'll clean up, so go and sleep. I'm sure you've missed your bed." He continued picking up rubbish.

She trudged to her bedroom—untouched and clean. Assuming the worst, she checked every corner before carefully removing her suit and folding it, placing it aside. She changed into pajamas and slipped into bed, pulling the covers over her shoulders, drifting away.

- --

# CHAPTER SIXTY-ONE

She woke to arms wrapped around her waist. Sanzu's hair was all over his face, tickling her back. She turned carefully, brushed his hair out of his face, pecked his bare forehead, and left the room.

A knock at the front door. She tiptoed and peeked through the peephole. *Mitsuya.*

She didn't know what he wanted, nor did she want to interact with anyone other than Mikey, Sanzu, and Kakucho. She left him waiting.

A little while later, Mitsuya was gone, and Sanzu had woken up.

"Morning, sweetheart." He walked toward her, rubbing his eyes. "How's your arm?"

"Could be better, but that's something I can't fix right now." She shrugged her right shoulder. "Oh, by the way, can you drive me to the tattoo parlor again? I'm gonna get another one."

"For Izana?"

She nodded. "Yea, right here." She pointed under her left collarbone. "Close to my heart, so I'll never forget him."

"Have you chosen the design?"

"His earring hanafuda." She replied. "Without color."

"Mmm, okay. We'll go after breakfast."

"Thanks, babe." She kissed his lips quickly and opened the fridge.

- --

Swinging the tattoo parlor door wide open, she skipped in.

"Morning, sir!"

"You again? Did you come here to get me into further trouble?"

She giggled. "Yea, I came for another tattoo."

He gave her a face. She didn't question her decision. He sighed deeply, patting the chair.

"Sit 'ere, then. And your boyfriend?"

"He's not getting one today."

"Okay, cool."

Sanzu looked around at the designs on the walls, then turned back to her, happily chatting with the tattooist.

"Sweetheart, I'm gonna go buy groceries. I'll be back in a bit."

"Okay, thank you!" She heard him walk out and close the door.

"So what design and where?" the tattooist asked.

She pulled out her phone, showing him a picture of Izana's earring.

"Can I get this hanafuda design, please? And in black only—no color."

He drew a quick sketch. "Like this?"

"A teeny bit bigger if you can."

He redrew it, only slightly bigger.

"Yea, that's perfect."

He nodded and transferred the drawing to stencil paper. She stared at the ceiling, covered in ink splotches.

"Where do you want it?"

She pointed below her left collarbone, moving her sling out of the way.

"Here."

He stared before sighing. "Might be a little more painful than the other one."

"Eh, it'll be okay."

He turned to his stencil markings, the quiet sounds filling the room. After a while, he turned back.

"Can you lie back on the seat for me?" She complied. "You're gonna have to remove your t-shirt and pull down your bra a little, and move your sling to the side. I'll leave the room."

She carefully removed her sling, grabbing her left elbow for support. She lifted her knee, changing the support, peeled her t-shirt over her left arm, then her right, slowly pulling it over her head. She lay back.

A small knock. "You ready?"

"Yea, you can come in."

He entered, grabbed the stencil, and brought it over. She pulled her bra down a little, allowing him to stick the stencil onto her skin. He patted it down, removing creases. He readied his inks, leaving the stencil on longer.

"I'm removing the stencil." He slowly peeled it off. "Check in the mirror before you get it permanently inked."

She stood, arm under her other arm.

- Looks good. What do you think, Izana...?*

She sat back down, resting her head, relaxing.

"I'm gonna start now." The whirring of the tattoo machine filled the room.

"Sure." She rested her left arm on her stomach.

The needle popped in and out, whirring. The closer he went to her injury, the more it hurt. He noticed her wincing.

"What happened to you this time? Another person left you?" He stopped.

"Someone broke my arm, I got shot, and I lost a family member." She mumbled.

"Damn, your life is full of dangerous things. Some life you're living." He dipped the machine in ink. "Want me to continue? It's close to the wound, right?"

She nodded. "Yea, but continue. I want to finish today."

He took his time, allowing longer, more frequent breaks.

Sanzu came back before the tattoo finished.

"How's it going, sweetheart?" He set the groceries on the floor and sat on the stool in the corner.

"My wound hurts, but other than that, it's fine. Nearly done, I think."

The tattooist wiped away the ink, stopped, and stared. "I think you're done." He stood and stretched, grabbed the clingfilm, and stuck it over the tattoo. "Same as last time—keep the wrap on for at least three days, and try not to scrub too hard until the skin fully heals."

"Thank you, sir." She carefully pulled her t-shirt over her head, threading her arms through. She paid and bowed, arm dangling in the sling.

"Take care, kid." She heard him as she closed the door.

Sanzu carried the groceries to the motorbike, storing them carefully in a backpack. He handed it to her.

"Wear this for me. There's eggs in there, so be careful."

"Maybe we should buy a car instead," she joked, grabbing onto his waist with one arm as he drove off.

"Maybe we should, sweetheart. One day in the future~" Sanzu laughed.

- --

# CHAPTER SIXTY-TWO

- *ONE WEEK LATER**

She woke to a fresh start. And it was Monday. School.

Sighing, she got out of bed and changed into her uniform. Except her shirt didn't let her cast through.

"Babe! Can I borrow your school shirt?"

"It's in the cabinet!"

She took out his shirt. His smell lingered. She pulled on her skirt, packed her bag, and left the bedroom, placing her bag at the door and putting on her shoes.

"No breakfast?" Sanzu asked, half-dressed.

"We're already late..." She walked out and down the stairs, waiting for Sanzu. She didn't want to go to school. She wanted to avoid everyone.

"Let's go, sweetheart." Sanzu broke her thoughts.

- --

The teacher rambled while Sanzu poked her thighs under the table.

"Mmm, what?" She was half asleep.

Sanzu pointed down and out the window at a figure in the middle of the oval. *Mikey.*

"What the fuck is he doing here!" She exclaimed a little too loudly. The teacher and classmates turned. "Oh, my bad, sir." She walked to the door. "I'll be back in a bit!"

She left, hearing the teacher mumble. She walked down the stairs, changed her shoes, and headed to Mikey.

"Mikey. Really? What are you doing here? Couldn't you just call me?"

"Nope. This is really important."

"Yea? What do you need?"

"I came to tell you that Touman is disbanded. Mitsuya came over to your place, but no one answered."

"Wait, wait. Lemme process this. You disbanded Touman?!"

"Yea... it's better for everyone." Mikey kicked the dirt.

"I see. Okay."

"You'll still be here for me, right?" Mikey looked at her.

She didn't respond. "I haven't told Sanzu about it yet, but I'm gonna go after my father's gang. I'll come back after that."

Mikey stared for a few seconds, mouth opening but quickly shutting.

"How long?"

"Huh?"

"How long will you be gone for?" He grabbed her right hand.

"I don't know, Mikey. I don't know." She averted her gaze.

An awkward silence.

"Well, I'll see you around, I guess." Mikey wrapped her in a hug. "Stay safe, okay?"

"Yea, I'll do my best." She grabbed his shirt tightly.

He let go and walked out of the school gate, disappearing.

She turned and headed back to class, sliding the door open, sitting at her seat, ignoring every pair of eyes.

"What did he want?" Sanzu asked.

"He disbanded Touman."

"I see..."

"Yea..."

"That's it? You guys hugged like you were never gonna see each other again." Sanzu watched, sharp as always.

"I—I'll tell you at lunch."

- --

She sat against the rooftop wall, wind blowing through her hair.

"So what did you need to tell me, sweetheart?"

She took a deep breath. "I'm going after my father's gang."

Sanzu's eyes widened. "You serious?"

"Yea." She nodded.

"How long? What are you planning to do?"

"I don't know how long. I'll check the situation, but it'll most likely take a while."

"I see." He looked at the ground. "So when are you leaving?"

"After my arm is completely back to normal, so in a few months?"

"Okay." A pause. "What about us?"

"Us? You mean the relationship?"

"Yeah."

"I—I love you too much to let you go..." She watched him turn bright pink. "So can you wait for me?"

Sanzu didn't say a word. He stared at her like she was crazy.

"Bab—" He cut her off with a passionate kiss. She felt the love, as he pulled her closer by the waist. His tongue briefly traced her lower lip before parting.

"I hope this answers your question, sweetheart." He smirked.

She turned bright red, punching his chest lightly.

"Thanks, babe."

- --

- *THREE MONTHS LATER**

"See you soon, sweetheart. Stay safe and love you." Sanzu hugged her tightly, almost cutting off her blood supply.

"Yea, see you soon." She tapped his shoulder to let go.

"Go, you're gonna miss the train."

She stood on her toes, pulling him down by his hair.

"Ow, what are you—" She shut him up with a kiss.

"I'm gonna miss these kisses. And you, of course." She smiled, pulling her luggage.

She'd spent the past couple months practicing killing techniques, making bodies unrecognizable with Sanzu. Shooting moving targets, improving with weapons, and hand-to-hand combat became the norm. Her skills were perfect according to him. It had also been more than a couple months since she'd seen the former Touman members. Her arm and shoulder had healed completely, leaving a scar. Izana's tattoo on her chest, partially hidden by a low-cut black t-shirt.

"Bye, babe. I love you!" She sent a flying kiss from the train doors as they closed. A sense of deja vu— leaving Yokohama for Tokyo nearly a year ago. So much had happened. Now she was leaving Tokyo, making her way back to Yokohama to hunt down the boss of her father's gang, Ryūken.

- --

It was a chilly first night out. Walking out of her temporary apartment under an alias, she began her hunt on Ryūken. Going around bars and shady shops in dark alleyways, trying to gain information. It wasn't long before she found a lead. In one alleyway, she hid behind a large dumpster, listening to two men in matching uniforms.

"Any more information on the death of Kurokawa?" one said.

They were talking about the "mysterious death" of her father. She thought they'd forgotten—it was at least four months ago.

"Other than what we have, nothing. He was definitely murdered. That's a fact."

She pulled out her gun, clicked on the silencer, and removed the safety. Loading bullets, she checked her surroundings. Clear.

"My, my, who are you to look into the death of my father?" She smiled at the men as they watched in terror.

They scrambled—she shot a warning shot. They trembled and didn't move.

"I'd suggest not to move. Could be the end of you, y'know?"

She grabbed one by the arm, holding the gun to his temple. "I only need one source of information, so bye-bye!" She whispered, pulling the trigger. A small sound left the gun, blood pouring. She cast him aside and turned to the other—out cold from fright. Sighing, she dragged him into another alleyway.

Slapping him awake, he finally woke, terror in his eyes.

"Now, you're going to listen very carefully and answer all my questions. Okay?"

He nodded aggressively.

"Why are you asking around about my father's death?"

"T-the boss's right-hand man asked me to. He said he found it highly suspicious."

She laughed to herself. *Of course it's suspicious.*

"Who's your boss?"

"I—I can't tell you that..." He trailed off as the gun got closer. "Eeek! I don't know the boss! I'm just an underling—you'll need someone much closer to the boss!"

She sighed, disappointed. "Where's the hideout?"

"At the bar, xxxx. You've got the bar for normal customers, and if you've got the special password, they'll let you into the back room through the back door. But you'll never see the boss there. His most trusted right-hand man always delivers important news. Meetings are every Wednesday, so tomorrow, around 5 PM."

She nodded, taking mental notes.

"So what's the password?"

He looked around before whispering. "Dragons before swords."

"Okay, thanks, man. I'll give you an opportunity to ask me one question before I kill you. Coz I'm nice." She winked, cocking the gun.

"Why'd you kill him?"

"Who? I've killed many."

"Your dad."

"Oh. He was a hindrance to my life. That's all." No emotion.

"That's it? That's the only reason?"

"Yup."

"How could you do that?!" He blabbered about how inhumane she was.

"Sorry, but I don't have time to listen anymore. Cya!" She pulled the trigger. The bullet passed through his head. He trembled for a couple seconds, coughed up blood, and died.

She sighed, finally grateful it was over. She grabbed the dead guy's uniform and wrapped it in a plastic bag. Whistling through the alleyways, she walked back "home."

Entering the quiet one-room apartment, she crawled onto the couch, flinging the uniform onto the floor. It had been a week since she left Tokyo, and she already missed Sanzu. His company, his smell, his kisses, his lame comebacks. She wanted to call but refrained—she wanted to keep him safe. Even if he could protect himself.

She removed the uniform from the bag. Larger than her size, but whatever. The Ryūken logo was largely imprinted on the back—a dragon with two swords crossed over, graffitied on walls over many alleyways in Yokohama, bringing terror to civilians.

Lost in thought, she didn't realize she was washing the uniform in the sink, removing stains. Hanging it on the small clothesline in the bathroom, she changed out of her black clothes and stared at her body in the mirror. Baji and Izana's tattoos decorated her body. Placing a hand over each, she felt herself become more at ease, relaxing her limbs.

After changing into cleaner clothes, she walked out and set out the small amount of food she had. After eating, she lay on the couch, drifting off, getting ready for tomorrow's meeting.

- --

# CHAPTER SIXTY-THREE

By the time she woke, it was late evening. She ate the leftovers quickly, licking the plate clean. Walking into the bathroom, she grabbed the uniform off the clothesline and slipped it on, buttoning up and zipping the baggy pants. A size too large, but she didn't roll the sleeves—it would give her away.

She grabbed the gun from under the bathroom counter, loaded enough bullets, clicked on the silencer, and slipped it into her pocket. Slipping on her mask to hide her face and scar, she left, locking the door.

- Show time.*

Finding the back door to the bar, she walked up to the buff man standing in front.

"Password?"

"Dragons before swords," she whispered without hesitation.

"Meeting starts in ten minutes. Big news tonight." He opened the door.

She waltzed inside, mesmerized by the sheer number of people—at least 200. She never thought Ryūken would be such a large gang, hosting a popular bar nonetheless. She tried to mingle and seem normal among the larger, taller men. The atmosphere was forced to be cheery. *Something was wrong.*

A man in the Ryūken uniform walked proudly onto the stage and grabbed the microphone.

"Evening, members of Ryūken!" The gang cheered loudly. "We have big news tonight. Firstly, Orochi has announced war upon us! Although this is the first time since the break of the peace arrangement, this will be the war to end this long feud!" More cheering, alcohol thrown in the air.

"Secondly, there have been two mysterious deaths. Both found within a couple meters of each other, with a single bullet to the head. There are two things I can say about these deaths." He held up two fingers.

"One, it was Orochi beginning their assault. Or two, there is a third party."

A long silence.

She wondered about this other gang, Orochi—her father's gang. He'd mentioned her mother and him were part of a peace arrangement. She knew Orochi was her mother's gang. When they parted, the peace treaty supposedly ended. So why was Orochi taking action now?

- Should I get involved in the fight? Or watch until the last minute and kill both leaders?*

She turned back to the speaker.

"—ight is in one month, on April 10th, Friday! Be prepared! Meeting is dismissed. See you all in a week!"

Members rushed out the back door. She hid behind the bar counter, waiting for everyone to leave. Once silence took over, she peeked from the corner. The man from the front was still standing, staring off into a corner. She gained ground slowly, shuffling closer, then pounced.

She tackled him to the ground, pinning his arms under her weight, gun near his head.

"Don't move."

He didn't flinch but understood. She grabbed rope from her back pocket, tied his hands behind his back, made him sit on a nearby chair. Gun still pointed.

"So what do you need from me?" He asked calmly.

His calm demeanor irritated her, giving her unease.

"I need to know what Orochi is, and more about this peace treaty between Ryūken and Orochi. And if you can, more about the boss."

"Ahhh." He breathed out. "You're her, aren't you?"

"What?"

"Daughter to M/N and F/N. The result of this whole peace treaty. Kurokawa Akari."

Her eyes widened. Found out this quickly. She tightened her grip, pointing the gun at his forehead.

"Oooh, you have a silencer too. Good to be prepared." He said. "But not a good idea to kill me now. I have all the information you need. So lower the gun. I'll tell you everything, since it's the least I can do for you."

"Tch." She lowered the gun, placed it in her pocket, but kept aiming from inside.

"So simply put: Orochi and Ryūken made a peace agreement, where your mother and father were chosen randomly. They were forced out of the gang to focus on being a family. You were born, then the accident happened—your mother damaged your face and stormed out. Your father told the boss and rejoined the gang. Your mother moved somewhere no one could contact her. Your father was the only one who knew her location. And stuff happened. The rest you know."

"So why are you waging war now?"

"'Cause your mother died, and Orochi found out. They blamed your father and Ryūken, but we denied it—it wasn't us. When your father died a few days ago, we blamed Orochi. And that's it."

"That's it?"

"Yeah."

"I see. Okay." She understood clearly now. "So why are you so calm? Why are you telling me this?"

"Because you're the only person who can solve this feud between the two gangs. You're the key to thi—"

"Sorry, but I'm not here to solve things. I'm here to end it." She spat out quickly.

He was shocked. "What? You're going to end Orochi and Ryūken? Both?"

"Yea, get you guys off the streets of Yokohama, and maybe I can take over." She smiled.

"I see... okay, cool."

"Don't you care?"

"Nah, not really. I was forced into this gang anyway. If I can leave, I'm happy you'll disband it."

"I'm not disbanding it. I'm eradicating both gangs." She stated simply.

"You'll be a mass murderer."

"Already am. What's another couple hundred deaths gonna do?"

That shut him up.

"Should I kill you or nah?" She mumbled.

"Spare me, and I'll be of good use to you."

"How do I know you'll benefit me?"

"I'm the boss's right-hand man. What more can you ask for?"

She thought.

"Fine." She untied his wrists.

"Akio. Natsuhana Akio." He reached his right hand out. She grabbed it.

"Akari. Kurokawa Akari."

"I'll get all the information you want. Just promise me you won't die somewhere."

"Sure thing." She replied coldly, leaving the back room.

- --

# CHAPTER SIXTY-FOUR

- *THREE WEEKS UNTIL RYŪKEN VS OROCHI**

It had already been a week since that eventful night. She walked to the bar's back door, hood covering her face.

"Dragons before swords." The door swung open. She was an hour early—the back room was empty, except Akio standing at the front of the stage.

"Oh, Akari. I have in—"

"Call me Eiji. That's the alias I'm under. Don't need anyone knowing my real name."

"Oh, my bad. Anyways, I have information. Come with me."

He walked toward the edge of the stage, disappearing behind the large black curtains, then popped his head out.

"There's a dressing room here. No one enters, so don't worry."

She jumped onto the stage and followed him in. An empty room—hardly any furniture. Two chairs. She sat, crossing her arms.

"So what's the news?"

"Another few murders in alleyways, about ten men." He stared at her eyes.

"Akio, the two from last week were me. These ten weren't me, so stop staring at me like that." She looked away.

"Okay, so it was Orochi then. Anyways, I came across Orochi's hideout."

She was shocked. Too quick.

"How?"

"I have a double agent. He's working—"

"How do we know this double agent isn't double-crossing Ryūken?"

"We don't. That's why it's dangerous." He began playing with his fingers.

"Tell me the hideout's location. I'm going."

"And what are you gonna do?"

"Same as here. Sneak in and grab information. Simple." She huffed, looking around.

"Okay, fine. Just don't do anything stupid."

"Yea, yea, I won't."

"Orochi's base is near the coast. The dock where Touman and Tenjiku fought, to be precise. Their meetings are every Monday."

Her eyes widened, memories flooding. "You need to go there b—"

"I know how to get there. Thanks, Akio." She cut him off sharply, got up, and left the dressing room.

Peeking through the curtains, the gang had gathered, turning attention to the stage as Akio walked out.

"Evening, Ryūken! I have some very tragic news." Silence. "We have lost ten men at the hands of Orochi." Whispers. "Take a look at this video we caught!" He pointed to a screen. He glanced at her and nodded.

She jumped off the stage and joined the crowd.

Loud screams and groans from the video. A sole man in a green gang uniform killing ten men with ease. No amateur moves.

"This is the man who killed our men! A man from a gang no other than Orochi!" Akio raised his hands. "Now, I'm not telling you to cower in fear. If anything, don't! If they attack, don't hesitate to fight back. Just do it away from the public eye. We don't need puny policemen menacing with our gang war!"

Loud cheering. "Ryūken! Ryūken! Ryūken!"

"Meeting is dismissed!"

She walked out the back door, making her way home.

- --

- *MONDAY**

She'd thought out a brief plan for tonight's raid. All necessary weapons in her pocket—rope, pistol and silencer, knife, etc.

She took a taxi to a house near the dock and began walking. So many unpleasant memories. Blocking most out, she glanced around and snaked around shipping containers. Dangerous, and she knew it.

A hand clasped over her mouth. Taken by surprise, she grabbed the hand and slammed him over her back onto the floor. She landed a foot on his neck, pressing hard, gun pointed at his head. Terror in his eyes. She noticed the gun in his hand—she'd kicked it away before he could do anything.

Keeping her foot on his neck, she removed his uniform and watched as he could do nothing.

"Sorry~" Smiling, she pulled the trigger. Blood poured out, pooling around his body. Wearing his uniform—olive green with a snake on the back—she waltzed out and joined the Orochi crowd.

A slim man stepped to the front, gazing down from a shipping container. She recognized him instantly as the man who took down the ten men.

"Thanks for gathering!" He exclaimed. "There are only two weeks left until the battle between Orochi and Ryūken! Remember to stay on your toes—they're known to launch dirty tricks. I gave them what they deserved, killing ten of their men!" He smiled, speaking proudly. The Orochi crowd roared. "However, they are beginning to retaliate. Don't hesitate to fight back!"

She pondered whether the man in front was the leader or a mere captain.

"Orochi will come out victorious! So prepare for the main battle in two weeks!" He raised his hand. The gang followed, cheering loudly.

Taking public transport, she headed back home after ditching the Orochi uniform in a nearby dustbin.

Arriving home, she sank onto the couch, arm over her eyes. Two weeks until April 10th, the day of Orochi vs Ryūken. She decided to stay home and visit neither gang until that day.

Akio continued to act normal throughout his gang meetings, fulfilling his job as the boss's right-hand man.

Ryūken's boss's and Orochi's boss's identities still remained a mystery. It didn't matter—they were both going to die either way. She had everything laid out. A plan bound to succeed.

- --

- *APRIL 14TH**

The fateful night of the final battle. Using information from Akio, she made her way to the fight's location—a large warehouse overlooking the ocean. The battle was scheduled for 8 PM, but being there earlier was a good opportunity to find a suitable hiding spot.

She wore black to hide in the dark. A long-sleeve low-cut black shirt clinging to her body, black leggings, black combat boots, and a large black coat to hide her stash of weapons.

It was already dark when she left. She rode the train to the nearest stop, watching her surroundings with sharp eyes. Walking toward the warehouse, there was nobody.

- Strange. Too quiet.*

"What are you doing here, pretty lady?" A voice echoed behind her.

Already on edge, a voice she didn't recognize didn't help. She turned and swung her leg high, hoping to make contact. A strong hand caught her ankle, tightening its grip and tipping her off balance. Not wanting that, she stabilized with her hands and brought her other leg from underneath, attempting a kick to his chin.

He let go before her leg made contact. She flipped acrobatically back onto her feet.

"Who are you?" She demanded, looking at his shady figure.

"You here to watch Orochi vs Ryūken?" He dodged the question.

"I'm here to end them both. I'll ask again. Who ar—"

He burst out laughing. Cackling. Gasping for air, wheezing. After a while, he calmed and looked at her from under his brows.

"You're going to end them? Good luck with that." He chuckled. "Considering you weren't able to land a hit on me, keep dreaming, girly~"

"Who are you?" She repeated, annoyed.

"I'm Orochi's boss." He paused, looking at the warehouse. "See you later~" He smirked, turned, and disappeared.

Disappointed but glad she'd met Orochi's boss, she scouted the warehouse for a hiding spot.

Walking the perimeter was difficult—the warehouse was huge. No wonder it was the best place for a gang battle, with at least 400 people from each gang. She glanced at the shipping containers in the corner, climbing to the top. Peering from the edge, she looked down, then at the rest of the warehouse. Not high enough—she couldn't see everything.

Glancing up, she saw a hook hanging from the ceiling. *Perfect.*

She climbed up and sat on the iron support bar for the roof. The perfect spot. High enough that no one could reach her, high enough to see over the whole warehouse, high enough to shoot down someone if necessary.

She checked the time. 8:05 PM. Ryūken and Orochi began their entrance, walking in from warehouse doors on either side. Two men walked to the middle—one the boss of Orochi she'd fought hours ago, the other presumably Ryūken's boss.

"All-out melee? Or fight between bosses?" A voice called. *Akio.* "All-out melee!" Both bosses exclaimed, walking back to their gangs.

Both gangs cheered, hyping each other up, then clashed. Red and olive green uniforms collided. Like Christmas, except eight months too early.

She continued watching from the metal rod. Many were already passed out. She looked around for Akio. There he was, fighting Orochi's right-hand man. She watched them exchange blows. The Orochi guy's fighting style was unforgettable and unique, but she was mesmerized by Akio's quick, light steps as he evaded blows time and time again. He landed lightning-fast blows with each evasion. He pushed his opponent back, closer to the warehouse wall, until he had him trapped. *This was the moment.*

Akio swung his fist heavily into his opponent's stomach. The man fell, clutching his stomach. Chuckling lightly, she watched Akio land blows until he was out cold.

Satisfied, she looked at Orochi's boss, who was smoking calmly, sitting on a shipping container. Ryūken's boss was on the ground, making his way over, punching, kicking, shoving Orochi's men to get to him.

- Bad move. He's gonna tire himself out before reaching Orochi's boss.*

Better for her. Her goal was to take advantage of the chaos and kill both bosses. Bored with sitting, she removed her gun and the silencer. Pointing to the roof, she shot one bullet. The gunshot echoed. Standing on the rod, she began her announcement.

- --

# CHAPTER SIXTY-FIVE

"Evening, members of Orochi and Ryūken!" Hundreds of eyes looked at her. "I was hoping for some excitement, but this fight hardly gets my blood pumping! Honestly, I'm a little disappointed..." Glares. "I'm only here for one thing! The tearing apart of Orochi and Ryūken!" She pointed her gun at Orochi's boss's head and fired.

The sound reverberated off the walls. Orochi's boss's screams joined in—a peaceful symphony. He slumped to his knees and landed heavily, cigarette burning out.

Triumphant, confused yells from Ryūken—believing she was some savior. Orochi's men glared with disgust.

Ryūken's boss stared, then smiled calmly. She smiled back nicely, scars stretching, then turned the gun to his head and shot without hesitation. No sound from him—just gasping from Ryūken's members. A soft thump as he landed. Blood seeped from both bodies.

"Now that things have finally gotten more interesting, I'm going to give all of you three choices." Murmurs. "Option one! You can continue this pointless fighting with each other. Option two! Place your weapons down and join me. Option three! Take revenge on me for killing your bosses. The choice is yours. I'll give you five minutes!" She set a timer and sat back down, legs swinging, humming her favorite song.

Five minutes ended with a breeze. Her phone went off.

"And what's your decision? Option one! Put your hand up!"

No one did.

"Option two! Joining my gang!"

More than 75% raised their hands.

"Oh, you guys are such sweethearts~" She clasped her hands, smiling widely. "First job! Can you form a large circle for me? And people who chose option three? Gather in the middle."

They hesitated but complied, forming a perfect circle, pushing those who didn't raise their hands into the middle.

"Perfect!" She laughed, climbing down from the metal rod, sliding down the hook, hopping onto the shipping container. She walked toward the circle, found Akio, and handed him her gun and ammo. She pulled out her knife, gripping it tightly.

"Well, doesn't this bring back memories?" She whispered, remembering Valhalla.

"My name is Eiji. Those who want to take revenge—this is your one opportunity. Don't hold back! Oh, and if you're firm about taking revenge, come at me with the intent to kill. Otherwise it'll end up worse for you." She chuckled, tilting her head to the ceiling. "And those of you forming the circle, this is your opportunity to watch the strength of your new boss!"

The men looked on in shock. The circle began chanting her name.

She glanced at Akio and nodded.

"Let the fight between Eiji and the revengers begin!" Akio exclaimed.

The men in the circle roared, raring, readying weapons—knives, swords, metal poles, ropes, batons, everything.

At least twenty-five men, all armed. Not an issue.

They charged. She skillfully evaded each attack. Gaining distance, she dropped to the floor, spinning her legs, tripping them. A couple stepped back, but many fell. Using the opportunity, she aimed to kill the ones still standing.

She jumped up, gripping the knife tighter, running swiftly. A man in the corner—she avoided his stabbing motion, grabbed his outstretched arm, and twisted it behind his back. Another man came with a knife— she used the man she was holding as a shield, watching him groan as a fellow teammate stabbed him. Casting him aside, she jabbed the attacker's chin with a fist, sending him flying. Chasing, she sent a quick stab to his abdomen. He slumped, clutching the wound, blood pouring. The others watched.

Three more charged. She evaded over and over. They became annoyed. She dodged another stabbing motion, but it caught her shirt, ripping the front open a little, revealing Izana's tattoo.

"Sorry, but I'm getting tired." She took a deep breath. Her heart rate went through the roof. "I'm gonna get serious now."

- She lost herself to the darkness.*

- --

By the time she came back, only one man remained in the circle, trembling in fear. He'd watched her slaughter the others with ease.

"Please! Spare me!" He whimpered.

"You do realize this decision is on you?" She tapped her finger against her waist, walking toward him.

"Y-yes. I-I'm aware, and it was a mistake on my behalf, so please, spare me!"

"Fine. You can be the sacrifice!"

"Sacrifice? What am I supposed to do?"

"Nothing. Just remain here with all the bodies and take the blame for me. That's all!" She smiled creepily. "If you confess," she paused, staring deep into his eyes from under her eyebrows, "I'm coming after your whole bloodline."

He shivered, nodding over and over.

"Now, for the rest of you! Welcome to my gang!" Cheering erupted, chanting her name. She raised her hand, silencing them.

"Firstly, I have news. One: I am going to decide on a gang name. Two: meetings will be held weekly on Monday nights at the bar of Ryūken. Make sure you enter from the back door. Ryūken members, let the members of Orochi know where the bar is."

"Other than that, I am highly aware that many of you are adults, and I am a mere teenager. But I expect you all to treat each other with the same respect you were to treat me with. Follow me and we will take over all of Yokohama! I will come up with a gang name by next Monday, so I expect you all to be there. You guys can head home now!"

"Have a goodnight, President!" They bowed.

She smiled, then turned to the sacrifice.

"Thank you for your hard work, sacrifice!" She dialed the police using Orochi's boss's phone, imitating a scared young girl.

"H-hello? I heard some gunshots from the warehouse at xxxx. Please come and check it out." She abruptly ended the call and tossed the phone to the sacrifice.

"I'll come visit you in jail, okay?" She smirked, walking out with Akio.

# CHAPTER SIXTY-SIX

Waking up the next morning was tiring. A pounding headache. The ceiling on the floor—everything upside down. Normal the day after losing herself. Yesterday was the worst, everything still new. It had been about two months since she left Tokyo, and she was growing to miss Sanzu even more. But it would be another couple months before she saw him again.

Holding her head, she rose, walked to the kitchen, grabbed a banana from the empty fridge, sat on the couch, and switched on the TV. Yesterday's incident was already on the news—police coverage live at the scene. The accused was the sacrifice. The video of him being led into the police car showed sheer terror in his eyes. Not from the police—from her. His trembling hands, unable to walk properly. He was forced into the car and driven off. The news moved to Tokyo. She switched off the TV.

Stuck at home, she tried to think of a suitable new gang name.

- Ryūken. Dragons and swords.*

- Orochi. Snake.*

Hours passed, words spinning. Both gangs had broken ties with their bosses to join her. A lightbulb.

- Ashinuke.* The act of breaking one's ties with something.

Perfect. The name fit. Now a logo.

She took a quick breather, left, and headed to the nearest park. She sat on the swingset, swinging slowly, kicking the dirt. She couldn't get the logo out of her head. Then it came.

Both Ryūken and Orochi had broken ties, only to unify under her rule. They had unified—she could combine their logos!

A dragon with a more snake-like body, swords on its back. Perfect.

She ran home, took out a pen and paper, and sketched the design. Satisfied, she placed her phone over the sheet and hopped onto the couch, rocking back and forth, thinking about the future.

Yokohama was huge. Orochi and Ryūken had split the land evenly. Now that news of the two biggest gangs disappearing had been broadcasted nationally, smaller gangs would try to take over. Fights for the Yokohama area had restarted. Time for her—boss of Ashinuke—to take back the area to its former glory and better.

She planned divisions like Mikey had done with Touman, setting them in charge of different areas to make the job easier. The meeting area—the bar—was already in the center. Ryūken's boss owned the bar and had left the property to his son—none other than Akio. She'd talked to Akio about it, but he didn't care much about his father's death. She appointed him right-hand man, since he was there from the start. Orochi's boss's right-hand man, Daisuke, would be left-hand man. There was sour tension between Akio and Daisuke, but she decided to make them resolve it. Taking back Yokohama would be a breeze, right?

She scribbled everything down so she wouldn't forget. Just needed to take care of her identity. Eiji would be her alias. However, the gang members all knew her real name—a problem she couldn't escape. Her potential downfall.

Snuggling into the couch, she played songs from her playlist, drifting off.

- --

"Evening, members of Orochi and Ryūken!" Loud cheers. "Firstly, our new gang name. I am pleased to announce I have come up with one! Ashinuke! I know well the negative connotation this word holds, but we will take it to another level!" Murmurs, then chanting of the new name.

"I'm glad you're pleased. For the logo, I have merged the two logos—a snake-like dragon with swords. All in favor, raise your hands!" All hands raised.

"Awesome! And for more news. Can I call up Akio Natsuhana and Daisuke Fuyukawa to the stage!"

The men looked around. The two made their way through the crowd onto the stage.

"Brief introduction, please." She passed the microphone to Daisuke first.

"Umm, I'm Fuyukawa Daisuke, right-hand man to the boss of Orochi. Pleased to join under Akari and Ashinuke." A small round of applause. He passed the microphone to Akio, nervously turning away.

"Evening, everyone. I'm Natsuhana Akio, current owner of this bar, son and right-hand man of the boss of Ryūken." Controversy and gossip—his father killed by her, and whether he despised her. "I pledge my loyalty to Akari and Ashinuke until this gang is over, if it ever does!" A long round of applause. He handed the microphone back.

"Uhh, look. I'm very much aware of my situation—a teenager leading a gang of adults—but for now, this is what's going on. The whole of Yokohama has heard the news of Orochi and Ryūken disappearing after the fight. Smaller gangs who were suppressed by the two major gangs may join forces to rule over the now 'rulerless' Yokohama. However, we cannot let this happen! As the leader of Ashinuke, we will take back the whole of Yokohama! We will rule over this area! That is our main goal for the time being." Cheers, drinks in the air, glass cups clicking.

"We will slowly get rid of the other gangs in Yokohama. It will be a slow, step-by-step process, but we will get there!" Roars. "This bar, run under Akio, will be our home base. If you ever need me, Akio, or Daisuke, we will be here."

She grabbed her uniform from behind the curtains—black, with the white Ashinuke logo on the back, title of her role on the breast pocket, "Ashinuke" in bold on both sleeves. She shoved her arms through. A little larger than expected, fingers hidden by the sleeves. She grabbed two more, gave them to Akio and Daisuke.

"Make sure you attend the weekly meetings! Every Monday from 6 PM, here. I will place guards at the back door. The password is 'Unity of broken ties.' See you all next week!"

Men flooded out. The back room was finally quiet, leaving only the three of them. She sighed, flopped onto the stage, staring at the ceiling.

"You did well for your first time." Akio patted her head.

"Ahaha, thanks, Akio. Oh, yea, nearly forgot. Can you two resolve your tensions, please? I have a feeling you two will be great friends if you ignore the past. It may be hard, but the two of you working together as friends and colleagues will be the greatest asset to me."

They looked at her, then at each other. Surprisingly, Daisuke made the move.

"Fuyukawa Daisuke. Pleased to be your colleague." He stretched his hand out, smiling.

Akio hesitated but accepted. "Natsukawa Akio. Likewise."

"Alright, perfect!" She sat up, brushing dust from her uniform.

"We have some work to do," Akio announced out of the blue.

"What? Already...?" She whined.

"Hey, hey. You brought this on yourself by being gang president." Daisuke snickered.

Sighing, she admitted defeat. "So what's the work?"

"Just as you predicted, smaller gangs from all around the districts have joined forces. At least four gangs, comprising 250 men each, taking over parts of Yokohama."

She laughed as they stared.

"Now this will be interesting. Daisuke, what do you think?"

"Nothing we can't handle." He shrugged.

A silence before she spoke. "What do you think of assassination missions?"

They looked at each other, then back at her.

"If it means we'll have control of Yokohama by the end, of course we'll join you," Daisuke announced, bowing.

"What he said." Akio jabbed a finger at Daisuke, following suit, bowing his head.

- --

# CHAPTER SIXTY-SEVEN

Sharing her phone number with Akio and Daisuke, she went home after the meeting. Pitch black outside, empty streets. Still wearing her Ashinuke uniform, she walked home, taking the shortest route—through dark alleyways. As a teenage girl, everyone knew that was dangerous. She was an exception. No normal teenager carried a gun with a silencer or ruled a gang of adults.

Turning a sharp corner into a narrow alleyway, she was confronted by two large men—bulky with muscles, just a bunch of human meat.

"Where you going, girly?"

"Interested in going out to eat with us?" They reached for her shoulder.

She smacked their hand away, glaring. "Don't touch me, you freaks."

Annoyed now—she'd rejected their "nice" offer.

"Who do you think you are?" One grabbed her shoulder tightly, fingers digging in.

The other noticed her gang jacket. "Boyfriend's gang jacket? Ashinuke?" He roared laughing. "Never heard of 'em."

She gripped the man's arm. Furious—he hadn't listened to her command. "I said, don't fucking touch me!" She threw him over her back. Heavy, but no trouble. He landed with a heavy thud. Nearby stray animals felt the vibration and ran.

Not giving him a moment, she dropped her heel into his stomach, lifted, and slammed it down onto his face. The other man stared in shock, backing away.

"Since you think you know so much about gangs, tell me." She walked closer, menacing. "What gang are you in?"

He kept backing up, not realizing he was cornering himself. "Well?"

"Bulldogs." He answered calmly. "Who are you? How come I've never heard of Ashinuke until now?"

The moon shone through the clouds, giving the alleyway light. He freaked out more seeing the scar at the corners of her mouth stretch as she smiled.

"I'm the one asking questions here." She leaned closer to his face. "What area of Yokohama are you currently occupying?"

"The northern part."

"I see." She stood straight, glancing at the other guy, still out cold. "I have a small favor for you."

He nodded.

"I'll let you go alive today. Only because I'm too tired to kill you. So go back to your area and tell the Bulldogs' boss that the gang Ashinuke occupies central Yokohama. Cool?"

He nodded again.

"Also, take your friend home. Don't wanna see either of you here again—otherwise, consider it war." She pointed to the passed-out friend.

"Who are you? Why do you talk like you are the bigshot of Ashinuke?" He walked over to his friend.

She stared and laughed. His eyes widened as he lifted his friend onto his shoulder. Turning around, she faced him once more.

"Oh. I thought you would've gotten the idea by now." She stopped laughing and shot him a toothy grin. "I'm the boss of Ashinuke, Eiji."

She disappeared into the darkness, leaving the musclehead and his friend alone.

- --

She finally made it home. Kicked off her shoes, crashed onto the couch.

- Bulldogs currently own the north. Ashinuke owns the center. I know Red Ace owns the West. South and

East remain a mystery.*

She pulled her phone from her back pocket and texted the group chat—her, Akio, and Daisuke.

- *Akari:**

- Hey, I need you to investigate the two gangs occupying the South and East.*

- *Akio:**

- Sure, I'll take the South.*

- *Daisuke:**

- I'll take the East.*

- What about the other two?*

- *Akari:**

- I've already got the names. North is the Bulldogs. West is the Red Ace. I just need the names of the

other two gangs. Try not to get caught.*

- BTW, I met with two Bulldogs members tonight. They tried to hit on me, and I taught them what they

deserved.*

- *Daisuke:**

- You didn't kill them, did you?*

- *Akari:**

- No, I let them go. I told them to tell their boss that Ashinuke owns central Yokohama.*

- *Akio:**

- Finally, a wise move from Akari.*

- *Akari:**

- Hey!*

- *Daisuke:**

- Pfft.*

- *Akari:**

- Glad you guys find this funny. Oh, yea, I'm under the alias Eiji as the boss of Ashinuke.*

- *Akio:**

- Kk.*

- *Daisuke:**

- Teenagers need a lot of sleep. Go to bed. It's already late.*

- *Akari:**

- Tch, fine. Goodnight. Make sure to grab the information. Meet you both at the bar tomorrow at 6 PM

for info sharing.*

- *Akio:**

- Got it. G'night.*

- *Daisuke:**

- Sure. Sleep well.*

Annoyed at being treated like a child, she threw her phone on the floor, placed her arm over her eyes, and breathed out deeply, eyes closing slowly.

- --

Waking up was a struggle. Subtle neck pain from sleeping on the couch in a weird position. She sat up, staring at the kitchen. A figure walking through—familiar long hair.

- Sanzu?*

She rubbed her eyes. No one. Just her eyes playing tricks. What a way to start the morning.

She checked her phone—11:25 AM, two notifications.

- *Daisuke:**

- Reminder: Meeting at 6 PM to discuss information about the gangs of Yokohama.*

- *Akio:**

- Thanks for the unnecessary reminder :P*

She snickered and got up to eat brunch.

She spent the rest of the day cleaning the messy house—dirty clothes, food containers. She cleaned herself up, taking a long-awaited relaxing bath.

Sinking into the bathtub, hot water running over her body, absorbed into her skin, warm from the core outward. She leaned her head back to the edge, staring at the ceiling and condensed water droplets. They slowly fell, one by one. She kept her eye on one—it landed on Izana's hanafuda tattoo, sending shivers down her spine. Ice cold. She watched it roll down her breast and back into the water. Her eyes trailed to the feather on her side. She ran her finger over it, briefly feeling the stab scar underneath.

She hopped out, sat on the stool, grabbed the showerhead, and washed her body and hair with sweetsmelling soap. Then tied her hair up loosely and sank back into the tub.

An alarm from her phone—5:30 PM. Spending any longer and she'd be late. She rushed out, drained the water, changed into clean black clothing, wearing her gang uniform over her shirt. Finishing the last clasp on her black boots, she tied her hair half-up, half-down, grabbed her phone, and left.

Her hair had gotten quite long—middle of her back. Time for a haircut. Neaten the wolf cut.

Locking the door, she walked down the stairs to the bar.

- --

Entering the back door with ease, she sat on a stool at the bar in the very back. The building was welldesigned—credit to Akio's father. The front was a popular bar, well-known throughout Yokohama. Heavy beat music echoed through bones, flashing lights. The bar and bartenders were at the back, always filled with customers. Men in posh suits or casual wear, women in revealing dresses—common, as this bar was also known for one-night stands. Nothing illegal about the bar, a relief.

But the bar was two-sided. A door in the very corner, hidden between rows of drinks. Many customers were unaware, sometimes the bartender hid into it. This door connected the backroom to the front. Strictly for the bartender. The backroom could only be entered via the back door—accessed by the dark alleyway people avoided, or the bartender's door. Occasionally, drunk people wandered through, but they'd never figured out the back door led to the secret room. The secret room was the meeting place of Ashinuke.

She rang the small bell, which connected to the front bar, signaling the bartender. A small creaking sound—the bartender appeared.

"Evening, Miss Akari. What would you like tonight?"

An old man, grey moustache curling at the ends, round glasses, bushy eyebrows, piercing blue eyes— uncommon in Japan.

"Can I please have a—"

"Orange juice for her, please, John." Daisuke cut her off.

"Heyyyy," she whined.

"You're underage. You shouldn't be drinking yet."

The door opened, revealing Akio.

"Just in time," Akio mumbled.

"Fineeee." She rolled her eyes as Daisuke snickered, nodding at John.

"Oh, John. I have a favor to ask."

"Yes, Miss Akari?"

"Firstly, you can drop the 'Miss.'" She smiled. "I would like you to teach me the arts of bartending."

"Handling the drinks to customers, or making them?"

"Both, if possible."

"Hey, I don't know if that's a smart move," Daisuke began. "There's a lot of—"

"Think about it. No one would suspect the boss of Ashinuke working in a bar. And think about the information I could gain. This bar is in the center of Yokohama, which other gangs are slowly starting to understand belongs to Ashinuke. But that doesn't stop other gang members from disguising themselves to have a drink in one of the most popular bars in the city." She casually explained.

"Not a bad idea," Akio started. "It could be our advantage. Daisuke, she's strong enough to take care of herself. Not to mention she is the boss of Ashinuke—I think she'll be fine."

Daisuke pondered, head in hands. He raised his head, looking her dead in the eyes. "Fine. Just promise me you won't drink any alcohol until you're at least twenty."

"Awww, fineee." John passed her a tall glass of orange juice. "Thanks, John. So when can I start?"

"How's tomorrow morning from 11 AM? The bar doesn't open until 4:30 PM, so plenty of time to learn the basics." John watched her drink.

"Okay!" She smiled widely, bringing smiles to John, Akio, and Daisuke as well.

"John, I'll take a beer," Akio spoke.

"Make that two," Daisuke announced.

"So did you find anything?" She asked the men on either side.

They nodded.

"The East is occupied by the Fangs." Daisuke took a sip of beer. "They're a mess right now—two smaller gangs just joined hands with them. I'd say we attack once they're fully together. Makes our job easier."

"I see. And you, Akio?"

"The South is occupied by the Kurogumo, or Black Spiders. The most violent and unpredictable of the four." Akio placed his glass down.

"Which one first?" She questioned. "The Fangs are too disorganized, so if we assassinate the boss, nothing good will come of it. The Bulldogs are highly aware of our existence, so I doubt they'll do much harm."

"Kurogumo," Daisuke uttered, gripping his glass tightly, knuckles white.

"You know them, Daisuke?" Akio asked.

"Not personally, but I've heard of the things they've done. Torture, rape, prostitution, drug trafficking, just to name a few."

"Kurogumo it is, then." She placed her empty glass down. "Can you two investigate more about them tomorrow while I learn from John?"

"Of course," Daisuke muttered.

"Sure thing, boss!" Akio finished his beer.

"Alright! Meet here at the same time tomorrow to discuss." She hopped down.

"I need to go back to help the main side, so I'll take my leave. See you all tomorrow." John exited through the small door.

"I've got work since I'm managing this business now." Akio climbed onto the stage. "The office is up the stairs behind the curtain, so if you need me, I'll be there."

"We should go home too." Daisuke opened the back door. She followed, looking around before walking out the alleyway.

They walked onto the busy main street in silence.

"I live this way. See you tomorrow at six!" She walked in the opposite direction.

"See you tomorrow. Have a goodnight." He bowed and turned.

# CHAPTER SIXTY-EIGHT

The ear-piercing alarm woke her at 10 AM. Early for her. Ever since moving back to Yokohama, most work had been late evening, leaving plenty of time to sleep in. Groaning, she rolled off the bed, landing with a heavy thud. She stared at the ceiling, eyes following every nook and cranny until her eyesight blurred. She rubbed her eyes, sat up, nearly bumping her head on the bedside table, and stood slowly, stretching and screaming a little.

She slid open the wardrobe. Boring—most clothes black. Black long-sleeve low-cut shirts, black sweatpants, black socks, black undergarments. Occasionally colored shirts, but they were at the bottom, never touched.

Today she felt excited. She dug around and pulled out a black pencil skirt and a white blouse. Set them aside, walked to the bathroom, washed her face, and did her hair to a presentable extent. A loose bun, half-up half-down, clipped the loose strands, and got dressed. The pencil skirt reached mid-thigh, tightly hugging her legs, shaping her body. She tucked in the white blouse and pulled on combat boots. Yes, they didn't go with the outfit, but it was the only pair she had. She pulled the Ashinuke jacket from a hanger and slipped it over her shoulders. Sliding the mask over her ears, covering her mouth and scar, she slipped her phone into the jacket pocket, grabbed a banana, and left, locking the door.

- --

She pushed the doors of the bar—a small bell rang.

"Sorry, we're not ope—. Oh, morning, Akari." John looked up from cleaning the wooden floors, smiling. "Just in time. I was about to set out the glasses."

He put the broom aside and walked to the bar counter, setting out glasses. She grabbed the broom, finished his job, created a pile of dust and broken glass, and swept it into the bin. She placed the broom aside and sat on the stool, watching John set out different types of glass cups.

"Thanks for cleaning up." John took out bottles from the wall. "That's one thing out of the way."

"No problem. That's another thing I needed to do if I was to work here. Working here means cleaning as well. They come hand in hand." She smiled.

"Okay, so firstly, we're going to start with the basic drinks. First up, the simple martini." John pushed the triangular glass forward. "Make sure to remember the glass and the drinks they go with. It'll make your job easier." She nodded, watching intently. "For the martini, you'll need the ratio for gin and dry vermouth—4:1, gin to vermouth. Place it in the metal shaker with about three small ice cubes, and shake."

She watched as John demonstrated, the loud sounds of ice breaking apart overwhelming the quiet bar.

"You then strain the liquid, removing any ice particles." John did this with ease, opening the shaker and carefully pouring it into the triangular glass. "Then place the green olive into the drink, and that's it. The basic martini!" He pushed the glass forward.

She picked it up, holding it up to the dim light. The clear, water-like liquid with a strong alcoholic smell filled her nose. She passed it back.

"I promised Daisuke, so I won't drink."

She hopped off the stool and walked around to the other side of the counter. Placing her jacket aside, she followed John's instructions—correct glass, correct ratio, three small ice cubes. Mixing, she glanced at John, who had taken a seat on the stool, patiently watching. She suddenly felt nervous, extremely pressured to do a good job. Smiling to herself, she poured carefully into the martini glass, straining any ice particles.

"Here you go, John." She pushed the glass forward.

He gave her a small glance, then looked at the glass. She bent over the counter, almost seductively, placing a green olive into the glass.

He chuckled. "I'd almost thought you'd forget the green olive."

"Of course not. All part of my charm!" She placed her hands on her hips, looking away proudly.

John placed the glass to his lips and slowly drank. His eyes widened. He looked back at her in shock.

"For your first time, this is almost perfect. You sure you've never done this before?"

"Nope!" A pause. "Almost perfect? What was wrong?"

"Something minor—there was a small ice piece in it. Strain it a little more carefully next time. Good job, though!" He gave her a thumbs up, smiling.

"Yesss!" She raised her hands.

"Alright. Next one is the Bloody Mary." John passed the martini glass back and walked around to the counter as she took his spot.

The rest of the day continued—she quickly learned each drink. So many to learn, many more to go, but she gobbled up the information quickly. It wasn't long before 4:30 PM arrived, signaling opening hours.

"The easiest drink is the beer. Just place the glass under the mouth of the tap and pull the lever. The beer should pour out and fill the glass to the faint line you can see here." John pointed to the line where the pattern on the glass ended. "The most important thing is to listen to the customer about which brand of beer they want. If they don't specify, you can pick, but I'd recommend Asahi."

She looked at the tap labeled Asahi and began to pour until the liquid reached the line. The froth rose to the brim, then slowly fell, the liquid reaching the line perfectly.

"Perfect job, Akari!" John looked at the glass. The main door opened—a slim, well-dressed woman. John quickly removed your gang jacket from the counter and shoved it under the bar. He stood next to you.

"How may I help you today, ma'am?" He bowed. You copied, eyes on your shoes.

"I'd like a basic martini for today. Just one will do, John." She sat on the stool, folding her coat onto her lap. "Oh, new face?" She eyed your facial features—only your eyes, but you felt threatened.

"Evening. I just started learning today under John. I'm Hana, glad to be at your service." You bowed again. You felt John's stare at the mention of another alias.

"I think Hana here should make your martini, ma'am." John's eyebrows wiggled.

"Very well, then, Hana. Surprise me with your work."

You nodded and got to work. Triangular glass, perfect ratio, metal shaker, three ice cubes. Mixing was loud, but the two paid no attention. The door opened—more faces. John tended to their needs while you strained the mix into the glass. You pushed it forward, sliding in the green olive. She accepted, raised it to her lips, drinking with delicacy.

"My, this is superb." She lowered the glass. "John!"

"Yes, ma'am?"

"Have you tried her martini?"

"Yes, of course. What do you think?"

"It's perfect. Just like yours!" She stood, unfolding her coat, removing her wallet, paying John, and walking over to you, passing small change.

"Keep working hard, Hana. I can't wait to see you improve!" She winked and headed to the door.

You looked down at your hand—two five-hundred-yen coins. (Approx. $10.) You quickly lowered your head, placing your hands behind your back, bowing.

"Thank you, ma'am! See you again soon and thank you for visiting the xxxx bar!" You heard her chuckle as the door closed.

"Good start, don't you think?" John whispered.

You nodded with excitement.

"What do I do with this?" You showed him the tip.

"Keep it. We got paid for the drink. Keep the tip for yourself." He smiled and walked to the other side to serve other customers.

A faint ding from somewhere.

"What's that?" you asked.

"Take the small door in the wall. It should be Akio and Daisuke asking me to come over. You can go and take my spot." He grinned. "Don't forget your jacket."

You nodded, grabbed your jacket from under the counter, and shuffled to the edge of the bar's counter. Standing, you watched the rest of the customers paying attention to John. You quickly opened the door and walked through the short corridor to the other door.

- That door needs to be hidden better.*

# CHAPTER SIXTY-NINE

Opening the door on the other side, Akio and Daisuke were surprised to see you entering through the bartender's door.

"Ohh, Akari. What a surprise!"

"I go by the name Hana when bartending now."

"Another alias? Geez. You're going to get us mixed up soon." Daisuke mumbled as you and Akio laughed.

"Well, sorry about that." You removed your mask, finally able to breathe. "So how was the information seeking about Kurogumo?"

"I actually went to their area today," Daisuke muttered quietly.

"What!?" Akio and you exclaimed.

Daisuke covered his ears.

"I said—"

"We both know what you said, Daisuke." Akio cut him off. "Moreover, what made you go there? It's dangerous to trespass another gang's land! Especially Kurogumo!"

"What he said." You pointed at Akio. You walked over to the beer taps and slowly filled two glasses to the line, passing them to Akio and Daisuke. "So did you find anything, since you already went?"

"I—" Daisuke paused. "I came across their boss today. By chance."

Your eyes widened.

"What the fuck?" Akio exclaimed. "How? What did they—"

"Okay, tell us what happened. Akio, please try to stay calm."

"My bad." Akio grabbed his beer and took a long sip.

"So I went to the South to grab information, but I couldn't find anything. Everything was normal—not a single person out of place. I was walking along the main road when I heard yelling from a nearby alleyway. I went to the building next to it, headed to the rooftop, and listened. The guy getting bashed by the so-called boss was a double agent who is also a member of the Bulldogs." Daisuke said.

You understood where he was going.

"So the news of Ashinuke has now reached Kurogumo as well," you said, sighing. Daisuke nodded.

"The boss of Kurogumo heard the news of the Bulldogs being threatened by the boss of Ashinuke after trespassing our land. The boss of Kurogumo is fuming that central Yokohama has been taken over. He was muttering some words after that, and I left. It can be assumed that Kurogumo is going to come after us, and the land here." Daisuke finished.

"So what'd the boss of Kurogumo look like?" Akio asked, finishing his beer.

"Want another?" you asked. Both glasses were empty.

"Sure," Daisuke answered for both. You grabbed the glasses and refilled while listening.

"You can't miss him. He had the Black Spider logo on the back of their white gang uniform. He's built a little like Akio—lean and muscular. He won't hesitate to kill anyone, so be on guard."

You passed the glasses and laughed.

"He sounds just like the male version of me."

"What part of that sounds like you?" Akio snickered.

"The 'won't hesitate to kill anyone' bit." You stated. Daisuke and Akio just stared at you, then nodded. "Please don't look at me like that. You know I only kill when I need to."

"Yea, that's the difference between the two of you. He kills for fun," Daisuke said glumly.

"Oh."

A small silence, broken by Akio downing his beer.

"Anyway, tomorrow is our weekly gang meeting, so we'll discuss everything with them. They should have some news about the other gangs while they're here." The other two nodded.

"Alright then, that's good," Akio said.

"By the way, Akari." Daisuke stuttered.

"Hmm?"

"Hope you haven't been drinking any alcohol yet."

You just stared at him.

"You made me promise not to drink alcohol until I'm twenty. So I'm not going to." You crossed your arms and looked away.

"Well, that's good. How's bartending?"

"It's actually really fun! I've learned so much from John! I already served my first customer today, and she said my martini was perfect!" You excitedly relived the moment. You continued talking about your day when a familiar sound came through.

"Oh, seems like John wants you back," Akio laughed.

"I gotta go back now, I guess. See you tomorrow evening at the meeting!" You said.

"Yup, see you!" Daisuke answered.

They waved as you exited through the bartender's door. Quickly pulling your mask on, you opened the door to the other side. You were shocked to see the number of people sitting and chatting, with John rushing back and forth. Waitresses swiftly walked past, grabbing newly made drinks.

"Ahh, perfect timing, Hana." John walked over. "Can you make five plain Martinis, three Bloody Marys, and four Kamikazes? You learned them all today, so you'll be fine. The recipes are on the wall behind you if you need to look."

You nodded and got to work.

A couple hours later, you'd completed all the drinks John asked for, plus the drinks other customers had asked for while you were making the other twelve. It was frantic—rushing back and forth, grabbing the necessary equipment and liquids. But you'd done each and every drink perfectly, earning many wonderful comments. The tips accumulated slowly. By the time all customers had left, it was nearing midnight.

"You should go home now, Hana." John tapped your back.

You nodded. "I'll see you tomorrow at 4:30 PM."

"Yes, of course!" He exclaimed.

You bowed, grabbed your gang jacket, and left, heading home, tired from the eventful day.
