# CHAPTER SEVENTY

You arrived a little earlier—4:00 PM. Shuffling through the main doors, you entered the bar, placing your gang jacket under the counter.

"Good afternoon, Akari." John was sweeping again.

"Afternoon!" You walked around the counter. "Oh, John, I think it'll be better if we hide the door to the back room a little better—with a black blind or something."

John stared at the door, hands on his hips, under his chin. "Hmm, yea, I'll take it into consideration. The bar is generally dark, so not many people see the door either way."

You nodded in agreement. "I just think it's still too visible. Considering this is a gang hideout, we should be taking utmost precaution."

You made your way back to the bar counter as the main door opened—a couple.

"Good afternoon, what would you like to order today?"

They waltzed slowly toward the stools and sat. They pondered the list of drinks, pointing to their chosen drink.

"Of course. It'll be ready soon!" You prepared their drinks energetically. More customers entered, sitting in available stools and other tables. John took their orders, letting you concentrate on perfecting the couple's drinks. You handed them over with a small smile, then took more orders.

As time went on, the bar became more crowded. Colored lights switched on, music overwhelming loud. You rushed back and forth, making multiple drinks and handing them to customers or Yui to give to the tables. John tapped at his watch, holding up six fingers. It was 6 PM—time for the weekly gang meeting.

The bell went off from the other room. Many customers ignored it, thinking it was part of the music. You served the last drink, grabbed your jacket from under the bar, and walked around the counter. You shuffled toward the bottle cabinet, quickly opened the door, walked in, and closed it behind you.

Opening the door on the other side, you were amused by the smiling faces all wearing their Ashinuke uniforms, which had finally arrived. The orders flooded in instantly, getting remarks about a new, younglooking female bartender. You shook your head with disappointment and smiled nicely, removing your face mask.

Many men sitting on the stools were gobsmacked, jaws falling.

"B-boss?"

"W-what!"

One dropped a glass cup, smashing it and bringing attention.

"My, my! No need for such surprise!" You clapped, walking toward the broom and mop. You cleaned up, returned the equipment, and walked onto the stage.

"Evening, members of Ashinuke!" The room was silent in shock. "I am currently working here as Hana, a new bartender, so pleased to be at your service." You took a bow. Some members began to clap—soon a thunderous round of applause.

"Anyways, enough of me being a bartender! As the boss of Ashinuke, there's major news. News of us taking control of central Yokohama has reached the gangs of Kurogumo and Bulldogs, so stay on your toes from any attacks. I assume it won't be long before the other two gangs take notice. I want you all to protect yourselves and your—"

You were cut off by murmurs at the back door.

The crowd split, revealing an Ashinuke member crawling on the floor, wounded. Bruises covered his body, blood pouring from his mouth. You hopped down and rushed over, carrying him onto the stage, ushering Daisuke to bring a first aid box.

The injured man declined, pointing to the vein at his elbow with a shaky hand.

"They drugged me with a new substance. I was their test subject for days. I'm gonna die soon, so don't bother with first aid." He panted heavily.

You gripped his hand. "Who's 'they'?"

"Kurogumo. They're indeed despicable. You need to—" He coughed out blood, running down his chin, staining his uniform. He took a deep breath. "They only let me go, half on the brink of death, to give you

a message. The boss of Kurogumo ordered me to tell you that he was waiting for you at the docks of the Kantou incident in a week's time."

His eyes grew darker. You reached to close his eyelids softly. He leaned in close, whispering.

"Ashinuke forever. Take back Yokohama for me, for us—"

He drew his last breath. You knew.

You motioned Daisuke and Akio over.

"He's just resting," you announced, hiding your pained expression. "I'm going to go after Kurogumo first before any other gang. Make sure you all protect yourselves and each other."

Loud roars erupted, not realizing one of their own had fallen.

You raised your fist. "ASHINUKE WILL COME OUT VICTORIOUS!"

The rest followed, grabbing their uniforms, raising their fists.

"ASHINUKE WILL COME OUT VICTORIOUS!"

- --

After the meeting, members continued drinking and partying. You talked with Daisuke and Akio.

"I think I should go," you mumbled.

"Whatever your decision, we're both coming with you." Daisuke said. Akio nodded.

"I have a plan. I don't know if it'll work on the boss of Kurogumo, but it's worth a shot."

"Giving it a shot equals risking your life," Akio said, worried.

"A young girl like me leading a large gang is already me risking my life," you snapped back.

"So what's the plan?" Daisuke asked.

You whispered the plan. Daisuke and Akio smirked.

"That'll definitely work," Akio announced, smiling widely.

"Good. It needs to work." You exhaled, tired.

"What are you gonna do with their men afterward?" Akio asked.

"They can join, but I'll be keeping a close eye on them." They hummed.

"What are we gonna do with him?" Akio jabbed his thumb toward the stage curtains.

"Oh, um. I think it's appropriate if—"

"I'll take care of it," Daisuke cut you off, giving a reassuring look.

"Okay, thanks." You gave a small smile.

You continued the night, serving drinks to gang members, getting comments—both concerned and enthusiastically hyping you up. Grateful, you kept serving until they were content, leaving only when nearly wasted. The bell rang again—another hour or two on the other side.

You walked to the back door, locked the latch, swept the floors quickly, cleaned the used glasses, and left. Opening the secret door, you removed your jacket, folded it neatly over your forearm, disguising it as a large towel. You pulled the door open, sneaking into the bar area carefully, trying not to get spotted.

You worked tirelessly for another two hours until John closed, ushering the wasted people out.

"Phew." You wiped sweat from your hairline, relieved the long day was finally over.

"Well done today, Akari." John began cleaning. "You can go home and take a long-deserved rest."

Laughing, you bowed, thanking him.

"See you the day after tomorrow, John!" You waved and left, breathing in the night air.

Step by step, you walked home, feeling your legs dragging.

CHAPTER SEVENTY-ONE

The next couple of days whizzed by too quickly, hardly giving her time to prepare for the meeting with the boss of Kurogumo. The next Monday arrived in no time.

Knowing the gang meeting and the meeting with Kurogumo would clash, she placed John in charge of delivering her message to the gang.

Meanwhile, she, Akio, and Daisuke were at the docks, waiting for Kurogumo's arrival. Well—only her. Akio and Daisuke were hidden away. Part of her plan.

This place gave her unfavorable memories—they continued to resurface, replaying Izana getting shot over and over.

The loud clobbering of heavy steel boots approached. She turned, seeing the boss of Kurogumo for the first time. Exactly as Daisuke described—similar build to Akio.

"You shouldn't be here, girly." He almost growled. "I'm waiting for Ashinuke's boss, so scuttle along now."

"You're looking right at her," she snapped.

He burst out laughing. "Nice joke." He sucked in a large breath.

"Anyway, what do you want?" She was annoyed with his antics.

"I want your area. I want all of Yokohama, and you're in the way. So I'm here to kill you. Bit disappointed the boss of Ashinuke is a puny teenage girl, but that's better for me!" He placed his hands behind his head, relaxed.

"Nice to know we have the same goal. Saves me time."

"What can you do, anyway?"

"Fight me and maybe you'll find out." She spurred him on—he was so close to taking the bait.

"You do realize I have fifty men here with me right now. While you are here on your own."

"And? Do I look like I care?" A long stare. "What? Do you need fifty men to protect you from a 'puny teenage girl'?"

Mocking him finally worked. He charged. "Men! Don't interfere!"

"Of course, boss!" They replied in unison.

She pushed his fist to the side. His swings were heavy, full of brute force—power level very similar to Taiju Shiba. She continued dodging, and he grew restless, swinging over and over. She twisted and landed a roundhouse kick to his abdomen. He read it and grabbed her leg, throwing her to the side. She flipped backward, landing on her feet. He didn't give her time to rest, rushing again.

He punched. She blocked, giving him an occasional kick. It connected, sliding him backward. He got up instantly.

She made sure he was looking before making her first tactical move—glancing at the top of a shipping container, squinting. He noticed and turned his head, searching. She hurried closer, punching him hard in the stomach. It took him by surprise—he coughed harshly, holding his stomach. She distanced herself, letting him recover. She wanted to toy with him a little more.

He stumbled to his feet, glaring. He attacked again—punches aimed at her head and stomach. She didn't expect the knee to her stomach. Stupid on her part. She winced, hopped backward for space. Glancing back at the container, she nodded. Time for the plan.

She waved her arms at the container. A glimpse of light reflected off a mirror. Daisuke was on top, lying flat, imitating a close-range sniper.

"That's low of you—getting a sniper." He spat.

"Funny, coming from the mouth of someone who tests drugs on innocents."

The glint of light reflected near his foot. It disappeared briefly. A bullet pierced the ground right where the light had been.

"Shall we continue?" She tilted her head, smiling. He was taken aback but ready.

She was tired of the battle continuing. She decided to let her instincts take over—but that would ruin the plan. Now aware of the sniper, he was more careful in his movements, paying less attention to her attacks.

She took advantage, launching a continuous barrage. A low kick, spinning on her hands, delivering a head kick, landing before jabbing his chin. To finish, she reared her hand back and jabbed at his neck. A vital paralysis pressure point.

He stopped moving and fell, twitching. She smirked, content. Giving Daisuke a thumbs up, she turned to the limp boss.

"You've lost."

"Fuck off—"

"Now, I need you to verbally announce that the Kurogumo gang and the land occupied by Kurogumo is now Ashinuke's."

Silent treatment. He turned his head away. She pulled out her gun and pointed it at his head. His eyes widened, but he smirked.

"You're not gonna shoot—"

A warning shot beside his ear. Blood trickled. Terrified expression.

"If you kill me, you're gonna become a murderer." He tried to distract her.

"Shut up already and say it. I'm tired and I want to go home." She twirled the gun around her finger. "It's too late for me to return to normal either way," she mumbled.

"Tch. Kurogumo is now under Ashinuke. South Yokohama is also yours. We will follow your instructions." He sighed. "Is this enough?"

"One little thing. It's 'them,' not 'we.'"

"Huh?"

"Don't you get it? Your reign ends here!" She shrieked, laughing. She stopped spinning the gun and aimed at the center of his forehead. His eyes pleaded, mouth opening and closing, no sound.

"Bye, bitch!" She pulled the trigger. A hole formed in the middle of his forehead. Blood trickled, then gushed. He twitched, then stopped completely.

"That's what you get for drugging one of my men." She turned to the fifty men. "You can come out now, Akio, Daisuke!"

Daisuke descended the containers. One of the Kurogumo members walked forward.

Mutters erupted from the terrified members.

"Where's his sniper?" "Is he a mole?"

She tried so hard to hold in her laughter at the confusion.

"Daisuke here never had a gun. Only a mirror, to make you think he was the one who shot. Akio knocked out one of your members on the way here and took his spot. I'm surprised no one noticed. He's the one who actually fired the gun at the feet of your boss. The only reason you heard it from Daisuke's direction was because Daisuke fired a fake, while Akio had a silencer on." She revealed everything, pointing to Daisuke's fake pistol and Akio.

"You fifty, plus your other two hundred men, now belong to me. Tell that to your men and get back to me when you've reached your decision. Anyone who opposes will be hunted down and killed. South Yokohama is also now under Ashinuke's control, so I expect you all to behave."

She walked to one of the men in front and handed him a slip of paper.

"My number." She winked, turned her back, and left.

"Why'd you give him a random number?" Akio questioned.

"Why don't you get it?" Daisuke sighed, facepalming.

"Oh, that's your phone number. Surprised you didn't recognize it." You chuckled.

"What?!"

"Make sure you answer their call properly, Akio." You rested your head on your arms, crossed behind your head, making your way home.

# CHAPTER SEVENTY-TWO

It was late when she got home. She kicked off her shoes, stumbled to bed, jumped on, and instantly switched off.

By the time she woke, it was already 4:30 PM. Late for work!

She sat up, changed into appropriate work clothing, and rushed out. Running toward the bar, she bumped into multiple people, earning dirty looks. She gave up apologizing. Finally arriving, she opened the main door with care, panting, trying to catch her breath.

John stared, then smiled and turned back to his customers.

She walked to the bar counter, sat on the stool, and placed her head down. John pushed a glass of icecold water toward her.

"Here."

"Thanks, John. Sorry I'm late." She banged her head on the counter.

"Don't worry. This time isn't really busy. It becomes busy after 6 PM, so I would've handled everything fine." He chuckled at her puffed-out state. "By the way—" The bell from the back room rang. "Yeah, you might want to tend to that first."

She nodded, finished the water in a gulp, and pushed the glass forward. John took it and placed it in the sink. She slid off the stool and walked toward the door—now covered by a thin black curtain.

"Nice curtain, John!" She gave a thumbs up. "Completely hidden now."

"I made sure it was the same color as the wall." John responded. "Now go. He's waiting for you."

She sighed, opening the back door. Walking through, she wondered who it might be. Surely either Daisuke or Akio. Opening the door on the other side, both were there. Akio held out his phone, wiggling his eyebrows.

"What?" she said coldly, closing the door.

"Phone call from the vice-leader of Kurogumo." He handed it to her.

She accepted, walked to one of the tables, pulled the chair back, and sat, crossing her legs. She motioned to Akio and Daisuke, who pulled their own chairs and sat opposite. She pressed the speakerphone button.

"Good evening, Vice-Leader of Kurogumo."

"You must be the boss of Ashinuke, I assume?"

"I'll get straight to the point. What's your decision?"

"We, Kurogumo, have come to a group decision. However, I would like to discuss some issues with you and arrange a meeting between you and me."

"Tch." She turned to Daisuke and Akio. "What do you think?" she whispered.

"I think you should meet with him. See what his decision and other inquiries may be," Akio whispered back.

Daisuke nodded. "This arrangement benefits us more than them either way. I think you should meet him."

Sighing, she spoke into the phone. "Fine. Meet me at xxx bar, Central Yokohama, at 7 PM tonight. I'll be waiting outside." She hung up.

"Aghgronffk!" She pulled at her hair.

"Calm down, Akari!" Akio screeched, pulling her hands back.

"Why does it have to be so complicated?! It's just a yes or no answer!" She crossed her arms and pouted.

"Akari, it is currently 5:03 PM. You have just under two hours to get ready and meet him." Daisuke looked at his watch.

"Why are you treating this like a professional job interview?"

"Because it is. Depending on his answer, his gang either formally joins under ours, or his gang are dead meat—literally." Akio answered.

"Go home and dress properly. Look presentable." Daisuke stood, dragged her to her feet, and began pushing her out the back door.

"I'll take your spot as a bartender for tonight, so take care of Kurogumo for us!" Akio disappeared behind the curtains toward his office.

"Daisuke, come with me." She spoke softly as he continued pushing her out.

"Fine. I'll be the judge of your 'presentableness.'" He muttered.

- --

They headed to her place, where she removed the black suit she'd previously bought. She remembered the last occasion she wore it and was instantly reminded of Emma and Mikey—and her promise to Mikey. She shook her head and carried the suit to the main room, where Daisuke was waiting.

No—he was cleaning the kitchen dishes.

"Wha—"

"You need to take more care of your apartment, boss." He didn't look up.

"I—umm. Thanks. Anyways, is this okay?" She held up the suit.

Daisuke looked up and stared, then gave a small smile. "Yeah, that's perfect. Are you going to wear your mask too?"

"Nope. Otherwise customers may recognize me as 'Hana,' and that'll be an issue." She eyed the black face mask on the table.

Daisuke hummed and went back to cleaning. "Go change. We don't have too long. Being there early is also part of etiquette."

She rushed into her bedroom and shut the door. She removed her work clothes and slipped on the suit pants, zipping up, clipping the button. She brushed her hands over the front, getting rid of dust. Grabbing the white dress shirt, she flung it over her shoulders, threaded her arms through, and buttoned the bottom five—leaving the first three open, just enough to reveal the top half of her hanafuda tattoo. She pulled the suit jacket from the chair and placed it softly over her shoulders, buttoning the middle buttons. Black socks—shaped like flat shoes—and she walked out, standing in front of Daisuke, hands on her hips.

"How's this?" she exclaimed proudly.

"Nice." He stated simply, looking up from his phone on the couch.

"Okay, let's go." She walked to the front door and pulled out black high heels from the drawer. Slipping them over her feet, she grabbed her phone and house keys.

"Ah! I forgot my earrings!" She took off her shoes and rushed to the bedroom. She grabbed her black dragon earrings and threaded them through the hole in her ear. She kept the remaining black ring earrings in the other three holes in both ears. She rushed back, wore her shoes, and left. Daisuke was already waiting outside.

"Don't think the earrings were necessary, but okay." He walked in front.

"Oh, shut up! It's supposed to represent the Ashinuke emblem."

"Oh. Makes more sense now." He placed his hands in his pockets.

- --

They arrived at the bar and waited outside the main door, leaning against the wall.

"Want me to wait with you?" Daisuke asked.

"No, I'm good. Go inside and watch along with Akio."

He bowed his head and pushed open the door.

She checked the time. 6:45 PM. Fifteen minutes early. She watched people walk past, staring. Wearing this suit felt awesome—gave her a feeling of true power.

A drunk man approached.

"Hey there, young girl!!!" He slurred, tipping back and forth, straightening his arm in her direction.

She stomped hard on his shoe with the point of her high heel.

"Fuck off, gramps." She muttered.

He yelped, fell, holding his foot, gave her a glare, and scampered away.

"You must be the boss of Ashinuke, I assume." A voice from her left.

She turned—a tall man with bleached hair.

"You must be the vice-leader, then." She scanned him. "I'm Eiji, boss of Ashinuke. Nice to meet you, I guess." She extended her hand.

He grabbed it tenderly and bowed his head. "Likewise. Call me Kai." He shook her hand. "Shall we enter?" He let go and walked toward the main door.

"Sure."

Following him into the loud bar, he sat at one of the tables furthest from the crowds. She slid into her seat, crossed her legs, placed an elbow on the table, trying to assert her power over him.

"So, what did you want to speak about?" She got straight to the point.

"Firstly, I would like to speak on behalf of all the members of Kurogumo." He began, and she nodded. "It was a difficult decision, but we have all decided to join under Ashinuke. The 250 men of Kurogumo are now under your power. We only have one issue with joining under Ashinuke—our drug trading routes as our method of money. Our drug business is currently doing well, and with many customers within the black market, we cannot afford to lose it now. I was in charge of it under our boss, Kou, whom you killed. I would like your permission to continue the drug business under the name of Ashinuke." He clasped his hands on the table.

She looked at the menu and raised her hand. Yui came over quickly, instantly horrified by the overwhelming aura both released—not to mention the scar on her face.

"What would you like to order?" Yui stammered.

"Orange juice for me. What would you like, Kai?"

"Sapporo beer, thanks."

Yui smiled and left in a hurry.

"Hmmm." She was torn. A drug business was a big deal. If they were caught, it would be placed under her name. Another alias? No—it would be messy enough to change Kurogumo Drugs to Ashinuke. It took a while, but she finally came up with the perfect decision.

"Alright, about your dr—" She stopped, noticing the drinks.

"Here you go." Yui's bottom lip quivered. "Orange juice and a Sapporo beer." She placed them down, bowed, and immediately left.

"About your drug business, I have my own conditions." She held up one finger. "One, you don't do drug tests on innocent people. Test them on lab rats instead. Two, focus only on your drug business. Forget

about the prostitution and other events going on in the Kurogumo gang. And three, don't change the name of the business to Ashinuke. Keep it under Kurogumo."

Kai's eyes widened. "A-are you sure? It would be a large asset to have the drug business under the Ashinuke name."

"I know. I just think letting you handle it would cause less hassle. Not to mention, your customers may leave once finding out the name has changed. Confusion would erupt on the black market, and the business might crash. As much as I hate the idea of the drug industry, you gotta do what you gotta do to survive." She acknowledged the issues of an underground business.

"I see." Kai whispered. "Thank you for the consideration. I shall allocate half the profit of the business to the gang, then."

She nodded, thankful.

"And one more thing. I want to give you the same position as my trustworthy men, Akio and Daisuke, whom you will meet soon. They were both vice-leaders of Ryūken and Orochi, whom I took under my wing. They were able to unify both gangs by working together. Now that we have the addition of Kurogumo, I expect you to do the same. Devote yourself to Ashinuke, like the other two, and the gang will unify. Now," she said, extending her hand. "As one of my advisors, I wholeheartedly welcome you and your men into the Ashinuke gang."

Kai looked at her hand, then grabbed it with both of his.

"Yes! I devote myself to Ashinuke!" He shook it with excitement.

"Phew. Now that's all over, let me show you around." She stood, leaving cash for both drinks, and made her way out, Kai following.

"Umm, where are we going, in such a narrow alleyway?"

"Our hideout." She stated sharply, walking further and looking around. Sensing no one watching, she walked toward a metal door.

"Unity of broken ties," she spoke softly to one of the guards. He stared down at her.

"Evening, boss." He opened the heavy door.

Kai followed her in. The back room was empty except for Daisuke, seated at the stool alone, drinking beer.

"What's this?" Kai asked.

"This is the Ashinuke meeting hall, where meetings are every Monday from 6 PM. I expect you to be here every Monday, since you are one of my advisors. Talking about advisors—this is Daisuke, former viceleader of Orochi."

"Nice to meet you." Daisuke said coldly, extending his hand. "Fuyukawa. Fuyukawa Daisuke."

Kai accepted. "Akinoue. Akinoue Kai. Pleased to work with you."

She watched them shake hands, then walked toward the bar and rang the bell. Kai stared.

"Ring the bell when you want to be served by a bartender from the bar from earlier. They're connected. In case you haven't realized—like your drug business—Ashinuke's is a bar."

The door opened—Akio walked in.

"This is the other advisor, Akio. Akio, say your greetings."

"Evening, I'm Natsuhana Akio. Nice to meet you!" He bowed.

"I'm Akinoue Kai. Pleasure to work with you."

She sat on the stool, asked Akio for apple juice, and placed her head down, yawning.

"Tired?" Daisuke asked.

"Mhm."

"You should go home, then, Eiji." Kai spoke.

Daisuke and Akio glanced at each other, then at her sleepy figure.

"Yea, I think I'll go home." She rubbed her eyes, got off the stool. "See you three here tomorrow at 2 PM. We have to discuss the plan for retaking the rest of Yokohama." She raised her hand and exited.

- --

# CHAPTER SEVENTY-THREE

The next day, she woke earlier than normal to arrive on time. She was waiting for Daisuke and Kai, wiping glasses dry with the towel on her shoulder, when Akio arrived from behind the curtain and took a seat.

"Now that I think about it, I've never been in your office," she said, handing him the menu.

He pushed it away. "There's no need for you to come in either way. I've got everything under my control." He placed a hand on his bicep and smiled widely. She laughed at his childish manner.

The back door opened—Daisuke and Kai arrived together.

"Afternoon, Eiji, Akio." Kai bowed.

"Hey, you two." Daisuke said coldly, making his way to the table, laying out photos and documents. Kai sat on the stool.

"Want anything to drink, Kai?"

"No, thanks. I'm good." He looked around the room.

"Here you go." Daisuke stood away from the table. Kai, Akio, and she gathered round.

She picked up the nearest photo and the attached document.

"The photo you're holding is the boss of the Red Aces. They currently own the west of Yokohama. The attached document is the information on his past and his current business. If you read carefully, you'd understand he's of quite a calm nature—only violent when necessary."

Scanning, she found the boss of the Red Aces owns a popular alcohol brand, varying from beer to wine.

"Alcohol, huh?" she mumbled. If they could rule them, there'd be a great partnership between the bar and their alcohol business. "Wouldn't their business benefit our bar?"

Daisuke nodded, but Akio spoke. "We never sold their alcohol here, due to rumors of the brand being led by a gang boss."

She hummed. Kai just stared at the photos.

"Is the boss the one managing their business?" Kai uttered.

Daisuke nodded. "Yes, that's right. So if we were to kill him, their business would disappear, which is a shame, since they're making quite a lot of money." He turned his back to the table. "Which is why I have this."

He pulled out a slim folder from his bag under the table. Multiple documents, ordered neatly. She skimmed, recognizing only the countless numbers. One page was flagged. She turned to it, eyes widening, then smirked, bursting into laughter, holding her stomach, tears pouring.

"Of course they're making a ton of profit," she choked out.

The folder passed to Akio and Kai.

"So according to this, their alcohol has a small percentage of xxx drugs, which makes the body go into a state of unquenchable thirst. Which leads them to drink more, and the cycle continues until they pass out drunk or drink water." Akio summarized.

"How'd you find this out, Daisuke?" Kai asked, taking the question from her mouth.

"Since they were one of the gangs we planned to take over, I did some research and found out about their business. I didn't feel comfortable drinking it myself, so I served it to some Ashinuke men, and the symptoms came through after their first glass. Extreme thirst, addiction—you get the idea. They didn't stop until out cold drunk. I gave one a glass of water, and their thirst was solved—still drunk, though. I knew something was wrong, so I took a bottle of their wine and beer and tested it. I assume the authorities have completely missed this—either hush money or threats. But now that we know, we can use it to blackmail their boss." Daisuke took a deep breath.

"The only issue is whether the boss will cooperate with the blackmail and listen to the orders of a teenage girl," she said. "How do we kn—"

Daisuke cut her off. "I'll take care of their business, then."

"What?!" Akio and she exclaimed.

"You guys kill the boss of the Red Aces, and I'll take care of his business. Either way, I'm the only advisor not taking care of a business, so I'll take that role. If we go on an assassination mission, kill the boss, the men of the Red Aces would never know their boss died. I'm assuming that since he takes care of his business alone, no one knows his true identity. If there are a couple who do, we can threaten them. I would act as the boss of the Red Aces, whom none of the men would suspect is dead. The Red Aces would continue life as normal, but in reality, you, Eiji, would give me the instructions when necessary." She nodded.

"So basically, we kill their boss and his most trusted men. You take over their gang as the 'boss,' while I give the orders you pass on. They remain under the Red Aces name but are under Ashinuke."

"This way, the men have no idea they're being controlled and betrayed. No conflict. If anything, a peaceful way of merging the gangs." Akio finished.

"We just gotta make sure we let our own men know not to attack the Red Aces afterward. The only issue is Red Aces men might attack Ashinuke members when they see them on their turf." Kai scratched his head.

"I'll let the men know we've entered a peaceful treaty with Ashinuke. The boss's word being final, no one would question it." Daisuke answered.

"Alright. Since we have our plan laid out, we need to investigate who in the Red Aces knows the real identity of their boss. They will be the only crucial part. The vice-leader is most important. If you can, kidnap him once we kill the boss. Bring him to me." She smiled creepily, watching the men shiver.

"Yes, boss," Daisuke answered.

"I'll add you to the group chat, Kai." Akio stated.

"Ohh, good idea. I forgot that thing existed."

"Done!" Akio announced. Kai had a puzzled look. "Who's Akari?"

"Oh, that's me. I forgot to tell you Eiji is an alias I use. Don't tell your men about my real name. I have enough people who can give my identity away. I don't need the police knowing any more than they already do." Kai nodded.

"So when are we planning the assassination?" Akio looked at her.

"When we have enough information about who knows the true identity of the boss of Red Aces." Daisuke stated.

"What he said." She mumbled. "Anyways, get the information as fast as you can. Actually—find the viceleader and kidnap him, bring him here. Tied up and blinded, of course. Before we assassinate the boss. Any questions, ask now or on the group chat."

Long silence.

"Okay, I'm assuming the instructions are clear. I'll give you all roles now. Akio, stay here and find anything you can on the net. Daisuke and Kai, research and find people who know the real identity of the boss. Kill everyone who knows except the vice-leader. You two will also bring the vice-leader here. Clear?"

They nodded.

"What are you going to be doing?" Akio raised an eyebrow.

She snickered. "I'm gonna walk around their district in my uniform. Make them acknowledge Ashinuke as a new gang in town. Make them see us as a threat, so when you announce the treaty, they'll be glad to

side with someone they shouldn't mess with. Plan starts tomorrow. Send me a message once you've kidnapped the vice-leader."

She made her intentions clear, then stretched, twisting her body, feeling the pleasant cracking of her spine.

"Okay, I'm going to work now, so I'll be here until around midnight if you need me. See yah!" She turned heel and walked through the door to the other side, leaving the three men.

- --

# CHAPTER SEVENTY-FOUR

- *Akari:** *Morning, everyone! Plan kidnap the vice-leader starts today. Kai, Daisuke—make sure you

kill anyone who knows the identity of the boss.*

- *Daisuke:** *Got it.*

- *Kai:** *Meet up at the bar, Daisuke?*

- *Daisuke:** *Sure, see you there in five minutes.*

- *Akio:** *I'll let you all know once I find something.*

- *Akari:** *Akio, set up the back room for me.*

- *Akio:** *What for?*

- *Akari:** *To hold the vice-leader there until I kill him.*

- *Akio:** *Ahh, gotcha. Will do that now.*

- --

She slid her phone into her gang jacket pocket, slipped on her combat boots, pulling them up, tugging the straps tight. She grabbed the gun hidden under the couch, tucked it between her back and the waistband of her pants, and left, shutting the door softly. She walked down the stairs slowly, breathing in the cool morning air.

It wasn't long before she reached the train station. She bought a two-way ticket to West Yokohama, dug her hands into her pockets, and walked to the platform, standing in the colored line. About three minutes later, the train arrived. People rushed out, desperate to get to work. The line moved forward, and she stepped on, leaning against the window.

Multiple stares from the public—a young girl wearing a gang jacket. Lucky she was wearing her mask. Her current worry was the gun behind her back. If someone leaned into her back, game over. She did her best to lean against the train wall, making sure no one found out about her illegal weapon.

The doors opened, and she stepped out, sighing in relief that the stressful part was over.

There were fewer people at this station, even though it was the largest and closest to the center of West Yokohama.

She walked toward the main road and instantly spotted a red gang jacket with a large black 'A' on the back. The gang name was cool, but the design could've been better.

She straightened her jacket and walked confidently through the main street. Almost immediately, growls and mumbles—she attracted the attention of the Red Aces. It wasn't long before she was grabbed by the collar from behind and dragged into a smaller alleyway.

She was slammed onto the wall, upper back making the most contact. She felt the rattle in her rib cage.

"Who do you think you are, walking into our territory?" One of them snarled.

"Aren't you a little too young to be playing around in a gang? Not to mention, you are a woman." Another, calmer and more respectful.

It wasn't long before the alleyway was packed with a sea of red uniforms.

"Let me go, will you?" She grabbed the wrist of the man holding her up. He snorted and gripped her collar, pushing her harder against the wall.

"You don't get to have a say here, young girl. Now answer our questions." He spat.

"Nahh, sorry. But that's not how this works." She smirked. She lifted her legs, dangling in the air, and wrapped them around his neck, squeezing tightly. He let go of her collar, and she slid off the wall, hanging upside down against his body, squeezing even tighter. He choked, gripping and clawing at her thighs. She just dangled upside down and didn't show mercy. He turned purple, froth foaming at his mouth. He sunk to his knees as she placed both hands on the floor and did a quick handstand. She flipped back onto her feet and brushed off her hands.

The rest of the gang looked in shock as she took out their largest man. Their eyes showed terror. Some had already made their getaway. One stepped forward, barely asking the question everyone wanted to know.

"W-what gang are you from?" He stuttered.

"Ashinuke. We currently own central and south Yokohama, so accept the consequences if you step into our territory."

"That's funny, especially since you stepped into ours." Another rolled his eyes.

She stared back with an amused smile but didn't say a word. It seemed to creep them out more than if she'd spoken.

"What are you here for?"

She chuckled as they took a small step back.

"Nothing, for now. Just a little fun and games. You'll find out later. Be grateful, bitches." She walked toward the exit. A hand on her shoulder. She smacked it away, quickly turned, and gave a death glare.

"Don't. Touch. Me." She spoke in a slow, low voice, growling.

"Name. What's your name?" The first man asked.

"We should report her name to the boss," another whispered.

"Go ahead and tell your boss my name. He'll be over the moon." She laughed out loud, wiping away fake tears. "Eiji. That's my name. See ya around." She turned her back and raised her hand, waving goodbye.

- --

She was walking back to the station when her phone began vibrating, a flood of messages coming through.

- *Daisuke:** *We've got him.*

- *Kai:** *We're driving there at the moment. Will be there in approx. 10 mins.*

- *Akio:** *I've set up everything. We're ready.*

- *Daisuke:** *We'll be waiting for you, Akari.*

- *Akari:** *Good work, you three.*

- *Akio:** *Thank you! :)*

- *Kai:** *Thanks, boss.*

- *Daisuke:** *Cheers.*

- *Akari:** *Be there in 15 minutes. Set up the chair and keep him blindfolded until I get there.*

- *Daisuke:** *Got it.*

- --

As she walked to the station, she realized she was being followed. She turned into a small shop and pretended to buy an item. Luring him into a corner away from the public eye, she grabbed his wrist, pinned it behind his back, placed her hand around his neck, and tightened.

"Why're you following me? What do you want?"

"Eiji-san, I have a request." He said calmly.

"Depends on the request."

"I—. Please help the boss. He's no longer himself and is going to go corrupt soon. His business is profiting so well, but he's blinded by greed, and he's adding more of his—" He stopped, shutting his mouth.

She sighed. "If you're talking about the drugs in the alcohol, I already know."

She felt the tension ease from his body.

"Yea, so he's going to increase the drug per bottle. It might kill someone, so I want to stop him, but he's gone nuts with greed. I can't do anything. So I'm begging you—please help him."

"Do you know your boss personally?"

"Not personally, but I'm one of the few who know how he really is."

"You are aware that we are Ashinuke, a gang trying to take control of all of Yokohama, right?" He nodded slowly as she loosened her grip. "So why are you asking me?"

"Because I feel like you're planning something that has something to do with the Red Aces."

- Man, his instincts are on point.*

"Sorry to disappoint, but I can't help you." She released his wrist and held out her hand. "What?"

"Gimme your phone."

He reluctantly handed over his unlocked phone. She entered her number.

"Call me in three days. I have a feeling you'll be of good use to me in the future."

He looked at her with a glint in his eyes, unaware of her assassination plan. He took back his phone and bowed.

"I will do so! I'm Nao. Pleased to be of any help, as long as I can be of use to help the boss."

She almost felt pity. "Sorry, but don't get your hopes up. I'm not doing anything to 'help' your boss," she mumbled, taking her leave.

She walked to the station and took the next train back to Central Yokohama.

- --

Arriving at the bar, she walked in calmly through the back door. A blindfolded man in the center of the room, a table next to him. She couldn't tell if he was unconscious.

"Is he alive?" she whispered to Daisuke.

"You took too long. He's sleeping." He replied, monotone.

"Ahh." She walked toward the blindfolded man, pulled out a chair, and sat in front of him. She removed his blindfold. He stirred.

"I'm finally not moving." He groaned. "I'm tired of being dragged everywhere. And? What do you guys need?"

"You don't seem to understand your situation, Ao." She laced a little threat in her voice.

His eyes met hers. She stared back for a while before he looked away first. *Small victory.*

"I hope you're aware of your situation. Your boss's situation. Your gang's situation." She smirked as his eyes changed—then changed back within the second.

"Do what you like. I don't care about the Red Aces. The boss forced me into it, so I don't really care." He looked back at her, then away, mumbling. "Just don't hurt my younger brother."

"Younger brother?" She tilted her head. "What makes you think I'll go after him?"

"Those two men over there," he nudged his head toward Daisuke and Kai, "killed men in front of me because they knew the identity of the boss. My brother also knows the boss, so I'm assuming you're planning to kill him too."

"What if we've already killed him?"

"You haven't. He was ordered to monitor the main street of West Yokohama. Those two didn't go there, so he's still alive."

She smiled to herself.

"What's so funny?" Ao asked.

"I was there today."

His eyes widened in fear, worrying for his brother.

"Don't worry, I didn't kill anyone."

He breathed out a long sigh of relief.

"You said you were forced into the gang. Was your brother also forced?" Daisuke asked, sipping a drink provided by John, who quickly returned to the other side.

"I was forced. He joined on his own after finding out I joined. He really admires the boss, which is why he wants to help him overcome his greed." He looked at his shoes.

"Why'd the boss force you to—" Kai started.

"Is your brother called Nao, by any chance?" She cut him off.

He quickly turned, eyes meeting hers with intent. "Yes. How'd you know?"

"He followed me after I attacked one of your men. He begged me to help the boss overcome his greed, since he was planning to increase the dosage of the drug in his alcohol. I asked him to call me in three days, as I felt he'd be of use to me." Ao continued to stare. "I see. But you're not planning to help the boss, are you? Especially since you killed everyone who knew the boss's identity except me and him."

"Man, both of you are so sharp!" She laughed, clasping her hands. "Yeah, so we're planning to assassinate your boss tomorrow night and take over the Red Aces from the shadows. Since you know—"

"I'll help your plan. I'll get Nao on board too." He cut her off.

"Oh, really?! That'll be of major help, since you both know what your gang is like. I was planning on having Daisuke here," she nudged him forward, "take over the Red Aces and the business as the 'boss.' No one in the gang would have to know he died."

"Yeah, like I said, I'll help him. You're just taking over the Red Aces but secretly controlling them from the shadows, right?" She nodded. "That is a genius plan."

"I know, right?" She was excited. "Anyway, I'm going to announce a 'truce' to the men of the Red Aces and Ashinuke, so neither attacks each other."

"That's good. How are you gonna kill the boss?"

"I found his office, if you need that information." Akio walked over and handed her printouts—maps of the surrounding area. The office was in the middle of West Yokohama, a tall office building. His office was one floor of the building.

"I'm familiar with the office. I can take you there and pretend you have a new deal for him that'll 'benefit' his business. Like a stronger drug." Ao suggested.

She turned to Kai. "Can you give me some powder? Doesn't have to be real—just something that looks real enough to fool him."

Kai nodded, turned heel, and left through the back door. "Be back in a bit."

"I'll take that suggestion," she said to Ao, untying him. He rubbed his wrists and ankles where the ropes had dug in. "Yeah, sorry about that."

"You need to dress appropriately, then." Daisuke referred to her.

"Yeah, yeah, I know." She rolled her eyes. "Is the same as last time okay?" Daisuke nodded.

"Maybe lose the dangly earrings and keep the ones you have on now."

"Fineee." She whined. "Anyway, I'll let you go for now. Meet me at the front of the bar, on the other side, tomorrow at 2 PM. Let the boss know about my visit tomorrow at 3:30 PM."

"Okay, sure. Do I let Nao know about this plan or no?"

"No, don't tell him anything. He'll know in three days when he calls me."

Ao nodded. "Are you going to join our gang after this? Since the Red Aces will be affiliated with Ashinuke."

"Yea, I'll join. I'll do everything in my power to help you reunite Yokohama."

"Okay, perfect! I'll add you to the group chat, then." She extended her hand, and he handed over his phone. She punched her number in, dialed her own number from his phone, then added his to the group chat.

"See you at 2 PM tomorrow!" She waved as he bowed and left.

She remained seated, leaning her head backward on the chair. The back door creaked—Kai walked in.

"I'm back." He panted, out of breath, shuffled over, and handed her a small bag with white powder at the bottom. "Here."

She extended her hand, and he placed it in her palm.

"It's MDMA. But it's been thinned, so it's only 5% pure."

She nodded and stuffed it into her pocket. "Thanks, Kai."

"No worries. Make sure you dispose of it after you kill the boss. Don't need the police to find drugs and tail our business, even if it is on the black market."

"Of course. If I burn it, is that okay?"

"Yeah. Make sure you don't inhale the toxins, though."

"Okay, will be careful." She stood and walked toward the back door. "I'll be heading home now. Take care, see you tomorrow night—or the night after at our weekly meeting." She motioned a goodbye and left.

- --

# CHAPTER SEVENTY-FIVE

She woke to her body half on the floor, half on the bed. She must've been rolling around. She groaned, her lower back aching from the awkward posture. She sat up carefully and stretched, screaming a little. Intertwining her fingers, she felt the satisfactory crack of her knuckles.

She jumped to her feet, walked to the bathroom, washed her face, and applied light makeup. Skipping into the kitchen, she prepared a small breakfast.

Once finished, she watched the morning news while setting out the suit—neatly ironed and cleaned, since she'd asked Daisuke to send it to the dry cleaners. She removed the plastic wrapping, cast it aside, and slid into the suit. She pulled the pants over her thighs, zipped up, threaded the belt through the loops, and tightened it at the waist. The long-sleeved white dress shirt, hardly any creases. She tucked it in and adjusted the collar. She removed the suit jacket from the hanger and slid her arms through. Grabbing the black tie borrowed from Daisuke, she tied it under the dress shirt collar and tightened it around her neck.

She tucked her gun into the small space between her lower back and the waistband, then sighed as she slowly buttoned the jacket. She dug around her gang uniform pocket for the small packet of MDMA and removed it, placing it carefully into her handbag. Removing her phone from the charging port, she slipped it into her pant pocket.

It was 1:15 PM. She left the house, high heels clicking against the floor as she walked confidently toward the bar.

She pushed the door open, walked in, and sat on the stool.

"Heya, John!" She exclaimed as he walked out from the corner.

"Good afternoon." He walked around to the other side and began making a small fruity drink. He pushed it toward her, and she gratefully accepted it. "I have asked Boss Akio to start paying you for your bartending services. You'll be discussing the matter with him tomorrow night, after the meeting."

"Oh, really? Thanks for letting me know, John." She brought the sweet drink to her lips.

"Big day today, isn't it?" John cleaned glasses.

"Sure is." She loosened her tie a little. "Actually, John—"

"Yes?"

"How are you so calm with me and the gang killing people?"

John let out a small laugh. "You don't know much about me, young woman. I may be old, but I was once part of a gang too. Don't worry about me knowing things. I've had more than enough time to get used to things like murder."

She smiled, grateful to have such a wise man to rely on. She continued conversing for a little longer, then glanced at the clock. She placed the glass down, pushed it gently toward John.

"Thanks for the drink. I've got to go now. I'll see you tomorrow night for my shift."

"Of course. Good luck with today's mission." John bowed as she walked out, lifting her hand in response.

- --

She leaned against the wall of the bar, waiting for Ao. She checked the group chat.

- *Daisuke:** *Text me once the job is done. I'll dispose of the body.*

- *Akari:** *Okay. Make sure it's unrecognizable first. I'm gonna kill him with one shot.*

- *Kai:** *Should I come with you, Daisuke?*

- *Daisuke:** *Up to you. It's not much of a task though.*

- *Ao:** *Akari, be there in 5.*

- *Akari:** *Kk.*

- *Akio:** *Should I revert the room back to normal?*

- *Akari:** *Yes, please. That'll be highly appreciated. Oh, Daisuke—*

- *Daisuke:** *Yes?*

- *Akari:** *Bring a body bag and a carpet cleaner.*

- *Daisuke:** *Ofc.*

- --

Gripping her handbag tightly, adjusting the mask, she watched a black car with tinted windows stop in front of the bar. The window rolled down—Ao in the driver's seat.

"Hey, Akari. Ready to go?" He bent his head to see her.

"Yeah, let's go." She walked to the passenger side, opened the door, and slid in, placing the seatbelt over her upper body. "Also, when we get there, please refrain from calling me Akari. Call me Eiji instead."

"Oh, of course." He started the engine and drove.

The ride was silent but not awkward. She stared out the window as hundreds of buildings passed. Ao kept his eyes on the road, listening to the radio.

"We're here." He nudged her arm lightly.

He unclasped his seatbelt and opened the door. She did the same, reaching for her door—but it swung open, Ao having opened it for her.

"Thanks, Ao." She stepped out, clutching her handbag. She sent a quick text to the group chat announcing their arrival.

Ao walked toward the main doors. The automatic doors slid open. He swiped his passkey to the lock in front of the elevator. It began its way down.

"Can I go to the bathroom before I meet the boss?" she asked carefully.

"Of course. There should be one on the same floor. I'll show you."

They boarded the elevator and took it to the 17th floor. The doors dinged open, and she stepped out, Ao following. She stopped and looked around—pleased to see absolutely nobody on the floor.

"The bathroom is here." He signaled to his right, showing her the shared bathroom. "I'll wait for you outside."

"Okay, thanks."

She entered and locked the door. She looked at herself in the mirror, adjusted the mask, and tightened her tie. She removed the gun from its hiding spot and the silencer from her handbag. Twisting the silencer over the mouth of the gun, it clicked into place. She wedged it back and washed her hands, unlocked the door.

"Okay, let's go, Ao."

He nodded and led her to the room where the boss was waiting. He stopped in front of an opaque glass door and knocked three times.

"Come in." A deep voice.

Ao pushed the door open and ushered her in first.

"Ahh, you must be the client Ao informed me of." The man stood from his leather chair and walked over, extending his hand. She grabbed and shook it. "Now to business. Please take a seat." He pointed to the chair opposite his desk, turned, and sat back in his chair.

"Yes. Ao here informed me of your alcohol business and the need for the new substance you wanted to test." She opened her handbag and pulled out the small plastic zip-lock bag with white crystallized powder. He snatched it from her hands and held it up to the light.

"How pure?" He demanded, not taking his eyes off it.

"50%," she replied quickly—a lie.

He hummed euphorically, staring at the drug with hunger in his eyes. He suddenly jumped out of his chair and walked toward the large glass windows overlooking the main street of West Yokohama.

"If you arrange a partnership with me, I can give you 35% of the profit our company makes." Meaning he gets the remaining 65%—a truly greedy man.

She pulled out the gun from her back and aimed at the back of his head. A last-minute thought: *It would be noticeable if blood splattered on the window. Daisuke may take too long, and we could be busted.*

She sighed and waited for him to turn around and reach for the glass of alcohol on the cabinet behind his desk.

"You have yourself a deal." She felt him smirk as he turned around. "We should celebrate with a whiskey." He walked over to the cabinet, reaching for the drink.

"Sorry, but the only profit you'll be getting from your greed is death." She aimed at his head.

"What do you—" She cut him off, pulling the trigger. The bullet pierced through his head. His body slumped, blood seeping out of the fresh wound, staining the grey carpet a rich mahogany red.

"That's done!" She said to Ao, who watched from the corner. He glanced around, taking in everything, staring at the body of his boss, then turned back to her.

"I am now part of Ashinuke. Pleased to work with you." He knelt in front of her.

"Get up, Ao." He got up. "Now tell me. Does anyone in this building know about the boss?"

"This is an office building. Multiple floors are owned by different companies. The boss only owns this one floor and kept it to himself. The only ones who can enter are those with the keycard I used earlier." He pointed to the one on the desk. "That's his. Of course, this keycard is only used for the elevator, so people within the building can freely move to other floors, though that's highly impractical. I think many knew the boss by his name, Terushima Sou, but don't know his face. So as long as you keep it under his name, there should be no issues."

"Ahh, that's good news, then." She pulled out her phone.

- *Akari:** *He's dead.*

- *Daisuke:** *Alright. Be there in 10 minutes. Don't touch anything unnecessarily.*

She looked around, walked to the window, and stared down the 17 floors. She walked back to the desk, took his keycard, and stuffed it into her pocket.

"Can you make replicas of the keycard?"

"I think I can ask the front desk."

"Okay, can you do that for me and give it to Daisuke?"

"Sure, I'll go down now." Ao left, leaving her alone with Terushima Sou's dead body.

She turned away and sat on the chair near the glass door, resting her head on the back, staring at the ceiling. She loosened her tie to breathe. She waited for Daisuke and Kai.

- --

It wasn't long before familiar knocks sounded. She slid the chair out of the way and opened the door as Daisuke, Kai, and Ao entered one after another. Daisuke and Kai immediately got to work—one readying the body bag, another vacuuming blood from the carpet with a steam vacuum cleaner.

"Is this really necessary?" Ao asked.

"Well, you wouldn't want a rotting body and a blood-stained carpet for your new office, would you?" She retorted.

"Well, yeah, but having an office where a murder occurred isn't really any better."

She snorted, agreeing. "You'll just have to get used to it."

Daisuke and Kai were efficient—the body quickly packed, the blood sucked from the carpet in no time.

"We're finished here." Daisuke lifted the body bag over his shoulder. "I'm gonna load the bag in the car. Be back in a bit."

She handed him the keycard, which he stuffed into his pocket as he left. She walked over to Terushima's desk, sat in his leather chair, swung around, and stopped at his computer—unlocked. She motioned for Ao. He walked over and glanced at the computer, eyes widening. He grabbed it and began scrolling through documents.

"It seems he was onto the underground Kurogumo drug business." Ao didn't take his eyes off. "He was going to order some high-purity drugs by the looks of it and expose the business. Luckily, we came to him with a 'better' deal—otherwise, the Kurogumo drug business would be in danger of exposure."

Kai rushed over and skimmed the details. "Man, that's a close call. Too close for comfort, if anything." He folded his arms. "Can you check his outgoing emails, Ao?"

Ao did. Multiple going out toward Kurogumo's secret email address—that Kai had never gotten.

- Something was wrong.*

"I never got these emails. And if there's a response to them—"

"You've got a mole within Kurogumo." She spat out. "Who has access to this email address?"

"Normally, only me. But I gave the password to one other man a few days ago, because I had to manage something else."

"Must be him, then." Ao continued going through the emails.

"Kill him, Kai. We can't afford leaks. It'll be the backdoor to your business, which means we could all be busted." She looked up at Kai with piercing eyes.

"Of course. It'll be done by tonight." He responded. "I'll take my leave now and find him, then." Kai left as Daisuke entered.

"I've loaded the body. We're ready to go." Daisuke noticed Kai leaving and asked for the situation, which she explained.

"Kai will solve it by tonight, so we have to get on with the next stage of the plan. Ao, does your boss have weekly meetings?"

Ao nodded. "We do. We have one tonight, but he never personally attends them, to protect his identity. He usually just gives me the orders, which I relay back to the gang."

Daisuke and she turned to each other. He smirked, and she smiled back.

"That's more than what we need." She chuckled. "Attend your meeting tonight and let them know there is now a 'truce' between Ashinuke and the Red Aces. I attacked a small group the other day, so word of Ashinuke should've spread. Of course, tell them as you normally do."

"Yes, of course, boss." Ao acknowledged her authority and called her 'boss,' which made her highly uncomfortable.

"Just call me Akari. It feels weird. Only call me Akari when Kai, Daisuke, and Akio are here, though. Refer to me as Eiji otherwise. Anyways, I'll let my men know at tomorrow night's meeting about the truce between Ashinuke and the Red Aces. Is it okay for both men to walk around freely within both territories?"

"I think if we didn't, they would become suspicious," Ao replied.

"Okay, then. That's sorted. Oh, I need you and Daisuke to work together to take on Terushima's business. Use his name for everything, make it seem like he's still alive." She cracked her fingers.

"Will do." Daisuke nodded.

"I'm going to stay behind and begin planning everything for tonight's meeting. You two can go ahead and go home. I've got this." Ao took a seat at Terushima's desk.

"Okay. Tomorrow is our meeting, so make sure you attend. The password for the back door is 'Unity of broken ties.' Hope to see you there, and message the group chat if you need anything. See you then." She left, Daisuke following.

"Here you go." Daisuke handed the keycard back. "You should have unlimited access to this building either way, so make sure you don't lose it."

She took it as they pressed the elevator button. The door opened on the ground floor.

"Have a good evening!" The lobby assistant exclaimed. She turned and nodded; Daisuke replied, "You too," in the most monotone voice.

Daisuke led her to the car. "Since when did you have a car?"

"This is now Ashinuke's vehicle. We bought it using the profit from Kai and Akio's business." He opened the car door. Sure enough, the strong stench of blood from Terushima's body bag in the trunk was evident.

"That's quick money."

"All thanks to you." He started the engine. "Sorry about him." He pointed to the trunk with his thumb. "I'll deal with his body tonight, so don't worry. Go home, rest, rewind, and get ready for tomorrow's shift at the bar and the meeting afterward."

"Alright, I got it." She rested her head on the back of the seat, closed her eyes briefly, then opened them. She pressed the button to open the window. Cool air rushed in, reminding her of riding Sanzu's motorcycle back in Tokyo. She sighed deeply.

"You missing someone or something?" Daisuke glanced at the rearview mirror, then turned to her.

"Yeah, I miss my boyfriend." She didn't give details.

"Maybe you should go see him. Take a small break from Ashinuke."

"I told him I don't know when I'll be back, but I wanted to end Orochi and Ryūken first."

"And you did that. You completed your promise." Daisuke cut her off, taking a turn off the highway.

"I know. But now, I want to unite all of Yokohama before I go back to Tokyo. Something both Ryūken and Orochi were unable to do. So I'm not going back until I do it." She looked out the window.

"I see. Well, in that case, you're now halfway there. Only two more gangs to go." Daisuke smiled, keeping his eyes on the road.

"Yeah, you're right. But after the meeting tomorrow, we're going to hold off on attacking. Get our businesses sorted first, especially the Red Aces' alcohol business."

"True that. We can do that in the incoming months. There's not much of a rush."

Daisuke stopped the car in front of her place. She clicked off the seatbelt and opened the door.

"Thanks for driving me home, Daisuke. See you tomorrow." She closed the door.

"Anytime, Akari. Have a goodnight, see you tomorrow evening at 5 PM." He closed the passenger window and drove off, probably to dispose of the body. She turned and walked up the stairs.

- --

The bar was quiet today. It had just opened, but there were hardly any customers. Even John found it strange. The two stood behind the counter, waiting. Customers occasionally walked in, which John served on his own. Once they'd been served, John nudged her side and pointed to the door with his eyes.

"You should go. Today seems quiet, so I'll be fine. Make sure you talk to Akio about your pay as well."

"I see. I'll head over to the other side, then. I'll be back after the meeting."

John nodded. She grabbed her gang jacket from under the counter and walked to the door. She walked slowly through the corridor and opened the door on the other end—blinded by bright lights.

"What the fuck is with the bright lights?" She covered her eyes, walking blindly toward the bar counter. The light switched off, revealing Akio, Kai, and Daisuke with a projector machine in between them. "Really? There's a blank wall right there." She pointed to the wall over the stage.

"We thought you were coming a little later," Akio said.

"We'll point it to the stage, then." Kai turned the projector around slowly.

"Oh, Akio—John told me to discuss my pay with you." She walked over.

"Oh, that's right! I keep forgetting. Here's the deal. Any day you work at the bar, ¥7500 (approx. $75). That includes the hours at which you serve this side of the room. Just turn up on any day, make sure to write it down in the paper on the other side. Ask John for it. John usually works here alone, so you'll be a large hand to him. I'll pay you through card, so set up a bank account, will you?"

"I'll do it tomorrow. Daisuke?"

"Yes, I'll come with you." He rolled his eyes.

"Thanks, Daisuke!" She smiled widely.

The door opened—Ao walked in. "Sup, Ao!" She raised her hand in greeting. He replied with a hello to everyone.

"So how'd it go with the Red Aces?" Kai asked.

"They took the news well. If anything, they were glad the truce formed. It seems the 'well-known Eiji' had really shaken them to the core." Everyone burst out laughing.

"That's good news. Just up to me to tell the men of Ashinuke, then," she said as the men nodded. "We've still got a little time. Do you want any drinks?"

She headed behind the bar counter as they ordered. They downed them quickly as the Ashinuke men flooded in. She served them until the clock struck six, and Akio took over bartending. She walked to the stage.

"Evening, Ashinuke!" The eyes of hundreds of men looked up. "We have big news. The boss of the Red Aces is dead!" Whispers—shock. "However, they have a new boss. The boss and I had a meeting yesterday and agreed on a truce. This truce will enable both gangs to walk upon each other's territory without a fuss. This will greatly benefit both gangs!" The crowd roared.

Questions were asked, which she answered, keeping the truth hidden. Once answered, the gang went back into party mode, the music playing. She walked off the stage and helped Akio serve drinks.

After a long night, all the men left, leaving only the advisors.

"Don't forget that my brother is supposed to call you tomorrow," Ao spoke up.

"Oh shit, I forgot! I need to go to the bank with Daisuke tomorrow." She facepalmed.

"We can go to the bank the day after tomorrow," Daisuke suggested.

"If that's okay with you, that'll be greatly appreciated." She gave a 'thank you' motion. "Ao, I'm going to ask Nao to come here tomorrow, so come here as well. We need to break the news of Terushima's death to him properly."

"Sure thing. I think we should do it together." Ao agreed.

"Thanks for tonight, guys. I'll see you all when I do. Any issues, text the group chat. See you!" She left the back room and headed to the other side, helping John for the rest of the night. A couple hours later, John closed, and she walked home and fell asleep.

- --

# CHAPTER SEVENTY-SIX

The next morning, she woke to her ringtone. She fell off the bed grabbing her phone, answered without checking the caller.

"Hello?" she groaned, half asleep.

"Hello? Is this Eiji?" A voice she recognized.

"Yes, is this Nao?"

"Yep!"

"Oh, whoa, you sound just like your brother."

"You know my brother?"

"Yeah, I do. Anyways, thanks for calling. You wanted me to help your boss, right?"

"Yeah."

"I have news about him. Are you free to meet up?" She yawned.

"Yeah, sure. Whereabouts?"

"Meet me inside the bar xxx in Central Yokohama."

"Ohh, cool. I've always wanted to visit Central Yokohama."

"Well, now you can, thanks to the truce."

"Very true. Although, it's very much unlike the boss to do so." *He was onto her.* Him and his sharp instincts.

"Anyways, meet me there in two hours."

"Okay. Sorry for waking you. See you in a bit." He hung up.

She yawned and got up, getting ready. She texted Ao privately.

- *Akari:** *I told Nao to meet me at the bar in 2 hours.*

- *Ao:** *Alright. Be there by then.*

- *Akari:** *Yep. See you there.*

She got dressed—comfortable attire with her Ashinuke jacket. She grabbed her phone and gun, then headed to the bar.

She got there and walked around to the back room. Whispering the password to the guards while looking around and on her toes, she pushed the door open. Surprisingly empty. Just her. She walked to the bar and poured herself a cold lemonade. Once ready, she carried it to one of the sofa seats, set it on the wooden table, and sat down. The sofa sunk under her. Relaxation washed over her, and she breathed out a long sigh. She brought the cold drink to her lips, enjoying the sweet and sour taste. *Heavenly.*

Her phone vibrated. She picked up.

"Yes?"

"Hey Akari, it's Ao. I'm outside the bar waiting with Nao."

"Oh, sweet. I'm in the back room. You can bring him in."

"Okay." She heard scuffles and talking before he cut the call.

It wasn't long before the back door opened, revealing Ao and Nao. She stood to greet them.

"Hey, you two. Hey, Nao." She reached her hand out, which he accepted.

"Hey, Eiji. You said you had news. Care to tell me?" He got straight to the point.

"Sure, take a seat." She pointed to the sofa. They scooted over as she walked toward the bar. "Want anything to drink?"

"I'll take a beer," Ao stated.

"I'll just have cold water, thanks." Nao smiled. "So where are we right now? Didn't you say we're meeting at a bar?"

She brought the drinks and sat opposite. She grabbed hers, brought it to her lips, feeling the liquid fizz before setting it down.

"This is the secret backroom of the bar, otherwise kept as the secret meeting place for my gang, Ashinuke."

"My gang?" Nao raised his glass of water.

"Yea, I'm the boss of Ashinuke." Nao spat out his water.

"What?! A teenage girl like you is the boss of a large gang like this?! Holy shit..." Nao looked at his brother, who just shrugged.

"Yea, so anyways, I'm going to tell you the truth about Terushima Sou, or the boss of the Red Aces." Nao nodded, urging her on. She looked up to face him. "Simply put, I killed him, and the Red Aces is secretly part of Ashinuke. We're planning on keeping both Ashinuke and the Red Aces members in the dark about this."

Nao stared, then suddenly stood.

"How could you kill him! I asked you for help, but I didn't mean to kill him!" He burst out, walking toward her and grabbing her collar.

She remained calm. "I was planning on killing him either way, regardless of whether you asked for help. My goal is to unite all of Yokohama, something Orochi and Ryūken were never able to do. It was necessary action." She stared at Nao, who gripped tighter, making it harder to breathe.

"Let her go, Nao." Ao spoke softly, tapping his brother's shoulder. Nao looked at him before letting go. She gasped a little, slumping back.

"Look, I know you're mad. But Terushima's greed would've ended his business. His greed would've gotten him caught, and the gang caught—the worst outcome for you. And Ao has joined Ashinuke's side, taking over Terushima's business and the position of the Red Aces' boss, alongside Daisuke. It'll be great if you would also help them out. Think of it as a top-secret mission."

Nao's eyes glistened at the mention of Terushima's worst outcome. Silence, then—

"Fine. I'll help out." He mumbled in defeat. She looked at Ao, who gave a small smile and a nod, grateful for the important role.

"So was the truce you?" Nao asked.

"Yep. It's a truce for the members of both gangs, but for those who know the truth, it's the secret unity of the Red Aces and Ashinuke, with Ashinuke ruling over West Yokohama. We are now one gang, although the men don't know."

"Are we planning on revealing it to the men soon?" Ao asked.

"Mhm. Not soon, but once everything has calmed down." She finished her lemonade, stood, took the empty glasses, and placed them in the sink.

"Anyway, that's all I wanted to discuss. Oh wait—for me here for a second."

She rushed toward the stage, disappeared behind the curtain, and reappeared holding two Ashinuke gang jackets, tossing them to Ao and Nao.

"Here, the official uniform, since you're part of us now." She gave them a wide smile. They accepted and wore them straight away.

"Thank you for this opportunity, Eiji." Nao nodded.

"No worries. Ao, add your brother to the group chat. Gang meetings are every Monday, so see you then." They left, leaving her alone.

- --

# CHAPTER SEVENTY-SEVEN

Half a year passed since Terushima Sou's death, and the alcohol business had gone through the roof— profits skyrocketing. Who knew the trio—Nao, Daisuke, and Ao—would work so well together at managing a business?

Oh, and running the Red Aces. The plan was working—members still believing nothing had changed. Although it was soon time to break the news of Terushima's death so the gang could finally be formed under the Ashinuke name.

She continued working at the bar alongside John and Akio (from time to time). Her hair was clean and tidy, back to the normal wolf cut, just longer—she'd recently visited the hairdresser. Kai's underground drug business was doing well, business coming and going.

Everything was going according to plan.

Within the past six months, the Fangs, who ruled the East, had cowered in fear from her growing power and disbanded, leaving the area in her hands. The Fangs' members disappeared into thin air with no trace—she assumed they'd joined the Bulldogs. That was trouble—the Bulldogs had risen in numbers, preparing for a gang war within the next few months.

However, Ashinuke now controlled all of Yokohama except the North.

She stood next to Ao at the meeting place of the Red Aces.

"Evening, members of Red Aces. I have some tragic news. I regret to inform you all, but the boss of the Red Aces has run away from his duties." Murmurs erupted as Ao continued. She felt the eyes staring.

"This person standing next to me is the boss of Ashinuke, Eiji. Our boss left a small note. Let me read it to you.

- Members of the Red Aces. Me leaving behind this letter means that I am in danger. I have run away

from everything I currently own to start a new life away from the city. In spite of this, I was able to meet the young boss of Ashinuke, Eiji. She has given me the greatest promise of taking care of my gang. So treat her as you would treat me. Accept her as your new boss. She will lead you all to the goal we all want achieved: the unification of all of Yokohama.*

- Sincerely, proud boss of the Red Aces.*

That is the final message from the boss." Ao folded the letter and pocketed it. "Now, I welcome Eiji to the microphone."

Silence. She walked forward from behind Ao.

"Hello, everyone. I'm Eiji. Nice to meet you all. I hope you will follow me to see the ultimate goal of the unification of Yokohama. The Red Aces will be no more. You are all now affiliated under the name of Ashinuke, so welcome to our gang. The truce is no more. However, you are now free to do whatever in Ashinuke's area, which currently resides everywhere but the North. Of course, some rules apply, including leaving the public out of our gang affairs. Other than that, I've got nothing else to say, except— "

She removed the microphone from close to her lips and yelled into it.

"WELCOME TO ASHINUKE!"

The crowd roared. She took a step back as Ao took the microphone back, smiling at her.

The Red Aces were finally no more, with the Bulldogs her only worry. She traveled back to the bar with Ao in his car. She walked through the back door, where Akio was drinking alone. She assumed Daisuke and Nao were at their office, and Kai at his place.

Akio seemed relaxed, drinking the alcohol he served himself.

"Everything alright, Akio?" She sat next to him. Ao sat on the other side.
