# CHAPTER SEVENTY-EIGHT

The dial tone rang. Once. Twice. Three times. Four. Nothing. She was about to hang up when the tone stopped. Sanzu had picked up.

"Hello?" His voice rang through her ears. She started to smile. "Hello?" He repeated.

"Oh! Hey, Sanzu. How have you been?" She was a little nervous.

"I'm fine. Back to first names already, sweetheart? Did you forget about me?" His teasing tone. She laughed.

"Sorry. I've just been so busy here. If anything, I'm a bit overwhelmed." She sighed, a little heavier than expected.

"Really now? What on earth is happening back in Yokohama?" She heard shuffling in the background.

She explained everything—from breaking up Orochi and Ryūken, to leading the new gang Ashinuke, to reuniting all of Yokohama. Not to mention learning bartending and the businesses associated with Ashinuke.

"No wonder you're so busy. You have a lot going on." Sanzu said quietly. She noticed his change in attitude.

"What's wrong, babe?" she asked softly.

"I—I, when are you coming back?" Sanzu suddenly raised his voice a little.

Her heart broke at his stuttering. She knew how much it had taken him to ask. But even she didn't know the answer.

"I don't know yet. I have yet to unify Yokohama. And even if I do soon, it'll take another couple months to stabilize everything. So, it might be another six months. Earliest."

"I see. I just miss you. I want to see you. I want to touch and hold you. I want to see you smile. I want to—"

"I know. I want to do all those things too. I miss you too. If I could jump through the phone, I would! I know the trip is only two hours by train, but I can't afford to leave the gang alone until I defeat the Bulldogs. Once I know it's safe, I'll come over to see you, but I'm gonna have to eventually come back to check up on everything too."

The line went quiet. Awfully quiet.

"Sanzu? Hello?"

"Yes, I'm still here." He replied softly. "Yea, I understand. What's your plan from here on?"

"Unify all of Yokohama, then stabilize the chain of businesses affiliated with Ashinuke. Once I see that everything is perfect, I can leave Yokohama and come back to you."

"Okay. Just be careful whenever you do anything, okay? Don't rush. Be patient."

"I know. It just became that little bit harder not to rush after hearing your voice, you know?" She heard him laugh a little. She was dying inside, not being able to see his smile.

"We're all waiting for you here," Sanzu said, feeling him smile.

He paused. "Akari." Serious.

"Yes?"

"You know how Mikey disbanded Touman?"

"Yeah, I know. Talking about Mikey—how is he?"

"Mikey made a new gang. Kantou Manji Gang, with Mikey as the leader. He's offered you a spot." Sanzu said, a little rushed.

"I'll figure everything out when I get back, okay? I'm going to concentrate on Yokohama first. Is Mikey doing okay, though?"

Another silence, then a long sigh.

"I think it's better if you come here and see for yourself. He's changed quite a bit. He might change back a little when you return, though."

"I see. Barely holding himself together, then." She understood through his sentence. "Give him my best regards. You can tell him everything. Say I'll be back in a year or so."

"Sure thing, sweetheart—" It felt great to hear that pet name from his lips again.

"Anyway, I've got to go now. My advisor is waiting downstairs."

"Yeah, of course. Talk to you soon?"

"I'll try, but no promises. Maybe once I've defeated the Bulldogs." She grinned.

"Make sure to beat the shit out of them, yeah?"

"Hell yea!"

"I love you."

"I love you too. Bye, babe." Her voice pained.

"Talk to you soon, sweetheart." He hung up.

It was painful to hear his voice so pixelated. It hurt not being able to see him in the flesh. It hurt knowing he was hurting. She tucked her phone into her pocket, stood, walked out of the office, and locked the doors. She rode the elevator down, walked out the automatic doors, and saw Daisuke's car waiting in the car park. The headlights turned on the second she walked out. The car rolled forward. Daisuke stopped in front of her, and she opened the door, sliding into the passenger seat.

"Did everything go well?" He asked softly, driving out of the car park.

"Yeah. I miss him, though. Can't wait to see him." A long pause before Daisuke spoke.

"You're planning on uniting all of Yokohama, waiting for it to stabilize, then heading back, aren't you?"

Her eyes widened. *She didn't think she was that readable.*

"Was it obvious?"

"No. Just a hunch." He took a turn onto the highway.

"You're okay with it?"

"Mmm, not really. I wish you would stay, since you are the boss and everything, but you've got your own personal reasons, and I respect that. Make sure you tell the others before you disappear, okay?" She nodded, grateful for his logical thinking. He knew she was going to leave without letting the others know. "We're adults. We can handle the businesses just fine. I'm sure they will understand your reasonings. You've united us all under the name of Ashinuke. We'll uphold that name. Just visit us sometime—either with him or alone." He gave a small side glance and smiled.

"Yeah, I will. Thanks, Daisuke."

"Now, we just have to end the Bulldogs. That's the most important thing at the moment. Any plans?"

"I've got two. One: we invade them. And two: we invade."

"That's only one option, Akari."

"I know. There's only one way to go about this—an all-out war." Daisuke hummed in agreement.

"When are you planning on doing so?"

"In two or so months. I need to get the men ready and let them know." She remembered she had a huge gang of 600 men by now. The Bulldogs had just over 400—a winning battle.

"Okay, I'll let the advisors know. You make sure to tell all the men tomorrow night about the plans. While I'm at it, I'll capture a Bulldogs member, and you can take it from there."

"Oooh, that's a great idea. Bring me the Bulldogs member the day after tomorrow."

"Of course." He slowed, having arrived at her place. "Have a goodnight, Akari. See you tomorrow night."

She stepped out, closed the door, waved as he drove away. She walked heavily into her apartment, shut the door, and flopped onto the couch, tired and stressed.

"Hey, Ashinuke! I have some important news. In exactly two months, on the 26th of June, Ashinuke will be butting heads with the Bulldogs. It will be the final showdown. It is the first and last war we will ever have here in Yokohama. We will come out victorious! We will beat the Bulldogs and gain control of all of Yokohama!" The members cheered. "Make sure to prepare yourselves. Two months will go by in no time, so let's do the most we can before this date. That's all for now, see you all next week."

The members chanted her name as she walked off the stage and behind the curtain, where Akio and Daisuke waited in all black.

"Are you both going now?" She looked at them.

"Yep, we'll be back before you know it," Akio said, smiling.

"Wait here for us. Better to do this all in one night." Daisuke tied his shoelaces.

"Okay. I'll be working on the other side. If you bring them here, just ring the bell." She walked out of the curtain toward the bar.

"Gotchu," she heard Akio say.

It was going to be another long night. She served multiple drinks. The orders kept coming, but it was fun—seeing the enjoyment on their faces. Satisfaction, joy. And of course, the small group who just had to order Daisuke's alcohol and cause trouble. Giving them water without them realizing was difficult.

Soon enough, the members left, leaving behind a messy room. The back door opened—Nao and Ao.

"Oh, hey you two."

"Evening. We came to help clean up, if that's okay," Nao began picking up cans.

"Aww, thank you." She grabbed a black plastic bag and set it in the middle. The three of them picked up cans and threw them in. Once done, Ao tied the bag and placed it in the corner. She picked up a broom and swept while Nao and Ao moved the furniture out of the way, along the walls, for the Bulldogs' interrogation session.

She swept the dust into a smaller dustpan, disposed of it under the bar counter.

"That's all. Thank you guys so much!" She quickly made their favorite drinks and handed them over.

"Thanks for the drinks," Ao said.

"Don't worry about the help. We're glad to be of service." Nao smiled, drinking quickly.

The bell rang from the other side. She stood and walked toward the connective door.

"I think it's best for you to leave this room before Daisuke and Akio return. Leave the glasses in the sink. I'll clean them later. See you all soon!" She pulled the door open, walked through the narrow corridor, opened the door on the other side, and rushed to John's side.

Orders came quickly, which she made quickly. Of course, the occasional comments. "Aren't you a little too young to work here?" "Take off your mask, darl." "Looking snazzy." And all that inappropriate behavior irritated her, but she had no choice. Sometimes they touched her inappropriately, and she wanted to punch the living shit out of them, but she couldn't. So she just mixed a little of Daisuke's alcohol into their drink. Honestly, it was on them. John seemed to notice but didn't say a word—if anything, he seemed content, laughing at times.

Tonight was extremely busy, orders coming left and right. She made a drink, passed it to Yui, and another order came through—no chance to rest. It took a lot of energy. *Think of it as stamina building.* With that mentality, she continued until the fated bell rang on the other side. John sighed, knowing he was alone with all the drinks.

"I'll call Akio over so you can relax a little." She whispered. His shoulders relaxed. He nodded and shooed her to the other room.

Opening the door, she saw a bruised, gagged, blindfolded man bound tightly to the chair—reminding her of Ao half a year ago. She looked at Akio and motioned him over.

"Yes?"

"Can you help John? Tonight's super busy, considering it's a Monday."

Akio sighed and rushed behind the curtain to change into his bartending clothes before heaving himself through the door.

"Now, Daisuke. Who is this?"

"One of the men of the Bulldogs. He works directly under the vice-leader." He replied instantly.

"Oh! That's great. He can relay our message with ease, then!" She walked over and removed his blindfold with a harsh tug. She removed her gun from her back and pointed it at his head. His fear grew immediately—sweat forming faster.

"Heya there. I'm Eiji, boss of Ashinuke. And this man here to my left is Daisuke, one of my advisors. We kidnapped you for only one reason—to make you relay our message. Understand?" He nodded, mouth gagged.

"Okay, good. I need you to tell your vice-leader that Ashinuke and the Bulldogs will have an all-out melee on the docks of Yokohama on the 26th of June, in exactly two months. Winner decides whatever they want to do with the other gang." She stared down harshly. She could almost hear him whimpering. She sighed internally, removed her gun, and placed it back.

Immediately, he relaxed.

"Hey, hey, hey, don't relax yet." He tensed. She removed his gag. "Just tell me one thing. How does the Bulldogs make their money?"

He whimpered, jaw quaking. "We don't have a business or anything of the sort. The boss is wealthy, and we just do whatever we like. We follow the boss's orders, but other than that, we do whatever we like."

Daisuke looked at her and nodded, proving his innocence.

"Okay, cool. Daisuke, you can drive him back to wherever you found him." Daisuke placed the blindfold back over his eyes and guided him to the car.

"You can go home and rest, boss." Daisuke urged once the man was locked in.

"I'm gonna finish up here for work first. See you soon. Have a goodnight, Daisuke." She headed toward the secret door.

"Mm, take care." He got into the car and drove away.

She entered the main side to find everything under control—John and Akio taking orders with ease.

"Akari," John called. She turned.

"Yes?"

"You can go home early. Take a good rest. I'm sure you're tired from all your duties." As if on cue, she let out a large yawn, tears brimming. "The yawns say it all." John laughed, motioning her away from the counter.

She sighed in defeat, walked around, and headed to the door.

"I'll take my leave, then. See you all soon." She pushed the door open and walked out into the empty street.

She was sure it was the same for him. It made her more anxious but more motivated to defeat the Bulldogs faster. She was going to defeat them and get Yokohama stable, then rush home to Tokyo—into Sanzu's waiting arms.

# CHAPTER SEVENTY-NINE

- *TWO MONTHS LATER**

Buildings passed by quickly, warm air circulating inside the car. The drive to the docks was silent, even though all seats were taken—her in the passenger, Kai, Akio, and Ao in the back, Daisuke driving. Traffic slowed the pace. The wind stopped, and a distant motorcycle echoed. How she missed riding on the back of Sanzu's motorcycle.

"Boss, we'll be there in five minutes," Akio announced.

"Okay, thanks, Akio." She responded coldly, not taking her eyes off the scenery. Late evening, sun already setting, the sky blood red.

Daisuke took a tight right, and a few minutes later they were at the docks. So many men—all Ashinuke. She opened the car door, walked out, closed it softly, and brushed wrinkles from her gang jacket, worn with pride. The crest of dragons and swords painted the back. She walked with confidence to the front, boots clicking. Daisuke and Akio followed, holding flags with the Ashinuke emblem.

"Let's go," she mumbled, walking toward the center where the Bulldogs' boss waited with four men. Two of them—the Haitani brothers.

She clicked her tongue in annoyance and continued walking, ignoring the brothers.

"Hope you don't mind, Eiji, but we brought some overseers. The well-known Rulers of Roppongi, the—" The Bulldogs' boss spoke.

"Haitani brothers. Yes, I know." She cut him off, glaring.

"Nice to see you again, love~" Ran looked down at her, smiling. Rindou just stared at her face, like there was something on it.

"Out of jail already? Nice to see nothing has changed." She spat playfully at Ran.

"Awww, you missed us that much?" Ran teased.

"Oh, please." She gave him a sly smirk. "Can we get started already?" She met Ran's stare, then looked back at the Bulldogs' boss. Ran returned the smirk and looked at the boss.

"An all-out melee?" They both nodded. "No illegal weapons—guns, etc. The winner will be whoever remains standing."

They shook hands—awkward. She and Hiro (the Bulldogs' boss) turned their backs and walked to their gangs.

"Ready? Go." Ran lacked energy, but it was enough to signal the start.

Men from Ashinuke rushed forward, Bulldogs did the same—blue and black uniforms clashing at the center. Daisuke and Akio planted the flags.

"We're off." Daisuke went with Akio. They'd work well together.

She was alone with the flags. She knew she'd have to fight too, so she walked slowly onto the battlefield.

It was tough fighting grown men—but she never expected this. They all charged with weapons. Sure, Ran said no illegal weapons, but he meant guns, snipers, those types. Ten men now held pipes or knives. They charged at once, forming a tight circle.

One charged straight forward. She grabbed his wrist, removed the weapon—a knife—and gripped it tightly. She dashed under his body as cover. The pipe men stopped mid-attack, not wanting to hit their own. She let go and dashed toward one with a pipe, launching a spinning heel kick into his open

abdomen. He flew backward. She used the momentum, turning a full 180 and throwing the knife high into the air. Their eyes followed it as she launched a barrage of punches and kicks while they were distracted. She moved out of the way as the knife fell, impaling the ground.

She backflipped toward the knife, picked it up, and armed herself again. She rushed the four remaining, threw the knife into one man's leg—loud scream, clutching his thigh, falling. The other three looked at him, wondering what happened. She rushed behind one and knocked him out with a chop to the neck.

Two left. They swung their pipes desperately as she created distance. They kept rushing as she moved backward. She looked around—getting cornered. Annoyed, she stopped and rushed at full speed. Just as she got in range, she dropped and slid underneath one man's legs, running back to the center.

She rushed back to the unconscious men and looked for a new weapon. A pipe—she disliked it. Best option: a knife. But hardly any time to look. Men kept rushing like rats.

- This was going to take too long.*

She was tempted to let the darkness take over, but it didn't feel right.

"Eiji!" Kai's familiar voice.

"Kai? What's—" A pipe struck the back of her head from one of the men she'd knocked out earlier. She landed on her knees. The world spun. The familiar warmth of blood trickled down her forehead and face, almost bringing a small smile.

She was lifted back to her feet, arms locked behind her back. *The familiar feeling of deja vu. Valhalla fight.* Funny—the Haitani brothers were watching this one too. She took a few punches and kicks to the abdomen, coughing out spit and blood, then whacked over the head again.

"F... off," she mumbled, anger growing.

"What was that, missy?" The man holding her arms jeered.

"Fuck off!" She widened her stance, stomped one leg against the floor, and lifted the other high above her head. Her body tilted, causing the man holding her arms to fall off balance. Once he fell, she readied her elbow and fell onto him, digging it into his stomach. The guy with the pipe rushed closer—she evaded, and he hit his mate instead. She grabbed his arm and flung him over her back, slamming him down.

Still dazed, she looked up at the sky, hoping to lessen the dizziness.

She looked around and stopped moving. The all-too-familiar red gang uniform in the far corner, near the shipping containers. A figure she recognized all too well.

- Izana.*

She thought she was dreaming, but it looked too much like him. Platinum white hair, red coat. It had to be.

She shuffled her feet and ran in his direction, fighting everyone in her way. The Bulldogs charged, trying to stop her. No trouble. She was blinded by Izana, who continued to appear and disappear behind the multiple people in front of her.

Punches, swinging heel kicks, occasional knockout temple kicks when she had room. Soon enough, she reached the other end where she'd last seen him.

"Izana?" she choked out, desperately looking. "Izana! I know you're hiding somewhere." Tears brimmed.

"Love, what are you doing here, calling out his name like that?" Ran looked at her with plain, boring eyes, showing a small hint of curiosity.

"Didn't you just see him? He was right there—" A small flash of red moved closer. She was frozen, staring at the blank space between her and where Ran and Rindou sat.

"I think she's hallucinating," Rindou whispered to his brother.

'Izana' floated effortlessly toward her, circling her frozen body. Her eyes tracked his every move. He stopped next to her ear and whispered.

"Baton... beat... Hiro... miss... you."

A sudden chill of wind—Izana's red uniform and outline disappeared into thin air. She turned to where he'd vanished.

"Miss you too," she choked out, tears flowing. She calmed herself, wiping her tears with the edge of her sleeves.

She'd deciphered his message instantly.

She walked toward Ran with light feet and extended her hand.

"What is it, love? You want my hand?" Ran drew swirls on her palm, then laced his fingers with hers. She ignored the flirtation.

"Can I borrow your baton? Please?" She looked up, determined.

Ran's eyes met hers. He sighed heavily, reached into his pocket, and handed it over.

"Make sure to give it back. Clean." He spat out as she extended her arm, the baton fully unsheathing.

"Of course. Thanks, love—" She teased back. His eyes widened, a small tint of red on his ears.

She rushed away and headed toward Hiro, sitting on one of the containers, overlooking the battle. She climbed from behind, crawling slowly, and whacked the back of his head with Ran's baton.

Hiro slumped. *Way too easily—it shocked her.* He was sitting, watching, in his blue Bulldogs jacket, a Gucci white dress shirt underneath, expensive boots. Not appropriate fight clothing.

She grabbed him by his well-gelled hair—disgusting to touch—lifted his head, and showed the men. Ashinuke members yelled, welcoming the victory.

Hiro suddenly twitched, arm moving in a smooth stabbing motion. She noticed early—turned her body to the side, lowered, moved back. He'd attempted to stab her chest. A twinge of pain in her arm—his knife had grazed her upper arm, leaving a gash. Blood instantly seeped, dripping off her fingertips.

"Oh, isn't that nice." Hiro cackled deep in his throat. "Nice movement you've got, girly. Shame you're a girl, though. If your dad had made you a boy, this fight would have been so much more entertaining."

"Oh, shut up. If anything, you're lucky you're a man, or else you would've been dead ages ago." She smirked widely, rushing forward.

She swung the baton at his head—dodged. She'd prepared a knee to his stomach. It connected, bending him over. While bent, she lifted his head by his hair and swung the baton hard into his face. A familiar crack—his nose. She swung again—another satisfying crack—his cheekbone. He slumped to his knees. She gripped his hair, flung him a little into the air, swung around, and made sure her heel contacted. He flew to the next shipping container, one level down. The thump echoed—everybody heard. The men below ceased fighting, looking at Hiro's state and her triumphant pose.

The Ashinuke men went wild, chanting her name.

She hopped down to his container, where he lay passed out.

"Why'd he talk so big if he was so weak?" she mumbled.

Footsteps behind her—she turned, steadying for another fight.

"Relax, love. We're here to check his state." Ran.

She relaxed. Ran walked over, stared down at Hiro, squatted, and smacked his face. Harshly. Hiro's eyes split open, and he shuffled away toward the edge.

"You're gonna fall if you continue that way," she said calmly, pointing to the edge. Hiro turned his head slowly, looked down—at least ten meters. An ear-piercing scream. She giggled at his disappointing state.

"You're a disappointment to your men. And to your mother who gave birth to such a wimp-like 'son.'" She quoted 'son,' mocking him.

Terror in his eyes, mumbling incomprehensible words.

Ran extended his hand to stop her. Rindou moved closer and listened. He nodded and stood, pointing at Hiro.

"He said he surrenders. He says Yokohama is now yours."

Her face lit up. She walked to the edge of the container and yelled at the top of her lungs.

"Men of Ashinuke!" Hundreds of eyes. "We have emerged victorious! Yokohama is now ours!"

Roars erupted, jumping and hopping. She turned back to the brothers.

"Here you go, Ran." She handed the baton back, wiped clean on her jacket.

"Hey, Akari—"

"It's Eiji for now, Rindou."

"Doesn't matter. What's with you and Izana earlier?" He looked at her with an irritated face, not actually wanting to talk.

"Awww, don't be so cold to me, Rindou—" She teased, grabbing his arm. He tensed.

"Oh, get off! You filth—"

"Noo, what about me~! I was nice enough to let you borrow my baton too!" Ran whined, jealous.

She wondered how she'd gotten so friendly with the brothers. She didn't know—it just happened. Sure, she'd been with them in juvie, but she'd always tagged along with Izana and Kakucho, never paying much attention. But it was fun. She smiled to herself. She was happy. The past year had been so stressful—no time to interact with someone her age, not to mention someone she knew.

"Come here, then~" She teased as Ran happily ran up, sweeping her into a tight hug. Like babysitting a young child.

"Man, your boyfriend's gonna be jealous. Just wait till I tell him."

"Oh, you wouldn't!" She looked up as he loosened his grip.

"Answer the question, Jesus." Rindou was annoyed.

"Oh, yea. I saw Izana. He led me to you and told me to beat Hiro with your baton. I don't know why—he just did." She shrugged as Ran released her.

"He's looking over you. He was probably a little worried." Ran spoke softly.

"He's got nothing to worry about, though." She looked down at the floor, then remembered the current situation—her advisors still looking up at her conversing with the brothers.

"I'm gonna go now. Thanks for overseeing the fight, you two." She turned heel, but Ran grabbed her wrist.

"Are you coming back to Tokyo? At all?"

"Hmm? Yeah, I'll be back before Christmas, I guess. Why? You miss me?" She teased.

"Rokuhara Tendai wants to recruit you," Rindou stated.

"What? Another gang?"

"What do you mean, 'another'? Did you already get asked?" Ran questioned, letting go of her wrist.

"Well, yeah. I called Sanzu the other day, and he said Mikey has a spot for me in his gang. So you already know my decision, if anything." She shrugged, walking to the edge.

"Kakucho is in Rokuhara Tendai too," Rindou exclaimed.

She stopped and turned back.

"Yeah, my answer is still the same." She raised her hand and hopped down, rushing toward her advisors.

- --

The car ride was lively compared to the ride there. Everyone was bruised and injured, somewhat bloody. The blood on her forehead had long dried, though her head still pounded. Everyone was happy—the unification of Yokohama, the ultimate goal of Ashinuke, was finally complete.

Daisuke drove everyone to the bar to drink and party while nursing their wounds. But he forced her to remain in the car and drove her home. She got home and immediately rushed to the bathroom to treat her wounds. Once done, she sighed a long breath and landed on the couch, passing out.

- --

# CHAPTER EIGHTY

- *SANZU POV**

He woke to the annoying birds on the windowsill. It took all his being not to reach for the gun and shoot them. *It's only 6 AM, Jesus.* Better to get up now than sleep again and suffer later.

Rolling his eyes, he sat up, swung his legs off the side, and sat for a couple minutes, random thoughts going round and round. Finally, a small ounce of motivation—he stood and walked sluggishly to the bathroom. Thankfully, he'd laid out clothes yesterday.

He tied his hair up, washed his face, brushed his teeth, rinsed and gargled, and changed into cleaner clothes, making sure he looked 'neat' in the mirror. He hovered toward the kitchen, grabbing whatever fruit his hand landed on, slipped on his shoes, and headed out to start the motorbike.

It felt empty, as it had for the past two years. The drive to the office was long, passing multiple cars, drivers giving looks of disappointment as he whizzed past.

Arriving at the office building, he parked and walked in. Taking the elevator to the top floor, he knocked on the main door. No response. He pushed it open and glanced around—nobody. He walked in and saw Mikey sleeping on the leather couch, a little tint of red under his eyes. He stared a little too long—Mikey noticed and suddenly opened his eyes wide.

"Don't you have anything better to do than stare?" Mikey scoffed, sitting up.

"Yes, boss. My apologies." He walked toward his office door.

Opening it, he was welcomed by the stack of papers on his desk. Sighing, he closed the door softly and headed to his desk, ready for a long day.

- --

It was about noon, and he'd just decided to take a break when his phone vibrated. He answered while completely relaxed.

"Who's this?" he demanded, annoyed.

"Wow, that's a little too cold, don't you think, babe?" The familiar voice shocked him—he jolted forward, catching Mikey's attention from the leather couch.

"Mmm, my bad. So? You won?" He tried to get straight to the point.

"Yeah, I did! Yokohama is all under my control right now! It feels unreal, honestly." He could hear her joyful tone.

"That's great, sweetheart! Congratulations!"

"Thank you, babe!" A pause. "Babe?"

"Hmm?"

"How much do you know about Rokuhara Tendai?"

The phone slipped out of his hand. He scurried to pick it up, feeling Mikey's eyes following.

"Hello?"

"Yes, yes, I'm here. Why do you ask?"

"I saw the Haitani brothers at the final fight. They were the overseers." He gritted his teeth. *They must've told her something.*

"I think it's better if you come back first. Then we'll tell you everything." He looked up, past Mikey, at the far wall. Mikey's eyes grew brighter, ears perking.

Mikey stared hard, and Sanzu couldn't help but turn to him. He motioned for the phone. Reluctantly, Sanzu passed it over. Mikey clicked the speakerphone button, placed it on the table, and talked into it.

"Hey, Akari-chin, it's Mikey." Monotone.

"Ohh, Mikey! How have you been?"

"I'm fine. How are things going over there? Good, I assume?"

"Yeah! I defeated all the gangs in Yokohama. I have all of Yokohama in the palm of my hands!" She laughed.

"That's good, then. And? What made Sanzu drop his phone?" He looked over at Sanzu.

The main door opened—Koko walked in.

"Hey, boss, I finished with the che—" Sanzu held his fingers to his lips. Koko looked at Mikey and the phone on speakerphone, understood, and shuffled to the sofa.

"Oh, he dropped his phone. Must be important, then." She snickered, then background noises. "Eiji, everything is ready." "Oh, thank you, Daisuke. I'll be there soon, gimme a minute."

"Yeah, so I asked him how much he knew about Rokuhara Tendai." Mikey's eyes widened; Koko stared, slowly shuffling to get all the drama.

"How do you know about them? You don't have men here in Tokyo, do you?" Mikey asked, pressuring.

"Huh? No, of course not. I fought with the last gang of Yokohama a few days back, and I saw the Haitani brothers. They were there to oversee the match. They told me Rokuhara Tendai wanted to recruit me." Mikey breathed out a large sigh, holding his head in his hands.

"And what'd you say?"

"I told them you'd already offered me a spot, so I declined."

Sanzu was immediately stared down by both Mikey and Koko. He swallowed thickly, but Akari kept going, thankfully causing them to turn back to the phone.

"He said Kakucho was in Rokuhara Tendai too. Is that true? Mikey?" Mikey stayed silent. Sanzu picked up the phone and answered instead.

"Yeah, he is." He looked down, knowing how much Kakucho meant to her.

"Okay, cool. I'll hear the rest of what you have to say when I come back, okay?" She tried to lighten the dark mood. She'd noticed the tension.

"Sure, be safe," he answered. "Love you, sweetheart~"

"Love you too, see you soon." Kiss sounds, sending a small blush across his cheeks. She cut the call.

"Nice way to make us feel single as shit, Sanzu." Koko scoffed, standing.

"Not my problem that you're stuck on someone dead." He snapped back, hitting the right spot. Koko was about to say something, then shut up.

Mikey didn't move, just stared, not coming back until Sanzu flashed his hand over his face.

"Boss? You good?"

"Yea." He responded coldly. "Just wishing she'll be back soon. I have a lot to—" He stopped, silence spreading, hanging dreadfully.

"She'll be back before we know it," Sanzu said, trying to reassure him.

- Hope you come back soon.*

- --

- *AKARI POV**

The next six months went by in a whizz as everything settled. Ashinuke members roamed freely, no more gangs in Yokohama, nothing to worry about—especially fights. Sure, some despised her for murdering the previous bosses, but what could you do? She didn't feel guilty—it was necessary. The only issue was Hiro, the Bulldogs' boss, but he had enough cash to be too large an asset to lose. So she asked Daisuke and Akio to bring him to the office building one night and forced him to work for her. He did, since he had nothing better to do anyway—his men were under Ashinuke too.

During these six months, she hadn't called Sanzu or heard any news from Tokyo. Seeing the Haitani brothers at the fight was shocking, but she'd gotten friendlier with them. She was on alright terms now, even if they'd done shit in the past. Not to mention, the only issue was that they were part of Rokuhara Tendai, and she was 'joining' the Kantou Manji Gang. A little worrying, but nothing she could do.

Since all gangs were under Ashinuke, she had more time to learn bartending and do what she liked— relaxing, sleeping in. Being a leader of a large gang was tiring and stressful.

John was super impressed with her skills and happy to let her run the bar on her own. He seemed pleased at the thought of a few nights off, though she'd have to disappoint him. She almost always had Daisuke and Akio with her during boss work, showing them what it was like. Daisuke understood quickly and didn't say a word, while Akio absorbed everything she spat out, occasionally confused but never pushing by asking.

- --

It was the last day in Yokohama. She'd asked Daisuke to pick her up and drive her to the bar. He was already one step ahead, asking all the advisors to meet before she'd even asked. The black car waited in front of the apartment she'd spent the last two years in. She'd packed everything neatly into the suitcase she'd brought from Tokyo—filled to the brim. The apartment was now empty and bare.

She rolled her suitcase out, walked down the stairs carefully, and loaded it into the car.

"I'm going to go talk to the landlord. Be back in a bit." Daisuke nodded, closing the trunk, and slid into the driver's seat.

She walked to the landlord's apartment, paid a quick visit, said her 'thank yous' for dealing with late monthly payments, then turned heel and headed back.

She opened the passenger door, slid in, and strapped on her seatbelt. "Okay, let's go."

The drive to the bar was quiet and surprisingly awkward. Daisuke finally broke the silence as she stared out the window.

"Last day, huh? How fast time flies by..." He sighed, looking at the road.

"Yeah, the past two years were amazing, honestly." She took a quick breath. "I'm going to miss everything here, but it'll be good to go home."

Daisuke hummed and continued in silence. She turned her head back to the buildings whizzing past.

- --

Arriving at the back door, the guards gave a small smile and opened the door without awaiting the password. Walking inside, she was met with the glum, pained faces of her advisors. They all gave a small smile before ushering her to the front, onto the stage.

"Wait, wait, why are you doing this?" Akio pushed her up to the front. He stopped when she reached the center, then hopped down and stood in front of her as she gazed at the advisors below. Kai, Akio, Daisuke, Ao, and Nao all bowed their heads—a full ninety degrees, the largest form of respect.

"Thank you for the last two years, boss!" They shouted as she froze. John was there too, watching from afar, also bowing.

"Please, lift your heads. I don't deserve this respect!" She shook her hands out, disagreeing. They lifted their heads and looked up. She looked at Daisuke—he just smiled and shrugged. "I can't believe you told them. I was gonna break it to them myself."

"Sorry, but I felt like you weren't going to tell them the truth," Daisuke replied, coolly.

She sighed, dropped down off the stage, walked to one of the couches, and sat.

"Okay, so as you've heard, I'm heading back to Tokyo. My job here is done. That's pretty much everything summed up. But I might come back a couple times to say hello." She gave a small smile.

"Why are you heading back though..." Nao whined. "We don't want you to leave. Are you gonna disband the gang? After everything?"

"I'm going home. I've got my family waiting for me." She immediately thought of Sanzu, Mikey, and Kakucho before continuing. "I know you don't want me to leave, but they're waiting for my return. And no, I'm not disbanding the gang, since we made it this far. Look at how much the gang is profiting off the businesses. They're so interconnected—breaking it apart would be detrimental for everyone. That's why I'm leaving Akio and Daisuke to run the gang together. I want you all to work together and continue the name of Ashinuke."

"Yes, of course!" Akio answered with energy, happy to take on the role. Daisuke nodded and smiled a little wider, already knowing.

- --

The rest of the day went by slowly. She gave each advisor a long hug before leaving the bar for the last time. She turned, walked to the front of the bar, walked in, and sat on the stool she always sat at. It was already late, the bar crowded. John noticed and walked around the counter.

"Hey, John. Just wanted to say a massive thank you for everything you've done for me." She bowed, staring at the floor as she felt his hand on the back of her head.

"It was my pleasure. Hope to see you again in the future soon. Maybe you'll own your own bar one day—make sure to credit me for your skills." He gave a large smile. "Wait here for a minute."

He rushed back to the counter, disappeared underneath, and popped up holding an alcohol mixer—the metal shaker.

"Take it. It's for you. Customized too, with your name, Hana. And the Ashinuke symbol on the bottom." He sent a sly wink, smiling widely.

She felt herself smile from ear to ear, grateful for John's hard work drilling her on bartending for the past two years.

"Thank you, John! I'll be back soon." She bowed once more and left the bar, heading to the car parked in front.

- --

Rolling her suitcase in one hand, holding her train ticket in the other, she made her way to the platform. The train to go back home. To Tokyo.

The train waited another ten minutes. She boarded and found her seat. She stared out the window, observing the buildings of Yokohama she'd grown used to seeing. The doors closed, and the train started moving toward Tokyo.

She checked her phone—the group chat flooding with messages. She responded to each.

- *Akari:** *Thank you all for following me to achieve my goal. I doubt I will be back soon, but I will come

to visit.*

With that last message, she clicked the information button on the group chat panel and left. It was for the better—they could be targeted by whoever. It was to keep her beloved gang safe. She knew the advisors wouldn't be happy with her cutting ties, committing ashinuke essentially, but it was for the best. She was planning on changing her phone and number so she'd become untraceable.

It marked the end of the era—Eiji of Ashinuke.

- --

# CHAPTER EIGHTY-ONE

- *KAKUCHO POV**

- *SEVEN MONTHS AGO**

He was a little shocked to hear Akari's name tossed around at the Rokuhara Tendai meeting. He didn't think she'd be mentioned at all, since no one had seen her in two years.

He'd contacted Sanzu about a year ago, asking if he knew anything. All he said was, "She's going after her father's gang." Normally, that would catch anyone's attention, but she just disappeared. He wasn't surprised—it seemed very typical for her, considering how much her parents' gang had affected her life.

He was currently sitting at his designated spot around the table, next to South and Ran. Rindou sat next to Ran, as always, and Madarame next to him, and next to him, Mochizuki.

"Anyone heard from Akari these past few years?" Madarame asked, since the topic at hand was recruitment for new members.

"She would be a great asset," Ran exclaimed, smirking.

"Who?" South boomed.

"We were all in the same juvenile detention center in the past." Kakucho pointed to pretty much everyone except South. Since the Kantou battle, all Tenjiku executives had gone to prison for a year and a half. South gathered them again, but one person was missing—Mucho. No one had seen him since he'd left prison.

"What's she like?"

"A devil in the form of an angel," Ran cooed. Rindou and Kakucho just turned their heads as Ran shrugged.

"I meant skill-wise."

Ran slumped, embarrassed.

"On par with the Invincible Mikey," Rindou mumbled.

South nodded. "So where's she at now?"

"Nobody has seen her in two years. It's like she's been wiped off the Earth," Mochizuki exclaimed, tired of just watching.

They all turned and looked at Kakucho. He kept a straight face, absorbing their stares.

"What?"

"You know something, don't you?" South interrogated, looking deeper.

There was no way out.

"She's in Yokohama, going after her father's gang. That's all I know. But still, it shouldn't take so long, I don't think."

"Talking about Yokohama—the two of us got a request from someone called Hiro. Apparently he's the boss of some gang called Bulldogs and wants an overseer for a battle against another gang called Ashinuke." Ran chimed in.

"Maybe Akari will be there," Madarame exclaimed, a little too excited.

South hummed, thinking. "Ran, Rindou. Go oversee the battle. Let us know what happens when you come back."

The brothers nodded, and the meeting continued as normal.

- --

- *SIX MONTHS AGO**

The return of the Haitani brothers sparked excitement.

"What's the big news?" South asked as they sat around the table.

"We saw Akari. She's grown up so much!" Ran exclaimed, talking with energy.

"Get to the point, Ran." Kakucho wanted details.

"Ashinuke is her gang. She's the boss of Ashinuke, under the alias of Eiji. The battle against the Bulldogs decided who claimed all of Yokohama." Murmurs erupted.

"It was strange—she was leading a gang full of adults. Her gang was strong, and her executives seemed to be quite a force too. She seemed fine, though it seems Izana still 'haunts' her." Kakucho flinched at the name. "For a gang that size, money is a huge issue. But it didn't seem to be much of an issue from an outsider's perspective, so she's got some business or something going on."

"A business?" Madarame questioned.

"To make money, y'know," Mochizuki replied, slapping the back of Madarame's head.

"She said she'll be back around Christmas," Rindou chimed in, then said nothing more.

"Did you ask about her recruitment?" South pushed for the answer.

Ran shook his head. "No need. We lost the race."

"What? You're saying she's already in another gang other than the one in Yokohama?"

Ran nodded. "Kantou Manji Gang, isn't it?" He and Rindou nodded at South's comment.

"I even played the Kakucho card, but that didn't work." Ran exclaimed as Madarame snorted, holding in laughter.

"Sanzu and Mikey, huh?" Mochizuki sighed, disappointed.

"Nothing we can do. What's done is done. It's just that we've got a larger problem on our hands." Kakucho stated, and everyone nodded.

- Christmas is still a long way away. I wonder what she's doing over there for so long...*

- --

- *AKARI POV**

- *PRESENT**

She finally arrived at Tokyo station. It was Christmas Eve, and the station was less busy than normal. Nearing midnight, Tokyo was illuminated with neon signs.

Walking outside, she glanced at the winter scenery—snow falling onto the ground, littering the road in small white patches. It felt great to be back.

She caught a taxi waiting at the side of the station.

"Can you send me to xxxx?" The driver nodded and drove away.

She stared out the window at the familiar scene—past her middle school, then stopping in front of her apartment building. She tapped her bank card over the machine, paid, and pulled her suitcase out. The taxi pulled away as she made her way to her apartment door.

Standing in front of the door, she heard small noises from inside. Light showed from under the door. She remembered handing Sanzu an extra key—but why would he be here, of all places?

She pulled out her house key, untouched for a long while, and slowly pushed it into the keyhole. Turning with caution, she heard the familiar click and pushed the door open.

The light was on. Inside—Kokonoi, Mikey, and Sanzu, all sleeping on the floor, legs inside the kotatsu.

She slid off her heavy shoes, stored them away to not give herself away, and snickered at their state. She carefully lifted her heavy suitcase to her room, trying not to make any sound. Opening the bedroom door slowly, she smiled—everything untouched. She laid her suitcase on the floor and unpacked her clothes into the wardrobe, setting the dirty ones aside into the empty basket in the corner. She placed the empty suitcase under the bed and toppled onto her bed, which she'd missed. She faintly smelled Sanzu on the sheets. Laughing to herself, she dozed off.

- --

She woke to loud banging and voices from the kitchen/living room.

"That's not how you make cake batter!" Koko yelled, followed by a crash. A metal bowl with flour— coughing.

"Maybe you should go buy the KFC chicken, since you can't do anything else," Mikey stated, no emotion. It concerned her a little. When she walked past him last night, she noticed him sniffling, some redness under his eyes as he gripped the kotatsu blanket tightly.

"That's for dinner, though, not breakfast!" Sanzu yelled, clearly stressed. "Why are we even making cake in the morning?!"

"Because if we want to put icing, it needs to cool?" Koko snapped. "And because you dropped the floursugar mixture, we don't have any more! We need to go buy some." He sighed, irritated.

"I'm hungry," Mikey whined quietly.

"Fine, we'll all have to go shopping for ingredients for the cake, and tonight's dinner while we're at it." Sanzu noted.

Silence, then the door closing.

She opened the bedroom door and checked the house—no one. She sneaked to the kitchen and saw the mess the boys had left. Sighing, she started cleaning the spilled flour and sugar, tipping it into the bin. She opened the fridge, took out eggs and bacon, grabbed ketchup and bread from the pantry. She made a quick omelet, fried the bacon in the same pan, toasted the bread, smeared ketchup on each slice, and placed the eggs and bacon on top—making four bacon-and-egg sandwiches. She took one, sat behind the kitchen counter, and ate, waiting for the boys to arrive and see the sandwiches and cleaned mess.

The door opened, the noise starting up again.

"Like I said, the cake is necessary. It's Christmas!" Koko yelled as Sanzu argued about it not being necessary.

"I'm still hungry," Mikey whined again. But he quickly turned quiet when he saw the sandwiches on the counter. A moment of silence as they noticed the mess had disappeared.

"Who's there?" Koko asked threateningly. She tried to hold her laughter in. Mikey was already munching on the sandwich.

"It's nice. And warm." Mikey already knew the person would still be here.

Not able to hold it in any longer, she jumped out from behind the counter and screamed.

"MERRY CHRISTMAS, BITCHES!"

Koko and Sanzu flinched, as Mikey continued nibbling. Their eyes widened, jaws dropped.

"Akari?" Sanzu stared from her feet to the tip of her head. "Is it really you?"

She smiled, looked deep into his eyes, and widened her arms.

"It sure is."

Sanzu dropped the bag of groceries and rushed around the counter, sweeping her into his arms, grabbing her so tightly.

"I missed you so much." He said into her neck. She felt warm from the inside, inhaling his homely scent, wrapping her arms around his neck.

"I missed you too." She backed her head away and leaned into his face. She placed two small kisses on the scars on both sides of his lips before kissing him softly on the lips.

He returned the kiss with such passion and love. *How much she missed this.*

A cough in the room. They parted.

"We get it, no need to shove it in our faces, you two," Koko scoffed.

"Sorry that you're jealous," Sanzu snapped back.

She walked over to Koko and gave him an awkward hug. "I don't know you too well, but Merry Christmas, I guess." She smiled.

Koko returned the hug. "Merry Christmas to you too. I guess I'll get to know you better over time." He stuck out his tongue playfully as he let go.

She looked over to Mikey, who stared with such empty, dark eyes—but a small glimmer of hope. His eyes becoming a little watery.

She grabbed Mikey by the wrist and ran toward the front door. Slipping on random shoes, she forced him out into the cold. She led him to the staircase and sat down, dragging Mikey down with her.

"I'm back, Mikey." She leaned into him, embracing his body in a tight hug. He was reluctant, but wrapped his arms around her waist. Faint sniffles. He was crying.

She patted his back up and down softly, trying to calm him.

"Welcome back, Akari." He replied, sniffling.

"You're not okay, are you? You were holding everything in. I'm back now. I'll be your shoulder to cry on. Now tell me what's wrong."

"It's not like I don't like the gang, but I feel like I'm supposed to carry on Izana's wishes. To be the strongest criminal syndicate in all of Tokyo." He choked out.

She understood.

"What happened to all the Touman members?"

"I haven't seen them in two years. You're not aware, but Takemitchy is a time leaper. He came twelve years from the future to save Hinata from dying. He should've achieved the perfect future, where everyone is happy, so he hasn't returned. It's been two years since he went back, and things have been like this. I distanced myself from everyone after the last Touman meeting. Since Takemitchy hasn't come back, it means that I'm doing the right thing. But why do I feel so unsatisfied? Is what I'm doing so wrong? I want to see them too! I want to be happy, but I keep being pulled back by—" Mikey teared up more, a large patch appearing on her shoulder.

She rubbed his back.

"Mikey, listen. I'll follow you, okay? Sanzu will too. We've stuck by you from the 8/3 incident, and I'm not planning on leaving anytime soon. So if you need someone to talk to, to cry with, we'll be right here. Sure, me and Sanzu are a little crazy in our own ways, but we're here for you. So don't be afraid to let us know." He looked up, wiping his tears. "I'll make you happy. Sanzu and Koko will do the same, I'm sure. So we won't leave you. I'll fulfill Izana's wishes with you. Let's face the future. Together."

Mikey nodded and hugged her tighter.

"Thanks, Akari-chin." He mumbled softly.

"Mmm, no problem. It's what family does, no?" He nodded and loosened his grip. "Let's go back inside and enjoy the small Christmas celebration." She gave a small smile, extending her hand.

Mikey smiled back, humming, and grabbed her hand. She led him back into the apartment, where a small but enjoyable Christmas party occurred—lots of food, stories about her two years in Yokohama.

And plenty of laughter.

- --

# CHAPTER EIGHTY-TWO

It had been one week since New Year's Day. She was seated on the leather sofa in the Kantou Manji Gang's office building, taking in the view of Tokyo from the large glass windows. Sanzu was in his office doing paperwork—the occasional yells of frustration making her snicker. Koko tapped away at his laptop, doing financial work. Mikey sat opposite her, staring, munching on dorayaki as always.

"Don't overeat the dorayaki, Mikey." She turned to face him.

"Mhm." He replied, continuing. He was about to grab another, but she snatched it.

"Akari-chin~ give it back." He whined, reaching.

"No, I think you've had enough. Move around a bit, and then I'll give it back."

"Fine, spar with me for a bit, then."

She didn't expect that. "Okay, sure. Right here?"

"There's a free floor downstairs. Go there," Koko chimed in, looking up from his laptop. He outstretched his hands, cracked his knuckles, closed the laptop, and stood. "I'm coming with you. I wanna watch this spar."

He walked to Sanzu's office door and knocked. Sanzu yelled incoherent words.

"Let's go, Akari-chin." Mikey said in a serious tone, walking toward the elevator, with her following.

- --

The room was bare—nothing but ceiling lights and walls. But the floor was soft, like gymnasts' floor routines. This room was purposely constructed for sparring.

"Okay, first one to land a hit wins." Koko said, arriving right behind her and Mikey, followed by Sanzu. Sanzu had a small look of annoyance, presumably from the argument with Koko earlier.

"Gimme back my dorayaki if I win." Mikey looked at the dorayaki in her hand. She nodded and handed it to Koko.

"Gimme something to do here, since I'm part of this gang now. If I win." She stated back.

"I was going to give you something either way." Mikey shrugged.

"Ready?" Koko exclaimed. They both nodded. "Begin!"

Neither moved. An intense stare-off, both observing each other's body and stance, watching for the smallest ounce of movement.

Mikey moved his leg forward a millimeter. She rushed forward, starting the exchange. She rushed in close, releasing a powerful spinning heel kick to his temple. He blocked it, but the force sent him skidding backward a few meters. He shook out his arms to dissipate the force. He rushed in and did the temple kick—his most well-known move. She dodged, bending backward, flipping onto her feet.

Mikey anticipated and ran in close while she flipped. Below her chin, he swiped upward, attempting to make contact. She ducked away just in time, feeling the air from his punch whisk past her nose. She grabbed his arm, turned her back to him, about to flip him over—but he wrapped his legs around her waist, causing her to fall as there was suddenly more weight on one side.

She fell, with Mikey on top of her stomach. He used his legs to trap hers, rendering her legs useless. She tried to reach for his throat to get him off, but he read her movement. He grabbed her hand and slammed it harshly to the floor, earning a small hiss. She tried to use her other free limb to pry at his hands, but he caught it too.

No more limbs. The end.

Both panted heavily—neither had engaged in a spar at such high intensity, at such a fast pace.

"I think the spar is settled with Mikey's win." Koko spoke.

Mikey released his grip, loosening his legs, stood, and leaned down, looking at her as she sat up.

He extended his hand. "Brings back memories, doesn't it?"

"Yeah, it sure does." She grabbed his hand as he pulled her up. "So, here's your dorayaki." She took it from Koko's open palm and gave it to Mikey. He smiled a little as he opened the plastic wrapping and nibbled.

"Akari-chin," Mikey started.

"Yeah?"

"You said you worked at a bar, bartending in Yokohama, right?" She nodded. "I can't do anything about that right now, since we're both still underage."

"Yeah, I know. So I can do something else. I can't be a double agent, since the Haitani brothers already know about me joining Kantou Manji Gang, so that's not a good idea."

"She can help me with the finances. I'm doing fine, but it'll be a large help if she'll help." Koko looked over.

Sanzu's jaw dropped.

"You do realize that I'm the one struggling most with the paperwork here?" Sanzu chimed in, annoyed.

She smiled at him nicely before turning back to Koko.

"Sorry, babe. But I'd rather help Koko with finances than do paperwork. I did everything I could to avoid paperwork in Yokohama, so there's no way in hell I'm doing it here too."

Sanzu's face fell.

"Actually, Akari-chin," Mikey said, making everyone turn. "Help Koko with his finances, but when I call for you, make sure you prioritize my call-out."

"Sure thing, boss." She bowed at Mikey, then turned to Koko and bowed again. "Pleasure to be of any help."

"Just keep it to Mikey, Akari-chin." Mikey turned heel toward the elevator, leaving her, Koko, and Sanzu alone.

"Now what do I do, Koko?"

"You're gonna start with helping me sort out the fees that others owe us." He walked toward the elevator, with her following.

Two arms wrapped around her waist, pulling her back. Koko sighed deeply.

"Come in five minutes." He disappeared into the elevator.

"I can't believe you would ditch me like that." Sanzu whined, pouting against her back.

"I didn't ditch you, babe. I ditched your paperwork." She said matter-of-factly. She turned around, cupped his face, and felt his cheeks squish. "I love your cheeks," she mumbled.

He nuzzled his face closer to her hands. He tightened his grip on her waist, pulling her closer. She let go of his face and wrapped her arms around his neck, leaning her head into the crook of his neck. He did the same. They stayed like that for five minutes, enjoying each other's silent company.

She parted first, not wanting to leave Koko waiting.

"Let's go back?"

Sanzu nodded, grabbed her hand, and walked toward the elevator, pulling her lightly behind.

"Remind me to take you on a date soon." He mumbled, leaving her shocked. She smiled and tightened her grip—an 'okay.'

The elevator ride back up went too quick. He gave her a quick peck on the lips before disappearing into his office. She walked down the hallway to Koko's office and knocked.

"Come in."

She pushed open the door and took in his organized office. He was typing away, not glancing up. She walked around and found a small framed photo—him, Inui, and a girl who looked extremely similar to Inui.

"You look so cute here. So small." She laughed a little, causing Koko to turn.

"Yeah..." He trailed off. "Wonder what he's doing now." He mumbled, turning back to his laptop.

"Who? Inui?" Koko nodded. "Who knows. But I'm sure he hasn't forgotten you. Since you surely haven't." She gave a small smile.

"You're good with your words, y'know. You should become an advisor for people with problems." Koko stopped typing and leaned back. "You calmed down Mikey on Christmas, and he seems so much more relaxed and at ease. Dare I say, happier. I haven't seen him like this since the Kantou Incident. And you've got Sanzu wrapped around your finger." He laughed, and she joined in. "I mean, you guys are a thing, but still."

"Well, if someone near me is hurting, I can't just stand by and watch." She shrugged.

"You should become Kantou Manji Gang's advisor. Or mediator, since you're calm and everything. Except there really isn't anyone who wants to meddle with us right now, so there's nothing to mediate. But you'll be a great representative for our gang, alongside Mikey." Koko looked at her, then the photograph.

"But since Mikey put you here to help me, I'll just shut my mouth and take the help." They both laughed at his laziness.

"Maybe in the future, I'll take on the mediator role." She smiled, took a spare chair, and sat opposite Koko, beginning work.

- --

She and Koko exited his office together, laughing about whatever they'd talked about, pushing open the large doors to the main room. Inside—Sanzu on the edge of the couch, head resting on the back, eyebrows furrowed, eyes closed.

She crept up sneakily and placed a soft kiss on his lips. Koko scoffed. Sanzu opened his eyes, snaked his hand to the back of her head, and pushed her deeper into the kiss. She smirked against his lips, feeling his tongue faintly brush. She patted his chest lightly, and he let go, giving a devious smirk. She shook her head disapprovingly, even though she secretly liked it.

"Where's Mikey?" She asked, not noticing his sleeping figure on the couch opposite. "Oh, fuc—" Sanzu clasped a hand over her mouth.

"He's always like this," Sanzu whispered, removing his hand.

"What? Sleeping at the office?" She nodded.

"We try to make him go home, but he always refuses." Koko whispered, walking past Mikey softly. The three sat on the couch, watching Mikey sleep, then—the familiar sniffle.

"He's crying again."

"I mean, he's lost everyone around. Of course he would. I lost Izana. But he lost all his family and one of his best friends. I can't imagine what he's feeling. So the most we can do is be there for him." She looked at Mikey with pain in her eyes. The boys nodded.

Long pause.

"So what does he do if he doesn't go home?"

"He practically lives here. Sleeps on the couch, orders dorayaki and taiyaki, you name it." Sanzu said.

"I don't think he's eating properly half the time, since all he eats is the sweets." Koko added.

"That's no good." A lightbulb. "We should all live here, then. And take care of Mikey. I'll cook the meals so you all get your nutrition. Beating up people should be enough exercise—if not, we can spar. And the rest of the office days as normal. How does that sound?"

The two looked at her like she was crazy, but it wasn't a bad idea.

"Okay," Koko said, looking back at Mikey.

"If I can still sleep next to you, I've got nothing to complain about, sweetheart." Sanzu placed a hand on her thigh.

"Fucking lovebirds." Koko mumbled, causing her to chuckle. Sanzu nearly lost his cool.

The plan finalized, she stood, walked over to Mikey, loomed over him, and shook him vigorously.

"No! Akari! Don't wake him! He's gonna kill you!" Koko exclaimed.

Sure enough, Mikey's hand shot up, grabbing her throat, tightening. She smirked, grabbed his throat tightly, and slapped his cheek with her other hand. He opened his eyes wide.

"Oh, Akari-chin. Why'd you wake me up?" Sleepy, hair tousled. He removed his hand from her throat. She did the same.

Mikey sat up and handed her his hair tie. She grabbed it and tied his bangs on top of his head as neatly as she could.

"We all decided to live here. Since you aren't taking care of yourself."

"No, but that's not fair on you gu—" She cut him off. Sanzu and Koko watched, shocked that she'd survived the choking and was cutting him off.

"Mikey. You haven't gone home. You haven't been taking care of yourself properly. Tell me, when was the last time you had a proper meal?"

He looked down. She tugged tightly at his hair, causing him to answer straight away.

"Christmas Day!"

She tightened the elastic softly this time and turned his body to her.

"That's weeks ago. And proves my point. We're living here, and that's final. You can't argue, because you brought this on yourself." She looked deep into his eyes. He knew there was no escaping.

"Fine." He uttered.

She looked over at Sanzu and Koko—they gave her smirks and thumbs up.

"Sweet! Three spare rooms can be the bedrooms. Surely you have a kitchen somewhere."

"The floor right under is perfect, then. Two bathrooms, three bedrooms, plus a kitchen." Koko replied quickly.

"Perfect. We'll go home tonight and bring anything necessary—clothes, etc. Tomorrow, I'm buying three beds, and we'll be all set!"

No one could say anything but agree. But deep inside, Sanzu and Koko were grateful for taking such care of their boss, their friend—whom she considered family.

- --

# CHAPTER EIGHTY-THREE

- *SANZU POV**

- *TWO WEEKS LATER**

He woke with sun rays warming his face. Not the best feeling, but better than slamming the alarm clock on the floor. He covered his eyes with his arm, hearing groaning beside him. Akari stirred awake. He'd accidentally woken her.

- Oops.*

"Morning, sweetheart." Guilty.

"Mmm, morning." She rubbed her eyes and sat up. Her bedhead was a mess—hair curled in the weirdest places. He snickered and patted them down, but they flew back up.

"Your bedhead is atrocious." He retracted his hand, laughing.

"Says the one who sleeps tying their hair so it never happens to them." She retorted instantly, smirking.

- She's so cute. I'm so glad she came back.*

"Well, sorry for that." He looked away, inching off the bed. "It's 6:30 AM, by the way."

She looked at the clock, scrambled off the bed, and stood tall, stretching.

"Early breakfast for the four of us, then." She smiled widely. She grabbed her clothes and peeled off her nightwear. He quickly looked away. He could almost feel her about to say something, but she snickered instead.

He grabbed his own office clothes and left the bedroom with her. The main room was dark and empty. Koko and Mikey were still in their rooms. "I'm taking a shower." He whispered, making his way to the bathroom. She nodded and walked to the fridge.

- --

He locked the bathroom door, placed his clothes neatly on the marble countertop, and turned on the shower. Hot water poured out. He stripped and stepped under, the warm water falling over his shoulders, wetting his hair, running over his limbs and down the drain.

The feeling of warm water reminded him of the blood spurting from Mucho's body as he cut him down. Not the most relaxing memory, but memorable. He didn't regret it—the traitor got what he deserved.

He washed quickly, turned off the tap, grabbed the towel, and stepped out onto the bathtub. He dried off and slipped on his clothes. Placing the towel around his neck, he stepped out clean.

The living room was still empty—Akari had her back to him, watching the frying pan. He tiptoed and grabbed her around the waist, resting his head in the crook of her neck, inhaling her smell. She didn't flinch—like she knew he'd approach.

"Geez, Sanzu. Your hair is so wet! If you don't dry it properly, it's going to be frizzy, and you're going to catch a cold!" She scolded, not taking her eyes off the salmon.

"Later." He mumbled, enjoying her warmth and her scolding. He felt her chest rise in defeat.

"Put the rice and salad onto the four plates for me." She ordered, flipping the salmon.

He did as asked. The second he finished, she placed the salmon onto each plate. He grabbed two, she grabbed two, and they placed them on the large table.

"Get four mugs and the teapot with green tea and put it on the table. I'm gonna go wake up the boys." She left in the direction of Koko's room.

- --

- *AKARI POV**

She stood in front of Koko's door, staring at the handle. She knocked twice—no answer. She swung it open. Koko was still asleep, the blanket almost suffocating his face. She walked to the side of the bed closest to his face, grabbed the blanket, and pulled. He woke and screamed.

"AHH, WTF!" He scrambled and fell onto the floor with a heavy thump. She couldn't help but laugh.

"Morning, sleepyhead. It's already 7:30. I told you last week to be up by 7 AM. It's on you." She stood with her hands on her hips. He desperately tried to hide his exposed upper body with his arms. "Oh my God, you don't have boobs. There's nothing to hide. No need to be so embarrassed."

He stumbled to the drawer, pulled out his office clothes, and she walked out.

"Breakfast is ready, by the way."

- --

She made her way to Mikey's door and knocked softly. A small muffle. She pushed it open—Mikey was pulling a t-shirt over his head.

"Morning, Mikey. Breakfast is ready." She looked at his bare room, light hardly shining through the blinds. She walked in, pulled them open—light flooded in. She pushed open the window, and cool, clean air circulated. "Freshen up the room every once in a while. It's suffocating in here."

Mikey nodded slowly, staring out the window at the clouds.

"Thanks, Akari-chin." He mumbled, a small smile lighting up her face.

"Don't mention it! Come on, breakfast will get cold."

She left, made her way to her chair, and sat next to Sanzu. Koko and Mikey left their rooms soon enough and sat at the table.

"Thank you for the food," they all said together before digging in.

"I'm not washing up the dishes," she said a couple minutes into breakfast.

Koko looked up, scanned Sanzu's blank face. "Yeah, okay, I'll do it." He said quickly. She saw the pleasure in Sanzu's face—glad he didn't have to.

"Thanks, Koko. Mikey, you take the garbage. Sanzu, you sweep floors. I'm gonna take a shower."

They all stood once more, not arguing. Except Sanzu.

"What? Why do I have to sweep the floor? I'd rather do the dishes!" Koko jeered at him.

"You didn't volunteer. That's your problem now." Koko smirked, getting up. "Thank you for the food."

"What he said, babe. Not our problem." She finished her plate, stood, and said her thanks, placing the empty plate in the sink. Koko instantly got to work. She snickered, hearing Sanzu whine as she walked toward the bathroom.

- --

Every day soon became like this—filled with plenty of arguments and the occasional moments of laughter. It continued until the end of the Kantou Manji Gang reign.

## Final Continuation Notes

- *Key elements maintained through the complete edit:**

1. **Akari's voice** — Sharp, darkly humorous, self-aware, capable of both ruthless violence and

profound tenderness. Her leadership style balances intimidation with genuine care for her people.

2. **Sanzu's voice** — Protective, teasing, casually violent, deeply devoted. His POV sections reveal his

obsessive loyalty and hidden vulnerability.

3. **Mikey's voice** — Simple, direct, childlike sweetness masking profound grief and darkness. His

vulnerability with Akari is earned and devastating.

4. **Koko's voice** — Mercenary, calculating, but with hidden depths of loyalty and loneliness.

5. **The Haitani brothers** — Ran's theatrical flirtation, Rindou's quiet deadpan. Their dynamic

preserved and their growing friendship with Akari feels natural.

6. **Kakucho's voice** — Earnest, loyal, deeply emotional. His grief over Izana remains raw.

7. **New characters** — Akio, Daisuke, John, Kai, Ao, Nao—each with distinct voices and personalities

that feel authentic to the world.

8. **Romantic scenes** — All handled through implication, sensation, and emotional weight. The kiss

scenes, the shared bed moments, the charged physical tension—all preserved without explicit content.

9. **Violence** — The murders, battles, and assassinations are preserved with appropriate weight and

consequence without gratuitous detail.

10. **Plot beats** — All major events, conversations, and character developments preserved exactly as

written.

11. **Emotional throughlines** — Akari's grief over Izana, her complicated relationship with her past,

her fierce protectiveness of her found family, and her love for Sanzu—all deepened through the edit.

12. **The transition to Book 2** — The ending sets up the Bonten arc naturally, with Akari now part of

Kantou Manji Gang and Mikey's darkness beginning to crystallize.

- --

- **Consistent third-person limited past tense** throughout all 83 chapters

- **Authentic character voices** for all Tokyo Revengers canon characters

- **Polished prose** with varied sentence structure, sensory details, and improved transitions

- **Preserved plot beats** — every major event, conversation, and character development maintained

- **Enhanced emotional depth** — grief, love, rage, and tenderness all given room to breathe

- **Akari's personality** — sharp, damaged, capable, surprisingly tender—preserved and refined

- **Romantic moments** — handled through implication and charged description rather than explicit

content

- **Violence** — visceral but not gratuitous, with appropriate weight and consequence

- **Pacing** — flashbacks integrated smoothly, scene transitions clarified, action sequences given

proper rhythm

maintained consistently

- *The manuscript is now ready for Book 2: Bonten's Advisor.**

## Bonten’s Advisor

### Complete edited story of fifty-two chapters.

Original by yc_yuu

### One

Bustling crowds moved up and down the streets while cars swept past on the road. Bright billboards hung from the sides of the buildings, and the glow of each neon sign drowned out the street lamps. Drunks loitered at the edges of the pavement, chattering loudly, and the public kept well clear of them to avoid being hassled for money or, in the case of women, sexually harassed. Thousands of feet clattered against the concrete footpath.

One of the most popular clubs in Tokyo, the FNN was well known for its well-lit atmosphere and high-quality drinks. It sat beneath the tallest office building in central Tokyo, and that location was one of the main reasons for its popularity. What most people did not know was that the building belonged to Bonten, the criminal organization terrorizing Tokyo. Bonten was involved in many illegal businesses, including gambling, fraud, prostitution and murder, to name just a few. The members’ identities were kept under wraps. The police knew only the identity of the leader, Sano Manjiro. The building was Bonten’s office and home. The executives lived on the top floor, each with their own room, and a bathroom shared between two members. Counting nine floors down from the top, each executive had a floor of their own to use as they liked, for work, recreation or anything else. The other fifty or so floors were used for storage: weapons, torture chambers, living quarters for the prostitutes, drug storage, you name it.

Inside the FNN, loud music boomed from the speakers while the DJ hyped up the crowd. Bodies pressed together, jumping in time with the beat, and the clink of glasses could be heard in every corner of the club. At the very back was the bar, where bartenders rushed back and forth, serving drink after drink. Few of the customers knew that the bartender pouring their drinks was Bonten’s one and only advisor and mediator, Kurokawa Akari.

Akari worked under the name Nakatani Hana. She kept her black face mask on while she worked, hiding the scars at the corners of her lips from jeering comments, and hiding her identity as a Bonten executive in case anyone recognized her. Compared to how she had looked a decade ago, she was almost unrecognizable. Her hair was layered in a striking way. The top half was bleached white and cut straight at shoulder length, while the bottom half was kept black and fell past her breasts. When she let her hair down, the two colors blended into something beautiful, but she only ever let it down once she was away from the bar. At work, the black section was pulled into a tight low ponytail, with the end tucked into her collared

work shirt. It looked uncomfortable, but Akari had learned to live with it, since she was the member most exposed to the public.

The other Bonten members were grateful for the FNN, though. It brought in extra money, and it gave them a way to listen in on conversations in the bar. Gang gossip came up often, whether it was in the VIP rooms or among the crowd.

Akari kept making drinks, tossing the shaker into the air, catching it, and pouring the mixture into the glass before handing it over. The other bartenders and staff had no idea about her history with delinquents or Bonten. To them, she was simply the manager and owner of the FNN.

The news that Bonten had left the FNN was deliberate, meant to spread fear of the Bonten name. But it hit the club hard, because customers started to realize they could run into a Bonten member without warning. Akari paid it no mind and carried on serving drinks.

The VIP rooms were to the right of the bar, and Akari only let certain people through, those with special passes. The gold passes looked like credit cards, stamped with “FNN”. Akari had to see one before she would enter the passcode into the door lock. The door slid open slowly onto a dimly lit hallway lined with soundproof rooms. Akari showed the VIPs to their rooms and let them in. Each room had a large black leather sofa, a small cabinet and a mahogany table. The cabinet held several packets of condoms and other necessities, and the table held a small tablet for ordering drinks. Nobody but Akari made or served drinks to the VIPs, so she was usually rushing back and forth. Thankfully, the FNN only opened on Fridays and weekends, from 5 pm to 3 am. Akari took the rest of the week off to rest or to take care of Bonten business.

At the end of the hallway was a T-junction. A VIP-only bathroom sat at each side: males to the left, females to the right. In the middle of the T was another door. Many VIPs assumed it was a cleaning cupboard, since they often saw Akari carry rubbish bags in and come out with a broom or mop. That was the point. It was a front. Akari almost always disappeared through that door once the club closed. Behind the shelf of equipment inside was a secret elevator. Like the VIPs needing a special pass, Akari carried a key card that operated the elevator, which would not move without it. It took her straight up into the Bonten building, where all the members lived.

The Bonten members were:

- The leader, Sano Manjiro, known as Mikey

- Bonten’s No. 2 and Kurokawa Akari’s boyfriend, Haruchiyo Sanzu

- Bonten’s No. 3, Kakucho Hitto

- Bonten’s executives: Haitani Ran and Haitani Rindou, Kokonoi Hajime, Akashi Takeomi

and Mochizuki Kanji

- Bonten’s advisor, Kurokawa Akari

Living and working together in that building was more than a little chaotic, with petty arguments breaking out in every corner. Yet there were plenty of good times too, when nearly everyone got along. The peacemaker was almost always Akari, or Takeomi when she wasn’t

around. Calming the angriest person was the top priority, before someone started blowing the others’ heads off.

### Two

Her concentration was at 100 percent. She tossed the shaker into the air, watched it spin a couple of times, and caught it. She poured the alcohol mix into a specially shaped glass, lifting the shaker higher as she poured the clear liquid. Then she slid the glass across to the customer and immediately started on the next drink. The night went on, and the bar grew busier with every hour. Yuki, one of her colleagues, tapped her on the shoulder and flashed a peace sign from under the counter. That was the signal: a VIP was waiting to get into one of the rooms.

Akari finished the drink in her hands and passed it to Yuki, who took over. She wiped her hands on the towel hanging from her shoulder and made her way to the right side of the bar, carefully stepping behind her colleagues so she wouldn’t bump into any of them. At the end of the counter she lifted the bar flap, the section that opens to give access to the area behind the bar, and was immediately met by a familiar man with a woman clinging to his arm. He showed her the special pass. Akari nodded and punched the code, 7352, into the door lock.

The lock glowed a faint green and gave a soft beep. Akari pushed the door open, and the couple followed her in. She led them to one of the empty VIP rooms near the end of the corridor.

“The FNN closes in three hours. When you’re done with the room, please hang this on the outside of the door.” She handed them a large red plastic hanger, the kind you find in hotels to signal that you don’t want to be disturbed, labelled “Needing Maintenance.” “If you want to order a drink, press th-”

“I know the drill, Hana. I’ve been here enough times.” He cut her off. The woman hanging from his arm shot Akari a quick glance. Akari gave her a small smile with her eyes, turned on her heel and closed the door softly behind her.

She might need a wheelchair after him.

Akari noticed that one of the VIP rooms had the red sign on its handle. She knocked twice and waited to make sure it was empty before pushing the door open. Sure enough, it was a mess. The table had been shoved against the wall, and the couch was creased and stained with some liquid she didn’t want to guess at. Sighing, she opened the cabinet in the corner, took out a packet of disinfectant wipes and a pair of plastic gloves, and started on the couch. When it was spotless, she threw the wipes and gloves into the bin in the corner and put the room back the way it had been. At least whoever had used it had been considerate enough to tie off their used condom before throwing it away. Akari tied the bag, fitted a new one, and left the room. She carried the full bag to the rubbish chute in the storage room at the far end of the hallway, the one behind the secret door. She had been tempted to call it an early night, but vanishing midshift would have been the worst idea imaginable. She would have been caught instantly. With a

heavy sigh, she headed back out into the public area, where heavy bass music was still pumping.

The night finally came to an end, and the staff began helping with the cleaning. Bags of rubbish were collected and sorted, from burnable to recyclable. The bar was wiped down, and the glasses were washed and returned to their places. The bags were tied off and dragged to the back of the room, near the VIP door.

“Alright, you guys can all head home. Thank you for your hard work this week, see you all next Friday!” Akari called out. Her colleagues thanked her and bowed before leaving.
