She watched them go through the front door, then turned and entered the code for the VIP door. She dragged the rubbish bags through and into the hallway, opened the door at the far end, and lifted the bags one by one into the rubbish chute, wiping the sweat from her forehead with her forearm. Then she checked both bathrooms for customers and locked them up for the week. She walked the length of the hallway and inspected every VIP room. Sure enough, the room with the red sign was spotless. Thankfully, the man was a regular at bringing whores to the club and knew what to do. He had cleaned up after himself, thrown everything in the bin and even tied off the bag. Akari swapped in a fresh bag and carried the old one back to the chute.

She stepped out of the VIP door and listened to the lock click shut behind her. She looked around the spotless club, walked to the front door, opened it and peeked outside, feeling the cold morning air on her face. She closed the door, locked it from the inside with the master key, and moved along the windows, closing the blinds. She tucked a stray chair under its table. Her night was finally over.

Swiping her key card over the scanner, she waited for the elevator to come to life. It took a few seconds to arrive, and then the doors opened and light flooded the room. Akari stepped inside and pressed the button for the top floor. If she remembered correctly, tonight was also the night the Bonten executives held their monthly meeting. By chance it had clashed with her shift at the FNN, so Mikey had excused her. Glancing at her watch, she saw it was already 3:30 am. The meeting was supposed to end by midnight, but judging by the last two meetings, she wasn’t surprised to find nearly all of them piss drunk and passed out, Sanzu high on whatever drugs he had taken, and Mikey staring out the window eating dorayaki.

As soon as the elevator reached the top floor, the doors slid open. Sure enough, she was right. Sanzu was prancing around Mikey with bloodshot eyes, while the rest of the executives were out cold. Sanzu spotted her stepping out of the elevator and let out an excited shriek, rushing over to sweep her off her feet. He twirled her around in his arms.

“Sweetheart~. Work, was how it?” he mumbled into her chest. Akari patted his head, unable to make out what he had just asked.

“Babe, stop taking drugs already. It’s going to kill you one day. Not to mention you promised you’d only take them when I’m around. Whatever happened to that?” She rolled her eyes and

pushed him off. He dropped to the floor dramatically and followed her around the room with his eyes.

The rest of the executives were drunk and passed out on the couch. Ran and Rindou sat side by side, Rindou’s head on Ran’s shoulder and Ran’s head resting on top of Rindou’s. Koko was sprawled on the floor with his hair over his face. Takeomi and Mochizuki sat hugging their papers tightly, as though they were still in an important meeting. Kakucho was the sensible one. He sat on a separate chair, keeping an eye on the passed-out men with a sleepy glare.

“Welcome back, Akari,” he said in a sleepy voice.

“You should go to bed. I’ll wake them,” she said, but he refused her offer.

“I’ll help with that, but look after him first.” Kakucho’s eyes flicked to Mikey.

Mikey sat in the chair facing the window, which overlooked Tokyo’s night skyline. Akari walked around his chair and crouched in front of him. She expected him to be wide awake, but he was asleep. She smiled to herself, gently lifted him from the chair, and carried him to his room. He stirred in her arms, but she laid him down softly on his bed and drew the blanket over him. She closed the door quietly and went back to the main area, passing Kakucho, who was dragging Mochizuki to his room.

Akari glanced at Sanzu, who was now passed out on the floor where she had shoved him off. Stupid drugs. Stupid Sanzu. I should burn his drugs, for fuck’s sake.

She ignored him for now and walked over to Koko’s limp body. She prodded his face and watched him groan. Good, he would wake soon. She grabbed his arms, dragged him across the floor to his room, and tossed him onto the bed. She brushed the hair from his face and pulled the blanket up to his neck. He grabbed the blanket sleepily and rolled over, his back to her. She shut the door and went to fetch the two inseparable brothers. All she needed to do was pull Rindou away from Ran to wake Ran. Ran woke and looked at her with drunk eyes. He saw Rindou being held up by her arms, gave her a small look, then took him and carried him to his room before heading to his own. Kakucho had already taken care of Takeomi and Mochi, so only Sanzu was left. He was still on the floor, out cold. She nudged his sides with her fingers, but he wasn’t ticklish. Sighing, she grabbed his arms and legs, hoisted them over her shoulders, and walked towards the room they shared.

She rolled him off her shoulders and covered him with the blanket. She peeled off her work clothes and dropped them into a small basket in the corner. In her underwear, she tiptoed to the wardrobe, took out her sleepwear and pulled it on. She tugged the hair tie from the bottom half of her hair and let it down for sleep. She shoved Sanzu aside, and he groaned. Slipping under the covers, she lay down and turned on her side. She heard shuffling beside her and felt Sanzu’s breath on her neck before she drifted off herself.

Loud, aggressive knocking woke her the next morning. She glanced at the clock on the wall: 10:30 am. She had barely managed seven hours of sleep, and being woken by aggressive

knocking was not how she wanted to start the day. She swung her feet to the edge of the bed, walked sluggishly to the door and pulled it wide open. She was met by Koko’s eyes.

“What? Is it worth breaking my sleep?” she asked, looking up at him. He wasn’t looking at her, though. He was staring past her at Sanzu’s sleeping form.

“He used my card without asking to buy drugs.” He held up the receipt for the recent purchases made on his card.

“Ohh, okay. Do what you like with him, then.” She stepped out of his way and watched as Koko began trying to wake Sanzu. “Why on earth are you buying a men’s lingerie set?” she asked, remembering an odd item on the receipt. He turned around and gave her an embarrassed look.

“I’m pranking the brothers.”

“Ohh, you can tell me the details after breakfast,” she replied, leaving Koko alone with Sanzu. Sanzu wasn’t getting out of that room without a bruise, she thought.

She headed to the kitchen, still littered with last night’s rubbish. Fast food containers and cans of alcohol covered the countertops. She shoved the mess aside, already planning to give the men an earful when they woke up. She opened the fridge, took out a whole carton of eggs, and started a large omelette. She set the rice cooker going, then focused on the omelette. Once it was done, she plated it and set it on the dining table in the middle of the room. She washed the tomatoes and lettuce, made a salad and set out dressing in case anyone wanted it. She placed the bread on the table with a small assortment of spreads, then served rice onto each plate and lined the plates up with the chairs.

She sat down, and Koko and Kakucho joined her. After saying her thanks for the meal, she dug in. The conversation was interesting as they discussed their plan to get the brothers to wear the matching lingerie set Koko had already ordered. It was cut short when the dining room went awfully quiet. The brothers came in, dragging their feet as they sat down.

“Well, good morning to you too,” Akari said, looking them over. Ran and Rindou both looked hungover, which was an interesting sight to see.

“Tch,” Rindou muttered.

“Thanks for brekkie, love~,” Ran said, holding his head in one hand and giving her a small smile, his eyes a little dead.

“How are you not hungover? You were dead on the floor last night.” She glanced over at Koko. He answered instantly but was cut off.

“He’s a lightweight,” Rindou said, taking a bite of omelette and rice from his spoon.

“Am not!” Koko retorted. Akari snorted, trying to hold in her laughter.

“He is,” Kakucho murmured to her, and she couldn’t hold it in any longer. She laughed out loud, clutching her stomach.

“Remind me not to give you a high-percentage drink when you come to the FNN next time,” she said, still holding her aching stomach. After a while she calmed down, and Kakucho stood and placed his plate in the sink.

“I’ll wash the dishes, so someone else needs to take out the rubbish,” he said, pointing at the cans and takeaway containers. Akari immediately looked at the brothers.

“I’d make you do it, but you both seem to be suffering. Koko, you can do it.” Koko opened his mouth to argue but did the cleaning anyway. “You two can do it next time.”

Akari walked over to Takeomi’s room and knocked. Footsteps approached, and the door swung open.

“Oh, morning, Akari.” He looked down at her.

“Morning, Takeomi. Breakfast is ready.”

“Oh sweet.”

“Can you wake up Mochi too?”

“Yeah, of course. I’ll be there in a bit.”

“Thanks,” she said, smiling, and headed to Mikey’s door. She knocked softly and waited. Nothing. She knocked again and still heard no reply. She pushed the door open slowly and found Mikey sitting up in bed, eyes fixed on the blank wall. His gaze moved to her as she sat down in his desk chair and turned it to face him.

“Thanks for last night,” he mumbled, looking up to meet her eyes.

“No problem. Did you sleep well?” she asked, studying the dark circles under his eyes, which had hardly faded.

“Yeah, I guess I did.”

“That’s a relief, then. Breakfast is ready. It’ll be cold if you don’t hurry.” She got up, pushed the chair back under the desk and felt his stare on her back as she left.

She was worried about Mikey. He hadn’t changed much in ten years, but his sleep had grown worse, and that worried her, since sleep was essential for the body to function properly. His mental state had improved since a decade ago, though. He could finally let out his pent-up emotions, but it came at a cost. She often went with him to visit Shinichiro, Baji, Emma and Izana, and he truly appreciated her company, since going there alone seemed to break him.

She walked down the hallway and opened the door to her room. Sanzu was half on the bed, his head hanging off the floor and his legs still on the mattress. He looked dead. She poked his cheek. Nothing. She poked his chest. Still nothing. She kept going, working her way down his body, until his eyes flew open.

“What are you doing, sweetheart~?” he growled, catching her hand.

“Oh, nothing. I thought you were dead.” She pulled her hand from his grasp and looked down at him with disappointment.

“You shouldn’t toy with me, sweetheart. You of all people should know that.”

“I should be the one saying that. What happened to you promising not to take drugs when I’m not around?” She looked down at him, one eyebrow raised. Then she jabbed his stomach. He flipped over the bed and slammed onto the floor. She snickered. “Now that’s your fault. Get up, breakfast is ready.”

She took one of her suits from the cabinet, folded it over her forearm, grabbed a bath towel and headed for the bathroom.

### Three

The water dripped from the shower-head and ran down her body. Akari was grateful to Mikey for setting up the club downstairs, since it let her use the bartending skills she had picked up years ago. It was also a handy source of intel. But she hated cleaning up after other people’s messes, especially after their “fun times.”

She turned off the shower, stepped out and patted herself dry. She wrapped her hair in the smaller towel and pulled on her clothes, then her suit.

Today was one of those days she went to the cemetery with Mikey. This time it was a little different. They also had to meet the boss of a rival gang in the area to settle some issues that had come up.

Once she was in her suit, she unwrapped the towel from her hair and switched on the hairdryer. God, it was loud. It drowned out every other sound in the bathroom and echoed off the tiles. Her hair whipped around as the hot air blasted it. She started at the roots and worked her way down to the ends, running her fingers through as it dried. It dried quickly thanks to the layers. She really loved the new style. It was easy to maintain, apart from the coloring. She had chosen the color and length on purpose: short and bleached for Izana, long and black for Baji. Not many people knew the real reason behind the haircut. Most just thought it was weird.

Her shifts as Nakatani Hana, the bartender and owner of the FNN, were over for the week, so she no longer had to tie the bottom half of her hair back until next Friday. She switched off the dryer, put it away in the storage space under the sink, and split her hair into two sections down the middle. Then she started a braid (think Haitani Ran’s old hairstyle). She loved this one for work. With the white and black layers mixed together, the braids looked almost like an ombre, fading from white through grey to black. She tied off the ends and cleaned up the loose strands around the sink.

She brushed her teeth, rinsed, and left the bathroom, dropping her towel and sleepwear into the laundry basket in her room.

“Mikey, shall we go?” she called. Mikey was sitting on the leather couch in the main area. The moment Ran opened his mouth, she knew he was going to comment on her hair. Again.

“Copying me are you, love~?” He smirked, standing up and reaching for her braids. She rolled her eyes but didn’t bother moving away. When she ignored him, he pulled her into a back hug and rested his chin on top of her head. His arms wrapped around her waist and settled on her stomach. She sighed and said nothing. Sanzu, however, was too busy scarfing down breakfast with Takeomi and Mochi to notice how close Ran was standing. Not that it bothered Akari. She had spent time with Ran in juvie, along with Izana, Kakucho and Mochi, and she had known him for the past ten years, of course.

Mikey turned, looked over at her and nodded. “Sanzu, Koko, you guys come too.” Sanzu stopped eating. He looked at Mikey, then at Akari with Ran clinging to her, and held the stare on Ran for a long moment. Then he finished his late breakfast, rushed to her room and came back seconds later in his three-piece suit, holding his bubblegum-pink tie, which matched his hair. He shoved it at her, leaving her no choice. She shuffled forward, since Ran still hadn’t let go of her waist. She wrapped the tie around his neck, tied it properly and fixed the collar of his shirt. Sanzu tucked his undershirt into his trousers, tugged his cuffs straight and pulled on his coat. Everyone had their own colored suit, except Mikey, who insisted on breathable black clothing.

“Okay, we’re all ready. Let’s go,” Akari said, letting go of Sanzu’s tie. Ran finally released her waist. She hurried back to her room, swapped her slippers for her black needle-heeled shoes, and walked back to the main area with confidence. She made her way to the elevator and waited for Sanzu, Koko and Mikey to get in. “See you all later,” she said as the doors closed. Mikey pressed the button for the basement. The basement was underground, a couple of floors below the FNN. It was where Sanzu did his torture work and where the expensive cars were parked.

“We have to go somewhere first, so you two make sure you get to the bar by 5 pm,” she said, glancing at her watch. It was 2 pm. Koko nodded, and Sanzu gave her a sad look. Honestly, he was like a lost puppy without her. A crazy one.

Akari got into one car with Mikey, while Sanzu and Koko took the other. The engine roared to life: the sleek black Mercedes-Benz. She followed Koko’s car out of the garage, through the metal roller doors and onto the main road, then took the turn towards the cemetery with care. The cemetery was close to many of the events of the past, especially Musashi Shrine, where the Tokyo Manji Gang used to hold their meetings. She stopped the car and turned to face Mikey, who was staring out of the window.

“We’re here.” Mikey snapped out of his thoughts, looked at her with a blank face, then opened the door and stepped out. She followed, locked the car, and walked behind him to Baji’s grave and the Sano family plot. He stood in front of Baji’s grave. She stood beside him and prayed. She had brought a bottle of water, poured it over the stone, and cleaned the grave with her hands before praying again. Mikey watched her clean, all the while holding a charm between his palms.

“Hope you’re doing well, Baji. We’ll be back again soon,” Mikey said, slipping the charm back into his pocket. He turned on his heel and walked towards the Sano family grave.

“Heya, Baji. I’ve kept my promise and looked after Mikey for the past ten years, and I’ll keep doing it, so keep watching over me, okay?” Akari let out a small sigh and looked up at the sky. “I’ll come back with Mikey again soon. See you then.”

She turned around the rows and rows of family graves and found Mikey praying in front of the Sano family grave once more. She watched from a distance and gave him the privacy he needed. She heard him mumbling, so she stayed where she was. Eventually he turned, nodded slightly, and she walked over. She stood before the family grave and said her prayers for Emma and Shinichiro, whom she had never met, then walked on to the Kurokawa family grave. She tugged her trousers up a little and crouched in front of it.

“Izana, I’m back. How’re you doing? I hope you’re doing well, I’m doing great! Mikey and I are both fine. We’re about to meet another gang to discuss some matters. Hope it goes well.” She crossed her fingers and smiled at the gravestone. “I’ll be back again soon, so I’ll see you soon.” She stood, brushed the dust from her black suit, and Mikey, silent until then, murmured a quick word to Izana before they headed back to the car.

The car ride back was livelier, as Mikey talked about the rival gang and the deal they were planning. Well, it wasn’t really a deal. It was more a one-sided argument between Bonten and Tensei (let’s call them that), where Bonten would dominate the men of Tensei, who were already frozen with fear. So it was a mystery why Tensei would try to strike up a deal with Bonten. Something was wrong. Tensei knew a little too much about confidential information on the Bonten executives, including Sanzu and Akari being in a relationship. That was better than them knowing she owned the FNN, but information in the wrong hands was dangerous. If the enemy learned about it, they would know there was a weak link in Bonten. Sure, she and Sanzu were strong alone and stronger together, but as a tag team they were each other’s strengths and weaknesses. One wrong move could lead to disaster. That was why Mikey never put the two of them on the same team, just in case.

They arrived at the meeting spot a little late and spotted Koko and Sanzu’s car. They were already inside. Akari got out, Mikey shut his door, and she locked the car. She walked to the main entrance and pushed the doors open, with Mikey close behind. Feeling the gun at the small of her back, she walked in without fear and began searching for Sanzu and Koko. The bar was empty, not a customer in sight. It must have been reserved for Bonten. But something felt off. The bartender wasn’t there either.

A gunshot rang out. She rushed towards the sound. A curtain separated her and Mikey from where it had come from. She drew her gun, aimed it at the area behind the curtain, and shielded Mikey, since he was her top priority. She lifted the curtain slightly and saw no one. The coast was clear. She singled to Mikey that it was safe and crept towards the sound. The door to a room in the corner was open. She pulled her phone from her pocket and placed it on the floor at the edge of the room. The black screen reflected the room’s interior. Inside, Koko and Sanzu were pointing their guns at something, or someone, lying on the floor.

### Four

Sanzu and Koko’s shoulders relaxed, their grips on the guns loosening. Akari made a low whistling sound through her lips, and Sanzu’s ears perked up. He spotted the phone in the corner, flashed a peace sign and grinned. She shook her head, stood up and went into the room, with Mikey still on her tail.

“So what happened? Who’s this?” she asked, looking down at the man on the floor, a single bullet in his forehead. Blood seeped from the wound and ran down his body, staining the carpet of the VIP room.

Koko glanced at the body again, then back at Akari and Mikey. “He’s a Bonten underling. A traitor, selling info to other gangs. Great way to make money. Not a great way to get caught.” He scoffed, a little disgusted.

“Well, he’s dead now. No problem.” Akari shrugged. Sanzu’s head snapped round, and he gave her a hard look.

“He sold information about us, sweetheart. Us. Confidential shit. He deserved a worse death.” Sanzu reached into his pocket for his pill packet. Akari noticed, gripped his wrist tightly and gave him a look. He got the message and sheepishly slid the pills back into his pocket.

“So you’re saying other people know this information, right?” Mikey asked, repeating everything they knew. The three of them nodded.

“The boss of Tensei should be here soon. Do we attack?” Akari raised an eyebrow at the boys. “Because I have a plan.”

Sanzu POV

She laid out the plan briefly, leaving them enough room to act on their own, as long as it didn’t wreck her part in it.

Sanzu watched her pull at the roots of her hair until it looked like someone had grabbed her by it. She undid one of the braids and let her hair fall loose against her neck and face. She told Koko to grab the duct tape she had spotted in the corner when she came in and tear off a piece long enough to cover her mouth and scar. She yanked hard at her dress trousers, and he heard the familiar tear of expensive fabric as her upper thigh came into view. She tugged the shoulder of her suit jacket until it hung crooked. She unbuttoned her white blouse, then buttoned it again, leaving one button mismatched right at her cleavage, just enough to hide the Bonten tattoo. It was the perfect look for her plan. This was their advantage over Tensei. They knew Akari and Sanzu were together, but had no idea what either of them looked like.

Mikey sat in the middle of the couch and pulled Akari down onto his thigh, while Koko and Sanzu stood on either side of him. Mikey held her duct-taped wrists loosely behind her back, but it looked convincing enough that Tensei would think she was a hostage. In fact, Koko had cut slits in the edges of the tape so it would tear easily. Soon, footsteps sounded outside. A tall man stepped into the room, followed by his two most trusted men.

“What the hell happened here?” he asked, looking down at the dead man slumped against the wall, then at Akari’s bound figure. His eyes lingered on the gap in her blouse before he looked back at Mikey.

“He’s a traitor. Selling our information to you lot. So he got what he deserved,” Mikey said calmly, keeping Akari on his lap.

“And who’s this pretty lady?” He looked her over again. Sanzu wanted to slit his throat for looking at her like she was his toy.

“One of our whores. She did a great job pleasing me while we waited for you,” Sanzu said, flashing a sly smirk and playing his part. He ignored Akari’s muffled, duct-taped protests and her crocodile tears, which were very convincing. “We’ll give her to you, since you’re the one who set up this meeting.” The boss’s face lit up, grateful to get his hands on a beautiful woman like Akari. Sorry to disappoint, though.

He glanced at the two men beside him and tilted his head towards Akari. Sanzu watched her look up at Mikey in terror, while Mikey just kept giving her a blank look. He shoved her off his lap, and she hit the floor with a muffled shriek. The two men grabbed her roughly and held her tight.

“You two can take her into the other room and have your fun,” the boss said. The men nodded, grinning creepily, and dragged the yelling Akari away.

“Now, shall we get started on the deal?”

Sanzu was already boiling inside. He could barely stop himself from ripping the skin off the man’s smug face.

Akari POV

Content note: this section includes an attempted sexual assault and violence.

One of the men yanked her along by the wrist towards the nearest VIP room. Her legs dragged across the floor as she kept up the crying. One man kicked the door open, and the other threw her onto the leather couch and pinned her down. With her hands taped behind her back, she waited for the moment they would lose their heads, blinded by greed. It was disgusting, but it was the only way the plan could work. She had to do her part.

She lay sprawled across the couch. One man sat heavily on her legs and hauled her upright by the shoulders. The other was at her feet, pulling off her heels.

“Aren’t you a beauty?” the man on her lap asked. He gripped her chin and tilted her face up to his, tear-streaked and terrified, exactly as she wanted him to see. She jerked her head away. The man at her feet started tugging at the torn fabric of her trousers.

“Untie her hands,” the man on her lap said. “I want her to fight back a bit.”

The one behind her moved in, tearing at the duct tape while keeping a firm grip on her wrist. The moment her hands were free, she turned. The man beneath her froze in shock, but he didn’t stop her. She smiled at him sweetly, then jabbed the pressure point under his jaw, right beneath his ear. He went limp and dropped unconscious.

The other man stopped and stared at her face, where the tape had come away. “What kind of scar is that?”

“Who cares?” She pulled the gun from her waistband, where she had hidden it earlier, and pressed it to his temple. Before he could finish reacting, she pulled the trigger. The silencer swallowed the shot. He slumped sideways, blood trickling down his temple and across the leather couch. She turned and shot the unconscious man too. She didn’t need any more hindrances to the plan.

She got off the couch and left the bodies on the floor. Stretching out her shoulders, she wiped the spit from her neck and smeared the dead man’s blood across her collar, making it look worse than it was. Gun in hand, she headed back to the room where Mikey, Koko, Sanzu and the Tensei boss were talking. The door had been left open, so she could see everyone from the corner. She noticed Koko’s quick glance at her. She pointed her gun at the boss’s head. Koko nudged Mikey and waited a few seconds before letting out a fake sneeze.

“Excuse me,” Koko said.

“Bless you, Koko,” Mikey replied. That was her cue. She fired, and the bullet tore through the boss’s abdomen. He stopped moving and clutched his stomach, trying to hold in the blood. Akari let out a short breath of relief. She walked into the room, still streaked with blood, and kept her gun trained on his head. She sat on Sanzu’s lap on the couch. He watched her every move, staring at her state. She felt his hands settle around her waist and his head drop onto her shoulder.

“So? What now? Should I just kill him?” she asked, looking at Mikey.

“Let me ask one thing first.” Mikey looked at the panting boss. “Do you have any family you care about?”

The boss’s eyes went wide, and he stared up at the ceiling. “Yeah, my wife. Please, don’t touch her. My death should be enough for you.”

Sanzu laughed out loud. “You messed with Bonten. Death is never enough.” Mikey stared at the dying man for a moment, then spoke quietly.

“Well then, looks like your wife is in for a big surprise. Akari.”

“Of course, boss.” She pulled the trigger. The bullet went straight through the middle of his forehead. Perfect.

“Are we delivering his body to his wife?” Sanzu asked, eyes shining.

“Ooooh, that’s a great idea!” Akari clapped her hands together.

“My god, you’re both crazy,” Koko said, shrugging and looking at Mikey.

“Go ahead.”

“Sweet! I’m gonna put the Bonten logo in the box,” Sanzu said.

“Don’t be stupid, babe.” Akari gave him a look of disappointment. “Brand it onto his body. He deserves it.” She smirked, and Sanzu grinned back. He tightened his grip around her waist and rested his head in the crook of her neck.

“I knew you’d get me,” he murmured. “But I don’t like the smell of other men on you. Even if this worked, I don’t want your body stained by other men’s germs. Especially hickeys.” He glared at the back of her head, so dangerously that it made her skin prickle.

“Let’s head back,” Mikey announced, standing up and walking to the main door. Koko followed but checked the room for evidence that could point to the Bonten members. Sure enough, he found Akari’s suit coat lying in the room with the two dead men. “Yeesh,” he muttered, grabbing the coat and leaving the rest of the room alone.

Sanzu left the bar and came back carrying a body bag. He packed the body in, zipped it shut, hoisted it onto his shoulders and carried it out to the car. He dumped it in the back, and he and Koko drove off to the hideout.

Mikey was waiting in the driver’s seat. Akari slid into the passenger seat and shut the door. Mikey started the engine and drove back to the building.

“Great plan you had there, Akari,” he said, taking a turn.

“Thanks. Wouldn’t have worked without the duct tape we found in that room.”

“Don’t do something like that again.” He glanced at her quickly. “I don’t like the idea of you being treated like a whore. Like a prostitute.”

She scoffed. “I can’t promise that. But Sanzu’s the only man I’ll ever fold under.”

“Too much information, Akari,” Mikey replied, pulling into the driveway as the roller door opened.

“But the plan worked, that’s all that matters. I’ll do whatever I have to for Bonten so I can be of use.”

“You’ve done plenty already for Bonten,” Mikey said, looking at her in the rearview mirror as he parked in the designated spot beside Koko and Sanzu’s vehicle. “So don’t talk like you’re useless. You’re not. But yes, thank you for your service. Now go upstairs and get cleaned up.” He climbed out and walked towards the elevator at the back of the garage. In the distance, Akari saw Sanzu dragging the body bag towards the torture table.

“Just brand him, babe. No need to do anything else to him. Leave the blood in too. Extra fun!” Akari squealed. She grabbed two pairs of plastic gloves and two hairnets, slipped the gloves on,

and pulled a hairnet over her hair, tucking in every strand. She tossed Sanzu the other pair, and he put his on over his mullet.

He set the iron in the fire and waited for it to glow bright red. He pulled on a pair of heatproof gloves, took out the poker, and lifted it over the body. He pressed it down slowly onto the chest and heard the sizzle of skin and muscle fusing together. When he lifted the iron away, it left the perfect Bonten mark on the bare skin, raw and red around the edges. Sanzu’s eyes met Akari’s, and they both smiled.

“We need a waterproof box,” she said, looking around.

“Already got one.” He pulled one from behind him and set it on the floor. “Hands under his legs, I’ll grab the other end.” Together they lifted the body and lowered it into the box, blood dripping slowly onto the floor. She pushed the body in, and Sanzu shut the lid.

“Woo!” Akari exclaimed, high-fiving him. “Alright, who’s delivering it?”

“I’m going myself. Better fresh, no?” Akari laughed at his comment.

“Okay, I’m going to clean up upstairs.” She pulled off her hairnet, then her bloody gloves, and tossed them into the fire with the brander. She walked to the elevator, swiped her card key and stepped in, watching Sanzu hoist the box into the car as the doors closed and carried her up.

### Five

The elevator dinged open, and Akari stepped out. Everyone turned to look at her at once. Her clothes were literally torn, after all.

“Love~ what the fuck happened to you?” Ran asked, raising a brow.

“I became a whore~” she moaned back, playing along with him.

“Explains the hickey,” Rindou said, pointing at her neck. Ran’s attention snapped to her neck, and he spotted the mark.

“Wait, are you being serious?”

“No, of course not. I belong to Sanzu. He belongs to me. I wouldn’t touch anyone else.” She shrugged. “Plus, it’s just a couple of hickeys. Sanzu can redo them later for me,” she said, as if it was perfectly normal.

“Tch. I want to sleep well tonight,” Rindou muttered, clutching his head.

“Well, whose fault is it that you decided to drink last night? Hmm, Kurage-kun?” she teased. He scoffed but didn’t reply. “Anyway, I feel gross, so I’m taking a bath. Someone start making dinner, please,” she announced, heading into her room.

She picked up the basket of dirty clothes and carried it to the laundry room in the corner of the floor. She sorted the clothes carefully, putting the delicate pieces into mesh bags before

starting the machine. She took the empty basket back to her room, grabbed a clean towel and a fresh set of clothes (black low-cut long sleeves, black sweatpants and underwear), and hurried into the bathroom to turn on the tap. As the hot water began to fill the tub, she realized it would take a while, so she headed back to the kitchen.

Of course, nobody had moved a muscle. Nobody was making dinner. Sighing, she quickly washed the rice, put it in the cooker and switched it on.

“Takeomi, Mochi and Kaku.” All three turned to face her.

“Yeah?” Takeomi asked.

“Make dinner,” she said. Ran and Rindou jeered at the three of them, and she shot them a glare. “Ran, Rindou. Keep laughing and you’ll be up early tomorrow making breakfast for everyone.” That shut them up fast. The three men stood and headed into the kitchen to start cooking. She was quietly grateful that every Bonten member knew how to cook.

She went back to the bathroom, locked the door, and turned off the tap, since there was enough water in the tub. She stripped off and tossed the suit aside. The dress trousers were ripped to hell, the jacket sleeve was stretched and creased, and the blood had soaked into it. The white dress shirt was now a deep crimson. The suit was going in the bin. It needed replacing either way. She stuffed the torn suit into a plastic bag, undid her braids, and stepped under the shower-head. The water washed the blood away. She scrubbed her neck and lower back several times with soap before finally sinking into the bath to relax.

She dried herself, pulled on her clean black clothes, and watched the water drain as she pulled the plug. She dried her hair again, watching it fly in every direction, then brushed it down until it fell straight and calm. She packed the dryer away, cleaned the bathroom, unlocked the door and stepped out. She dropped her underwear into the laundry basket in her room. Holding the rubbish bag with the suit in it, she slipped on her slippers and walked to the main room. She passed the three men still cooking and dropped the bag in the bin in the corner of the kitchen.

“Is that your suit?” Kakucho asked, halfway through cutting the carrots.

“Yeah, I need a new one now.”

“Want to go together tomorrow?”

“Sure, let’s go. How’s dinner coming along?”

“Curry. Give it another fifteen minutes.” He slid the chopped carrots into the pot. She nodded and sank onto the couch next to Ran, immediately feeling herself relax. She yawned, leaned her head back and stared up at the ceiling.

“Tired, love?” Ran asked, sliding his arm behind her and around her shoulders. He pulled her closer, and her head settled on his shoulder. He rested his head on top of hers and drew slow lines up and down her arm, watching her drift off.

Ran POV

Ran watched her fall asleep on his shoulder. She looked peaceful, but the dark circles under her eyes were getting worse. Her weekend shifts at the club had turned her into a night owl, sleeping through the day and waking up at night to head back to work. They sometimes went to the club, but Akari never sat with them, because she was always busy behind the bar. Maybe she should unwind with them this week, just for a change of pace.

Koko was on his phone on the other side of him, scrolling through whatever he was into, while Rindou braided his hair. It was cute to watch. Ran had cut his own hair, so Rindou didn’t braid his anymore, and seeing him do Koko’s hair was too cute! Ran missed his long hair, but it took far less time to maintain now, so it had been a good call. Rindou’s new style was cute too. It was so versatile. But Akari’s hair couldn’t be compared to Rindou’s. Her style was unique, and clever. Only she would ever have thought of it. It was like having two looks in one.

“Dinner’s ready,” Takeomi called from the kitchen. Rindou tied off the braid on Koko’s hair, and Koko waited for him to finish before getting up. Ran gently shook Akari awake. She groaned and yawned.

“What is it?” she asked, rubbing her eyes. She grabbed his wrist as he pulled her to her feet.

“Dinner’s ready, love.”

“Ohh! Finally! I’m starvin’!” she exclaimed, suddenly bright-eyed and wide awake. She rushed to the table and dropped into her seat. The elevator opened behind Ran, and Sanzu stepped out.

“Just in time, dinner’s ready,” Ran said, looking over at Sanzu, who was already hurrying towards his room.

“Be there in a bit,” Sanzu called back, disappearing inside.

Ran walked to the table and sat in his usual spot. They all said their thanks for the meal and dug in.

### Six

Akari grabbed the designer suit from its hanger and walked into the changing room. She drew the curtain, kicked off her shoes, and stepped onto the raised platform. She undressed and slipped into the suit, piece by piece. Once she was in it, she yanked the curtain back and stood confidently in front of Kakucho, who was sitting opposite her changing stall.

He gave her a small look and nodded. “It looks good on you,” he said, but his eyes were somewhere else. He was staring at her neck. She planted her hands on her hips and glared at him until he looked up at her face. He sighed deeply. “Your hickeys, Akari.”

“Yeah, what about them?” she snapped, turning back to the mirror to decide between this suit and another.

“Aren’t they darker?”

She stopped moving and glanced at Kakucho.

“I knew my eyes weren’t playing tricks on me,” he said, shaking his head at her.

FLASHBACK TO LAST NIGHT

She had been lying on her bed when Sanzu walked in and yanked the sheets away.

“What the fu—” He slammed his lips onto hers, kissing her hard, with passion and a bit of aggression. His hand slid under her shirt and traced slow patterns across her stomach, sending small shivers through her. He pulled back and looked at her, jealousy burning in his eyes.

“Where else did they touch you?” he demanded. She stayed quiet to see how he would react. He noticed her attitude and leaned close to her ear. “Don’t make me mad, Akari,” he said in a low, rough voice.

She tried to turn her head towards him, but he held her cheek and turned her face back. He kissed her again, then moved his hands up to her collarbones and traced the length of her neck. He paused over the mark there, then pushed her shirt up, and she felt him smirk against her mouth.

“Found one, sweetheart~” he said, running his fingers over the bruise and circling it. “Where are the others?”

She lifted her hands and cupped his face. He leaned into her palms, and she tugged his hair sharply, earning a small squeal. She pulled his head down towards her mouth.

“There’s a couple on my lower back,” she murmured into his ear. She felt his breathing catch. He pinned her wrists above her head and looked at her for a long moment, jealous and possessive. Then he rolled her onto her stomach, his weight settling across her legs, and turned his attention to the marks the men had left on her back. He traced them carefully, and she didn’t stop him.

“There, better,” he mumbled, sitting back. He stared into her eyes and let go of her wrists. “Remember, you’re mine, and I’m yours. Today’s plan was good, great even, but I don’t want any other man handling you like they don’t deserve to.” He leaned down until his lips brushed her ear. “I haven’t even started yet, Akari. Just wait until I’ve got you screaming my name. Over and over again.”

She swallowed hard and gripped the pillow tighter.

He turned her to face him and settled over her, his arms tightening around her back. The length of his hair tickled her bare shoulders.

“Akari,” he said.

“Yes?”

“I love you.”

She let out a soft sigh, wrapped her arms around his back and pulled him closer. She ran her fingers through his long hair. He melted into her touch, his breathing slowing. She realized he had fallen asleep on top of her. She smiled and kept stroking his hair until she drifted off too.

END OF FLASHBACK

“Akari?” Kakucho’s voice pulled her out of the memory. He stood in front of her stall, holding two other suits.

“Oh, yes. Thanks, Kaku.” She took the suits from him, stepped back into the stall, changed out of the one she was wearing and into the first. “How’s this one, Kaku?” She pulled the curtain back. He looked her up and down.

“I think this one’s good too.” Then he pointed at the waist. “I don’t like the red buttons.”

She nodded. “Same. So this one’s out.” She shut the curtain and tried on the last suit. When she stepped out some time later, this one felt the most comfortable of the three. “I think this is the one,” she said, pulling the curtain again. He stared at her and nodded.

“Yeah, I think so too. Put your shoes on and walk.” He pushed her shoes towards her, and she slipped them on. She strode up and down the corridor of the changing rooms, then stopped in front of her stall. She twisted her body, feeling her back crack. Then she suddenly threw a fist straight at Kakucho’s face. He blocked it easily with his palm. She smiled, lifted her leg and aimed the toe of her shoe at his temple, but pulled back before it made contact.

“Hey, this suit’s good!” she exclaimed, giving him an apologetic look. “I’m gonna buy this one.” She walked back into the dressing room, grabbed her clothes and headed out to the shop floor. Kakucho followed with the other two suits and hung them back on the rails. “Where’d you find this one?” she asked when he came back.

“Over there,” he said, pointing at the rack near the cash register. She went straight over, grabbed two more of the same suit, and put them on the counter.

“Hi, I’d like to buy these two, and the one I’m wearing,” she said, smiling at the cashier.

“Of course,” the cashier said, scanning the barcodes, including the one Akari was wearing. “I hope you realize these three are the same color and design.” She took the security tag off the collar of each suit.

“Yes, I’m aware.”

“Cash or card?”

“Card, thanks.” The cashier handed her the machine, and Akari tapped her black credit card while the payment went through. The cashier packed the suits into an orange paper bag with the well-known logo and slipped the receipt in. She handed the bag over, then came around the

counter with a pair of scissors. Her hand suddenly reached for Akari’s neck. Instinct kicked in. Akari caught her wrist and twisted it behind her back. The woman squealed in pain.

“What are you doing?” Akari snapped, tightening her grip.

“I was trying to cut the tag off your suit, since you’re wearing it out,” the woman whimpered. Akari felt a little guilty and let go.

“My apologies.” She let the cashier get on with it. The woman snipped the tag and brushed the dust off the new suit.

“Smooth moves, though, ma’am,” the cashier said with a small, pained smile. Akari noticed the red marks on her wrist and quickly bowed, apologizing again.

“No, it was my fault. I should have said something before I moved. Thank you for your purchase!” The woman bowed back, and Akari turned on her heel and headed out the door. Kakucho was waiting outside, leaning against the brick wall.

“Geez, took you long enough,” he sighed, taking the paper bag from her hand. He glanced around quickly, then handed her gun back. She tucked it into her waistband and felt whole and safe again.

“Thanks, Kaku.” She gave him a small smile. He nodded. “Now let’s go to that café over there,” she said, pointing at the one on the corner.

“Didn’t we go there before?” He seemed to recognize it. It was the same café she had visited with Sanzu, Kakucho and Izana twelve years ago.

“Yeah, we did.” She pushed the door open. The inside looked the same. The waitress from back then wasn’t there, but Akari recognized a familiar face: Taiju Shiba. He was working here. She followed the waitress to their table with Kakucho. At Akari’s request, the waitress led them to a secluded table. She seemed nervous around the two of them, but that was no surprise. A woman and a man in suits, both with facial scars? Quite the picture. Akari ordered two coffee jellies and two cups of black tea.

“Thank you,” she said when the drinks arrived. She passed one jelly and one cup to Kakucho, but his attention was elsewhere. It was on the TV on the far wall, where the store manager had turned up the volume.

“And just in with breaking news is ____ ____, with new information about the notorious criminal organization, Bonten.” Akari’s ears pricked up, and she listened to the reporter too. “Yes, I’m outside a house in Shibuya, Tokyo, where a large box was delivered this morning. To the shock of the homeowner, it held her husband, dead. He appears to have been shot twice, once in the abdomen and once through the middle of his forehead. The motive seems to be gang-related, as he was the leader of another gang in the area, Tensei. What’s most shocking is the Bonten symbol stamped on his chest.” Akari felt herself smirk at the memory of the hot iron burning through his skin. “Forensic examiners are searching the body for DNA that might link him to Bonten members, but the chances are looking slim. Back to you, Kaori.”

Kakucho’s gaze shifted from the TV to her. “You and Sanzu are crazy,” he said.

She shrugged and sipped her tea. “What can I say? We’re the crazy couple.” Around them, the other customers were whispering.

“Wow, how scary.”

“I hope they don’t come after innocent people like us.”

Akari and Kakucho kept listening to the chatter around them, trying hard not to laugh. There were two Bonten members in the café at that very moment.

“Hey, you must be Akari, right?” Taiju’s voice rang out across the café as he stared down at her.

### Seven

“Oh, hey, Taiju. How have you been?” Akari said calmly. Kakucho gave her a small look.

“I’ve been fine. On a date with your new boyfriend?” Taiju asked, glancing at Kakucho.

“Hmm? Oh, no. He’s my childhood friend. We’re just catching up.”

“So you and Sanzu are still together?” She nodded. “Wow, long time. Twelve years, huh?”

She turned to Kakucho. “You can leave if you want. I’ll go back on my own.” He nodded and picked up her paper bag.

“Nice seeing you again, Taiju,” Kakucho said politely. “I’ll take my leave, so catch up with Akari if you’d like.” He walked out without a sound, and Taiju slid into his seat.

“What are you doing now?” Taiju asked, staring at her intently.

“Me? I’m working at a martial arts school out in the countryside.” His eyes widened. She was lying about her job, and it didn’t sit well with her. But she had to do what she needed to do.

“Oh wow. That’s a great job.” Taiju paused. “So why are you here?”

“I’m just visiting friends from back then.” She gave him a small smile. “Fancy seeing you here, though. You must really love this café, huh?” she teased. He went pink with embarrassment.

“Oh, shut up!” He slammed his fist on the table, and the rest of the café turned to look. “Sorry,” he mumbled, going an even brighter shade of pink.

“So? What have you been doing these past twelve years?”

He was quiet for a moment before answering. “You must remember the battle we fought twelve years ago.” She nodded. “After that, I apologized to my siblings for what I put them through, and I left to live on my own. Since then I’ve been looking after myself and working, and now I’m in a high-ranking position at one of the corporate firms. Every now and then we get scammed by those rats in Bonten, but we can’t do a thing about it. We might as well be

dead meat if we complain or say anything.” He had no idea he was saying exactly what he shouldn’t.

“Oh wow! That’s a pretty dangerous job you’ve got,” she replied.

“Sure is,” he said. She glanced at her phone, then back at Taiju. “Sorry, I’ve got to go.” She slid a few banknotes onto the table. “For the drinks. See you again soon, Taiju. Stay safe!” She smiled and left the café.

She walked through the streets and wound her way through narrow alleys, turning in nearly every direction. Finally she reached the garage of the Bonten building, opened the roller door with her key card, waited for it to close behind her, and headed for the elevator.

“I’m back~” she called as the doors opened. Today was quiet, but it was a forced kind of quiet. Sanzu and Rindou both had bruised faces. Ran sat cross-legged on the couch, watching the two on the floor with an intense stare. Koko was at the dining table, tapping away at his keyboard. Mochi and Takeomi were out on a job. Kakucho and Mikey were nowhere to be seen.

“Where’s Mikey and Kakucho?” she asked, sitting on the couch next to Ran and joining in the staring.

“They went out,” Koko said without taking his eyes off the screen. “Kakucho told me to tell you he left your suit outside your bedroom door.”

“Oh sweet! Thanks, Koko.” She turned to him. “Can you put some cash into my account? I spent a bit too much today buying new suits.”

“Hmm? Sure, give me a couple of hours.” Sanzu suddenly lifted his head.

“Favouritism~” he whined. “How come you give her cash, but not me~?”

“You spend it on unnecessary drugs. She bought clothes, which are necessary. Do you get the difference, or do I need to spell it out in a way a five-year-old can understand?” Koko snapped, and Akari and Ran burst out laughing.

“So what he’s saying is, no more drugs.” Akari spelled it out for Sanzu. He flopped onto the floor in a star shape, whining and babbling like a child. She rolled her eyes. “Oh, grow up, babe.”

Ran turned his attention to her and started undoing her braids. She scooted closer and turned her back to him so he could do whatever he was doing to her hair. “So what happened to these two while I was out?” she asked as Ran raked his fingers through her hair, working out the knots.

“They were arguing about whether milk or cereal goes in first,” Ran explained, twirling a long strand around his finger. She felt Sanzu’s eyes on her immediately.

“Seriously, that’s stupid.” She looked over at the two on the floor. “Who said what?”

“I said cereal, he said milk,” Rindou said, pointing at Sanzu.

She gave Sanzu a disapproving look. “Sorry, babe, but I’m siding with Rin on this one.” She stuck her tongue out at him. “So what’s with the broken ceramics on the floor?”

“They threw them at each other,” Ran said, tying her hair into a neat low bun. A few white strands slipped loose, so he undid it and started again.

“So you both argued about something that petty, and then threw ceramic plates at each other?” She glanced at them without moving her head much. Her tone sharpened.

The room went silent. The two on the floor stared at her, a flicker of fear in their eyes. She sighed loudly, and their attention snapped to her. “Rin, Sanzu, go clean up. It better be spotless, or someone’s going to get hurt. You don’t want to see me come after you when that happens.” They scrambled to their feet and went off in different directions. “Jeez, they’re such children,” she muttered under her breath.

“You’re the youngest of all of us. I don’t think you get to say anything,” Ran chimed in, tugging lightly at her hair as he braided the bottom half and left the white on top to fall loose.

“Oh, shush,” she said with a laugh, pressing a finger to her lips. She heard him laugh behind her as he tied off the ends. He crossed the two plaits over and around the white half of her hair and made a small ponytail, tied together by the black braids.

“Done,” he said, tapping her shoulder. Cool air curled around her bare neck, something she hadn’t felt in a while.

“Ohh, it’s so cute! Thanks, Ran!” She turned and smiled at him.

“No worries, love.” He looked away and turned his attention to the two cleaning up the ceramics. Rindou was sweeping around the leather couch, back and forth, careful and methodical. Sanzu was in the kitchen with a small dustpan. Rindou had taken the big brush, which left Sanzu struggling.

The elevator chimed and opened, revealing Kakucho, Takeomi and Mochi. Mikey was still nowhere to be seen.

“Welcome back,” she called as the three came into the main area. Mochi flopped onto the couch and shut his eyes. Takeomi perched on the dining table a few seats from Koko and lit a cigarette. White smoke curled around him and drifted into her nose. She scrunched her face, got up and switched on the air vent. The air rushed in and cleared the smoke. Kakucho disappeared into his room and came back with a stack of paperwork, which he set on the table in the middle of the room. The Bonten executives gathered around and stared at it.

“What’s this?” Rindou asked, stopping mid-sweep to look at the papers. Akari leaned over his shoulder and saw the symbol at the top of the page, one she knew all too well.

“Ashinuke,” she mumbled, picking up a single sheet. Kakucho nodded.

“Yeah. Ashinuke wants a meeting between executives. They’ve been asking for a couple of months. We ignored it until now because we didn’t have the information we needed about them. I’ve talked to M—”

“You could’ve just asked me for information about them,” she cut in. The executives all looked at her.

“How do you even know about them, Akari?” Takeomi asked, stubbing out his cigarette on the table. Smoke drifted slowly into the air.

“I ran Ashinuke ten years ago,” she said. Takeomi’s eyes went wide, while the others nodded, since they knew the story all too well. “Things may have changed since then, but I didn’t expect it to still be running.” She shrugged.

“So how come we didn’t know about this?” Takeomi asked, eyeing her suspiciously.

“Oi, don’t go suspecting me of being a traitor. Mikey knows about it. And if Ashinuke’s executives are still the same, then it should be fine.”

“Well, I guess that’s okay, then,” Kakucho said. “But they’re requesting a meeting with all of us. That’s Mikey’s call.” The executives nodded in agreement.

“Where is Mikey?” Sanzu asked. “Wasn’t he with you?” He looked at Kakucho.

“Hmm? Yeah, he’ll be up soon.” Right on cue, the elevator dinged and Mikey walked in, gripping a small black suitcase tightly.

### Eight

Mikey walked silently to the couch and set the suitcase on the table. He entered the code, and the lid flipped open to reveal thousands of dollars in banknotes. She grabbed a small stack and inspected it.

“What’s with all this money?” Mochi asked, breaking the silence.

“It’s fake. Don’t even bother with it.” She noticed the subtle differences in the detail in the corner of a note, then held it up to the light, pinching the corner with a tissue. Mikey nodded, confirming it was fake.

“So? Are we meeting Ashinuke or not?” Rindou asked impatiently. “Why do they even want to meet us?”

“They’ve offered us better access to the underworld auctions,” Mikey said, closing the suitcase.

“We already have everything we need, so what’s the point?” Koko snapped, glancing quickly at Mikey.

“Exactly. We don’t need their help,” Takeomi backed him up.

“I don’t think that’s their main goal.” Akari spoke up, and their heads turned to her. “Sanzu and I will go meet them alone. You can wire us and listen in. We’ll find out what they want, and if it’s good enough for you guys, we accept. If not, we politely decline.”

“You can’t just politely decline. They’ll know the identities of two of our members. That’s risky,” Mochi said, and the rest of the executives agreed.

“Better two than all, no?” she replied, making her point.

“Better one than two?” Kakucho said quickly, and a few of the executives laughed.

“You’re right, Kaku. Then I’ll go alone. How’s that? Mikey?” She looked over at him. He gave her a blank look.

“Do what you like. Just make sure you come back.” His voice was cold.

“Where am I meeting them?”

“They said somewhere private, where it suits us,” Kakucho explained.

“Then the FNN club. That way you guys have clear access if anything goes wrong. Accept their meeting for me, Kaku. Tell them to be at the FNN at 4 pm tomorrow.” Kakucho nodded and got up to do exactly as she asked. “Alright, now that’s sorted, let’s eat. I’m starving.” She headed for the kitchen, and Sanzu and Takeomi followed to help set up dinner.

- * *

She waited outside the FNN the next evening in her uniform, dressed as the manager and owner of the club, her face mask on. She stood patiently at the door as two black cars pulled up out front and a group of familiar Ashinuke members stepped out.

“Good evening, gentlemen. I’m the owner of the FNN. The Bonten members are expecting you. Please follow me.” She held the main door open, walked through, and keyed the pin code into the VIP door. It beeped open. “Go into the first door on your left, please, gentlemen. The Bonten members will join you shortly.” They filed in, and the door shut behind the last of them. She walked back to the main door, peeked out through the glass, and bolted it shut.

She lifted the bar flap, took off her bartending uniform, and changed into the black suit she kept under the counter for Bonten meetings. She untied the bottom half of her hair and braided it quickly, using the hair ties on her wrist. She folded the club uniform, tucked it beneath the bar, and began making six drinks, starting with the first one John had taught her: a basic martini. She set the drinks on a tray, removed her face mask and walked into the VIP corridor. She knocked three times, and the door opened to reveal Akio.

“Here are your drinks, gentlemen,” she said sweetly, walking in and setting the tray on the table in the middle of the room. She took the chair opposite the couch and smiled at them. “It’s been a while, hasn’t it? You’ve gotten so old!”

The men just stared at her in shock.

“What? You didn’t recognize me? I’m so sad…” she said, wiping away a fake tear.

“We’re supposed to be meeting Bonten here, so what are you doing here?” Akio asked, oblivious as ever.

“Connect the dots, dummy,” Daisuke said, handing out the drinks.

“Oh shit. How things have changed,” Kai said, taking his glass. “So? Where are the others?”

“They’re a little too cautious about their identities. Since you already know me, they sent me to meet you instead. Sorry about that.” She apologized on their behalf.

“Well, that’s understandable,” Ao chimed in.

“Anyway, as much as I’d like to catch up, we should get back to the matter at hand.” The men nodded. “What are you offering Bonten that we don’t already have?”

“You know about the underworld auction?” Daisuke began. “I know Bonten is a big part of it. But what a lot of new gangs don’t know is that the underworld auction has two sides. Bonten has only been around a few years, so you wouldn’t know about the darker side.” That was new information to her.

“I see. So what’s different about the darker side compared to the ‘lighter side,’ so to speak?”

“The lighter side is open to anyone with connections. It’s for people with minor links to the asset holders. The darker side works the same way, except it’s for people with connections that run deep with the ‘oldies,’ I guess. We’ve been running for ten years, so we count as one of the oldies. If you form an alliance with us, the darker side of the underworld auction opens up to you.”

“Is there a difference in what’s sold between the two?”

This time Ao answered. “The lighter side is the minor stuff. Illegal drugs, illegal weapons, rare items and so on. The darker side is the more gruesome stuff. Prostitutes, organs, that kind of thing. We attend them, but we never buy anything, because we don’t take part in that. We thought it might benefit Bonten more than us, so we’re risking our own gang by offering this partnership.”

“Did you need anything in return?”

“You should probably discuss this with the rest of your executives before you make a decision. This would benefit you more than us, so—” The door flew open, cutting Ao off.

“There’s nothing you can offer us. Our partnership is already big enough,” Sanzu declared, striding in with his head held high and a gun in one hand. Mikey stood behind him, scanning the Ashinuke executives with a cold stare before his eyes met hers.

“I see,” Daisuke said, standing to meet Sanzu’s gaze. “If you want to accept our proposal, that’s up to you. But I ask that you don’t interrupt our work back home in Yokohama.” Sanzu and Akari both turned to look at Mikey, who was still staring blankly at Daisuke.

“Why are you giving us this opportunity when we offer you nothing back?” Mikey asked in a flat monotone, breaking the staring match.

Daisuke and Akio glanced at her, then back at Mikey. “It’s simply to repay Akari for forming Ashinuke all those years ago. She may never have visited us like she promised, but this is our way of repaying her for her service.” Akari felt a small pang of guilt. She had broken her promise to visit them, but she was grateful for their repayment all the same.

Sanzu gave her a small, suspicious look. She returned it with a raised eyebrow and a slight shrug.

“How did you know she was part of Bonten in the first place?” Sanzu asked, trying to put his suspicions to rest. It bothered her a little that the Ashinuke men seemed to know. She had never told anyone from the past that she had joined Bonten.

“Her tattoo,” Daisuke said. “She’s had it since back then, so it’s no surprise she joined Bonten.”

“How are you so sure she joined Bonten?”

“Just a hunch,” Daisuke said, looking at Sanzu. Sanzu was about to press him harder, but Mikey cut him off.

“Sanzu, that’s enough. We’ll accept your offer,” Mikey announced, looking straight at Daisuke with dead, dark eyes. Daisuke seemed taken aback by the emptiness in those eyes, but he held out his hand for a handshake. Mikey stared at the hand, refused it, and nudged Sanzu forward to take it instead. Sanzu reluctantly shook Daisuke’s hand in Mikey’s place.

“The auctions run weekly, as you know,” Daisuke said. “People who enter the lighter side can get in with a password that changes every week. Those who go into the darker side need a special badge. With the badge, security will guide you with specific instructions.”

“I’ve seen that badge on several people,” she said, glancing at Sanzu. He walked out of the room, leaving her and Mikey alone with the Ashinuke men. “You don’t need to supply us with the badge. We’ve already got some.”

“I see. How many have you got?”

“Mm, about tw—”

“We’ve got four,” Sanzu said, cutting her off as he walked back in, holding four badges. He showed them to Daisuke, who hesitantly reached out to inspect them.

“Yeah, these are the ones. I won’t ask how you got them, but you can bring four people to the auction now. Bring masquerade masks to hide your identities. Everyone wears them there, so make sure you fit in. Now that’s all we wanted to discuss, so we’ll be on our way.” Daisuke stood, and the Ashinuke men followed him out the door.

“See you all soon, I guess,” she said quickly as they left the VIP room. Akio and Kai nodded at her and went out. She followed them to the main door, unlocked it, and watched them climb

into their cars and drive away. She locked the door again, carried the tray back from the VIP room and began clearing the empty glasses. Mikey and Sanzu took seats on the barstools and watched her work on the martini glasses.

“Do you want something to drink? Or are you good?” she asked. Sanzu rested his elbows on the counter.

“Can you make me a drink, sweetheart?”

“Which one? There are hundreds.”

“Surprise me~,” he said with a playful wink. She got to work, aware of his stare.

“Mikey? What about you?”

“I’m good.” He glanced at the menu, then turned to Sanzu. “Go get the others.” Sanzu obeyed and went through the pin code on the door, leaving her alone with Mikey. “You’re lucky they haven’t changed much,” he said, watching her shake the metal shaker.

“Yeah, I’m lucky I led them back then. But I’ve got Bonten on my hands now. I left Ashinuke for you and Sanzu, so there’s no way I’m going back, in case that’s what you’re wondering.” She poured Sanzu’s drink into a glass and slid it to his empty seat.

“Grateful to have you on Bonten’s side,” Mikey said quickly. His eyes lingered on the glass, bubblegum pink like Sanzu’s hair. She noticed his glance and started on her own concoction. When she was finished, she poured it into another glass: a pure white mixture with a black olive, to match his eyes.

“Here you go!” She pushed it towards him. He stared at it blankly. “It’s low in alcohol, in case you’re wondering. Just milk, a teeny bit of vodka and a black olive.”

“Thank you, Akari,” he said with a small smile as the VIP door opened and the executives poured in. They took seats along the bar. She made their drinks, some ordering specific ones, others leaving it to her. She was careful with every step, much more so than when she served the public.

“We have four seats for the new auction Ashinuke told us about,” Sanzu announced, grabbing the attention of the executives. “Who’s going?”

She put her hand up. “I want to go,” she said, and every head turned to her. Mikey looked at her, and she could tell he knew she wouldn’t back down. So he picked the other three himself.

“Rindou, Ran and Koko. You three go with her. Best behavior. Don’t tarnish the Bonten name,” Mikey said. Sanzu’s face drained of color by the second, jealousy written all over it.

“Awww, babe, maybe next time~” she teased, leaning over the counter to give him a quick peck on the nose.

“The auction is tomorrow night, so I expect all four of you there.” Mikey turned to her. “Akari, ditch the suit. We need you to blend in.” She nodded, unable to argue with that.

“Of course. I have a black dress in my room,” she said. He nodded and finished his drink. The night went on, with the executives knocking back a few glasses of alcohol. She was the responsible one, and she stopped serving them after three each, to keep their brains working well enough to think straight.

### Nine

The black car slowed to a stop outside the auction venue. Adjusting the masquerade mask tied at the back of her head, Akari stepped out once the driver had opened the door. She placed her foot on the concrete footpath and stood tall. Looking back at the car, she saw Ran, Rindou and Koko climbing out after her.

The auction was a formal event. A normal one would have been fine in a suit. But tonight was the hidden side of the auction, new ground for Bonten, so they had to tread carefully. She was glad Mikey had told her to ditch the suit. Plenty of women arrived on their partners’ arms in flowing designer dresses and masquerade masks.

“Shall we go in?” Koko asked in his usual tone, sizing up everyone around them. He had swapped his red tunic with yellow trim for a burgundy designer suit that set off his long white hair.

“Let’s go,” she said, climbing the steps to the main doors with the men behind her. For tonight, Mikey had made her wear a dress to suit the setting: a slim black low-cut dress that showed off the Bonten tattoo clearly. It fitted her perfectly and brushed the floor lightly as she moved. She had changed her hairstyle too, tying the bleached half into a bun at the back of her head and wrapping the mask’s string around it to hold it in place. The dress had a thigh split that came dangerously close to the top of her leg. It had its downsides, though. It gave her full range of movement, just in case, but there was nowhere to hide a gun. She had given hers to Ran for safekeeping, and she felt a little exposed without it. Ran and Rindou were in their usual outfits, teal and lavender suits with ties to match their hair.

She finally understood why Mikey had picked these three to come with her. With her in the dress, all four of them showed their tattoos, so they were clearly representing Bonten. Still, there was nothing to worry about, especially from the cops, since everyone here had some connection to gangs or criminals.

As they walked through the main doors, whispers broke out across the crowd.

“Hey, isn’t that—”

“Shush, they’ll hear you!” She turned her head in their direction, just to mess with them. They instantly looked scared and walked the other way.

“Bonten!” someone whispered in shock. Ignoring them, the four of them walked in silence to the far end of the building, where two security guards were watching the room. The guards’

eyes went to the badges pinned to their clothes. One of them had noticed the commotion and raised an eyebrow.

“Bonten?”

“Yes?” she answered, looking up to meet his gaze.

He glanced around for a moment before giving the instructions. “Go through these doors like the others. Once you’re inside there’s a bar. Ask for a black coffee, or four in your case. The bartender will lead you to your seats. A free drink is included.” The other guard pushed the doors open. “Enjoy.”

They walked through with the boys behind her and headed straight for the bar. Immediately, she caught a faint smell in the air, a little too familiar.

“Do you smell that?” she whispered to Rindou, who was on her right.

“Yeah, isn’t it weed? Smells just like the other times we’ve come here.”

She nodded. “But there’s something else mixed in with it. Something that isn’t weed.” She kept walking, scanning the room.

Ran reached the bar first. Of course he did, with those long legs. “Four black coffees,” he said. The bartender waited until they had all caught up, then left the bar and led them down a narrow, dark hallway, insisting they follow.

As she walked, she kept looking back. She spotted the security guard from the entrance talking to another bartender by the bar. It was strange. She wasn’t looking ahead, and she bumped straight into someone’s broad back.

“Look where you’re going, Akari,” Koko said, turning around and holding her shoulders as he looked down at her.

“My bad,” she said, shrugging off his hands. She followed the bartender through another door, which he opened by entering a pin code, and then held open for them.

“Take the stairs on the left and sit in room 10B. Drinks will be brought in a few minutes. The auction starts in about five minutes, so please get there in time.” He pointed to the stairs at the far left of the auction room. The stage at the front was covered by velvet curtains, with the lights set low.

She took the stairs and entered room 10B. It was surprisingly plain, with four chairs and a small table in the middle. The walls were lined with the same material as the stage curtains. She sat down and looked out over the crowd waiting for the auction to start.

“This is anything but normal,” she said, looking around. “It gives me eerie vibes.”

“It’s fine,” Koko said. “But why are we all the way up here if we’re supposed to be guests?”

“Something’s off,” Ran agreed, scanning the room for clues.

“Something’s going on here,” Rindou said. “Either Ashinuke set us up, or nobody expected Bonten to show up and they’re scared.”

“I don’t think Ashinuke would do it, since they know who we are,” Koko said, crossing his legs.

“Then if it’s not them, there’s a third party,” Rindou said.

She opened her mouth to tell them about the guard and the bartender talking earlier, but then someone knocked on the door. The boys exchanged a suspicious look.

“I’ll get it,” she whispered. She unlocked the door from the inside. “How can I help?” she asked, smiling politely at the man outside.

“I’ve got your free drinks.” He lifted a tray to show them.

“Oh, yes, of course. Come in.” The bartender walked in and crouched down to the low table in the middle of the room, placing the glasses on it one by one. Ran immediately grabbed a glass and set it in his lap. The bartender watched him closely.

“If you want refills or need anything, press this button on the wall,” he said, nodding at it.

“Thank you,” she said, watching him leave and locking the door behind him. She turned back to the boys. Ran was about to drink, but she rushed over and snatched the glass from him. “What do you think you’re doing?” she hissed.

“What? I wanted a drink,” he said with an innocent look.

“You’re so stupid, brother,” Rindou said, disappointed. “You should’ve seen the bartender watching you when you took the glass. There’s something in it.”

“I’m not stupid, I’m playing with you,” Ran said, poking out his tongue with a grin.

“Well, don’t play with us now. This isn’t the time,” Koko said, looking down at the stage as the curtains began to rise. “Don’t touch the drink. Just watch the auction.”

She looked down as the curtains finished rising.

“Welcome to the Noir auction!” The room erupted in applause, and the crowd cheered the presenter on. “Tonight’s auction will include the following items.” As he read them out, the goods were either dragged or wheeled onto the stage on trolleys.

The bidding went on for everything from a child’s organ and prostitutes to a stranger’s life and rare artifacts. The presenter was the same one who had run the earlier Blanche auction, but the atmosphere here was far tenser. She let her eyes drift from the stage for a second and scanned the room without moving her head. Sure enough, a few strange figures in the seats weren’t watching the stage at all. They were watching Room 10B, as though waiting for something to happen.

“Guys,” she whispered, getting their attention. “Don’t turn your heads towards me. Just listen.” They all hummed in response. “There are about ten men watching our room. Two in the room opposite us, seven in the crowd below, and one in the room next to us.”

“How’d you know about the room next to us?” Rindou asked, still watching the presenter pace across the stage.

“The guy who brought us the drinks never went back out the door we came through. And I’ve been watching the stairs. Nobody’s come down them, so he has to be here somewhere.”

“So what are you trying to say?” Ran asked.

“We need to leave. Something’s going on, and I don’t like it. I want out of here.” She adjusted her mask. She had known it from the moment they walked through the guarded door. “I saw the security guard and the bartender talking earlier, when the other bartender led us down that dark hallway.” She picked up the drink and held it in her lap. “See? We didn’t touch the drink, so the ice has melted. The ice isn’t floating anymore. There’s something in the ice.” Koko picked up his own glass and studied it.

“So what do you want to do?” Koko asked, swirling the liquid around. “How are we supposed to leave with all these people watching us?”

“I’ve got an idea,” Rindou said. “It might work, but it’s all we’ve got right now.”

### Ten

“What have you got in mind?” Ran asked, staring blankly at the stage.

“It relies on Akari heavily, though. Are you up for it?” Rindou asked. She hummed a yes as she listened to his plan. It was an ingenious plan, but as Rindou had said, it depended heavily on luck and on her.

“Yeah, I’ll do it.” She stood up from her chair and walked to the door. Then she turned to look back at the auditorium. She was hidden in the dark at the back of the room, out of sight of everyone watching. She pressed the button on the wall that the bartender had told her about. The wall vibrated faintly, and she waited a couple of minutes before there was a knock at the door. “He’s here,” she whispered. The boys didn’t reply, but they tapped their feet softly in response.

She opened the door slowly and looked at the bartender from earlier. “Did you call, ma’am?”

“Yes, could you please take the empty glasses? We’ve finished our drinks,” she said with a smile. He nodded and stepped inside. She walked behind him and sat back down while he gathered the four empty glasses. While his eyes were on the glasses, she glanced at Koko beside her. Koko whacked the bartender hard on the back of the head. His head snapped back at an unnatural angle, and he slumped to the floor, unconscious. She quickly picked up the glasses before they could smash and set them back on the table. She sat for a couple of

minutes, then stood and walked back to the door, dragging the unconscious man to the back of the room. There she stripped him of his bartending clothes and set them aside. She felt a bit bad for him, having to wake up without his work clothes.

She took off her ball mask, stepped out of the black dress, and pulled on the bartender’s clothes. She heard a faint whistle from behind her.

“Oh, shut up,” she whispered back at the boys, pulling her legs into the trousers. They were a little too long, so she folded the ends. She buttoned the white shirt, adjusted the collar and tied the bow tie. She slipped on his work shoes and tied the laces, then buttoned up his black waistcoat. She was lucky the bartender had fairly long black hair. She grabbed his hat from the floor and tucked her hair under it neatly. She pulled on his white gloves and looked back at the boys.

“Ran,” she whispered. He immediately began to shuffle in his seat. He took her gun and mask from his pocket and slid them across the floor to her, pretending to tie his shoelaces.

“Take this while you’re at it,” he said, handing her an earpiece. It was for communicating with the boys in Room 10B. She pushed it into her ear, wound the cord around and tucked it into her shirt. It was well hidden under her hair.

She placed her heels, ball mask and dress in the far corner, neatly folded, then stood tall. “I’m leaving.” The boys tapped their shoes softly on the floor again. She unlocked the door, left, and closed it behind her. She slipped her face mask on and walked down the hallway to the stairs.

Checking around, she made her way down the stairs to the door she had come through. The auction was still going, and the watchers didn’t suspect a thing as she walked past them. They kept their eyes on the auction, glancing at Room 10B only now and then. That meant she only had a few minutes before they noticed she was gone.

She pushed through the door and walked back along the dark hallway to the bar. She lifted the bar flap and went behind the counter, where an order came in straight away. She had no choice but to make the drink, or suspicion would fall on her.

“What’s up with the mask?” one of the other bartenders asked, serving a customer.

“I felt a sore throat coming on. Didn’t want to pass it on to you, hence the mask.” She lowered her voice to match the bartender who had been knocked out. “Room 10B wants refills.”

“What? They’re pickier than I thought,” he said, disappearing and coming back with four more glasses, the ice already in them. She touched one, and it was ice cold. She was right: the ice was poisoned, and it had been kept whole in the freezer. He passed her the gin and tonic, which she mixed in the shaker before pouring it into the four glasses.

“And Room 5B wants refills too,” she said quickly. She watched him, and sure enough, he took the ice straight out of the icebox rather than the freezer. He dropped a couple of cubes into the glasses and passed them over. She poured the same alcoholic mix into them and set the glasses

on the trays. She lifted one tray in each hand and walked behind the other bartender, who opened the bar flap for her.
