“Could you open the door up ahead too?” The bartender nodded and walked ahead of her. She had lied about Room 5B wanting refills. She just needed her hands full, so the bartender would enter the pin code, which she didn’t know. He pressed the numbers on the keypad.

She memorized the code as he pressed it: 1478. It was simple and easy to remember. The door opened, and he held it for her as she walked back into the auditorium.

“Thanks,” she said, starting up the stairs nearest the door. Carrying the trays carefully, she stopped outside Room 5B, the room opposite theirs. She knocked and waited. The door opened, and a young woman in a glamorous indigo dress stood in front of her.

“Evening, ma’am,” she said, smiling with her eyes.

“We didn’t order them,” the woman snapped, looking down at her with a filthy look. Akari hated people like her.

“It’s on the house,” she said calmly, hiding her irritation.

“Well, get on with it, then.” The woman pulled the door wider and sat back down in her chair. Akari set the poisoned drinks on the table. The woman and her husband, or whoever he was, were the only ones in the room. Once the drinks were down, she turned to leave, closing the door behind her but not leaving. She crept up behind the man, whom she saw as the biggest threat, pressed the pressure point in his neck hard and fast, and slipped back against the wall in the dark. He coughed up a little spit and slumped in his chair, his head falling towards his lap.

“Darling?” the woman said, staring at his unconscious body. She tried to shake him awake, but it was no use. Taking advantage of her confusion, Akari did the same to her. She dropped straight to the floor.

She pressed the small button on her earpiece and spoke into the mic on the cord. “I’ve dealt with Room 5B. The one directly across from you.” She saw the boys still watching the auction.

“Good job,” Ran’s voice said through the earpiece. “Now I need you to shoot the guys in the room next to us. 10A.”

“Copy,” she answered quickly, pulling the gun from her waistband. She lowered herself to the floor, the barrel peeking over the ledge. She looked down the sights at the man sitting alone in Room 10A. She set her finger on the trigger, and her hand didn’t waver as she pulled it. She watched the bullet pierce the man’s head in an instant.

“Done,” she said into the mic.

“Perfect. Now come back over here and change back.”

“Got it.” She stood up, moved the woman back into her seat, and swirled the drink around the melting ice. She tilted the woman’s chin and poured the drink into her mouth. The woman

choked, but Akari didn’t care. She took the woman’s thin wrist and forced her to grip the glass. Then the glass slipped from her grip and smashed on the floor. She did the same with the man. She didn’t know exactly what poison was in the ice, but she guessed it was potassium cyanide, since the ice had melted so abnormally fast, even in a chilled glass. If it really was cyanide, the two of them were as good as dead. She lifted the empty tray, picked up the other tray with the four drinks, and walked out of the room, locking the door from the inside before closing it.

She walked back down the staircase as if nothing had happened, then climbed the other staircase.

She knocked on the door of their room, and Koko opened it and welcomed her in. “Welcome back,” he said with a small smile, holding the door wider.

She put the drinks on the table and stepped out of sight of the people below. She grabbed the black dress, took off the bartender’s clothes, and slipped back into her dress. She changed her shoes, took off the hat and gloves, and put them back on the bartender, who was still unconscious. Dressing the limp man again was a struggle, but she got it done, then left the room. She gripped the door handle with the edge of her dress and went into the next room, 10A, after picking the lock. The man was slumped against his chair, blood dripping from his fingertips onto the floor. She held the door open and spoke into the mic that was still attached to her.

“Bring the bartender to Room 10A. Ask Rin.” She heard shuffling from the other room, and Rindou came into view, dragging the unconscious bartender across the floor. She pointed to the edge of the room, and he dropped the bartender against the wall. She asked Rin to stay in the room for a bit, then hurried back to Room 10B, grabbed the tray with the hem of her dress, and carried it back to Room 10A. She lowered the tray onto the lap of the dead man and gave Rindou a thumbs-up. He stood and left, and she followed him out, locking the door from the inside once more.

Back in Room 10B, she sat down and tied her hair back up the way it had been, wrapping the ball mask around the bun at the back of her head. Rindou started squirming in his seat, pulled a scope from his back pocket, and held out his hand. She passed him her gun. He clipped the scope on, slid down to the floor, and she kept her eyes on the stage. She heard the faint click of the trigger. Electrical sparks flew from the stage, and the stage lights began to flicker. The sparks spread in every direction, and the velvet curtains caught fire. The crowd began screaming and rushing for the doors. Using the chaos, the four of them opened the door and calmly walked out of the room. They went back through the dark hallway into the main area, out the main doors and down the steps at the bottom of the building. As soon as they reached the bottom, she looked back and saw Ran running after them. He gave her a small thumbs-up. He had done something.

She looked back at the building. The air around it shimmered in the extreme heat pouring out of it. It wouldn’t be long before the whole place went up in a fireball.

“Love, let’s go,” Ran called, waiting by the car. She walked to the door, and the building exploded behind her. A wave of heat and a heavy gust of wind rolled over her. Her dress fluttered wildly, but she didn’t care. She smiled darkly as she slid into the car and shut the door. She clicked her seatbelt on and pulled off her ball mask.

“What a night,” she said, letting out a long sigh and leaning her head back as the buildings slid past the window. The driver didn’t react. He just drove to the Bonten building as he’d been told. “So, Ran.” She turned to face him. “Why were you late getting out of the building?”

### Eleven

Ran looked back at her with a smug smile and amused eyes. “I left a small hint for the cops,” he said with a wide grin.

“Oh no,” Koko muttered from the passenger seat. Akari laughed at him.

“Better be a good hint, brother,” Rindou said, uncrossing his legs and shuffling in his seat as the car turned into the garage of the Bonten building. The car slowed to a halt, and the garage door rolled shut behind them. The driver switched off the engine, got out and opened the door for the four of them.

“Thank you,” Akari said, giving him a small smile. Her heels clicked against the concrete floor, echoing with every step. The boys followed closely as she swiped her key card. The elevator lit up and the doors opened. She stepped in carefully so the dress wouldn’t catch on the door. Rindou pressed the button, and the elevator whooshed up to the top floor.

When they arrived, she walked into the main area, where the rest of the Bonten members were sprawled across the couches. Dinner had been left out for the four of them. She hadn’t even made it past the couch before Sanzu tackled her.

“Sweetheart!” He wrapped his arms around her waist and bowled her onto the cushions. She landed softly, with Sanzu sprawled on top, clinging to her like a leech. She stroked his head and wound her other hand around his neck.

“Yes, babe?”

“You look stunning in that dress,” he muttered, burying his face in her chest and pressing small kisses there.

“Thank you,” she said, kissing the top of his head. She felt him smile into her. “Now let go of me, please. I’m starvin’.” He released her waist, and she crawled out from under him. She slipped off her shoes, holding them by the heels, and walked into her room. She swapped the dress for something more comfortable, then sat in her usual seat at the dining table. After washing her hands, she served herself and started eating. Food was food at this point, and she was grateful to whoever had cooked it.

“Thank you for the meal,” she said, standing once she had finished. She put her dishes in the sink and sat back down on the couch beside Sanzu. He immediately wrapped his arms around her shoulders and pulled her close. She snuggled into him and rested her head on his shoulder. He rested his head on hers after kissing her forehead gently.

“Wanna take a bath together later?” she murmured.

He shifted in his seat. “Of course, sweetheart. How could I say no to seeing you naked~” he teased, drawing small circles on her shoulder.

“I changed my mind,” she chuckled, gently trying to push him away.

“No, I was kidding. I’m sorry~” he whined, giving in straight away.

“Hello? We’re all here, you know?” Koko coughed, and Sanzu and Akari looked up to find the other executives staring at them.

Mikey walked in from the elevator and took the separate seat. “So what happened at the auction? Apparently the whole building’s burnt down.”

“Yeah, so about that—” Akari began.

“It was Akari’s fault,” Ran announced, pointing a finger at her.

“Wha—” Sanzu’s gun was already in his hand, aimed at Ran before she could finish. “Babe, put the gun down.” He ignored her.

“Care to explain, Haitani?” he snarled, his hands perfectly steady, the barrel aimed at Ran’s forehead.

“Hope you’re talking to my brother, not me,” Rindou muttered, loud enough for everyone to hear. A few snickers went round the room.

“Can’t believe you’re just gonna abandon me like that, Rin~” Ran whined.

“Care to explain, Ran?” Mikey suggested, pulling a taiyaki out of nowhere.

“Can I do it instead? He’s a little delusional right now,” Akari said, smirking at Ran’s face. Mikey nodded.

“Go ahead.”

“Okay, so, in short, people tried to poison us,” she said. “Rindou came up with a way to escape, since I didn’t like having watchers everywhere. There were bartenders going back and forth, so I knocked one out and took his place. I found the source of the poison, potassium cyanide, and gave it to one of the watchers across from our room. Then I shot another watcher, the one in the room next to us. Ran told me to come back, so I did. I changed back into my dress, and Rin dragged the unconscious bartender into the room next to us, with the dead man. Then Rin shot the fuse box thing, and a fire started. That’s all I know.”

“These three saw you undress?!” Sanzu exclaimed.

“Is that all you got out of that?” she snapped, amused. He gave her a sly smile and turned back to the meeting. “Anyway, just as we were leaving, Ran said something about leaving the cops a hint.”

All the executives, Mikey included, turned to Ran. He was too busy looking at his phone to notice.

“What was the hint, Ran? It better be plausible,” Mochizuki said, trying to see what was on Ran’s screen.

“Turn the TV on. I’ll screen-share it there,” Ran said, and that was all. Mochizuki had no choice but to comply. Ran didn’t need to screen-share anything, because his ‘hint’ was already on the TV.

“Breaking news. We have live images of the burnt hall here in Shibuya, Tokyo. I’m standing in front of the building now.” The reporter turned to a police officer at the scene.

“Sir, what’s the situation inside?”

“I’m too shocked myself. What was done in there was the work of a monster who has abandoned all humanity. I believe it’s the work of Bonten, the criminal organization.”

“How do you know it’s Bonten?” the reporter pressed, pushing the microphone closer to his mouth.

“The blood of some of the victims was smeared across the marble floor. It formed the wellknown Bonten symbol.” He took a breath. “It was horrible.”

The reporter stepped back from the officer. The camera showed the burnt remains of the hall and the bright police tape before the reporter spoke again.

“As you’ve just heard, this building is the aftermath of Bonten and their trail of destruction, their merciless slaughter of innocents. However, what we don’t understand are the numerous handcuffed bodies found at the scene. This could point to several different situations, and it continues to puzzle the police. Kaori, back to you.” Mochizuki switched off the TV and set the remote on the coffee table.

“Nice one, Ran!” Takeomi said, rolling his eyes.

“So much for Mikey’s warning about behaving,” Kakucho added.

“Well, what’s done is done. There’s nothing we can do now,” Akari said with a shrug.

“Finally, someone on my side.” Ran threw his hands in the air.

“Depends on Mikey, though,” she said with a snicker. Ran gulped, and she could see the suspense was killing him.

“Ran.” Mikey stared at him until Ran met his eyes. “Are you okay with not being able to attend the auction anymore?”

“I mean, they’re probably going to move venues and write off the lost merchandise anyway,” Ran said with a shrug, looking away from Mikey.

“Fine, if you think there’s no problem. But if I find we need something, you’ll be the first and only one going. Clear?” Ran nodded slowly, took a cigarette from his pocket and lit it. Rindou, Takeomi and Sanzu held out their hands, and Ran reluctantly handed each of them one. Akari got up and switched on the vent to pull the smoke out of the building. The cool night air swept round the room, and she shivered. She sat back down and felt the couch sink beneath her. Sanzu passed her his cigarette, and she took it.

She put it to her lips and breathed in, feeling the familiar burn in her throat before the smoke settled in her lungs. She tilted her head back and blew the smoke at the ceiling through pursed lips. It spiraled up and faded. She handed the cigarette back to Sanzu, who held it between his fingers before lifting it to his own lips.

“Is the meeting done?” she asked, looking at Mikey. He nodded. She stood, stretched, and started towards her room. “I’m having a bath now, then I’m going to sleep, because I have work tomorrow.”

Sanzu’s body twitched at the word bath. He stubbed out his cigarette and jumped up. “Wait, I’m coming too!” He followed her like a lost puppy.

“Night, everyone!” she called, disappearing into her room after the others had replied.

She stepped into the warm water and splashed it over her body. She sighed heavily and sank lower. Feeling a tap on her shoulder, she sat up and let Sanzu slide into the tub behind her. His long legs wrapped around her on both sides, and his arms gripped her waist, pulling her back against his chest. She went along with it, leaning into him while her hair floated on the surface of the water. He ran his fingers through her two-toned hair, cut to two different lengths. She felt his chest rising slowly and heard his heartbeat faintly behind her. It calmed her.

Sanzu shifted, sinking lower. His toes poked out of the water because his legs were too long for the tub.

“Need a bigger bathtub,” she said with a laugh, looking up at him. He looked down and kissed her forehead softly.

“Mmm, I’m too tall for it,” he murmured against her skin. She turned back to face the wall, and she felt his lips on the back of her neck. He sucked over the same spot again and again. The warm water widened the blood vessels, so hickeys stayed darker and lasted longer. He pulled away, kissed the mark, and moved his lips to the crook of her neck.

“Babe, stop~” she said, laughing and squirming as his fingers teased along her sides. He was doing it on purpose, because he knew she was ticklish.

“I haven’t got to spend time with you lately,” he mumbled into her neck. “I want to go out somewhere with you, but everywhere is dangerous.”

“What are you on about?” she laughed. “We’re the definition of dangerous. We can do whatever we like. So what’s on your list of things to do with me?”

He answered straight away, counting off on his fingers. “Take you on dates. Travel overseas. Get engaged. Get married. Have kids. Grow old. Everything normal people do.”

She linked her fingers with his and sighed. “I’d love to do that too, Sanzu. But even if we did, it would have to be anything but normal. We aren’t normal. We’re criminals. Murderers. Sorry, mass murderers. Starting a family would be hard. There would be more things to watch out for.”

“I’m willing to take the risk,” he said quickly, smiling against her back. She smiled at the wall in front of her.

“I’m glad, because I want to start a family with you too. Not right now, though. Everything’s a bit too messy.” She raked her fingers back through her hair.

“Yeah, I know. One day, in the future.” He climbed out of the tub and gave her the biggest smile. He turned on the shower and washed his long hair with shampoo, then conditioner, then rinsed it out. He washed his body, then handed her the soap so she could wash his back. She did, and then he turned her around and returned the favor with a small laugh before rinsing them both off. He tied his hair into a high bun, catching all its layers, and lowered himself back into the water. She washed her hair, tied it into a high bun too, and slipped back into the tub between his legs.

“This is so calming,” she sighed, leaning back into his chest. She reached up out of the water for his head, which rested on her neck. He leaned into her touch as she ran her fingers through his pink hair, drawing the strands through her fingers.

“The water’s going cold now, sweetheart. Let’s get out before we catch a cold,” he said, taking her hand and pulling it away from his hair. She hummed and stood first, stepping out of the tub. She opened the door and grabbed two towels from the hook on the outside wall. The bathroom was split in two: the washroom with the tub and shower, and the main bathroom with the sink, mirror, toilet and cabinets. She tossed him one of the towels as she stepped through. He wrapped it around his waist, drained the tub, scrubbed it clean with a special sponge as the water ran away, then sprayed the floor down and switched on the fan to clear the damp from the washroom. She wrapped a towel around herself and stood at the mirror, applying moisturizer. Sanzu followed and closed the washroom door behind him. He draped a smaller towel around his neck to soak up the water dripping from his hair. While she was busy with her face, he wrapped another small towel around her hair and started drying it for her.

“Thanks, babe,” she said, watching him in the mirror as she carried on with the cream. When she finished, she walked to the far end of the bathroom, near the door, where her clothes were

folded. She slipped on her underwear, then her trousers, then pulled a shirt over her head. Sanzu stole a few glances while she dressed, and she noticed.

“You’ve seen me naked already. Haven’t you had enough yet?” she asked.

He smirked, rushed over and hugged her, resting his head on top of hers. “You’re too beautiful to ignore, you know?” he said, smiling so widely that the corners of his eyes creased.

“Put some clothes on. You’ll catch a cold.” She grabbed the hairdryer from under the sink, plugged it in and switched it on. Hot air whirred out. A couple of minutes later, she paused, and Sanzu nudged her side and turned his back to her. She smiled at his childish behavior. She tied her hair up out of her face and turned the dryer on again. She aimed it at the top of his head and ran her fingers slowly through his hair, guiding the dryer down with her other hand.

She lay on the bed and stared at the empty ceiling. She tucked her hair under her head and pulled the covers over her body. Sanzu stepped in, and the light from the hallway spilled into the room, along with the loud noise from the living room. Hopefully everyone would go to bed soon. Sanzu slid under the covers and toppled onto her. He wound his arms under her neck and pressed his face into her chest. She felt him settle against her, his legs tangled between hers, until his breathing slowed as he dozed off. She wrapped her arms around his upper back, pulled him closer, rubbed his back slowly, and drifted off to sleep too.

### Twelve

She woke to Sanzu nipping at her neck. “What the hell…” she groaned, turning to face him. He gave her an innocent smile, pecked her nose, then grabbed her hips and pulled her against him.

“Morning, sweetheart~” he sang, grinning. She snuggled into his chest and enjoyed the warmth he gave off.

“You have work today,” he said, loosening his grip.

“Noooo~” she grumbled. “Can’t I skip work for one day…?” She rolled over and sat up, leaning against the wall, while Sanzu propped his head on his hand beside her.

“You’re the owner. You don’t have to go, y’know? Just take a day off,” he suggested, looking up at her. Her eyes widened as it sank in.

“Oh shit, you’re right! I can technically do whatever I like!” Sanzu laughed at her dumb moment. He rolled off the bed and hit the floor with a heavy sigh. She did the same, pulling herself off the mattress and walking to the black suit hanging on the wall. She pulled off her nightclothes, tossed them in the full basket, fastened her bra and slipped on the white dress shirt. She pulled on her suit trousers, tightened the black tie around her neck and slung the jacket over one shoulder. Sanzu got up off the floor and pulled on his shirt, then asked her to tighten his tie. He pushed his arms through his vest, rolled his sleeves halfway up his forearms to show his Bonten tattoo, pulled on his faintly striped indigo trousers, did up the fly, then put on socks and slippers. They left the room together and walked into the living room.

“Morning,” she called to the executives who were awake. It was only the Haitani brothers, Kakucho and Takeomi.

“Don’t you have work today?” Takeomi asked, noticing she was in her normal suit, not her bartending uniform. Kakucho and the Haitani brothers looked her way.

“I’m taking the day off because I don’t feel like going,” she said, walking into the kitchen to start breakfast for everyone. “Are pancakes okay?” They nodded. “You can’t just take a day off because you feel like it,” Kakucho said. “That’s not responsible.”

“Says the one who has the whole weekend off until Mikey calls for you,” she said, rolling her eyes as she whisked the batter in a huge bowl.

“She’s got a point,” Rindou said, looking back down at his phone.

“Why don’t we all have a day off, then?” Ran said, his droopy eyes lighting up. “We’ll take one VIP room at your club, and just—”

“You just wanna get piss drunk,” Sanzu cut him off, heading to the kitchen to light the stove and pour oil into the frying pan. Takeomi, Rindou and Akari laughed, because everyone knew it was true.

“It’s not like you’re not gonna join me,” Ran retorted, earning snorts from the other executives. Sanzu shot him a dirty look.

She ladled batter into the frying pan while Sanzu spread it around. “You know that’s true, though,” she laughed, setting a plate down beside the pan. “I don’t mind. But you have to ask Mikey for permission.”

“Maybe someone else should ask. Especially after what you did yesterday,” Rindou said. She choked on the air she was breathing. Takeomi went red, trying not to laugh.

“Weren’t you the one who started the fire?” Kakucho said quickly, pulling Rindou down with him in the process.

“At least I didn’t pin it on Bonten. If he hadn’t started making post-modernist art with blood, it would’ve just looked like an electrical fault,” Rindou said, pointing at his brother beside him.

Sanzu slid the cooked pancake onto the plate and topped up the oil while she poured another ladle of batter into the pan. Realizing it would take too long, she pulled a second frying pan from the cabinet and set it on the stove. “So we need someone who didn’t go to the auction yesterday to ask Mikey about a day off,” she said, pouring out another batch. She carried the plate to the dining table and set out butter, maple syrup and honey. “Someone eat it while it’s warm.” Takeomi walked straight over and took the first pancake. “Can someone go and wake the others?” Ran and Rindou got off the couch right away and went into the hallway, knocking on Mochizuki’s and Kokonoi’s doors, then carefully knocking on Mikey’s.

Sanzu flipped both pancakes with the spatula, then covered both pans with lids to trap the heat. She pulled out two more plates and set them beside him.

Takeomi slid into the seat next to Kakucho. “Are you okay with taking the day off?” he asked, as she placed a pancake in front of him with a knife and fork.

“Thanks,” Kakucho said, and she headed back into the kitchen. He turned back to Takeomi. “I don’t mind. But it’s up to Mikey.” As if summoned, Mikey, Mochizuki and Koko walked in and sat at the table. She set the latest pancake in front of Mikey with the utensils, then returned to the stove and poured batter into the two pans.

“What’s with the suit, Akari? Don’t you have work today?” Koko asked, rubbing his eyes.

“Taking a day off, because I’m tired,” she said, putting the lid on the pan.

“That’s not right. You shou—”

“I’m not here to get lectured again. Kaku already said it, and I think I got the message,” she snapped, rolling her eyes. Mochizuki laughed loudly at her sharp reply.

“She deserves a break. This week was eventful enough for her,” Mochizuki said, glancing at the brothers who had just come out of the hallway. “How about we all take the day off? We could go to the club later tonight and unwind?” He glanced at Ran with a small smile. Ran gave him a tiny wink, which Mikey missed because he was busy with his pancake.

She carried two pancakes to the table and set them in front of Mochizuki and Koko. “What do you think, Mikey?” she asked. He lifted his head, fork still in his mouth.

“As long as we don’t cause trouble for the club, or for Akari, since she owns it, I have no objection,” he said quickly, then took another bite.

“Ohh, thanks, Mikey!” she said, giving herself a small fist pump. Sanzu handed her two more plates he had already made. She took them to the brothers, then went back for their utensils. She poured the last of the batter into the two pans, and Sanzu shooed her away from the stove. She gave him a small smile and a kiss on the lips, took utensils for the two of them, and sat down in one of the empty seats, listening to the executives chatter. Someone nudged her side. It was Ran.

“He approved~” he whispered happily. He stabbed a small piece of pancake and stuffed it in his mouth. “Thanks for breakfast, it’s nice,” he said, smiling.

“Lucky you, then,” she replied as Sanzu set her plate in front of her. She started cutting the pancake while steam rose from it. “No worries, glad you like it.”

Sanzu sat down beside her, cut into his pancake, and poured a huge pool of maple syrup over it. She looked at him questioningly, but he just shrugged. “It’s better this way.” He cut off a small piece, dunked it in the syrup, stabbed it with his fork and pushed it into her mouth. Taken aback, she had no choice but to chew. She was glad she did, because he was right. It tasted better. She took the maple syrup from him and did the same, and he chuckled beside her.

By 4:30 pm she unlocked the main doors of the FNN from the inside so her staff could come in. The sign still said ‘closed’ until 5 pm. She was still in her suit, with her black hair tied back and

tucked neatly into her collar, hoping nobody would notice. She checked the club, making sure the chairs were tucked in and the barstools were wiped down. Behind her she heard low heels on the wooden floor, which stopped suddenly. Familiar arms wrapped around her waist.

“Yes, babe?” she asked as he rested his chin on top of her head.

“Nothing,” he mumbled, his chin bumping her head with every word. “We’re waiting for the other workers to come in before we open. Go back—” The main door opened, revealing Yuki, one of the most trusted bartenders. Well, the only bartender she really trusted, though she had never told Yuki anything about herself.

Yuki knew vaguely about the VIP rooms, but Akari kept her in the dark about what went on in them.

“Evening, Yuki,” she said, trying to shrug off Sanzu, who wouldn’t budge.

“Evening.” Yuki glanced at Sanzu behind her. “Nice to meet you, Hana’s boyfriend. I’m her colleague, Yuki.” She gave him a small bow. He lifted his head briefly to acknowledge her. Yuki walked past them and started getting ready for the crowd a regular Friday night would bring.

“Oh, Yuki,” she called, turning slowly, since Sanzu was making things difficult.

“Yes?”

“I’m taking the night off, so I’m leaving you in charge. I’ll be in the VIP room if you need me. Call my number.”

“Oh, okay, no problem. What do I do if someone wants a VIP room?”

She glanced at Sanzu. He just shrugged. “Turning them away for the night would be great. If they get aggressive, call me, and I’ll deal with them.”

“Of course.” Yuki went back to the bar and started setting menus out in front of every second stool. “You look fabulous in that suit, by the way. It suits you so well,” she added with a wink.

“Thanks, Yuki.” She smiled back and walked to the front door, flipping the sign to ‘open’ since it was 5 pm. She headed for the VIP room door and looked back at Yuki. “I’ll be coming back and forth for drinks, though. I’ve got important clients already waiting in the rooms, so…”

“Got it!” Yuki said as the first customer walked in. Akari entered the pin code on the padlock and slipped through the door, Sanzu still hanging off her.

“Is this bear hugging really necessary?” she asked, tugging at the arms around her waist.

“Yes. Yes, it is, sweetheart~” he said, kissing the top of her head before pushing open one of the VIP rooms.

“The club’s open to the public now,” she announced, walking to the leather couch and sitting down in the corner. She sighed and rested her head against the back.

“Want one, Akari?” Takeomi asked, offering her a cigarette. She smiled, took it, and borrowed his lighter. “Thanks, Omi.” She handed the lighter back and drew the smoke into her lungs, feeling it burn before she let it out. The TV on the wall started playing music, and the brothers began singing into the karaoke machine on the table. They were surprisingly good. Sanzu watched her smoke from across the room, and Mikey did the same.

“What? Want one too?” she asked, blowing smoke playfully into Sanzu’s face. He blew it right back before he could breathe it in. She crossed her legs, tugged at her tie to loosen it, then pulled out her hair tie and let her black hair fall and sway around her shoulders.

Koko scrolled through his phone, looking bored as usual. Kakucho sat beside him, staring blankly at the brothers belting out their songs. Mochizuki and Takeomi shared a few laughs, each with a cigarette.

When the brothers finished their song, they threw the microphone to the one person not paying attention: Koko. They passed the second mic to Sanzu, who grudgingly took it. He didn’t even get up, just sat there and sang. He wasn’t half bad. He could do with some tweaking here and there, though.

“Can we get some drinks?” Ran asked, looking at her with pleading eyes. She rolled her eyes. He had been waiting for someone to offer, and when no one did, he’d had to ask for himself.

“Sure thing,” she said, standing up, tying her hair back and tucking it into her suit. She stubbed out her cigarette and pulled her mask over her face. “I’ll get everyone whatever. Is that okay?”

They all nodded. She pulled open the door and left them alone. Inside the club, heavy bass music was pumping, and the DJ was hyping the crowd. She lifted the bar flap and stepped behind the counter, where Yuki was serving customers. She started on nine beers for the Bonten executives, pouring them from the taps. While they filled, she grabbed a tray and loaded the glasses onto it as they were finished. Once the nine beers were on the tray, she took some shot glasses and a full bottle of vodka and set them aside. She gave Yuki a small nod, entered the code, and walked back into the VIP room with the drinks.

### Thirteen

The party carried on in the VIP room, with the executives having a blast. Karaoke went on all night, and almost everyone had hoarse voices by the end, Mikey included. Many of them had never seen Mikey laugh, let alone smile, but tonight he did. He laughed hard when Sanzu tripped over Ran’s leg, spilled his drink over Takeomi and Mochizuki, and left the whole room in chaos. Sanzu cleaned up the mess while Mikey and the others laughed at him.

It was a great night, and it ran into the early hours of the morning. She stayed away from the alcohol and only had a few glasses of beer, since she had to work the next evening and didn’t want a hangover. Most of the executives stuck to beer, but Ran, Sanzu, Mochizuki and Takeomi were having a drinking contest with the shots and vodka she had brought in. Koko, Kakucho, Rindou, Mikey and Akari were the sensible ones, looking after the drunk idiots. Sanzu tried to

swallow a pill he had been hiding from her. He was too drunk to think straight, so he pulled it from his pocket, tossed it into the air and tried to catch it in his mouth. She shot off the couch, ran over and caught the pill just in time. He stood there with his eyes closed, waiting for the pill to drop into his mouth, but it never came. He opened one eye and saw her disapproving look, hands on her hips. She watched his Adam’s apple bob as he swallowed thickly.

“If you want to start a family, this is the first thing you should quit,” she said, staring up into his eyes.

“Sorry,” he mumbled, sitting back down, grabbing his shot glass and carrying on with the contest, ignoring the stares of the sober executives.

“Family? You’re not pregnant, are you?” Kakucho asked.

“With his child, nonetheless,” Koko said. “Questionable.” Laughter broke out from Akari, Kakucho and Rindou.

“Yeah, no, I’m not pregnant,” she said, sipping her beer. “It would be nice to start a family someday, though.”

“What about Bonten?” Mikey asked quickly, glancing up from his drink for a moment before lifting it to his lips.

“Yeah, we’ll still be here, probably just not as often.”

“It’ll be difficult, balancing family and wor—” Rindou started, but she cut him off.

“Guys,” she said, looking each of the sober executives in the eye. “Please, it won’t be for a couple of years either way. Relax~” They just raised their eyebrows, but let it pass.

Her phone buzzed in her pocket. She checked the caller ID. It was Yuki. She didn’t bother answering and let it ring out. She grabbed her face mask from the table and fitted it around her ears, careful of her piercings. “Be right back,” she said, slipping out of the VIP room into the main area, where Yuki was trying to calm down an aggressive customer.

“Why’s the VIP room closed, bitch?!” he yelled, trying to climb over the counter to grab Yuki’s collar.

Yuki stepped back out of his reach.

“Sir, please. Come back tomorrow, it’ll be open then. It’s only closed for one night,” she said, trying to reason with him. It did nothing.

“I don’t give a fuck!” He snatched a beer glass from the counter and threw it at her. Akari dashed over, grabbed Yuki’s head and pulled her in against her body, bending her back to take the blow. The glass hit her back and shattered on the floor. Cold beer dripped down the back of her suit. She let Yuki go and gave her an apologetic smile. She turned to the man, who was now splashing more alcohol onto her face. Luckily, the mask soaked up most of it. She wiped her face with her hands and shook the liquid off her fingers. She turned her back on him and

ignored him. Taking off her mask carefully, she wrung the alcohol out of it, then put it back on and turned around. It felt like a damp towel on her face, but that was better than soaked through.

“Are you done now?” she asked the man calmly, meeting his gaze. The crowd had started to back away from him, and whispers spread. The music had died down as the DJ turned the volume down. She gave the DJ a quick nod, a silent thank-you. The man went red, but he didn’t seem to care that everyone was watching.

“Am I done now?” he mocked. “Do I look done?” He grabbed another drink and hurled it at her. She just stepped one pace to the right, and the glass shattered against the wall.

“I don’t remember giving you a VIP pass,” she said, staring at his face. He pulled out a gold VIP pass and held it up for her to see. “What’s your name?” she asked calmly, and asked Yuki for the list of VIP pass holders.

“_____ _______,” he huffed, folding his arms. She flipped through to the second page and found his name. Sure enough, ‘aggressive’ was written in red beside it.

“I see. My apologies, sir. Let me give your card an upgrade.” His eyes lit up at the mention of a free upgrade. She held out her hand, and he handed over the card without hesitation. She pinched the edges of the golden card between her thumb and middle finger and snapped it in two.

“What the fuck do you think you’re doing?”

“What does it look like? I’m revoking your card. Sorry, but you’ve lost your VIP privileges,” she said with a shrug. She knew it would make him angrier. She smiled under her mask, watching him shake with fury. His hands balled into fists. He was about to get violent.

“Hana.” Yuki gripped the hem of her sleeve. “Should we call the cops?”

“Nah, don’t bother. I’ve got this,” she said, and Yuki reluctantly nodded.

The man grabbed the collar of her suit over the counter. “Are you going to pay the dry-cleaning bill for my designer suit?”

“Fuck no! This is what you deserve, bitch!” He swung to slap her, but she caught his wrist before his hand reached her face. She tightened her grip and tried to pull his arm back, but it didn’t budge. He had to let go of her collar and use his other hand to try to break free. She laughed quietly and suddenly let go. He toppled backwards onto the floor. She kept snickering as he fell.

“You motherfucker—” He scrambled to his feet and grabbed her collar again.

“Haven’t you had enough already?” She smirked at him with her eyes. In the corner of her vision, the VIP door swung open. It was Rindou. Hopefully he was still sober.

“What do you think you’re doing to the owner of the beloved FNN club?” Rindou growled, grabbing the man’s forearm where it gripped her collar. The man stared at Rindou, and his eyes went wide when he saw the Bonten tattoo on Rindou’s neck.

“B-B-Bonten!” he screeched, stumbling back into the crowd. With the music off, every eye in the place was on Rindou, who let go of the man’s arm. The secret was out. A Bonten member was standing in front of the public, and phones came out as people tried to film. This was bad. Rindou was one step ahead, though. He pulled out his gun, aimed it at the man’s head and fired a warning shot. Everyone screamed and crouched down in fear.

“Press record and I’ll slaughter everyone right here. Right now.” The room went silent. Slowly the public lowered their phones and put them back in their pockets. “Call the cops, and you’ll have more than one hostage,” he continued, smirking as he looked around the room. He gave her lower back a small tap for reassurance. Rindou walked round the counter to the man, keeping the gun pointed at his forehead.

“Now,” he said, looking down at him, and placed his shoe on the man’s stomach, pressing slowly down. “Nakatani-san here was kind enough to think about the safety of the general public, and she made sure the VIP rooms stayed closed for the night while we were being served.” He pointed his free hand back at her. “Don’t you think it would be better for you if you didn’t run into us in the VIP rooms? I could’ve killed you any time I liked,” Rindou went on, pressing harder. The man began whimpering under his foot. It wasn’t long before something else was going to happen, and Rindou noticed the man’s behavior. So did she.

Taking precautions, she herded the public out of the club. “Everyone, please leave the club. Any drinks you haven’t paid for will be covered. If you’re worried for your safety, please leave now.” Many of the customers left, and so did most of her staff, including the DJ. She knew it wouldn’t be long before police arrived, because the people leaving would be calling for help. Yuki hesitated and gave her a look. “You should go,” she said. Yuki nodded, crouched below the counter and crept towards the main door.

As soon as the door shut behind Yuki, the aggressive man gave a faint whistle, and three men in the crowd pulled guns from their waistbands. She and Rindou already had their guns out. Rindou shot the aggressive man under his foot and rolled out of the line of fire from the other three. She ducked behind the counter. She popped up and shot one of the three men, and he screamed and dropped to the floor. She dropped down again, shuffled along the floor to the edge of the counter, lay flat, peeked round the corner and fired at the second man, while Rindou shot the last one. There was some movement. She looked over the counter and saw that two were dead, and the other two were wounded. Rindou called to her.

“Can I?”

She gave him the all-clear signal. He fired two more shots and finished off the wounded men. They stopped squirming, and the club went quiet.

“What do we do with ’em?” Rindou asked, pointing his pistol at the dead men.

“Leave ’em. The cops will be here soon, so let them deal with it,” she said, quickly retying her hair and adjusting her face mask. She entered the pin code for the VIP door and pushed Rindou back inside. She hurried to the room where the executives were partying. “Oi! I need you all to leave. Now. Cops.” Everyone turned to look at her.

“What’s happening o—” Kakucho started, but she cut him off.

“Rindou will tell you later. Hurry up and go!” They did as they were told and quickly hauled the drunk executives towards the elevator in the storage room. She grabbed the shot glasses and beer bottles and piled them onto a tray. She swept the cigarette ends into one of the shot glasses, lit fresh cigarettes and left them in the ashtray so the smell would stay in the room. By the time the police searched it, it would just be ash anyway. She hurried out of the VIP room back to the bar, where she immediately started washing glasses and drying them with a towel. She smashed a shot glass and a beer glass on purpose to make it look like a scuffle, and it would also speed up the washing.

It was lucky she was the only witness left in the club, since everyone else had gone. They’d have to take her word for whatever had happened there. Sirens grew louder in the distance. She set the clean glasses on the shelf, ducked back behind the bar, crouched into a ball and covered her head. The main doors swung open as police stormed in.

“Police! Anyone in here?”

She took a short, shaky breath. “Here!” she called out.

### Fourteen

Rindou POV

Rindou burst into the room where the others were enjoying themselves. “We have to go. Now!” he yelled. The sober Bonten members rose at once, grabbed a drunk each and dragged them towards the elevator. Mikey swiped his keycard as they reached the storage room at the back, and the shelf rotated to reveal the open elevator. Rindou threw Ran inside, and Sanzu, Takeomi and Mochi followed. Kakucho, Mikey, Koko and Rindou stepped in, trying not to tread on the drunk idiots, and the elevator took them up to the top floor. They dumped the drunks onto the lounge, switched on the TV and waited for the news to show them what was happening to Akari.

“What happened down there, Rindou?” Mikey asked, not taking his eyes off the screen.

“Aggressive customer had his men in the crowd with weapons. Shootout.” Kakucho and Koko looked at him in shock.

“Did you kill them?” Mikey asked quickly.

“Yeah. They’re dead now,” Rindou said. Kakucho sighed, glanced at him, and turned back to the screen.

“Who were they even affiliated with?” Koko asked. Rindou just shrugged.

“Breaking news regarding Bonten,” the TV blared, and their attention snapped to the screen. “The well-known FNN club was attacked earlier this morning, by none other than Bonten.” The screen showed Akari and the so-called ‘Yuki’ being interviewed by a reporter. Rindou had thought Yuki had left the club, but apparently she was still there.

“So, please tell us what happened,” the reporter urged, shoving a microphone at the pair.

“I was serving the Bonten members when I got a call from Yuki here about an aggressive customer. I came out, and the customer attacked me.”

“You said you were serving Bonten members? Does that mean you know who they are?”

“Well, yes, of course. But if I told anyone, they’d find out it was me, and they’d come after me. Then the FNN would be finished. They’ll be watching this broadcast, if anything.” The reporter raised an eyebrow at her and carried on.

“We have reports of one of the Bonten members pointing a gun at the aggressive man. Onlookers described him as ‘a tall man with a purple-blue mullet wearing a turquoise suit.’ Is that accurate?”

Yuki answered this time. “Yes, but he saved Hana from that man.”

“Turns out the aggressive customer had armed men hiding in the crowd. It’s some shady underground business the FNN was unlucky enough to get tangled up in. But he did save me from being slaughtered by them, so I’m grateful to him,” Akari said, cutting across Yuki.

“Bonten are well known for their illegal activities. Are you saying they’re not as bad as they seem?”

“I said I’m grateful to him. What more do you want me to say? That I wish I’d died?” Akari said sharply, annoyed. Koko and Kakucho laughed quietly, amused by her. “They’re human too. They need a break. No one would serve Bonten in their club, and I welcomed them. Why? Because they’re human. They deserve the same service as anyone else. I’m sure other businesses have served serial killers without knowing it. What difference does it make, serving Bonten?” She finished, and the reporter stood there stunned.

“That’ll be all from me. Back to you, Kaori,” the reporter said, and the broadcast switched back to the studio.

“Well, that was eventful,” Koko said, switching the TV off.

“We just have to hope Akari comes back to us. Alive,” Mikey said, staring at the floor. Rindou walked over and looked out at the concrete, red and blue police lights flashing across it. He could just make out the outlines of body bags being loaded into ambulances.

Rindou woke the next morning to someone pounding on his door. He groaned, stumbled out of bed and yanked it open, rubbing his eyes.

“What.”

“Check this out,” Koko said, holding out his phone. Rindou took it. Countless newspaper articles about last night’s shootout at the FNN had gone up, and fake rumors from tabloids were spreading. “Yikes,” he said, handing the phone back. “Has she come back yet?” He yawned, covering his mouth with his palm, brushed his hair back with his fingers, and followed Koko to the dining table.

“Nothing. We haven’t heard a word from her since,” Koko said, sitting down and glancing across the table at Sanzu, who was asleep with his head on the wood, still out cold from last night and oblivious to what was going on with his girlfriend.

“Should we be looking for her?”

“No need,” Mikey said, glancing at Rindou. “She’ll be fine. He’s very questionable, though.” He pointed his thumb at Sanzu’s sleeping figure.

“Finally someone says something about him,” Koko said, and slapped Sanzu awake.

Akari POV

After the news interview, Akari was taken to the police station, where she and Yuki were questioned separately. The questions kept coming all night, and by morning they finally let her go. The police said they would clean up the club after the “traumatic experience” of four men dying there. She thanked them for their service and walked out of the station with Yuki, who had been released at the same time.

“What are you going to do now?” Yuki asked, sighing loudly as they walked away. Dawn was already breaking.

“I want to sleep,” Akari said with a yawn, tears gathering at the corners of her eyes.

“What’s going to happen to the FNN?” Yuki asked, looking back at her.

“Take a couple of weeks off. The police said they’re going to clean up the club and search the VIP rooms.”

“Ahh, I see,” Yuki said quietly. She stopped at an intersection. “I live this way, so I’ll head home now.” She bowed her head slightly and walked away.

“Yuki!” Akari called after her. Yuki turned and looked back. “If you ever need someone to talk to, don’t hesitate to call me, okay?” Yuki nodded and hurried off down the road. Akari hoped she would be all right. She turned back towards the police station and headed for the FNN.

When she reached the club, police tape was strung across the entrance, with reporters and TV crews crowding the pavement. Ignoring the tape, she stepped over it and went inside. Officers were chatting among themselves, photographing the club and the bloodied floor, and the white tape outlining four bodies.

“Ma’am, you can’t be in here,” an officer said, trying to escort her out.

“I was going to show you the VIP room where the Bonten men were this morning,” she said calmly, turning and heading for the door.

“Oh, then please show us,” the officer said, apologizing. She turned back and walked to the VIP room. She entered the pin code and held the door open for the officers to file through. Once they were inside, she showed them the room where the Bonten members had been. She had cleaned away all the evidence, so there was nothing left except cigarette ends, crumpled seats and the karaoke machine, still playing music at full volume.

“Smells heavy of cigarettes,” the lead officer said, wrinkling his nose.

“Heavy smokers, yup, that’s them,” she sighed.

“Didn’t you serve them drinks?”

“I did.”

“Where are the glasses?”

“I washed them to get rid of the evidence.”

“You realize you’re obstructing police work by doing that. It’s against the law,” he said, giving her a piercing look. She wasn’t scared of weak stares.

“Well, then, I’ll just die, and you’ll have no one to interview about this case,” she said with a shrug, looking straight back at him. He was thrown by her answer and her stare, and she noticed him take a small step back without realizing it.

“How much can you tell us about the Bonten members?” he asked instead, changing course.

“Not much,” she said. “Since you’ve had eyewitness reports of one of the members, the least I can say is that the description is right. He has a Bonten tattoo on his neck.” She touched her own neck to show where it was.

“I see. Thank you,” he said, snapping his fingers. The officers in the room began circling it and taking photos of random objects. They bagged the ashtray and the ash in zip-lock bags. Idiots. She smiled to herself behind her mask. The lead officer asked another question.

“Could I ask you to take off your mask? And could I see some ID?”

She handed him the ID card from her wallet, then hooked her fingers behind her ears and pulled off the mask. He took the card, stared at the picture with wide eyes, then looked back at her. “Name?”

“Nakatani Hana.”

“Birthday?”

“March 20th, 1990,” she replied, giving him the fake birth date printed on the card.

“Thank you,” he said, handing the card back. She took it.

“Can I put my mask back on?”

“Ah, yes.” He hesitated. “May I ask what happened?”

She pulled the mask back over her face. “Family abuse,” she said flatly, without a hint of emotion, and looked away.

“I’m sorry to hear that,” he said quickly. “Anyway, the investigation should wrap up later this evening. The cleaning will happen tomorrow, so you’re free to reopen by Monday.”

“Great. But we don’t open on weekdays, so next Friday evening, then,” she said, smiling with her eyes.

“Keep in mind that undercover officers may be keeping an eye on the place over the next couple of weeks,” he warned, which was rather stupid of him to say.

“Thank you for letting me know,” she replied in a sickly-sweet tone.

“If you need counseling for what you witnessed, don’t hesitate to come to the station for some help.”

“Of course.” He started walking back out into the main area. “We’re putting the club on hold until Monday, so you’re free to go home now.”

“Thank you for your hard work!” she said, bowing to the officer before leaving the club. She walked along the morning streets as the crowds began to gather. People in suits and business clothes passed by, and she realized she was still wearing her suit, stained with alcohol and getting stares. How embarrassing. She went into the nearest clothing shop, bought some ordinary clothes, put the suit in a plastic bag and walked back out. She had changed into sweatpants and a jumper, with a cap on and her bleached hair tucked under it. Her phone was in her pocket. As much as she wanted to call the Bonten office, that was her work phone. She had kept her Bonten phone and her work phone strictly separate, because being traced would only add to her worries.

She walked into a pachinko parlor and felt the stares and whispers of the people inside. She strode up to the front desk and leaned over the counter.

“Can I borrow your phone?”

The woman behind the counter looked up at her, stared, and then snapped out of her daze. “Uh, sure. It’s down the hall, on the wall to the left.” Akari nodded and followed the directions to the wall phone. She felt a little uneasy. This wasn’t somewhere she would normally go alone, especially with old pervy men around. She could handle them, of course, but the worst could still happen. She reached the phone at the end of the hallway, picked it up, and dialed the Bonten building.

It rang for a while before a familiar voice answered.

“Who’s this?” Takeomi groaned. He had got wasted last night, so it was a shock for him to be answering the phone so early. “Oi. If this is a prank—”

“Omi, it’s me,” she said calmly. The line went silent for a moment, and then incoherent yelling came from the other end. “Omi?”

After a couple of seconds, things calmed down. “Good to hear from you, Akari. So what do you—” He cut off abruptly, as someone behind her held down the button to end the call.

### Fifteen

She turned around quickly and saw a man in his mid-thirties. She reached for the gun tucked at the small of her back and found nothing. She had given it to Rindou earlier that morning. She slid her hand away from her back and forced herself to calm down before looking at him properly.

“How can I help you?” she asked, looking up at him from under her cap.

“You got money?”

“What?”

“I asked if you’ve got money.” He was probably losing at gambling. Gambling wasn’t something she did often, though she sometimes went along with the brothers whenever they went, always to places far more extravagant than this one. Ran spent a lot and got an earful from Koko afterwards. Rindou spent a fair amount too, but he knew his limits. Once he realized he was on a losing streak, he stopped, even if the other players jeered at him. And his brother.

“Here.” Wanting him gone quickly, she pulled a couple of notes from her wallet and shooed him off. His eyes lit up, and he hurried away. She had to tell the Bonten boys where she was before the man came back for more. She dialed the same number, and Takeomi picked up again.

“Yes?”

“Omi, can you pick me up, please?”

“I can arrange a car—” A sudden scuffle sounded on the other end, and a new voice came through the phone.

“Akari! Are you okay?” It was Rindou, sounding rushed.

“Yes, I’m okay. I’ll explain everything when I get back, so can someone pick me up?”

“Yeah, I’ll come. Where are you?”

“Pachinko parlor near the mall,” she said, turning to check the hallway. No one.

“Be there in five,” Rindou said, and hung up. Relieved that someone was coming, she ended the call, wiped the number pad and phone clean with the hem of her long T-shirt, and walked down

the hall. She passed the rows of poker machines and other games, then waited outside the store, crouched against the wall. Footsteps sounded to her left, followed by a tap on the shoulder.

“You got more money?” It was the same man.

“Did you use it all already?” she asked, looking up at him. He nodded. She sighed. “I gave you everything I had, sorry, mate.”

“Oh, come on. You’ve got at least a thousand yen to spare?” he begged, gripping her shoulder hard.

“I said I don’t! Geez, you’re so persistent!” She stood, grabbed his arm off her shoulder, twisted it and pinned it behind his back. He whined and babbled in pain, but she kept his arm locked. She marched him back inside to a poker machine near the front entrance, out of the public’s view, knocked him out and laid him across the machine. Then she walked back out. Thankfully Rindou’s car was parked right out front. He tapped the horn as soon as he saw her. She checked both ways before crossing, and when she knocked on the tinted window he unlocked the door, and she slid into the passenger seat.

“You alright?” She nodded, leaned back and buckled her seatbelt.

“Let’s go home. I want to sleep.” He hummed, turned the key, and the engine revved. He flicked on the indicator, swerved onto the road and headed for the Bonten building.

At the building he reversed into a space in the garage, switched off the engine and pulled out the key. He tapped her shoulder lightly, snapping her out of her daze.

“Akari, we’re here,” he said, swinging his door open and getting out, closing it softly. She groaned, unclipped her belt, climbed out and shut the door. Rindou locked the car with the key and followed her to the elevator. She swiped her key card on the panel and waited for the lift to reach the ground floor. The doors chimed open, and she stepped in and turned to face them.

“Ugh, I’m so tired.” She pulled off her cap, and her bleached hair slid back into its usual place. She smoothed it down, raking her fingers through it, then shook her head lightly.

“Mikey wants to hear your side of the story. You can sleep after that,” Rindou said, watching her closely. “You should shower first. You smell like alcohol.” He pinched his nose, his voice jumping an octave, and she snickered.

“Mmm, yeah, okay,” she said as the doors opened. The executives were waiting around the couch in the main area, except Takeomi, who she assumed was in his room taking calls for Bonten. Mikey was calmly munching on a taiyaki, staring at the floor. Koko was on his phone, reading articles by the look of it. Kakucho was lying back with a book over his face. Mochi and Ran were whispering to each other. Sanzu was dead to the world on the dining table, arms folded under his head.

“Well, welcome back to me, I guess,” she announced, shrugging and tapping the book balanced on Kakucho’s head. It toppled onto his lap, and he snorted.

“Oh, Akari. Good to see you back safe,” Kakucho muttered, tilting his head against the couch to look up at her. The others glanced over as she walked to the empty spot on the couch and sat down. Rindou followed and dropped into the seat beside his brother.

“Akari,” Mikey began, swallowing the last of his taiyaki before taking another bite. “What happened down there?”

She explained everything from start to finish. It took a while, and she yawned several times along the way. “The police said they’ll send undercover officers from time to time, so it’s best to stay away from the club during business hours, I guess.” She covered her face with her hands, then slid them back down into her lap.

“Hmm, yeah, okay. Good thing you came back to us,” Mikey said. He stood, walked over, patted her head, and slipped off towards the corridor and his room. She watched his back until he opened his door and disappeared.

“Is he alright?” she asked, turning back to the others.

“Who?” Mochi asked, glancing at Sanzu’s sleeping form behind her, then at Mikey’s door.

“Mikey,” she said, crossing her legs.

“He was probably the most worried out of all of us,” Koko said, glancing up at her briefly before looking back down.

“Wow, that’s so nice,” she said, rolling her eyes. “Don’t you care about me?”

“We were worried too.” Ran started, then pointed at Sanzu. “Can’t say the same about your ‘soon-to-be husband.’ He’s probably still unaware of what happened to you.” She turned to look at his sleeping form. “What’s up with him?”

“No one knows. He was wasted with us last night. Probably still hungover?” Mochi offered.

She stood and walked to the dining table where Sanzu was passed out. She poked his sides, and he shot upright at once, making her jump.

“Whoa, what the fuck!” she yelped, stepping back so fast she nearly lost her balance. “I thought you were dead for a minute!”

“How mean~” he whined, getting up and waddling over with his arms open. She stood still and let him wrap his arms around her waist and pull her in. “Good to see you back,” he whispered into her neck. She put her hands on his waist and pinched his sides hard. He twitched and tried to wriggle free, but she held him there.

“I can’t believe you slept through everything~,” she teased, letting go of his sides only to pinch him again. “Don’t you care about me~” she pouted, then released her grip. She left him whimpering in pain and strutted into her room. She grabbed the laundry basket, carried it to

the laundry room and threw it in the machine, along with the alcohol-soaked suit. She brought the empty basket back to her room, took out a fresh set of clothes and went to the bathroom to shower off the smell of alcohol.

When she came out, dressed comfortably with her hair dry, she put the clothes she had bought into the empty basket, shut the door quietly and headed for the main room. She could barely keep her eyes open. She was practically asleep on her feet.

“I’m leaving you in charge of dinner and cleaning. Don’t disturb me until seven,” she said, heading for the elevator.

“Where are you going?” Mochi asked, tilting his head.

“My office downstairs. I’m sleeping there until then, so call me at seven.” She stepped into the elevator and pressed the button for her floor, only about four floors below the living quarters. The doors opened, and she walked down the short corridor, turned left and went into the first door. The late morning light blinded her as she entered. She crossed to the window and pulled the blinds shut. Behind her desk, she yanked open the bottom drawer and pressed the ‘Do Not Disturb’ button. It came in handy more often than she liked. It blocked anyone from reaching the floor by lift. The emergency stairs still gave access, but most of the executives were far too lazy to bother with the stairs. She closed the drawer, walked to the leather couch opposite her desk, lay down and rested her head on the armrest. She tossed her hair over the arm, stretched a couple of times, covered her eyes with her forearms and drifted off.

She woke to her phone ringing. She groped around the floor for it, found it, and answered.

“Yeah?” she groaned, blinking before pushing herself up. She leaned her head back and stared at the crown moulding on the ceiling.

“Dinner’s ready,” Koko’s voice said on the other end, followed by screeching and arguing.

“What on earth is going on over there? Sounds like that Christmas when you and Sanzu were arguing,” she said sleepily, and heard Koko laugh.

“Rindou, Ran and Sanzu are fighting. Like always. Anyway, come on up and tame your wild dog, please,” Koko said, and hung up. She brushed her hair back from her face, pushed herself off the couch and went back to her desk. She pulled the drawer open and pressed the button again, turning off the lock. She opened the laptop on the desk and checked her emails. Nothing. She closed it, left the room, walked back down the corridor and took the lift up.

Dinner was chaotic. Sanzu, Rindou and Ran kept glaring at each other every couple of seconds. Someone’s knee kept knocking the table, and the drinks kept spilling. Eventually the rest of the executives, Akari included, had had enough, and they sent all three to separate corners of the room with their plates. Shaking her head at them, she started talking with the more grown-up members. Their version of adult conversation mostly involved teasing the three sulking in the corners.

After dinner, she took the emergency stairs up to the roof, where the helipad was, and sat on the edge with her legs dangling over. The cool night breeze hummed through her hair, which danced in time with it. The sun had already set, and what little light it had left barely touched her eyes. The Tokyo skyline was slowly lighting up, the tall buildings switching on their lights, and the cars below turned on their headlights.

The sound of heels clicking on concrete made her turn her head.

“Careful, sweetheart. Don’t want you dying on me now,” Sanzu said, sitting down beside her and laying his sword across his lap.

“You going somewhere tonight?”

“Yeah. Mission with the brothers, Takeomi and Mochizuki.” He spoke softly, staring off into the distance. “It’ll be late when we get back, so don’t wait up for me.”

She hummed and leaned into him. He welcomed her, slung his arm around her shoulders, pulled her closer and rested his head on hers. “I’ll hold down the fort, then,” she said with a soft smile. “Make sure you come back safe, okay?”

“Of course I will, sweetheart. Who do you think I am? I’m not Bonten’s number two for nothing,” he boasted, and they both chuckled. He let go of her shoulder, stood up, and she watched his back as he walked towards the door.

“See you later, babe. Love you~” she called. He stopped, turned, grinned widely, then opened the door and was gone. She turned back to the skyline and enjoyed the small moment alone, staring at the glittering lights and neon signs lighting up the night. She tilted her head back to look for stars and found none, hidden behind dark rain clouds. A drop of rain landed on her nose, rolled down her cheek to her jaw and fell onto the concrete. Soon the clouds gave in, and thousands of raindrops came down, drowning out the city lights. She backed away from the edge, stood, and headed for the door, down the emergency stairs and into the living quarters.

“It’s raining outside now,” she said, walking to the couch and sitting down.

“Yeah, doesn’t look good right now,” Kakucho said, gazing out of the window for a long while.

The rain pattered against the glass. She watched the droplets on the window race each other down the pane, then merge with another drop higher up.

A couple of hours later, the rain had grown harsher and began to lash at her bedroom window. She lay on her cold, empty bed, tossing and turning and wrapping the sheets around herself again and again. Sighing in annoyance, she shut her eyes and let the rain drum against the glass. A sudden chill ran up her spine, and as if she had summoned it, her phone rang.

### Sixteen

Sanzu POV

Sanzu walked into the warehouse where the meeting with the other group was to take place, and he knew at once that something was wrong. There were too few people for a deal like this. He looked back and forth, again and again, and the empty space made his skin crawl. He gripped the hilt of his sword, bracing himself for whatever came next.

“Why are you so tense?” Mochizuki asked, walking beside him as if nothing was wrong.

“Something doesn’t feel right,” Sanzu said, keeping his eyes open.

“Aww, is little Sanzu scared~?” Ran teased, slinging an arm round his shoulders.

“Fuck off!” Sanzu shoved him away and twisted out of his grip. Sudden footsteps sounded in the distance, and he pulled out his gun with one hand, aimed it towards the sound, and tightened his other hand on his sword.

“Lower your weapon,” a man’s voice called, but Sanzu kept his gun up and aimed it at the man’s head. He felt a nudge at his side. Takeomi nudged him again and gave him a look. Sanzu had no choice. He lowered the gun and slid it back into his pocket.

“Do you have what we asked for?” Takeomi asked, his patience thin.

“Well, yes, of course,” the man said, turning on his heel and walking away from them. “Follow me, and I’ll give it to you. I hope you’ve got what we asked for.”

“Of course,” Rindou said, holding up the black locked suitcase. They followed the man deeper into the warehouse. Small, muffled women’s screams drifted through the air, along with the rattle of chains. The man stopped suddenly and took something from his pocket. There was a faint beep, and then loud metallic clanging came from above.

“Oi! Move!” Sanzu moved on instinct and shoved the other four executives out of the way. He hit the floor hard, and when he lifted his head, a huge metal box had come down around him, locking him in. He couldn’t see what was happening outside. He pulled out his gun and fired at the middle of one of the metal panels, but it did nothing.

“Sanzu! Are you good?” Mochizuki yelled from outside, and gunshots rang out beyond the walls. They’d been led in here. A trap. His gut had been right.

“Yeah, I’m fine! We don’t need more than one executive trapped, so hurry up and go!” Sanzu shouted back. Then he heard a hiss of gas. He looked up and saw small holes in the ceiling of the box, pumping gas in. This was bad. He emptied the spare bullets from the pocket inside his jacket, reloaded and fired at the spot where the gas was coming in. Useless. He drew his sword and tried to jam it between the floor and the metal walls, but that was useless too. He lowered himself to the floor and tried to buy as much time as he could, until he either died or fell asleep. He pulled out his phone and tried to message Akari, but something in the box was blocking the signal. He typed the message anyway and hit send, so it would go through when the box was opened. There was no way out. Soon the odorless gas was in his lungs, and after a few breaths, he lost consciousness.

When he woke, he was out of the box and in shackles. His wrists were cuffed and hung above his head from a chain attached to the ceiling. Another chain was wrapped tightly around his neck and joined to the wall. He was kneeling on the floor, but at least his legs were free, though there was not much he could do. The room was dimly lit, and it took a while for his eyes to adjust. In front of him, on a chair, sat the man behind it all, with a half-dressed woman on his lap. She was crying silently, and he held her by the hip as if she were a piece of property.

“Enjoying the show?” he asked, sounding amused. He immediately jolted his hips up suddenly, causing the whore to squeal in delight, as she quivered before slumping onto his shoulder. She fainted. He chuckled as he shoved the whore off his lap, and she hit the cold floor and lay still, unconscious. He chuckled, buckling his pants up and stepped towards Sanzu, keeping a safe distance. “You’ve been out for a while now,” he whispered into Sanzu’s ear, running a finger down the arm that hung from the ceiling.

“Fuck off,” Sanzu spat, lunging forward, but the chains yanked him back. The man moved his finger to Sanzu’s chin, lifted it, and then walked back to his seat.

“You won’t be saying that for long.” The man smirked. “I called your bitch. She’ll be here soon. Maybe she’ll be kind enough to fold under me, like this one here,” he said, pointing at the woman on the floor. Sanzu’s blood surged, and anger filled him. The man noticed and kept pushing. “I can’t wait. Imagine her begging for mercy while you watch. Oooh, gives me shivers.” He faked a shiver, rubbed his arms and grinned.

“She’s not what you think. Don’t say I didn’t warn you,” Sanzu said, pressing his back against the wall and using it to haul himself to his feet.

“What’s she gonna do when your—” The man pulled a gun from his back pocket and aimed it at Sanzu. The shot echoed through the dark room.

Akari POV

The unknown caller made her shiver even more. Hesitantly, she answered, and a robotic voice spoke.

“You must be Akari, I assume.”

It was a voice changer, but she knew this was no prank. Something was wrong, and she could feel it. “Who’s this?” she demanded, sitting up on the bed, swinging her legs over the side and slipping on her slippers.

“No one you need to concern yourself with,” the voice said. “Now, about your boyfriend—” There was shuffling and the click of shoes on a hard floor, then the clink of metal. Chains. “Your poor boyfriend is bleeding. I suggest you come and save him before it’s too late,” the man whispered, sending a shiver down her spine.

Then a raspy voice came through the line. “Akari. Don’t e—”

“Uh oh, time’s up,” the robotic voice cut in. “I’ll send you the address, so make sure you come alone. You’d better hurry, or he’ll bleed out.” The line went dead. She stormed out of her bedroom, slammed the door behind her and strode to the couch. Nobody was sitting there. She glanced at the clock: 11:30 pm. The others were probably asleep. Her phone buzzed in her hand. The same number had sent the address. She looked it up quickly and set it up on the map. She was about to rush back to her room to change when the lift doors opened, and the Haitani brothers, Takeomi and Mochizuki came out.

“Akari—”

“If it’s about Sanzu, I know,” she cut Ran off. She left the room, changed into black clothes, grabbed her combat boots, and went back into the living room.

“How—”

“The guy who’s got him sent me the address. I’m going alone. Don’t come, or they’ll kill him.” She kept getting ready. The commotion woke Kakucho, Koko and Mikey, who came into the room with sleepy faces. “Explain it to Mikey. I’m going,” she said, turning towards the lift. A large hand closed around her wrist. She looked round. Rindou.

“Calm down, and think it through first. Make a plan. Then go.” He pulled her away from the lift and forced her down onto the couch.

She huffed in annoyance but sat. “So what’s happening?” Mikey asked, perched on the armrest, nearly falling asleep.

“Sanzu got captured,” Rindou said, putting down the suitcase. It had a bullet hole through it.

“He’s bleeding out. I need to hurry,” she said.

“How do you know this, Akari? You weren’t there,” Kakucho asked, covering a yawn.

“The man holding him called. He said Sanzu’s bleeding and that I should come alone to save him.”

“Yeah, that’s not happening,” Mikey said coldly.

“No! I’m not letting him die on me now. Mikey! I’m leaving Bonten if you’re saying we’re abandoning—”

“Akari!” Mikey raised his voice, and she snapped her mouth shut instantly. It was the first time Mikey had ever raised his voice at her, and honestly, she was a little scared. “Let me finish. I was going to say we aren’t letting you go alone.” He sighed and shook his head. “Ran, Rindou. Go with her. I need both of them back alive. Got it?” The brothers nodded. “Koko, decline their offers now. Kakucho, follow their car with Mochi. Takeomi, answer any calls. Clear?”

“Yes!” they all answered together. Everyone scattered to their posts. She got into the lift with the brothers and stopped at the weapons floor. She grabbed a second handgun and another sword, strapped the sword to her back, and waited for Rindou to follow her back in.

“Okay, let’s go,” she said as the doors opened again and took them down to the garage.

The car ride to the address was awkward, since the only conversation was about how to get Sanzu out. She spent most of the drive braiding her hair, because there was nothing else to do. The car slowed and stopped.

“Take this, and tell us if anything happens,” Rindou said, handing her an earpiece and a mic. She took them from his palm, pushed the earpiece into her ear, ran the cord under her shirt and pinned it to the inside.

“Okay, I’m going in.” She took the sword from the seat, opened the door, got out and shut it softly. She crept towards the main gate of the building.

The building was an abandoned mansion, with overgrown vines creeping up over the brick wall. She pushed the gate, and it opened just wide enough for her to squeeze through. The front garden was long and overgrown, which gave her cover. She crept through the grass and reached the steps to the main entrance. She tiptoed up them, tightened the sash connecting her sword, and pulled the gun from her waistband. She tapped the earpiece and whispered, pressed against the wall, away from the windows.

“I’m about to go into the house.”

Static crackled in her ear, and then a reply came. “Alright, be careful,” Rindou said, and the line went silent.

She reached for the doorknob, turned it slowly and aimed her gun into the gap. She heard nothing, so she kept the gun raised and flung the door wide open. Nobody was there. But yellow tape was stuck to the carpet in the shape of an arrow. She assumed she was meant to follow the arrows, and she watched every step. As she stepped onto the arrow, a loud whoosh came from behind her. She turned, and a log swung on a rope straight at her. She hadn’t expected traps set up with such flair, especially on such short notice. She waited for the log to get close, then ran in the same direction it was traveling. She climbed a few flights of stairs and jumped as the log swept under her feet. She landed on it safely and rode it as it swung from side to side. Using the momentum, she hopped off and landed on the fourth arrow at the top of the staircase. The paintings on the walls slid aside, revealing darts ready to fire. She dropped and rolled against the wall, where they couldn’t reach her.

She looked down the hallway where the arrows continued and crawled along the wall, following them. After dodging the next few traps, she came to a staircase in the kitchen, which she guessed led down to the cellar.

“If you need to come in and help, follow the arrows, but watch for traps,” she whispered into the earpiece.

“Got it,” came the immediate reply.

She carefully lifted the hatch, closed it behind her, and stood on the rung of the ladder, waiting for her eyes to adjust to the dark. She climbed down slowly. Laughter and the rattle of chains

echoed from somewhere ahead. She crept towards the sound, peeked round the corner, and her eyes widened in horror and disgust.

Sanzu hung by his arms from the ceiling, his neck fastened to the wall by a single metal choker. Blood was seeping from his thigh and trickling slowly from the wound. A woman lay on the floor, alive but badly beaten, in torn clothing. A man stood over Sanzu with knives in his hands. Akari watched him step back, take aim and throw one. The knife flew past Sanzu’s cheek and clattered on the floor. He threw a second straight after, and it pierced Sanzu’s arm. Sanzu flinched, then raised his head and glared at the man.

The man laughed and walked over to him. “Man, what fun!” He gripped the knife’s handle sticking out of Sanzu’s arm and yanked it free. Sanzu sucked in a sharp breath. “But damn, your girl’s sure taking her time,” the man said, turning his back on Sanzu and walking back towards a line drawn on the ground. Akari tightened her grip on the gun and aimed at the chain hanging from the ceiling that held Sanzu’s arms.

She took a quick breath to steady her hands and pulled the trigger. The chain rattled, and the man turned his head sharply towards Sanzu. Sanzu’s arms dropped heavily from the ceiling and hung at his lap. He smirked into the darkness, knowing she was somewhere close.

“Spoke too soon, I think,” Sanzu said, as the man in front of him shook with rage. Sanzu was still attached to the wall by the metal choker. The man rushed at him, knife gripped tightly. Akari stepped out of hiding, drew her sword and blocked the man’s stabbing motion.

“So you’ve finally arrived,” he snarled, baring his teeth. “Well, now that you’re here, I’m only here for two things.”

“Two?”
