“It’s a secret~” She winked at him, pushed his knife back and kicked him in the stomach. He skidded across the floor towards the wall.

### Seventeen

She glanced at Sanzu and noticed the color draining from his face. He gave her a small smile, trying to reassure her. She turned back to the man, who was charging at her again. She couldn’t move from where she stood without leaving Sanzu open to attack, and with Sanzu unarmed, that would be a problem. She stopped the man’s slash with the tip of her sword and slid it upward to take the pressure off. She swung at him, but he jumped back in time. He moved deeper into the darkness, and his outline faded. Keeping her eyes on him, she reached into her waistband, pulled out the gun and dropped it discreetly into Sanzu’s lap. He noticed it fall and caught it, keeping still and hiding it under his palms. She advanced on the man this time, catching him off guard, because she was supposed to be protecting Sanzu.

“Don’t you care about him?” the man jeered, nodding towards Sanzu. She kept a blank face and said nothing. He flicked one of his spare knives from his pocket, and it grazed her cheek. She

thrust her sword forward, and it hit something. Blood dripped to the floor, but she knew it wasn’t the man’s. Looking at the tip of her sword, she saw that he was holding up the unconscious woman as a human shield.

“That’s low,” she spat, clenching her teeth. She pulled the sword out of the woman’s body. The woman groaned as the blade came free. Akari had stabbed her in the abdomen, and she knew there was nothing ahead of her but death.

“Does it look like I care?” the man said. Irritation built in her chest. She had to finish this quickly. The man lunged at her, knives between his fingers like claws, and threw them one by one. Dodging them in the low light was hard. She had to rely on his erratic movements and the glint of the blades. She closed in and slashed at his upper body. The blade connected this time, but the cut was too shallow. She swung again, using the opening when he was off balance. His leg lashed out, too fast, and struck her in the stomach. She coughed as the air was knocked out of her, but she kept moving. With one hand she grabbed both his wrists, pinned them behind his back, and held the sword at his throat.

“Looks like this is it for you,” she sneered, drawing the edge of the blade slowly across his neck. He squirmed in her grip and coughed up blood.

“I wasn’t aiming for you,” he smirked. Then blood gushed from his neck and sprayed in every direction. He slumped to the floor, blood pouring from the open wound.

What?

She glanced quickly at Sanzu, who now had two more knives in him, one in his shoulder and one in his abdomen. This was bad. She rushed to his side.

“Oi! Sanzu! You alright?!” she asked, panicking. He was pale, even paler than usual. “I’ll get you out of here, okay?” She picked up one of the knives from the floor, wedged it between the wall and the choker, and snapped the choker off his neck. He was free. She hoisted him over her shoulders, his arms and legs dangling. He was heavy and tall, and it was a real struggle. She climbed the ladder one rung at a time, careful not to tip over, since a fall now would be disastrous. She lifted the hatch and came up out of the cellar into the light, which made her pupils contract painfully. She staggered back the way she had come, making sure not to step on any arrows and set off more traps. She tapped the earpiece and spoke, her voice unsteady.

“Rin, I’ve found him, but he needs to go to hospital.”

“Akari, you know how hard that is for us—”

“I know. I’ll go with him and sort it out. He’s going to die at this rate.”

“What’s wrong with him?” he asked, and she could faintly hear a car engine revving.

“Bullet wound to the thigh, three stab wounds: one in the shoulder, one in the upper arm and one in the abdomen,” she said, walking down the grand staircase with blood running down her back from Sanzu’s wounds.

“Yikes, that’s definitely no good. Ran’s updating Mikey on the situation now.”

“I’ve just come out of the main door, so I’ll be at the car in about two minutes,” she said, stumbling across the grass towards the car at the front. She slipped past the squeaky gate, and she watched Rindou open the back door for her. She eased Sanzu onto the seat, which had been lined with plastic to protect the upholstery from blood, then got in and shut the door. The car sped off towards the hospital, taking back roads to avoid traffic. Sanzu’s breathing was getting sharp and shallow, and beads of sweat were forming on his forehead. She was really worried.

“How long?” she asked frantically.

“Not long,” Ran said, speeding through the streets without taking his eyes off the road. She looked at Sanzu and wiped the sweat from his forehead gently. His eyes opened a little, and he gave her a faint smile. He gripped her hand, lacing his fingers through hers, then closed his eyes again.

“I’ll hold on just fine,” he huffed, coughing up blood, which she wiped away with her sleeve. Ran stopped the car and turned off the engine.

“Ran and I will go and grab a nurse. Stay here till then,” Rindou said, getting out with his brother and leaving her alone with Sanzu.

The car was silent. She rubbed her thumb over the top of his hand, still linked with hers. A knock came at the window, and Ran stood there with a stretcher. He opened the door, and she slid out, lifted Sanzu onto the stretcher and out of the car. He winced as she lowered him, but there was no time to waste. A nurse wheeled him straight into an operating room.

She waited outside the operating room, watching people hurry back and forth. Ran and Rindou had left to report to Mikey and clean up the mess at the abandoned mansion, so she was waiting alone. Earlier, Takeomi had called her about the man at the mansion. He had run background checks, and it turned out the man was a former Bonten member who had doublecrossed them, teaming up with Tensei and selling their information. He was dead now, so that should be the end of it. But Tensei was still alive and thriving, and that worried her, especially with Tensei currently lacking a leader. The light above the operating room switched off, and a middle-aged man walked out.

He looked around for Ran and Rindou, who had probably threatened the surgeon into operating on Sanzu. She stepped up to him and pulled down her collar to show him the tattoo. His eyes widened slightly, then he relaxed and told her how things stood.

“He’s stable. He’ll have to stay in hospital for at least a week before he’s released,” the surgeon said. “He came in in quite a state, though.”

“I see,” she said, brushing away the tears stinging her eyes and pretending to yawn. “Thank you, sir.”

The surgeon was clearly thrown by her calm. “It’s what I do,” he said. “He’s been moved to a private room at the far end of the hospital. It should be safe from anyone. I’ll check on him myself a couple of times a day. I’ve been told by the two earlier not to speak a word about your identities.”

“Thank you again,” she said, bowing her head slightly, and headed for the room the surgeon had described.

“Ah, wait, ma’am!” the surgeon called after her. She stopped and waited while he caught up.

“Here.” He handed her his business card. “I think it might be useful to you in the future. Don’t hesitate to call if one of your members is injured.” He gave her a small smile.

“Why?” she snapped, questioning his kindness.

He rubbed the back of his neck. “I saw the news report a couple of days ago about the owner of the FNN club. I heard her speech, and it made me rethink some things. Sure, you’ve done a lot of crimes, murder included. It terrifies me to be talking to one of you right now. But the lady from the FNN said Bonten saved her from being killed. They aren’t the monsters everyone makes them out to be. This is only my opinion, and it might be the death of me one day, but…” He smiled again. “It is what it is.” With that, he turned and walked back the way he came.

She walked towards Sanzu’s room, the surgeon’s words going round and round in her head. She almost laughed out loud at his opinions. The power of media, huh?

When she reached Sanzu’s door and opened it, she was met with the click of a gun being cocked. It was a shock to see Sanzu already awake after coming out of anesthetic, and pointing a gun at her, which was understandable but still.

“Oh, it’s just you,” he sighed in relief, lowering the gun. He looked at her with soft eyes, almost begging her to come in. She stepped inside, closed the door quietly behind her and sat on one of the stools next to his bed.

“Aww, don’t be so distant from me, sweetheart~” he whined, pleading like a child. She just gave him a look.

“You had me so worried, you know? I know you’re naturally pale, but being literally white freaked the fuck out of me, you know? I—” Her voice cracked, and she turned her back to him and faced the door.

She heard rustling behind her, and an arm slid gently around her waist. “I couldn’t do anything about the situation I was in. It was either me or all five of us,” he muttered against her back. “Turn around, sweetheart. I want to see your face.”

She turned slowly, tears welling in her eyes.

“Look at me,” he said. She lifted her head, and their eyes met. “I’m okay now. It hurts, sure, but it’s nothing I can’t deal with.” He took her hand and laced his fingers through hers. “Come here,” he said, patting the space he’d made beside him on the bed. She walked round the bed

and sat where he motioned. The moment she sat, he pulled her into a hug and rested her head on his chest, away from the wounds. He wrapped his arm around her and drew small circles and shapes on her forearm to comfort her. She leaned into him, and he kissed the side of her head.

They stayed like that for a while. Then Sanzu stopped drawing on her arm. She looked up and saw his eyes closed and his breathing steady. He had fallen asleep. She let out a breath of relief, glad he was all right. She took the gun he’d been holding from the bedside table and gripped it tightly. It looked like she was going to be on night duty, watching over an injured and precious member of Bonten, and her boyfriend.

About two hours passed. Nothing changed. Sanzu mumbled in his sleep, called out a few names and snuggled closer to her. That gave her comfort. He was breathing. His heart was beating. He was alive. A noise outside the door made her flinch. She grabbed Sanzu’s head with one arm, pulled his body closer and shielded him. She pointed the gun at the door and waited. There was a moment of stillness, and then the door burst open. She clutched Sanzu tightly and took a quick breath to steady the gun. She let the breath out as a sigh, lowered the gun and loosened her grip on him.

“Couldn’t you knock?” she snarled quietly, glaring at Mochizuki in the doorway. He shook his head, closed the door behind him, walked over to the stool by the bed and sat down.

“Didn’t think you’d still be in here,” he said, staring at the back of Sanzu’s head, his eyes drifting down over his body beneath the hospital sheets. “Thought you’d have left by now.”

“Well, I’m staying here all night,” she said, looking down at Sanzu’s face, which was resting against her chest.

“Lucky man,” Mochi muttered under his breath, making her flush pink.

“Find someone yourself,” she snapped playfully, looking away. He laughed softly, careful not to wake Sanzu. “Oh, the surgeon gave me his card, by the way. He was quite a character, I’d say.”

“Oh?” Mochizuki said, taking the card she handed him, reading it, and looking back up. “What happened?”

“The power of media. He wants us to call him if one of us gets injured. He seemed to ‘admire’ the owner of the FNN club, saying her speech made him rethink Bonten after Rin saved her.”

“That’s definitely something,” Mochizuki said, snickering. “Good work, then. Hmm? Owner of the FNN club?”

“Looks like I did something I didn’t mean to,” she said with a shrug. She looked down at Sanzu again and smiled, then yawned and covered her mouth with her hand.

“You should rest. You had a long night.”

She shook her head. “No, I need to look after him. I’m worried.”

“Worried about what, exactly?”

“He’s vulnerable. I’m staying awake to protect him.” Mochizuki sighed and shook his head.

“Fine. I’ll stay here tonight. It’s two in the morning. I’ll wake you up at six, so get some rest until then.” He reached over and took the gun from her palm.

“Okay, thanks, Mochi. I owe you one,” she murmured, laying her head down on the edge of Sanzu’s pillow. As if he knew she was drifting off, Sanzu pulled her closer, then flinched. He had used his injured arm. He groaned, swearing as he woke.

“Fuck!” he gasped, catching Mochizuki’s attention.

“Whoa, careful there,” Mochi chuckled, looking down at him.

“Why the fuck are you here?” Sanzu growled, shifting on the bed and wincing again.

“Here, I’ll help,” she whispered, moving him carefully onto his back so his stomach faced the ceiling. Their eyes met for a second, and she flicked his forehead lightly.

“Heyyy~” he whined, rubbing his forehead.

“He’s here to watch over us while we sleep, because I’m paranoid. So be grateful,” she scolded, and he started to pout. He glanced at Mochi.

“Don’t be a creep, watching my girl while she sleeps,” Sanzu said, sticking his tongue out at Mochi. Mochi was visibly annoyed by Sanzu’s childish behavior, but he let it go for now.

“Hurry up and go to sleep,” Mochi said sharply to Sanzu. Then, “Akari.”

“Yeah?” She looked over at Mochi and began to lie down on the bed beside Sanzu.

“Call Mikey when you wake up.”

“Huh? I—okay,” she said with a yawn. She rested her head on the same pillow as Sanzu and leaned in close to his shoulder. He pressed a small kiss to her cheek and rested his head on hers, falling asleep. “’Night,” she murmured to Mochi, who hummed in response. She closed her eyes and drifted off quickly as the tiredness finally took over.

### Eighteen

She was woken by a pair of strong arms shaking her gently and the occasional light flashing over her eyes. She rubbed her eyes, sat up carefully and moved the arm that had been lying across her waist, taking care not to wake him.

“Akari, it’s 6 am,” Mochi announced, settling back onto his stool.

“Ahh, thank you, Mochi,” she replied sleepily, sitting up in the hospital bed and leaning against the wall. She glanced to her right and watched Sanzu breathing slowly and steadily. He hadn’t

moved an inch since the early hours. His wounds must be taking a toll. Her eyes travelled over his body under the thin white sheet, and she smiled at his calm face before turning back to Mochi. “I’m supposed to call Mikey, right?”

Mochi nodded slowly. “Maybe not right now. He’ll be annoyed if you wake him up.”

“Why do I need to call him at all? Didn’t Ran and Rindou tell him what happened?”

“He wants to hear what happened from you, including Sanzu’s condition.”

She looked down at her hands in her lap and twiddled her thumbs. “Mmm, okay,” she said quietly, leaning her head back against the wall.

“I’m going now. I’ve got a job to attend to,” Mochi said, standing up from the stool. He tossed her the gun, and she caught it.

“Is anyone coming here later?” she asked, emptying the magazine and checking the bullets before reloading them herself.

“Not that I know of. Want me to ask Kakucho to come?”

“Yeah, that’d be great. I need to change. Sanzu’s blood is probably still on my clothes and dried on my back. It feels gross.”

“Sounds gross,” Mochi said, chuckling. “Yeah, I’ll let him know. And I hope you know this room has a shower and a bathroom, since it’s private.” He pointed at the door beside the bed.

“Oh, I didn’t notice.” She glanced quickly towards the bathroom. “All the more reason to stay here, then.”

Mochi sighed and shook his head. “You worry too much,” he said, heading for the door. “Make sure to call Mikey later.” With that, he slid the door open and left, closing it behind him. She sighed deeply and looked over at the bathroom. She got off the bed and adjusted Sanzu’s body carefully. He groaned and whined softly. She went over to the bathroom, opened the door and peeked inside. Nobody was there. A toilet sat against one wall, with a shower in the corner, and the floor sloped towards the drain. A nurse call button was fixed near the handrails by the toilet and shower. Towels hung from the rails, and a bar of soap sat in the corner. The mirror and sink were beside the toilet, with another small towel folded over the edge. She closed the bathroom door and turned back to Sanzu, who was still asleep. She walked around the bed, sat on the stool and kept staring at him.

About five hours later, Kakucho came through the door carrying a small bag with her clothes and some fruit.

“Thanks, Kaku,” she said, giving him a smile, to which he replied with a small nod. Sanzu was awake now, sitting up against the wall for support. Kakucho set the fruit on the bedside table and handed her the clothes. She took them out of the bag. “Can you watch him while I shower?”

“Sure,” he said, and she took the clothes and left Sanzu in his care. She shut the bathroom door behind her and laid her clothes on the closed toilet lid, along with the larger bath towel. She turned on the tap, and hot water came pouring out at once. She peeled off her clothes, which had stuck to her back, and dropped them on the floor away from the spray. She stepped under the warm water and felt the dried blood flake away, running down the drain and turning the water a pale rose pink. She scrubbed herself with the bar of soap and washed her hair with it too. Once the soap was rinsed away, she turned off the tap, reached for a towel on the rail and dried herself quickly. She pulled on the clothes Kakucho had brought. He had brought her one of her suits. She rubbed her hair with the same towel to get rid of as much moisture as she could, then stepped out of the bathroom in a pair of disposable slippers.

When she came out, she found herself staring at a strange sight. Kakucho was carrying Sanzu in his arms and swinging him round the room in circles.

“What—” she started, but she didn’t finish, too shocked. Kakucho stopped spinning and turned his head to look at her. Sanzu covered his face with one hand in embarrassment.

“Don’t question anything you just saw, sweetheart,” Sanzu said, turning his head away from her, his face bright pink. Kakucho was just as flushed, but because he was holding Sanzu up, he couldn’t hide his face.

“Umm, anyway. What’s happening back at base?” she asked, as Kakucho set Sanzu down carefully on the wheelchair in the corner, which hadn’t been there at the start of the day. “Oh shit! I need to call Mikey!” She grabbed her phone and started scrolling through her contacts, until Kakucho caught her wrist.

“Don’t even bother,” he said, tightening his grip.

“Huh?”

“Sanzu and I were just talking about leaving the hospital.” Sanzu nodded in agreement.

“But the surgeon said—”

“You can look after him back at home. That way you’ll get enough sleep without being paranoid. Mikey would let Sanzu heal either way, and I’m sure he’ll let you stay with him, so we might as well leave the hospital,” Kakucho said.

“I—okay. How are we getting him out without being busted?” she asked. He pointed at her lips and then at her hair.

“You can wear your mask, tie up the top half of your hair and hide it under this.” He tossed her a beret that came out of nowhere.

“Were you planning this the moment you got here?” she asked. Kakucho nodded.

“Anyway, sorry, Sanzu, but we’re going to wrap your face up in bandages,” Kakucho announced, pulling out two rolls of bandage and tucking his own hair under his hospital gown

before he started wrapping Sanzu’s head. She snickered at them as she tied her hair up, tucked it under the beret and put her mask on.

“Kaku? What about you?” He turned to her quickly, then went back to bandaging Sanzu’s face.

“I’ll wear a mask with you,” he said flatly. “We’ll look like a suspicious rich couple.” He stood up and released the brakes on Sanzu’s wheelchair.

“Do you have a car?”

“Of course. Grab everything, and let’s go,” he said. She grabbed everything she had in the private room, shoved it all into the bag Kakucho had brought and set it on Sanzu’s lap. She stepped out of the disposable slippers, pulled on her heels and walked up beside Kakucho. He began to wheel the chair out of the room and down the corridor, with her walking beside him, head held high, drawing stares from nurses and other patients. They reached the exit, left the hospital and headed for the sleek black car. Kakucho stopped the chair, unlocked the car and opened the back door. He slid one arm under Sanzu’s shoulders and one under his knees and lifted him in, while Sanzu winced.

“Get in. I’ll take the wheelchair back,” Kakucho said, and set off back towards the hospital entrance. She climbed into the back with Sanzu and shut the door softly. She heard him mumbling, and realized his face was still wrapped in bandages and he couldn’t speak properly. She laughed at the sight of his bandaged face.

“Man, this is funny,” she said, staring at him. He started to mumble and whine from under the bandages. “I’m keeping you like this until we get home,” she smirked, taking off her mask and beret as the driver’s door opened.

“Alright, let’s head back,” Kakucho said, turning the key and reversing out of the car park.

The car entered the garage and parked as close to the lift as it could get. She slid out, opened the door, and unlocked the lift with her car key. Kakucho carried Sanzu into the lift effortlessly, and it shot up to the top floor. She stepped out ahead of him and opened her bedroom door. Kakucho laid Sanzu on the bed and unwrapped his bandages.

“Fucking finally,” Kakucho wheezed, relieved to be able to breathe and talk properly.

“Stay here. I’m going to talk to Mikey,” she said, pointing a finger at Sanzu as a threat. He whined but nodded. She left the room with Kakucho and shut the door behind her. “Thanks, Kaku,” she said with a smile.

“No problem. I’ll be in my room if you need me,” he said, turning and disappearing into his room. She walked over to the couch and found Takeomi there, smoking another cigarette.

“Who was that?”

“Who?”

“The guy in the bandages.” He exhaled a cloud of smoke.

“Your brother,” she said softly, standing opposite him.

“Ohhh, glad to see he’s okay now,” he said, eyeing her quickly. “And you? Are you okay?”

She gave him a peace sign and a smile. “Yup, as good as before! Just sleepy.” He chuckled and took another drag. “By the way, where’s Mikey?”

“In his office downstairs.”

“Ahhh, okay. Thanks.” She walked to the lift and pressed the button. The doors began to open.

“Ah, Akari. Take the stairs. He’s locked his floor,” he said, nodding towards the staircase.

“Ohh, sweet.” She stepped out of the lift before its doors closed and walked past her room to the emergency stairs. She pulled the door open and started down the long flights. As she went, she heard the echo of a woman screaming, probably one of the women being held there before she was sold. She ignored it and kept going. A gunshot rang out, and she flinched before pushing open the door to Mikey’s floor. It was very dimly lit, with barely any light reaching her eyes. She made her way almost blindly to Mikey’s main office. She knocked, and heard the sound of slow footsteps. The door swung open.

“I locked the floor for a fucking reas—” He stopped when he saw who it was. “Oh, Akari.” He stood aside to let her in and walked back to his desk, while she sat down on the couch.

“You should really work in the light. It’s better for your eyes,” she said, pointing at the blinds covering the windows. He sighed, picked up a remote and pressed it. The blinds began to part to either side.

“Any better?” he asked, putting the remote back where it had been. “Anyway, how’s Sanzu?”

“He’s fine now, I guess. Shot in the thigh, stabbed three times. Don’t expect him back at work for a month. Earliest.”

“I see. And you? How are you doing? No injuries, I hope?”

“I’m fine. Just sleep-deprived,” she said with a yawn. “I’m not opening the bar downstairs for another week or so, so I’ve got plenty of time to recover.” He nodded.

“So what do you want to do?”

“Look after Sanzu until he’s better. We haven’t had much time together, so I think this is the perfect opportunity.” Mikey hummed and rested his head in his hands, deep in thought.

“I mean, that’s fine with me, but it means fewer executives and more work for each one of the rest.”

“Give me work from time to time. I can’t stay inside all day either,” she said, trying to strike a deal with him.

“Hmm, sure thing.” He said coldly, staring out of the window. “Actually, I’ll give you a job right now.”

“Whaaat?” she whined. “I’m tireddd.”

“Not right now. For later.”

“Oh, okay, cool. What is it?”

“You know how to ride a motorcycle, right?”

“Yeah,” she said, wondering what on earth the mission could be.

“Perfect.”

She trudged back up the emergency stairs to the top floor, dragging her feet. She pushed open the stair door and shuffled towards her room, but the moment she reached for her bedroom door, a voice stopped her.

“Akari~!” Ran’s voice echoed down the hall as he ran towards her. He wrapped her in a tight hug and rested his head on top of hers.

“Yes, Ran?” she said wearily.

“Glad to see you’re all safe after spending the night in the hospital.”

“Were you expecting something to happen?” she asked, raising an eyebrow.

“Nope,” he said. She felt his jaw move into a smile against her head. “How’s Sanzu doing?”

“Much better. They stitched up his wounds, so he should be fine to go back to work in about a month,” she said, inching out of his tight grip. “I’m going to sleep now, so keep quiet outside the room, please.”

“Mmm, sure,” he said, letting go of her. She opened the door and stepped into the bedroom, closing it behind her. Sanzu was staring at the ceiling with a bored expression.

“Babe?” His head turned towards her, and his face lit up instantly.

“Sweetheart~” he whined, lifting one arm towards her. She went to him, not even bothering to change out of her suit, and slid carefully onto the bed beside him. He didn’t move, still staring at the ceiling, but he brushed her hair softly with his fingers.

“Mikey said he’ll give you a month off work to heal,” she whispered.

“Okay, cool. More time with you, then,” he smirked.

“Yup. I’m not opening the bar for another two weeks. I’ve got some work from Mikey, but that’s for whenever. So I’ve got one week all for you.” She gave him a peck on the cheek. He tightened his grip on her hair, pulled her in and began to kiss her with intensity. She bit his lip lightly and slipped her tongue into his mouth, tasting something slightly metallic. She ran her

fingers up his neck into his long hair, then cupped his face and squished his cheeks. She parted her lips and laid her head on the pillow.

“I’m going to sleep now,” she murmured.

“Of course, sweetheart,” he answered, using his good arm to pull her closer to his side. She moved closer on her own and kissed the scar on his face before snuggling into him and drifting off to sleep.

### Nineteen

She woke early the next morning. She had slept through the whole day on her bed without stirring once. She sat up slowly, listening to the birds chirping softly outside. She looked to her side and found the bed empty. Her eyes widened, and she jumped up and rushed to the door. She tripped over the laundry basket she had left in the middle of the room the night before, fell forward and landed heavily on the floor, her head hitting the door. She groaned, pressing a hand to her forehead to ease the pain. She picked herself up, clutching her head, opened the door and trudged to the kitchen. She opened the freezer, grabbed an ice pack and pressed it to her forehead, which was starting to swell.

“What happened to you?” Koko asked, eating his breakfast at the table and looking up from his meal.

“I fell,” she mumbled, embarrassed. “Where’s Sanzu?”

“He’s with Ran and Rindou downstairs,” Koko said, pointing at the floor.

“Oh.” She cracked her knuckles. “He’d better not be doing anything stupid or strenuous.”

“That’s a little far-fetched. Just a little,” he scoffed, lifting his teacup to his lips.

“Well, thanks, Koko. I’ll catch you in a bit,” she said, heading for the lift. She heard him hum in response. The lift doors closed, and she pressed the button for the Haitani brothers’ floor. Luckily they had left it unlocked, so she didn’t have to use the emergency stairs. The doors opened, and she stepped out and walked towards the door at the end of the hallway. As she got close, she heard laughter, the clinking of glasses and a strange electric buzz. She knocked, and they scuffled around inside.

“Oh shit,” Ran said, not even trying to keep his voice down. The door opened, and Rindou stood in it. She peered past him. The room was a mess. Ran was trying to shove things into a corner, and Sanzu was sitting on a chair in the middle of the room. She pushed Rindou aside, walked straight in and headed for Sanzu.

“Hey, sweetheart. What are you doing here?” Sanzu asked, one eyebrow twitching.

“Came to check on you. That’s all. Making sure you’re not doing anything ‘stupid,’ so you don’t hurt yourself more than you need to,” she said quickly, glancing at the two brothers before turning back to Sanzu.

“Hey, don’t look at us like that. We didn’t do anything!” Ran said quickly, noticing her stare.

“Sure, says the one who was hiding shit the second I knocked on the door.” She walked over to the corner and pointed at the badly hidden pile of alcohol and glasses. She heard all three of them gulp audibly. “See?”

“Yeah, and?” Rindou started. “We just wanted to have a drink, and you were still sleeping, so we took bored Sanzu with us.”

“He’s injured,” she said.

“I’m fine, though,” Sanzu said, swinging his arm around normally.

“That’s your non-injured arm,” she pointed out. She walked back to him and pushed gently at his thigh, causing him to suck in a sharp breath through his teeth. “How much did you drink?”

“One glass,” he replied quickly.

“No more than that. It’ll only make the bleeding worse.”

“Yes, ma’am,” Sanzu said in a quieter voice.

“So what are you doing now?” Ran asked, picking up the drinks and the bottles from the corner and putting them back on the table. He poured a glass of whiskey and held it out to her. She declined.

“I was planning on going out with Sanzu today, but I guess not now,” she said, noticing the small excited squeak from Sanzu. She looked over at him. “But not anymore, because you ruined it.” She poked her tongue out at him playfully.

“I’m gonna cut that tongue off if you poke it at me again,” he said, a faint edge of anger in his voice.

“Just try it.” She poked it out again. “You’re the one who’s going to struggle.”

“Wha—. How exactly?” She sent him a wink, and he shut up quickly. She smirked at his reaction.

“Anyway, don’t you two have anything to do?”

The brothers looked at each other. “We’ve got work this week and next, but we can finish it in four days, so we’d have all of next week free.”

“Oh, when are the four days?”

“Planning to start later today,” Rindou said.

“Hmm, are you two interested in going to the beach with the Bonten members next week?” she suggested. Their eyes lit up a little.

“Beach!” Sanzu yelled, excited. “Haven’t been in years.”

“The last time we went was with Izana.” She nodded, instantly remembering that day. She smiled to herself, but the smile was wiped away when she remembered what had happened afterwards. “Anyway, are you interested?”

“Yeah~” Sanzu said.

“Sure. How long are we staying?” Rindou asked, pouring himself another drink into a smaller glass.

“I’ll have to ask Mikey. I think it’d be a good opportunity for Mikey to get out, so—”

“I don’t think he’s been outside in months,” Ran said, putting his glass down on the table. She nodded.

“Ran, I think that’s enough drinks. Same with you, Rindou,” she said, taking the whiskey bottle away from them. “I’ll ask the rest of the executives and Mikey, so you can carry on with whatever you were doing before I came in.” She headed for the door and went back to the lift.

She took the lift one floor up and knocked on Mikey’s office door. It was silent, so she opened it slowly. Mikey had fallen asleep at his desk. She sighed and tiptoed towards him. His arms were folded under his head as a pillow, and his body was slumped awkwardly over the table, yet he was sleeping peacefully. She stepped closer, and he began to murmur in his sleep.

“Nii-san, I’m sorry. Baji, I’m sorry. Emma, I’m sorry. Izana, I’m sorry.” He muttered, with tears sliding down his face, his eyes still closed. She felt a sharp pain at his dream. Without thinking, she put her hand on his back and began to rub slowly up and down, trying to soothe him. He grew calmer as she did, and she kept going until his tears stopped. Seeing him like this made her eyes sting. She decided to come back later to ask about the beach, and she turned to leave when Mikey called out.

“Akari. Don’t go.” She turned around quickly. He had lifted his head off his arms and was looking straight at her with wet eyes.

She couldn’t leave him looking at her like that, so she walked back. He got up from his chair and stood. She reached for the remote and pressed it at the curtains, and they slid apart, flooding the room with light. She set the remote down and looked at Mikey, who stood opposite her.

“What do you want me to do, Mikey?” she asked softly, holding his gaze. He didn’t say anything. He just stepped closer, wrapped his arms around her waist, slid down her body and dropped to the floor, crying softly. She looked down at his small figure, clinging to her legs. She crouched to his level, gently pried his arms from her legs, placed them under her arms, and hugged him tightly, brushing her hand softly across his back. “Do you want to talk about it?” she whispered. He sniffled and wiped his tears on her suit.

“It happened again,” was all he said, and she understood at once.

“I see,” she said, holding the back of his head with one hand and smoothing his hair. Mikey had recurring dreams in which he relived the deaths of Shinichiro, Baji, Emma and Izana. He would watch them die again and again, in the same dream, and it happened most nights when he tried to sleep. It was no wonder the dark circles under his eyes were so pronounced. “Mikey,” she said, still stroking his head. “Let it all out. It’s okay.” He gripped her tighter, his nails digging into her skin, as if she might vanish.

“Don’t leave me, Akari,” he mumbled into her shoulder, tears pouring. “You’re all I have right now.”

“That’s not true,” she said softly. “You have Sanzu, Koko and me, plus everyone else in Bonten.”

“Yeah, but—” he sniffled, his nose blocked. She grabbed the tissue box from his desk and handed it to him. He took one and blew his nose.

“We’re all here for you, Mikey. And don’t worry, I won’t leave you,” she said, stroking the back of his head. He slowly lifted himself away from her.

“Thanks, Akari. For everything,” he said quietly.

“That’s okay. I’ll be here for you whenever you need, okay?” He nodded. She handed him the tissue box again, and he took another one and wiped away the last of the tears clinging to his lashes. He kept hugging her until he calmed down, his breathing steady again.

“Why were you in here, anyway?” he asked, back to normal, almost as if he had switched his emotions off and never had them at all.

“I was going to ask if you had anything on for everyone next week.”

“Why?”

“Some of us want to go to the beach next week.”

“Why?”

“To unwind. Relax. Have a break. Have fun?”

“Hmm,” was all Mikey said before picking up the phone on his desk and pressing the buttons. “Can you check my schedule for next week, Takeomi?” He nodded slowly, painfully slowly, as he waited for the answer. “Okay, thanks.” He put the phone down.

“And?”

“Since Sanzu’s injured, we’ve got more work to do. And you’re off taking care of him, so it’ll be difficult—”

“I’ll take on Sanzu’s work, then. I’m sure he’ll understand. It’s not like everyone will be out at the same time, leaving him alone either way.” Mikey scribbled something on a sticky note and handed it to her.

“This is the list of things Sanzu had to finish before next week.” She read the notes.

- Sell the prostitutes at the auction

- Buy medical stocks

- Send one of the cars to get checked

- Assassination of xxxxx

“Yeah, this is doable,” she said, glancing up at Mikey.

“It’s one job a day, plus the job I gave you yesterday.”

“Ohh yeah, I need your keys.” He opened a drawer and handed them over, and she slipped them into her pocket. “Okay, sweet. I’ll start this afternoon, then. Does that mean we can all go to the beach next week?”

“Depends on the other executives and their work,” Mikey said flatly.

“Okay, I’ll let them know about the plans. I’m sure they’ll all be on board.” She left the room and hurried back to the lift.

“Koko, are you interested in going to the beach next week with everyone?”

“Depends,” he said quickly, typing away at his computer like a maniac.

“Koko~” she whined. He finally looked up from the screen.

“Whaaat~” he mimicked.

“We’re going to the beach with everyone next week, so finish all your work for this week and next. Thanks. Bye!” She dumped all the information on him and left him to make sense of it.

“Fine,” he muttered, rolling his eyes and getting back to work.

“Omi,” she knocked on the door and waited for him to open it. He pulled it open and let her in. Takeomi and Kakucho were both in the office, which was perfect. Two people at once.

“Oh, hey, Kaku.”

“So what did you need this time?” Kakucho asked, turning his chair to face her.

“We’re going to the beach next week, so I need everyone to finish their work for this week and next.”

“Is that why Mikey asked about his schedule?” Takeomi asked, and she nodded.

“Is Mikey coming?” Kakucho asked calmly.

“Yeah, he’s coming. Well, I’m going to drag him along either way.”

“That’s good. I haven’t seen him go outside for anything other than work in months,” Kakucho said, sounding worried about Mikey.

“Okay, we’ll make sure our work is done, then,” Takeomi said.

“Thanks, Omi,” she said with a smile.

“What about Sanzu’s workload? Are you doing it?” Kakucho asked.

“Yeah, I’ll be doing it, so I’ll be busy this week.” She scratched the back of her neck. “I need to catch Mochi before I start, so see you all in a bit.” She left the room and headed for Mochi’s floor, one level above Takeomi’s.

“Mochi~” she whined outside his office door, but then she remembered he was out on a job. She sighed, took the lift back to the top floor and walked quickly past the couch to her room. She swapped her suit jacket, put on a little make-up, and tied her black hair into a low ponytail, tucking it into her suit. This job had to be done as Nakatani Hana, or it would look too suspicious. She hooked the face mask around her ears and pulled on her black flats. She grabbed the gun from the bedside table, tucked it into her waistband and left the room for the lift. In the lift, she sent Sanzu a quick message saying she was going out. When the lift reached the garage, she took the keys Mikey had given her from her back pocket and walked to his motorbike. It was dusty, so she blew the dust off and coughed. When she ignited the engine, it roared just the way it had twelve years ago. Mikey had had the Touman mark removed after the reign ended, so the manji symbol was gone and the bike was plain black. She swung onto it, kicked the stand away and rode it out of the garage towards her destination.

Riding through the streets of Tokyo on Mikey’s beloved bike felt strange. It was his only keepsake of his older brother, and letting her ride it showed how much he trusted her. It was nothing like riding behind Sanzu on his motorbike. On Sanzu’s bike she had always been shielded from the wind by his back. Now she was fully exposed, the wind slapping her face as she wove through traffic and her hair whipping out behind her. Car drivers turned to stare as her engine echoed off the buildings. She set her foot down to steady the bike while she waited for the light to turn green. A black car pulled up beside her, and its window rolled down. It was Ran and Rindou.

“Haven’t seen anyone ride that in a while,” Ran said. “Last time I saw it was about ten years ago, I think.”

“Yeah, Mikey asked me to get it checked,” she said. “Part of my job now.”

“Strange he trusted it to you, though,” Rindou said.

“He wants it checked by no one other than Draken, so—” She trailed off as the light turned green. “See you later tonight, boys.” She rode off towards Draken’s shop, which was visible in the distance.

### Twenty

She slowed to a halt outside D&D Motors. Almost at once, Draken pulled open the door and rushed out towards the street. She guessed he had recognized the sound of Mikey’s bike. She saw his face drain of color as disappointment and pain set in. She turned off the engine and began to wheel the bike into the shop, and Draken followed her in.

“Sorry about that,” Draken said, walking round behind the counter. “So what can I help you with, ma’am?”

She looked around. The shop was lined with motorbikes. She kicked the stand down, and the bike balanced on it. She went to the counter and explained the situation.

“Hi, I’d like a check-up on the bike, if you can. If there are any repairs needed, I’ll pay for them,” she said, tapping the seat. Draken came round the counter, squatted beside the bike and began to inspect it. “Cool tattoo, by the way,” she said, pointing at his head. He smiled and muttered a quiet thanks.

“Inupi!” he called loudly, and Inui came out of the room behind the counter.

“Yeah?” Draken pointed at the bike, and Inui understood at once. She knew this was going to be a difficult spot to get out of, so she had to leave.

“Is it all right if I leave this with you for the day?” she asked, looking down at Draken, who was still inspecting the bike, with worry and hope both in his eyes.

“Uh, yeah, sure. Can I ask where you got this bike?”

“I’ve had it for a few years. I think about five years? Thought it was time to get it checked. Why?” she lied, clenching her jaw while she told it.

“I had a friend a while back who had exactly the same bike,” he said in a pained voice.

“What a coincidence, I guess,” she said, biting her lip behind her mask.

“Yeah. You know, you remind me of one of my other friends from the past. She always wore a mask, and she was about your height. I haven’t seen her in years, though.” Draken looked up at her with a small smile.

“You seem to have lost a lot of friends over your lifetime. What’s stopping you from going after them?” The silence hung in the air for a long moment before he answered.

“I don’t know about Akari, but I’m sure she’s with him,” Draken said. “Akari is the friend I said you look like.”

“They’re in Bonten,” Inui said bluntly.

“Oh, makes sense.” She tucked a loose strand of platinum hair behind her ear.

“Aren’t you shocked?”

“Eh, not really. Bonten’s chill. Well, I don’t know them personally, but they’re chill people, if you ignore their crimes.” She laughed slightly and scratched the back of her neck.

Draken suddenly stood and gripped her shoulders. “Have you seen the boss?” he demanded, eyes wide. She nodded, and she felt his fingers loosen on her shoulders. “Is he alright?” he murmured.

“So he was the old friend with the same bike, then?” Draken said yes. “He seems okay. He’s quite quiet, so I can’t say much. The others are rowdy, though.” She let out a small laugh, and Draken let go of her shoulders and turned back to the bike.

“How do you even know them?” Inui asked, giving her a hard look. “Hope you’re not an underworld figure, because that’d be trouble for our business,” he growled, his blond hair swaying as he stepped towards her.

“Here.” She handed Inui her FNN business card. “I hope this says it all.” He took it, studied it, and passed it to Draken.

“Oh, you’re the woman from the TV the other night. That must’ve been terrible for your business,” Draken said.

“Mhm. We’re not opening for another two weeks, just to be safe. Anyway, I’ll be on my way. Give me a call when the bike’s serviced.”

“Of course. Is the number on the card the right one?” Inui asked, taking the card back from Draken and heading behind the counter.

“Yeah, the mobile would be great. About what time should I expect a call?”

Inui started scribbling notes onto a sheet of paper on the counter. “Probably later in the evening. Maybe near closing, which is about six. Could be earlier, though.”

“Your bike needs quite a bit of touching up,” Draken said, chuckling. She handed him the key to the bike. Just in case, she had added a small feminine key ring to it.

“Oh, I see. Well, I’ll be back by then. See you later,” she said, turning on her heel and leaving the shop with a little wave.

She let out a heavy sigh. It was hard to see Draken like that, worrying and hoping that Mikey would come back one day. She hoped she had given him some reassurance about Mikey, even if it was only vague. She walked away from the shop and towards the nearest pharmacy to buy the medical supplies, another job on Sanzu’s list.

Once she was out of sight of D&D Motors, she ducked into an alleyway, pulled off her face mask, untucked her hair from her shirt and started braiding it into two plaits. Then she headed back onto the main road and went into the pharmacy. The customers and the staff behind the counter all looked at her. She wandered the aisles, grabbed a basket and started loading it up.

She had bandages in multiple rolls, muscle cream, antibiotics, instant ice packs, tweezers, plasters and a few other things. She put the basket on the counter. The cashier gave her a small, mischievous look and began to scan the items.

She handed her the plastic bag with everything in it. “Have a good day, ma’am,” the cashier said, her voice trembling slightly, before she turned to the next customer. Carrying the bag in one hand, Akari left the shop and walked back towards the Bonten building.

When she got back to the garage, she took the lift up to the top floor, where Koko was still typing at the dining table. She set the plastic bag down beside him.

“Do you think this is enough for all of us?” she asked. Koko stopped typing, emptied the bag onto the table, and his eyes widened. He turned slightly pink when he saw one of the items.

“Really? Condoms?” he asked, ignoring her question. “Sanzu’s injured.”

“Gee, I totally didn’t know that,” she said, rolling her eyes. “I live with men, and you want to tell me Sanzu’s injured? Why would I have sex with him now of all times, when he’s literally injured?”

“Mhm,” Koko shrugged.

“Maybe you’ll need them in the future. Same with me, who knows,” he said, and then coughed at his own comment.

“You really need to learn to have a filter sometimes, Akari,” he said, recovering from the shock.

“Yeah, yeah. So is this enough, or do we need more?”

“I think it’s enough. I doubt more than one person will be injured at once, and we can top up when we need to.” He put the items back in the bag and handed it back to her to pack away. She put them into the nearly empty first aid box and returned it to its place. She tied up the plastic bag and set it by the bin for when it was needed.

She walked down the hallway into her room and found Sanzu asleep on the bed, a faint pink flush across his cheeks. She leaned close and caught the smell of whiskey on his breath from earlier that morning. She realized the brothers had been drinking and driving this morning. She facepalmed at their behavior but just shrugged. She smiled at the sleeping Sanzu, pulled the blanket over him and turned to leave.

She was back in the garage and slid into the car labelled ‘needing servicing.’ She pulled the note off the windscreen. She leaned over the steering wheel and accidentally beeped the horn with her chest.

She chuckled quietly to herself to brush off the embarrassment, put the note on the passenger seat and turned the key, and the engine rumbled softly. She pressed the accelerator, opened the garage door and drove out towards the car service area.

When she reached the service station, she handed over her car keys. “When should I come back to pick it up?”

“It should be done by tomorrow afternoon, but it depends on how much work it needs,” the man said, ticking things off on the paper clipped to his board.

“Alright, sweet. Give me a call when it’s all good,” she said, giving him her number. She left the service station and started walking. After a couple of minutes, a black car pulled up beside her, with a white van following close behind.

“Akari~!” Ran called in a strange voice that made it hard to ignore him.

“Yes?”

“We’re going.” He opened the back door quickly.

“Umm, where exactly?”

“Selling the whores. It’s the job I originally had with Sanzu.”

“Oh. Okay, then,” she said, climbing into the back seat and clicking her seatbelt on.

“I’m so lucky Sanzu’s injured. I get to go on a date with you~” he said, turning the steering wheel. She leaned forward and smacked the back of his head.

“You’re not so lucky. Calm down.” She sat back and glanced behind them to make sure the white van was still there. At the red light, he smoothed down the stray hairs on the back of his head. He took a turn, then another, and they arrived at the new venue for the auction. He switched off the engine, took the keys and climbed out of the driver’s seat. She unlocked her door, stepped out and shut it softly. She stepped up onto the footpath and walked through the main doors of the venue beside Ran.

“Did you shrink?” he asked, climbing the spiral staircase to the left of the main doors, his hands in his trouser pockets.

She clicked her tongue in annoyance. “I didn’t shrink. I changed my shoes.” She was very tempted to kick him back down the stairs while he snickered. When they reached the top, he stopped at the furthest door from the staircase. He knocked hard and waited, then swung the door wide. A chubby man sat in an office chair, wearing an expensive suit, a gold watch and other accessories. A glass of rum sat on the desk beside him, in a cup decorated with intricate patterns.

“Well, hello, Bonten,” the fat man said, lifting the glass to his lips. “New face today, I see. Hello, ma’am.” She nodded at him respectfully, but she kept glaring at the fat man while she studied the room.

“We brought what you asked for,” Ran said, sitting opposite the fat man, crossing his legs and resting his hands in his lap. She stood behind Ran, looking over his shoulder, as the two of them talked for a while.

“Here you go,” the fat man said. He ducked under the desk for a moment, then came back up with a black suitcase in his chubby hands. He set it on the desk carefully, making sure not to spill a drop of his rum. He flicked the locks and turned the case to face them. Ran pulled it closer, took out a single stack of notes and passed it back over his head to her without looking at her. She took it from him and pulled a single note from the pile, holding it up to the light. She slid it back into the stack and handed it back to Ran, who put it into the case. She tapped Ran’s shoulder twice, and he looked up. She shook her head slightly and raised an eyebrow. He looked back at the fat man and slowly pulled his gun out of his pocket. The fat man was flicking through his papers with such concentration that he didn’t notice a thing.

She flicked her tongue twice, a warning for the fat man. He looked up from his papers and finally saw the gun Ran was pointing at him. “Did you really think you could dupe us twice with fake money?” Ran snarled. The man began to cower, his eyes darting back and forth, searching for anything to protect himself with.

“Ahaha—” the man laughed awkwardly, waving his hands in front of his face. “W-what do you mean, twice?”

“This isn’t the first time. The last one was fake too,” she said, pointing her own gun at the middle of his head.

“Eeeek—” he whined, trying to scramble out of his chair and hide under the table. She moved the muzzle an inch to the side and pulled the trigger. There was no sound, but the bullet whizzed past the fat man’s cheek and into the wall behind him.

“I’d suggest you don’t move,” Ran said, taking the words right out of her mouth. “I’ll give you two options. Give us the money we earned, from both last time and this time. Or you can die right here, right now. So what’s your decision?” The sudden buzz of her phone in her pocket snapped all three of them out of the tense scene.

“Excuse me,” she said, lowering her gun from the man. “Ran, do what you need to do,” she said with a smirk, and she left the room, closing the door softly behind her.

She took the phone out of her pocket and put it to her ear, pressing answer.

“Hello?”

“This is D&D Motors. Draken speaking. Is this Nakatani Hana?”

“Oh. Yeah, this is she.”

“Great. Just wanted to let you know the servicing on your bike is done and ready to pick up.”

“Sweet. I’ll be there in about an hour, is that okay?” she asked, tapping her foot softly on the carpet.

“Yeah, of course. See you in an hour.”

“Yup, thank you,” she said, hanging up and sliding the phone back into her pocket. She walked back to the room, knocked twice and waited for Ran’s voice before going in.

Ran was holding two black suitcases this time. He unlocked one and showed her, and she looked over the money again. “Have you ever thought about doing bank transfers instead of physical cash?” she asked him.

“Gotta ask him and the boss about that. And I can’t be bothered doing that, so here we are,” Ran sighed, shrugging as he shut the case.

“At least learn how to tell fake from real money. No wonder we got duped last time,” she said, rolling her eyes. She turned to the man on the floor, who was slumped against his chair, passed out, with the front of his trousers stained a darker color. “What did you do to him?”

“Nothing much. He got scared shitless and passed out.”

“And pissed his pants,” she said, pointing at the stain. Ran laughed out loud, passed her one of the two cases, and headed out of the office, down the spiral staircase and towards the car parked outside.

“Yay, that’s one job done!” Ran announced, dropping heavily into the driver’s seat. She slid into the passenger seat, shut the door and clicked on her seatbelt.

“Time to go home,” he said, starting the engine.

“Oh, can you drop me off a couple of streets away from D&D Motors?” she asked, pulling her mask from her pocket and undoing her twin plaits. She flipped down the sun visor, used the mirror to tie her black hair back, then tugged her shirt to make room to tuck the hair inside. She pulled the front of her shirt straight and checked the mirror to make sure the tattoo was covered, adding an extra button just in case. She ran her fingers through her platinum hair quickly and hooked the mask around her ears.

“It’s like I just watched Akari disappear into thin air. I’m sitting in a car with a stranger now,” Ran said, watching her change from Kurokawa Akari into Nakatani Hana.

“So can you drive me there or not?”

“Yeah, okay.”

Ran dropped her off a couple of streets from D&D Motors and drove back to the Bonten building. She walked to the shop and went inside.

“Heya, Draken!” she called cheerily, raising a hand to her face in greeting.

“Hey, Hana,” he said, coming out from behind the counter towards Mikey’s bike in the corner of the shop. He kicked the stand away and began to roll the bike towards her. He pulled the key from her pocket, dangled it from his finger, and handed it to her. She took it and slipped it into her own pocket. “Do you want to pay cash or card?”

“Card, thanks,” she said, walking to the counter and pulling out her wallet. Luckily, she had thought ahead and brought both cards. She stared at the two black cards, trying to find the Nakatani Hana one. Finally she found it, took it out and held it over the machine. There was a small beep, and she pulled her hand back.

“Thank you for shopping at D&D Motors,” Draken said, bowing slightly. She gave him a smile with her eyes, then walked back to the bike, kicked the stand away and rolled the heavy machine out of the shop.

She rolled it off the footpath and onto the road, turned the key, and the engine roared to life. It sounded far better than it had earlier. She pulled her suit trousers up a little, swung her leg over the bike, sat with a leg on either side and tucked her platinum hair behind her ears. She was about to twist the throttle when Draken burst out of the shop, running towards her with a piece of paper in his hand.

“Hana! Wait!” he shouted, and she turned towards him and sat back up in the seat.

### Twenty One

“Did I forget something?” she asked, genuinely wondering whether she had left something behind in the store.

“No, no, nothing like that,” he huffed, relieved she hadn’t driven off yet. He stood tall at the edge of the footpath, looking down at her where she sat on the motorbike. He glanced around quickly. “You said Bonten comes to your club from time to time, right?”

She nodded. “Yeah. Why?”

“Can you give this to the boss?” Draken handed her a slip of paper, folded neatly.

“You do realize it could get me killed?”

“Surely not. It’s just paper. But tell him it’s from Draken, and that’ll surely stop you getting killed,” he said, laughing awkwardly, scratching the back of his neck and giving her a small smile. “Please. I haven’t spoken to him in ten years.”

She sighed deeply. Taking the letter wasn’t a huge task. If anything, it was an easy one. But she was worried about Mikey. If he got a letter from Draken, it might make him worse, and she was torn about what to do. Reluctantly, she held out her hand, and Draken placed the letter in it.

“Thanks, Hana. I owe you one,” Draken said. “He’s not going to reply, so you don’t have to worry about that.”

“I see,” she said quietly, and tucked the letter into her trouser pocket.

“Aren’t you going to wear a helmet? You really ought to,” Draken said, raising an eyebrow.

“Nah, I’m good. I know what I’m doing.”

Don’t want to hear that from someone who still does the same, she thought, laughing on the inside.

“Anyway, I’ve got to go. I’ll come back for another service when I need it,” she said, giving him a small smile with her eyes.

“Of course. See you around,” he replied, smiling back. She leaned forward, twisted the throttle, and the engine revved. She checked the right-hand mirror before pulling onto the main road. At the traffic lights she sat back up and planted one foot on the road, waiting for the light to change. A police car pulled up close beside her.

“You need to wear a—” She didn’t let him finish. She ignored the red light and shot forward, away from the police car. The sirens screamed behind her as it followed closely. She weaved between the cars, pulling further and further away. She checked the rear-view mirror and saw the police car in the distance. She took a sharp turn onto another main road that led onto the highway. She recognized the highway at once. After about ten minutes she took a small exit and dropped off onto the smaller roads. She knew the area like the back of her hand by now, having spent most of her teenage years living there. She slowed the bike to a stop and parked in a small covered area. She stepped off and looked at where she had ended up.

It was her old apartment, where she had lived with Sanzu for a couple of years, and where they had attended their first Christmas party. She smiled to herself as she walked round the building’s perimeter and climbed the stairs to the old front door. She stood in front of it while memories flowed in. Then she turned and looked out over the night sky and the small lights in the distance.

She walked back down the stairs to the bike. She had time to spare, so she decided to take a quick ride around the area. She started the engine and drove to the shrine where all her Touman adventures had begun. She parked at the bottom of the stone stairs and climbed the steep steps to the top, a little out of breath. She walked through the torii gate and made her way to the far end of the flat ground. Seeing no one, she went to the raised platform where Mikey often made his announcements. She sat on the top step, placed her hands behind her to prop herself up, and looked up at the dark sky, lit only by the full moon.

She remembered the letter in her pocket and took it out. Half of her wanted to give it to Mikey, and the other half wanted to burn it to keep him sane. She couldn’t decide, so she looked for a middle path. She unfolded the letter and read it.

Mikey,

Take care of yourself.

Draken.

Draken was a man of very few words, and it showed. A small smile crept onto her face. This was a message she could pass on to Mikey.

The ride back was peaceful. The moon was out, casting light onto the dim streets. The bike hummed beneath her as she rode back to the Bonten building, the wind pushing her hair back and kissing her face.

At the building she entered the garage, switched off the engine, pocketed the key and took the lift up to Mikey’s office. She knocked, got no answer, and pushed the door open a crack to peek in. Mikey was sitting in the dark at his desk, with only the desk lamp on over his paperwork. He hadn’t noticed her come in.

“Mikey,” she said as he lifted his head and searched for her. She walked to the desk and sat down opposite him.

“Akari, what’s up?”

“The motorbike is all good now,” she said, sliding the keys back across the desk. “You can keep the keyring.” She smiled at him and took off her mask.

“Cool. Thanks,” he said, taking the keys and putting them in his drawer.

“I went to D&D Motors like you asked. Draken recognised the bike straight away and thought of you, you know?” He looked at her with his dead eyes, though they were a little wider than usual. “He said: ‘Take care of yourself.’”

Mikey’s eyes widened even further, almost as round as the full moon she had just seen. He ducked his head back down and picked up his pen to carry on working. She stood, patted his head lightly and walked towards the door. “I think dinner will be ready soon, so come up later, okay?” She closed his office door behind her, went back to the lift and took it to the top floor.

The doors opened, and Ran’s voice flooded in. “—he had pissed his pants!” Laughter erupted as she walked round the couch towards the kitchen.

“Welcome back, Akari,” Kakucho announced, and the executives turned to look at her.

“Yeah, I’m home,” she said, taking the letter out of her pocket. “Omi, can you pass me your lighter?”

“Oh, sure.” He tossed it to her, and she caught it. She held the letter by the tips of her fingers over the sink and set the lighter under it. She flicked it on, and the flame lit up her face. The fire caught the edge of the paper, ran up towards her fingertips and blackened as it went.

“What are you doing?” Rindou asked, watching the paper burn.

“What does it look like?”

“Why, though?”

She didn’t answer for a while. She decided it was best to keep it to herself, so she gave Rindou a small smile. “Secret,” she teased, and dropped the burning paper into the sink. She watched it shrivel, darken and turn to ash. The smoke rose slowly and vanished, and she followed it with her eyes.

“Here you go,” she said, tossing the lighter back to Takeomi, who fumbled it. She picked up the ash with a damp tissue and threw it in the bin. “Someone make dinner, please. I’ll help.” The two brothers stood and headed into the kitchen.

“Nah, we’ll do it, don’t worry,” Rindou said, taking a frying pan off the shelf.

“Thanks, Ran, Rin,” she said, walking down the hallway into her room. Sanzu was sitting up in bed, reading a book.

“Oh, hey, sweetheart~” he said, putting the book down and holding out his arms.

She walked over, climbed onto the bed and crawled into his arms. He wrapped his arms round her and kissed the top of her head. “Strange to see you reading a book,” she laughed. “So? How are you feeling?”

“Much better. I think by tomorrow I’ll be okay to start walking around,” he said cheerfully.

“Don’t you dare start jumping and prancing around tomorrow, then,” she said, feeling his chest rise and fall as he laughed.

“I’ll think about it,” he answered.

“It isn’t something you have to think about,” she retorted, looking up at him. His eyes met hers, and he pressed a wet kiss to her forehead.

“Stay with me tomorrow,” he whispered into her ear, sending shivers down her spine.

“I’ve got work tomorrow evening. I have to pick up the car.”

“And assassinate xxx with Kakucho by the end of the week,” he cut in.

“Yeah, I’m doing your jobs,” she said, rolling her eyes.

“Think about the end result, though,” Sanzu said. “We’re going to the beach next week.”

“How exciting!” she said, smiling into his chest. He brushed her hair with his fingers, reached into the back of her shirt, pulled out her low ponytail, slipped off the hair tie and combed the strands out. “Anyway, Ran and Rin are making dinner, so let’s go,” she said, pushing away from him, helping him to his feet, and then carrying him over her shoulder towards the dining table.

“I’ve got a nice view of your ass from here,” he said, poking at it with a finger.

“Keep doing that, and I’m dropping you,” she said, and he stopped at once.

She woke the next morning to an empty bed and scuffling noises. She rubbed her eyes, sat up and looked round. She was a little surprised to see Sanzu half-dressed, sweatpants hanging low on his hips, a T-shirt round his neck and his pink hair falling around his shoulders.

“Morning?” she asked. He turned to face her at once. “You couldn’t wait, could you?” she sighed, swinging her legs over the edge of the bed.

“Nope, I really couldn’t,” he said with a cheeky grin, stepping towards her with great care, one step at a time. “Can you help with the shirt?”

She stood up sleepily, took the hem of the T-shirt and gave him enough room to thread his arms through. She pulled the shirt down over his belly, then lifted the edge to check the stab wound. It was stitched closed and a little raw and red, but healing well.

“Looking at my abs?” he snickered, with a teasing smile.

“I see enough of them every day.” She rolled her eyes. “I’m checking your wound, dumbass. Does it hurt?”

“Only with harsh movements. Quit staring now,” he chuckled, ruffling her already messy hair. She lowered his shirt and gave him a standing hug, which he returned, wrapping his arms carefully round her waist.

“Okay, let’s go and grab breakfast,” she suggested, pulling away from him. He let go but grabbed her hands, and she held on tightly while she helped him walk slowly down the hallway to the dining table.

“Morning, everyone,” she said, guiding Sanzu step by step to his seat. Takeomi and Mochizuki were making breakfast, and the rest of the executives sat at the table chatting and waiting.

“Morning, Akari. Sanzu,” Kakucho answered, watching her hold Sanzu up as he walked slowly.

“Good to see you walking again,” Rindou said quietly, without bothering to glance at Sanzu. She pulled out Sanzu’s chair, sat him down carefully and walked into the kitchen.

“Thanks, Omi, Mochi,” she said, smiling at them, leaning against the kitchen counter. “Need any help?”

Takeomi slid two plates towards her. “Can you take these to the table?”

“Sure.” She took the two plates and placed them on the table, as the executives went quiet and stared hungrily at the food. She went back for two more and kept walking back and forth until every plate was on the table. Then Mochi and Takeomi joined the others, and everyone dug in.

“Okay, let’s try the stairs to my floor,” she suggested as Sanzu stood up on his own and made his way towards the emergency staircase. She followed close behind in case he fell. She reached for the door handle, but he caught her hand and stopped her.

“I’ll do it.” She let go, and Sanzu twisted the handle slowly and pulled the door open. He leaned on the door a little, then walked through. She followed, watching every step he took.

“Wait. Hold on,” Sanzu said, stopping and grabbing the handrail. She rushed round in front of him and watched as he made his way down, gripping the railing. He reached the landing one floor down. “Try not to use the handrail this time,” she said, looking up at him. He nodded slowly and balanced himself on the stairs. He took one small step at a time until he reached the

next floor, and then the next, until they reached her floor. She pulled open the door, and Sanzu walked through much faster than before.

“Good job, babe,” she said, reaching up to kiss him softly on the lips. “You’ve already got better,” she said against his mouth, and walked towards her office. He followed, keeping up with her slow pace.

She held the office door open. He walked to the couch and almost fell onto it. She watched his body droop, and she snickered.

“What’s so funny?” he groaned, sprawling on the couch, his head on the armrest and his legs stretched out.

“Oh, nothing. But imagine being tired just from walking,” she said, sticking her tongue out at him. He glared at her playfully, then stuck his tongue out too. She walked over, took his tongue between her fingers and pulled it further out, which made him groan in surprise.

“Wa a yu doin?” (What are you doing?) he asked, unable to speak properly while she held his tongue. She just gave him a smirk. She leaned her face closer to his and blew air over it, making him flutter his eyes shut. Just as she was about to grab his tongue with her teeth, her phone buzzed in her back pocket. Sanzu heard it too and opened his eyes. She rolled her eyes, let go of his tongue, took out the phone and answered.

“Hello?”

“Hi, is this the owner of the car with the number plate GY-87-IH?”

“Yeah, that’s me,” she answered, glancing at Sanzu as he sat up on the couch.

“Your car is ready to be picked up. Please come within two hours.”

“Sure, be there soon. Thank you,” she said cheerfully, hung up and slid the phone back into her pocket.

“Who was it?” Sanzu asked, studying her face.

“Up for a walk?” she asked, with an evil smile. He groaned but rolled off the couch and dropped softly to the floor.

“Finee,” he whined, holding his arms up at her like a child wanting to be carried.

“Okay, let’s go.” She lifted him off the floor and helped him walk to the lift.

### Twenty Two

“Are we there yet~?” Sanzu whined as they walked slowly towards the car service station to collect the car.

“Another ten minutes at your speed,” she said, walking beside him. He groaned and slowed his pace even more. She stopped, turned, and watched him drag his feet across the floor. She sighed, put her hands on her hips and shook her head. Then she turned her back to him and crouched down.

“What?”

“We’re going to be late at your pace,” she said, ignoring the stares from the public, who were watching a pair of crazy people in suits. “Hurry up and get on,” she said, pointing her thumb over her shoulder. He stared at her back for a moment, glared at the people around them, then scrambled over and wrapped his arms round her neck and his legs round her waist. She slid her arms under his backside and stood up, jumping once to hoist him higher on her back.

“This feels weird,” he said, far too loudly into her ear. “It should be the other way round,” he went on as they walked down the road towards the station.

“Hurry up and get better, then,” she snapped, as he tightened his grip round her neck and dug his chin into her shoulder. He swatted her twin braids out of his face as they drooped over her chest.

“I’m trying~” he whined, pouting. She kept trudging down the road, and after a while of carrying Sanzu on her back, she finally reached the service station.

“Finally,” she huffed, sinking to the floor as he slid off her back.

“I should’ve told you to move your gun. It was rubbing against my dick and it hurts,” he groaned, leaning over.

She rolled her eyes. “You should’ve said something earlier, my god.” She walked over to the man with the clipboard at the front, who sat behind a glass window.

“Hi, I’m here to pick up my car. The licence number is GY-87-IH.”

“Oh, yes. Come this way,” he said, stepping out of his office and leading them to the car, which was waiting in an open area. He handed her the clipboard. “If you sign here and pay at the counter, you’re free to go.”

“Sure.” She signed with the blue pen attached, then took out her wallet and her black credit card and followed him back to the office. “Wait here for me, Sanzu,” she said. He just stood there, then walked back to the car.

“Can you tap your card here, please?” the man said, pushing the card machine towards her. She used her real credit card, not Hana’s, tapped it, heard the beep and put it back in her wallet. He took the machine back. “Do you want the receipt?”

“Yes, please.” She heard the receipt printing, and he shuffled around his office, then handed her the receipt and the car keys. “Thank you,” she said with a smile. He stared at the way her scar creased as she smiled, gave a short nod and went back to his work. She walked back to the car, where Sanzu was leaning on the bonnet with his arms crossed, glaring at the other workers.

She clicked the button on the keys, and the car unlocked, giving Sanzu a little jump. “Maybe let me know when you’re done,” he muttered, walking to the passenger side and sliding in. She got into the driver’s seat, shut the door and pushed the key into the ignition. The engine roared. She placed her hands on the wheel, pressed the accelerator and drove out of the service station. At a red light she squirmed in her seat, then tossed Sanzu her phone.

“Can you call Koko for me?” Sanzu unlocked her phone with his fingerprint and scrolled through her contacts.

“Love the nickname for him,” Sanzu snickered, pressing call. “‘Rich ass’ sounds about right.”

“What’s up, Akari?” Koko asked from the other end.

“Put it on speaker for me, Sanzu,” she said. Sanzu did as she asked.

The light turned green, but the cars in front hardly moved. “Hey, Koko, can you transfer about $3000 into my account?” The car in front barely shifted, so she leaned on the horn. “Hurry up and fucking move!” she yelled, and the car finally rolled forward.

“Why? And calm down. You’re busting my eardrums,” Koko said.

“Tch,” Sanzu clicked his tongue.

“Oh, hey, drug addict. Don’t be jealous again,” Koko teased, realizing Sanzu was listening in.

“I’ve got the receipt as proof if you want it. It’s for the car service,” she said, and she heard the faint tapping of keys from his side.

“No need for the receipt. I trust you,” he said, and then she heard the enter key pressed hard. “There. Five thousand is transferred. I didn’t give you the money for your suits last time, so there you go.”

“Thanks, Koko,” she said cheerfully.

“Anything else?”

“No,” Sanzu cut in, hung up and pouted.

She laughed at him, keeping her eyes on the road. “No need to be so jealous. Maybe if you’d quit buying drugs, you’d have more money in your account.”

“I did~” he whined, turning his head to look at her.

She glanced at him, one eyebrow raised. “Sure.”

“No. Sweetheart, you don’t understand. I actually did. Check my account if you don’t believe me.” She half believed him. “I’m trying to change for the future. The future we both want, and I know that’s the first step. So that’s what I’m doing.” He placed a hand on her thigh as she drove towards home.

She smiled at the road. “That’s so sweet, babe. Thank you.”

The second she drove into the garage, Kakucho was standing right where she was about to park, and she nearly ran him over. He knocked on the boot as she reversed, and she slammed on the brakes, convinced she had hit someone. She pulled up with her left hand on the handbrake and stuck her head out of the window.

“What the fuck, Kaku? You could’ve waited for me by the lift or something. I thought I’d run something over,” she breathed, glaring at him as he walked to her window.

“My bad. Anyway, we don’t have time to talk like this. xxxx has made his move, and we need to get him before we lose track of him again.” He opened the back doors and began shoving weapons into the car. Sniper, smoke canisters, a gun, grenades, you name it. “Sanzu, it’s up to you whether you come with us, but don’t hold us back.”

Sanzu didn’t move an inch. “I’m coming with you,” he said flatly, arms crossed over his chest.

“Okay, cool,” Kakucho answered quickly, shutting the back door and sliding into the back seat.

She released the handbrake, pressed the accelerator and turned towards the exit. She drove straight onto the main road, following Kakucho’s directions. She took the highway, and he pointed at the car ahead, checking his phone to be sure. “Yep, that’s the car.” He looked up at the navy car in front. She pressed the accelerator harder, but Kakucho held her back.

“Just follow them off the highway, and then we’ll launch.”

She eased off, dropping her speed a little and trailing the navy car by a few meters so as not to look suspicious. Soon the car took the exit into a suburban area and turned onto a larger road in the suburb. “Okay, now what?” she asked, following at a distance.

“Pull over,” Kakucho said, and she did. “The man we’ve been ordered to kill is about to enter one of the residential buildings. We need to kill him before he goes in. Clear?”

“So what are you suggesting?” She glanced round the area.

Kakucho pointed at the building beside them. It was tall. He reached down to the floor of the back seat, pulled up a slim black bag with a sniper inside and handed it to her. “Kill him before he enters the building. Once he’s dead, I’ll throw a smoke bomb as the signal to leave the roof. Come back to the car and leave. Clear?” She nodded. He gave her a communication earpiece.

“What do I do?” Sanzu asked, turning to look back at Kakucho.

“You’re injured. What more do you need to do but get better quickly?”

“Fine.” He leaned his head back against the passenger headrest. She leaned over to kiss his forehead, then swung open the driver’s door and left with the sniper bag. Kakucho got out too, with smoke bombs in his hands.

“Okay, see you later, you two,” she said, walking towards the tall residential building. She went round to the side and inspected the metal staircase attached to the wall. It didn’t reach the ground floor. She slung the sniper bag onto her back, reached up, jumped and caught the edge

of the metal base. She hooked one leg up onto the railing, then the other, released her hands and hung upside down. Doing a sit-up, she pulled herself up and slid in between the two railings. She stood, brushed the dust off her trousers and climbed the metal stairs, her heels clicking loudly on each step. At last she reached the roof. She put the earpiece in and spoke into it.

“Kaku, where?”

Kakucho’s voice came through the static. “Face north-east.” She did as he said, checked her shadow and turned 45 degrees to the right. She walked to the edge of the building, crouched down and unpacked the sniper. She set up the stand, clicked the sniper into place and attached the scope from the bag.

“Do you see the orange building?”

“Yep,” she said, spotting it.

“The one on your left. He should be going into that building in about—” He paused. “One minute.”

“Cool,” she said. “Basic description?”
