“He’s wearing a white suit. His men are in black. You can’t miss him.” She snickered quietly to herself.

“Are there any rules I have to follow?”

“Nope, as long as the mission is complete, nothing else matters.” Kakucho breathed out deeply, knowing exactly what she was thinking. “Don’t get too excited.”

She lay flat on the roof, propped herself on her forearms, squinted and looked through the scope with her right eye. She turned the scope to the orange building, then moved slowly across to the building on its left. She set the rifle over the edge and aimed it at the entrance. Sure enough, the navy car pulled up in front of the building. She zoomed in on the car door, which opened. A black suit stepped out, then a white one, then another black-suited man. She followed the man in the white suit, when a familiar figure walked up to him. Kakucho.

What the fuck?

She had no idea what he was doing, but she guessed he was buying her time to take the shot. She aimed at the head of the man in white, took a breath and pulled the trigger. Instantly, Kakucho had to catch the man as he fell forward onto him. The white suit was slowly soaking red. She swung the rifle onto the two men in black, who drew their guns and pointed them at Kakucho. She fired again, and one of the black suits dropped to the floor. The other swung his gun away from Kakucho once he realised it wasn’t Kakucho who had fired, and searched for the shooter. Kakucho dug into his pocket and pulled out a smoke bomb. Smoke filled the area outside the building at once. She packed the rifle back into its bag and raced down the stairs. She heard another gunshot as she went. At the bottom she hung over the edge and dropped

carefully. She sprinted to the car, threw open the door, slid into the driver’s seat and tossed the sniper at Sanzu, who was napping in the passenger seat. She floored the accelerator and drove back towards Kakucho.

“Akari. Don’t come here,” Kakucho’s voice said in her head.

“Then where?”

“Stay where you are. I’m nearly there.”

“Okay.” She let up on the accelerator and waited. Soon she saw him sprinting towards the car in the distance, with men chasing behind him. She shook Sanzu awake.

“Sanzu, shoot away.” He grinned widely, finally glad to be able to contribute. She drove closer to Kakucho and drifted the car, cutting off anyone behind him. While Kakucho scrambled into the car, Sanzu’s passenger window rolled down, and he fired five or so bullets at the men chasing Kakucho. She reversed quickly, turned the car round and drove off.

She let out a long sigh as they joined the highway. “What the fuck were you doing there?” she asked, breaking the silence.

“Me?” Kakucho asked, pointing at his chest, which she could see in the rear-view mirror.

“Yes, you! Who else?” she said, eyes on the road.

“Giving you time to shoot him.”

“You didn’t say that in the plan. I was fine without you,” she huffed, changing lanes. She glanced in the rear-view mirror again, then at the wing mirror, and spotted the navy car from earlier. “We’re being followed.”

“Geez, how many men have they got?” Sanzu sighed, reloading his gun. Kakucho did the same. The car was boxed in on three sides, with only the road ahead clear.

“Three cars. We can do it. Easy.” She smirked and tapped Sanzu’s thigh. He looked at her profile while she drove. She pointed at the glove box. He opened it and took out the only thing inside.

“Gum?”

“Yeah, can you give me one?” He opened the packet, took out a single piece and handed it to her. She unwrapped it one-handed, keeping her eyes ahead, and popped it into her mouth. Sanzu put the packet back in the glove box. She kept one hand on the wheel and reached behind her back with the other to pull out her gun.

“I’ll shoot the one behind us,” Kakucho said, winding down the back window. Sanzu did the same on his side.

“Shoot the wheel,” she said. Five gunshots rang out, and two cars skidded. Bullets smashed into the back and side of her car. The last car pulled up alongside them, and its occupants raised their guns at her. “Hold on!” she shouted, slamming on the brakes. The car skidded for several

meters, the smell of burning rubber filling the air, before the airbags exploded out. She shoved the airbag aside and saw the car slowing down to come at them again.

“Get ready,” Kakucho said, aiming at the car heading their way. “Step on it, Akari!” She did. They shot past the other car, exchanging a hail of bullets as they went, and she looked back to see them still following.

“Who’s got the best aim out of all of us?” she asked, but Kakucho and Sanzu just stared at her. “Oh, well. Um. Kakucho, swap seats with me.” Kakucho raised an eyebrow. She gripped the wheel with one hand and pulled the lever on the seat with the other, shoving it all the way back. Kakucho had no choice but to obey. He shuffled over and sat in the driver’s seat, trapping her between himself and the wheel. His legs slid alongside hers and took over the pedals one at a time. She was finally free. She swung her legs over Kakucho’s as they moved across to Sanzu’s lap.

“I’ve got the wheel. You can let go,” Kakucho said, and she nodded and let go. The car didn’t swerve at all, as he had it under control. She slid towards Sanzu and climbed off Kakucho’s lap. Sanzu pulled her gently in towards him, still glancing at the wing mirror at the car behind.

“Sanzu, where’s the sniper gun?”

### Twenty Three

He pointed between his legs, where the sniper bag was resting. She grabbed it and climbed into the back seat, unzipping the bag for the second time that day. She took out the rifle, rested it on the back seat and pointed it out of the rear window. She fired once at random, shattering the glass and giving a clear view of the car behind.

“Steady the car as much as you can. And speed up a bit,” she ordered, reloading the sniper quickly. She balanced the rifle on the back seat, resting one end on her shoulder. She looked through the scope and set the crosshair on the driver’s head. “Hold the car steady, right here.”

“There’s a small turn coming up, Akari. I can’t hold it straight much longer.”

“Drift the car, then,” she said coldly, chewing on the gum still in her mouth. She shut out everything: every sound, every distraction. She held the trigger, took a breath and pulled. The rifle kicked backwards as the car swerved suddenly, sending her rolling sideways into the door, the gun tumbling with her. The car balanced on two wheels for a second before crashing back onto all four. Kakucho jolted in his seat and stamped on the accelerator, driving away from the car, which had landed on its roof.

“Did you get them?” Sanzu asked, twisting round to look.

“See another car following?” she said from the floor of the car, gun in her arms, smiling up at him.

“I think that’s done,” Kakucho said, taking the exit off the highway.

“Finally. What a day,” she breathed, pulling herself off the floor and back into her seat, packing the sniper away.

“The car’s trashed now. So much for getting it serviced,” Sanzu said, pushing his fringe back from his face, but it fell straight over his forehead again.

“It’s time,” Kakucho said quickly, eyes on the road, as the other drivers stared at the bullet holes in the side of the car and the smashed back window.

“Time for what?” she asked, glancing behind them.

“Getting rid of the car, since it’s so banged up. I’m taking it to a scrapyard.” He took a turn off the exit and drove towards a very familiar place.

Kakucho stopped the car inside the scrapyard, the familiar one. They all got out. She grabbed everything, including the sniper bag and the packet of gum. Kakucho held up a grenade. “We’ll blow up the car. Cool?” She and Sanzu nodded and were already walking away. Kakucho waited until they were far enough away, then walked round to the front and back of the car, took the number plates, pulled the pin and tossed the grenade into the car. He ran to catch up with them and out through the gate.

Sanzu took her hand and held it tightly, rubbing his thumb across the back of it as the memories came flooding back. She pushed them to the edge of her mind, gave him a pained smile and walked carefully to the nearest train station on the way home.

She swiped her key card over the sensor, and the three of them stepped into the lift, which took them up to the top floor. She wobbled towards the couch with the sniper bag still on her back and fell face-first onto it. Sanzu followed, unclipped the bag from her back, dropped it on the floor and collapsed on top of her. She turned her head to the side so the leather couch wouldn’t suffocate her.

“Whatever happened to you guys?” Mochi asked, scratching his head before sitting at the far end of the couch.

“We need to buy another car. The one we used got trashed,” she mumbled, her cheeks squashed under Sanzu’s weight.

“Is it the car you just got serviced today?” Koko asked, closing his laptop. She hummed in reply.

“What a waste of money,” he muttered, and disappeared into his room.

“But these two have finished their jobs for this week and next, so they’re free for the beach,” Kakucho said, sitting on the chair by the dining table with his chin on one knee.

“Yayy,” Sanzu groaned, his jaw moving against her shoulder blades as he spoke. He snuggled into her back until he found a better spot, then went still, letting his arms fall to her sides.

The lift chimed open, and Mikey, the brothers and Takeomi walked in. She followed them with her eyes. Takeomi glanced at the two of them and at Kakucho, then switched on the TV on the

wall. The news reporter was back, ironically talking about the three crashed cars in the middle of the highway.

“We were late for our meeting because of this,” Mikey said, pointing at the TV with his eyes.

“Oopsies~” she said from under Sanzu. He gave her a quick look, then his eyes travelled up to Sanzu’s figure on top of her.

“Nowhere that you need to concern yourself with,” she said, pulling out her gun and pointing it at his head before she pulled the trigger. He fell to the floor, and the other men turned. Two more came running at her, and she shot them too, leaving their bodies for Hanma to deal with.

Payback, bitch.

Finally, the men left her alone, and she walked confidently to the exit. The doors slid open, and the cool night air filled her lungs. She didn’t want to disturb the other executives to come and pick her up, so she decided to make her own way home. She braided her hair into two, out of the public’s eye, and walked to the nearest train station. Watching her surroundings, she arrived at the station, tapped her black card on the scanner, and the gates parted to let her through. She walked down the concrete stairs to the platform. She waited in the line marked by

colored tape on the floor, watched a train arrive, saw the passengers get off and waited for it to leave. A couple of minutes later, a second train came in and spilled out its passengers. The line moved forward, and the people in front boarded and took their seats. She walked to the door on the far side of the carriage, leaned against the glass and stared out at the darkness of the underground tunnels. The doors beeped shut, and the train rattled forward towards the next stop. The carriage filled up as it went. She was staring out of the window when she noticed a middle-aged man with rectangular glasses inching closer and closer to her.

The train lurched hard, and the passengers swayed. The man took the chance to lean towards her, pushing her against the doors. She felt his hand grope her backside briefly before he pulled it away, making it look accidental. She turned to face him, and his expression said it all when he realized he had messed with the wrong woman. She gave him an evil smile, the corners of her lips lifting, the scar stretching as she did, her eyes narrowing. He backed away, but the train had other plans and threw him back towards her. He was falling into her again, but she caught him by the collar.

“Oh, my apologies,” she said in a sweet voice, letting go of his shirt. He fell forward and cracked his head against the door. The glass shook at the impact, and the other passengers turned to look. She crouched down to his level and helped him up. The train was nearing her station, so it was the perfect moment. She faced the doors, and he was facing the other way. She placed a light hand on his shoulder. He flinched under her touch, and she whispered a few words in his ear.

“Don’t harass women, or you’ll see the end,” she said, and the doors opened just in time for her to step out and leave the horrified man standing in the carriage.

She strutted up the stairs and out of the familiar station towards the Bonten building. She entered the garage, swiped her card key on the lift reader and rode up to the top floor. The lift stopped at one floor, and the doors opened on Kakucho.

“Oh, Akari.” He stepped in beside her. “How’d it go?”

“I don’t remember telling you where I went, but anyway. It went well, I guess. I saw Hanma for the first time in, what, twelve years? He seemed the same, still as annoying as ever,” she said. He chuckled softly.

“That’s good. He was the one behind the murders of the women, right?” She nodded. “Did you do anything?”

“Nah, not really. Mikey gave me the choice to kill him or not, but I feel like he’ll be of use to me in the future,” she said as the doors parted and they walked out. Kakucho went quietly to his room. It was late, so the living quarters were empty and silent. She walked softly to the kitchen, took some leftovers from the fridge and reheated them in the microwave. The microwave beeped loudly when the timer finished, so she opened the door quickly to avoid waking anyone. She took the food out carefully, put it on the kitchen counter and took out some cutlery. She sat down at a random seat at the dining table, taking bites while she looked out of the window at the Tokyo skyline at night. She was so absorbed in the view that she didn’t

notice a figure creeping closer. She put a mouthful of food into her mouth, and felt a tap on her left shoulder. It startled her so badly that she turned sharply and jumped out of her seat.

It was Mikey. He was breathing hard, panting and pale.

“M-Mikey? Are you okay? What happened?” She put a hand to his forehead, then to her own, and realized he was running a fever. He was burning up. She helped him down into the chair she had been sitting in. She rushed to the bathroom and came back with a small hand towel. She soaked it under cold running water, wrung it out, folded it and placed it on Mikey’s forehead, tilting his head back. “Can you stay here for a minute? I’ll be right back.” He let out a small grunt. She rushed to her room and quickly changed into more comfortable clothes. She didn’t realize that she was changing in front of Sanzu, who was resting on the bed.

“Sweetheart, do you know what you’re doing to me?” he asked, blinking to make sure he wasn’t dreaming.

“Babe, not now. Mikey’s running a fever,” she said quickly, throwing her suit onto a hanger and hurrying back out to where Mikey sat. She left Sanzu in the bedroom so quickly that her words didn’t have time to sink in. But it wasn’t long before he followed her out to check on his boss.

By the time she got back to the dining table, Mikey had got a lot worse. He was wheezing and sweating but shivering too, his skin pale and cold, and his dark circles were even more prominent. “Mikey, when was the last time you ate a proper meal?”

He wheezed out his answer in broken breaths. “This… morning… for… breakfast.” She crouched down to his level and reached for his neck, feeling softly for his pulse. It was faster than she liked, but it wasn’t too bad, and she breathed a small sigh of relief. She took the towel from his forehead and handed it to Sanzu, who had been watching everything. He hurried to the kitchen to wet it again.

“What do you think caused the fever?” she asked calmly, putting a hand on his thigh to let him know she was with him. He kept his eyes shut and squeezed them tighter as he worked through her words.

“I-I don’t know?” he stammered, pressing a hand to his bare forehead. Sanzu came back, squeezed the towel dry, moved Mikey’s hand away and laid the towel back. Mikey let out a long sigh, feeling much calmer with it back in place.

“Are you working yourself to the bone? Is that why? Or a bug or a virus or something?”

“I really don’t know.” He opened his eyes and looked at her with his blank stare. His gaze roamed the room, trying to focus on something, but he couldn’t. Headaches and dizziness, she guessed.

She stood up and motioned to Sanzu. “Can you carry him to his room for me?” Sanzu nodded and took Mikey to his room almost at once. She turned on the stove and heated up a packet of shop-bought pumpkin soup, then poured it into a bowl. She took a spoon and a tray and put the spoon and bowl on it. She opened one of the kitchen drawers, took out the medicine box,

pulled out an antibiotic tablet and filled a glass of water, then put them on the tray too. She carried it to Mikey’s room, nudging the door with her foot until it opened. Sanzu let her in. She set the tray on the messy table and pushed the papers aside carefully. She knelt beside the bed.

“Mikey, I need you to eat the soup before you take the medicine. You can’t take medicine on an empty stomach.” She passed him the bowl. He stared at her for a moment, then at the bowl, and took it from her. She watched him eat until every drop was gone, then handed him the tablet and the glass of water. He swallowed the pill easily and handed the half-full glass back to her.

“Thanks, Akari. Sanzu,” he said softly, letting his head sink into the pillow with a heavy sigh. She took the towel back from Sanzu, who hurried back to the kitchen. She pressed her hand to Mikey’s forehead to check his temperature, but it was much the same.

“Akari.”

“Yeah?”

“Can you stay here with me for the night?” he huffed, turning his head towards her, his eyes half open.

She gave him a small smile. “I was planning to, even if you hadn’t asked.” She leaned over and pulled the blanket up to his neck. “Don’t hesitate to tell me if you need anything else, okay?”

“Yeah…” he squeaked, turning his head back to the ceiling. Sanzu came back into the room with the towel and a bucket of water this time. Smart thinking. He placed the towel gently over Mikey’s forehead, then sat down next to her. She scooted closer and rested her head on his shoulder, feeling his arms wrap round her waist. They heard Mikey’s breathing slow and even out. He had fallen asleep. She smiled, and Sanzu felt her jaw move.

“Good to see you again, sweetheart,” he whispered, pressing a kiss to her head.

“I’m home,” she whispered back, snuggling closer. He tightened his arms, lifted her off the floor and settled her between his legs, crossing his arms under hers and resting them on her stomach. She leaned into his chest, soaking up his warmth, and felt herself drifting off.

She woke at about four in the morning to the sound of movement in the room. Sanzu was still asleep, holding onto her. The noise came from Mikey, who was sitting up in bed, staring blankly at her and Sanzu. “You okay, Mikey?”

He didn’t say anything, just kept staring at them. She freed one arm from Sanzu’s grasp and waved it in front of Mikey’s face. He snapped out of his trance, shook his head once and turned back to her with those dead eyes. “Sorry about this,” he whispered, and let out a small sneeze.

“Bless you,” she answered, as Sanzu tightened his grip on her and woke up too. “Don’t worry about it, Mikey. Being sick is something that happens to everyone.” She gave him a reassuring smile, but she felt a small itch in her nose. It was coming for her too.

### Twenty Six

Just as she had predicted, she lay in bed with the blanket pulled up to her neck, sweating and freezing at the same time. She was breathing like she had just run a marathon, panting hard. Every time she closed her eyes, odd shapes ran past her vision. She tried to follow them, but they always slipped out of reach. When she opened her eyes, they watered and blurred, and tears spilled for no reason, and she couldn’t focus on anything. Her head pounded. She could feel every beat of her heart.

Every now and then she sensed someone coming in and out of the room to change the wet towel on her forehead. She heard rustling clothes each time, and it annoyed her, because her hearing was extremely sharp with the fever. She drifted in and out of consciousness, so her sense of time was badly scrambled.

Sanzu POV

It had been about two days since Mikey fell sick. He was completely fine now, but Akari had caught the cold from him, and she was suffering badly. The cold seemed able to spread to the others, so Sanzu had to take precautions to stop the other executives and himself from getting it too.

“How’s she doing?” Mikey asked, with a guilty look on his face.

“She’s okay. I think she’ll be fine in another two days or so,” Sanzu answered, pulling a surgical face mask over his nose and mouth. He handed Mikey a mask too, and Mikey put it on before they both went in to check on her. She turned her head towards the door at once, but her eyes were glazed and staring at nothing in particular. Sanzu sat down on the floor beside her bed, took the towel from her forehead, dipped it in the bucket, wrung out the excess and laid it back on her forehead. She let out a long sigh of relief and turned her head back to the ceiling. He pushed the water bucket aside, leaned over and wiped the sweat and tears from her face, then stood up. Mikey watched from the corner of the room, worried and guilty. They left the room together, closing the door softly behind them. They pulled their masks down under their chins and walked back to the kitchen. Mikey sat in his usual spot on the leather couch, and Sanzu took out the medicine box and the antibiotics.

He opened the pantry and dug around until he found a can of soup. He grabbed a knife from the drawer, held the can still with one hand, and stabbed the top with the knife, making a slit.

“Just use a can opener,” Takeomi said, staring at him.

Sanzu clicked his tongue. “Can’t fucking find it,” he snapped, pouring the soup into a pot on the stove to heat it. He set the knife and the empty can down on the counter and stirred the pot with a wooden spoon when he heard the bedroom door creak open. He rushed over, leaving the soup unattended, and pulled on his mask. Akari was leaning against the doorway for support.

“Akari, what are you doing? Go back to bed,” he said, steering her back towards her bed.

“No,” she said, pushing against his chest and trying to make her way to the dining area. “I want to move around.” He looked at her with worried eyes. She couldn’t see much, by the look of it. Her eyes were still watering and wouldn’t focus. He could see them darting around in their sockets at any movement.

He sighed in defeat and helped her towards the dining table. “I’m going to get you to eat, alright?” She nodded and leaned into him as he guided her. He pulled out a chair and helped her sit before going back to the kitchen. The pot was empty, but a bowl and a spoon were already laid out on the counter for him to give her. He glanced at the leather couch, and Takeomi gave him a small smile. Sanzu ignored it, though he was grateful as he carried the bowl to the table. She stared blankly at it, her eyes moving quickly from side to side. He dipped the spoon, watched her eyes follow the movement, and lifted it to her lips. She turned her head towards him and leaned in, closing her lips over the spoon. He pulled it out and dipped it again. He kept going until the soup was gone. He carried the bowl back to the sink, then brought the antibiotics and a glass of water and handed them to her. She gulped down the water and the pill at once, then stood up suddenly and stumbled towards the couch.

Sanzu followed her and sat beside her. She leaned her head on his shoulder and glared at Takeomi, who was sitting opposite. He squirmed in his seat under her stare. Sanzu tried hard not to laugh, shaking in his seat, but Akari slapped him across the chest. He looked down, and she gave him the same look she had been giving Takeomi. She turned, lay down and rested her head on his lap, swinging her legs off the edge of the couch. “Thanks for looking after me, babe,” she murmured, and closed her eyes with a relaxed look on her face. Sanzu stroked the top of her head while she slept and let out a huge sigh of relief that she had finally fallen asleep.

“You’ve done well,” Takeomi said quietly. Sanzu gave him a blank stare. “What?”

“Nothin’,” Sanzu spat, turning to stare out of the window. “Don’t you have anything better to do?”

“He has a free day today,” Mikey answered for Takeomi, without taking his eyes off Akari’s sleeping figure.

“Oh, perfect. Go shopping for food, then,” Sanzu said, handing his brother the shopping list. Takeomi read down the list and looked up. “All of this?”

“Nah, only one item. What do you think?” Sanzu answered with sarcasm, rolling his eyes.

“Kitchen knives? Soda? Tea?” Takeomi read out loud. “Why do we need ten kitchen knives?”

“Oh, that’s for me,” Sanzu smirked, remembering one of the traitors downstairs on one of the floors, currently bleeding out.

“Keep it as clean as possible, Sanzu,” Mikey said, breaking his train of thought.

Sanzu just stared at him. “Sorry, but I think it’s a bit too late for that.” Mikey shrugged and looked out of the window. Sanzu looked down at Akari, breathing peacefully in his lap, and smiled at her relaxed state.

TWO DAYS LATER

The sound of the bedroom door opening brought worry and dread, and the sound of feet tapping quickly on the floor came rushing towards him. He turned round and saw Akari launching herself at him. His eyes widened as he dropped the knife he was holding and caught her in his arms.

“Let’s not do that when I’m holding a knife, okay, sweetheart?” he said into her neck, kissing it tenderly, grateful that she was fully healed. Since she had been sick, he had kept away from her to avoid passing germs, which meant no kissing either. It was good that she was back to normal.

“Okayyy,” she said, squeezing his waist with her legs. She nuzzled into his shoulder, leaned back and gave his nose a quick peck. She glanced at the floor, at the knife on the counter and the half-cut apple.

He noticed her gaze. “Want a slice?” She nodded, slid off him, picked up the knife, rinsed it under the tap and handed it back to him. She sat on the couch and watched him cut the apple into slices. He put the slices on a plate and brought them over to her. Ran appeared out of nowhere, swiped two slices and handed one to his brother.

“Fuck you, Haitani,” Sanzu spat, glaring at him. Ran gave him a playful smirk and disappeared into the lift with his brother.

“Thanks, babe.” She took a slice and popped it into her mouth in one go. “And thanks for taking care of me when I was sick,” she went on, with her mouth full.

“No problem, sweetheart. But speak when your mouth isn’t full, please.” She nodded and reached for another slice. Mikey came out of the lift, tapped her head and sat down on the couch.

He fumbled with his fingers, hesitating, but got there in the end. “Thanks for taking care of me, and I’m sorry for giving you the cold, Akari,” he said quickly.

“Ahh, don’t worry about it. It happens,” she replied coolly. A phone ringing broke the awkward moment. Mikey answered and spoke into it. It sounded serious. Soon he hung up and looked at the two of them.

“I don’t want to do this, but I have no choice.” He glanced at Akari, who had another slice stuffed in her mouth, then at Sanzu. “One of the Bonten under-workers has betrayed us and is on the loose. We have information that they’re planning to meet with Ichthus to sell us out. Ichthus has agreed to meet them at the five-star restaurant in the centre of Tokyo. Luckily for us, Ichthus is ‘partially’ on our side. I need the two of you to pretend to be a couple eating at the restaurant—”

“Ichthus’s boss is going to be there?” Sanzu asked, raising an eyebrow at the new name. “Is that a new gang?”

Akari turned and looked at him. “You weren’t there, because you were with Ashinuke, but Ichthus is Hanma’s new gang. They came into power through prostitution, so they’re quite a force to be reckoned with. Wait. So Hanma’s going to be there?” She turned back to Mikey, who nodded.

“As much as I hate him, it’s better for us this way. He already knows most of the Bonten members, and we don’t have to worry about him selling us out, since he’ll rat himself out in the process. It’s a stalemate, if anything,” Mikey said coldly.

“Oh yeah, I forgot to mention last time, but Hanma seemed interested in partnering up. He was keen on us switching our prostitute sellers to his gang,” Akari said, catching Sanzu by surprise.

He turned to her with a sharp look. “You met up with him? When?”

“The night Mikey got sick. Anyway, what time is their reservation?” she asked, glancing at the clock on the wall.

“Tonight at ten. I expect you both to be there in formal attire. The reservation is under yours, Sanzu. Is everything clear?” Akari and Sanzu both nodded.

“Is there a specific way we’re supposed to kill him?” Sanzu asked.

“There’s a single waitress working for Ichthus, just for that night. No witnesses. So run wild,” Mikey said. Akari and Sanzu exchanged looks, smiled at each other, and left the couch for their room to get ready.

In their room, Akari pulled out one of the few dresses she owned. “How’s this one?” she asked, holding it against her body. He looked her over from head to toe and considered it for a while.

“What do you think about matching me?” he asked, with a playful smirk. She stared at him blankly for a second, then smiled widely, on board with the idea. She put the dress back on the rack, left the room and disappeared for a moment. While she was gone, Sanzu changed into his usual deep purple suit and tugged at the waistband of the trousers. He took a white dress shirt from the hanger, pulled his arms through and buttoned up the front, then put the pink tie round his neck, waiting for her to come back and tie it for him. He set his purple leather shoes out, slipped on some socks and put his shoes on. Akari burst through the door, holding a different dress.

“I forgot about this one. What do you think?” she said, standing tall and holding it against her body. The color was perfect, a much lighter shade of his suit, and it matched well.

“I think that’s the one, sweetheart~” he said, giving her an encouraging nod. He pulled the tie from his neck and handed it to her.

“C’mere,” she said, placing the dress on the bed and taking the tie from his hands. He crouched so she could tie it properly. He felt her lift his collar, loop the tie round his neck, pull the collar back down and tighten the knot. She gave his chest a light tap. He stood, pulled on his waistcoat, buttoned it up and folded his jacket over his forearm.

He sat on the bed and watched Akari change into her dress. She pulled her sweatpants down and dug through her drawer for a pair of sports shorts, slipping them on. She tugged at the waistband, which hugged her waist tightly and outlined her hips. Then she pulled a pair of flower-shaped adhesive covers from a drawer.

“What’s that?” he asked, with no idea what they were for.

She removes her bra and turns her back to him.

"Nipple covers," Is all she answered before she turns back around. Sure enough, the black flowers were covering her nipples.

Sanzu’s eyes, however, were drawn to the Bonten tattoo just beneath the collarbone and above her nipple covers.

She unzipped the back of her dress, stepped into it and adjusted the straps. She came over to him. “Can you zip it up for me?”

He took hold of the zip and pulled it up slowly until it wouldn’t go any further. “Done,” he said, pressing a soft kiss to her shoulder blade. She shivered at the touch, turned round and kissed him back, sloppily, on the lips. She rushed out of the room towards the bathroom, and he pushed himself up off the bed and followed. He found her leaning over the sink, pressed as close to the mirror as she could, curling her lashes. He leaned against the doorframe and watched her go through mascara, eyeliner and whatever else she did. She put on a light pink lipstick and pressed her lips together to spread it evenly. She brushed out her hair, braided the top half, tied off the ends, then gathered everything into a low bun, with the braids framing the sides of her head.

“You look beautiful, sweetheart~” he said, and her face lit up in a wide smile.

“You look handsome as well, babe,” she replied with a wink. It gave him butterflies, but he didn’t tell her that. “Shall we go?” She rushed back to the bedroom and came out with a small purse and her white high heels in her hands. He nodded. They walked to the lift and pressed the button, waiting for it to come up. The doors opened, and the two brothers stepped out.

“Where are you two going?” Ran asked, glancing at them, mainly at Akari.

“Date night,” Akari answered quickly, pulling Sanzu into the lift by the arm and waving at the brothers as the doors closed. She pressed the button for the weapons floor. “What do you think we’ll need?”

“Just the usual, I think,” Sanzu answered as they walked out into a room of weapons. He grabbed his usual kit, and Akari did the same, then fitted a silencer to her gun the way she always did. She slid in a fresh magazine and aimed at the target on the wall. He watched her face turn serious before she took a quick breath. Her hands were incredibly steady as she pulled the trigger and punched a hole right through the middle of the target. He applauded her skill, then followed her back out and towards the lift. In the garage, he slipped into the unlocked car and took the driver’s seat. Akari noticed and slid into the passenger seat.

“Are you going to leave that on show?” he asked, pointing at her Bonten tattoo. Her eyes went wide as she realized her mistake. She glanced at the clock on the dashboard: 9:45 pm.

She shuffled out of the seat and swung the door open. “I’ll be right back!” she shouted, disappearing into the lift. He kept his eyes on the clock as the minutes ticked by. Five minutes later, the lift doors opened, and Akari finally sat back in the car. He started the engine and drove towards the five-star restaurant.

He parked the car, and they walked side by side towards the entrance. As they approached, his eye was caught by a man already seated by the window, overlooking the Tokyo skyline at night, with another man beside him. Hanma Shuuji. He noticed their arrival and sent Sanzu a sly smirk.

### Twenty Seven

Akari POV

As she stepped through the entrance, she was taken aback by the sheer detail and ‘luxury’ of the place. Even though she had plenty of money herself, she had never been one to indulge in things she had no use for. Ancient Chinese vases sat on smooth marble pillars along the walls, and historic artworks hung between them. The ceiling was crowned with intricate detail, some of it so small she couldn’t make out what it was. In front of her stood a young woman she assumed was one of the waitresses. She was the picture of what society calls beautiful: smooth pale skin, wavy brown hair and large round brown eyes. Her uniform suited her perfectly, shaping her figure just right.

“Good evening. Can I take your name for the reservation, please?” she asked, in a voice any ordinary man would fall for. She looked at the two of them and then down at her clipboard.

“Haruchiyo, thanks,” Sanzu answered, and the waitress ran her finger down the list until she found his name.

“Busy night tonight?” Akari asked.

The waitress found the name and ticked it off before leading them to a table. “Not too busy today,” she said, pointing at their table and pulling out Akari’s chair. Akari grabbed her hand and whispered into her ear.

“You’re part of Ichthus, I assume,” she whispered, and the waitress froze. “I hope you’re aware of tonight’s situation?” The waitress gave a quick nod. Akari let go of her arm and spoke at normal volume, as if the whispered exchange had never happened. “Can I order a bottle of champagne before we order our main? Thank you,” she announced a little too loudly, and some heads turned. The waitress left at once, and Akari looked across at Sanzu, sitting opposite.

Sanzu was staring up at the golden chandelier glowing in the warm yellow light. He noticed her stare, put his elbows on the table and propped his head up with his hands. “Anything wrong?” he asked, raising an eyebrow.

She glanced at Hanma and the traitor, sitting by the window. “I just wish this wasn’t a mission. It would’ve been nice to go out, just the two of us, a proper date night,” she said, sighing and turning back to him.

He gave her a small, cheeky smile. “We can go somewhere after the mission?” His voice rose slightly. She felt her face flush at the idea.

“Can we?” she said excitedly. He nodded, and a smile spread across his face too.

The waitress interrupted the happy moment by placing a champagne bottle on the table with two tall, narrow glasses, rounded at the base and made of crystal. She opened the bottle with a small knife she kept in her apron, slicing from under the cork to the top. The cork flew off, white vapor drifted up for a second and then dispersed. She poured a glass, letting the drink run down the edge so it bubbled up gently, and slid it to Akari. Then she poured another and passed it to Sanzu. She set the half-empty bottle at the far edge of the table, stepped back and took out her notepad.

“Would you two like to order?”

Akari picked up the menu, scanned it and pointed at one of the dishes. “I’d like one of these, thanks.” She passed the menu to Sanzu, who closed it without looking.

She rolled her eyes, and he sat back down as the traitor carried on talking to him about the price for handing over information about the Bonten members.

Honestly, the traitors needed to do a better job. The executives always gave their orders by message, so they had never seen the underlings, and the underlings had never seen them. But Takeomi kept paperwork in his office on every underling, so finding this traitor wasn’t hard, not when they had all his personal details. “Now go. You have work to do,” Mikey said, ushering them out of his office.

Akari was on the couch, head back, staring at the ceiling and sighing. She waited for time to pass until it was late enough to change into her bartending uniform, since tonight was a Sunday. She was more than excited about the beach trip with all the Bonten members, and she had everything packed and ready in her room, but waiting was harder than she’d expected. This time she had checked the weather, and it pleased her that it would be beautiful all week. She was so lost in thought that she didn’t notice the lift open behind her, or Koko and Rindou walking out.

A sharp flick of a finger landed on her forehead. She sat up at once, one hand over the spot, and turned to face the two men standing in front of her. “Guess who?” Koko asked, scoffing and holding in a laugh.

“Real nice, Koko,” she pouted, rubbing the red mark in the middle of her forehead. “Haven’t seen you guys much. Are you excited for tomorrow?”

“Yeah, I guess so. It’ll be a nice, well-earned break,” Koko said, stretching his arms behind his back.

“My pocket feels much lighter, though. It cost quite a bit.”

“You went with Kakucho and Mochi and scared the guy selling the place. Akari, it was 75% off for us,” Rindou explained, looking at Koko and her. She laughed out loud at the story.

“Better for us, and for your pocket, then,” she said, poking Koko.

“Also, please do something about Ran,” Koko said, turning to Rindou.

“Oh yeah, he’s still sulking,” Rindou said, shaking his head. She scoffed and crossed her arms. “I don’t know what happened, he won’t tell me.”

“He can apologise first. I’m not doing shit,” Rindou said.

“What’d he even do?” Koko asked, sitting opposite her on the couch, with Rindou beside him. They were trying to squeeze the gossip out of her.

“He didn’t knock on the door. Sanzu and I were changing after we came back, on the morning after the mission.”

“Oh, I’ve heard you two had a ‘fun’ time,” Rindou said, raising an eyebrow and smirking.

“From who?”

“My lips are sealed.” That earned a scoff from her.

“Anyway. I got mad and said that was the reason I preferred Rindou over Ran. And now he’s sulking.” Rindou and Koko exchanged looks and covered their mouths to stop laughing.

“I didn’t think he’d be that lame,” Koko said, calming himself down.

“That’s a bit rude, doncha think?” Ran’s voice echoed from down the hall. He appeared in the kitchen, noticed her on the couch, stuck his tongue out at her in spite, then left for his room with a glass of water.

“He’s such a child sometimes,” she sighed, leaning back into the couch.

“You’re still the youngest of all of us,” Rindou said quickly.

“I heard that from Ran a while back. I don’t need another reminder…”

Koko stood and headed for the kitchen. “As much as I think this argument is stupid, I can’t be bothered dealing with it for the whole week at the private beach, so I’m going to convince him to apologise.”

“Ohhhh, thanks, Koko, you’re the best!” she exclaimed, clapping her hands together. She glanced at the clock and saw it was four. “Oh, time for me to go. If you need me, call me. I’ll have my Bonten phone with me tonight.”

“Ran might come down to apologise if it goes well,” Rindou called after her, as she got up and followed Koko down the hall. She went into her room to change into her uniform.

She was working the bar beside Yuki, with the music booming and the screams and laughter of the dancers bouncing off the walls. She pushed a drink to a customer on a barstool, turned her back on the crowd to prepare the next one. Yuki handed her a bottle of gin and a fresh shaker with ice already inside, and she handed Yuki the old one. As she poured the gin into a glass, her phone vibrated in her pocket. She passed Yuki the shaker and the glass, pointed at her phone, and Yuki nodded. She weaved through the crowd and pushed out of the main doors. It was quiet for once, probably because it was only ten. A motorbike rumbled past as she answered the call.

“Yes?”

“Hey, love. I just wanted to say I’m sorry.” Ran’s voice was so quiet it was almost inaudible.

“Mhm, okay. Anything else?”

“I’ll knock on the door next time,” he said, still speaking softly.

“Okay, apology accepted.” She smiled behind her mask and laughed a little at how slowly he was talking. “Anyway, I’ll see you tomorrow. Make sure you get ready for tomorrow and the week ahead!”

He laughed at her excited tone. “Of course. I’m already packed. Got my swimmers and drinks and everything.”

“I love how we’re on similar wavelengths. But hopefully the beach has shops nearby, because we need to go shopping.”

“I’ll do some research, then,” Ran said, and she heard the faint tapping of a keyboard on his end.

“I’ve got to go back to work, catch you later!” She hung up, pushed back through the main doors and walked round the club, collecting used glasses and wiping down the tables. She tucked a tray under her arm, loaded the glasses onto it and carried it back to the bar. Yuki noticed her and tapped her shoulder, giving her the signal under the counter. She turned towards the VIP door and sighed when she saw who it was.

She walked over with heavy steps, muttering curses under her breath. “Hey, Hanma,” she said, rolling her eyes.

“That’s a wonderful way to treat your customers, Akari,” he replied, chuckling heartily.

“I go by Hana here, so please don’t expose me,” she spat, punching the code into the VIP door.

“No.” He said it quickly, as she opened the door and ushered them in.

“No?”

“This is Hana. I ain’t calling—”

“Okay, okay, I get it.” She turned to Hana. “I’m so sorry you have to be with a dick like him.”

“Oh, no. He’s great, please don’t say things like that about him,” Hana said softly, gripping his large hands.

“I heard you had a great time with Sanzu a couple of nights ago,” Hanma teased, winking at her with a smirk.

She sighed deeply and pushed the two of them into a VIP room. “Please stay out of my private life, Hanma. Anyway, clean up after yourselves when you’re done. I don’t want to clean up after you. Again. And when you’re finished, put the red hanger on the door handle. If you do anything stupid, I won’t hesitate to kill you, or get someone from Bonten to shoot you both, so—”

“Okay, okay. I get it, now shoo,” he said, ushering her out and locking the door at once. Almost immediately, loud breathing and kissing noises came through the door. She gagged a little and rushed back into the club.

She woke to violent shaking at seven in the morning. Rubbing her eyes, her head lolling, she felt strong hands rocking her. “Okay, I’m awake. You can stop shaking me now, Sanzu.”

“Wrong person, Akari.”

Her eyes snapped open, and she screamed. Heavy footsteps sounded outside, and the bedroom door burst open as Sanzu rushed in. “What happened?!” he asked, worried by her scream.

“Why is your brother waking me up in the morning?!” she groaned, clutching her head.

“I was busy getting both our luggage to the main area, so I asked him. Everyone except us and Mikey has already left, about an hour ago.” Sanzu took her hand and pulled her up to sit on the bed. A soft knock on the doorframe came from behind the three of them. Mikey stood there, sleepy-eyed, clutching his shirt, his hair a mess.

“What happened?” he asked, yawning.

“Sorry to wake you up, Mikey. I’m guessing we’re late, so let’s leave in about fifteen minutes?” The men nodded. “Sorry for my reaction, Omi. I just didn’t expect it,” she said. Takeomi laughed and stood up.

“Don’t worry, I don’t think it’s the first time it’s happened,” he said, leaving the room with Sanzu. Mikey stayed in the doorway, looking at her on the bed.

She gave him a small smile. “Want me to brush your hair out, Mikey?” He nodded timidly, sat on the edge of her bed and turned his back to her. She grabbed the hairbrush from the bedside table and brushed his hair gently. She felt his body sink into the bed as he leaned into the brush. After a few strokes, his hair was much flatter than it had been when he woke up. She tapped his shoulder, and he stood and walked out, muttering a small “thank you.”

She changed out of her nightwear into warm, comfortable clothes, then stepped out of the bedroom with a hair tie. She walked into the living area, tying her hair into a low, loose ponytail, and bumped her head into Sanzu’s broad back. “Let’s go?” he asked, and she nodded against his back. He turned round, kissed her forehead, lifted her onto his back and carried her to the lift, where the luggage was waiting. He rolled the luggage in with his feet, step by step, while carrying her. Takeomi and Mikey joined them in the lift with their own bags.

Takeomi pressed the button for the garage, and the lift took them straight down. Sanzu walked out first, carried her to the car and lowered her into the back seat. He leaned her against the closed door and clicked her seatbelt on for her. She smiled up at him. He disappeared from her sight, and the moment of quiet in the car sent her straight back to sleep.

Sanzu POV

When I got back to the car to load the luggage into the boot, Akari was already asleep again, breathing softly. Takeomi helped me load the bags neatly, while Mikey got into the back seat next to Akari. That meant my brother and I had to sit in the front. Ugh.

“Who’s driving?” Takeomi asked, glancing at the two in the back. “I think they’re going to be asleep the whole way.”

I nodded. “You drive.” I tossed him the keys, pulled open the passenger door and slid in before he could say anything. I heard him sigh in defeat, and then he got in.

He turned the key, revved the engine, took a quick look at the two in the back, and waited for the garage door to open before driving onto the road and towards the highway.

An hour into the drive, just as I was about to fall asleep myself, my phone buzzed in my pocket. Sighing, I leaned to one side and pulled it out. The contact said Ran.

“Who is it?” Takeomi asked, glancing at me before returning his eyes to the long road ahead.

“It’s Ran,” I answered, rolling my eyes. I clicked the window button and shut the window. I stared at the screen, then pressed answer. “What.”

I heard him laugh down the line at my tone. “No need to be so rude, Haru,” he teased.

“What do you need? Don’t make me murder you when the holiday’s only just started,” I threatened, as Takeomi gave a disapproving sigh and shook his head.

“Jeez, you’ve got a stick up your arse. Just letting you know we’ve reached the beach. We wanted to ask how long until you guys get here.”

I looked at Takeomi, covered the speaker and asked, “How long?”

“About another hour, I’d say,” he answered, glancing to his right at the ocean view.

“Another hour, he says,” I repeated into the phone.

There was scuffling on the other end before Kakucho’s voice came on. “We’ll be going shopping for tonight’s dinner. We’re doing a BBQ at the accommodation. Any requests?”

“Good wagyu beef and pork,” I replied instantly, my mouth watering at the thought of expensive meat.

“Okay, see you soon. If you find the accommodation empty, it means we’re still out shopping. We shouldn’t take too long, so—”

“I get it, ciao.” I hung up and tucked the phone back into my pocket, tired of the conversations. I leaned against the window and stared blankly outside. “Do you want to swap? I’m tired of being stuck here.”

“Uh, sure. Just don’t go over the speed limit.”

“That’s exactly why I asked you to swap with me. I’m bored.” Takeomi sighed but pulled over onto the hard shoulder. We switched seats, and I sat in the driver’s seat, pulling it back a little to get comfortable. “Ready?” I asked my brother, with a cheeky smirk.

“Lord, save me.”

### Thirty One

Sanzu POV

Adrenaline rushed through my veins as I pressed harder on the accelerator. The car was doing 40 kilometres an hour over the speed limit, whizzing past the other cars. We’d soon have to take the turn off the highway, so I was enjoying the moment while I still could. Takeomi sat beside me, staring out of the window with his phone in his hand, giving directions. He had given up praying that we would survive the drive to the accommodation.

“Slow down, we have to get off the highway at the next turn,” he muttered, pointing ahead. I ignored him and sped up until I saw the exit. Then I let go of the pedal, and the car slowed sharply. I turned the wheel gently as the tyres took the car off the highway. “Drive along this road for five traffic lights, then take a left.”

I followed his every instruction, rolling my eyes at being lost, which was a different experience altogether. I knew I was going to get yelled at, by Akari and everyone else. The narrow winding roads narrowed further as we got close. Then the road opened out, and there was the accommodation Koko had ‘bought’: a holiday house on top of a lush green hill, surrounded by seaside plants that could cope with strong winds and salty soil. It had lots of rooms. It looked like one of those houses from a horror film, which made it all the more exciting. I parked near the house and saw the other car parked beside it, so they were already home.

I switched off the engine, pulled out the keys and shoved them in my pocket. Takeomi got out and walked towards the steps up to the front door. I clicked my tongue, sighed and turned round to look at the two sleeping in the back. Akari smiled in her seat and leaned towards the window, until her head hit the glass and jolted her awake with a curse.

“Ow! Fuck!” She yelled, her eyes snapping open. She glanced round, eyes flickering, noticed Mikey asleep beside her, then the different scenery outside, and finally realised I was in the driver’s seat, watching it all and snickering at her. Her eyes narrowed, and she folded her arms over her chest and pouted. “What are you laughing at?”

I gave her a cheeky smile. “I’m laughing at how cute you are, sweetheart~” I teased, and she turned to look out of the window. I got out, stretched my arms and legs, then opened her door.

“We’re here, so let’s go,” I said, holding out my hand, which she took. I pulled her out and into my body. I gripped her back tightly, lifted her off the ground, spun her round and set her down, letting go of her. Then I pushed her gently towards the steps leading to the main door.

“What are you doing, babe?” she asked, looking over her shoulder, a stray strand of hair poking out at the side of her head.

I pointed at it, and she flattened it down. “I need to bring the boss in, so go first. Okay?” She nodded, walked up the steps and into the accommodation. I turned and slid into the back seat where Mikey was still asleep. For once, he was sleeping peacefully. I unclipped his seatbelt carefully. He didn’t stir. I slid one arm under his knees and the other under his neck, lifted him out of the car, shut the door with my foot, carried him up the steps and kicked the bottom of the front door, hoping someone would let us in.

The door opened, and Koko pulled it wide. “Oh, it’s you,” he said, before turning and heading back into the main area. I walked in and had a quick look round the furnished house. I laid Mikey down gently on the sofa in the living room.

Akari POV

“You went shopping?” she asked Mochi, who was packing food into the fridge, one packet at a time.

“Yeah, lots of meat for tonight’s barbecue,” he said, holding up a packet of expensive wagyu beef.

“Ooooh, so much planned while I was asleep,” she exclaimed, clasping her hands together.

“You’re the one who planned this whole thing. You should be the most organised, since you’re the one who wanted to come,” Ran said, appearing out of nowhere and rubbing the top of her head, messing up her already messy hair.

She glanced out of the window, then ran over to it, staring at the weather outside. “Hey, let’s go to the beach now!”

Mochi closed the fridge and stood up tall. “Is that okay with everyone?”

They all nodded and scrambled towards their luggage, grabbing swimwear, sunscreen and whatever else they needed.

She did the same, changed into her swimwear, pulled loose clothes over the top and packed the rest of her things into a smaller bag. “Hey, Kaku?” He was walking past the food bag, right on cue.

“Yeah?” he said, turning round.

“Did you buy snacks, drinks or whatever?”

“Yeah, they’re in that bag there. There’s plenty for everyone,” he said, pointing at a plastic bag on the kitchen counter. She grabbed it and walked back to Mikey, who was asleep on the sofa, and shook him awake.

“Mikey, we’re all going to the beach now. Let’s go?” He looked up at her with sleepy eyes, sat up and nodded. “Grab some swimmers if you want to go swimming, okay?” He pushed himself off the sofa and disappeared.

“Woo! It’s the beach!” she yelled at the top of her lungs, dropped the bag of food and her belongings, and ran towards the water’s edge.

“Hey! Don’t get your clothes wet!” Koko shouted after her. She turned and poked her tongue out at him, then waddled into the sea until it was at her knees. The water lapped at her legs, threatening to reach the edge of her shorts. The cool water felt good on her skin, and the summer sun warmed her back. She stood there for a minute before she heard splashing beside her. Ran and Rindou were wrestling under the water, as if they were trying to drown each other.

Rindou surfaced and noticed her looking. “Come join us—” He was pulled under again by his brother. She headed back to where she had left her things, but they weren’t there.

“I moved everything over with Koko,” Takeomi said, pointing. Koko and Mikey were sitting under a sun umbrella. Mikey was lying on a towel, probably trying to sleep again, while Koko had his nose in his book. Mochi and Kakucho were setting up two more umbrellas. She walked over to them with sand trapped between her toes, found her small bag, took off her loose clothes so she was in her two-piece swimwear, stuffed the clothes into her bag and ran back to the two brothers in the water.

They heard her, popped their heads up and grinned as she waded towards them. Ran dipped under the surface and came back up with Rindou sitting on his shoulders. Together they towered over her, and she felt tiny. “Wanna play chicken, Akari?” Rindou asked, looking down at her.

She looked around for Sanzu. “Sure, let me go and get my man.” She spotted his pink hair sticking out from behind a rock. She ran over, climbed onto the rock and looked down at him.

“Watchu doing?” He stopped moving, looked up, and let out a small yelp, covering himself. “What the fuck?!” He turned his back to her, and all she could see was his bare backside and broad back.

“Nothing I’ve never seen before,” she said with a shrug, but she stayed on the rock and kept staring at him.

“That’s not even the point,” he huffed, grabbed his swimming shorts and pulled his slim legs into them.

“Anyway, hurry up. We’ve got a match-up against the Haitanis,” she said, standing tall on the rock, then hopping down and landing beside him carefully.

“What match-up?”

“Chicken, you know. The game where you push the others over while you’re on their shoulders,” she explained. He breathed out loudly, took her hand and led her to where the brothers were still waiting.

Sanzu muttered something under his breath, then smirked to himself. “Alright, then. How many rounds are we doing?”

“We should do a round-robin or elimination. Ask the other executives if they want to play too,” Ran suggested, tipping Rindou off his shoulders and running off to ask.

A few minutes later Ran came back with the rest of the executives, and Mikey, who didn’t want to take part. He said he’d referee, which surprised all of them.

“Are there any illegal moves in this game?” Mikey asked, sitting on top of Kakucho’s shoulders so he wouldn’t get too wet.

“No weapons. Once the person on top falls off their partner’s shoulders or into the water, it’s game over, and they’re out. I think it’s best if we do a proper match-up,” Kakucho said, giving Sanzu a look.

“Hey, I don’t have any weapons on me,” Sanzu said, turning out his empty pockets as proof.

“Pick your partners,” Mikey said, and the executives started pairing up. She was with Sanzu, of course. The Haitanis were a pair. Koko was with Kakucho, the 2K’s, and Mochi and Takeomi were the oldies. Mikey stayed on Kakucho’s shoulders. “Alright, the Haitanis against you two, since you’re the main four who wanted this,” Mikey said, pointing at the brothers and then at Sanzu and her.

“Sweet!” She shouted as Sanzu dipped under the water and rose with her on his shoulders. The brothers did the same, with Ran at the bottom and Rindou on top.

“Ready?” Mikey asked, and both pairs nodded. “Haruchiyos versus the Haitanis, begin,” Mikey said, sounding as though he had no energy for it.

The two pairs stayed locked for a while, until Ran suddenly lunged at Sanzu. Sanzu’s grip on her ankles tightened. “Sanzu, let go of my ankles. I’ll hold myself up. Use those hands and push Ran back for me,” she ordered, and he did as he was told, releasing her ankles. Her legs hung over his chest, and she wrapped them under his arms and dug her feet into his back for strength. With his arms free, Sanzu shoved Ran back, opening up some space. She had a short stare-off with Rindou before she smirked at him. She leaned down and whispered in Sanzu’s ear.

“Okay, let’s do that. And if it doesn’t work?” she whispered again, and he smirked too. “This is bound to work.”

“What are you two lovebirds whispering about? Get on with it,” Ran said, sounding irritated.

“Why don’t you get on with it, then?” she snapped, taunting him.

“Don’t complain when you’re in the water,” Rindou said, as Ran rushed at them a second time. Rindou’s arm clashed against hers, and Ran’s against Sanzu’s. Sanzu swayed back and forth, and she swayed with him. Rindou smirked, sure that this was going to be his victory. Sanzu tapped her ankle once with a finger, their signal. He suddenly dropped under the water with her still on his shoulders. Rindou lunged forward from the sudden loss of resistance. She grabbed a handful of seawater and splashed it straight into Ran’s face, blinding him for a second, and he staggered backwards. Sanzu stood back up tall, hooked his leg under Ran’s, and she shoved Rindou to the side, throwing them both off balance. They fell backwards.

“It’s Haruchiyos’ win,” Mikey said, slowly applauding. The brothers climbed out of the water with glum faces.

“Teehee,” she teased them. “Maybe next time, losers,” she said, sticking her tongue out. Sanzu walked over to where Mikey and Kakucho were. He lowered himself so she could hop off, and Mikey moved from Kakucho onto Sanzu. She stood and leaned back into Sanzu’s chest, and he rested his chin on the top of her head. Kakucho and Koko, and Takeomi and Mochi, walked towards each other to begin their match. Kakucho was a strong base for his pair, and Mochi and Takeomi were strong too.

After a lot of pushing and shoving, both teams were level. But the oldies lacked the energy and stamina and retired from the game, giving Kakucho and Koko the win. “Well, that means Kakucho and Koko win. You’ll be facing the Haruchiyos next,” Mikey said, climbing off Sanzu’s shoulders and moving over to Rindou.

Sanzu lowered himself again, and she hopped back onto his shoulders. He waded through the water to meet Kakucho and Koko. “Well, this brings back memories,” Kakucho said, letting out a sigh.

“It does,” she said, looking down at him. Koko, perched on Kakucho’s shoulders, had no idea what they were talking about. Well, he did, but only a little.

“Ready?” Mikey asked, and they nodded again.

“Good game, Kaku, Koko,” she said, and they nodded a second time.

“Likewise,” Koko answered.

“Start!” Ran shouted, taking over Mikey’s job and earning a quick glance from him. Rindou took it upon himself to smack Ran on the back of his head.

This time Kakucho charged straight at the two of them, and she and Koko butted heads. Her legs were round Sanzu’s chest as before. Sanzu tapped her ankle again and dropped under the surface. She splashed water into Kakucho’s face, but he had seen the move coming. Sanzu moved forward in the brief moment while Kakucho’s eyes were closed and rose up under him. She tried to knock Koko off by punching the bottom of his chin, but Koko shouted instructions to Kakucho.

“Large step back!” Kakucho obeyed, wiping seawater from his eyes. Sanzu closed the gap again. This time she tried to push Koko over, but he didn’t budge. Koko gave a huge heave, using Kakucho’s momentum, and she lost her grip on Sanzu’s chest and fell backwards. Sanzu grabbed her ankles and yanked her back up.

“Nice save!” she said. “But I was just going to hook my legs round your neck.”

“Yeah, I know, but you’ll break my neck,” Sanzu said, gripping her ankles.

“Only one thing left to do now,” she said, taking a quick breath. Sanzu nodded at once, understanding the plan. He charged at Kakucho again. She stayed on his shoulders until she felt his hands underneath her, supporting her. He hoisted her high into the air with all his strength, like an acrobat. Lighter now, Sanzu gave a hard kick to Kakucho’s thigh under the water, and Kakucho lost his balance. Sanzu caught her and put her back on his shoulders, then rushed at the other two. Koko jabbed at her face, but she dodged it. She was about to kick Koko’s chest when—

“That’s the end of the match,” Mikey called out.

“Eh? Why??” she shouted, shocked.

“You left his shoulders. That’s a violation of the rules.”

“No, it isn’t,” Sanzu said, backing her up. “Kaku said that if the person on top falls off, it’s game over. But she didn’t fall. It was part of the strategy.”

“Yeah! What he said!” she shouted, arguing with the ruling. “Now we have to start over—”

“We’ll take the loss, then,” Koko announced, after a quick word with Kaku.

“Really? Yayyy!” she shouted, standing on Sanzu’s shoulders and flipping off into the water with a huge splash.

“You’re such a child, love,” Ran said, laughing at her childishness.

“You don’t have to remind me all the time, Ran,” she spat, venom in her voice. “Just suck up the fact that you lost to us.”

“Oh, the burn,” Rindou said, clutching his heart and then his forehead, nearly making Mikey fall off. “Also, Mikey, don’t be a wet sock.”

“What’s that supposed to mean?” he huffed.

“I mean you should join us in the water,” she said, dragging Rindou closer to the sea. Mikey screeched.

“NO! I mean—no.” He calmed down, but she kept tugging at Rindou’s arm.

“Akari, I think Mikey’s made himself clear,” Mochi said, trying to calm her down.

“Fine,” she said, rolling her eyes and letting go of Rindou’s arm. She heard Mikey breathe a sigh of relief.

“But I’m getting you to do something else with us later. Got it?” He nodded reluctantly, gulping nervously.
