### Thirty Two

A couple of hours later, she was floating in the water with Sanzu. He held her as he pushed himself off the sea floor now and then, drifting around.

“Isn’t this so peaceful?” he asked, sliding his hand up and down her back.

“Yeah, it’s really nice,” she breathed.

“Remember this morning, when you saw me changing?” The memory made her chuckle. Sanzu rested his head in the crook of her neck and peppered kisses along it. He mumbled into her skin and began playing with the band of her bikini top, unhooked it and yanked it off.

She covered her chest at once, the water suddenly colder, and she shivered. “What’s the meaning of this, Haruchiyo?” she said, using his proper name. He ignored her and began swimming for shore, her bikini top in his hand. A few metres from the sand, he called back to her.

“Payback!” He gave her a wide smirk, ran onto the beach and threw the top up into a tall tree, where it stuck.

“Fuck you, Sanzu!” she yelled back, covering her chest with her arms. How ironic. The one person who got jealous whenever anyone else looked at her was playing a dangerous game. She looked round for something to cover herself with, and the other executives began to notice.

“Need help, love?” Ran asked, raising an eyebrow with a teasing smile, though she knew what he really wanted.

“No thank you!” she shouted. She waddled towards the shore and saw that Sanzu had taken her bag too, with the rest of her clothes in it. That fucker…

She turned her back to the shore and spotted a clump of seaweed floating on the water. It was gross and slimy, but she held it over her chest with one hand, stood and waded out towards Sanzu, who had started running and looking desperately for somewhere to hide. She wanted to chase him, but she needed to cover up first. She walked through the sand to the group and found a floral button-up shirt. She turned her back, pushed her arms through the sleeves, covered her front with it, let go of the seaweed, buttoned the middle two buttons and tied the bottom ends together in a bow. A cute cropped shirt.

“Hey, that’s my shirt…” Ran began, then stopped when he realised she was wearing his shirt. “I—never mind.”

“Where’s Sanzu?” she growled, looking for him. Mochi pointed behind a rock. “Somewhere over there.”

Koko handed her a knife without looking up from his book. “Here you go,” she said, running her finger carefully along the edge.

“Perfect.”

“Don’t murder him!” Takeomi called after her as she crept towards the rock. She climbed up slowly and held the knife over the edge, tilting it to see whether Sanzu was hiding behind it. In the reflection, there he was, peeking round the rock to see where the other executives were, eyes desperately searching for her. She threw the knife high into the air, then jumped on him, knocking him backwards onto the sand. She straddled his waist, leaned back and watched the knife fall, catching it just inches from his blue eyes. She gave him a smile that said it all. His body shook beneath her as he looked away from her and the knife, turning his head the other way. She grabbed his cheeks roughly, turned his face back to hers and stared into his eyes.

“Anything you want to say to me, Haruchiyo?” she growled, stabbing the knife into the sand right beside his cheek.

“Nope,” he said, smiling smugly. She let go of the knife and sat up, still straddling him.

“You know, it’s funny. You’re the one who gets jealous when I’m not with you, but you play petty tricks like this… Didn’t you think the others would get a peek at my half-naked state too?” His eyes widened as he realised, and he went a little pink. He looked at her covered chest and then at the shirt, and recognised it.

“You’re seriously wearing his T-shirt?”

“Shut the fuck up, that’s not the point,” she spat. They stared at each other for a moment, then she breathed out a long sigh. She rolled off his waist and lay on her back, looking up at the bright blue sky. She covered her eyes with her forearms, because it was too bright. She heard shuffling beside her, took a quick peek and saw Sanzu sitting next to her, leaning against the rock in the shade. He noticed her looking at him, stretched his legs out and tapped his thighs. She smiled, scooched over and laid her head on his lap. She kept her forearms over her eyes as she felt him run his fingers through her long hair, which spilled over his lap and onto the sand. The repeated brushing relaxed her so much that it wasn’t long before she was out like a light.

By the time she woke, it was dusk, with the sun sinking behind the ocean. She was lying on the couch back at the accommodation, taking up the whole thing. Nobody else was in the room. It was dimly lit, with lemon-yellow light coming calmly through the rectangular windows. She sat up and stared round the empty room for a quiet minute, then realised she had fallen asleep earlier. Looking down, she saw she was wearing her bikini top and Sanzu’s T-shirt, not Ran’s shirt. She chuckled quietly, got up and walked to the window. Shielding her eyes from the yellow light, she looked outside and saw all the executives on the porch. Mochi and Takeomi were flipping meat on the barbecue. Ran, Rindou and Koko were having a civil conversation with beers in their hands. Sanzu and Kakucho were talking together, and Mikey sat in a chair on the porch, watching the sun go down.

She walked away from the window, grabbed a couple of spare plates and cutlery and headed out to the barbecue. She handed the plates to Mochi and Takeomi. “Here you go,” she said, a little too cheerfully.

“Fuck, you scared me,” Takeomi said, fumbling with his tongs. He took the plates from her and handed her a can of beer, the water dripping down its sides as it began to warm. She pulled the tab, gulped the beer down and felt the cool liquid cool her from the inside out.

“Thanks for cooking,” she said with a smile, then went over to Mikey’s chair. “How’s the break going?”

He didn’t answer at first. He stared out for a moment longer before he noticed her beside him. “Did you say something?”

“Nah, never mind.” She gave him a reassuring smile, then sat on the porch next to him, the beer can between her thighs, and watched the sun go down with him.

“This was a good suggestion. The beach, I mean,” Mikey murmured, fiddling with the can in his hands.

She turned to look at him. His face glowed a mellow orange, though the darkness behind his eyes hadn’t gone anywhere. “Of course! It’s a great chance to relax and everything.” He turned to her, and their eyes met. He stared into her as if he could read her thoughts.

“I wish they were all here too,” he said. She hummed in response and turned back to face the sun, now half sunk behind the ocean line. The sky was a beautiful pink and blood orange, blending and mixing in places, the clouds catching the light. A sudden arm came out in front of her face, and Mikey’s too.

“Make sure you eat. This is top-quality meat,” Rindou said, handing her and Mikey each a paper plate of meat and vegetables, with a pair of chopsticks.

“Thanks, Rin,” she said, giving him a warm smile. She set the beer down elsewhere, picked up the plate and dug in. The marinade and the meat itself melted in her mouth. “Mmm, this is delicious!” she exclaimed, standing and holding up her plate as if offering the meat to the gods. The meat was gone in seconds, and she headed back to the barbecue for seconds, handing Mochi her plate and shoving it at him.

“Hey, hey, everyone needs to finish their firsts before anyone gets seconds,” Mochi said, slapping her hand away with the tongs and going back to flipping the meat.

“Tch,” she clicked her tongue in annoyance, but went back sulkily to sit beside Mikey. She grabbed her beer, downed the whole can, lay back on the porch and stared up at the wooden awning. Just as she closed her eyes, a drop of liquid landed in the middle of her forehead. She flicked her eyes open and looked up at the person above her.

“What?”

“You can get seconds now,” Koko said, with a cheeky grin.

“Oh, come on,” she whined, sitting up. “I just sat down.” She handed him her plate.

“Aw, hell no. I ain’t getting you seconds,” he complained, shaking his head.

“It’s your fault. This is the least you can do for me, since you were the one who spilled on me.”

“Nahhh.” Koko walked off, leaving her fuming. She mumbled under her breath, leaned back on the porch and closed her eyes again.

A strong salt breeze blew over her, and she shivered. She tugged the blanket up to her neck, trying to keep warm. She was suddenly shaken awake. A figure was kneeling beside her, its outline hazy and almost shifting. The familiar platinum hair made her eyes widen, and she jolted upright. “’Zana?”

There was an awkward silence, and then her vision cleared. It was only Mikey, his face pained at the name. They looked at each other, and she turned her head away and mumbled an apology.

“Yeah,” Mikey said quietly. He got up off the floor, patted the top of her head gently and went back inside the accommodation.

Wait. Did he go inside?

She sat up, and the blanket slid messily into her lap. She had fallen asleep on the porch after the barbecue, and nobody had thought to take her inside? She looked round and saw that most of the executives were also out cold, sprawled across the grass. The only ones who had made it inside were Koko, Mikey and, surprisingly, Rindou. Shaking her head and combing her fingers through her hair, she stood, stretched and heard her spine crack. She grabbed the blanket, folded it over her forearm and walked over to Sanzu, who was curled into a ball next to a bush in the front garden.

She tapped his cheek and poked at it. His nose twitched, like a rabbit’s. She smiled and draped the blanket over him. As soon as he felt the warmth, his body loosened and he unfurled from his ball and turned onto his back. He groaned as the sunlight hit his face. She turned away and faced Ran, who was out cold right beside Sanzu, also curled up tight. She sat on the grass between the two of them.

“Akari~” Sanzu whined, wrapping his arms round her waist, realising she had tucked the blanket over him.

“Hmmm?”

“Morning,” he grumbled, pulling her close. But he pulled with much more energy than she’d expected so early in the morning, and she fell backwards onto his stomach. Her back arched over his body, and her head landed on the grass on the far side of him.

“We should get up. I can’t believe we slept outside. In the cold,” she said, looking at the bush hanging upside down above her.

“At least you had a blanket. I hate to admit it, but Ran and I had to huddle together last night, because neither of us could be bothered to go inside and get one.” That made her laugh, and the noise woke Ran.

“Nice way to wake up this morning,” he said, rubbing his eyes and sitting up. He turned to look at her, but all he could see was her body draped over Sanzu’s. Sanzu’s possessiveness got the better of him. He suddenly sat up, dragging her up with him. Her back cracked again, and she swore at the sudden movement.

“Please don’t do anything so suddenly. We’re not as young as we used to be,” she mumbled, still draped over Sanzu’s lap, face down and nearly kissing the grass.

She felt Sanzu’s hand on her lower back, rubbing it softly. “M’bad swe—”

“Get the fuck up, everyone!” Rindou shouted, and everyone turned to him. “Breakfast is somewhat sorted, so it’s first come, first served!”

“Rin~, why didn’t you wake me up last night? I was freeeezing cold~” Ran whined at his brother, who was leaning against the doorframe.

“Well, you just looked sooo comfortable with druggie on the grass, I thought it’d be a good bonding opportunity. The pics turned out great, by the way,” he said, giving her a wink before going back inside. Ran and Sanzu exchanged a glance, and it turned into a glare. Their faces suddenly softened, and she knew what was coming. She snorted, burst out laughing, got to her feet and went after him.

“Quick! Send them to me!” she squealed, running after him. The thunder of two more pairs of footsteps followed hers, with the brothers chasing both her and Rindou to stop the pictures spreading.

After breakfast, Sanzu and she decided to take a walk along the beach. Since the whole place had been booked by Bonten, there was no worry about being seen or recognised. (Take that however you want.) They walked hand in hand along the edge of the water, kicking up sand and foam, swinging their linked hands. She looked back at their footprints in the sand, but the next wave washed them away.

“This is nice,” he whispered.

“The last time you said that, something happened,” she said, and he laughed. She turned back to the direction they were heading in and noticed a small cave up ahead. “Wanna go and explore that?” she asked, pointing at it.

“I mean, sure, something to do,” he said, leading her away from the water’s edge, cutting diagonally across the sand towards the cave. At the mouth of the cave, she sensed right away that something was wrong. She looked round, her hand still in Sanzu’s. He gave her hand a reassuring squeeze that she didn’t need but was grateful for.

“Ready for adventure?” she asked, excited but a little uneasy.

“Of course.” She stepped inside and had only walked a few metres when she saw something in the dim light, an object glistening against the cave wall. She took out her phone and switched on the torch. She was a little shocked by what she had found. Not the gruesomeness, which she was long used to after living and working with Bonten. It was a jar.

A jar with two red pupils floating in preservative.

She let go of Sanzu’s hand, knelt down and lifted the jar. She shone her torch through the liquid, which acted like a lamp and lit up the rest of the cave. The eyes stared back at her, glossed over. Dead, like Mikey’s, but with more life in them. It was strange that they held more life than Mikey’s did, when he was the one who was actually alive. Whoever those eyes had belonged to must have been through a great deal before they were taken out.

The main focus, though, was no longer the jar. The light picked out the rest of the cave, revealing a skeleton, still in the middle of decaying, with scraps of flesh still attached and flaking away. Next to it lay another body, a man, also long dead, beginning to smell, though he was still fairly fresh. A single bullet wound sat at his temple, and gunpowder residue had stuck to his skin, which meant the gun had been pressed to his head. She searched his body with her eyes, and something caught her attention.

“Sanzu, look.” She pointed at the underside of the man’s bicep.

“I thought this was a private beach,” he said, his voice bouncing off the walls.

“Same, but I guess not.” She let out a long sigh.

“Time to call Hanma.”

### Thirty Three

“Hello?” Hanma’s irritating, teasing voice squeaked through the phone.

“We found a dead guy and a skeleton in a cave. The man has your gang tattoo—”

“Ohhhh, you found him? Wait, why are you even there?”

“That’s our question to you, asshole,” Sanzu spat into the phone.

“Heya, Haru~.” Akari sighed, and Sanzu rolled his eyes.

“You gonna answer our question, or what?”

They both heard Hanma laugh on the other end. “That cave is part of a private property we owned earlier. But we put it on the market, since we had no more need for it. Guess we forgot something~”

She facepalmed at his stupidity. “Anything else we should know?”

“There’s random weapons at the accommodation on the top of the hill that overlooks the beach. Check the attic. Man, what a relief that you guys found it. I completely forgot I asked someone to dump the body in the cave.”

“The body is at least three days old. What are you, an old man with Alzheimer’s?” Sanzu retorted, grabbing the phone off her. “I’m going to have to update the boss about this. Is there anything else you wanna say?”

“Yeah, a couple of things, actually.” They heard the sound of him blowing out smoke from his cigarette before he spoke again. “Tell your boss that I want a partnership with Bonten. I want you guys to import the prostitutes to us. I want Ichthus to be the main supplier. Ditch the old company.”

“That’s up to the boss to decide. It’ll be better if you talk to him about it personally.” Akari’s voice echoed in the cave. “I’ll update him on the situation, including what’s in the cave and the weapons in the beach house. Is there a specific way you want us to get rid of the body? Oh, and the jar with the eyes.”

“Ooooh yes. Keep the eyes. I want them back.”

“Koko might ask you to pay for them, though. Have fun getting them back,” Sanzu snorted, as Hanma clicked his tongue in annoyance.

“Money freak—” Hanma scoffed under his breath.

“Okay, we’re going to dispose of the bodies,” she said, telling him before he could ask for anything extra.

“Yes, yes. Go wild,” he replied.

“Bye,” Sanzu said quickly, and cut the call.

“Phew, thank god that’s out of the way,” she sighed, placing her hands on her hips. “Let’s just take the jar and report back?”

“Yeah, let’s go.” He grabbed her free hand and led her out of the cave.

“We’re back~!” she sang as they walked through the main doors of the accommodation. She nudged Sanzu, and he took the stairs straight to the attic.

“You guys took a while. Did something happen?” Kakucho asked, leaning his elbows on the kitchen counter.

“Yeah, everything was normal, except we came across a dead body. This—” She put the jar down on the kitchen counter, and Kakucho’s eyes widened, like the eyes in the jar. Sure enough, it caught the attention of the other executives on the couch, who gathered round the table.

“Where’d you get this?” Ran asked, lifting the jar to the light and turning it to view it from underneath.

“The cave, with the body.”

“What body?” Koko interrupted, snatching the jar from Ran and inspecting it. “Man, a pair of eyes like this are a rarity nowadays.”

“Ichthus’s traitor, we assume. We came across it in the cave. Turns out Hanma ordered one of his men to dump the body there three days ago and then forgot about it. He also owned the land here before you guys did. Sanzu’s checking the attic for—”

“FOUND IT!” Sanzu yelled, tumbling down the stairs and pointing up. “Had to pull on the ceiling light to get up there. He was right. There’s literally everything you want up there.”

“What are you guys talking about?” Mochi asked, raising an eyebrow at her.

“Yeah, he stuffed weapons in the attic too,” she answered with a sigh. “Where’s Mikey? I have to ask him something.”

“He’s sleeping. I’m surprised he hasn’t woken up yet from Sanzu screaming,” Takeomi said, glancing at Sanzu. Sanzu returned the gesture with his middle finger and a stuck-out tongue.

“Alright, thanks. I’m going to ask Mikey something, and depending on his answer, I’m going to ask you all for favours. You can all chill for now.” She smiled at the executives and headed up the stairs towards Mikey’s room.

“What about the jar?” Rindou yelled after her. She stopped and turned, then came back down the stairs.

“Koko!”

“Ah—yes?” he replied, dropping his little black notebook.

“You’re in charge of the jar. Hanma desperately wants it back, so find out what it’s worth. Go all out.” She gave Koko a wink and an evil smirk, then headed back up the stairs.

She knocked softly on Mikey’s door and waited a couple of seconds. When she was sure he hadn’t got up yet, she pushed the door open carefully. So much for sleeping, like Takeomi had said. He was sitting on the bed, staring out the window with his back to the door. “Mikey?”

He slowly turned his head and looked at her blankly, then rubbed his eyes and turned his whole body round. “What,” he asked coldly. “Something’s going on, isn’t it? It’s rowdy downstairs.”

“Yeah. Turns out Hanma wants a partnership with Bonten. He wants to be Bonten’s main export for prostitutes.”

“What’s so good about his offer, though?”

“He didn’t specify much,” she answered, taking her phone out of her pocket. “Want me to clarify by calling him?”

“Sure. Get Koko up here too.”

“Of course.”

“I’d say it’s a pretty good deal, Mikey,” Koko said, checking his notes, the jar in his lap.

“I’ll trust your judgement, then,” Mikey replied, turning to face the camera on the phone. “Hanma, consider this a deal. But remember, we are Bonten. Wrong us, and we won’t hesitate to mess with you.”

Hanma let out a chesty laugh, lit a cigarette and put it to his lips. It was strange to watch a pixelated Hanma smoking. “Of course~. I’ll make sure not to mess with you guys.”

“We’ll sign the contract when we get back from our holiday at the end of this week.”

She quietly left the room, went down the stairs and whistled to catch the executives’ attention. They were chatting away on the couch.

“Okay, so the favours I need shouldn’t be that complicated,” she said, glancing at the two brothers. “What? Are we in trouble?” Ran asked, his eyes saying he was guilty of something.

“I don’t know what you’ve done, Ran. Chill. Anyway, Ran, Rin. I need you both to break ties with the old whorehouse owner. We’ve moved to Hanma’s gang.”

There were some whispers between Kakucho, Takeomi and Mochizuki. “Did Mikey make that decision?” Kakucho asked.

She nodded. “Koko helped with it, so there’s no way the deal won’t benefit us.”

“Cool, that’s simple enough. Consider it done before tonight,” Rindou said, leaving the room and walking past her, dragging his whining brother along.

“Kaku, Sanzu. Can you clear the attic for me? I need you to check the weapons for duds, and see which ones can still be used.” She glanced at her boyfriend and sent him a small warning.

“Hon, I know you love crazy things. I do too. But not today, okay? If you want to test the weapons, go far away from the house. Kaku, please look after my big baby.”

Sanzu looked a little sad. He had clearly been planning to blow something up. She was glad she’d sent Kakucho with him too. “I’ll keep him in check. Don’t worry.”

“Thanks, Kaku. I owe you.” Sanzu and Kakucho walked past her and up the stairs. Except Sanzu just had to be extra and pinched her backside as he passed. She let out a little squeak, which caught the attention of Takeomi and Mochizuki.

“Cute,” they heard Sanzu whisper to himself as he skipped down the hallway upstairs. She coughed to hide her embarrassment.

“I—. Umm, I need you two to go down to the beach. There should be a cave. Check it for any other valuables. And please burn the bodies. They’re starting to smell.”

“You should’ve given this job to my brother instead. He would’ve enjoyed it,” Takeomi said with a sigh.

“Yeah, that might’ve been a better, safer idea. A little too late now,” she said, hanging her head.

“Don’t worry, we’ll get it done,” Mochi answered, giving her a reassuring smile.

Takeomi and Mochi stood and went into the kitchen, grabbing a matchbox and other items. Takeomi rubbed the top of her head, gave her a small smile and left the accommodation. The living room was dead quiet. She trudged back up the stairs and into Mikey’s room.

Standing beside Mikey, she watched Hanma’s eyes move to Koko, sitting in the chair beside him. “I’ll need that jar back, Koko,” Hanma said, spitting out the name.

Koko noticed the poison in Hanma’s tone and blatantly ignored it. “You’ll get it back once you decide to pay us for it. You forgot it, so it’s your loss.”

“How much for it, then?” Hanma asked, an irritated vein appearing on his forehead. She couldn’t help coughing and chuckling. “I can hear you laughing, Akari.”

“¥500,000,000 (about $5 million). I checked the price for it, and—”

“He doesn’t need to know that much, Koko. He can work it out himself.” She cut him off and grabbed her phone. “Have fun with that, Hanma~! Anyway, catch you later.” She was a fingernail away from ending the call when he shouted into the phone.

“Wait! I have something else to say. It’s a different matter from the deal, and it involves Bonten.”

She looked over at Mikey, who made grabby hands at the phone in her hand. She threw it to him, and he caught it. “I’m listening.”

“There’s no way you’ve forgotten him, right?”

“You might want to specify which him, Hanma,” Mikey spat, his eyes glowing despite their lifelessness.

“I’m talking about that kid. Man, he was so annoying, ruining Kisaki’s plans time and time again.”

“You mean Michi?” she cut in, popping her head into view of the screen.

“Yeah, just forgot his name.”

“So the rat—”

“If anyone, you’re the rat, Hanma,” she spat, a little annoyed.

“Calm your farm, girlie,” he replied, sending her an irritating smirk. “Do you want the news or what?”

“Continue,” Mikey said, giving him a brief but dangerous look.

“He’s starting to use his head. Seems like he’s realised you were part of Bonten. And guess what~?” There was an awkward silence in the room.

“You’re supposed to say ‘what.’ Man, you guys are dull,” Hanma coughed. He was really playing around.

“What happened next, Hanma?” she said sarcastically, rolling her eyes.

“Thank you, Akari. So he’s going round asking the clubs and bars whether they know Bonten. Obviously, he’s getting kicked out. Nobody wants to be asked about Bonten. They’re scared shitless.”

“And?” Mikey asked.

“He’s looking for you, duh.”

Takeomi POV

“Surely this is the cave?” Mochi said, standing at the mouth of it, breathing heavily. Takeomi wasn’t much better. Walking fast over the sand, with their feet sinking into it, hadn’t helped.

“I think this is the one. I think there’s only one cave.”

“Oh,” Mochi said, squinting to see inside. “Let’s go,” he suggested, switching on the torch and pointing it into the cave. Takeomi followed him in, keeping close while taking in the sight in front of him.

A few steps in, the loud buzzing of flies drew their attention to the skeleton and the rotting body propped against the cave wall. “Seems they weren’t lying,” Takeomi said, walking towards the body, lifting the dead man’s bicep and finding the tattoo.

“There might be something else in the cave. Should we check before we burn everything?”

“Yeah, that’s the least we can do. We might find some other artefacts that Koko can sell back to Hanma. Money is key nowadays.” They walked past the bodies and deeper into the cave. A couple of minutes in, they found more skeletons. At least ten more.

Mochi sighed deeply. “Is this a cemetery or something?” Takeomi laughed and began inspecting the skeleton closest to him. Nothing was left on the bones, no tendons or scraps of meat. Nothing at all. It had been cleaned of every trace of human flesh. Acid, maybe?

“There’s no point burning this whole cave for one body,” he said, glancing at the other remains.

“We still have to dispose of the bodies, though. Should we just grind them up or something?”

He thought about it for a while. “We could put the remains in a mesh bag, dump it in the middle of the ocean and weigh it down with something heavy.”

“We could. But that’ll be difficult to organise.” Mochi thought about it too before speaking up. “You know how Viking funerals work?”

“Putting a body in a boat, letting it drift away and setting fire to it?”

“Yeah, that. We could do that.”

“Wouldn’t it be noticeable? With the smoke and everything?”

“It’s like two plans put together. I don’t think there’s anything much better than that.”

Takeomi sighed in defeat. There really weren’t many other options. “We’ll do that, then. I’ll go and find two or three wooden boats.”

“I can’t believe we’re sending these stupid bodies off as if we respect them,” Mochi scoffed, as Takeomi left the cave to look for the boats.

Mikey POV

The thought of Takemichi going round countless bars and nightclubs gives me the shivers. I don’t understand why he would go so far as to save me. If I could choose, I would love to visit old friends. Draken, especially. But I can’t. I chose this life, and I won’t hesitate to keep it this way. I may regret the choices that brought me to where I am now, but I don’t regret having Akari and the others by my side. Especially Akari. I know I act cold towards her sometimes, but I hope she knows how much she has helped me through everything. She’s the only one capable of countering my dark impulses. She’s like a source of light in the dark for me. I can’t explain it, but that’s what she is.

I don’t understand why Takemichi is coming for me now, of all times. He could have come back from the past and left me alone. I know I won’t be able to hold myself back from—

“Mikey?” Akari’s voice came from the other side of the bedroom door and cut through my thoughts.

“It’s open.” She pushed the door open, closed it softly behind her, and shuffled to the edge of my bed before sitting down. Her eyes met mine, and I felt as if I were being absorbed. She opened her mouth to say something, then closed it again. She was hesitating. “Did you want to say something? I’m all ears.” She stared at me as if it were strange for me to say something like this. She was right. It was so out of character for me, and I knew it.

“Do you have a fever again? Are you okay?” She placed a hand on my forehead, then on her own. I covered her hand with mine and replied calmly.

“Yeah, I’m fine. So, what did you need?”

“Umm, it’s about what Hanma said earlier. What are you going to do about Takemichi?” There was a small quiver in her voice. Honestly, I didn’t know what to do either, so I couldn’t give her much of an answer. Part of me wanted to meet him and break down. I wanted him to tell me everything would be okay. But I have Akari as well. The other part of me wanted to push him away, keep him out of my life and protect him. Protect the others, like I’ve done for the last ten years. It’s a dilemma.

“I’ll give you an answer to that when the time comes,” I said, giving her a broad answer.

She sat on the bed for a while, nodded and stood up. “Excuse me,” she said quietly, and left the room, leaving me alone once again.

Thoughts kept drowning me. I didn’t know what to do. What on earth did Takemichi want from me? Should I be making up my mind now? Was that the right choice?

I don’t know anymore.

Is he worth the ten years of work I’ve done to build Bonten to the power I have now?

“Takemichi…” I murmured.

“Why…?”

### Thirty Four

Akari POV

It was the car ride home. The afternoon sun was slowly draining away, staining the white clouds orange, red and yellow. She was squashed between Sanzu and Koko in the back seat, screaming her lungs out along with everyone else to the music blasting from the speakers.

“I’ll hit the ceiling—” Rindou yelled out the first line of the chorus, tapping his foot to the beat in the passenger seat.

“ Or else I’ll tear up this town—” Ran joined in and finished the line for him.

When the next part came on, everyone joined in, even Koko. “ Tonight I gotta cut loose, Footloose.”

They were singing the title song from Footloose at the top of their lungs. Akari threw her shoes off and pointed at them as she sung the next part “ Kick off the Sunday shoes,” Akari exclaimed and Sanzu laughed at her.

Sanzu finished the chorus for her, and she gave him a cheeky smile as he sang. "Please, Louise. Pull me up off my knees," He gave her a playful wink.

Koko surprisingly got into character. He leaned across and shoved Sanzu on the shoulder.

“What was that-"

"Jack, get back. C'mon, before we crack." Koko sang, cutting off Sanzu

Sanzu scowled and was about to do something, but she held him back with a hand and a death glare. He sank back into his seat and joined in for the last line, and the whole car shouted the chorus together. “Lose your blues," Ran sang, tapping the steering wheel and pressed harder on the accelerator.

"Everybody cut Footloose!"

They all burst out laughing at how they were acting out the lyrics. Just as she was about to sing out loud, Rindou changed the song.

“Heyyy, bitch! At least finish the song,” she whined, kicking the back of his chair. He jolted forward, and his phone flew out of his hand and hit the windscreen. He had tapped another song when he let go.

“Careful there,” Ran scolded, keeping one eye on the road, slowing the car slightly and reaching for the phone, which had ended up in front of him. A slow song began to play, and most of them grimaced.

“What is this slow song?” Sanzu exclaimed as it reached the chorus. It was a soft, sentimental love song. Akari thought it was cute, and her head swayed to the rhythm.

"~Baby, I'd give up anything to travel inside your mind~ Baby, I fall in love again come every summertime~"

"Damn, this is a cute song though," You exclaimed, head moving side to side with the rhythm of the song.

“Not the best for a road trip, though,” Koko said. When even he agreed, she knew something was wrong.

“Pick something else, jellyfish,” Sanzu said harshly, leaning forward and looking over his shoulder. He took the phone from Rindou, who had just got it back from his brother, and scrolled through the list. He slowed his finger when he landed on a certain song, and his face changed into a wide smirk.

She recognised the song within the first few seconds. So did everyone else, except Koko, who didn’t recognise it until the first line played.

"Shawty had them apple bottom jeans."

It was a hip-hop track, Apple Bottom Jeans. Sanzu started the chorus, and everyone shouted the responses back at him like a call and response, Ran loudest of all.

"Jeans," Koko added finally recognising the song only with little to no enthusiasm.

"Boots with the fur"

"With the fur~" Ran added this time.

"Got the whole club looking at her~"

"She hit the floor,"

"She hit the floor," Sanzu responded, like the call and response that was expected.

Everybody joined in, finishing the lyrics. "Next thing you know, Shawty got low, low, low, low, low, low, low, low."

"Yeah! Get it!" Ran laughed out, beeping the horn at the slow car in front of us. "Fucking move!"

“If I could dance right now, I would’ve dropped to the floor and busted out dancing,” she said, moving her arms in a circle.

“It’s painful to think we’d all have to watch that happen,” Koko said, looking out the open window as the music almost drowned out his comment.

“Oh, shut it,” she snapped back playfully, and gave him a nudge on the shoulder.

Ran kept driving along the highway, and before long he changed lanes and turned onto the main road into central Tokyo.

Suddenly Sanzu yelped in surprise, because Rindou’s phone was vibrating in his hand. She turned and saw the caller ID.

Boss

Sanzu looked at the phone and handed it back to Rindou in the passenger seat. “Call from the boss,” he said. Rindou grabbed the phone, turned off the music and answered. The car went quiet as they all listened in.

“Yes, boss?” he said. “Mmm, okay. See you soon.”

“What did he say?”

“He just wanted to let us know he’s arrived back at HQ.”

“That’s it?”

“Yeah.”

Now that the call was over, Rindou turned the music back up, and the rest of them went back to singing along to the next song.

THREE DAYS LATER

And here she was again, working at her FNN club. It was busy again tonight, the crowd rowdy and loud. Music poured out of the speakers, and the floor vibrated with every bass beat. Glasses clinked, and customers shouted “CHEERS!” as they laughed, gossiped and talked about their own lives. She kept serving drinks and accepting their thanks and the odd tip. The few VIP customers who came tonight arrived too, including the all-important Hanma (with an eye-roll) and Hana.

“Can I have one glass of—” A loud noise interrupted the customer, and the shouting of one of her workers caught her attention.

“Hana,” Yuki said, tapping her on the shoulder. “I’ll deal with the customer here. Check out the issue over there instead, okay?”

Grateful for Yuki’s help, she smiled at her with her eyes, said a quick thank you, and made her way over to the commotion.

“What’s the issue here?” The yelling died down as all eyes turned to her, the owner of the FNN club.

“Oh, boss.” One of her workers moved out of the way to reveal the all-too-familiar figure. Takemichi. “This man is asking for information about Bonten.”

She pretended to be shocked, widening her eyes to play the part. She walked closer and squatted down to his level. “You can’t just waltz in here and ask for information about Bonten. You should know that they’ve attacked this place more than once.”

“I came here on purpose. I’ve heard that you serve them, so—” Takemichi started, but she cut him off at once.

“That information is highly private and confidential. I can’t give you any more information.” She said it calmly, gazing deep into his eyes. She watched his face crease, his eyes narrowing slightly.

“Akari?”

She was taken aback for a moment, but she kept going. “Sorry? It seems you’ve mistaken me for someone else. I’m Nakatani Hana, the owner of the FNN club. Now, since you’ve caused a

disruption in the club, you can either leave without causing any more fuss, or I may have to force you out. So what will it be?”

He got to his feet, his eyes a little watery, and bowed slightly in apology before turning and leaving the club. “Thanks, boss,” the worker said, and went back to work.

A little stressed by Takemichi’s surprise visit, she ruffled the top of her hair and smoothed it down with her fingers. She walked straight to the VIP door and punched in the code. Ignoring the red tags hanging on the door handles, she walked into the storeroom and headed up to the living area of the Bonten building.

“Wassup?” was the first thing she heard when the lift doors opened.

“Takemichi came to the club. Just like Hanma said,” she announced.

The sound of hurried feet came through the floor. “What do you want us to do?” Koko asked.

“Can you tell Mikey?”

“Yeah, I’ll do that. I’ll send Sanzu to tail him as well.”

“Yeah, that’ll be great. Thanks, Koko.” With that, she went back down to the club to finish her night.

She had just served her last customer. She walked up to the main entrance, flipped the sign to closed, and locked the door. The music was still playing, but with so few customers left, she asked the DJ to turn it down and put on something slower. He played some slow jazz that suited a small, cosy café, not a club run by the nation’s worst criminal organisation. But she went with it. People left slowly while she cleaned the glasses one by one, drying them with the towel hanging over her shoulder. She passed the dried glasses to Yuki, who put them on the shelves behind the bar.

At last, the washing was done, and the last customer had paid and left.

“Phew, long night!” Yuki sighed, wiping her hairline with her wrist. She laughed a little, hanging the wet towel over the handle of one of the drawers.

“Thanks for tonight, Yuki,” she said, starting to close the blinds.

“No worries, see you later!” Yuki replied, rushing out of the main door. She watched from the doorway as Yuki disappeared into the night. Sighing quietly, she finally let herself breathe, removed her mask and yawned to stretch her face. She stepped back into the club and locked the door from the inside. The reflection of her face in the glass made her stare into her own eyes. Her fingers moved to her cheek without thinking, running down to her jaw and feeling the scar beneath her fingertips. She snapped out of it and took the lift up to turn in for the night. By the time she reached her room, her phone was buzzing in her pocket.

She pulled it out and answered at once. “Yes?”

“Akari! Mikey and Takemichi are about to meet. Meet me at the abandoned bowling alley,” Sanzu said, and cut the call. She was left standing there, listening to the dial tone, as she began to process what he had said.

This might not end well.

She rushed to change out of her work clothes and into her suit, then took the lift back down to the garage, hopped into the nearest car and sped off to the abandoned bowling alley.

Arriving at the bowling alley sent a shiver down her spine. There were hardly any people around, and the car’s headlights were the only things that caught her attention. She switched off the engine, locked the car and ran up the stairs, trying to reach Mikey before he did anything he might regret. She slammed open the door and saw Sanzu pointing a gun at Takemichi’s head, with Mikey sitting a row behind him.

Takemichi flinched at the sound of the door banging open. Mikey slowly turned round, his eyes widening a little when he saw her in the doorway, panting from climbing the stairs as fast as she could.

“What are you doing here?” he asked her.

“Making sure you don’t do anything you might regret,” she answered quickly, walking up to Mikey and sitting down next to him.

He didn’t respond. He kept silent and turned his attention back to Takemichi. “Great future, isn’t it? Got anything you want to ask?”

Takemichi kept silent, shifted in his seat, and took a white envelope out of his pocket, holding it up in the air. “I wanted to give you this.”

Mikey stared at the envelope and then at her. She sighed, stood up and took the envelope from Takemichi. He seemed to realise that it wasn’t Mikey who had taken the letter, and he turned his head slightly. Sanzu pressed the gun harder into his head.

“Akari?” Takemichi trembled slightly.

“Yeah. Good to see you again, I guess,” she replied coldly.

“So what is that?” Mikey asked, getting back to the matter at hand.

Takemichi paused before he continued. “It’s the invitation to my wedding. I want you to come, no matter what. Everyone is doing well, just as you promised me twelve years ago. Everyone— including Hina—is living a happy life. Everyone except you.”

“Hey, shut your mouth, or I’ll kill you,” Sanzu interrupted, pushing the gun harder into his temple.

“Sanzu,” she said calmly, shaking her head at him. He looked over at Mikey and waited for his approval, which Mikey gave with a nod. Sanzu lowered the gun, slid it back into his pocket, but stood opposite her, watching everything unfold.

“Your coming here, meeting with me, has made all of this more difficult,” Mikey said, his cold, empty eyes boring into the back of Takemichi’s head. “Everything was going fine until you came here. I am happy, living this life.”

Takemichi was silent, shocked by Mikey’s words. So were she and Sanzu.

“You can live a—” The click of a gun echoed through the bowling alley, and Takemichi fell silent immediately.

“Mikey!” She stood in front of Takemichi at once, shielding him.

“Akari. Move.” His tone sent a shiver through her body. She knew she was in the wrong for shielding Takemichi, but she didn’t want Mikey to carry any more guilt or regret. She stood her ground and kept Takemichi behind her. “Sanzu, move her out of the way.”

Sanzu stared at Mikey, then looked back at her. She gave him a deadly glare, and he stepped back under the intensity of her eyes. He was torn. No matter what he chose, he would be killed, either by his boss or by his girlfriend.

“S-sweetheart, move out of the way,” he stuttered, not wanting to choose sides, but he did— siding with his boss.

“No, I’m not mov—”

A gunshot rang out. The bullet grazed her arm. She felt the blood trickle down her arm, drip from her fingertips and land in vermilion drops on the floor. She gripped her arm tightly but didn’t move.

“Move.”

“Mikey,” she said in a calm voice, meeting his eyes. He kept the gun pointed at her head. “This isn’t the right thing to do.”

That got a reaction. His eyes softened slightly. He looked away from her quickly, and began to shake a little.

“Manjiro,” she said again, walking slowly towards him. She made sure his grip on the gun loosened before she took the final step. She knelt down and looked up at his face. “Think it through. Michi came here to tell you that you can live a happier life, and that he’s grateful for what you’ve done to make their lives better. You said yourself that you’re happy living this life. If you really believe that, there shouldn’t be any need to shoot Michi, right?” Mikey looked down into her soft eyes and held her gaze, intense, as if he was going to lose everything all over again.

She placed a reassuring hand on Mikey’s thigh, and he flinched. “Michi, I hope you realise you’re asking a criminal to attend your wedding. For the wedding to run smoothly, it would be best if he doesn’t come,” she said, turning her head to look at Takemichi.

“Yeah, I know. But I want him there.”

She knew Takemichi really wanted Mikey to go, but if Mikey reacted like this to Takemichi, imagine what he would do to the others. In the worst case, it would be a massacre.

“Sanzu, escort Michi out. I’ll deal with Mikey.” She sent Sanzu a quick, spiteful glance. She waited until she heard the door close before she spoke to Mikey again.

“Mikey. I need you to understand this.” He looked at her again, his eyes showing his confusion. “If you’re happy with Bonten, that’s great. We can carry on living the way we have, killing, making money, all of it. But if you’re unhappy, that’s fine too. You have a chance to turn your life around. But think it through, because if you disband Bonten, there would be a huge power imbalance in the country. The government would find out about everything: your connections, your crimes, your past. There would be nowhere to hide. You’d put them in danger all over again.” She stopped talking for a moment and let him take it all in.

“You don’t need to lose any more people you love,” she whispered, standing up and holding out her arms. “Whatever you decide, I’ll support you. I’m not going to leave you.” He looked up at her, stood and accepted her hug. After a moment of silence, he answered quietly.

“I’ll stay.”

She smiled at his choice and rubbed her hand up and down his back to comfort him. “If that’s your decision, I’m happy.” His eyes met hers, for the hundredth time that night.

“Sorry about your arm,” he mumbled, glancing down at it, which was still bleeding.

She let out a small laugh. “No worries. I’ll go to the doctor later. We’ll talk more about the plan for attending the wedding back at home. Shall we go back now?”

Mikey nodded slowly and started towards the door, with her following closely behind.

Sanzu POV

I’m screwed. Akari’s going to kill me later. But I really had no choice. Well, I did, but—

“Thanks,” Takemichi’s voice squeaked into my head. I turned quickly, and he flinched.

“Scram,” I said sharply, flicking my wrist to shoo him away. He gave a quick bow of his head, then turned and disappeared back onto the main street. I sighed and walked back to our car, parked behind the bowling alley.

??? POV

Wedding? What wedding? Why would anyone from Bonten attend a wedding? I had just left the bowling alley after following Haruchiyo Sanzu in. I stood behind the metal door, listening to their conversation, until I heard Sanzu and another pair of footsteps coming closer.

I hid on the upper floor and watched the two of them climb down the stairs and out through the back door. Of course I followed. The boss had made sure I grabbed any information I could. I took out my phone, snapped a photo of Sanzu and the man, and quietly followed Sanzu down the stairs.

SOMETIME LATER

Haruchiyo Sanzu. Bonten’s number two. He was leaning against the fence, watching the blackhaired man walk towards the main street. He breathed out a quick sigh and turned on his heel.

I watched him turn the corner quickly towards the back of the bowling alley. I followed at a safe distance, because I could feel an immense aura coming off him. He reached a black car and slid into the driver’s seat.

But he didn’t have the key. Was the car his?

I kept watching from the shadows as the engine turned on and the headlights lit up the abandoned area. The car drove past me slowly, and I looked inside and recognised a person in the back seat.

According to the boss’s documents, Haruchiyo Sanzu was still in a relationship with Kurokawa Akari.

She was in that car with him, along with the boss of Bonten.

### Thirty Five

??? POV

I made sure their car was long out of sight before I left the area. I walked onto the main road, blending in with the crowd as it walked past me. I went to the edge of the footpath and signalled for a taxi.

“Good evening, sir. Where can I take you?” the taxi driver asked politely. I took out my phone and showed him the address.

“Take me there,” I ordered. He glanced at the address and entered it into the machine.

“I hope you’re aware that the location you’re asking me to take you to is—”

“I know,” I said, giving him a smile. I watched his hands start to tremble with fear, and then he drove us to the location.

Akari POV

She was sitting on a hospital bed, the white sheets stained with red, hissing in pain as the doctor stitched her skin together. He was closing the graze on her arm from earlier. She felt him working near the edge of the wound, tying off the thread. He picked up a pair of scissors and snipped the thread as close to the knot as he could.

“There,” he sighed, placing the needle and scissors back on the tray. He dabbed on a sterile gauze pad, then picked up the roll of bandage and began to unwrap it. She lifted her arm and held the gauze in place while he wound the bandage round the wound. He clipped the metal

bandage clip on and leaned back in his chair. “All done,” he announced, crossing one leg over the other.

“Thank you,” she said, standing up from her chair.

“What happened to you?” the doctor asked, packing away the dirty needle and the spare thread.

“Bullet wound, nothing more,” she sighed, moving her arm to test how much mobility she had.

He gasped in shock. “Dangerous world you’re involved in,” he said. “Be careful. It’s no world for a young woman like you.”

“Too late to back out of Bonten now, isn’t it?” she said with a shrug, slipping her jacket over her shoulders.

“Stay safe out there,” he said quickly, as she closed the door behind her. She walked down the empty, dark hospital corridor and out through the main doors. Crossing the empty car park, she spotted her car and knocked on the window. The doors unlocked, and she stepped into the back seat beside Mikey.

“What did he do?” Sanzu asked worriedly, starting the engine and switching on the headlights, since it was dark outside.

“Stitched it up,” she said sharply, giving him no more information. She heard him sigh heavily. She knew he understood why she was angry.

“Sorry again,” Mikey apologized, glancing at her arm.

She turned and faced him after buckling her seatbelt. “It’s not a problem anymore. Don’t worry about it.” But her thoughts had already moved elsewhere. “Anyway, the wedding. Are you okay with not going?” she asked quietly, studying his face carefully.

He answered her question with another question. “Are you okay with going in my place?”

“I’ll get some shit for it, but whatever. It shouldn’t be any harder than managing two identities at once.” She took the wedding invitation from her pocket and tore open the envelope.

“Did he treat you?” Mikey asked.

She nodded. “He seemed to remember me from last time, when Sanzu was in hospital.” She pulled out the invitation and read it, then handed it to Mikey, who read it too.

“It’s a week from now, at a church. Traditional,” he said, handing the envelope back to her. “Make sure you bring some protection with you, just in case.”

“Of course.” The car drove through the open garage doors, and Sanzu cut the engine after parking. She opened her door with her uninjured arm and stepped out, waiting for Mikey to get out before she shut the door. Sanzu locked the car and slipped the keys into his pocket.

“Sweetheart, talk to me~” he whined, poking her sides in the lift. The lift stopped at Mikey’s floor, and he got out.

“Take a good rest, Akari, Sanzu,” he said. The lift doors closed slowly as she watched his back walk down the corridor towards his office.

“Akari~”

“What.”

“I’m sorry~” he whined, resting his forehead on her shoulder and pressing apologetic kisses along her neck.

She sighed long and hard, then took his face in her hands and turned him to face her. He looked down at her with wide eyes. “I’m sorry too. I shouldn’t have got mad at you like that.” She pulled his face down and kissed his lips softly. He seemed surprised, but he gave in and kissed her back with love and passion. She parted from him and kissed both sides of his mouth, deliberately kissing his scars. What she didn’t notice was that the lift doors were already open on the top floor.

“Ewww, they’re kissing,” Ran exclaimed, pretending to be sick. Rindou and Koko both laughed at him. Sanzu, going red from the teasing, grabbed her collar and pulled her lips back to his. She was shocked by the sudden move, but she understood why he’d done it. She pushed him back against the wall and pressed the button for her office floor. The lift doors closed, and Sanzu immediately broke the kiss.

“Sorry, sweetheart,” he said, breathless, his face a little flushed.

She gave him a teasing smirk. “No worries. I quite enjoyed that.”

“You’re gonna wish you’d stopped me earlier,” he growled, guiding her out of the lift onto her floor. She smiled into another hungry kiss. “I’m gonna keep you up all night.” She felt him smirk against her mouth before he pushed his tongue into hers.

??? POV

I picked my phone up off the ground, trying not to touch the blood. The screen was cracked, and I was a little irritated. I looked down at the taxi driver lying in a heap of blood at my feet.

Ew. I tapped the screen. Thankfully the phone still worked.

I dialed the boss’s number straight away.

“Yes?”

“I have information about Bonten.”

“I hope you remember the document about Sanzu’s apparent girlfriend, from all those years back, that was on your desk.” I heard paper rustling on the other end.

“I happened to find him last night, tailing a man with black hair, so I followed them. They led me to Bonten’s leader, and to her. They were having an ‘argument’ with the black-haired man about his wedding. Apparently he’s an old friend from Toman.”

“I see. And your point?”

“I think we should leak the pair’s identities to the police. The news stations will go all over it, and that should keep their attention for a while. The wedding is when I’ll strike, and I’ll bring whoever attends back to you.”

“Hmmm,” the boss hummed, weighing the suggestion. “And what are we going to show as proof that they’re in Bonten?”

“I have a photo of Haruchiyo Sanzu from earlier today.”

“Send it through now,” he ordered.
