“You already know my answer. This is a perfect opportunity to grab one of the Bonten members.” He laughed again so loudly that I had to pull the phone away from my ear. “Cheers.” He abruptly hung up. I sighed and slid the phone back into my pocket. I crouched down to the level of the dead taxi driver, fished out his phone and began the plan.

Akari POV

NEXT MORNING

She woke to banging on her office door. She groaned, turned over and buried her head in Sanzu’s bare chest. He felt her head nudge against him, and he wrapped his arms round her and pulled her closer. The harsh knocking continued, getting louder by the minute. Having had enough, she yelled out.

“What?!” She pulled the thin sheet up to cover herself somewhat.

The door swung open, revealing Koko. “Terrible news!”

“Care to explain?” Sanzu asked groggily, rubbing her back calmly.

“It’d be better to show you,” Koko said, stepping into the room and trying to drag her off the couch.

She groaned again. “Okay, okay, I’ll get up.” She pushed herself out of Sanzu’s tight grip, rolled off the couch, grabbed his shirt and followed Koko up in the lift to the living area. She sat on the couch and lifted her sleepy eyes to the TV on the wall.

Her eyes were suddenly wide awake. Her own mugshot was on screen, from when she was in the juvenile detention centre all those years ago. “Why is my face plastered on the TV?” she yelled, as Koko pointed at the screen, trying to get her to listen to the news reporter.

“This woman, known as Kurokawa Akari, is suspected of being involved with Bonten. Her boyfriend, Haruchiyo Sanzu, has also been identified as a member of Bonten.” Her face vanished, and a blurry, zoomed-in photo of Sanzu climbing down the stairs of the abandoned bowling alley took its place.

This was not good.

She rushed back to her office and stood in front of Sanzu. “Oi, they’ve found out our identities,” she said calmly. He jolted awake and sat up on the couch.

“What the fuck do you mean?”

“They know that you, Haruchiyo Sanzu, and I, Kurokawa Akari, are together and still in a relationship. And that we’re both part of Bonten.”

“Oh. That’s not too good.”

“Mhm,” she said, dragging him into the living area, where the TV presenters were discussing the new information.

“Who would’ve guessed a woman would be involved with this notorious criminal gang? How shocking,” the reporter said, turning to her partner in the studio.

“Very shocking indeed.” Her mugshot came back on the screen. “This photo dates back fifteen years or so. Hard to believe, but it was taken in a juvenile detention centre, where she was held for two years for the murder of her mother in cold blood. However, this photo doesn’t give much insight into what she looks like now,” the reporter sighed.

“How did they even take the mugshot with the mask on? Don’t they usually remove all accessories?”

“Usually, yes. This seems to be a different situation,” the presenter said with a small laugh. “Viewers, if you have any further information, please contact the police. Now, on to our next news—”

“Nice,” Koko sighed in defeat.

“That’s my line. But I’m more worried about the picture of Sanzu they showed.” Sanzu nodded in agreement.

“What’s so bad about—”

“It’s a photo from last night.” The rest of the executives stormed into the living area, some from the lift and some from their rooms.

“We just saw the news—”

“We know,” she said sharply.

“You two need to be much more careful now,” Mikey announced, appearing from his room.

“Of course.”

“Especially you, Akari. Now that you have an event to attend in a few days.” She nodded in agreement.

“Quick question,” Koko said, as all the attention turned to him. “I can’t help being a little curious. Why does your mugshot have your mask in it?”

Rindou, Ran, Kakucho and Mochi burst out laughing.

“Now this is a story to tell,” Mochi said, chuckling.

“It was quite interesting to watch it unfold,” Kakucho smiled.

She smiled at the memory. “I’m smarter than you think, Koko,” she said, pointing at her temple and tapping it with her finger. “I thought ahead and made sure my identity would be somewhat protected. Especially with a scar like this, anyone would spot me straight away. I fought all the officers—”

“You could hear her yelling and screaming swearwords of all sorts,” Ran chimed in, giving her a wide smile.

She shook her head, laughing. “Yeah, that too. I went totally berserk on them until they gave in. I was put in isolation for about a week, but it was totally worth it.” Everyone burst out laughing, including Mikey, who was chuckling to himself at the thought. She stole a glance at him and felt glad that he was laughing a little. “Anyway, that’s that. The other matter is that we were tailed.”

“The photo they showed of me was from last night, when we met Takemichi,” Sanzu said.

“This is dangerous. It means they’ll be close behind us,” Takeomi said, and the rest of them nodded.

“With the wedding coming up in a few days, we need to take the utmost caution,” Mikey concluded. “But other than that, there shouldn’t be any real cause for alarm.”

A WEEK LATER

DAY OF THE WEDDING

She pulled her black dress trousers up over her legs, tugged at the waistband and zipped up the fly. She took the crisp white dress shirt from the hanger on the metal rail in the wardrobe, threw it over her shoulders and pushed her arms through. She buttoned the front, leaving the top two buttons undone so the Bonten tattoo showed clearly. That was all part of the outfit. She threaded a belt through the loops and slid a gun between her body and the trousers, the way she always did. She took the blazer from the back of the chair and folded it over her forearm, then slipped on her high heels and hurried to the bathroom to apply some light makeup.

When she left the bathroom, she walked quickly to the living area, where Mikey and Sanzu were sitting.

“I’m about to leave now,” she said, and they turned to look at her. Sanzu didn’t answer. He just stared.

“What?” He stood, walked over and kissed her forehead.

“Beautiful,” he murmured. She put her hand on his face, pulled him down a little and kissed his lips. Her red lipstick stained them. She pulled away and smirked at her new masterpiece.

“Thanks, babe,” she said, winking. “I’ll see you later?”

He nodded. “Yeah. Be careful.”

Mikey walked over and took her jacket from her arm. He held it out in front of him and stuck a small tracker sticker on the underside of the collar, then handed her a remote. “Press this if something bad happens. It’ll alert us right away. Get rid of it as soon as you press it, so they don’t suspect anything. The tracker is always on. If you move away from the church without alerting us, I’ll assume something’s wrong—”

“Mikey, I’ll be fine.” She took the remote from his open palm and slipped it into her pocket. “I’m more than capable of looking after myself. But yes, I’ll keep everything in mind,” she sighed. Mikey handed her blazer back, and she folded it over her arm again. She turned away from the two of them and stepped into the lift. She gave them a wide smile as the doors closed.

The lift took her down to the garage, where she slid into the nearest car, started the engine with the key already in the ignition, and drove towards the wedding venue.

She stepped out of the car, and her heels clicked against the concrete. She closed the door softly, locked the car and slid the keys into her other trouser pocket. She looked at her reflection in the car window and redid her hair. She made a bun at the back of her head with the white half and let the black half fall over her shoulders. She hesitated over whether to bring her mask, then decided against it. She took a deep breath, gathered her courage and walked towards the church entrance, where the organisers were checking the guests’ names.

She lined up behind the others, shuffling forward bit by bit as the guests filed into the church. She was shaking inside. It was harder than she’d thought. By choosing to follow Mikey, she had

cut ties with everyone she had known from Toman. Meeting all of them at once was overwhelming. And there were people she had deliberately avoided.

“Excuse me? Name?” the organiser asked, staring a little too long at her face. Well, at her scar.

She gave him a small smile. “Is it alright if I see the list?”

“Ah, sure.” He handed her the clipboard. She ran her eyes down the page, spotting familiar names, until she found the one she was looking for. Mikey’s name.

“Yeah, that’s me.” She pointed at Mikey’s name.

Sano Manjiro.

“Are you sure—” He reached for the clipboard.

“That’s me,” she said, handing it back. Her smile stayed on her face, but her eyes said otherwise. The man shivered at her smile and still wasn’t convinced. Then she felt a hand on her shoulder. Startled, she grabbed the hand, gripped it tightly, spun round and pinned it against the person’s back. The man gave a wince of pain but chuckled a little.

“Yeah, this is Manjiro,” the man said, turning his head to look at her.

Draken.

### Thirty Six

“I see. Apologies, then,” the organiser said with a bow, and she let go of Draken’s hand. He shook out his arm and guided her inside the church, trying to keep the fuss to a minimum.

“He couldn’t come, huh?” Draken said painfully.

“I was afraid he’d massacre everyone here,” she replied softly. “Especially after he tried to kill Michi.”

He nodded slowly. “So you came instead.”

She hummed in response. The conversation had turned awkward in an instant. She stood beside him, unsure of what to say next. He walked to a round table and took a seat. Not knowing what else to do, she started to walk away, trying to slip out of the public eye and lean against the wall. But Draken didn’t let her, calling out to her again.

“Akari.” She turned and stared at him. “Your seat’s here.” He pointed at the chair beside him. She hesitated, then walked over and sat down.

She couldn’t help stressing about the situation. She buried her head in her hands as soon as she sat down and let out a stressed sigh.

“Calm down, Akari. It’ll be alright,” he assured her, trying his best to soothe her worries.

She looked up at him with wide eyes, taken aback by her own movement. “Is it really? You’re sitting with a ‘wanted woman,’ wanted for multiple crimes, including murder. Can you really say that after knowing it?”

He looked at her with understanding eyes. “I already know that. Most of the guests know it too. It’s a special day for Takemichi and Hinata, so the least you could do is attend. And you’re here. So there should be nothing else to worry about.”

“Easy for you to say. My being here is bringing trouble back to your peaceful lives.”

“Don’t forget Toman was once the best in Japan,” he said cheekily.

“Times have changed, Draken.” She sighed, took out her gun and showed it to him. “You won’t get anywhere without this nowadays.”

“You might want to hide that,” he said sharply, giving it a quick look before shooting her a dirty look.

“Sad to say, this little thing is my best friend.” She tucked the gun back into her waistband. “On a happier note, what are you doing now?” She knew he was running a motorbike shop with Inui, who hadn’t arrived yet.

“Oh, I’m running a motorbike shop, D&D Motors, with Inupi downtown. It’s going great,” he said. “I’ve been meaning to ask. Do you know Nakatani Hana?”

This might not end well.

“Yeah? She always saves us a VIP room at her club. Why?”

“She came to ours once to get her motorbike checked over. It was weird, because she had exactly the same bike as Mikey. And she had the same hair colour as you. Well, just the platinum bit.”

She let out a small sound. “Oh yeah, I did see her occasionally riding her bike home after work.”

“I see,” he answered quietly. He glanced round as the guests started to fill the room. The big group came through the doors. Draken stood and waved to them. Mitsuya, Hakkai, Yuzuha, Chifuyu and Kazutora smiled at him as they noticed him at the table. As they neared it, her leg began to shake furiously under the table, and she kept her head down. They gathered round the table, looked for their names and took their seats.

What?

She slowly lifted her head, and her eyes moved from one person to the next.

“Who are you?” Yuzuha asked, her voice laced with disgust.

She was taken aback by her tone, but she stood her ground. “It’s been a while, Yuzu. I’m here in Mikey’s place.”

“Akari…?” Yuzuha started, and she nodded slowly. Yuzuha began to tear up, stood up from her seat, rushed over and hugged her. She was confused.

Why are they treating you with such warmth?

I don’t deserve this warmth from them. I’ve killed hundreds of people. So why?

Why are they treating me like this?

Yuzuha wrapped her arms tightly round her neck and wept into her shoulder. She stood there, unsure of what to do. Hesitantly, she placed a hand on the back of Yuzuha’s head and patted it softly.

“I’m… fine. It’s good to see that you’re okay,” she mumbled. Yuzuha nodded, wiped her tears away and sat back down. Mitsuya, Hakkai, Chifuyu and Kazutora all nodded at her, a way of saying hello. As awkward as it was, it was expected. There was one empty spot at the table, which Inui quickly filled as he arrived just in time. He stood behind his chair and stared at her.

“What are you doing here?” She knew he wasn’t one to like her, or anyone involved with criminals.

“She’s here for the wedding in Mikey’s place,” Draken answered for her, as Inui took his seat.

The rest of the guests arrived, the lights dimmed, and the music started. The church doors opened wide, revealing Hina in a beautiful wedding gown. She walked slowly down the aisle with her father towards Michi, who was standing at the altar in a suit. Her father stepped aside at the front and took his seat with his wife and a younger man.

The two exchanged their vows, then took the matching rings. “Do you take Tachibana Hinata to be your lawfully wedded wife?”

“I do,” Michi answered, slipping the ring onto her finger.

“Do you take Hanagaki Takemichi to be your lawfully wedded husband?” “I do,” Hina replied with a smile, placing the ring on his finger.

“I now pronounce you husband and wife!” Takemichi and Hina exchanged a quick glance, and Michi looked round at the huge crowd in front of him.

“Kiss her!” Kazutora yelled, and the crowd burst out laughing. Takemichi began to weep as he leaned in and kissed his wife. She felt a small smile creep onto her face, and she started clapping. The crowd joined in, applauding and cheering. In the happy mood, the newlyweds took their seats as the cake was wheeled in. They cut the cake, and another round of applause rang round the church.

Some time later, the dancing began. Hina and Michi took to the floor and danced slowly to the slow music. It was sweet. Other couples and friends joined in. She backed away, feeling uncomfortable, and clumsily bumped into someone behind her.

“I’m sorry,” she apologised, turning round to look at the person she’d bumped into. Short blonde hair, piercing blue eyes, long and thick blonde lashes. She reminded her exactly of Sanzu.

“No, it’s okay,” the woman said, giving her a warm smile. That hurt. Suddenly two figures appeared behind her: one with lazy eyes, yellow and purple hair tied back neatly, chewing on a stick, and the other a large, muscular man with blonde hair in a buzz cut. They looked down at her and glared furiously. She stared back, not knowing who they were.

“Waka, Benkei, it’s fine,” the woman said, and their faces softened a little. Their names rang a few bells in her head, but she couldn’t remember where she had heard them. “I’ve never seen you around before. Who are you?”

“I-I’m Kurokawa Akari, nice to meet—” The woman gasped, stepped back and took a defensive stance.

“Why are you here?” she growled.

“I’m not here to cause a fuss. I’m attending the wedding in Mikey’s place.”

“Tch,” the woman clicked her tongue at the mention of Mikey’s name. “Bonten, huh?”

She nodded. The woman grabbed her wrist and dragged her away from the centre of attention, into a darker, quieter corner. She let go of her wrist and turned to face her. “How are Omi and Sanzu?” she asked, looking straight at her.

She was shocked. She knew more than she’d thought. “I can’t tell you that.”

“Just tell me if they’re alive or not. I have the right to know.”

“What’s your relation to them?”

“I’m Akashi Senju, the youngest of the Akashi siblings,” she said quickly, a little annoyed. Akari was stunned, because she had never known there was another sibling.

“Oh. Well, that’s not the greatest first impression. I’ll start again. I’m Kurokawa Akari, Haruchiyo Sanzu’s girlfriend of twelve years.” She held out her hand. Senju stared at it for a while, then accepted it.

“That’s you?” Her tone changed at once. “Oh my gosh! He told me back then that he had a girlfriend, but I never believed him! Nice to finally meet you!” She grabbed her hand tightly, then remembered she was part of Bonten and let go quickly.

“I’m not here to hurt anyone, don’t worry.” She tried to reassure her, but Senju was still hesitant. “So to answer your question, yes, they’re both alive and well. Sanzu had an incident a while back, but he’s fine now.”

“That’s good to hear. I haven’t heard or seen them at all in the last ten years, so I got a bit worried.”

“I’m shocked to learn there’s another Akashi sibling. This is the first I’ve heard of it. But you have some of the same features as Sanzu, for sure,” she said with a small smile.

“Twelve years, huh? That’s as long as those two lovebirds,” Senju said, pointing at Takemichi and Hina. “Are you planning to tie the knot any time soon?”

Akari flushed a little at the thought. Senju noticed and laughed politely. “We’ve talked about the future, but when you live and work in a dirty, dangerous environment, marriage and kids aren’t really a priority.”

Senju nodded in agreement. “Well, let those two idiots know I have a message for them. If that’s okay with you.” She nodded, saying it was. “Tell Omi to stop smoking. And tell Sanzu to man up.” Senju sent her a little wink, and she flushed with embarrassment.

“I-I’ll make sure to tell them.”

“Anyway, it was nice knowing you,” Senju said, turning and leaving with the two men from earlier. She stayed where she was, leaning against the wall and watching the dancers.

Before she knew it, her peace was disturbed as Michi appeared next to her. “What the hell? Michi?! Go back to dancing with Hina, this is your special day.” She tried to push him away, but he didn’t budge.

“I just wanted to say thanks for coming. It must have been difficult to see everyone again,” he said quietly. She fell silent and nodded.

“You probably won’t see me again after this, so it’s the least I can do, I guess.”

In the middle of their awkward conversation, an ear-piercing scream rang out from the crowd. She looked round and saw a ring of guests gathered in the middle of something. She knew this wasn’t good news.

She pushed through the crowd, with Michi right behind her. At the front, Hina was leaning against a taller man in a black suit, with a gun held to her head. A louder voice boomed from the corner.

“Police!” She turned her head and saw the younger man who had been sitting at the family table earlier.

“Naoto…” Michi whispered. She assumed the officer was Hina’s younger brother. He was holding a gun, aimed at the intruder’s head, but his hands were trembling. One wrong move and his sister would be gone. She sighed in defeat, moved to the front of the crowd, and gasps rang out.

“Let her go,” she demanded, looking at the intruder.

“No.”

“Take me instead.” She slid her hand into her waistband slowly and took out her handgun even more slowly. The crowd stepped back as they saw the gun. She crouched down and set the gun

on the floor. She slipped her hand into her trouser pocket and pressed the button on the remote Mikey had given her. She took out her car keys and phone, and quickly threw the remote in Draken’s direction. She gave him a pleading look. He gave her a small, understanding nod and quietly picked it up. Thankfully, the man didn’t notice.

“Take me instead,” she repeated, watching him loosen his grip on Hina. He suddenly shoved Hina away towards her. She rushed to her, making sure she wouldn’t hurt herself.

“Akari…” Hina said, her lower lip trembling.

“I’ll be fine, don’t worry,” she said with a reassuring smile. “Congratulations, by the way.” She stood up and walked towards the intruder.

“Who are you?” The man wasn’t stupid. He might already have known who she was, and was just taking extra precautions, though killing an innocent person didn’t matter to him. She pulled down her shirt, revealing the Bonten tattoo.

“Is this enough for you?” He smirked at her, walked over, roughly pinned her hands behind her back, pressed the gun to her head and pushed her out through the church doors. The crowd’s murmurs and gossip started, but they were quickly silenced as the door closed behind her.

He dragged her outside to a car. Before he put her into it, he handcuffed her wrists behind her back.

How annoying.

She clicked her tongue, and he pressed the gun harder into her head. “Why do you even want me?” she asked, already knowing the answer.

“To kill you, after taking all the information about your group. Money as well. Unless the boss has other orders.”

“You must be part of a gang, then,” she said, trying to pull information out of him without him realising.

“Kurayami Group.” He slapped a hand over his mouth the moment he realised what she had done. “You’re done.” She chuckled in her head and squirmed in her seat as the car pulled away from the venue. The windows were heavily tinted, so she couldn’t see out at all. She could only guess where she was.

The car finally slowed to a halt. The door slid open from outside, and a younger man pulled her out in a rush. “Hurry up and get out.” She had no choice but to obey as he led her into a large building. He took her down the stairs to a lower, darker floor and threw her into a room lit by a single candle that gave almost no light. He closed the door and locked it, and she heard his footsteps disappear back up the stairs.

She was completely confused about what was happening, but escaping was the priority. She squirmed and twisted her wrists as much as she could, but it was no use. Instead, she searched

the room for anything she could use to break the handcuffs. Then she remembered that she had a bobby pin in her hair today.

What luck!

She shook her head, trying to loosen it, and used her shoulder to work it free. It came out. She turned round, picked it up with her hands and pried it open against the edge of a table in the room. Once it was straight, she pushed it into the handcuffs and started to work it around.

It took a while, but the small click of the cuffs coming apart brought her a rush of joy. She smiled, free at last, and got ready for her next move. She picked up the candle between two fingers and moved it round the room to look for anything useful. A table, a chair and the candle. She searched the table’s drawers but found nothing.

Sighing, she picked up the chair, set it on the edge of the table, making sure the legs stuck out, and lifted her leg and brought her foot down hard on one leg of the chair until it snapped. She did the same with the other three legs.

She put the candle back on the desk, picked up the bobby pin again and began fiddling with the door lock. Then footsteps came back. Knowing time was limited, she grabbed one of the chair legs, hid behind the door and held the leg like a baseball bat.

The jingle of keys outside the door made her tense, ready to put every ounce of force into what she was about to do. The door swung slowly open, and the man stepped inside. The dark worked in her favour, because he couldn’t adjust his eyes fast enough. She swung hard, and the chair leg struck him over the head. He slumped to the floor at once.

She grabbed the keys he’d been holding and shoved them into her pocket. She also took the handgun from his holster and tucked it into her trousers. She quickly took the handcuffs from earlier and fastened them round his wrists behind his back. She dragged him to the far corner of the room, away from the door. There she picked up the candle, smirked, and held the flame over his head and chest. His hair caught fire, and so did his clothes. She propped the chair legs around him, just in case.

Laughing, she left the room and closed the door behind her.

### Thirty Seven

Sanzu POV

A loud beep was all it took for me to jolt up in my seat and watch the small red dot on the screen begin to move.

“Boss! She’s pressed the button!” I yelled, and the executives rushed to the computer screen in front of me. Mikey walked over and stared, watching the red dot intently.

“Let’s go. We’re going to get her back,” he announced after a while, as the dot began to move faster.

“She’s in a car now.”

I nodded, and the others began getting ready to bring her back. I grabbed the computer, then my sword and gun, as always, and headed down to the car park.

Please be safe, sweetheart.

Akari POV

She hid behind a corner, keeping to the shadows in the hallway as the guards walked back and forth. She crept from corner to corner, gripping the gun tightly. When she got close enough to one guard, she struck him with the hilt of her gun, and he slumped to the floor. The sound of him falling was loud enough to draw the attention of the other man. He drew his gun and walked slowly towards the unconscious guard, then grabbed his walkie-talkie and began talking into it.

“Hiru here, intruder—” She shot him in the middle of his distraction. The bullet pierced his neck, and he was as good as dead. Once the alarm had been raised, it wasn’t long before she was in an all-out brawl. She grabbed the dead man’s gun and the unconscious man’s gun, reloaded while she was at it, and crept down the hallway, trying to find a way out.

“She’s here!” a man yelled, pointing at her. She ducked into the corner just in time, as bullets showered down and chipped at the wall. When the shooting paused for a reload, she leaned out and fired with impeccable aim, and the men dropped one by one.

This went on until she was almost out of bullets. She had six left, and eight men were still standing. Waiting for the next break was nerve-wracking, but she had no choice.

When the break came, she stood up and ran out of the corner straight at them. A few of them were so surprised to see her come out of hiding that they reached for their guns, but it was already too late. She fired her six bullets at six men, hitting each one in a vital spot. Blood poured everywhere. She hopped over the bodies and stepped through their blood, which splashed across her face and her white shirt, which was no longer white. The two remaining men stood frozen in shock.

She threw her empty gun at one of them with full force, and it hit him square in the face. She spun round and delivered a strong kick in a whirlwind motion, and he flew back against the wall with a heavy thud. He was out cold. The other man was clutching his nose, which was probably broken by the gun. She had no time to lose. She rushed at him, raising her arm for a knockout punch.

It connected, only just. Another second, and a bullet would have gone straight through her lower stomach. That would have been fatal.

There was no time to lose. She picked up the men’s weapons and reloads, knowing there was more to come. She wiped most of the blood from her face with her sleeve and pushed through the bloody corridor, hoping she would be close to getting out.

Draken POV

The wedding was a mess after she was taken away. Hina and Takemichi were worried about Akari, and so was most of the crowd, even though she was part of Bonten. I had picked up Akari’s gun, which the man had carelessly left behind, along with her phone and some kind of remote. I pressed the button to turn on her phone. Her lock screen showed a photo from twelve years ago, at the beach, when Izana was still alive. Not wanting to invade her privacy any more than I already had, I tried to call her emergency contacts, but there were none.

Of course, she didn’t.

I mentally face-palmed at my own stupidity. Not able to do anything, I tucked her phone, gun and remote into my pocket.

“What should we do, Draken-kun?” Takemichi asked, comforting the distraught Hina.

I let out a sigh. “I think it’s best not to get involved, Takemitchy. It’ll be better for her and for us. I’m pretty sure the other Bonten members can take care of it,” I replied, hiding my worry for her.

The rest of the crowd was hesitant about continuing the wedding, afraid of Bonten or other gang members crashing it. Some were considering leaving. I mean, who would want to stay and risk being annihilated? But many chose to stay, out of respect for the newlyweds and because Akari had protected Hina.

Something bad was happening with Bonten, and many of us old Toman members had realised it. Bonten had probably butted heads with other gangs before, but we all knew this was different.

Mitsuya came up to me while I was deep in thought. “This new gang is more dangerous than we know,” he said. I nodded, waiting for him to go on. “I’ve never seen a picture of the Bonten members on TV. Ever.”

“If you exclude Manjiro’s picture, then yeah.”

“They have two identities of their members, excluding Mikey. That must be a blow for them,” he went on, thinking aloud.

I shook my head. “We’re not getting involved with them. If Takemichi’s words are the truth about Mikey, then it’s best not to intervene.” Mitsuya nodded in agreement.

“Let’s just hope nothing bad happens. They were our friends back then, after all,” he said, giving a small smile as he remembered those days twelve years ago.

Akari POV

She threw a bullet dud from behind the corner and listened to it hit the floor. Plink, plink, plink. The men’s attention turned instantly to the sound. The moment they turned their heads, she fired, and the bullets pierced their heads. They dropped to the floor, and blood stained the carpet. She rushed through the dark hallway and came face to face with another man. She shot him, but out of shock, so the shot didn’t kill him. He let out a loud yell of pain, and reinforcements arrived at once.

This was one huge gang.

She fired back as a shower of bullets came from both ends of the hall. When she heard the groans of the men on their side, she quickly peeked to count them. Three men.

She did what she had done before. She rushed at them in a zigzag to make herself harder to hit. She shot two bullets into one man, and the other two watched him fall. She pulled off her jacket and threw it at one of the two remaining men, blocking his view. He fired through the jacket to protect himself. She ducked and sat on the ground, shooting at the other man, then fired at the man behind the jacket. They both fell to the floor. Dead. Their blood bubbled out of their wounds, dripping down their faces and onto the carpet.

Ignoring the blood on the carpet and on her body, she stood and moved into the next corridor. It led her to a grand staircase, with marble steps and a red carpet running down the centre. It was tempting to go up the stairs, but there was no time. More men were patrolling the ground around the foot of the staircase, and she didn’t have much ammunition left.

Sanzu POV

I watched the screen intently as the car rocked from side to side, taking turn after turn towards her location. It was a mansion on the outskirts of Tokyo. Her tracker, which was stuck to her jacket, was moving much more slowly inside the mansion. Then it stopped.

“She stopped moving,” I said, getting more and more worried about my girlfriend.

“What do you mean she stopped moving?” Rindou asked from the passenger seat.

I couldn’t deal with his question right now. “Literally what I said. Her tracker stopped moving.”

“She better be alive,” Koko said, gritting his teeth.

“You better not jinx it, asshole,” I growled, gripping the computer tightly, hoping and praying for some movement.

Akari POV

She was hiding in the shadows underneath the grand staircase, but the hiding hadn’t gone well. She was dripping in the blood of the men she had just killed, and her shirt was only freckled with white now. The blood that kept dripping down from her face wasn’t hers, though. It was a miracle she had made it this far, perfectly fine and uninjured. If only she had some way to tell the Bonten members who were coming here.

Her trail of footprints to the staircase had been careless. The alternative was to stay hidden in the corner of the hallway and wait to be shot from behind, so she had little choice. It wasn’t long before the men spotted her trail. They began hollering to let the others know she was hiding behind the staircase. She held them off for as long as she could, shooting each one who opened his mouth. But the loud bangs of the gun weren’t helping. She wished she had brought her silencer.

The men kept coming and dying, and she was running out of ammunition. She had no choice but to make a run for the exit. She looked left and right from under the staircase and slowly emerged at the bottom of it. She glanced up at the main exit and saw no one there. Perfect. She swiftly ran up the stairs, taking two at a time.

Then suddenly she was no longer running up the stairs. She was falling. She put her hands out in front of her face to brace for the impact. She looked down at her thigh and saw a bullet had torn through it. Blood gushed out furiously. On instinct, she pulled her belt free and tightened it just above the wound, biting her lip against the pain. The bleeding slowed to a trickle, giving her some time.

She looked round and saw a tall man with dark features standing at the top of the staircase. He hadn’t been there earlier.

“Finally, nice to meet you, Kurokawa Akari. Advisor of Bonten.” His deep voice boomed through the open space and echoed off the marble. She just stared at him, with no idea who he was. She could only guess that he was connected to the Kurayami Gang. “You must be wondering who I am,” he said, walking down the stairs, taking each step painfully slowly, as if he were exaggerating his entrance. Eventually he reached her level and stood tall over her injured body. His gaze travelled over her face. After studying it intently, he suddenly grabbed her hair and dragged her down the staircase. The sting on her scalp was terrible, but at least it hid the pain in her thigh for the time being. It left a trail of blood, her blood, across the already red carpet.

He finally let go of her hair, and she dropped to the floor heavily. He stood over her, watching her squirm. “I never thought I’d live to see the day I’d be looking down on a Bonten member,” he said with a scoff, before laughing. “How pitiful, to see you in such a state.”

As if a switch had flicked, he began to kick her. Again and again. She curled into a ball, protecting her belly as much as she could, just in case. He kicked her with rage until he calmed down enough to notice her strange behaviour. She heard him crouch to her level. She opened her eyes a crack, and he immediately grabbed her chin and lifted her face to his. She turned her head to the side and spat out the blood that had gathered in her mouth. He forced her head back round to face him, and she felt his breath on her face.

He grinned evilly. “Are you pregnant?” he asked, in a menacing tone.

She had no choice but to answer. “I’m assuming so,” she replied weakly, as the pain began to take hold.

“Have you run a test?”

“Didn’t have the time to yet,” she said truthfully.

He let go of her chin, and she held herself up with her hands to stop herself from hitting the floor. “You’re coming with me. To Australia.”

This man was clever. He was taking full advantage of her condition, forcing her to go with him to Australia. If there was a chance she was carrying a baby, her body would deteriorate and change as it prepared to carry and support a child. She wouldn’t be able to act the way she wanted, and any risk to the baby would be unbearable.

“You don’t have a choice,” he added, making sure she fully understood. Normally she would accept her fate and wait for the perfect chance to attack, even if it meant dying. But the words Sanzu had whispered in her ear a week ago, on the couch in her office, as he held her hands above her head with their fingers intertwined, made her second-guess her decision to leave this world. They gave her the mental strength to live. She wanted the days when she, Sanzu and a possible child could live together.

“How long?” she asked, her body almost giving out from the pain and blood loss.

She saw the smile spread across his face as he realized she was going to comply. “As long as it takes to deal with the business I have over there. Shortest, two years. All depends on you, and whether you’d help me or not.”

She couldn’t help but nod slowly. He let out a boisterous laugh, and she looked up at the sound of it, her eyes slowly starting to fail her. It was now or never. Behind her body, she began to write a small message in her own blood, hoping that Bonten would find it.

“We’re leaving now. We’ll treat your leg on the way,” he said, snapping his fingers as three men ran towards him. She instinctively hid the message with her body. One man pulled her away from the floor, while another shoved his fingers into her mouth and forced her to swallow. A pill.

Before long she succumbed to the pill and faded out. A warm tear slipped down her cheek, and she wished Sanzu could have been there to wipe it away.

### Thirty Eight

Sanzu POV

The car finally arrived at the mansion, but everyone knew something was wrong. The gate at the entrance had been busted wide open, and not a single light was on in the house. We all got out of the car and made our way to the main entrance, weapons raised. Rindou and Ran burst open the front door, turning their backs to us as they swiftly aimed their guns into the mansion.

“No one’s here,” Ran whispered, starting to make his way inside. We all spread out, and I headed down the stairs. It wasn’t hard to notice the heaps of bodies lying on the cold marble

floor. I rushed over to look at them. Every one of them had a single shot to the head, perfectly in the centre of the forehead.

No one could shoot that perfectly. Except Akari.

I bent down and touched one of the bodies. It was still warm. Akari could have been here at any time in the last two hours. But her tracker had stopped moving half an hour ago, which meant we had just missed her.

“FUCK!” I yelled, pulled out my gun and emptied the whole cartridge into the pile of dead bodies. They flinched as the bullets kept entering them, making more holes for their blood to escape.

She was gone—

“Boss! We found her jacket!” Takeomi said, coming out of the corridor with her jacket in his arms. “Found it on top of a pile of bodies.” He was out of breath, presumably from running a few metres.

He handed me the jacket. I checked the pockets and found nothing. It had a single bullet hole through the back. I breathed out, relieved that the hole had been made by her, and not that she was injured.

I found myself hugging her jacket tightly when Kakucho found another clue on the marble floor. We all crowded round it, since it was the most useful thing we’d found. It was scribbled in blood on the marble, most likely her blood.

?? (?????? Kurayami?

“What’s this?” Mikey asked, as we all studied it.

“This is Akari’s handwriting. I can assure you,” I said, bending down and touching the blood. It was still fresh.

“Kurayami…” Rindou whispered beside me.

Kakucho shook his head. “Doesn’t ring any bells, but if she wrote it down, we can assume it’s the gang responsible for taking her.”

We found no more clues in the mansion, so we had no choice but to return to HQ, with no information about Akari except the so-called Kurayami Gang.

### Thirty Nine

Akari POV

It had been a couple of days since she arrived in Sydney, Australia. The ten-hour flight had been excruciating. She sat in a window seat in business class, which Ichinose, the boss of Kurayami, had arranged. Thankfully, it was a compartment for her alone, so she had all the privacy she

could ask for. But the pain from her wound was almost unbearable, and the vibrations of the aeroplane had made it reopen.

Still, nobody suspected a thing about the fake passport Ichinose had organised in under half an hour. Even she thought that was incredible. She had looked out of the window as they landed, and the runway reflected the orange colour of the setting sun.

After they left the airport, she sat in a taxi beside Ichinose, and the change in scenery was striking. She had never been here, and she had never thought about it, so the view shocked her. Nothing could have prepared her for the difference in environment, from the trees to the animals to the way the streets were laid out.

She sat on the edge of her new bed, looking out of the window at the darkening sky, the light slowly draining away. She heard a knock on the door, and she had no choice but to let him in. “Come in.”

“Here,” Ichinose said, throwing her a box, which she caught easily. She looked at it. A pregnancy test. “Test yourself, so we can meet your needs,” he explained, then closed the door and left.

She sat on the bed, shocked and speechless at his calm demeanour, despite having kidnapped her and moved her to the other side of the world. She couldn’t understand why Ichinose had brought her here in the first place.

Why?

She went into the bathroom with the test. Unboxing it was nerve-wracking, and so was the stick itself. She read the instructions and followed them.

A few minutes later, the stick showed a positive result. As expected. She wanted to rejoice, because this was the child she and Sanzu had always wanted. But the timing was terrible. She had just been kidnapped, and she was injured too. This was the moment she most wanted Sanzu’s comfort.

Ichinose’s treatment of her here wasn’t as bad as she’d expected. She had assumed he would lock her in her room for the next nine months and give her the bare minimum to survive, her and the child. But no.

He had given her everything she needed, all the basics. In return, he expected her to behave: to follow his instructions, to work in his office and to tell him the details of Bonten she had no choice but to reveal.

Of course, it pained her to talk about Bonten to someone who had taken her away from them. And it terrified her that Mikey might kill her if she ever returned, since she had betrayed them. Sanzu despised her most of all.

A lowly traitor.

“Do this for me,” Ichinose said, entering with a tall stack of paperwork, which he set on her desk. She stared at it and then back at him. “Two hours. You’re pregnant, not disabled,” and he

left the room. She was irritated by his rudeness but had no choice but to comply. She couldn’t move around much in her current state anyway. The plane ride had worsened her bullet wound and opened it wider than she wanted, so it would take longer to heal.

She had no choice but to do the work he had assigned, sitting at her desk. He had said it himself before they left Japan: “All depends on you, and whether you’d help me or not.” She picked up her pen and stamp and started flicking through the pages, signing and stamping over and over.

Ran POV

I watched Sanzu leave his room for the first time in three days. His body was weak and frail, his legs looking as if they might give out under him. I doubted he had eaten anything in three days. The bedroom door closed behind him as he stumbled into the kitchen. He leaned against the counter, grabbed a glass from the drying rack and placed it under the tap. The water began to fill.

He was staring right at me, but his eyes didn’t meet mine. He seemed to be avoiding eye contact with everyone. He kept the glass under the tap, and the water filled it quickly. He didn’t even notice that it was already full, and water spilled over the edge. I sighed heavily, pushed myself off the couch and turned off the tap. He trudged back towards his room, each step heavy and painfully slow. The overfilled glass spilled water onto the floor as it trailed behind him. The whiteness of his knuckles showed his emotions, even though his face was blank and empty.

He closed the door behind him softly, and the living area went quiet. The dripping of the tap was the only sound keeping the room alive. Drip, drip, drip. I leaned over the counter and watched the drops fall from the tap, gather at the bottom of the sink and swirl away down the drain, never to be seen again. It was mesmerising and distracting, but it was painful to watch. It was like watching the life drain out of someone, waiting for it to disappear completely.

I couldn’t imagine what Sanzu was going through. She might not be blood-related to him, but I knew for a fact that he loved her deeply, and losing her was like losing half of himself. I wasn’t surprised he had locked himself in his room for three days. I would do the same if I lost Rindou. I don’t think I’d ever be able to stand up again, so I would follow him wherever he went. We’ve stuck together since birth, so I’d follow him to the end.

I felt my nails digging into my palm at the thought of losing him. I was terrified by it.

After the incident three days ago, we had searched desperately for any news or information about the Kurayami gang. We even ended up asking Hanma for help, but it came to nothing. There was no trace of anything. Because of Akari’s disappearance, Mikey had forced the FNN club to shut down until she came back. We were all hoping for her return.

Curiosity got the better of me, and I knocked on Sanzu’s door. There was no sound of footsteps on the other side, only sniffling, which I assumed were tears.

“I’m coming in,” I said, turning the knob and pushing the door open. He was sitting on the floor, leaning over the table. White powder was lined up near his face. He turned his head to look at me, with bloodshot eyes.

“What do you want, Haitani?” he spat, in a dangerous tone. I was taken aback, not by his voice but by what he did next. He reached for the gun lying beside the drugs and pointed it at me.

“Everyone’s worried about you,” I said. It wasn’t a complete lie, but it wasn’t the whole truth either. “At least eat something before you die of starvation.”

“There’s no point living if she’s not here with me,” he growled.

“No one said she was dead,” I said, and saw his eyes twitch. “Stop assuming things and have some hope in your woman. Hold on tight to the last thing she whispered to you. And live, so you can see her again.”

He stared at me again, more intensely than before. I watched him hesitate, then stuff the powder into a small plastic bag and shove it into his pocket. I left his room and went back to sit on the living room couch, where Koko was sitting now.

“How’s he doing?” he asked as I took a seat opposite him. I shook my head.

“He’s not doing much better than when you last saw him. But I think he’ll be all right soon. I hope,” I murmured, as Koko went back to his work. I sighed heavily and let my mind wander.

Hope she’s really okay.

### Forty

Sanzu POV

I pulled up at the front of the mansion and noticed a black car parked outside the property. It wasn’t one of Bonten’s. Someone else was here. I got out with my sword and handgun and went through the overgrown front garden. The grass was tall enough to cover me if I lay down, so I did. There was a path through the grass, recently flattened, leading to the main entrance.

I slipped through the open gap in the front door, keeping to the shadows. The bloodstains from the men Akari had killed were still there, but we had already disposed of the bodies. Faint shuffling echoed from the hallway on my right. Further down, the dark corridor was broken by a small light from an open door, where the room had its lights on. It was strange.

“Drug import paperwork?” a voice said softly, while the rustle of papers drowned out the man’s words. I heard another man’s voice in the distance, presumably on the phone, giving instructions.

“How’s the woman doing?” the voice asked. I moved closer to the doorframe to listen. I peeked round the edge and saw the man had his back turned to the door. I took a few quick steps, hooked my arm round his neck and pressed the gun to his forehead.

“Wha—” He dropped the phone, which clattered onto the floor. Papers were scattered across the desk. I ordered him to pick up the phone, and I crouched down to keep him compliant. He held it out with a shaking hand, and I pressed the speakerphone button.

“What was that?” the man on the other end asked, sounding suspicious.

I nudged the man with the tip of my gun. “Oh, I saw a roach and freaked out. Sorry, boss.” The boss sighed and went on.

“Did you find the paperwork?”

“Yep, I found it. Would you like me to email it to you?” he asked, trembling in my arms. I leaned in close to him.

“Ask again about the woman,” I whispered in his ear, and he shivered.

“Yes, thank you,” the boss answered.

“How’s the woman?” he asked, almost cutting off the boss’s words.

There was a small silence on the other end. “I don’t know. She went into labour earlier this morning. She could be dead for all I know.” He laughed, and I nearly dropped the gun.

Labour…?

The man in my grip forced out a laugh too, going along with the boss. “Would you like anything else sent, or is the paperwork all?”

“That’ll be all. Thanks.” The call ended at once. I grabbed the phone from his hand and threw it against the wall, hearing it crack. I pressed the gun to the man’s temple.

“Answer my questions, and I might let you die quickly,” I growled, gripping the gun so tightly that the trigger shook under my finger.

He nodded quickly, and I forced him to sit down in the chair. I stood against the wall and kept the gun on his head. “Is this woman you referred to the one the boss took from here about ten months ago?”

“Yes,” he answered at once, keeping it to one word.

So Akari is safe for the time being.

“What gang are you and the boss part of?”

“Kurayami.”

“Where is the boss right now?”

“I can’t answer that,” he said calmly.

“I’ll ask again. Where is the boss right now?”

“I can’t answer—” My finger pulled the trigger, and the bullet went through his foot. He screamed. I decided to ask a different question. “What were the papers for?”

“Drug importation documents.”

“What for?”

“The boss is planning to import drugs from his current residence into Japan, as a business.” He was smart. He answered without telling me where the boss was living.

“Why are you still here, and not with the boss?”

He stayed quiet for a while before speaking. “He ordered the men of Kurayami to stay here in Japan. He’s the only one who moved overseas—”

“So he’s overseas?”

The man slapped a hand over his mouth, realizing too late what he’d said. “…Yeah.”

“So I just need to kill the boss, and Kurayami would be finished. Correct?”

“Correct,” the man answered.

“One last thing,” I said, lowering the gun. “Send that email for me. Now.” The man scrambled to the laptop in front of him, typed for a while and sent the email to the boss. He turned the screen to me. I glanced at the email and back at him.

“Thank you so much for all your help,” I said with a smile. He seemed to know his time was up.

“No, no, no! Please spare m—” I emptied the cartridge into him, and blood poured from every hole.

“Serves you right for taking my woman,” I snarled, furious. I grabbed the laptop, closed the lid, left the room and headed for the car. If it hadn’t been for that strange tingle down my spine earlier, I would never have learned any of this. I drove back to HQ as fast as I could.

The lift opened on the top floor, and I rushed out and dropped into one of the chairs at the dining table.

“What’s the ruuuuush, Sanzuuu?” Ran stumbled towards me, alcohol on his breath.

I pushed him away. “Fuck off. Come back to me when you’re sober.” He fell to the floor and immediately dozed off.

“So did you find something?” Kakucho asked. He looked over my shoulder at the laptop in front of me.

“Yeah. I found out that Kurayami’s boss is overseas. With Akari.” Kakucho’s eyes widened at her name.

“You know where she is?”

I shook my head. “She’s alive, right?”

“Yeah, she gave birth this morning, apparently.”

“I see. That’s good.” He answered, but didn’t take in what I’d said. “Wait. She gave birth?!”

I nodded and kept staring at the screen. Kakucho’s voice had drawn the attention of the other sober executives. “Akari was pregnant?” Rindou asked again.

“Didn’t you use protection, Sanzu?” Koko asked, one eyebrow raised. “What was the point of her buying that huge box of condoms if you don’t use them?” He sighed.

“Maybe if you hadn’t barged into her office that morning, I would have reminded her to take the morning-after pill,” I snapped.

“Hey, that’s your responsibility, not mine.”

“Do we even know it’s yours?” Rindou asked, and I immediately looked at him with deadly eyes.

The silence that followed was thick with dread. “Sorry,” Rindou said, turning his head away.

“What matters most is that she’s fine and alive,” Mikey said, walking into the living room and listening to the conversation. “She might not be back for a while, but it’s good to know she’s well.”

“Stay positive,” Koko added.

Yeah…

Akari POV

ONE YEAR LATER

Yuuma was sleeping peacefully in her arms, his small, calm breaths easing her too. The past year had been difficult. He woke in the middle of the night for one o’clock feeds, and that was before the nappy changes. Some nights she was so desperate for sleep that it took every ounce of willpower not to leave him crying in his room.

Chloe had been there to help too. She made the meals for both of them and took care of other little details that Akari felt comfortable asking her for. It felt wrong to wake her in the middle of the night to settle Yuuma. But now he was a year old, and much easier to handle. About three months ago he had started saying a few words, like his name, a basic greeting, and calling for her or Chloe when he wanted attention. It would have been nice for Sanzu to witness all the milestones Yuuma had reached this past year.

In recent months, Akari had been planning Ichinose’s murder so she could finally go home. Determined to make the murder a success, she pushed her body as hard as she could to regain the fitness she had before the birth. It was difficult, since she had motherly duties on top of it, but Yuuma, being the curious child he was, joined in. He copied her movements as she practiced kicks and punches with Chloe, who was happy to help her get back into shape without any idea what Akari was really planning. It was sweet to watch him kick his little foot while she unleashed her own.

Wiping the sweat from her forehead with her wrist, she grabbed her water bottle and handed Yuuma his. “Yuuma, here.” He stretched out his arms and fumbled with the bottle. She sighed at how cute he was and showed him how to open it before passing it back. He brought it to his lips and gulped greedily. “Calm down a little,” she said, taking the water from him so he could breathe and didn’t drown.

She drank from her own bottle, feeling Yuuma’s eyes on her as he grabbed his bottle back from her and copied her again. “You’ve been very motivated these last few months,” Chloe said, taking off the pads from her arms and legs.

“Ahh, yes. About that. I’ve been meaning to tell you,” Akari said calmly, glancing at her son, who was starting to doze off on the floor. “Give me a couple of minutes, and I’ll get back to you on it.” She waited for Yuuma to fall asleep, because she didn’t want to expose him to anything harsh just yet. He seemed to realize he was falling asleep, crawled over to the space between her legs, curled into a ball and laid his head on her thigh. She looked at his terrible posture, lifted him onto her chest and rocked him back and forth.

“So what is it?” Chloe asked. Akari took a deep breath before explaining.

“You know I’m part of a criminal organization.” Chloe nodded. “I have no idea how long Ichinose wants me here, but I’m not planning on staying any longer. I can’t.”

There was a moment of silence while Chloe worked out what she was getting at. “So you’re planning on, um, killing him?” Akari nodded. “Oh.”

“Yeah, I just want to go home. I can’t stand Yuuma being without a father for so long. Not to mention, I miss him too.”

“I see. Uhh, when and how are you planning to kill him?” Chloe asked, a little hesitantly. “Do I have to play a part in any of this?”

Akari let out a nervous laugh. “I just need you to take care of Yuuma for the night. He should be asleep, so there shouldn’t be any cause for concern.” She thought about it a little more, then realised a major part of the plan needed Chloe. “Is that—”

“One more thing,” Akari interrupted.

“What’s that?”

“Are you coming to Japan with me?”

Chloe took a while to answer, but then said yes. “I’ll have nowhere to stay, but I’m willing to try something new.” She smiled.

“Great, because accommodation will be the least of your worries.”

“What do you mean?”

“I mean you can live with me. Well, us.”

“Us as in Bonten…?”

“Yeah. I’m sure I mentioned it before, but all the executive members live together. It’ll be great having you around too. I love the company, since I haven’t had female company like this in a very long time. It does mean you’ll be associated with criminals, which brings me to my final point.”

Chloe stayed quiet, then got to the point Akari was building towards. “You’re saying you’re going to expose me to—” She pointed in the direction of Ichinose’s office. “His body, as practice for what’s to come?”

“Bingo!” Akari said, a little more excited than she should have been. “I mean, at the end of the day, it’s just a dead body. You won’t have to see me kill him, at least. I’m not the nicest person.” Chloe shivered and shuffled away from her. Not a surprise.

It was hard to imagine a female murderer with a sleeping child in her arms, but that was the situation. “So are you in?” Akari asked, rocking back and forth with Yuuma, who was sleeping, completely unaware of the careful planning going on around him.

“How about the tickets, and the passports and other important docume—”

“I’ll have all of that sorted by tomorrow night.”

“That quickly?” Chloe asked. “There’s no way documents can be forged or created that fast.”

Akari laughed. “You underestimate what Bonten can do, Chloe.”

“Wait, so you’re planning to kill him tonight?!” Chloe exclaimed in shock.

“Mhm. The faster the better,” Akari said.

Chloe’s mouth fell open. She hadn’t expected to see a dead body so soon. “Ookay,” she stumbled out. “What are you using?”

“That’s something I still have to think about. I want him to suffer as much as possible,” Akari scoffed, her eyes going dark for a second, which made Chloe squeak.

“I’ll make sure I never get on your bad side,” Chloe said, and Akari let out a stifled laugh.

“That goes for pretty much anyone in Bonten.” She fell quiet, then recapped the plan for later tonight. “So, tonight. We eat dinner together as normal. We do our after-dinner routine as normal. I’ll put Yuuma to bed, and I need you to read him his bedtime story, like I always do. Then close the door. I should be done by the time you finish the book.”

“And then you’ll come back to the room all bloody, and Yuuma will ask what happened tomorrow morning?”

“Oh, god, no.” Akari laughed at Chloe’s skeptical humor. “I’ll wash myself up, then come and get you. You’ll see the body, and then I’ll call home. Order the tickets and get the documents. And the rest is easy.”

“Okay. It seems simple enough. I’ll do my best.”

“Perfect. Now that everything is in place, all we have to do is wait for things to unfold tonight.” She smiled as she said it.

### Forty One

She was sitting in front of the TV with Yuuma lying with his head in her lap while she brushed his teeth. He was watching the TV, or trying to.

“Yuuma, stop moving your head so much,” she said, trying to keep him still for a second. He did listen, but then stared right back at her with a concentrated face and those beautiful blue eyes he had inherited from his father. She took the toothbrush out of his mouth, and he sat up straight away and swallowed. (She had brushed his teeth with water, so it was fine.)

She stood up from the couch to take his toothbrush to the bathroom and put it in its holder, but Yuuma clung to her leg so tightly that she couldn’t move. “Mummy,” he mumbled, gripping even harder. She looked down at him and gave him a soft smile.

“I’m not going anywhere, Yuuma,” she said. She lifted him up, carried him on one arm, and pushed open the bathroom door with the other hand. She set him down on the vanity, his legs hanging over the edge, and he watched her every move as she rinsed his toothbrush.

She looked at herself in the mirror and noticed how much her hair had grown over the past two years. She really needed to get it touched up.

“Mummy,” Yuuma called again, and she looked over at him.

“Hmm?” He made grabby hands at her, and she sighed and picked him up again. “Time to sleep, Yuuma.”

He let out a small hum or a groan, she couldn’t tell which. But bedtime wasn’t going to change. Today especially. She walked back into the living room, where Chloe had just finished washing up after tonight’s meal. Chloe glanced over, and she nodded and shuffled into Yuuma’s room. She leaned forward, put him in his cot and laid the blanket over him. Chloe came in holding a book and sat down beside the cot. She switched on the night light and turned off the main light, leaving just enough to see the words on the page. Akari bent down, kissed Yuuma’s forehead, and gave Chloe a warm smile. Chloe smiled back and started to read. Akari closed the door behind her, and her face changed at once.

She went to the kitchen, opened a drawer and checked for the sharpest knives she could find. She picked out two large kitchen knives. She practiced with them for a while, tossing them into the air and catching them again. Once she felt at home with the knives in her hands, she was ready.

Standing in front of his office door, with the knives hidden, she breathed out a long sigh before knocking. “Come in,” he answered gruffly. She pushed the door open, stepped in and closed it behind her. He looked like a man she had never seen before. His hair was disheveled and messy, and it seemed he hadn’t left the room to sleep in a while. He needed a shave too.

“What happened to you?” she asked, taking a seat in front of his desk. He lifted his head, glanced at her, and propped his head up on his arm. He let out a long sigh and sent her a look full of murderous intent, which faded after a second.

“My drug route was found out. My men think it’s to do with Bonten.” He gave her a dirty look.

She immediately put her hands up in surrender. “You of all people know I have no contact with them. Your men are just less capable than you think,” she said, insulting his men. He jumped up, walked round the table towards her, grabbed her throat and dragged her off the chair.

“Just because you’re not pregnant anymore doesn’t mean I’ll tolerate—” She didn’t let him finish. She lifted her lower body and wrapped her legs tightly round his throat. He released her throat at once and clawed at her legs to get free. She wasted no time. She twisted her body so her upper half faced the same way he was facing, leaned back and stabbed him in the back with one of the knives, then pulled it out. She punched his head a couple of times and hopped off him. He fell to the floor heavily. Using the same knife, she threw it at his thigh, the same thigh

where he had shot her two years ago. He screamed as she pulled the knife out again, and blood splashed over her face and clothes. Disgusting.

“I waited two whole years to drag you six feet under, and that time is finally here,” she muttered, and threw the knife at his stomach. It impaled him, and she didn’t stop. She pushed down on the hilt, driving it further in. He coughed up blood, which ran down the side of his face and onto the floor.

“Please, just kill me already,” he gasped, his eyes glazed.

She let out the eeriest laugh, one that came from the very depths of her soul. She picked up the chair that had toppled over, placed it just in front of his feet and sat down. She tilted her head to one side and smiled widely. “Did you really think I’d have any mercy for you? Try giving birth. Try spending two years away from the person you love. Oh, wait. You don’t have one.” She laughed at his pitiful state again, then sat back and watched his life drain out of him. The floor began to pool with his blood, and it soon reached her feet. She just sat there and waited for all the blood to seep out of his wounds.

Five minutes later, she got to her feet and walked over to Ichinose’s body. His eyes had rolled back in his head. She bent down and checked his neck for a pulse. There was none. He was dead. He was finally gone. She was free. Overjoyed, she let out a small yell of victory. His threats to hurt Yuuma were over. She calmed down, opened the office door, closed it again and trudged to the bathroom to turn on the shower.

She stripped off her clothes and threw them aside. She stepped under the warm water and let it wash the man’s blood from her skin. The water ran down to the floor, turning pink as it swirled into the drain.

She wrapped a towel round herself, went to her room to change into her nightwear and dried her long hair quickly before rushing to Yuuma’s room, where Chloe was.

“Chloe,” she whispered as she opened the door. Chloe was sitting in the chair with the book on the table beside her, her legs pulled up to her chest.

Chloe stumbled off the chair and hugged her tightly. “I heard him scream. Thank God Yuuma fell asleep.” Akari smiled, rubbing her back, and felt Chloe’s tears soak into her shoulder.

“We’re finally free, Chloe,” she said, ushering her out of Yuuma’s room so they could talk without whispering. She led her straight to Ichinose’s office.

“Wait, I’m not ready,” Chloe said, pulling her hand free.

“It’s better to see a fresh body than an old one. Trust me on this.” She gripped Chloe’s hand tightly, reassuring her, and pushed open the door. Chloe stared at the body on the floor beside the desk, the blood pooled round it. She covered her mouth with her free hand, tears spilling down her face. The chair blocked her view, so she shuffled sideways to see better. Her eyes travelled from his feet to the wound in his thigh, then to the knife handle still sticking out of his stomach. Chloe closed her eyes, let go of her hand and ran to the bathroom. The sounds of her

retching and vomiting echoed through the house. Akari let out a small sigh, with a smile. It was the expected reaction from someone who had never seen a dead body before.

She sat Chloe down on the couch in the living room and made her a cup of tea to calm her down. Chloe took the cup with shaking hands. “Thank you,” she whispered, bringing it to her quivering lips. There was a pause before she spoke again. “Did you do all that?”

“Yeah,” Akari answered quickly. “You get used to it after a while, so—”

“No more. I don’t want to hear any more for a while,” Chloe cut her off, putting the cup down and covering her ears.

Akari smiled gently and nodded. Chloe uncovered her ears when she saw the nod. “I’m going to call home and buy some tickets to Japan. Just to confirm, you’re coming, right?”

Chloe hesitated, then answered. “…Yeah.”

“Great!” Akari said enthusiastically, standing up from the couch and walking back to Ichinose’s office to use his phone and computer.

She sat down at his desk, ignoring the body beside her. She typed away on his computer and bought three one-way first-class tickets to Japan. She reached for the phone on the desk and dialled the Bonten office number, but it didn’t connect.

Of course, she was overseas!

She added 0011-81 in front of the number and dialled again. (0011 is the international access code and 81 is Japan, she was fairly sure.) The dial tone rang for a while before someone picked up. “Who’s this?” a voice asked.

“Promise me you won’t cause a fuss,” she said calmly, but then came the sound of something crashing, and she sighed.

“Akari? Is that you?”

“Yeah, I’m alive.” She laughed. “Did you just fall off your chair?” She guessed from the groaning in pain.

He let out a pained laugh. “Still as sharp as ever, I see. I’m not as young as I used to be.”

“Well, neither am I,” she laughed too, before getting to the point. “Omi, I need a favour.”

“This isn’t a favour anymore. We’re getting you home.” He paused. “What do you need? Fake documents?”

“Bingo. For the three of us.”

“Three?”

“Yeah, one for me, my son, and Chloe. She’s a—” She stopped, trying to think of what Chloe was to her. “A friend. I’ll send the photos through to you now.” She typed and sent three photos to his email.

“Yep, I’ve received them,” he confirmed.

“Our flight is at nine in the morning, the day after tomorrow. Can you send the passports and everything by then?”

“Depends on where you are,” he answered.

“Sydney, Australia. The address is xxxx.” She heard him scribbling it down.

“Yeah, I can organise that for you. Luckily, one of my men is on his honeymoon there right now,” he said. The poor man.

“Thanks, Omiiii. Also, keep this chat a secret from everyone else.”

“Eh? Why?”

“I think it’ll be better that way,” she said, snickering.

“Okay, then.” He laughed along with her. “See you soon. Stay safe.” He hung up. She placed the phone back on the desk and printed out the document with the seat confirmation for the flight in two days.

They sat at the dining table to eat dinner. It was quiet and a little awkward. Chloe still seemed shaken by the sight of Ichinose’s body, which was no surprise. Akari took a bite of her sandwich, then lifted a spoon to feed Yuuma his fruit. Just as she raised her hand to wipe the mess from his mouth, the doorbell rang. Chloe jumped in her seat. Paranoia set in at once, because there were only two possibilities for who might be at the door.

She hurried to the intercom and checked. A man in a black suit stood there, holding an envelope with the Bonten mark stamped on the front. “Delivery for Kurokawa-san,” he said politely.

She answered the intercom. “Be there in a bit.” She grabbed a kitchen knife, just in case, and went to the front door. When she opened it, the man in the suit was waiting at the gate. “Thank you so much,” she said, taking the documents from him. “Enjoy the rest of your honeymoon.” She smiled, walked back inside and locked the front door.

“Who was it?” Chloe asked, giving Yuuma his next mouthful.

“One of Bonten’s men.” She opened the envelope and took out the contents, laying them on the table. There were instructions and fake Japanese passports for Chloe, Yuuma and herself. They were almost identical to real passports, made to fool anyone. Chloe picked up her passport and stared at it in complete disbelief.

“It was organised this quickly?” She nodded, opening her own passport and Yuuma’s. “When did you even get this photo?”

“I took it from your résumé photo,” she admitted, and Chloe laughed softly.

“That makes sense.”

“Anyway, pack your things. We’re leaving early tomorrow, so get a good night’s sleep,” she said, as Chloe nodded and scooped the last of Yuuma’s dinner onto his spoon. He giggled as she pulled the spoon from his mouth. They both smiled at him, and she stood to collect the plates and cutlery and put them in the sink.

“I can do the washing up,” Chloe offered, but Akari politely declined.

“I’ll do it. I’ve got nothing to pack except Yuuma’s things, so it won’t take long. You can do the same and just bring yourself to Japan, if you want to.”

“What about clothes—”

“I have more than enough money to buy you some,” Akari said with a wide grin. “But it’s dirty money, so it’s up to you.”

Chloe looked uncertain, then decided to bring her clothes. “I’ll start packing, then,” she said, lifting Yuuma off his seat and setting him on the floor, where he crawled over to Akari and clung to her leg. She sighed at how cute he was and kept washing the dishes while Chloe went to pack. There was really no point in cleaning up, since nobody was going to come here for a long time.

She stayed up all night, because she had no alarm clock to wake her in the morning. She spent the night sorting her “papers” and Yuuma’s belongings. At five in the morning she knocked on Chloe’s door to wake her.

“Be ready in ten minutes,” Chloe croaked, and Akari heard the rustle of bedsheets from the other side. She sat on the couch to wait for Chloe to come out before she woke Yuuma. When the door opened, Chloe appeared, still half asleep. “Did you stay up all night?”

“Yep,” Akari answered, a little drained. “Can you call a taxi? The phone and the taxi number are on the table.” She stood and shuffled towards Yuuma’s room. She opened the door and found him sitting against the side of his cot, waiting for someone to come in. “Morning, Yuuma,” she said, and his face lit up as soon as she walked in.

“Mummy!” he squealed, reaching for her. She lifted him out of the cot, set him on the table, changed his nappy and clothes, then took one last look round the room before she tucked him against her chest with one arm under his bottom.

“Akari! The taxi’s here!” Chloe’s voice echoed through the house.

She closed the door of Yuuma’s room, grabbed his bag, his passport and the tickets, and walked out of the house. Yuuma was already asleep on her chest, though it was only half past five, far too early for him. She closed the front door for the first and last time and walked to the taxi waiting outside.

“International airport, please,” Chloe told the driver, who nodded. Akari slid into the back with Yuuma, and put his bag on the seat beside her.

They waited in the queue to board the flight. Akari showed the airline staff at the desk their first-class tickets and identification. They compared her face with the passport photo and let them through. She carried Yuuma while Chloe carried his bag and followed her through the boarding bridge. They were led to their seats, which were close, since they had booked first class. Akari sat down, and Chloe put Yuuma’s bag in the overhead bin and sat beside her.

“This is nice,” Chloe said, letting out a long sigh of relief.

“It’ll be nicer when you get to Japan. With freedom,” Akari said with a smile, excited to finally be going home.

Chloe smiled back. “I can’t wait to meet everybody, I guess. You should get some sleep on the flight. I’ll look after Yuuma if he starts to fuss.”

Akari gratefully accepted. “We can take shifts if it gets really bad. But Yuuma’s a good child, so things should be fine. The only problem will be take-off and landing, when your ears start to pop,” she said, rubbing Yuuma’s back as he drifted off.

After a while, the captain spoke over the loudspeakers. “Ladies and gentlemen, welcome aboard Flight 4B7 from Sydney to Tokyo. We are currently third in line for take-off and expect to be in the air in approximately seven minutes. Please fasten your seatbelts and secure all baggage beneath your seat or in the overhead lockers. Please ensure your seats and tray tables are in the upright position for take-off. Please switch off all personal electronic devices, including laptops and mobile phones. Smoking is prohibited for the duration of the flight. Thank you for choosing Japan Airlines. Enjoy your flight.”

Yuuma began to fuss and squirm in her arms at the sudden loud voice. “It’s okay, Yuuma,” she soothed.

The plane started to rumble and move, and she felt herself pressed back into her seat as it picked up speed. It was unbearably loud for Yuuma, who began to cry as the wheels left the ground. All she could do was try to calm him while she returned the dirty glares the other passengers gave her. They looked away as soon as she glared back.

It was hard to believe that in another ten hours the flight would touch down in Tokyo.

### Forty Two

Akari POV

Ten hours later, she walked out through Japanese customs, which let her through without any trouble. Yuuma held her hand tightly as they made their way through the maze of the airport. She had already taken precautions for her identity by wearing a face mask over her nose and mouth. Chloe led the way to the spot written on the paper the man in the suit had given her in

Sydney. “It says he’ll meet us here,” Chloe said. Akari picked Yuuma up again so she could walk faster.

She felt a light tap on her shoulder. She wasn’t ready to be attacked this early, certainly not with a child in her arms. Instinctively she sank to the ground and folded Yuuma’s small body into hers to protect him.

“Calm down, Akari,” Takeomi said softly from behind her. She lifted her head and saw him looking down at her, then at Yuuma, with a gentle smile. She stood and set Yuuma down. He immediately wrapped himself round her leg and hid behind her. She grabbed Takeomi and hugged him tightly.

“Welcome back,” he said. He let go and crouched down to Yuuma’s level.

“Yuuma, this is Uncle Takeomi, or Uncle Omi,” she told her son. He didn’t react and only clutched her leg tighter. She laughed at his shyness.

“He’s cute. He’s got the same eyes as his dad,” Takeomi said, with a flicker of disgust for his brother, before turning to Chloe, who was standing behind her.

“Chloe, this is Takeomi, a fellow Bonten executive. And Yuuma’s uncle. Takeomi, this is Chloe, a dear friend.” Chloe blushed at the word “friend,” but she reached out to shake Takeomi’s hand, and he accepted.

“Thank you for looking after Akari. I’m sure she and Yuuma were a handful,” he said with a chuckle. Chloe laughed, and Akari jabbed him in the side.

“No, it was no trouble. If anything, she helped me more than I helped her,” Chloe said, picking up the bags from the floor.

“Shall we go? Looks like Yuuma might fall asleep any moment,” Takeomi said. He was right. Yuuma was already asleep on her chest.

She followed Takeomi to his car and slid into the back seat, waiting for the moment she would arrive home.

Takeomi reversed into the garage, which hadn’t changed in the two years she’d been gone. She got out and lifted the sleeping Yuuma back into her arms. Takeomi had taken his bags from her, so she was carrying only Yuuma. She walked to the lift and pressed the button, waiting for it to arrive.

“I’m assuming Sanzu is here?” Chloe asked Takeomi, and he nodded. Chloe reached over, lifted Yuuma out of her arms and soothed him as he fussed at being handed over. “I’ll hold him while you go to him,” she said as the lift doors opened. All three of them stepped in, and Akari was splitting in half with nerves.

The lift door finally opened, and the executives were sitting on the couch, laughing and drinking as usual. But it went quiet the moment she walked in, and their jaws dropped. Ran was about

to speak, but she put a finger to her lips. Sanzu hadn’t noticed her, because his back was turned to the lift. She walked up behind him and placed her hands over his eyes.

“Takeomi, this isn’t funny,” he said gruffly, reaching into his pocket, probably for his handgun.

She clicked her tongue and rolled her eyes. “Fuck you,” she said, with a wide smile. He stopped moving, recognising her voice.
