“No, it can’t be…” he trailed off. She removed her hands from his eyes, and he slowly turned his head towards her. His eyes met hers, and she watched them widen and fill with water. “Akari…?”

“I’m home,” she said, giving him a warm, teary smile. Before she could say another word, Sanzu had jumped over the couch and tackled her to the floor. He gripped her so tightly she could barely breathe. He pressed his face into her shoulder and began to sniffle. She patted the back of his head and ran her fingers through his pink hair, which had grown a lot since she last saw him.

“I-I thought you were—”

“I’m right here,” she assured him, kissing his head. He lifted his head from her shoulder, looked deep into her eyes and kissed her lips. She waited until he parted from her, and when he did, it was because he had noticed something. He stood, pulling her to her feet beside him and holding her hand tightly. Chloe was standing by the lift holding Yuuma. Sanzu’s eyes settled on them.

“Who’s this?” he asked, pointing at Chloe.

“She’s my friend, who I lived with for the past two years. She helped me look after Yuuma,” Akari answered.

“N-nice to meet you,” Chloe said, her lip trembling as she held Yuuma tighter.

“Does she know you’re in Bonten?” Mikey asked from the couch, chewing on his taiyaki.

“Yep. I told her everything about myself and my past. And just so you all know, Kurayami is no more. I disposed of him while I was there—”

“Was he living with you?” Ran asked hesitantly.

“Yeah. He had me do some of his paperwork while I was pregnant. Then he threatened to hurt Yuuma if I didn’t obey him, so I didn’t really have a choice but to follow his rules until I thought Yuuma was old enough,” she explained.

Chloe gave a small squeak as Sanzu took Yuuma out of her arms, holding him under the arms and lifting him up above his face. “Is this kid mine?” he asked, with a flicker of pain in his eyes.

“Whose else would he be, Sanzu?” she said quietly.

“…Yuuma…” he repeated to himself. “I like the name.”

“I’m glad.” Yuuma seemed to wake up and realised he was in the hands of someone he didn’t know, and he began to fuss. But he calmed down as soon as he stared into Sanzu’s eyes, which were an exact copy of his own. She laughed softly.

She watched them together. Sanzu had a soft smile on his face that he couldn’t wipe off. Yuuma giggled at him, and Sanzu held him against his shoulder, gripping his father’s finger tightly. Then he sat back down on the couch, with Yuuma still giggling in his arms.

She went over to Mikey and gave him a tight hug, which he returned. “I’m sorry for everything over the past two years,” she said. He gave a hum in response, and it was more than enough as an apology.

“I’m just glad you’re safe,” he said quietly.

She went round the room, laughing and hugging the rest of the executives. Chloe was still standing in the same spot where she had arrived, so Akari invited her over to the couch and made room between herself and Mikey. “Chloe, this is Mikey, the leader of Bonten.”

Chloe froze in fear and nerves. “P-p-pleased to meet you!” she shouted, a little too loudly. Everyone burst out laughing at her stiffness, and she flushed pink with embarrassment.

“Nice to meet you too, Chloe,” Mikey said politely, a small smile creeping onto his face. He picked up a taiyaki and handed one to her. “Try one,” he offered, and she took it reluctantly and ate it.

“I love this!” she exclaimed, her eyes wide as she took another large bite and finished it in one go.

“It’s my favourite,” Mikey said. “I have a whole lot more, but I guess I have to share now.”

Everyone was a little shocked by Mikey’s unexpected friendliness towards Chloe, but they all let it slide before he said anything else. Yuuma had fallen asleep again, this time in his father’s arms, with his tiny hand still wrapped round Sanzu’s finger. She smiled at the sight, sat down on the couch and leaned her head on Sanzu’s shoulder. “I missed you so much,” she whispered. He turned his head and kissed her temple.

“I did too,” he answered.

Ran laughed. “He went back to his drugs three days after you were gone, you know,” he said loudly, earning a jab from his brother and a finger to the lips, along with a nod at Yuuma.

She laughed at Rindou’s gesture. “Thanks, Rin. Don’t worry, Ran. I had a feeling something like that would happen. The only question is whether he kept it up. Did he?”

Ran shook his head. “He turned to murdering dead people instead,” he said, and everyone laughed, except Chloe, who wasn’t used to the way the Bonten members talked.

“W-what do you mean?” she asked. She really had the guts to ask Bonten members a question like that. Sheesh.

“He kept shooting someone who was already dead. I’d describe it for you, darling, but I think I’ll keep your innocent mind safe,” Ran said, winking at her. Akari shook her head at him, but she was smiling.

“Anyway, guys, introduce yourselves to Chloe. She has no idea who anyone is,” she suggested. She stood and walked to the kitchen to get the alcohol and the glasses for a celebration. Sanzu got up and followed her with Yuuma in his arms.

“Can I go and sleep with him?” he asked softly, looking down at Yuuma.

“Hold on,” she said. She grabbed the glasses and the bottle and put them on a tray, but Kakucho stopped her as she lifted it.

“Go and rest with Sanzu. I’m sure you’re both as tired as each other. Think of it as family bonding,” he whispered, taking the tray from her and carrying it to the rest of the group.

“Well, that sorts everything out,” she laughed. “Chloe!” she shouted over the voices of the men, then realised Yuuma might be sleeping. He was, and he started crying at the sudden yell. Sanzu laughed at her and led him away to their bedroom, rocking him from side to side, hoping he’d settle.

“Yes?” Chloe asked.

“Sleeping arrangements, but um—”

“You can take my room until we sort it out,” Mikey began, and everyone nearly dropped their jaws.

“I can’t take your room, Mikey—”

“I’ll sleep in my office. It’s nothing out of the ordinary, so there’s nothing to worry about.” He cut her off, giving her a reassuring nod.

“Oh, okay. Thank you,” she said with a small smile and a flushed face.

“Thanks, Mikey!” Akari said, giving him a warm smile before walking towards her room. “Goodnight, everyone. I’ll see you all tomorrow morning.”

“You mean afternoon,” Koko mumbled, and the others laughed.

“I heard that, bitch,” she shouted back, and they cracked up even harder.

She stepped into her bedroom for the first time in two years. It had hardly changed at all. The only exception was a photo frame on the bedside table with her smiling face in it. “You really treated me like I was dead, huh?” she laughed, staring at the photo. She picked up the frame, turned it so the photo faced the top of the table, and said, “Get a new one instead.”

“Will do,” Sanzu whispered, bouncing his leg up and down to soothe a sniffling Yuuma. Once Yuuma had calmed, Sanzu sighed with relief, toppled back onto the bed and laid Yuuma on his

chest. “You gonna join me, or what?” he asked, peeking an eye open to look at her as she was still busy looking round the room.

She looked at the two of them, then took off her clothes and slipped into one of Sanzu’s big Tshirts from the pile on the floor. She crawled carefully over the two of them and lay down on her side of the bed. She felt Sanzu’s arm snake round her and pull her closer. Her head rested on his shoulder, and she felt him kiss her hair. Then she heard him sniffling, and his arm began to tremble.

“I really thought I’d lost you, you know? I—” He stopped to hand Yuuma to her so he could grab some tissues and blow his nose. She placed Yuuma on her chest, sat up and leaned against the wall. “I went back to the place we last saw you and found one of Kurayami’s men there, by chance, and I found out you’d given birth. It felt amazing to know you were still alive, but the doubt was always at the back of my head, you know?”

She nodded and let him release everything he had been holding onto for the last two years. “I don’t want to go through that ever again,” he said, resting one hand gently on her cheek and the other on the top of Yuuma’s head. “I’m not losing sight of either of you again.” He wiped the tears from his cheeks. She lifted a hand and placed it on his cheek, wiping away his tears, then leaned forward and kissed his lips softly.

“I’m sorry, but there was nothing I could have done. This was the earliest I could come back,” she said softly after they parted. He nodded, then looked down at her chest, staring at Yuuma with soft, teary eyes.

“I still can’t believe you delivered this beautiful child,” he said, lifting Yuuma onto his own chest and lying back down.

She snorted and snuggled up beside him. “It was hell. Not proud to say it, but I cursed you for putting him in me.”

“How rude,” he said, pouting.

“But I regret none of it.” She kissed Sanzu’s lips, then Yuuma’s head. She felt his hand rest softly on her head, heard him breathe out a calm sigh, and they all fell asleep.

Finally together.

She woke the next day to find Sanzu and Yuuma no longer beside her. Feeling unsafe without her son, she jolted up, got to her feet and stumbled out of the room to search for him.

Yuuma’s soft laughter echoed from the bathroom. She rushed in and slammed the door open, then calmed down at once when she saw Yuuma sitting on the sink, and Chloe teaching Sanzu how to change a nappy.

“And then you just fold it over here,” Chloe explained, and Sanzu copied her, folding the other side. “And that’s it!” Sanzu lifted Yuuma to his feet on the sink top, gripping his waist to make sure he didn’t fall.

“Morning,” she said, and they turned to look at her. “Thanks for that, Chloe.”

“No problem!” Chloe said enthusiastically.

Sanzu lifted Yuuma off the sink and set him on the floor, and he waddled over to her leg, clutching it tightly and trying to get her to pick him up. “Mummy, up!”

“Yes, yes,” she said, bending down and lifting him high into the air before tucking him against her chest with an arm under his bottom. “Has he eaten yet?”

“Yep,” Sanzu said, looking at Yuuma giggling in her arms. He looked down at his hands, then at himself in the mirror, and turned back to her. “Do you think he knows I’m his, um, dad?” he asked hesitantly, the pain plain on his face.

Her heart ached at the sight of his pain. “It’ll take some time, but I’m sure he knows. You should’ve seen how he calmed down in your arms the first time he met you,” she said, holding Sanzu’s hand and guiding it to Yuuma’s head. Yuuma giggled and reached for Sanzu’s hand. Sanzu just stared, looking straight into Yuuma’s eyes. A normal child would have started crying at such intense eye contact, but Yuuma didn’t fuss at all.

“Yuuma,” Sanzu said, holding his small hand. “I’m your father. Daddy.” He was trying to get Yuuma used to the word. Yuuma kept hold of his hand but stared blankly at his father.

“We’ll get there, don’t worry,” she said, kissing Sanzu’s forehead and passing Yuuma to him so they could spend some time together. He held him tightly and carried him out of the bathroom.

“Thanks again, Chloe,” she said, turning to Chloe, who was packing away the spare nappies and disposing of the used one. “I wouldn’t be here without you.”

Chloe smiled warmly. “It’s fine. I’m happy to be here.”

“How was everyone last night?”

Chloe giggled, covering her mouth as she laughed. “I got to know everyone quite well. I never expected to be so comfortable around—um, murderers, I guess.”

Akari just smiled. “Stay loyal to us, Bonten, and we’ll promise to look after you.”

“Is that a warning?”

“Mmm, yes and no. But you already know not to mess with us, so I’m sure you’ll be fine.” She watched Chloe shiver a little. “Don’t worry, though. If you decide to officially join Bonten, then there’s nothing to fear, except other gangs and the government.”

“I-I see,” Chloe replied quickly, stumbling over her words.

“Anyway, I saw you and Mikey getting along,” Akari said, wiggling her eyebrows playfully. “What did you think?”

Chloe blushed at once and tried to hide her face, but failed miserably. “H-he seems nice,” she said.

“I can tell, Chloe. No need to hide it. But he’s been through more than you can imagine, so look after him well, okay?” Chloe looked confused but nodded. “He’ll tell you when he’s comfortable. I know that much.”

She led Chloe out of the bathroom and back to the living room, sat her down on the couch and took the empty spot beside her. Mikey was already sitting there, sipping from a cup. “Morning,” Akari said cheerily.

“You mean afternoon,” Koko chimed in, and she glared at him while Rindou and Mochi chuckled. “I know you too well.”

“Okay, smartypants,” she said, rolling her eyes playfully.

“Akari,” Mikey began, turning to her. “How do you feel about opening the FNN again?”

“Hmm, not sure yet. I think it’s a bit too early. Yuuma’s only one.”

“I understand, but it’s been two years, and I’m sure people are starting to worry about the sudden disappearance of Nakatani Hana.”

“It’s only a weekend job, right?” Chloe interjected, and Akari and Mikey both nodded. “I’d be happy to learn how to bartend,” she said, looking at Akari.

“Are you sure?”

“Yep! There isn’t much to do here anyway.”

“If you’re okay with it, then I’m sure Akari will be happy to teach you,” Mikey said, leaning over the couch to take a dorayaki from the table.

“I’ll start later this week. I’ve got to get you used to the noise of the club and everything,” Akari said.

“Oh, by the way, do you happen to know where my phone is? I lost it at the wedding.”

“The car you took there is still missing too,” Mochi replied.

“Then I think I know who to go to,” she said, looking out of the window.

### Forty Three

Akari POV

She quickly changed into her work suit and rushed out of the lift, passing Sanzu and Yuuma on the couch. Yuuma followed her with his eyes and giggled as he saw her again. She smiled at him, kissed his head, and turned to do the same to Sanzu.

“Where are you going?” he asked.

“I’m going to get my phone and car back,” she said simply, smiling again at Yuuma.

Sanzu looked at her with worried eyes and nodded. “Want me to come with you?”

“I’m just going to Draken’s shop. I’ll be right back.” Sanzu flinched at Draken’s name, but he didn’t say anything about it.

“Okay. Stay safe.” He turned his full attention back to his son. She waved to Yuuma, went down in the lift to the garage, opened the gate and hurried out on foot towards D&D Motors.

She pushed open the door of the shop. Draken had his back to the front and was busy at work. He stood up and towered over her as he spoke. “Welcome to D&D Mot—” He stopped when he saw her. “Akari?!” he exclaimed in shock, wiping his oily hands on the apron round his neck.

“Yep, I’m alive,” she said, giving him a faint smile.

He let out a long breath and smiled back. “Thank God. Everyone was worried about you. What happened?”

She wasn’t sure how much she could say, but this was Draken. Mikey’s best friend. “I can’t say much.”

“But—”

“I went on a ‘holiday’ to Australia,” she said, making quotation marks with her fingers.

Draken’s eyes widened. “Everything okay now, though?”

“Yup, he’s been disposed of, so don’t worry too much—” She realised she had said too much and stopped. “Oopsies.”

Draken looked at her, a trace of scepticism on his face. “Did you gain weight?” he asked, changing the subject.

“How rude to ask a woman about her weight,” she said, laughing it off. “Yeah, I did. I had a child.”

Inui walked in from the back room at the worst possible moment and dropped the toolbox in his hands. “Say that again?”

“I had a child?”

Draken was still stunned. “I-it’s not like you were sexually assaulted or anything, and forced to carry it, right?”

“Oh no, no. If that was the case, I would’ve—” She stopped herself before she could say more.

“Congratulations,” Inui said coldly, picking up the tools that had spilt across the floor. He got straight to the point. “So why are you here?”

“I was hoping you’d still have my phone, car keys and handgun from the wedding. It’s okay if you don’t.”

Draken gave her a quick flick of the hand to follow him into the back room. He pulled a chair over, stood on it and reached for a box on the top shelf. He opened it to check the contents, then handed everything over. “The bullets are still in the gun. The phone’s been dead for ages. The car is at Chifuyu’s place, since he’s the only one with a two-car garage.” He pulled out the remote from that day. “And whatever this is.”

She laughed when she saw the remote. “You can throw that away. It’s a one-use thing.”

“What even is it?”

“Nothing to worry about now,” she said, shrugging. She took the box from his hand, and he stepped down from the chair. She checked the gun and the bullets and slid it into the waistband of her trousers. She pressed the button on the phone, but it didn’t turn on.

He walked back out of the back room, and she followed. “Go to Chifuyu’s pet shop. He’s got your car,” he said, scribbling the address on a slip of paper and handing it to her. She read it and recognised the place at once.

“Thanks for everything, Draken. I really appreciate it.”

He gave her a warm smile. “Of course. Congratulations on the child, by the way.”

“Yuuma.”

“Huh?”

“That’s his name,” she said quickly, pushed the doors open and made her way to Chifuyu’s store.

The little bell above the door chimed as she walked in. “How can I help you today?” Kazutora’s voice called from the register. He noticed her at once and called Chifuyu, who was on his break, holding a cup of tea.

“Akari?”

“Hey, Chifuyu, Kazutora,” she said, raising a hand in greeting.

“Good to see you’re okay,” Kazutora said, still behind the counter, with a little fear in his eyes.

Chifuyu walked round the counter and leaned against the front, sipping his tea. “So, you’re here for your car?”

“Yeah. I’ve just been to collect my things from Draken.”

He nodded. “Yeah, he texted me earlier.”

Another customer came in: a mother with her young daughter, who squealed with excitement at all the creatures in the glass boxes lining the walls. Akari smiled as the girl ran to a ginger cat at the far end of the shop, while her mother hurried after her, not wanting to lose sight of her.

“Kazutora,” Chifuyu said.

“Hmm?”

“I’m taking Akari to get her car, so look after the store for me. I won’t be long.” Kazutora nodded, and she followed Chifuyu out to his car parked behind the shop. He unlocked the black car, opened the passenger door for her, walked round to the driver’s side and took his seat. He turned the key and looked over his shoulder as he reversed onto the road.

“Never thought this would happen,” he said quietly.

“What does?”

“Everything. You in Bonten. The kidnapping at Hina’s wedding. All of it,” he explained, and she nodded.

“There’s not much I can say to that. I chose this life, so I can’t complain.”

Chifuyu let out a small sigh. “I’m glad you’ve got Sanzu and Mikey by your side. But I just hope they aren’t the ones projecting their wishes onto you. You should have your own path too, you know?”

“I’m well aware of what I’m doing with my life, Chifuyu,” she said, standing her ground before continuing. “You won’t see me again for a long time after this, so don’t worry about me.”

“How can I not worry?! You’re a wanted woman in a notorious criminal—”

“Chifuyu. Mikey wants this, and so do I, so just shut up and let us do what we want, okay? We’re both aware of what we’re doing.”

He fell silent, his knuckles going white as he gripped the steering wheel. “I just wish we could go back to how we used to be, when all of us were together and happy—”

“There’s nothing we can do now,” she said, shrugging. “Besides, even though I want to live a normal life, I already know my life was never going to be normal. Especially since I was the product of a peace treaty between gangs.”

“What are you talking about?”

“That’s a story for another day,” she said quickly, as the car slowed in front of an apartment block. A black tarp covered the whole car, under the roof of a garage. She stepped out and went to the gate, pushed it open, took the car keys from Draken and pressed the unlock button. The headlights flashed under the tarp, and there was a small beep. She looked back at Chifuyu, who was slowly making his way over after locking his own car. She pulled the tarp off and dropped it messily onto the side of the garage. She opened the car door, sat in the driver’s seat and was relieved to find nothing had changed.

“Thanks for looking after my car, Chifuyu,” she said from inside, watching him look nervously round.

“Uh, no problem.”

“I’ll get going now. I don’t want anyone seeing me around here any longer.” She turned the key, and the engine roared to life. “Stay safe, and tell ’Michi that I’m alive and well,” she said with a reassuring smile, before driving out of the gate and onto the street. Little did he know she was going back to how she’d been before all this: a stranger.

She parked in the car park, walked to the shopping centre and went into the first supermarket she found. Some people stared at her scarred face, but she was used to that. She grabbed a basket and headed straight for the toiletries aisle. Nappies, toothbrushes, toothpaste and other things filled her basket. When she was satisfied, she went to the till and put the basket on the conveyor belt.

“Hello, how are you today, ma’am?” the cashier asked, scanning the items and bagging them.

She gave the woman a warm smile that seemed to make her a little uneasy, though the woman tried to hide it. “I’m fine, thanks.” The conversation ended there.

“Would you like to pay by cash or card?”

“Card, thanks.” The cashier handed her the machine, and she took out her black card and passed it over the reader. The cashier noticed it and gasped quietly. Akari waited for the receipt to print, collected her bags and took the receipt when it was handed to her.

“H-have a great day,” the woman stuttered.

“Cheers,” Akari said, and walked back to her car.

She parked the car back where it belonged for the first time in two years. She opened the boot and took out the shopping bags. It was strange to think that the car, which was usually full of weapons or body bags, was now full of everyday things, like groceries. How much her life had changed. She pressed the lift button, and the doors opened wide. She carried the bags in one by one and pressed the button for the top floor. Once she had unloaded the groceries and carried them to the dining table, she realised how silent the whole floor was. Not a single light was on, and there was no sign of anyone. She packed the food and toiletries away quickly, then hurried to her room, desperate to find her phone’s charger. She dug through her wardrobe until she found the cable.

She plugged it into her phone, and the screen flashed on. She switched it on at once and looked through the many missed calls, messages and voicemails from two years ago. She scrolled through her contacts and dialled Sanzu’s number. The dial tone went on for a while before he picked up.

“Hello? Is that you, sweethear—”

“Where are you?” she huffed into the phone.

He laughed, and Yuuma’s happy gurgling came through the line. “We’re downstairs, in the VIP room of your club.”

“Did you seriously bring our child to a bar?” she squeaked, worried.

“Yeah, but don’t worry—”

“How can I not?!” She hung up at once and rushed to the lift, down to the club. She pushed the shelf out of the way, slammed it back into place and burst into the VIP room. All the executives were sitting on the couches, along with Chloe and, surprisingly, Hanma and Hana.

“What the fu—”

“Language, Akari,” Hanma warned, with an irritating smirk.

She let out an annoyed breath, ignored him and went straight to Sanzu, taking Yuuma off his lap. She glared at Sanzu. “In what world is it okay to bring a child into a club room?” she asked, raising her eyebrows at him.

“Our world said it was fine,” Rindou said, and Ran nodded in agreement with his younger brother.

“You two, Roppongi brothers, are an outlier,” she said.

Ran just laughed. “Doesn’t seem like it now. Little Yuuma got into the club at one. He beat us by quite a margin.” She sighed in defeat and sat down beside Koko and Mikey. Yuuma suddenly fussed in her arms, reaching towards Sanzu.

“D-daddy,” he cried out. The whole room went quiet. Sanzu and she looked at each other, then back down at the crying boy in her lap.

“Did you hear that?” Sanzu choked out. She nodded, smiling widely at him. She handed Yuuma back to him, and he calmed down at once.

“I don’t know what you two got up to today while I was out, but it was definitely a successful father-son bonding session,” she said.

Mikey shook his head beside her. “I don’t think you want to know what the rest of us did.”

She jabbed him lightly. “Don’t make me worried…”

“It was nothing much, just the two of them running around naked after they had a bath together,” Mochizuki answered for Mikey.

“Hey now! For your information, I was chasing him, because he ran away from me. I was trying to dress him up,” Sanzu said, trying to defend himself.

“And you couldn’t put your underwear on either?”

“I—”

Hanma’s laughter rang round the room, and the rest of the executives burst out laughing too. Laughter really was contagious. Sanzu was embarrassed, but Yuuma sat on his lap, giggling innocently as if he knew exactly what was going on. “Next time, I’m going to have to help you both out,” she sighed, smiling.

Takeomi poured himself a glass of beer and offered her one too. She nodded, and he filled her glass. It went round the executives until it reached her. “Cheers!” she said, and downed the whole glass almost at once. She held out her arm for a refill, and Kakucho poured it, giving her a warning look.

“Don’t drink too much. Between the two of you, someone here needs to be the responsible parent—”

She immediately pointed at Sanzu. “He can do it tonight. I’m getting drunk tonight, and no one can stop me.”

Sanzu said nothing, but he nodded, agreeing to be the responsible one for the night, which let her loosen up for the first time in a long while. She hadn’t touched alcohol since she found out she was pregnant. While she had been working hard to develop, deliver and nurture a healthy baby boy, Sanzu had been out killing people and drinking away his pain. You could say that she felt she needed to let go and release all the pent-up frustration and emotion, even if it was the alcohol talking.

She let out a heavy sigh and leaned her head on Mikey’s shoulder. He didn’t move or say anything. “I’m so glad to be home,” she murmured, her head spinning after her tenth glass of beer. Mikey gave a hum of agreement. “I’m going to murder anyone who hurts my precious family. I’m not going to let anyone take anyone away from me.” She clutched the handgun in her hand tightly.

“Of course,” Mikey said, taking the gun out of her grip and hiding it from her.

“Wise decision,” Hanma remarked, chuckling as he handed Hana another glass.

She slurred her words. “Chloe and I are going to open the club together, but I’ll need someone to look after Yuuma while I’m gone. Promise me Yuuma will be in safe hands…” Her voice trailed off, and she fell asleep in the middle of her mumbling.

Sanzu POV

I watched her fall asleep on Mikey’s shoulder. She was breathing so calmly, her chest rising and falling slowly. Yuuma noticed his mother had fallen asleep and began to fuss on my lap, trying to get over to her. I loosened my hold on him, took his hand and walked with him to Akari. He tugged at the hem of her trousers, but she didn’t react at all. Yuuma looked as if he was about to cry, because he wasn’t getting his mother’s attention.

“Yuuma, let Mummy sleep, okay?” I said softly, trying to calm him. He began to sniffle, wiping his nose.

“S-sleep?” Yuuma asked, and I nodded.

“Sleep. Mummy’s sleeping,” I repeated, lifting him up, resting him on my forearm and placing my other hand on his back.

I looked at Akari’s face for a while. Her nose twitched, her eyelashes fluttered slightly, and her cheeks had flushed a light pink. Her head hadn’t moved from Mikey’s shoulder, and surprisingly, he hadn’t moved away. He kept his shoulder still for her. “Want me to look after Yuuma while you take Akari upstairs?” Mikey asked softly, glancing down at the top of her head. “She might get neck pain if she sleeps like this.”

“Yeah, that’ll be great,” I answered. I handed Yuuma to Mikey, and he instantly clung to his chest, nuzzling in and giggling. Mikey had a small smile on his face and began to play with him. I adjusted Akari’s body, slid my arms under her legs and back, and carried her out of the room and up to our bedroom on the top floor.

I laid her down softly on the bed, and she instantly rolled onto her side, grabbed my pillow and hugged it. I couldn’t help smiling at how cute she was. I pressed a light kiss to her cheek and went back downstairs to carry on with the night.

Apologies for the extremely long break. Things have been really busy with home and school, and I just haven’t had the time to write or update. I doubt I’ll update again soon, but thank you all for still being here: reading, voting and following. I really appreciate it.

Thank you all, and I hope you enjoy the chapter!

Yuu :))

### Forty Four

Sanzu POV

I headed back down in the lift to the VIP room and heard the sound of glass shattering on the floor, followed by an uproar of laughter. Maybe leaving Yuuma with Mikey was a bad idea, but I could never say that out loud. I burst into the room to find Yuuma in Kakucho’s arms. Kakucho was standing in the corner, watching the rest of the scuffle unfold. Mikey was somehow out cold on the floor. Koko was crouched between the sofa and the wall, covering his head with his hands. Chloe, Mochi and my brother were trying to shake Mikey awake, their faces full of worry. The Haitanis were as clueless as ever, especially Ran, who was almost passing out drunk and leaning on Rindou for support. Hana and Hanma were making out in the dark corner of the room, of course.

Kakucho bounced Yuuma gently up and down, trying to calm him, as Yuuma cried. Yuuma noticed me come in and cried out for me. My heart swelled. I felt I had earned the title of father, from my own son.

“What the hell happened in the two minutes I was gone?” I asked Kakucho, who just breathed out a long sigh.

He rubbed his eyes. “I’d rather not talk about it.”

I shrugged, with Yuuma’s head on my other shoulder, his tears staining my purple vest. “I’ll go back upstairs and turn in for the night, so I’ll leave them to you,” I said, rubbing a hand slowly up and down Yuuma’s back.

“Mmm, yeah,” Kakucho replied defeatedly, urging the two of us out of the VIP room and shutting the door behind us. Loud noises erupted almost at once, so I left as quickly as I could.

Yuuma and I had just finished brushing our teeth together. I changed his clothes quickly, because he was already starting to fall asleep on the bathroom counter. I was so focused on changing him that I didn’t notice Akari had opened the bathroom door. It was a bit terrifying to feel arms suddenly wrap round my waist when I had my child, my son, on the counter. But I calmed down as soon as I felt her face nuzzle into my back.

“You feeling okay, sweetheart?” I asked, and she nodded. I lifted Yuuma into my arms and turned to face her, wrapping one arm round her waist to pull her closer. She looked up at me. Her eyes were still clouded from the alcohol, but she seemed to want to say something.

“Is there something you want to tell me?” I asked. She nodded, but then her neck went limp, and she leaned into my chest and fell asleep again. Good thing I was holding her waist. I slowly squatted down and laid her on the floor for the moment. I rushed into our bedroom, to the cot we’d newly set up, lowered Yuuma onto his bed, and then went back to Akari, who was asleep on the bathroom floor.

I carried her back to her bed and laid her down as gently as I had Yuuma. I quickly changed out of my vest and work clothes, pulled the blankets aside and lay down beside Akari, kissing her bare shoulder before pulling her close and falling asleep.

Akari POV

Waking up the next morning was pure chaos. She had a throbbing headache, a crying child and the sound of jingling bells from the hallway. There could only be two reasonable culprits behind the bells. Holding her head with one hand, she carefully climbed over Sanzu, who was out cold, reached into Yuuma’s cot, lifted him out and settled him on her chest. “Morning, Yuuma,” she said, kissing his forehead. He calmed down quite quickly and began wiping his tears with his chubby hands, then wiped them on her shirt.

She sat on the edge of the bed, cradling Yuuma, and looked at Sanzu, still sleeping. His pale skin, and the old scars across his upper body that the sheets barely covered. The bells were still ringing in the hallway, with Ran and Rindou calling out as they walked up and down, trying to wake everyone. She was very close to beating them up later. Sanzu tossed and turned, grabbed her pillow and tried to smother the noise by pressing it over his face.

“What the fuck is going on?” he grumbled, his voice muffled by the pillow. She smiled, feeling a little giddy, scooted over to his side and laid her legs over his stomach. He instantly reached out and placed a hand on her shin, drawing small circles with his thumb.

“Morning,” she whispered. He pulled the pillow from his face and sat up. He gave her lips a tender kiss, then looked at his son in her arms and smiled softly.

“Morning, sweetheart,” he replied, noticing Yuuma’s gaze on him. She handed him over, and Yuuma instantly nuzzled into his chest.

“It sure seems like he has a favourite now,” she laughed, watching Yuuma with his father.

Sanzu gave a proud, toothy grin. “He’s like me in a way. We both have favourites.”

“What do you mean by that?” She bonked his head with her fist. “You’d better not have another woman waiting, since you have ‘favourites.’” She rolled her eyes, slid off the bed and changed into her suit.

“Wait! That’s not what I meant!” he exclaimed, desperately trying to make his case. She grabbed her heels and slipped on a pair of slippers for now.

“Mhm, sure thing.” She opened the door to find the Haitani brothers walking past, still ringing the stupid bells. “You two are really asking for a beating from me right now.”

Ran and Rindou gulped and put a hand on the metal of the bell to stop it ringing. “We have a good reas—”

“I’m sure you do.” She gave them a look they had never seen before, then turned on her heel and walked towards the kitchen. Sanzu followed a second later, half dressed, with Yuuma asleep in his arms once more.

“I’ll beat you two up to the point of no recovery if you wake Yuuma like that again,” Sanzu scowled, glaring at the two brothers.

“Oooh, scary daddy,” the brothers mocked. A vein throbbed on Sanzu’s forehead, and he was so close to chasing after them. Thankfully he still had enough sense not to drop his child and run. He took a few deep breaths, exhaled and walked to the kitchen and dining area.

After a while, everyone was seated at the dining table, eating breakfast. It was a little crowded, with an extra chair and two extra people, but the group was livelier for it. It might have been better if Yuuma hadn’t decided to throw his banana mush at Ran’s face. Karma for waking him, maybe?

Ran came back with a paper towel and wiped his face. She just poked her tongue out at him. That’s what you get, bitch. Mikey was eating a slice of toast, with a plaster over a part of his forehead. He stood up, and the whole room went quiet. Of course, Yuuma saw this as an opportunity to giggle and laugh at nothing. The executives smiled warmly at the cuteness, but she put a finger to her lips and made a shushing sound, which caught his attention. He copied

her finger movement and laughed again. “Sorry,” she said, knowing she wasn’t going to get anywhere trying to quiet Yuuma.

“It’s fine,” Mikey answered. “So, I have some news. We have a client who’s willing to hire us for one night.” He turned round, picked up the TV remote and changed the channel to the news. As if on cue, the 8 am news began. They all watched until it ended and moved on to an entertainment show that was taking the internet by storm. He switched off the TV and went on. “I’m sure you all just saw where I’m going with this.”

“The police drug raid? That wasn’t our group, though,” Mochi said, but Mikey shook his head.

“No, I’m talking about the arrival of the Pink Diamond.” Koko’s eyes glazed over, and she could swear she saw yen signs in them.

“Boss, are we stealing the jewel?” Koko asked, a little too eagerly.

Mikey looked at Kakucho and then at the rest of the executives for a while. “This is why I wanted to discuss this with you all. We’ll be stealing the jewel, but, as I mentioned, it’s at the request of a client.”

“So we steal the diamond, only to give it to the client?” Takeomi asked, drinking from his glass of water.

Mikey nodded. “The client is the original owner of the Pink Diamond. Apparently it was a family heirloom or some shit like that, and they were forced to hand it over for some reason,” Kakucho explained.

“Since when are we heroes?” Rindou exclaimed, and his brother, Sanzu and she all nodded.

“Why does it have to be us? Can’t the client just—” Kakucho cut in before she could finish.

“They’re the child of a criminal,” Kakucho said, flicking through his paperwork. “Despite the diamond being a ‘supposed’ heirloom, there’s really nothing they can do about their father’s record.”

“What did their father do?” Mochi asked.

“Murder, arson, theft. The list goes on.”

“And the child doesn’t have a criminal record?”

“Not that’s listed here.”

“How did this person even find us? That bit’s a little concerning…” Koko said.

Mikey answered this time, after listening to everyone discuss it. “Ashinuke handed it to us, saying we were more ‘capable’ than they were.”

“Is that it?” Sanzu asked, and Mikey nodded.

“Oh, that reminds me, I have to visit them soon,” she muttered.

“Do that after this case, thanks,” Mikey replied.

She nodded. “So I’m assuming we’ve technically all agreed to help this person?” Takeomi asked. “How many people do we need to steal the diamond?” He turned to Mikey and Kakucho.

“Since a pink diamond is such a rarity, it’s currently on display at the Central Tokyo Museum, under bulletproof glass. It’ll stay there for the next two weeks, until the exhibition ends,” Kakucho said, giving the rest of the details. It would be a hands-on mission with almost all the executives, excluding Mikey and Chloe. After the announcement, she glanced down at Yuuma in her lap, who was thrashing his hands against his legs. Mikey noticed her worried face.

“Akari, I know you’re worried about Yuuma, but I really need you there,” Mikey said, as Sanzu put a reassuring hand on her lap, while Yuuma began playing with his finger. “I’ll look after him with Chloe. I’ll be giving you all instructions from a nearby location, so you might be able to hear him from time to time.”

“What about our identities? Can we really trust the client with them?”

“I’m assuming that’s where I come in,” Sanzu said, and Kakucho nodded.

“You’re the only Bonten member with up-to-date information about identities, so we’ll use that to our advantage. We’ll have you meet up with the client before and after the mission. Before, to tell them we’ve accepted the request, and after to hand over the diamond.”

“You keep saying ‘them,’ but do we know who they are?” Koko asked. “And what do we get for finishing this?”

“We know their name and their father’s information, but nothing else. About the reward, Ashinuke said something about stolen goods, which I assume came from the father’s stash,” Mikey said, grabbing his glass of milk to wash down his toast.

“I wonder what it could be…” Koko whispered, a little too excitedly.

“I’ll go over the plan in detail the night before the mission, so until then, make sure you finish your list of jobs.” The executives stood, stacking their crockery. She lifted Yuuma onto her arm and began to lift her plate when Mikey stopped her. “Akari.”

“Yeah?”

“Can you help Chloe learn the basics of bartending this week? It’ll be easier for you both, since you can look after Yuuma while you’re at it. Short working hours, too.” She gave him a thankful smile.

“Sure, I’m up for it.” She turned to look for Chloe, who was talking with Rindou and Mochi. “Chloe, do you want to start now?”

Chloe spun round, eyes bright, and nodded hard. Arms took Yuuma from her. “I have a free day today, so I’ll look after him,” Sanzu announced, watching Yuuma giggle and squeal with excitement.

“Thanks,” she said, kissing his cheek. “Take him to the park or something. Wear a disguise, please.”

“Of course,” he said, walking away with Yuuma to their room to get dressed. Chloe hurried to the lift, excited to learn.

“Let’s go!”

“Okay, I’m coming. Hold up,” she said, laughing.

### Forty Five

Akari POV

The darkness wrapped round her body, the only light coming from the street lamps a few metres away. She stood behind a large marble pillar, peeking over her shoulder now and then to watch the guards in front of the museum. She had dressed normally today, in her plain black suit with a face mask over her nose and mouth, as always. But today she wore a blonde wig, the hair falling just past her shoulders. She pressed her earpiece and whispered into the microphone hidden on her shirt.

“I’m going.” Mikey gave a hum of approval. She walked quickly out from behind the pillar and made her way to one of the two guards standing in front of the door. He stopped her from going in.

“Ma’am, we’re just about to close the museum. I’m afraid I’ll have to turn you away,” the guard said. She looked up at him with wide eyes.

“Please, sir. I left my handbag in the museum somewhere, and I really need it back,” she whined. She suddenly broke into a coughing fit. “Please. My medication is in the bag.”

Guard No. 1 waved over Guard No. 2, who came swiftly across. The two of them began discussing whether to let her in. She let out a sneeze, a really loud one. She fumbled a tissue out of her jacket, turned her back to both guards and blew her nose. “Go,” she whispered into her microphone, then pulled her mask back over her nose and turned to face the two guards.

She let out another convincing fit of coughing, pretending to struggle for breath as she inhaled deeply. “Please, sirs, help me,” she said in a strained voice. She noticed the Bonten men tiptoe behind the guards, slip through the door and hide in the shadows.

“…Fine,” Guard No. 2 said. He walked over and grabbed her wrist. She winced at the sudden contact and pulled away. “We’re doing you a favour, so please comply for the time being.” He pulled her into the museum through the main entrance. In her earpiece, she heard Mikey giving instructions to Koko.

“Koko, hook up the repeat videos,” Mikey ordered.

“Doing it right now,” Koko replied, and she heard the tapping of his keyboard. Koko was hacking into the museum’s security cameras from one of the two getaway cars. That way, it would look as though no one had entered or left, and the diamond would seem to have vanished into thin air. But she had spotted a serious flaw in the plan, and she needed to let him know quickly. She walked behind Guard No. 2 for a while, waiting for the right moment.

“Where did you say you left your handbag?” he asked, turning round to face her. She kept a puzzled look on her face.

“I-I’m not sure mys—” She dropped to the floor in a terrible coughing fit, biting down on the blood capsule she had placed in her mouth earlier. She coughed up blood, and it stained the inside of her mask. It had been a smart choice to wear a surgical mask, so the blood would soak through and be visible to Guard No. 2. She watched his face go pale with worry when he saw the blood on it.

“Ma’am, you’re coughing up blood,” he said, his voice anxious. She pulled off her mask, because it was disgusting, and held it in one hand. His eyes widened a little when he saw the scars on her cheeks, but after seeing the blood, that was the least of his worries.

“I know,” she said calmly, reaching into her coat for her gun. He would have assumed she was taking out a tissue to wipe her mouth. “We need to find my medicine quickly, or the symptoms could get worse.” The security guard nodded and helped her to her feet. She held her gun tightly, wrapped one arm round his waist and rested her hand on his shoulder, while the gun was actually pressed to the back of his head.

“Thank you for all the help,” she whispered, a smile creeping onto her face and her lips curving at the corners. She pulled the trigger, and he slumped forward and landed heavily on his face. Blood seeped from his head and pooled on the marble floor.

She spoke into the microphone. “Koko.”

“Yeah?”

“I need you to keep my image on the security cameras.”

“Huh? Why? You do know they’ll see us coming in and out, right?”

“No, no. Erase that part. Just make sure there’s footage of me going in and out of the museum with a handbag. Sanzu’s got a handbag on him right now.” She spoke to Mikey this time. “Mikey, is that okay?”

“Yeah, just don’t mess up the whole plan, okay?”

“Yes, boss.” She spoke to Koko again. “Thanks, Koko.” She smiled and walked towards the Pink Diamond exhibition. A few steps into the museum, she felt a friendly tap on her shoulder. She turned round and saw Ran grinning from ear to ear, brimming with excitement.

“Man, you really are a five-year-old,” she laughed, following him into the Pink Diamond exhibition. The rest of the group were waiting for her, gathered round the thick glass panels

surrounding the diamond. Even though it was locked behind bulletproof glass, the pink diamond lit up the room, throwing soft pink light on the walls as it bounced the dim lighting in every direction. It was like a disco ball, scattering light across the room. The lustrous pink diamond sat on a holder with a velvet cushion underneath, just in case an earthquake tipped it over. People really did think too far ahead sometimes.

Sanzu trotted over and handed her the handbag, in a colour that matched her suit and businesslike clothes. She rummaged through it and found a small device that emitted a laser. The laser was powerful enough to cut straight through glass, even bulletproof glass.

“Are we all ready?” Mochi asked, his voice coming to her twice: once through the earpiece and once in real life.

“Yep!” most of them answered, with varying amounts of enthusiasm.

“Alright, then,” Mikey began. “Koko, disable the security alarms and the motion-detection lasers.” Almost at once, she heard the tapping of keys, and Koko’s very quiet groan of frustration.

“Hurry up, before the other security guard thinks of something,” she said, trying to sound as sweet as she possibly could.

Koko sounded even more annoyed. He huffed. “I’m tryiinggg.” He got there in the end, and Rindou sprayed some dust into the air to make sure the motion-detection lasers were switched off.

“Overlay the video, Koko,” Mikey continued. “The rest of you, go and get the diamond.”

Most of the executives gave a thumbs-up and a hum of agreement, though they knew Mikey couldn’t see anything happening inside the mission.

“Here,” she said, handing Takeomi the glass cutter.

“Don’t give it to me,” he growled, passing it on to the person beside him, which was Rindou.

Rindou sighed, took the cutter and walked over to the glass panel. He stuck the cutter to the glass, where it held fast by suction. He used the little laser to cut a perfect circle into the glass, and repeated it several times until the glass was thin and worn. “Someone swap with me. I’m getting a hand cramp,” he announced, and Mochi happily took his place.

“Weakling,” his brother snickered, earning a whack on the head from Rindou.

“Hold the laser tightly for long enough, and you’ll cramp up too,” Rindou shot back, as Ran rubbed the back of his head. It took a while, but Mochi finally cut through the glass panel.

He held out the glass cutter and passed it back to her. “Take the diamond, Akari. You’ve got the skinniest arm out of all of us,” he suggested. She nodded, put on gloves and got ready to handle the diamond.

She held out one arm, ready to take the diamond. Sanzu placed a sandbag of equal weight into her palm. “Here.”

“Thanks,” she said. She quickly removed the diamond and replaced it with the sandbag. She held the diamond carefully and dropped it into a white padded bag. Sanzu packed it into her handbag and handed it back to her.

Kakucho tapped her shoulder and handed her a piece of paper and a dip pen. “What’s this for?” she asked, taking the pen and paper from him.

“Write a note and leave it on the sandbag. Give the guards a little surprise when they check,” he said quietly, with a small smile.

She thought about what to write, but no ideas came to her. “What am I supposed to write?” she said, scratching at her blonde wig.

“Fuck you all!” Koko yelled into the earpiece, and every member flinched at the sudden noise.

“Huh?”

“No, that was my suggestion…” he trailed off, a little embarrassed by the confusion.

Mochi gave a small snort. “That sounds more like something Sanzu would say, not you, Koko,” he said, and the rest of the Bonten members snickered.

“Fuck you, Mochi,” Sanzu muttered under his breath, which only made them laugh harder.

When the laughter died down, Ran came up with an idea, and for once it was good enough. “What about just drawing the Bonten symbol?”

“Damn, Ran, that’s a pretty good idea, especially coming from you,” she said, smiling widely. Rindou snickered at his brother’s embarrassment. “Kaku, hand me the ink, please.”

“Don’t have any,” he answered simply.

She sighed loudly and ran off from the others. “I’ll be right back. Don’t move!” she called, rushing towards the dead guard. She dipped the dip pen into the puddle of blood, laid the paper flat on the floor for a good surface and held the pen just above it. The moment of truth. The pen touched the paper, and her hand moved, drawing a thin rectangle with a small circle and a half circle beneath it. She filled in the shapes with blood, and droplets splashed over the edges of the lines. Satisfied with the result, she stabbed the pen into the thigh of the dead guard and hurried back to the group waiting in the Pink Diamond room.

“I’m done!” she said cheerfully. She pushed her hand back through the hole in the bulletproof glass and gently placed the note on the sandbag. Then she picked up the circular piece of glass that Mochi and Rindou had cut out, and slid it back into place as carefully as she could.

She took off her gloves and stuffed them into her handbag. “Good to hear,” Mikey’s voice suddenly boomed in everyone’s ears. “Now leave. There isn’t much time before the other guard

gets suspicious.” Then Yuuma’s gurgling and giggling reached her through the earpiece. She turned and gave Sanzu a wide smile.

She went to him and kissed his cheek, then took his hand and led the way back out of the museum. Once they reached the main doors, she let go of his hand.

“I’ll distract him, so you guys leave while I do. Koko, get the footage ready, please.”

“Already done,” Koko answered, and she let out a sigh of relief. She left the museum through the doors, and the guard from earlier turned to face her. She walked out and round to face the main doors, so that the guard’s back was to them. This was the only chance for the Bonten members to escape, so she had to make sure the guard’s full attention stayed on her.

“Thank you so much,” she told the guard, letting out a small cough, far more restrained than before, to make it look as though the ‘medicine’ was working.

“Of course, anytime, ma’am,” he said, but then he began looking round, searching desperately for the other guard. Thankfully, by then the boys were long gone, round the corner and into their cars, where Koko was waiting in one of them. “Where did the other guard go?”

She tilted her head to one side, letting her blonde hair fall over her face a little. “Oh, we got separated inside. He should still be in there…” she trailed off. The guard nodded.

“I see. Well, it’s getting late. You should leave before it gets too dangerous for a woman like you,” he said respectfully. She took this as a sign to leave the museum before he started questioning her about the other “missing” guard.

“Of course. Have a good night, sir,” she said, turning her back on him and walking away with a huge, evil smile across her face. She kept going until she reached one of the cars, pulled open the door and slid into the empty spot in the back seat. “Phew,” she said, sighing loudly.

“Glad that’s all over,” Takeomi said, opening the window a crack.

Sanzu shook his head. “There’s more to this Pink Diamond fiasco, remember?” he said, and the others groaned. “You have the diamond, right, sweetheart?” he asked, raising an eyebrow at her.

“Yeah, of course,” she answered, pulling the white padded bag out of the handbag and handing it to Sanzu.

“Cheers,” he said, opening the bag and shaking the Pink Diamond out of it.

“Gloves!” Koko exclaimed, just as Sanzu was about to touch it.

Sanzu rolled his eyes and used the bag to put the diamond back until they got home. She tapped her earpiece and reported to Mikey. “Mission successful. We’re heading back now.”

“Well done, all of you. See you at base,” he replied quickly. She could hear Yuuma laughing in the background, and Chloe talking to him. Knowing that Mikey, Yuuma and Chloe were all safe,

she removed the earpiece, rested her head against the headrest and closed her eyes for a brief moment. It wasn’t long before she fell asleep.

### Forty Six

After the meeting with the rest of the Bonten members, Mikey handed me the bag with the Pink Diamond and a pair of gloves. “Make sure you handle the diamond with care. Come back with the reward,” he ordered, then turned and walked down the hallway towards his room.

I walked casually into the bar and ordered a vodka on the rocks. The bartender recognised the order and brought me a glass with a note slid under the coaster. I followed the instructions, drank the contents of the glass, walked round to the back of the bar and knocked on the side door. The door swung open at once, and Akio and Daisuke pulled me into the dimly lit back room. I followed them into Akio’s office, where a woman in a very revealing black dress sat on the mahogany chair, wearing red-bottomed stilettos.

“Hiii~” she said in a flirty tone, getting up from the chair and wrapping her arms round her body just under her breasts, almost as if she was trying to lift them to get my attention. It wasn’t going to work. She held out her hand, and I was forced to accept the handshake for the deal to go through. She gripped my hand tightly, and when we parted, she made sure her touch lingered. Was she the supposed child of the criminal, the person who had hired us for this mission?

“Who’s this?” I asked Daisuke and Akio, who were still in the room, watching everything unfold. They wore dark expressions at our interaction. They were probably thinking I was being unfaithful to Akari, but it was a shame they couldn’t read my mind.

“She’s the one who organised this whole mission,” Daisuke said quickly, shooting me a dangerous glance.

“This isn’t what she looked like when I met them last time,” I muttered under my breath.

I took the bag with the Pink Diamond out of my trench coat pocket, put on my gloves, took the diamond out of the bag and placed it on the table in the middle of the room. I saw her eyes move instantly from my face to the diamond. She put on a pair of gloves, picked it up, inspected it with a special tool and smiled widely.

“Thank you, hun!” she said excitedly. She jumped up from her chair, trotted over to me and went in for a kiss on the cheek. I reacted faster than she did. I reached for the handgun in my pocket with one hand and placed the other over her lips before she could do anything. I pointed the gun at the middle of her forehead.

“Just because you fancy me doesn’t mean I fancy you,” I snarled. I’d had enough of this lady’s horny behaviour. I felt arms wrap round mine, locking my hands so I couldn’t pull the trigger. Her demeanour changed at once, and she looked frightened of me and the gun still in my hands. “Take your fucking hands off me, Akio!” I shouted, trying to shake him off.

“Calm down and—”

“How can I stay calm when I’ve got two of the best people in the world waiting for me to come home? Why do I have to deal with this ugly whore?” I spat. “Take the jewel and leave.”

She squealed in terror, scrambled to her feet and ran out at once. She left a bag behind, which I assumed was the reward for completing the mission. Akio finally let go of my arms, and I slumped onto the floor with my head in my hands, breathing heavily after being clouded by anger. “I’ve never seen you like this before. Is everything okay back home?” Daisuke asked, handing me a glass of water.

“Ever since Akari came back with Yuuma, I’ve been on edge. That’s all.” I sighed and gulped the water down.

“I know Akari came back, but who the fuck is Yuuma?” Akio asked, raising an eyebrow. “She didn’t ditch you for him, did she?”

“Oh no, Yuuma’s our son,” I answered.

Silence blanketed the room. “Say that again?” Daisuke said, his voice quivering a little.

“We have a son called Yuuma?” I repeated, looking from Akio to Daisuke.

“You’re telling me she was pregnant when she disappeared, and nobody thought to tell us?” Akio said, a little anger in his voice.

That was the night I was nearly killed by two of the most important figures in the Yokohama underworld.

…

I returned later that night, around midnight, with the reward in my arms. When the lift doors opened, I found all the male executives (except Mikey) sitting on the couch, passed out. The only light in the room came from the television, which was playing some sappy romance film. I put the reward down on the dining table, stepped over the tangled bodies and made my way to my room.

Just as I’d expected, Yuuma and Akari hadn’t moved at all. They were still asleep in the same position as when I had left them. As I undressed, Daisuke’s words kept echoing in my head.

Let us meet them, you jackass. Tomorrow. Or else.

You know things are about to go badly when the calmest person snaps. I’m usually quite calm when someone snaps, but this was the first time (not counting Mikey and Akari) that I felt shivers down my spine. They were small shivers, though. Nothing compares to how terrifying Mikey or Akari are when they snap.

I did decide to bring Yuuma and Akari to Yokohama tomorrow, to meet the whole of the Ashinuke gang, before Daisuke decided to hunt me down. For now, sleep seemed the smartest move, or I’d be dead before I even reached Yokohama.

Akari POV

She woke to a pair of arms wrapped round her waist and wet lips slobbering over her shoulder.

“What happened to your neck?!” she exclaimed, rushing over and touching his red neck.

He touched his neck himself, as if he were trying to feel for an indent. “Then we have to go and visit them,” she said, adjusting Yuuma on her chest. “And maybe Izana, Emma and Baji too.” Sanzu nodded and finally sat up on the bed to wake himself properly.

She got out of the car and parked in a spot reserved for the owners of the bar. She knew it would tick Akio off, but she really couldn’t care less at this point. While Sanzu unbuckled Yuuma from his baby seat, she walked to the back door and gave it a hard knock.

I’m so glad to see you again!” He struggled to his feet, stumbled, then engulfed her in a hug. She hugged him back, and he swept her off her feet and spun her round. She couldn’t help laughing, until he set her down gently.

“Why don’t you go and take a holiday somewhere?” Daisuke suggested.

Her mind immediately went to beaches with crystal-white sand and clear blue-green water. “That sounds lovely…” she said.

She looked over at Sanzu and met his eyes, as if asking for permission. “Go for it, sweetheart. I’ll stay with Daisuke and Akio and help look after Yuuma.” He gave her a reassuring smile. “You deserve this much.”

“If you’re all okay with looking after this ball of energy for a week, that’ll be amazing,” she sighed, already feeling at peace.
