She knocked at Mikey’s office door and waited for an answer. Nothing. She knocked again, turned the doorknob and went into his office.

It was dark, with only his computer screen lighting the room and painting his face with its bright white glow. He was so focused on whatever he was doing that he didn’t notice her come in, let alone the knocking.

“Mike—” she murmured quietly, trying not to startle him.

A fountain pen whizzed past her face, grazed her cheek and hit the back wall. “Oh, it’s just you,” he sighed, rubbing his eyes and adjusting to the darkness. “Did you need anything?”

She took the chair opposite his desk and faced him. “I just wanted to ask for your permission. I want to take a week off and go on holiday. I’ve been feeling so overwhelmed lately with work and looking after Yuuma. Akio and Daisuke suggested I take a short break.” He thought about it for a while. “So who’s going to look after your kid?”

“Sanzu, Daisuke and Akio. I think that’s better than leaving him with Bonten.” Mikey gave a small chuckle at that.

“Yeah, I agree with that.” He turned his eyes back to his laptop screen. A small ping came through on his computer, and she saw his eyes widen. His eyebrows pulled together, and he let out a long sigh of disappointment.

“What’s wrong?”

“It seems like we have a rat,” he said quickly, annoyance coating his tone. “All the way in Austria.” Mikey began typing furiously while the printer whirred loudly. He turned, grabbed the sheet of paper and handed it to her.

It was an identification page for the rat, with his name, face and age, practically everything she could ever ask for. “Is it okay for me to see this? I know how you like to keep unnecessary information away from us Bonten members,” she said, handing the page back to him.

“Of course. I’m giving you this mission, after all,” he said. “He’s planning to sell us out to the Viennese mafia in three weeks, at their annual ball. I want you to go. Silence him before he opens his mouth.”

She wasn’t sure she was the right person for the job, especially since it was a solo mission. “Are you sure you want me to go?”

“It has to be you,” Mikey said quickly. “I doubt the Viennese mafia will have any idea Bonten will be there, let alone a female member. They’re known for being very male-oriented. Pack your things. You’ll leave tomorrow evening. Spend the three weeks before the ball wisely. Get used to the venue. You already speak English, so it should be easier for you to blend in.”

She sighed. So much for that holiday. Mikey noticed the disappointment on her face. “You can take as long as you need for a holiday after this mission. You have my word.”

Her face lit up. “Thanks, Mikey.”

“I’ll organise everything for you tonight: flights, accommodation.”

“That’ll be wonderful, thank you.” She stood up and started walking towards the door.

“Akari.” He stopped her. “Don’t get too involved with the Viennese mafia. They’re dangerous.”

She looked back at Mikey and gave him a reassuring smile. “Don’t worry, I’ll be fine.” She closed the office door softly behind her.

This was going to be one long mission.

### Forty Seven

Mikey really outdid himself this time. He had booked a business-class flight from Tokyo to Vienna and a five-star hotel room in a restored building. When she walked into the reception area, she was taken aback by the chandelier hanging from the ornate ceiling, and by the grand staircase lined with rich velvet carpet.

“Hello, ma’am, how can we help you today?” the receptionist asked, standing and bowing slightly in welcome.

She rolled her suitcase closer to the desk. “Hi, I have a room booked under the name ‘Saito’,” she said, with a small smile.

The receptionist typed away on her computer, then turned and took a key from the hooks on the back wall. “This is your room, number 204. You’ve booked your stay for three weeks, so please be ready to check out on the 18th by 11am. We’ll send you a reminder in the days leading up to the 18th. Enjoy your stay at the Park Hyatt Hotel in Vienna.”

“Thank you,” she said, walking towards the lift.

…

She closed her room door quietly and put her suitcase behind it. She checked every room carefully, searching every nook and cranny for cameras and audio devices, and planted her own. After the quick sweep, she began building escape routes in her mind, for the “just in case” moments.

It truly was a majestic room, with modern and classic touches woven together. She went to the bathroom and was instantly drawn to the Victorian-style bathtub. Looking out of the window, she saw that it was already dusk. The sun was setting the clouds alight in orange, pink and purple.

The bath was quick to fill with warm water. She had brought yuzu-scented bath bombs from home, and they dyed the water a light green. She stood in front of the full-length mirror and carefully peeled off her disguise mask and wig. With this mask on, nobody in all of Vienna would ever know her true face. It was a security precaution, and Mikey had insisted on it. With it off, she finally felt like herself again.

She sank into the warm water, and the tiredness from the twelve-hour flight washed away.

…

She woke up the next morning to sunlight in her eyes. It was six in the evening Tokyo time, so it had thrown her body clock off. But she remembered that Mikey had given her an address to find weapons for the night of the annual ball. Her ball gown had already been arranged before she left Tokyo, and it was due to arrive at the hotel two nights before the big day.

Using her second phone to connect to the hotel Wi-Fi, she searched for the address of the weapons shop. It was an underground shop, open only to members of recognised criminal organisations. This shop in Vienna was run by a small café owner who was directly tied to the International Criminal Organisation Committee (ICOC). The ICOC organised the quarterly black market and handled the buying, selling and importing and exporting of dangerous goods, all under the government’s radar. Back home, Bonten was already affiliated with the ICOC and so had access to any international markets and stores.

She pulled on a completely new disguise. Today she was a blonde, blue-eyed woman in business attire, with a leather briefcase.

Walking in heels over cobblestones was far from easy, but when she reached the café, she felt a small sense of pride. The bell above the door chimed as she pushed it open. The café was cosy and quite busy.

She went up to the cashier. “Hello, I’d like one large black coffee, no milk, no sugar, and a strawberry cheesecake.” The cashier looked straight into her eyes as she gave her order.

“Sure thing, that’ll be five euros,” he said, holding out his hand. She handed him the money, and he gave her a small wooden disc with a number etched into it. “If you could head down that corridor and sit at the table with the number that matches your disc, that would be much appreciated.”

“Of course, thank you very much,” she replied, following his instructions down the corridor. It reminded her a lot of the FNN club back home. She soon found the table with the matching number and sat down. This area was isolated from the rest of the café, and there were several doors along the corridor walls, which kept her on alert.

After a short wait, her black coffee arrived in a takeaway cup. She sat there, waiting for something to happen. To her right, a door creaked open, and she turned her head. A tall, buff man stepped out. He had a scar over his left eye, dark hair that was slightly greying, green eyes with wrinkles starting to show, and an olive complexion.

“Hallo,” he said with a respectful nod. She nodded back and answered in German.

“Hallo, Herr.” With that brief exchange, he disappeared round the corner, and her attention moved to the door he had come through. A young man stood there, in his late twenties, with blonde hair, brown eyes and freckles across his light skin.

“Wie kann ich dir helfen?”

“Oh, sorry, do you speak English? Englisch?” she asked, not understanding a word.

“Ahh, yes. My apologies,” he replied with a small nod. “Before I let you in, I just need to make sure the ICOC approves of your group.” He walked towards the door, engaging in a low, confidential conversation.

Once she stepped through the door, the room was very small, with another door straight ahead of her. “Of course,” she began. “I’m a member of the criminal organisation Bonten.” She unbuttoned the top three buttons of her shirt to reveal her tattoo. The man stepped back, bent down to pick up a clipboard from the floor, and flicked through several pages before stopping at one.

“You’re part of a Japanese gang?” he asked.

“Yes,” she answered quickly. He looked her up and down.

“You don’t really look the part,” he said, raising an eyebrow.

“Well, this is a disguise after all,” she said, lifting the fake mask a little. He gave a small smile and a thumbs-up. “Ahh, I see. Follow me, then.”

He opened the door, and she was met with dim lighting over shelves and shelves of weapons. There were handguns, silencers, grenades and knives. They had it all.

“Wow,” she whispered. The man heard her and gave a small chuckle.

“Yes, it is impressive. Feel free to look around, and once you’ve chosen your weapons, come and find me. I’ll be at the counter at the back of the room.”

“Sure thing, thank you very much.” As his footsteps receded, she began her tour of the room, looking around with wide eyes.

So what kind of weapons do I need for this mission? she thought, trying to plan ahead.

Maybe a handgun, a silencer, a hand knife and a sniper rifle?

Her hotel room was directly opposite the venue, so the sniper rifle might come in handy. After a few minutes of thought, she grabbed those items, along with a long bundle of thick rope and a small anchor gun.

She put everything in a basket and brought it to the same man at the counter. “That was a quick trip,” he said, scanning the prices and packing the items into discreet bags. He packed everything she’d bought into a cello case.

“Yep, so that comes to 150 euros,” he said. “Cash or card?”

“Uh, card, please.”

“Of course.” He placed the card machine in front of her, and she opened her briefcase to get her wallet. She tapped her card and heard the beep of the confirmed transaction. He read the name on her card. “Himawari Saito. Japanese name, indeed.”

She laughed and put a finger to her lips. “You’d better keep that on the down low, Mr. My identity is supposed to be a secret. I can’t have people knowing my name.”

“Yes, of course. My lips are sealed,” he said, pretending to zip his lips shut.

She smiled and slung the cello case over her shoulder. “Just know who’ll be coming after you if you spill, Mr. Schmidt,” she said with a wink.

His eyes widened. “How—”

She closed the door behind her and turned down the corridor. On the way out, she bumped into a petite woman, and they both dropped their belongings. “Oh, my apologies,” she said, picking up the nearest item. It was a Japanese nursery book for young children. Acting as though she didn’t recognise it, she handed it back. “Here’s your book.”

“Oh, thank you, and your briefcase as well,” the woman said, and she took it from her hands gracefully.

They nodded at each other and went their separate ways. “Take care.”

“Likewise,” the woman replied, shuffling back down the corridor.

…

The day of the ball

She was ready to leave.

Armed with a handgun and a dagger strapped to one thigh, she was ready to go and dance. She wore a floor-length ball gown in dark navy blue with a slit up the leg. A deep V-neck covered her Bonten tattoo. Her back was completely bare, which left her vulnerable to attack, but it was also a reminder that this was an assassination mission.

Kill and leave.

Not kill and get captured.

Over the last two weeks, Mikey had sent her intel that the rat had hired protection from the Viennese mafia, which made the job harder than it had been supposed to be.

But that didn’t change the objective.

She slipped on her disguise, with straight black hair and bangs. She walked over to the bathroom window, rested her sniper rifle on the sill and looked through the scope. Sure enough, there he was: the one Asian man, surrounded by tall, bulky men, walking up the steps. Confirming he had arrived, she rushed to pack her things, because she was leaving Vienna once the mission was done.

…

She stood at the bottom of the staircase leading to the entrance of the annual ball. After a moment to mentally prepare for what was coming, she sighed, climbed the steps and went through the large wooden double doors.

### Forty Eight

Just as she took her first step through the doors, classical music began to play. She had made it in time for the ball. Following the movement of the crowd, she stepped towards the centre of the floor. People of all ages followed, making their way to the middle.

All the men wore black suits, tailored magnificently to their bodies.

The women wore a wide variety of colours: reds, blues, purples and yellows.

In the quiet of the music, everyone began to find partners for the dance. A man behind her lightly touched her arm. She turned slowly to find a young man lifting his hand to her, asking her respectfully for permission to dance.

“Of course,” she whispered, taking his hand.

The music sped up as they began the Viennese waltz. She had practised the basics of the dance during the two weeks before the event. In this dance, you changed partners every so often, so there was no set partner. Luckily for her, she only needed to make sure she ended up spinning round with her target.

Her partner took the lead, resting one arm lightly on her waist and holding her hand with the other. Leaning slightly back, the two of them began to waltz, black and navy blurring into one shade on the dance floor.

“You’re an amazing waltzer, ma’am,” he said, gazing into her eyes with a smile.

“Why, thank you,” she smiled back. “It was a pleasure to dance with you,” she said with a chuckle, letting go of his arm and spinning towards her next partner.

Her new partner moved gracefully to meet her, spinning as well. She felt some odd vibes coming from him, and she was right. He gripped her hand a little too tightly, and the arm on her waist kept sliding up and down. If she hadn’t been a woman on a mission, he would have been dead long ago.

Instead, she stepped on his toe with her very pointy shoe, and his face said it all. “You’d better watch your hands, or you’ll lose them,” she snarled, giving him her iciest stare.

She was thrilled to move on to the next partner, and startled to find it was her target. It was sooner than she’d expected, but there was no time to waste.

“Hello, sir,” she said, putting on an act and letting her breathlessness show.

“Are you alright, ma’am?” he asked, noticing her apparent shortness of breath.

She kept playing the part. “My airways… constricting… need… break.” Being the gentleman he was, he guided her swiftly outside the circle of dancers, leading her through some doors and into a small room. As the door closed, the music faded to a soft background hum. Two of his men were already in the room, and two more followed him in.

Perfect.

According to Mikey’s information about the rat’s hiring arrangements, his contract included protection until the moment of his death.

Which meant she had to kill him before the bodyguards could kill her.

Whether the men would honour that contract was another matter. She decided to bet on the contract and make her move.

She sat down on the sofa in the small room and kept up the act of struggling to breathe. He sat beside her and handed her a glass of water. She hunched over and took the glass from him, giving him a grateful smile. Two men in front of her, two behind.

You can do this.

While she was hunched over, she lifted the glass to her lips. In a split second, she grabbed the handgun and pressed it to her target’s temple. As she did, she threw the glass aside, drawing the attention of the men on that side, and swung her weight forward, bringing her target down onto the floor with her.

Just as the men reached for their guns, she shot her target in the temple. He was as good as dead. She didn’t have much time, though, because bullets were about to fly. She dived out of the way as shots tore towards where she had been crouching and took cover behind a wooden table, her back against a row of bookshelves.

“He’s dead! You have no reason to protect him anymore,” she announced.

Silence.

Whispers passed between the men.

She threw her gun out in front of them, waited a moment, then slowly got up from behind the table and stood with her hands in the air. “Check for yourselves. He’s dead.”

Blood had spilled from his forehead and stained the pale rose-coloured carpet a vivid red. Two of the men bent down to check his pupils and feel for a pulse, while the other two kept their guns trained on her. The two guards scoffed at the dead client, then straightened up. “He’s gone,” they said.

She kept her hands up and flicked her hair back, since it had fallen in her face. “Why did you kill him?” one of the men asked.

She wondered whether to lie or tell the truth. “Don’t try to wriggle out of this one,” the other said gruffly, aiming his gun at her as well.

She sighed in defeat. “Orders from the boss. I had no choice but to keep his mouth shut.”

“Of course you’d know about keeping information within the group. Traitors deserve death.”

The men exchanged glances, stunned that a woman of her size was speaking with such authority. “What group?”

She didn’t answer. She slowly moved one hand over her dress and pulled down one strap, revealing her Bonten tattoo. It took a while, but one of the men recognised the symbol. “Bonten?”

She nodded. “I thought the rumoured female member was nothing more than a lie, but I see we’ve been proven wrong.”

“I came here with no other objective than to take out this man,” she said, pointing at the body on the floor. “If you men pose a threat to me, I won’t hesitate to end you all as well.”

She didn’t realise that the bookshelf directly behind her had swung open. A strong hand gripped her arms, and cold metal pressed against her neck. “Don’t move,” a gruff voice said behind her. She stood her ground and listened to his instructions, because she was very clearly outnumbered.

Light footsteps sounded behind her, coming out from behind the bookshelf. The petite woman from the weapons shop stepped into the room, holding the book of Japanese nursery rhymes.

The four men in the room dropped to their knees and bowed to the woman. The man behind her didn’t budge, holding her firmly.

“What’s going on here?” the woman asked, looking at her, then at the four men, then at the dead body. She gave the dead man a quick prod with the toe of her shoe. “Why is our most recent client dead?”

One of the four men quickly explained what had happened. The woman’s eyes lit up, and she signalled to the man behind her to release his grip. She turned round at once, gave the man a hard stare and stepped out from the corner.

“How exciting to see another woman in the same business as me,” the woman squealed, delighted, grabbing her hands in excitement.

She was taken aback and didn’t know how to respond. “Uh, yeah, likewise,” she said, giving a quick smile.

“Oh, I’m sorry, you have no idea who I am,” the woman said. She had a vague idea, but she wasn’t sure. The woman leaned close to her ear and whispered, “I’m the don of the Viennese mafia!”

Her hunch had been right.

“Nice to meet you, ma’am,” she said as respectfully as she could. The last thing she wanted was to get on the don’s bad side and have all of Europe after her and Bonten.

The woman was visibly thrilled to meet another woman in a similar line of work. She bounced on her toes as she twirled her round the room by the hands. “You know what? You should come over for tea!” she squealed.

“Uh, as much as I would—”

“No, you will not be taking no for an answer,” one of the men cut in, staring her down.

This might be a long night.

…

She arrived at a large villa in the countryside, about an hour and a half from her hotel. Luckily, she had been allowed to collect her suitcase from the hotel room first. She knew there was an expectation that she would reveal her true identity, but the level of trust that required was very high. She weighed the positives against the negatives, and in the end, she made up her mind.

The car reached tall metal gates, curved and decorated with flowers and birds. They slowly swung open, and the car rolled over the gravel towards the main entrance of the villa. The same woman from the ball was waiting there.

“Welcome to my villa! This is the first time I’ve ever had a guest, so I’m very nervous,” she said, as the car door shut. She shook her hand and followed her inside.

“Thank you for having me, ma’am.”

“Oh, you can call me Laura,” she insisted, guiding her to the tea room. She sat her down on a beautiful, artistic piece of furniture that was controversial, in fact. “Sorry, it’s a bit uncomfortable if you’re not used to it, but it really is a work of art.”

She was seated on one of the chairs that Catherine II of Russia was said to have commissioned, decorated with intricate carvings of nude figures. “I thought they were all destroyed in the Second World War,” she said.

Laura looked shocked. “I can’t believe you know about these! Yes, nearly all of them were destroyed, but I bought this one at auction. It could have been in a museum, but what’s the point of a chair nobody can sit on, you know?”

She laughed. Laura wasn’t wrong.

A knock came at the door, and a butler entered with a tray holding two cups of tea and some biscuits. “Thank you, Humphrey,” Laura said with a nod. He smiled and left the room.

“So, firstly, cheers,” Laura said, smiling and raising her cup. It wasn’t a traditional toast, but she went along with it and clinked her cup lightly against Laura’s. “So what’s work like over in Japan? I’ve been trying to study Japanese, but it’s really hard.”

“Oh, it’s a bit tiring right now,” she began, and she told Laura her story, from the FNN bar to the long “kidnapping” in Australia, to getting back to Japan with a young child.

“WOW, HOW ADMIRABLE!” Laura squeaked. “Having a child and carrying on with such business must be tiring.”

“Yeah, it really is. I asked my boss for a holiday, and he gave me a three-week mission to finish first,” she said playfully, rolling her eyes and laughing.

Laura was easy to get along with, and by the time she realised, she had spent the whole day talking. So much had been shared about their lives.

“I feel like I owe you my real identity after all we’ve talked about,” she said, hooking her hand under her chin and peeling away the fake mask. Laura wasn’t surprised at all. She had known the whole time that she was in disguise. She also took her FNN business card from her back pocket and handed it over.

“If you ever come to Tokyo, please visit us. I’ll welcome you with open arms. We can even have a drink together,” she said with a smile. Laura accepted the card gratefully.

“I’m assuming Nakatani Hana is an alias too?” Laura asked with a chuckle. “You already know so.”

…

“See you next time, friend,” Laura said solemnly.

She waved back, climbing the steps of the private plane that Laura had arranged to take her back to Tokyo. “Make sure you come and visit!” she called as the plane door closed.

Time to fly home.

What a mission.

### Forty Nine

To say the private plane was luxurious would be an understatement. It had state-of-the-art leather reclining seats, a full en suite bathroom and five-star cuisine. It was almost too much.

But it was nice. It was a pleasant reminder of the holiday Mikey had promised her waiting at home. This time next week, she would be somewhere in the Caribbean, sipping a margarita by the beach at a private villa. She had been planning a solo trip, but after three weeks alone on the mission in Vienna, she was craving some time with Yuuma and Sanzu.

Just before landing, she changed quickly into her Nakatani Hana outfit, tucked her black hair into her collared shirt and pulled up her face mask. Perfect.

…

Standing outside the FNN bar door at eight in the morning, with two suitcases and a cello case, she certainly looked out of place. She snickered to herself, thinking about her plan to scare her fellow Bonten members upstairs. But first she had to get ready.

She unlocked the FNN door, went straight to one of the VIP rooms, opened the cello case and took out the handgun and silencer. She swapped the bullets for paintballs, loaded the gun and kept a few spares in her pocket. She was ready to go.

She scanned her lift pass, took the lift to Mikey’s office floor and decided she wasn’t stupid enough to shoot Mikey, but giving him a heads-up about what was about to happen might be more fun. He might even want to join in.

She knocked on his office door and heard a small groan from inside. “Yeah…”

She pushed open the door and watched his eyes widen. He hadn’t expected her back so soon. He had given her three weeks, but she had finished in two. She was that efficient. She wasn’t Bonten’s advisor for nothing.

“Hey, I’m hom—” she started, but she was cut off by the clatter of him stumbling to his feet and coming over to hug her tightly.

“Yes, welcome back. Glad to see you’re okay,” he said, letting her go and walking back to his desk. He gestured for her to sit in the chair opposite. “I’d like an update on what happened in Vienna, if you don’t mind. How did you get an earlier flight home? I booked a whole commercial plane for you a week from now.”

She laughed lightly at his seriousness. “Yeah, about that… I know you told me to be careful with the Viennese mafia, especially since they’re a male-dominated group.” He nodded, listening carefully. “But it turns out the don was a woman all along.”

Mikey was shocked. “What.”

“Yeah. I was caught killing her client, the rat you sent me to deal with. She was surprised to see me, a woman, and she ended up inviting me to her private estate for tea, and, um, we’re best friends now!” she said with an uncertain smile. But she was happy to have some female company in a house full of men and Chloe.

“I see,” he murmured, scanning his desk. “That’s definitely a turn of events. But it might work well for both of us. Neither of us has safe access to the other’s territory, so this might lead to a

new partnership, if she’s willing to accept.” She nodded, because she had reached the same conclusion as Mikey, but there was one worrying thing about the plan.

“There’s one problem,” she said, looking at him.

“Yeah, there’s bound to be people unhappy about this, whether that’s other gangs or men within our own groups.”

“The worst-case scenario is that other mafia groups come after us both. The Italian mafia and the Bratva, the Russian mafia, are strong, and not something to take lightly.”

“We can think it through later,” he said calmly. “What’s that handgun you’ve been resting in your lap for the last few minutes?”

“It’s a paintball gun. I thought it’d be funny to give them a bit of a scare.” She snickered, pointing the gun at the ceiling where the cameras were. “Want to join?”

She saw his face change as he considered it. “Sure,” he said, with a rare smile.

“Let’s go!” she laughed, standing up and handing him a few paintballs.

…

She and Mikey crept up the emergency stairs, trying not to make any noise. She entered the floor of Koko’s office and checked whether he was in.

He was. Mikey crept quietly to the door, and she followed closely behind, taking the other side. She reached for the handle and counted down with her fingers. “3…”

She burst the door open, and Mikey rolled into the office and took cover just behind the sofa. She peered round the doorway and checked the room. Koko was at his desk, asleep with his arms under his head. Poor guy, he was so overworked. She turned to Mikey and whispered, “Maybe we should let him slee—”

She was too late. Mikey had already fired at Koko’s left shoulder.

“Ow! What the fuck?!” Koko scrambled, reaching for the handgun he kept in his jacket pocket.

“Whoa, whoa, whoa. Don’t actually shoot us, we’ll die,” she said, walking in with her hands in the air.

He sighed with disappointment. “Surely you could’ve just let me sleep,” he grumbled.

“I tried to make Mikey reconsider, but I was a bit too late,” she announced, pointing to Mikey, who was still hidden from Koko’s view. Koko turned round and saw Mikey standing over him. Mikey rested a hand on Koko’s head and shook it slowly, as if disapproving.

“You’re getting rusty if you didn’t notice me until now, Koko,” Mikey said calmly.

Koko scoffed and rolled his eyes. “Maybe if you let me sleep more regularly, I would have.”

“So real,” she laughed, nodding in agreement.

“Anyway, good to see you’re back, Akari. Your hubby and your kid have missed you, and it’s driving me up the wall. It’s always ‘Akari this, Akari that’ with Sanzu and—”

“Yes, yes, I understand. We’ll go and surprise them now.” She put a finger to her lips, asking for Koko’s silence. “Do me a favor too, please.”

“What choice do I have?” Koko sighed in defeat, listening to her request.

Sanzu POV

I woke to a sliver of light peeking through the curtains. A nice sunny day. Akari would have loved this weather. I glanced over at Yuuma’s cot, where he was standing up, holding onto the side and staring at me.

I rolled out of bed in a hurry, tripped over the sheets and nearly hit my head on the floor. I lifted him out of his cot and set him on the floor, and he giggled with delight.

“Good morning, Yuuma.”

“Daddy!” he squealed, wobbling as he got to his feet before running at full speed towards me.

I shuffled back a little, holding out my hands and calling his name. He ran to me again, giggling loudly, and clutched my leg.

I looked at the clock on the bedside table. It was already time for breakfast, and we were late. I quickly changed Yuuma out of his pajamas, singing and talking to him as I did, and rushed out of the room. I forgot to change out of my own pajamas. Whoops.

Everyone was already at the breakfast table, except Koko, Mikey and, of course, Akari. She was set to return in another week, but I honestly didn’t think I could wait that long. I was itching to leave for Vienna and see her myself.

“What was all the noise from your room, Sanzu?” Ran asked, looking at me, then at Yuuma, with a smirk. “Surely you weren’t mast—”

“Shut it, you,” I snapped, already irritated by his antics. “Yuuma’s going to grow up to be a track star. Don’t be disgusting.” Everyone’s jaws hit the floor.

“There’s no way you think that’s going to happen.”

“He’s the son of a criminal, what are you talking about?”

All at once we heard the lift ding. Every head turned as the doors opened onto an empty lift.

“What the hell?” Mochi said, visibly confused.

Something felt off. I held Yuuma tightly, one arm clutching him to my chest, my other hand resting on my handgun, ready to go. “That’s not right,” I said. Ran and Rindou nodded.

Suddenly, shots came from the direction of the emergency staircase. Two shots. Mochi and Takeomi, who were seated closest to the staircase, were hit instantly. They groaned, fell to the floor and hid under the dining table. The Haitani brothers, Kakucho and I took cover too, hiding behind the sofa, the kitchen island and the dining table, and aimed our guns at the staircase.

I fired a bullet towards the staircase.

“Wait! Sanzu! Everyone stop!” Takeomi shouted.

“What could it possibly be, old man?!” Rindou yelled back. “Stay down and stay quiet. You’re hit.”

“Yeah, about that. It’s a paint bullet.”

“What?”

“Yeah. Paint bullet.”

“So who the fuck is playing pranks?” Kakucho said, irritation in his voice.

“Surely it’s not Koko and Mikey. They would never,” Mochi said.

I peeked over the kitchen counter, and another bullet whizzed past my hair and splattered on the wall behind me. “Surprise!” Akari yelled, running into the dining room, spinning the gun on her finger.

“Akari??” I said in shock, standing up and holding Yuuma tightly.

“Heya, hubby, I heard you missed me,” she said, sending me a wink. God, she was so beautiful. I walked over to her, put Yuuma down by the kitchen for a moment, then walked up to her and hugged her tightly. Yuuma followed straight away and sprinted to grab her leg.

“Holy shit. Sanzu, you were right, but what the hell, Akari?” Ran said, then looked down the corridor and saw Mikey holding the other gun. “Not you too, Mikey,” he whined.

Akari laughed out loud. “Bet you weren’t expecting that.”

“Just wait until you hear what Yuuma did this morning,” Mochi grumbled, slowly crawling out from under the table.

I saw Akari’s ears perk up, and she looked up at me. “Hmm? What happened?”

I sighed and separated Yuuma from her leg for a moment. “Wait and see.” I set him down a little further away and stood beside her. He looked between her and me with a puzzled expression, then began crawling towards us. He stopped, got to his feet and bolted, crashing straight into Akari’s leg.

“What the hell, he’s so quick,” Akari squealed in delight, picking him up and smothering him with kisses. “Yuuma!! Mummy’s so proud, well done!” He giggled and tried to kiss her back. I

watched them together. I had missed this so much. I leaned over, gave Yuuma a quick peck on the forehead, then kissed Akari.

“Welcome home,” I whispered, before going back into the kitchen to start breakfast. Everyone returned to their meals, sitting in their usual spots and chatting. Koko eventually came up too, with a red paint splotch on his back, and Ran and Rindou teased him about it.

…

Akari POV

She sat in Mikey’s office beside Sanzu, with Yuuma on Mikey’s lap, giggling and reaching for his platinum locks.

“Yuuma, be good,” she said.

“So, as promised, I’ll grant you your holiday, Akari,” Mikey began, gently holding Yuuma’s hands to stop him tugging at his hair. “You said you were interested in the beach, so I’ve booked you a ticket to the Caribbean for next week.”

She was thrilled and leapt out of her seat to hug him. “Yay! Thank you, Mikey!” Then she looked at Sanzu, who gave her a small smile. But she could read him like a book. He whispered something into Mikey’s ear, and Mikey sighed in defeat and nodded.

“Who’s going to look after the kid?”

“Huh?” Sanzu exclaimed. “It’s my son. I’ll look after him.”

“No, no. You’re coming with me, Sanzu.”

“Oh.” The grin on his face widened, his eyes glittering with excitement. “Surely Chloe and Ashinuke would be happy to take him for a week.”

She and Mikey hummed in agreement. “Our boys are great, but I don’t really trust them with my son just yet.”

“Yeah, I’d have to agree with that,” Mikey said, tapping away at his computer.

“Are you sure I can go, boss?” Sanzu asked, still unsure about Mikey’s decision.

Mikey looked up from his computer and into Sanzu’s eyes. “Do you want to go or not?”

“I do.”

“Then go before I change my mind.”

A moment of silence filled the room, and then Sanzu gripped Mikey’s hand tightly. “Of course. Thank you, boss.”

### Fifty

White sand. Beautiful crystal-blue water. The sound of waves crashing against the shoreline. Seagulls chattering overhead, crying for the tourists’ food.

There she was, sunbathing on a beach chair in a bikini, with Sanzu by her side. Well, he wasn’t sunbathing. He was sitting in the beach chair under the umbrella, a little restless, constantly looking over his shoulder.

“What’s got you so nervous, Sanzu?” she asked, pushing her sunglasses onto her head as she hopped off her chair and onto the sand in the umbrella’s shade.

He moved his long legs aside, letting her lean against his chair. “Just a little uneasy,” he muttered. “There are a lot of people, and I feel a bit exposed.”

She reached up, grabbed his thigh and drew little circles on it. “I see.” A moment of calm silence passed between them, before she suddenly stood, took his hand and pulled him to his feet. “How about we enjoy this week while it lasts?” she asked, with a mischievous smile.

“Whoa, what are you plan—”

She smacked his backside playfully and ran for the water, knowing he would come after her.

“Oh, you’re getting it now,” he growled, chasing her into the sea. In no time he caught up and dragged her under the surface. She surfaced gasping for air, then dived back under, grabbed his leg and pulled him down too, before swimming away.

She laughed out loud as she pulled seaweed out of her hair. Sanzu popped up beside her, holding out her sunglasses, which had fallen off. “Oh, thank you.”

“I can’t believe you got me into the water. I’m going to burn,” he muttered, grabbing her by the waist and pulling her close, then peppering her shoulder and neck with small kisses.

She squeaked at his kisses and wrapped her arms round his neck. “Hope you put on some sunscreen. You’ve always been awfully pale,” she said, running her fingers down the middle of his chest and feeling him shiver slightly at her touch.

There was a silence as they floated together in the water.

“I love you, Sanzu,” she whispered.

He looked down at her with a tender expression full of love, his pupils widening slightly. The corners of his eyes creased as his lips curved into a rare smile. Lines she hadn’t noticed over the last few years, the marks of age, were there now.

Time really did fly.

He leaned in, rubbing his nose against hers. “Love you too, sweetheart.”

“Thanks for coming here with me. I missed having you around in Vienna.”

He chuckled. “I can’t say I missed you, though,” he joked, earning a pinch on the side and a small yelp. “I still can’t get over the fact that you made friends with the Viennese boss. That’s so wild. So badass of you.”

“What can I say?” she said with a shrug. “I’m just cool like that.” She noticed a pink tinge across his shoulders. “Oh, honey, you’re already burning. Let’s go back into the shade. I don’t want you to match your hair, that would be disastrous.”

She took his hand and waded through the waves towards the shore, humming softly. Sanzu’s grip tightened slightly on her hand, his thumb moving over the back of hers.

She suddenly tugged at his arm and hopped and ran towards her beach umbrella. “Fuck, the sand’s burning my feet!”

Sanzu laughed behind her, quickened his pace and caught up. He lifted her up and over his shoulder and sprinted to the shade of her umbrella, letting her down softly onto her beach towel. “My princess,” he said, lifting her hand to his lips and kissing it.

“Gosh, you’re corny sometimes,” she giggled, pulling two beer bottles out of the ice cooler, cracking them open and handing him one.

“I know you love it, though,” he snickered, dropping down beside her and chugging his beer to cool off.

“This is nice,” he said quietly, and she hummed in reply.

…

She woke to a sudden scream. Out of instinct, her hand went straight to her hip, only to find that the gun she usually kept holstered in her trousers wasn’t there. (Well, she was at the beach in a bikini.) “Calm down, sweetheart,” Sanzu whispered from behind her, resting a hand on her thigh.

“It’s just a child.”

“Oh,” she said, feeling a bit embarrassed.

“You looked like you were having a good nap, so I didn’t want to wake you.” He reached over and wiped the drool from the corner of her lips.

“You should have woken me up, though. It’s already this late. We’ve got a dinner reservation at seven, remember?” she said, checking the time on her phone.

“Shit, yeah, I forgot,” he said, scrambling to pack up their things, and they headed back to the hotel room.

By half past six she had left the hotel room and was driving to the restaurant. It was a high-end place, so she had to dress up. For identity security, both she and Sanzu had covered their scars with make-up.

She handed the car keys to the valet, threaded her arm through Sanzu’s, held on tightly and walked to the man at the restaurant door.

“Booking for Nakatani,” she said slowly, watching him scan his clipboard.

“Yes, of course. VIP room three. Please follow the blonde woman. She’ll direct you to your table.” He ushered them to a middle-aged Caucasian woman, very well presented. Her mouth smiled, but her eyes shone with fear. She already knew Sanzu was the reason, because he was staring daggers into her soul.

“P-please, follow me this way,” she stammered, leading the way. She and Sanzu walked behind her, watching every customer and every doorway. Suddenly she felt a light tap on her shoulder. Sanzu reacted faster than she did, pulling her towards him and grabbing the stranger’s hand, while she reached for the gun holstered on her thigh.

“You?” His eyes widened in surprise, and he let go of the hand.

She immediately let go of her gun. “Omg, Mitsuya, what are you doing in the Caribbean?” Behind him, Hakkai and Yuzuha stepped out. They bowed their heads slightly.

“Hello.”

It was a little awkward, the six of them standing in the middle of the busy restaurant, while the blonde waitress nervously tried to guide them to the VIP rooms. She glanced at Sanzu, then at the other customers, then looked back at Sanzu pleadingly. He sighed in defeat, reading her mind. “Go ahead,” he muttered, a little annoyed that his dinner date had been interrupted.

“Have you three eaten yet?” she asked quickly.

“We were just about to be seated, too,” Mitsuya said, pointing to his table.

“Do you want to sit with us? Catch up a bit?”

The trio looked at each other, and Yuzuha spoke up. “Are you sure? Isn’t it a bit dangerous?”

“It should be fine. I doubt anyone we know knows that both of us are here,” Sanzu said, shrugging. “Plus, we all know how to fight,” he added with a toothy grin, earning a smack on the shoulder from her.

She turned to the waitress. “They’ll sit with us in the VIP room, if that’s okay.”

“Yes, that’s fine, ma’am,” the waitress said, leading the way.

…

The VIP room was decorated in Chinese style, with a round table in the centre. The yellow lighting from the lampshades and the ceiling made the room feel warm and calm, but the room was anything but. Tension hung thick in the air.

Once the waiters had left after placing the food on the table, she broke the silence. “So, what are you three doing here in the Caribbean? I’m assuming it’s work-related.” She picked up a pair of chopsticks and put some noodles on her plate.

“Yeah, I’m modeling for Taka-chan. And Yuzu’s overseeing everything, like always,” Hakkai said briefly.

“Oh wow. Is it a big show?”

“Mhm, it’s a show for my personal collection,” Mitsuya said. “I’ve finally made a name for myself, enough to have a runway for my designs, though it’s quite far from home.”

“You must be proud of yourself,” she said.

“Mitsuya’s worked really hard to get to this point, so I hope I don’t let him down tomorrow, when I walk down the runway wearing his clothes,” Hakkai said, nervously pushing a dumpling around his plate. “I want to make his name bigger, so we have to appeal to the buyers tomorrow at the showing. It all comes down to the design and how I present it.”

She nodded, not fully understanding, but she knew the runway was important tomorrow.

“Do you two want to come and watch the show?” Mitsuya asked. Yuzuha dug into her handbag and handed them two VIP passes. “Only if you’re free and want to.”

Sanzu took the tickets from Mitsuya and inspected them, then handed them to her. “Don’t see why not,” he said. The trio looked surprised, and so was she. It was very unlike him. “I’d like to come in through the back, though, if you don’t mind. I don’t need security patting me down.”

She nodded in agreement. “We do need to take precautions, as always. I hope you understand.”

“Of course. It’s great that you even agreed to come,” Mitsuya said. The rest of the evening passed cheerfully as the five of them caught up on everything since Takemichi’s wedding. She and Sanzu had to ignore some of the trio’s questions for security reasons, but thankfully, they understood and didn’t press further.

…

The day of the fashion show arrived. She and Sanzu were both in tailored black suits, with clear coiled earpieces and fake ID passes hanging from their breast pockets to look like security. Their goal was to blend in with the crowd.

She spotted Yuzuha in the distance as they pulled up to the venue. Sanzu parked quickly, and they were ushered in through the back as quietly as possible. Backstage, models were collecting their outfits, while hair and make-up artists layered on make-up and styled hair, following the model brief pinned in front of the mirror, as Mitsuya had suggested. People were bustling everywhere.

She spotted Hakkai on her right. He saw them in the reflection of the mirror, gave them a quick smile, then closed his eyes and let the make-up artist keep working. Yuzuha ushered them away from the chaos towards the front, where the runway was laid out.

She guessed Mitsuya was going for a celestial theme, because the runway seemed to float on clouds, with massive balls of cotton, smoke and light. “These are your seats,” Yuzuha whispered, showing them to seats at the back of the show, slightly raised so the people in the back rows could see the stage. “As you asked, the exit is just to your left, behind the curtain. It leads backstage to where the models wait for their turn on the runway, so be careful not to be spotted.”

She and Sanzu nodded.

“Thanks for all this,” she said.

Yuzuha smiled. “No problem. I’ve got to get back and help Mitsuya, so hopefully we’ll see you after the show?”

“We’ll see,” Sanzu said quickly, noticing a few eyes from the crowd on Yuzuha. Yuzuha seemed to understand his concern, because she was watching his rapid eye movements. She gave a small bow and slipped through the curtain, the exit route she had arranged.

Despite the seats Yuzuha had assigned them, she and Sanzu decided to split up and blend into the shadows against the walls, near the curtain. Through her earpiece, she heard Sanzu.

“Something gives me the tingles.”

She had the same gut feeling. “Yeah, something is definitely going to happen at this show.”

“Stay alert, sweetheart,” Sanzu warned. She turned her head in his direction and nodded.

“Will do.”

The lights in the venue dimmed. The show was about to start.

### Fifty One

“Ladies and gentlemen!” a voice announced through the speakers. “Please welcome the designer of this show, Takashi Mitsuya, to the stage for a few words.” The crowd broke into applause as Mitsuya stepped into the spotlight.

“Good afternoon. Thank you all for your support and patience. Today’s collection is based on the theme of celestial beings. It was inspired by the close bonds I had with my friends back in middle school, and the troubles we managed to overcome together. I hope you enjoy each

design, and the show.” He finished with a polite bow to the audience, and the applause rose again as he walked off the stage.

The lights dimmed once more, leaving only the centre of the runway lit, and music began to play softly in the background. The opening model walked out, strutting slowly down the runway. The design was magnificent. A flowing, slippery material shimmered in the light, and the dress left a silhouette behind as the model walked.

“Isn’t that Hakkai?” a voice rang in her earpiece.

It was. She could barely recognise him in the dress, because a large, wide-brimmed hat covered most of his face. His heels clicked in time with the slow beat of the music.

“You’re right,” she said, looking up at Hakkai on stage in awe. Both Mitsuya and Hakkai should be proud of themselves. As Hakkai reached the end of the runway and turned, her eyes followed him and landed on a familiar face in the crowd. She couldn’t place exactly who it was, but she knew it wasn’t a good sign.

“Sanzu.”

“Yes?”

“Can you spot the Asian man in the dark navy suit on the other side of the runway from us? He has sunglasses resting on top of his head and a white handkerchief in his breast pocket.”

“Yes. What about him?”

“Does he look familiar at all?”

There was a moment of silence on the other end.

“Yeah, actually, he does. I feel like we’ve seen him before.”

“I swear he was on the wanted list on Mikey’s blackboard, on the wall of his office,” she said, and Sanzu hummed in agreement.

“I think you could be right,” Sanzu replied. “I’ll send Mikey a quick message and get back to you. Keep your eye on him in the meantime.”

“Sure thing.” She did as Sanzu asked, watching the man’s every nose scratch and every move. “Hey, he’s itching his nose an awful lot. It’s almost suspicious, Sanzu.”

“Yeah,” he replied. “You reckon it’s a signal or something?”

“I wouldn’t be surprised if it was.”

The next model walked past and blocked her view of the man for a second. In that time, the man beside their suspect had vanished. “Hey, the man who was on his right is gone.”

“Akari, duck!” Sanzu exclaimed urgently, keeping his voice low.

She reacted at once and ducked. Just in time. Something flew over the top of her head. Glancing at the wall behind her, she spotted a dent where a bullet had hit. Someone was definitely trying to kill her. “I knew something was wrong,” she said.

“You okay, sweetheart?”

“Yeah,” she replied quickly, staying low, crawling along the floor and taking cover under the audience seats. Luckily, the seats above her were empty, the ones they had been given. “I’m taking cover under our original seats.”

“Okay, that’s good. I’ll keep an eye out for you. And I’ve got a reply from Mikey,” Sanzu started, and her phone buzzed in her pocket. He had forwarded the image to her. “This guy is wanted for backstabbing us. Apparently he leaked our details to Ashinuke without knowing our ties to them. Thankfully, his information about us and our inner workings didn’t go public, but we should take him out before anything else happens.”

“Sure thing,” she said, looking round as she came out of hiding. “Just make sure he doesn’t escape. I’m one hundred per cent sure he’s working with people and isn’t acting alone, so be care—”

Pain. Warmth.

Fuck. She had been stabbed in the left bicep. Luckily she was right-handed, so she could grab the gun from her waistband and shoot the man who had done it. He dropped to the floor and was dead at once. Blood poured from the wound in his head, but she couldn’t clean up the mess, not in a place with this many people.

“Sanzu, I’m injured. We have to leave.”

“What!? How?”

“I’m not sure. He just appeared out of nowhere. The normal lights will be back on soon, too. I think we should retreat for now.” She paused. “It’s a bit of a waste to let him go when we’ve finally found someone on Mikey’s wanted board.”

“Nah, he won’t escape us a second time,” Sanzu said, and she could picture the wide grin on his face. “I’ve got a plan.”

“I’d love to hear it, but I’m bleeding. There’s only so much I can do to help.”

“Sweetheart, I never said you were part of this plan.”

Her jaw dropped. “How rude,” she huffed. She took off her jacket, tore off the sleeve and tied a tourniquet round her arm just above the wound to slow the bleeding. She pressed down on the wound as well.

“I need you to leave the way we came in,” Sanzu said. “I’ll follow once I’ve planted a tracker on the target. I won’t be long. Now go. The lights will be on soon.”

“Okay,” she replied, walking slowly and carefully, watching her surroundings. “He’s got a few men here for sure, and they know we’re here. So be careful.”

He laughed. “Of course, darling. Who do you think I am?”

“I’ll wait in the car.” He hummed in response. “Don’t take too long. I don’t want to die waiting for you.”

She pulled back the curtain and made her way towards the exit when she heard faint footsteps behind her. She spun round, swinging her left leg at head height, then stopped mid-kick when she realised it was Yuzuha.

“Whoa,” Yuzuha said, a little surprised. She took one look at her arm and quickly ushered her out of the venue through the doors. The sunlight flooded her eyes and blinded her for a moment. “What happened to you?”

She sighed in annoyance. “I got stabbed. I was careless. Anyway,” she said, getting straight to the point, “there’s a dead man inside. One for now, maybe more later.” She handed Yuzuha a card with the Bonten symbol on it, along with her fake ID pass. “Take these. Throw them on the floor once the confusion and fear begin.”

Yuzuha reached out to take them, but she stopped her. “Don’t put your fingerprints on them.” Yuzuha nodded and used her sleeve to hold them.

“I know I shouldn’t ask what’s going on, but is there anything you can tell me?”

She thought for a moment. “Tell Mitsuya and Hakkai this too. I’m sorry we ruined the show. Hakkai’s entrance and Mitsuya’s design were beautiful, breathtaking. I wish them all the best in making their name known. Hopefully this won’t affect you guys badly, but that’s probably wishful thinking. Sorry again.” The blood loss was slowly taking its toll, and she bowed her head apologetically.

Yuzuha was silent for a moment. “Sure. I’ll let them know.”

“Thanks.”

“You know, you’re not as bad as the news make you out to b—”

“Hush,” she cut in, placing a finger to Yuzuha’s lips. Her eyes had turned dark. “You don’t know what really goes on, and you don’t want to know.”

Yuzuha had no words left. “Thank you, though. I appreciate that you think of me that way. Give my regards to the boys, but I have to go.” She rushed to the car she had parked earlier, got into the driver’s seat and drove towards the exit.

“Sanzu, how’s it going?” she asked into her earpiece.

Gunshots rang out from the outside, and screams of panic came from the audience. “I’m running out as fast as I can!” he exclaimed, and the door she had come through slammed open. Sanzu stumbled out, limping.

He pulled the door shut behind him. “Go! We need to beat the crowd, or we’ll be trapped!”

She slammed her foot on the accelerator and drove recklessly, anywhere, as long as it was away from the venue. “So what happened in there?”

“Quick change of plan, that’s what.” He snickered, though he winced in pain when she took a sharp turn.

“He got up to go to the bathroom for a smoke, so I followed him,” he went on.

She shook her head in disappointment. “Really, you couldn’t wait, could you?” She glanced at him in the mirror and saw the gunshot wound on his thigh. “That looks horrible.”

“Yeah, hurts like a bitch. Anyway, I knocked him out, stuffed his mouth with a shitload of toilet paper and then strangled him with my tie. I rushed out, but I must have taken too long with the toilet paper, because by the time I left the bathroom the lights were back on and the panic had started. I rushed to the exit, then some guy shot me, and here we are,” he said, finishing with a shrug. “Glad to see you’re okay, though.”

“Let’s just hope I don’t crash this car. My eyesight’s getting blurry,” she said, feeling as though she didn’t have long before she passed out from blood loss.

“Where exactly are we headed?” Sanzu asked, starting to tie a tourniquet round his own leg. “There’s no way a hospital will let us in—”

She laughed. “You’re lucky I always plan for the worst, honey.” She looked at his slightly blurred reflection in the mirror and winked at him.

“Gosh, you’re so sexy right now, Akari. I just wanna gobble you up,” Sanzu said, his eyes turning into hearts.

She took a sharp turn and pulled into a run-down alleyway, rolling slowly until she reached the end. A roller door and an intercom stood there. She leaned out of the window and pressed the button. “Two orders of spaghetti for Mr. Aizawa,” she croaked.

After a moment of silence, the roller door creaked open. “He’ll be waiting in room 112.”

The car rolled down the slope, and she parked as quickly as she could. She got out, went round to the back where Sanzu was, and tried to pull him out with her uninjured arm.

“God, you’re so heavy!” she grunted, dragging him out. He suddenly leaned forward, and she fell backwards. Sanzu reached out to stop her and grabbed her left arm.

“FUCK!” she screamed, clutching her shoulder. The wound bled much more heavily, and her vision began to fade.

“Shit, sorry.” Sanzu apologised, hobbling out of the car and slamming the door. The two of them wobbled towards the lift, with Sanzu guiding her, because she could hardly see anything.

“Level one,” she huffed, leaning against the wall of the lift. Blood dripped from her arm onto the floor and began to form a small puddle. Sanzu’s leg was bleeding just as badly.

The lift doors opened onto a short corridor. “This way, Akari,” Sanzu said, tugging gently at her little finger towards room 112. At last they reached the room, and she banged her fist on the door.

There was the faint shuffle of footsteps behind it, and the lock clicked. The door swung open onto a room lit by bright white hospital lights, with two surgery tables, equipment and two men in scrubs.

The moment she took her first step through the doorway, her legs gave out, and she collapsed in a heap on the floor.

An arm reached out and wrapped round her chest, just seconds before her head hit the linoleum. “I’ve got you, sweetheart,” was the last thing she heard before she passed out.

### Fifty Two

Akari POV

She woke to blinding white light shining over her body. Glancing round the room, she found she was wearing a patient gown with her left shoulder bare. A blood transfusion needle was in her right arm. One man was leaning over her, glancing at her briefly before going back to stitching up her shoulder wound.

It hurt.

“It’ll be done in just a moment. Hold on,” he said, his voice muffled behind his mask. She turned her head away from her shoulder and saw Sanzu lying on the other surgery table, with another man leaning over his injured leg.

Sanzu let out a grunt as the man dug into his wound, pinched out the bullet and dropped it into a metal tray with a light clink. “Fuuuuuuck,” he groaned as the doctor began stitching the wound closed.

“Oh, good, you’re okay,” she said slowly, watching Sanzu get stitched up. He turned his head towards her.

He smiled through the pain, looking at her with concern. “I was worried, you know,” he said. “It’s been a while since we’ve both been injured like this, but I’m glad you’re okay.”

“If you weren’t so reckless, I probably wouldn’t have passed out,” she grumbled, rolling her eyes but smiling as she turned her head back to the ceiling. The doctor threaded the last stitch, then wrapped her shoulder tightly in bandages. “Thank you,” she said, sitting up on the table and watching the last of Sanzu’s stitches.

…

Mr. Aizawa, the man who had arranged for these two underworld doctors, sat in a black leather swivel chair behind his desk. She and Sanzu sat on the couch at right angles to the desk, drinking their tea in silence.

“Here,” Aizawa said, picking up the remote and switching on the TV. Every news station was covering what had happened at Mitsuya’s show. “Look at what you’ve done.”

“—it seems Bonten was involved in this incident. Let’s hear from an audience member. Can you tell us what happened?” the newscaster asked, and the camera turned to a middle-aged woman.

“I was watching the models walk on stage one by one. When the last model disappeared and the lights came back on, there was a loud scream beside me. I looked over, and there was a dead man on the floor. Gosh, it was traumatizing. Then a man ran past us, through backstage. He must have been shot, because he started limping after a security guard fired at him.”

“Did you get a good look at the man who ran away?”

“No, but he had bright pink hair.”

She couldn’t help laughing. “Of course that’s your giveaway,” she said, poking him softly.

He shrugged. “Gotta keep it interesting somehow.”

“—and here is the designer of the show, Takashi Mitsuya. How do you feel after this incident?”

“Umm, it was quite unexpected. I didn’t think it would happen at my show. I didn’t think they’d be interested. So, yeah.” Mitsuya looked clearly shaken that his show had ended like this, though he didn’t seem as surprised as he might have been.

“There’s been some evidence suggesting Bonten were interested in your opening dress. What do you think of that?”

Mitsuya gave a quick chuckle. “That’s surprising, but it’s going up for sale in the online auction tomorrow at noon, Japan time, so…” He ended the interview with a shrug.

“HAHA!” Sanzu let out a hearty laugh. “Gosh, he’s gotten interesting lately.”

She smiled. “This will surely help promote his brand.”

Aizawa watched the screen in silence and switched it off when the broadcast ended. “Now that we’ve come to the end of this saga, I expect full payment,” he said, getting straight to the point.

“Of course,” she said, standing up and taking her wallet from her breast pocket, which she placed on the table. She counted out a large sum of notes and handed them over. “Here’s most of the fee.”

“And the rest?” he scowled. “We’re not a charity, you know.”

“Hush now.” She went back to her wallet and found her black card. “Surely you take card payments too, right?”

He snickered, opened the bottom drawer of his desk, pulled out a card machine and slid it across to her. “Of course.” She tapped her card, closing their business partnership.

“Thank you for all you’ve done for us, Aizawa,” she said. “I’ll give you a call when I need you next time.”

“Of course, thank you for your business.” He stood, shook her hand and walked them to the door.

“Sanzu, let’s go back,” she said.

“Huh? Where?”

“Home?” she answered, leading him out of Aizawa’s office.

“But it hasn’t even been a week yet,” he pouted.

She laughed and squeezed his cheeks at how cute he was. “Aww, don’t worry, darling. We’re just relocating to Jeju Island.”

“Oh yay. I’ve always wanted to go there,” he said, buzzing with excitement and restlessness. “But more than anything, I just want a good nap.”

“Real. Let’s go there quickly, then.”

…

The private jet landed on the tarmac at Jeju Island and was taken into a cave to hide it from the public. But another private jet was already parked there. The cave was big enough for both, but it could only mean one thing.

Another member of Bonten was here.

She sighed. She and Sanzu were never going to get a proper break, whoever was on the island.

“I wonder who’s here~” Sanzu sang, a little creepily. His eyes went so dark when he saw the other jet that it almost frightened her. She followed him to the Bonten property at the top of the hill, where a second car was parked, just as she had suspected.

She flung the door open. “Who the fuck’s here?!” she yelled into the house. Feet scuttled towards the door. “Of course it’s you. Ran and Rindou.” She sighed, annoyed.

“Hiii~” Ran sang, trying to get a rise out of her. He got one out of Sanzu instead, who threw his shoe at Ran’s face, and Ran only just dodged it.

“You fucking twat, why are you here?” Sanzu growled.

“We have a mission here?” Rindou answered. “Why else?”

“I thought you were in the Caribbean. It’s actually you two who are invading this house,” Ran said, and he had a point.

“We went on holiday there, but instead we had to kill someone on Mikey’s wanted board,” she explained. “We completed the job, but we were slightly injured, so we ran off for now, just to be safe.”

“Sounds like a great holiday,” Rindou said, walking away towards the kitchen.

“Was it you guys who caused all the trouble at Mitsuya’s show?” Ran asked, clearly interested, perhaps because of some history between them. She nodded.

“Anyway, I’m glad you’re not too badly hurt. Here,” he said, setting four cups of tea and some snacks on the dining table. “Eat and drink while I’m still feeling nice.”

“Aww, Rinnie, you’re so sweet!” she exclaimed, hugging him with one arm. “You should be nice more often.” She sat down at the table, grabbed a mug and sipped her tea. Sanzu and Ran sat down too.

“Psh, you’ll be the perfect housewife, Rinnie,” Sanzu said sarcastically, earning a whack on his injured thigh.

“Fuck!” he doubled over, twitching in pain.

It was likely that this short “group” holiday was going to turn into a chaotic nightmare.

…

It was the middle of the night, around half past three, when she was woken by the sound of movement outside her bedroom door. Sanzu was no longer beside her. Maybe he’s in the bathroom? She rolled onto her right side and watched the light under the door move back and forth, until the door creaked open slowly.

Ran stood in the doorway, a little surprised to find her awake. “Oh, hey, Akari,” he started, looking nervous.

“Why are you still awake?” she asked, raising an eyebrow.

He was silent, as if searching for an excuse. “I-I was just getting ready to go shopping for foo—”

“Cut the shit, Ran. Don’t lie to me,” she cut in, her voice sharp.

Ran audibly gulped. “The other two already left the house.”

That’s interesting, that Rindou and Sanzu would even get along, but— “I’m not sure where they went, but Sanzu told me to look after you while he was gone, so…” Ran finished, shrugging. She sighed. She was disappointed that he would leave her like this without a word. “Hmmm, okay, then.”

“That’s it?” Ran asked, expecting more of a reaction.

“Well, neither of us knows what they’re doing, so what can we really do?” she said. “Plus, Sanzu pretty much ordered you to look after me, and I know you’re a light sleeper too, so—” She pointed at the space Sanzu should have been in. “You can take this space here.”

“If you insist,” Ran said.

“If Sanzu has a problem with it, that’s his problem. He left me here alone, anyway,” she said with a shrug, turning over to face the wall with her back to Ran and the door. “I’m going back to sleep.”

The bed dipped under Ran’s weight, and the room fell silent again.

“Goodnight,” he murmured.

“Goodnight,” she replied, already drifting off.

Sanzu POV

I was stuck in the car with Rindou, and not by choice. “Why did you have to come? You could’ve stayed with Ran and watched over Akari,” I huffed, irritated by his presence in the passenger seat.

“Just be grateful I’m driving you where you want to go,” Rindou snapped, suddenly braking, so my head jerked forward.

“Bitch, I would’ve been fine on my own.”

“Tell me that again when you’ve stopped limping.”

I couldn’t argue with that, so I kept quiet. All I wanted was to grab a few things from the shop to surprise Akari, as an apology for everything that had happened in the Caribbean, and as a thank-you for everything she had done for me and for Yuuma. I hadn’t thought it through, though, because it was nearly four in the morning, close to sunrise.

“Where exactly are we headed?” Rindou asked.

“You’re telling me you were driving without knowing where we’re going?”

“Well, you didn’t say anything,” Rindou shrugged, and I was so close to kicking him out of the car and driving myself.

I held back a forced sigh. “To the nearest open store.”

“You do realize it’s four in the morning.”

“Yeah. That’s why I said ‘open.’”

…

“You could’ve got these things for her at a better time, you know. I could’ve had my beauty sleep instead of driving your ass around,” Rindou sighed, packing the flowers, groceries and snacks into the boot.

I hobbled over to the passenger door. “Oh, shut up. It’s the gesture that counts. You wouldn’t understand.”

“Hmm,” he said, with a blank stare. By now it was close to half past five, which gave me more than enough time to get back to the accommodation and make breakfast for Akari. “What’s with all the trays of red meat? Isn’t that a bit heavy for breakfast? For anyone…?”

“That’s for lunch or dinner later today. I was thinking barbecue outside, since there’s a stove in the back garden. If you and your brother are busy, that’s a shame, but—”

“Wait, that sounds like a pretty good idea,” Rindou said, his mouth watering. “We should be here for lunch.”

I hummed. “Sounds like a plan, then.”

…

Akari POV

She woke to a pair of arms wrapped round her waist. She turned onto her back and glanced at the clock on the wall. 7:30am. Early for waking, but she couldn’t really sleep any longer anyway. Ran was still asleep beside her, his grip on her waist quite strong.

She sighed, admiring his restful state, brushed the hair away from his face and laughed at his drooling. She grabbed her phone, took a quick photo for blackmail purposes, then slowly removed his arms and got out of bed.

Walking down the stairs, she smelled something sweet in the air. Syrup, maybe? She wasn’t quite sure. When she entered the kitchen, she was honestly surprised. Sanzu stood with his back to her, over the stove, so focused that he didn’t notice she was there. On the table nearby was a vase of beautiful summer flowers in full bloom, reds, yellows and pinks. Beside the vase was a small wrapped box, along with the syrup and other utensils.

She tiptoed up behind him and hugged him tightly, squeezing his backside lightly. “Good morning, sexy,” she said, in a flirtatious tone. “What’s the special occasion this morning?”

He didn’t seem surprised that she was there, as if he had known she would come. “Me? Sexy?” he said, turning to face her and looking down at her. “Have you looked in the mirror, sweetheart?” He pressed a soft kiss to her lips, then turned his attention back to the French toast and pancakes in the frying pan.

He plated up the pancakes and toast and carried the plate to the dining table, and she followed him over. She sat down in front of the plate, and Sanzu sat down beside her. “So?” she asked again. “What’s with these gestures?”

“Can’t I just do it because I feel like it, sweetheart?” he asked, chuckling as she ate, and wiping off the syrup that had smeared across the corner of her lips. After a moment, he slid the small box across the table towards her. “Here, open it for me.”

She stopped stuffing her mouth, put her fork and knife down and looked up at him. He gave her a reassuring nod. She began to unwrap the box, her eyes widening slowly at what it might hold.

“Sanzu, wha—” she started, opening the box and realizing it was an engagement ring. She gasped and covered her mouth as tears began to spill.

“Akari. I think it’s about time I asked you this. We’ve been together since we were teenagers, and I wouldn’t want anyone but you. I’ve cherished every single moment we’ve had together over the years. I’m sorry I missed Yuuma’s birth, but he’s a gift no one else could have given me. Our treasure, which no one could ever put a price on. I love you too much to still just be your boyfriend. I’d like to be your husband.” He took the ring out of the box and held it up in front of her. “I’m so sorry I can’t get down on one knee right now, but, Akari, will you make me your husband?” he asked, looking into her eyes with so much love and adoration.

She nodded, still a little shocked. She had no idea this was coming. To be honest, she had given up on the idea of properly tying the knot, since it wasn’t an ideal situation, being criminals and everything, but look where she was now. “Of course, Sanzu. I look forward to the next seventy years with you.” She smiled through her tears. His fingers brushed her cheeks, wiping the tears away. “Thank you, Akari. For everything.” He kissed her forehead and then her lips. “I love you.”

She laughed. “I love you more.”

…

In the living room, Rindou was asleep on the couch. He hadn’t realized that the whole thing had happened just as he woke up. He smiled to himself through sleepy eyes, listening to Sanzu’s heartfelt words. He was a little surprised that Sanzu could express himself so well, and then he went back to catching up on his missed sleep.
